jobs.title: Technical Officer – Ocean Observations
jobs.body:
## Description

The **Pacific Community (SPC)** is the principal scientific and technical organisation in the Pacific region, supporting development since 1947. We are an international development organisation owned and governed by our 27 country and territory members. In pursuit of sustainable development to benefit Pacific people, our organisation works across more than 25 sectors. We are known for our knowledge and innovation in such areas as fisheries science, public health, geoscience, and conservation of plant genetic resources for food and agriculture.

The **Geoscience Energy and Maritime (GEM) Division** provides advice, technical assistance, research and training support to Pacific Island countries and territories (PICTs). There are four (4) areas of scientific programming within this division:

1. **Oceans and Maritime Programme (OMP)** – assists member countries with services that provide applied ocean science and knowledge for evidence-based policy-making and technical solutions for improved ocean and maritime governance, management and capacity development.
2. **Georesources and Energy Programme (GEP)** – assists member countries by applying technical knowledge in the areas of geoscience and sustainable energy use.
3. **Disaster and Water Resilience Programme (DWRP)** – assists member countries to demonstrate strengthened resilience through integrated action on disaster risk management, climate change adaptation, natural resource management and increased access to water and sanitation.
4. **Earth and Ocean Observation Services** – Promoting spatial data and systems analysis and capacity to improve decision-making to improve resilience and sustainable resource management.

The role – **Technical Officer – Ocean Observations** will provide technical hands-on support for SPC’s regional ocean observation and monitoring activities, with a primary focus on wave monitoring systems. The role operates within SPC’s technical workshop capability, supporting the deployment, maintenance, and operational sustainability of wave buoys, while contributing to other in situ ocean observing systems (e.g. ADCPs, water-quality sensors, and multi-sensor platforms) across SPC member countries, including applications relevant to fisheries, maritime, and ocean and climate services.

The key responsibilities of the role include:

**Wave and Ocean Monitoring System – Deployment and Field Operations**

- Plan, coordinate, and participate in deployment, recovery, and redeployment of wave buoys and other in situ ocean observing instruments, in collaboration with SPC teams and national counterparts, including participation in diving operations where required.
- Undertake or contribute to site assessments, mooring design and deployment planning ensuring alignment with local environmental conditions and operational requirements.
- Lead or support offshore and coastal field operations, ensuring compliance with SPC safety and operational procedures, and alignment with mission objectives.
- Prepare mission plans, risk assessments, and field operation reports, documenting technical outcomes, issues encountered, and lessons learned.

**Maintenance, Troubleshooting and Technical Support**

- Provide technical maintenance and troubleshooting support for wave buoys and other in‑situ ocean observing systems, including sensors, telemetry, power systems, and moorings, in collaboration with national counterparts, SPC teams and service providers.
- Plan and coordinate preventative and corrective maintenance activities, to ensure operational availability and longevity of observing systems.
- Diagnose technical faults, recommend corrective actions, and support their implementation by relevant SPC teams, service providers, or national partners.
- Maintain accurate maintenance logs, calibration records, and technical documentation to support asset tracking, audits, and knowledge transfer.

**Data Quality Assurance, Data Management Procedures & SOP Development**

- Support the application of agreed data management and data quality assurance procedures for wave buoys and other in situ ocean observing systems, in line with SPC and country arrangements.
- Support the timely and reliable ingestion of observation data from SPC‑supported systems into SPC and agreed national data management platforms.
- Work with national counterparts to support the sharing and integration of country‑owned observation data in accordance with agreed processes and data governance arrangements.
- Contribute to the development, maintenance, and application of standard operating procedures (SOPs) covering deployment, maintenance, data handling, and incident response.

**Procurement and Asset Management**

- Provide technical input to procurement processes for ocean observing equipment and services, including preparation of technical specifications, participation in evaluations, and engagement with suppliers, in line with SPC policies and procedures.
- Maintain accurate and up-to-date records of ocean observing assets, including inventories, warranties, servicing requirements, and lifecycle status, to support effective planning, maintenance, and sustainability of observing systems.
- Coordinate logistics for ocean observing equipment, including shipping, customs clearance, insurance, and freight documentation, in collaboration with SPC logistics, procurement, and finance teams.
- Ensure asset and logistics documentation is complete, current, and accessible to support audits, reporting, and effective handover between staff and teams.

For a more detailed account of the key responsibilities, please **refer to the online job description**.

## Key selection criteria

**Qualifications**

- Degree in electronics, electrical engineering, marine science or technology, ocean instrumentation, or a closely related technical discipline or an equivalent body of knowledge and experience.
- Open Water Diving certification or equivalent occupational diving certification, and fitness to undertake work‑related diving activities.

**Technical expertise**

- Minimum 4-5 years’ progressive technical experience in marine, oceanographic, environmental monitoring, or related operational fieldwork.
- Demonstrated experience in the deployment, recovery, commissioning, testing, and validation of in situ observation systems, such as wave buoys, moorings, current meters (e.g. ADCPs), or multi‑sensor platforms.
- Practical experience maintaining and troubleshooting marine instrumentation, including sensors, telemetry, power systems, and associated electronics.
- Experience supporting or applying preventative and corrective maintenance practices, including record‑keeping and technical documentation.
- Understanding of marine field operations, including site selection, environmental conditions, operational risks, and safety requirements.
- Experience delivering hands‑on technical training or mentoring to adult learners or technical counterparts.
- Proven ability to work effectively with government agencies, technical services, and regional partners.

**Language skills**

- Excellent English communication skills (oral and written) with a working knowledge of French being an advantage.

**Interpersonal skills and cultural awareness**

- Ability to work in a multicultural, inclusive and equitable environment.

## Salary, terms and conditions

**Contract Duration** – **Until 30 June 2028** – subject to renewal depending on funding and performance.

**Remuneration** – The **Technical Officer – Ocean Observations** is a band 8 position in SPC’s 2026 salary scale, with a starting salary range of 2,146‒2,683 SDR (special drawing rights) per month, which currently converts to approximately FJD 6,632–8,290 (USD 2,876–3,595; EUR 2,595–3,244). An offer of appointment for an initial contract will normally be made in the lower half of this range, with due consideration given to experience and qualifications.Progression within the salary scale will be based on annual performance reviews. Remuneration of expatriate SPC staff members is not subject to income tax in Fiji; Fiji nationals employed by SPC in Fiji will be subject to income tax.

**Benefits for Staff in a position advertised internationally (EPAI) whose duty station is Suva –** SPC provides a housing allowance of FJD 1,500–5,200 per month. Establishment and repatriation grant, removal expenses, airfares, home leave travel, health and life and disability insurances and education allowances are available for eligible employees and their eligible dependents. Employees are entitled to 25 working days of annual leave per annum and other types of leave, and access to SPC’s Provident Fund (contributing 8% of salary, to which SPC adds a 10% contribution).

**Languages** – SPC’s working languages are English and French.

**Recruitment principles** – SPC’s recruitment is based on merit and fairness, and candidates are competing in a selection process that is fair, transparent and non-discriminatory. SPC is an **equal-opportunity employer**, and is committed to cultural and gender diversity, including bilingualism, and will seek to attract and appoint candidates who respect these values. Due attention is given to gender equity and the maintenance of strong representation from Pacific Island professionals. If two interviewed candidates are ranked equal by the selection panel, preference will be given to the **Pacific Islander**. Applicants will be assured of complete confidentiality in line with SPC’s Privacy Policy.

jobs.title: Administrative coordinator (F/M) - Ukraine
jobs.body:
Do you want to join a committed, activist-driven organization and take meaningful action for social justice?  
For over 40 years, Médecins du Monde has been delivering healthcare to the most vulnerable, challenging barriers to access, and driving long-term change in health policies.

In France and across nearly 30 countries, our work is built around six core missions:

- Sexual and reproductive health and rights (including access to safe abortion)
- Migration, exile, human rights and health
- Harm reduction
- Health and the environment
- Healthcare systems
- Humanitarian spaces

**MdM in Ukraine**

MdM International Network has been operating in Ukraine since 2014, improving access to health care, especially providing comprehensive Primary Health Care (PHC), Sexual and Reproductive Health (SRH) and Mental Health and Psychosocial support (MHPSS) services.

Since February 2022, MdM Spain is leading the country response for the network, while MdM-France is in charge of the operations in Southern Ukraine. The global strategy aims at ensuring the access to quality comprehensive healthcare services for the conflict-affected population in Ukraine.

In Southern Ukraine, MdM-France has set up its country office and a base office in Mykolaiv. An office in Odesa is still running for specific activities monitoring in Odesa. The program consists in supporting various local-based organizations in the delivery of health services for people facing severe constraints to healthcare in Mykolaev and Kherson Oblasts.

The main strategic objectives for the Adminisrative department are, to consolidate the operational process at mission level to strengthen the quality of support services, to transfer competencies to national staff as well as working closer with national partners to build capacities.

Living conditions in Mykolaiv are pleasant (access to restaurants, presence of other organizations, places to relax...).

Expats share modern, well-equiped guesthouse. However, there are strict security rules (curfew imposed by the authorities) and a volatile environment (regular activation of air alerts).

**About the role**

As Administrative Coordinator, you ensure completeness, correctness, timeliness and integrity in your role. As a strategic partner to the operations, you will contribute to the definition and implementation of the mission’s objectives, participate in the sizing of the HR and financial needs and provide technical support to operational staff on the HR and Financial management of the mission.

**What you’ll do**

More specifically, your main responsibilities are the following:

- Nationalize the administrative coordinator position
- Review & implement a new HR set up of Finance & HR department post nationalization
- Supervise the implementation of the mission’s HR set-up
- Define, adapt, plan, and supervise the implementation of the mission’s human resources frameworks, procedures and policies while respecting the local context, local legislation and MdM policies and values (compensations and benefits, recruitment good practices, performance reviews, staff safe guarding, talent management, staff disciplines, career development and learning or team building)
- Plan, centralize, coordinate, and supervise the financial management and administration of the mission (accounting, budget construction and follow-up, internal and external reporting, donor compliance, audits, administrative legal obligations, etc.)
- Follow up the evolution of the legal environment and ensure MdM remains in line with official guidelines and policies in the framework of its principled approach
- Recruit, train, and manage an administrative department team
- Provide technical support to operational staff on the HR and financial management of the mission
- In terms of coordination and representation, you will ensure, when needed and by delegation of the General Coordinator, the representation of MdM in front of donors and liaise with INGOs heads of Admin Departments in-country
- You will provide strong oversight to MDM local Partner activities, including compliance with donor regulations

**Who you’ll work with**

Under the supervision of the General Coordinator (F/M), you will manage the HR and Finance team in the coordination office and functionally support the HR and Finance team in the operational base(s). You will closely interact with the HR and Finance Advisors based in the HQ and the other departments at mission level (logistics, programs etc.)

## REQUIREMENTS

**You are the right match if you:**

- hold a 3 years’ higher education management qualification
- have at least 4 years of experience in administration (HR and Finance) in a humanitarian context (including at least two years’ experience in an international NGO at coordination level)
- have an experience in a conflict setting or challenging environment. like in Ukraine (strong asset)
- have previous experience with MdM (preferred)
- proved your ability to negotiate and build / consolidate a network with authorities in a complex and volatile legal environment
- have a previous successful experience in team management (preferred)
- have a significant experience in PSEA management (an advantage)
- have a solid experience in budget management backed by institutional donors, payroll and accounting in a humanitarian context (prerequisite)
- you proved you are able to understand and interpret the legal administrative framework for staff and the MdM rules
- you have excellent Microsoft Office skills (especially Excel) and knowledge of accountancy software (like Saga or any relevant ERP)
- are fluent in English (mandatory, C1 level minimum), and have some knowledge of Ukrainian and/or Russian (would be an asset

**This role may not suit you if:**

- you are not aligned with MdM’s values and activist approach
- you are not able to defend the Administrative point of you in front of other actors/leaders
- you are not diplomatic and assertive

**Recruitment process**

If shortlisted, you will first meet with our HR team. Technical and managerial interviews, which may include practical case studies, will follow during the month of November.

Please note: as part of our anti–money laundering and counter-terrorism policy, international background checks may be conducted. Data is processed confidentially and securely. More info: https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/  
All successful candidates must provide a criminal record extract (B3).

**Ready to apply?**

We only need your CV and a cover letter.  
If this role sounds like the right fit for you, apply now – we’d love to hear from you!

## EMPLOYMENT CONDITIONS

**Contract & status:**

- Gross monthly salary: 3'392 €
- Fixed-term contract (6 months), starting in beginning of December
- Single posting

**Work environment:**

- Position based in Mykolaiv
- Regular field visits

**Benefits**:

- 13th-month salary (for employees with more than 6 months’ seniority)
- Expatriation allowance: 10% of gross monthly salary
- Coverage of travel (home – mission), visas, and vaccinations
- Accommodation: guesthouse managed by the mission
- Health insurance (50% covered by MdM and 50% by the employee)
- Repatriation insurance
- MdM promotes training and internal mobility

**Essentials**:

- 5 weeks paid leave + 22.5 RTT days per year
- Strong commitment to inclusion and fighting all forms of discrimination
- More info: https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/

**Our commitment to diversity and inclusion**

MdM is committed to the inclusion of people with disabilities and to fighting all forms of discrimination.  
if you are officially recognized as a person with a disability and/or require workplace accommodations, please let us know.

jobs.title: Responsable Relation Bailleurs - H/F - Tchad
jobs.body:
**PRÉSENTATION ALIMA**

L’ESPRIT ALIMA : La raison d’être d’ALIMA est de sauver des vies et de soigner les populations les plus vulnérables, sans aucune discrimination identitaire, religieuse ou politique, à travers des actions basées sur la proximité, l’innovation et l’alliance d’organisations et d’individus. Nous agissons avec humanisme, impartialité et dans le respect de l’éthique médicale universelle. Pour accéder aux patients et aux patientes, nous nous engageons à intervenir de façon neutre et indépendante.

LES VALEURS et PRINCIPES de notre action, inscrits au sein de notre CHARTE :

1. Le patient d’abord
2. Révolutionner la médecine humanitaire
3. Responsabilité et liberté
4. Améliorer la qualité de nos actions
5. Faire confiance
6. L’intelligence collective
7. Responsabilité environnementale

ALIMA promeut et défend les principes des droits humains fondamentaux. ALIMA a une approche de tolérance zéro envers les personnes coupables d’actes de violences sexistes et sexuelles ainsi qu’envers l’inaction face à des faits de violence supposés ou avérés. La protection des personnes bénéficiant et impactées par notre intervention est notre priorité absolue dans tout ce que nous faisons. Toute personne collaborant avec ALIMA s’engage à :

- respecter la charte, le code de conduite, les politiques institutionnelles incluant la politique de protection contre les abus de pouvoir et les violences sexistes et sexuelles, la politique de prévention de la corruption et de la fraude ;
- signaler toute violation aux politiques, documents cadre et procédure à une supérieure, un supérieur, une référente, un référent ou à l’adresse prévue à cet effet

**SOIGNER - INNOVER – ENSEMBLE** :

Depuis sa création en 2009, ALIMA a touché plus de 18 millions de bénéficiaires dans 15 pays, principalement en Afrique. En 2024, nous avons développé 59 projets de réponse médicale humanitaire pour répondre aux besoins de populations touchées par les conflits, les épidémies et l’extrême pauvreté.

L’ensemble de ces projets se font en appui aux autorités sanitaires nationales à travers les structures de santé (dont hôpitaux et centres de santé). Notre action découle d’une adaptation constante aux réalités du terrain et aux progrès de la médecine. En 2024, ALIMA a atteint 5,9 millions de bénéficiaires.

Nous travaillons en partenariat, notamment avec des ONGs locales, dès que cela est possible afin de nous assurer que nos patients et patientes bénéficient de l’expertise là où elle se trouve, que ce soit au niveau de leur pays ou du reste du monde. Par ailleurs, pour améliorer la réponse humanitaire, nous menons des projets de recherches opérationnelles et cliniques notamment dans le domaine de la lutte

Contre la malnutrition et les fièvres virales hémorragiques.

L'ÉQUIPE ALIMA : Plus de 2000 personnes œuvrent actuellement pour ALIMA. Les équipes terrain, au plus proche des patients, reçoivent leur support des équipes de coordination généralement basées en capitale des pays d’intervention. Celles-ci reçoivent le support des 4 équipes desk et de l’équipe du service urgences et ouvertures basées au siège opérationnel de Dakar, Sénégal. Les équipes de Paris et New-York travaillent activement à la collecte de fonds ainsi qu’à la représentation d’ALIMA. Le reste de la Galaxie ALIMA comprend des individus et des équipes partenaires qui travaillent pour le compte d’autres organisations telles que les ONGs médicales BEFEN, ALERTE Santé, SOS Médecins / KEOOGO, AMCP, les organismes de recherche PACCI, INSERM, les Universités de Bordeaux ou de Copenhague, l’ONG Solidarités International et bien d’autres.

**NOS PAYS D’INTERVENTIONS** : Mali, Burkina Faso, République Centrafricaine, Nigeria, Niger, Tchad, République Démocratique du Congo, Cameroun, Soudan, Soudan du sud , Mauritanie, Ethiopie, Haïti.

NOS THÉMATIQUES PROJET : Malnutrition, Santé Maternelle, Santé Primaire, Pédiatrie, Paludisme, Épidémies (Ebola, Choléra, Rougeole, Dengue), Hospitalisation, Urgences, Violences Basées sur le Genre, Protection transversale, santé mentale …

**CONTEXTE DE LA MISSION** : Les programmes ALIMA AU TCHAD

Le Tchad connaît une crise alimentaire et nutritionnelle sévère, accentuée par des afflux de population importants mais aussi par sa vulnérabilité aux catastrophes naturelles et aux épidémies.

ALIMA a débuté ses activités au Tchad en 2012 en partenariat avec l'ONG médicale tchadienne Alerte Santé.

En 2012, le projet implanté dans le district sanitaire de Ngouri, dans la province sanitaire du Lac, a été mis en œuvre grâce au soutien d'ECHO, de OFDA, de l'UNICEF et du PAM. Dans le cadre de ce projet, l'accent a été mis sur l'amélioration de la qualité de la prise en charge, un défi majeur au Tchad étant données les difficultés à mobiliser des compétences médicales qualifiées. Depuis 2021, Alerte Santé & ALIMA mène dans le DS de Ngouri, Dibinitchi et Isserom, le projet d’étude OptiMA grâce au soutien financier de Givewell ainsi que le projet d’hôpital résilient CRESH grâce au soutien de plusieurs fondations.

A partir d’avril 2013, ALIMA & Alerte Santé appuient également la prise en charge de la MAS à N’Djamena. Avant la mise en œuvre de ce projet d'ALIMA & AS, seul le dispensaire de Notre Dame des Apôtres dans le district Sud, proposait une prise en charge gratuite de la malnutrition dans la capitale. Fort de deux années d’activités, le projet a permis de montrer l’ampleur de la problématique de la malnutrition en milieu urbain (à N’Djamena où le taux de MAS atteint 2.8%).

Depuis 2021, un projet d’étude OptiMA est en cours au sein de l’UNT de l’HATC à N’Djamena.

ALIMA mène également un projet communautaire dans le 9eme arrondissement de N’Djamena depuis 2022 en partenariat avec l’Agence Française de Développement pour le traitement et la prévention de la malnutrition.

Dans le bassin du Lac Tchad, la situation humanitaire s’est dégradée consécutivement à la recrudescence des attaques des GANEs et aux effets du changement climatique.

Depuis 2019, ALIMA/AS offre des soins médico-nutritionnels gratuits et de qualité aux enfants de moins de 5 ans et des soins de santé préventifs et curatifs gratuits aux populations déplacées et hôtes du DS de Liwa affectées par la crise du Lac. L'approche d'ALIMA/AS permet d’offrir des soins médicaux et nutritionnels dans des zones éloignées des centres de santé et ainsi permettre l’accès aux soins de santé pour les populations déplacées.

En réponse à la crise soudanaise et l’afflux de réfugiés soudanais au Tchad, ALIMA est intervenu dès 2023 pour mener des activités en santé et nutrition en faveur des réfugiés et des communautés hôtes présentes dans l’Est du pays. ALIMA intervient actuellement dans la province du SILA, appuyant la prise en charge médicale des patients dans les sites de réfugiés ainsi que dans un centre de santé.

De par son importante couverture et la qualité reconnue de son intervention, ALIMA s’inscrit au Tchad comme un acteur majeur de la santé.

Entre janvier et septembre 2024, ALIMA a pris en charge plus de 35000 cas de malnutrition aigue chez les enfants de moins de 6 ans, soit près de 9% du total des prises en charge du pays.

Sur la même période, 140669 consultations ambulatoires, 1146 hospitalisations et 13000 prises en charge à domicile ont été réalisées par nos équipes sur l’ensemble de nos zones d’opérations.

LIEU DU POSTE : N’Djamena, TCHAD

**PROTECTION DES BÉNÉFICIAIRES ET DES MEMBRES DE LA COMMUNAUTÉ**

Niveau 3 : Dans le cadre de ses fonctions, le ou la titulaire du poste sera amené·e à visiter les programmes et être en contact avec des enfants ou/et des adultes vulnérables. Par conséquent, la vérification du casier judiciaire ou la présentation d'un certificat de bonne vie et mœurs sera nécessaire. Dans les situations où l’impossibilité de fournir un casier judiciaire ou un certificat de bonne vie et mœurs est constatée, une déclaration sur l’honneur sera demandée.

**LIENS FONCTIONNELS ET HIERARCHIQUES**

- Responsable Hiérarchique : Chef.fe de Mission (basé à N’Djamena)
- Responsable Fonctionnel : Référent Bailleurs ‐ Desk 1 (basé à Dakar)

**MISSION PRINCIPALE**

Sous la supervision du.de la Chef.ffe de Mission, le.la Responsable Relations Bailleurs est responsable de la mise en œuvre de la stratégie de financement en lien avec le plan d’actions pays d’ALIMA.

Plus spécifiquement, il.elle est responsable de mobiliser des financements qui permettront la mise en œuvre des projets. Il·Elle entretient des relations régulières avec les bailleurs de fonds, et mène une recherche active de financements. Il.Elle est le garant ou la garante de la rédaction des propositions de projet et rapports aux bailleurs. Il·Elle appuie le suivi des indicateurs contractuels bailleurs, en collaboration avec les Coordinateurs.trices de projet et le.la Coordinateur.trice Médical.e.

**ACTIVITÉS PRINCIPALES**

- Définition et suivi de la stratégie de financement pays

Le.la Responsable Relations Bailleurs effectue une analyse de la stratégie des bailleurs et la disponibilité de financements pour le pays concerné, afin de maintenir un niveau élevé d’information et de compréhension des enjeux. Il.Elle identifie les besoins de financements sur la mission en collaboration avec l'équipe de coordination et propose une stratégie de financement pertinente pour la mission. Il.Elle évalue les enjeux et propose l'adaptation de la stratégie selon le plan d’action opérationnel du pays. Au cours de la mission, le.la responsable Relations Bailleurs effectue le suivi de la stratégie de financement et l’adapte selon l'évolution des besoins. En lien avec le Chef de Mission et le.la Référent.e Bailleurs au siège, il.elle appuie la conception et la mise en œuvre d'une stratégie d'acquisition de subventions et de mobilisation de ressources

- Entretien de la relation avec les bailleurs de fonds

En lien avec le Chef.fe de Mission, il·elle assure la représentation auprès des bailleurs de fonds et négocie des financements pour les projets d’ALIMA. Il.Elle entretient les relations avec les bailleurs de fonds qui financent les projets pour assurer une communication régulière de qualité. Il.Elle coordonne la visite des bailleurs de fonds sur les projets quand la situation sécuritaire le permet, avec l’appui du.de la Chef.ffe de Mission.

- Recherche de financements

Le.la Responsable Relations Bailleurs, en appui au Chef de Mission, mène une recherche active de financements et identifie les nouveaux bailleurs de fonds à approcher dans le but d’assurer la bonne connaissance d’ALIMA et des projets mis en œuvre par ses acteurs. Il mène une veille active sur les priorités thématiques des donateurs et des mécanismes de financement dans le pays. Il.Elle effectue la cartographie des donateurs et la collecte de renseignements, et informe régulièrement la coordination pays ce sujet. Il.Elle développe des fiches projets et plaquettes pour assurer la communication institutionnelle tout au long de l’année

- Appui à la planification opérationnelle en lien avec les priorités des bailleurs de fonds

Le.la Responsable Relations Bailleurs appuie les Coordinateurs.trices Projet et l'équipe de coordination dans la conception d’interventions en lien avec la stratégie des bailleurs de fonds. Il.Elle s’assure que les interventions sont alignées avec les priorités thématiques et opérationnelles des bailleurs de fonds, et que les soumissions respectent les formats requis par ces derniers.

- ## Production de concepts notes et de propositions de projet

Afin d’obtenir des financements, le.la Responsable Relations Bailleurs est responsable de la soumission des concepts notes et propositions de projets dans les délais imposés par les bailleurs de fonds. Il.Elle assure l’écriture des documents de projet pour répondre aux opportunités auprès des bailleurs de fonds. Il.Elle est garant de la qualité et conformité des documents produits.

- ## Diffuse les informations clés sur les procédures bailleurs, les contrats de financement et appui les Coordinateurs.trices de Projet dans le suivi des exigences contractuelles

Le.la Responsable Relations Bailleurs est responsable de la mise à jour de l’équipe de coordination sur les guidelines des bailleurs de fonds. Il.Elle informe continuellement les équipes de l’évolution des procédures et exigences des bailleurs de fonds. En plus, le.la Responsable Relations Bailleurs appuie les Coordinateur·rice·s de Projet dans le suivi des exigences contractuelles des bailleurs de fonds. Le.la Responsable Relations Bailleurs suit les évolutions opérationnelles, y compris budgétaire, afin de proposer des modifications contractuelles si nécessaires.

- Suivi des données pour répondre aux exigences du reporting

Le.la Responsable Relations Bailleurs développe et incorpore des éléments solides de monitoring et de suivi dans les rapports dans les outils de suivi des projets et il.elle participe donc, avec le.la Data Manager et le.la Coordinateur.trice Médical.e, au contrôle et à la compilation des données opérationnelles. Il.Elle s’assure de la mise à jour des outils de suivi de données en lien avec les contrats de financement, et anticipe les échéances des rapports afin d’assurer la complétude des données et une analyse de qualité.

- Assurer la production de rapports narratifs précis et analytiques dans les délais définis

Le.la Responsable Relations Bailleurs est responsable de l’élaboration des rapports intermédiaires et finaux pour les bailleurs de fonds, selon les formats et règles de reporting imposés. Il est directement chargé de la rédaction des documents, sur la base des informations précises, quantitatives et qualitatives et capitalisées au cours de l’année. Il·Elle établit une liaison régulière avec les Coordinateur·trice·s et responsables de projet et, pour l’élaboration des rapports, fait le lien entre les engagements auprès du bailleur et la réalité des projets et des terrains. Il.Elle s’assure du respect des deadlines et est responsable de la qualité des rapports.

- ## Assurer la gestion contractuelle des contrats de financement

Le.la Responsable Relations Bailleurs est garant du suivi des contrats de financement avec les bailleurs de fonds. Il·Elle est en contact direct avec les représentants nationaux du bailleur pour les questions de gestion contractuelle. Il·Elle s’assure de connaître et respecter les procédures du bailleur et que celles‐ci soient connues du reste de l’équipe. Il·Elle dispose pour cela d’un outil commun de suivi de contrat qu’il·elle contribue à mettre à jour.

- ## Assurer l’application des standards en prévention contre les abus

Le.la Responsable Relations Bailleurs doit participer aux formations et aux séances de sensibilisation. Il·Elle applique les standards relatifs à la prévention contre les abus dans toutes les tâches qu’il·elle entreprend (ex: ajout de la thématique dans les rapports, les propositions de projet, clause sur la prévention des abus, etc). Il·Elle contribue à créer et maintenir un environnement épanouissant et protecteur.

**EXPERIENCES ET COMPETENCES**

- Diplôme d’études supérieur (niveau Master ou équivalent) en lien avec le poste (études du développement, santé publique, relations internationales, gestion de projet…)
- Excellent niveau d’anglais et de Français, à l’oral et à l'écrit
- Bonne maîtrise des outils de gestion de projet (cycle de projet, cadre logique, proposition de projets, reporting, etc…)

**Type de contrat** : CDD de droit Français avec possibilité de renouvellement

**Durée du contrat** : 6 mois renouvelable

**Lieu du poste** : N’Djamena, TCHAD

**Salaire :** Selon grille salariale ALIMA (niveau 11BIS) + valorisation de l’expérience + Perdiem

ALIMA prend en charge :

Les frais de déplacements entre le pays d’origine de l’expatrié et le lieu de mission

Les frais d’hébergement

La couverture médicale du premier jour de contrat à un mois après la date de départ du pays de mission pour l’employé et ses ayants droit

L’évacuation pour l’employé et ses ayants droit.

Date de prise de poste : **ASAP**

- Une expérience professionnelle en reporting, conception et/ou gestion de projet d’au moins un an, ainsi que d’une expérience de terrain.
- Excellentes capacités d’analyse, de synthèse et rédactionnelles
- Autonomie, capacité d’initiative, facilité à travailler en équipe et à communiquer
- Rigueur, motivation, volonté d’atteindre les objectifs d’appui aux projets
- Compréhension et adhésion aux valeurs et à la mission d’ALIMA

jobs.title: Team Leader, Syria Education Programme III (SEP III)
jobs.body:
**SYRIA EDUCATION PROGRAMME III (SEP III)**

Building on SEP I (2018–2022) and SEP II (2022–2027), which supported primary educatio in Idleb and Aleppo, FCDO plans to procure a new Technical Assistance (TA) contract, SEP III, to support the Syrian Ministry of Education (MoE) in implementing its nationally-led reform agenda, complementing the Ministry's wider reform programme, including support provided through the Global Partnership for Education (GPE). Since December 2024, the MoE has begun to reunify a fragmented education system, but progress has been constrained by limited institutional capacity, a lack of data, weak policy development processes and the absence of a clear long-term strategy for recovery. Unlike earlier phases, which focused primarily on service delivery in northwest Syria, SEP III will work directly with the MoE and local Education Directorates, generally at national level and directorate level, in partnership with Ministry officials, to help the Ministry translate its policy and process reforms into practice through technical advice, capacity building, coaching and support to implementation.

SEP III has two components. The first, which is the subject of this contract, is politically informed TA to the MoE and Education Directorates to strengthen inclusive, effective and evidence-based policy making. The second is non-formal education (NFE) for returning refugees and internally displaced persons, which is outside the scope of this contract and will be delivered by a separate provider. The TA supplier will be required to work collaboratively with the NFE component.

The exact scope of the TA work will be determined jointly with FCDO and the MoE through a demand-led, co-designed and flexible approach. No reform priorities are set in advance; they will be identified with the Ministry during inception. The work is expected to focus on strengthening the education system to improve foundational learning outcomes for primary-school-aged children across Syria, delivered through: 1) Services and Analysis to inform TA and policy decisions; 2) Foundational Learning thematic TA (for example teacher development, coaching and supervision, safeguarding, learning data generation and use, and inclusive education); and 3) Education Systems Strengthening TA (sector planning and prioritisation, policy development, financial management, and monitoring and accountability). Given the difficult fiscal choices likely to shape the sector over the coming years, the programme is also expected to support the Ministry's public finance and value-for-money decision-making. Illustrative technical priorities include: supporting policy reform and Ministry-led coordination, standard-setting, and system strengthening; supporting the roll-out of child safeguarding and Codes of Conduct; improving the quality and consistency of teaching through professional development and a national Teacher Competency Framework; and data-driven planning, including through education management information systems (EMIS/SIMIS).

Given the fluid transition context, the programme will need to operate flexibly, respond quickly to changes, and seize windows of opportunity for reform as they arise. FCDO expects a politically informed, 'test, learn, adapt' approach rather than a fixed blueprint. Delivery must be aligned with government systems, avoiding parallel platforms and the substitution of government functions, and must be underpinned by gender equality, disability and social inclusion (GEDSI) and conflict sensitivity. This requires strong political judgement, including a clear understanding of how decisions are made within the Ministry and government and where opportunities for reform are most likely to emerge, an in-depth understanding of the Syrian education system and its institutional actors, and the ability to sustain trusted relationships with the Ministry, FCDO, and other sector stakeholders, including UNICEF, GPE, Education Cannot Wait (ECW), and the World Bank.

The anticipated delivery model comprises i) a **Core Delivery Team** responsible for overall leadership, technical oversight, coordination, MEAL, governance and quality assurance, which should be predominantly Syrian and mostly based in Syria; and ii) a **demand-led TA Pool** of experts with education and governance backgrounds. The contract is expected to begin on 1 July 2027 with a six-month inception period, during which the supplier must mobilise rapidly, establish a presence in Damascus and operationalise its delivery systems. Details are indicative and will be confirmed in FCDO's Tender Notice.

**POSITION SUMMARY**

The Team Leader holds overall accountability for the design, rapid mobilisation, and delivery of SEP III, including leading the Core Delivery Team and overseeing the TA Pool, ensuring the programme is implemented in accordance with the contract, FCDO requirements, IRC policies and principles, and internationally recognised quality of assistance standards. The Team Leader is the primary point of contact with FCDO and, working closely with the ESS Technical Director and senior Ministry counterparts, provides strategic direction to support the Ministry's implementation of its reform priorities.

The Team Leader is responsible for the programme's overall management, including budget oversight and value for money, performance against contractual KPIs, and risk management (including fiduciary and reputational risk in a sensitive political environment), with the technical quality of the programme's workstreams assured by the ESS Technical Director. The postholder ensures the programme operates adaptively — using political analysis, evidence, monitoring data, and regular review points to prioritise, test, learn and adapt in response to a fast-moving political and institutional context — while maintaining the flexibility needed to respond to emerging windows of opportunity for reform.

The Team Leader maintains strong working relationships with the implementing team, consortium/delivery partners (if applicable), the MoE and Education Directorates, FCDO, the provider of the NFE component, and other education sector stakeholders, and represents the programme and IRC in relevant coordination fora, technical working groups, and policy dialogues. The postholder also oversees programme staffing, procurement, and administrative functions, and ensures robust communications and knowledge management, both internally and with external stakeholders, to share progress, evidence, and lessons learned.

**JOB RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Strategic Leadership**

● Provide overall strategic leadership for SEP III, ensuring the programme's support to the MoE and Education Directorates, led technically by the ESS Technical Director, is relevant to, and aligned with, the Ministry's evolving reform priorities and helps translate these priorities into practice.

● Lead the six-month inception period (July –December 2027), including establishing the Damascus presence, mobilising the Core Delivery Team and TA Pool, operationalising delivery systems, formalising ways of working with the MoE, developing the screening and prioritisation framework and Tasking Order criteria, and delivering inception milestones to FCDO's standard and timetable.

● Provide strategic oversight of the ESS Technical Director's technical leadership, ensuring the programme's technical direction remains aligned with strategic priorities and senior-level MoE relations.

● Ensure the programme operates flexibly and applies a 'test, learn, adapt' approach: agreeing clear reform objectives and decision criteria with the Ministry, co-designing and trialling options, using evidence and learning to decide whether to continue, scale, adapt, pause or pivot workstreams, and documenting adaptation decisions.

● Think and work politically, with a strong understanding of how decisions are made within the Ministry and government and where opportunities for reform are most likely to emerge, drawing on strong contextual and institutional analysis to ensure these opportunities are identified early and acted upon in a timely way.

● Take explicit responsibility for reform sequencing, political economy analysis, and navigating institutional constraints, ensuring a regularly updated PEA and periodic political reviews inform programme design, prioritisation and delivery, and that support is prioritised and paced in line with the Ministry's capacity and the political space available for reform.

● Ensure delivery remains aligned with government systems, avoids parallel platforms and substituting for government functions, and is designed for sustainability and capacity transfer, while supporting coalitions of reform-minded actors within and beyond government.

● Champion evidence-based, gender-responsive, and inclusive approaches throughout programme design and delivery, including dedicated attention to the needs of girls and children with disabilities, and ensure conflict sensitivity is embedded throughout.

● Provide leadership on GEDSI, ensuring diversity and inclusion are reflected in team and partner selection, programme design and implementation, and programme reporting.

**Donor, Government and Stakeholder Relations**

● Serve as the primary point of contact and representational link with FCDO, ensuring high-quality, timely reporting through formal and informal debriefings, and annual and semi-annual reports.

● Build and maintain a trusted, politically informed working relationship with senior officials in the MoE and other relevant government counterparts, supporting the Ministry's stewardship of the education sector and complementing the ESS Technical Director's ongoing technical-level engagement with MoE and Education Directorate representatives at all levels to identify technical assistance needs and design and implement ESS interventions.

● Coordinate with sector stakeholders, including UNICEF, GPE, ECW, the World Bank, and other donors and implementing partners, to support coordinated reform efforts across government and development partners, and to ensure the programme complements ongoing initiatives and other TA investments and adheres to national and global standards.

● Ensure close coherence and collaboration with the provider of the separate NFE component of SEP III, including joint planning, information sharing and coordination of engagement with the Ministry.

● Represent the programme and IRC at national and international forums, including technical conferences and policy dialogues, sharing programme achievements and lessons learned.

● Champion accountability to affected populations, partners, and diverse stakeholders, ensuring that feedback and complaints mechanisms, transparent communication, and participatory approaches inform programme design, delivery, and adaptive management.

**Programme, Risk and Financial Management**

● Oversee overall programme and budget management, ensuring value for money across all components, informed by a sound understanding of the Ministry's public finance context, and robust compliance with FCDO and IRC financial and procurement requirements.

● Oversee the Tasking Order mechanism for the TA Pool, ensuring requests are screened and prioritised against agreed criteria, co-created with the Ministry and Education Directorates, approved by FCDO, costed transparently against the agreed rate card with clear milestones, and delivered to a high-quality standard.

● Lead on identification and management of programme risks, including fiduciary, safeguarding, political, and reputational risks associated with operating within Syrian government structures during a period of political transition.

● Develop, review, and monitor, in coordination with key programme staff, the annual work plan (updated quarterly) and performance plans, and ensure quarterly and annual reports are submitted in the agreed format and to the required standard, so that long-term and short-term priorities remain on track.

● Take responsibility for contractual performance against FCDO's KPIs (indicatively covering reporting, work planning, expenditure variance, risk, safeguarding and fraud notification compliance, political analysis, timely delivery of TA outputs, Ministry adoption of TA outputs, and evidence of adaptive management), taking early corrective action where performance is at risk.

● Ensure monitoring, evaluation, and learning (MEL) data systematically feed into adaptive management processes, including regular reviews of cost-effectiveness and progress against outcomes.

**People and Operations Management**

● Manage programme staff, including through direct line management of the ESS Technical Director and other senior team members, and, where applicable, consortium or delivery partners, ensuring proper reporting, financial management, and compliance with donor and organisational requirements.

● Build a Core Delivery Team and TA Pool, drawing on national and international expertise only, and ensure all consortium or delivery partners can deploy Syrian expertise, with at least one member registered in Syria.

● Create and maintain a work environment that promotes teamwork, trust, mutual respect, and empowers staff to take responsibility.

● Oversee procurement, logistical, and administrative functions in support of programme delivery.

● Ensure appropriate internal and external communications and knowledge management, sharing achievements and lessons learned with diverse audiences.

**PROFILE AND QUALIFICATIONS**

● Advanced degree (Master's or equivalent) in education, public administration, international development, or a related field; equivalent experience may be substituted for a graduate degree.

● Minimum of 10 years' experience managing large-scale, complex, donor-funded technical assistance or education programmes, ideally including experience with FCDO-funded contracts and performance-based or KPI-linked payment mechanisms.

● Significant prior experience working directly with government ministries or line departments on system-level policy and process reform, ideally within the education sector.

● Substantial experience working in conflict, crisis, or politically sensitive transition contexts; experience in Syria or the broader MENA region strongly preferred.

● Sound understanding of public finance and value-for-money principles, with the ability to support the Ministry in navigating the fiscal choices shaping education sector reform.

● Proven ability to provide strategic leadership while harnessing the multi-disciplinary skills of technical personnel, consortium or delivery partners, and government counterparts.

● Demonstrated ability to create and nurture strong, trusted working relationships with Ministry of Education representatives and other relevant government, donor, and sector stakeholders.

● Strong political judgement, including a sound understanding of how decisions are made within government and where opportunities for reform are most likely to emerge, and demonstrated ability to apply thinking and working politically, using PEA to inform decisions, and to operate flexibly and adaptively in a fast-moving, sensitive institutional environment, responding to windows of opportunity as they arise.

● Demonstrated ability to build and sustain effective, trusted relationships with senior government officials, donors, and a broad range of stakeholders, including civil society and multilateral partners.

● Familiarity with the Syrian education system, or comparable fragile/post-conflict education systems, and with the priorities of foundational learning, safeguarding, and inclusion, including for girls and children with disabilities.

● Experience with adaptive management approaches and evidence-based programming, ideally including leading demand-led technical assistance facilities that use tasking orders or similar call-down mechanisms.

● Experience rapidly mobilising a programme team and establishing an operational presence in a new or complex setting, ideally Syria or a comparable context.

● Demonstrated commitment to localisation, including experience leading predominantly national teams and working in partnership with national and sub-national organisations.

● Strong analytical, communication, and writing skills, with the ability to articulate evidence-based positions to influence sector and government stakeholders.

● Demonstrated ability to apply safeguarding, ethics, and do-no-harm principles throughout programme delivery, particularly when working with or on behalf of children.

● Fluency in English required; Arabic language skills strongly preferred.

***Please note that this position is contingent on the outcome of the FCDO procurement and award of SEP III (tender publication currently anticipated for January 2027 and award for May 2027). Programme details are indicative and remain subject to FCDO approval and the final Tender Notice.***

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

jobs.title: Deputy Director of Operations for Programme and Development – Geneva, Switzerland
jobs.body:
**Department:** Operations

**Duty Station:** Geneva

**Contract Type:** Full-time (100%)

**Direct report:** Director of Operations

**Grade:** Head of

## **Mission**

Geneva Call is a neutral and impartial non-governmental organisation dedicated to promoting respect by Armed Groups and De Facto and/or Provisional Authorities (AGDAs) for international humanitarian norms in armed conflict and other situations of violence, in particular those related to the protection of civilians. Geneva Call focuses its efforts on banning the use of anti-personnel mines, protecting children from the effects of armed conflict, prohibiting sexual violence in armed conflict, working towards the elimination of gender discrimination, protecting civilian infrastructure, and ensuring humanitarian access.

## **Why this role?**

Under the overall supervision of the Director of Operations, the role of Deputy Director of Operations for Programme and Development (DDOPD) is to lead the Programme and Development unit and develop standardised programmatic approaches and models in alignment with programmatic cycle management tools and ensure programmatic interventions are based on Geneva Call’s mission – Theory of Change, strategic priorities, conflict specification framework and humanitarian principles. The DDOPD is accountable for the global programme strategy and quality.

## **Work Relations**

The DDOPD will partner and coordinate as a peer with other operational heads of units such as Policy, Research and Legal (PRL), MEAL and Donor Relations units, and with the Deputy Director of Operations for Africa, to promote coherence in programmatic plans and strategies for internal applications and external dissemination. The DDOPD will be the functional manager of the Regional Heads of Programme and Development to ensure technical guidance and support on programme models and designs from inception to implementation and end evaluation is provided at a regional and country-level, and medium to long term impact is generated. The position in coordination and collaboration with other units will develop strategic programmatic partnerships with other international organisations and networks and organise events in global capitals on protection of civilians through AGDA engagement.

## **Duties and Responsabilities**

**Programme Quality Assurance and Standards**

- Sets global Project Cycle Management standards and ensures the dissemination and application of the Project Cycle Management handbook across all existing and new missions. In consultation with PRL and MEAL units, leads the design, development and streamlining of specific programme models, particularly for new missions, based on Geneva Call’s conflict spectrum framework while incorporating humanitarian engagement principles and thematic priorities in line with Geneva Call’s mission and strategy.
- Leads programme quality reviews at a global level, based on the results matrix and evaluation methodologies developed by the MEAL unit, and contributes to the development of Geneva Call’s internal programmes audit framework in consultation with relevant programme focal points at HQ and regional levels.
- Identifies and coordinates learning needs at a global level and supports the Regional Heads of Programme & Development in building the capacities of programming teams to develop long-term sustainable programmes and measurable impact by incorporating data and lessons learnt from the MEAL unit.
- Uses the progress tracker system designed by MEAL across all missions and produces quarterly reports on programme progress and implementation quality against agreed targets. Develops a standardised programme versus cost estimation simulation model based on GC AGDA engagement programme design.
- Provides functional guidance to Regional Heads of Programme and Development in their technical advisory role to country teams, facilitating the coordination and implementation of projects and programme activities in close consultation with country teams, which retain ownership and accountability for programme delivery. Owns global learning approaches and supports Regional Heads of Programme & Development to host regular learning and collaboration opportunities for field and HQ staff to discuss programme/project implementation strategies and good practices.

**Operational Coordination**

- In close coordination with the Deputy Director of Operations for Africa and Director of Operations, aligns programmatic plans and supports Geneva Call’s institutional strategic development through the implementation of the updated Theory of Change and Strategic Plans in line with GC mission.
- Designs thematic programmes with policy and legal input from the PRL unit on protection of civilians in different conflict context situations.
- In coordination with the MEAL unit, ensures the organisational MEAL framework is fully integrated into programmatic designs from inception to end evaluation stages, utilising data from MEAL activities to enhance programme quality. Ensures all programme designs fully incorporate conflict sensitivity, gender equality, diversity and inclusion, and do not harm principles.
- Provides technical guidance in developing high-quality new project proposals for cross-regional programme design and multi-country donors and leads the management of multi-regional grants.
- In coordination with the Humanitarian Diplomacy & Communications unit, guides programme team to produce impact stories based on successful programmatic intervention. Develops global strategic partnerships and relationships with international organisations to support country missions.

**Fundraising, Grant Management and Donor Briefings**

- Coordinates programme input globally for overall fundraising and relationship building efforts, in close collaboration with the Donor Relations unit.
- Provides regular updates and briefings to donors on programmatic updates and impacts and leads global programme briefings and reporting.
- Provides programmatic guidance to the Grants and Reporting Coordinator.

**Representation and Strategic Partnerships**

- Maintains and strengthens Geneva Call’s role as a neutral, impartial and independent humanitarian actor, positioning the organisation and its operations within the geographical areas to gain maximum access to AGDAs, influential stakeholders and affected populations.
- Engages frequently with high‑level stakeholders and international organisations to secure appropriate support for Geneva Call operations.
- In coordination with the Director of Operations, the DDOPD represents Geneva Call in global forums and performs such other duties as may be assigned.

**Management**

- Shared direct line management of the Regional Heads of Programme and Development, with clearly defined and complementary areas of responsibility. The DDOPD exercises line management authority over programmatic strategy, technical quality, programme delivery, and achievement of functional objectives, while the Deputy Director of Operations exercises line management authority over regional operational management, coordination, and alignment with regional priorities.
- Direct line management of the Programme and Reporting Coordinator at headquarters.

## **Requirements**

**Education (Essential)**

- Master’s degree in political or social sciences, Humanitarian Affairs, International Relations, International Humanitarian Law, Human Rights Law or a related field.

**Experience (Essential)**

- 14+ years of highly relevant experience, with a minimum of 8 years of experience in the field and 3 years of experience at headquarters.
- A minimum of 3 years of experience leading and managing senior managers, included within the overall professional experience requirement.
- Demonstrated experience in implementing programme cycle management tools and leading programme development and quality assurance, as well as experience in humanitarian settings and/or crisis and post-crisis settings.
- Progressively responsible experience in liaising with governmental and diplomatic authorities and international institutions. Demonstrated experience in engaging with armed actors and facilitating constructive dialogue on humanitarian concerns, particularly to promote respect for international humanitarian law and the protection of civilians.
- Advanced understanding of the complex needs of humanitarian operations. Proven experience in resource mobilisation.

**Job related Competencies (Essential)**

- Sound knowledge of financial and business administration and of the principles and practices of management.
- Outstanding interpersonal communication skills and ability to work in a team and across departments to ensure an inclusive, respectful and safe working environment.
- Sound knowledge of the project cycle, as well as of monitoring and evaluation.
- Strong analytical thinking, planning and organising skills, with attention to detail, and structured, strong planning and organisation skills.
- Strategic thinking combined with strong execution skills.

**Organisational Competencies**

- Strong leadership and people management skills.
- Ability to build and maintain trusting and collaborative relationships.
- Ability to promote teamwork and effective collaboration across departments.
- Commitment to fostering an inclusive, respectful and safe working environment.
- Ability to demonstrate accountability, sound judgement and alignment with Geneva Call’s organisational values.

**Language (Essential)**

- Fluency in English and French both spoken and written.

**Language (Desirable)**

- Knowledge of Spanish, Arabic, or any other language relevant to Geneva Call’s operations is an advantage.

## **Why join Geneva Call?**

Geneva Call brings together people of diverse nationalities, cultures, languages and perspectives, fostering an inclusive working environment for all staff.

This role offers the opportunity to advance a meaningful humanitarian mission by strengthening the protection of civilians in armed conflict. The role combines strategic leadership, programme quality and innovation to develop sustainable, impactful programmes, strengthen partnerships and foster collaboration across missions, ultimately contributing to lasting change for communities affected by armed conflict.

jobs.title: Operations Manager, MEAL & Technology
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
jobs.body:
**Background:**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises and helps people to survive, recover, and gain control of their future.

We aim to make our programs a model for the highest global standards and to cultivate power and lasting change not just for our clients but for all people affected by humanitarian crises. To achieve that vision, the IRC’s Technical Excellence (TE) group, located within the Crisis Response, Recovery and Development (CRRD) Department, provides technical assistance to IRC’s country program staff and shares what we learn to influence policy and practice.

**Location:** This position is open to national candidates or candidates who have residency in either the U.S or UK.

**Internal Candidates:** Internal.staff from any other country that has an IRC Office, are welcome to apply and will be hosted in that country as a national staff if selected for the position.

**Languages:** Fluency in written & spoken English required. Fluency in Spanish, French, or Arabic a plus.

**Monitoring, Evaluation, Technology, Accountability, and Learning at the IRC**

The METAL Unit is responsible for supporting CRRD to have a culture of strong data and evidence use through stewardship of the Data & Performance Ecosystem, and for coordinating successful piloting and uptake of innovative technology solutions. The METAL Unit provides specialized support across four pillars to strengthen program effectiveness, improve decision-making, and enhance organizational learning:

- Global MEAL Practice: Global MEAL Practice works with the Technical Units to set and maintain the highest standards for measurement, analysis, and data use, promoting a culture of continuous improvement and learning.
- Technology for Programs: The T4Ppillar drives the identification and testing of cutting-edge technology for IRC’s programming areas, by focusing on advancing digital solutions that enhance program reach and impact. Leads T4P innovation and scaling for CRRD and coordinates between CRRD/IT/Signpost/Airbel.
- Data Systems and Analytics: The Data Systems and Analytics pillar ensures the widespread iteration, adoption, and sustainability of data systems, leading data governance for CRRD and coordinating between IT/others at an org level.
- Regional METAL Support: The Regional METAL Support team provides direct technical assistance to IRC Programs, ensuring programs meet MEAL maturity benchmarks and optimize data utilization. They also provide strategic support implementing and generating learning from MEAL systems and activities, providing regional leadership with data insights and informing global practice.

**Job Overview**

The Operations Manager, METAL provides dedicated administrative, knowledge management, and coordination support to METAL Unit leadership and the wider team. This role keeps the Unit organized to support uptake of key initiatives – maintaining shared knowledge products and resources, supporting meeting and event logistics, and supporting communications across all four pillars. The ideal candidate is highly organized, detail-oriented, and motivated by driving organizational change through strong communications and effective team operations.

**Major Responsibilities**

*Administrative and team support*

- Provide day-to-day administrative support to METAL pillar leads and the wider Unit, including invoice management.
- Plan and organize the Unit's team retreat, including venue research and booking, agenda coordination with pillar leads, travel logistics, budget tracking, and on-site/virtual materials
- Coordinate unit-wide meetings (e.g. all-staff calls, SMT meetings, pillar check-ins): scheduling, agenda preparation, notetaking, and follow-up on action items
- Support logistical planning of METAL-related events, workshops, and trainings
- Support onboarding logistics for new METAL Unit hires, including scheduling introductory meetings with pillar leads and colleagues, ensuring new hires have information and system access (i.e. Integra, Claude, WorkDay, etc.), and training staff on required systems

*Knowledge management*

- Collect, organize, and maintain knowledge products developed across the four METAL pillars (standards, guidance, templates, tools) in a well-organized, easy-to-navigate central repository
- Manage and maintain the Unit's Box folder structure, ensuring consistent naming conventions, version control, and appropriate access for all team members
- Maintain and update METAL's RescueNet pages and resource libraries on an ongoing basis, ensuring content stays current and easy to find in service to TechEx and CRRD at large
- Act as the Unit's knowledge management focal point, liaising with IT and other platform owners on folder structure, taxonomy, and content organization
- Maintain shared trackers and issue logs used by the Unit, ensuring they remain current and accessible to relevant stakeholders
- Maintain the organizational chart and keep a staff roster list (with TTA tracking) and sharing information with TechEx FinOps team

*Communications support*

- Support internal communications for the Unit: update shared trackers, standard presentations, and resource pages with current information
- Support department-wide communications for the Unit: gathering inputs for the CRRD newsletter,
- Maintain METAL distribution email list

*Other*

- Provide additional administrative and coordination support to METAL Unit leadership as needed
- Support in data inputs, data clean up, or data analyses as per request of TechEx
- Other duties as requested

**Key Working Relationships**

Position Reports to: Senior Director, METAL

This position works closely with the leads and teams of all four METAL pillars (MEAL Global Practice, Regional METAL Support, Technology for Programs, and CRRD Data & Analytics), as well as IT and other platform administrators, as needed.

**Job Requirements**

*Essential*

- Bachelor's degree, or equivalent combination of education and experience (e.g. in library science, information/knowledge management, or business administration)
- Minimum 2–4 years of experience in an administrative, knowledge management, or team coordination role; experience in a nonprofit or international development context a plus
- Experience planning and coordinating meetings, workshops, or team events, including logistics, scheduling, and materials preparation
- Proficiency with Microsoft 365 tools (SharePoint, Teams, Outlook, Excel) and file management/storage platforms (e.g. Box)
- Exceptionally well-organized, with strong attention to detail and a proven track record of managing multiple priorities and deadlines
- Strong written and verbal communication skills; able to produce clear, user-friendly documentation and reference materials
- Strong interpersonal skills, with a collegial, service-oriented approach to supporting colleagues and leadership across a distributed team
- Excellent spoken and written English

*Desirable*

- Experience with SharePoint site administration, document taxonomy, or metadata management
- Working knowledge of Arabic, French, and/or Spanish
- Experience supporting humanitarian or international development program teams

***This is a remote position open to internal candidates based in countries where IRC operates who have the right to work in their location. Successful candidates will be hired on a local employment contract and according to local salary scale.***

***This role is open to candidates located and with the right to work in United Kingdom and United States of America.***

**Compensation:** (UK Pay Rate: £41,767 - 49,599/yr; US Pay Rate: $73,000 - $85,000/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

jobs.title: Medical coordinator (F/M) - Sudan
jobs.body:
For more than 40 years, Médecins du Monde (MdM), a campaigning medical organisation committed to international solidarity, has been caring for the most vulnerable populations here and abroad. It has continued to bear witness to obstacles that exist in accessing healthcare and has secured sustainable improvements in health-for-all policies.

Those working for this independent organisation do not solely dispense care and treatment but condemn violations of human dignity and rights and fight to improve matters for populations living in precarious situations.

MdM France currently works in 30 countries across all continents to facilitate access to healthcare through 6 political battles:

- Sexual and Reproductive Health Rights
- Migration, Exile, Human Rights and Health
- Harm Reduction
- Environment and Health
- Humanitarian Space
- Healthcare systems and rights

**MdM in Sudan**

MdM maintained a presence in Jebel Marra until 2011. Mid-December 2025, MdM decided to launch an exploratory mission in West Darfur and allocated core funds to provide medicines, recruit an exploratory team composed of a head of mission, a medical coordinator and a logistics coordinator, and start activities in Darfur.

Since end of April 2026, MdM is managing a clinic in the Dar Omo camp in Feina (South Darfur) hosting approximately 25.000 displaced persons.

Since August 2026, 2 mobile clinics are operating around Feina and mid-September 2026, MdM has launched a response to a cholera outbreak in North Darfur.

MdM France has decided to register itself and consolidate its presence in East Sudan to have a balanced presence in all Sudan and be able to answer humanitarian needs in this part of the country.

**About the role**

You are in charge of designing, planning, implementing, adapting and monitoring health activities. You directly manage the medical team.

**What you’ll do**

- Participate in the definition of the country strategy led by the general coordinator and drive the medical and technical aspects in the development of this strategy
- Design, plan, implement, adapt and monitor the programme’s health activities
- Ensure the quality and relevance of health activities, supervise the collection and analysis of medical data
- Recruit, manage, train, and motivate the medical team
- Ensure the management of pharmaceutical products
- Carry out health needs assessments and evaluations of medical partners
- Monitor, analyse and share health and epidemiological data and assess needs and contribute to medical response planning and emergency preparedness for epidemics and mass displacement
- Cooperate with the administration team regarding budgeting and supervise the medical purchase process
- Represent MdM with authorities, partners and other NGOs on health issues
- Participate in the writing of proposals and reports

**Who you’ll work with**

You work under the supervision of the general coordinator of the mission (based in El Geneina) and in collaboration with the health advisor, the MHPSS advisor and the pharmacy officer based at HQ. You manage directly the activity manager and the pharmacy officer. In Feina, the medical team is composed of a medical team supervisor and a midwife supervisor.

**You are the right match if you:**

- Have a medical degree (medical doctor, nurse, midwife)
- Have a minimum 4 years of experience in the humanitarian sector in a similar position
- Have experience in emergency responses, outbreak management, nutrition, health assessments and medical programme start-up
- Demonstrate experience working in complex, politically sensitive or rapidly evolving environments
- Are able to work in high security context
- Have solid background in team leadership, capacity building and technical supervision
- Have strong communication, negotiation and diplomacy skills
- Have strong ability to work collaboratively with diverse teams and multicultural stakeholders
- Have excellent organisational and time-management skills
- Have mapping skills with Google Earth or ArcGIS
- Have strong proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint)
- Are fluent in English (spoken and written); knowledge of Arabic is an asset

**This role may not suit you if you:**

- Are not aligned with MdM’s values
- Don't have experience in volatile security environments

**Recruitment process**

If shortlisted, you will first meet with our HR team. Technical and managerial interviews, which may include practical case studies, will follow.

Please note: as part of our anti–money laundering and counter-terrorism policy, international background checks may be conducted. Data is processed confidentially and securely. More info: [https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/](https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/)  
All successful candidates must provide a criminal record extract (B3).

**Ready to apply?**

We only need your CV and a cover letter.  
If this role sounds like the right fit for you, apply now – we’d love to hear from you!

**Employment conditions**

Contract & status:

- Gross monthly salary: 3 663 €
- Fixed-term contract starting as soon as possible and for 6 months
- Single posting

Work environment:

- Position based in El Geneina , West Darfur, with regular field visits

Benefits:
