jobs.title: MERL Assistant
jobs.body:
**Aperçu de l'organisation**

Tostan is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization headquartered in Dakar, Senegal, and currently operating in five West African countries. Strategically, the organization is committed to further developing its core competency—education-based empowerment—and to documenting and scaling up the sustainable impact it creates across a range of issues. Tostan’s flagship model, the three-year Community Capacity-Building Program (CCBP), has already reached thousands of communities in West and East Africa since 1991. Results in the areas of governance, education, health, economic empowerment, and the environment are currently being tracked, and Tostan is particularly proud to have played a significant role in the large-scale empowerment of women and girls and in the community’s abandonment of harmful practices such as female genital mutilation and child marriage. As part of its plan d'engagement stratégique 2023-2030, Tostan is focusing on strategic scaling. The organization is developing new implementation strategies to support community leadership by driving systemic change on a larger scale at the regional level. It is also creating new models to share and replicate its programs with other development partners and is expanding its capacity to share Tostan’s comprehensive approach to support and influence a range of local and global audiences. For more information, please visit: [www.tostan.org](http://www.tostan.org)

**Department overview**

The Monitoring, Evaluation, Research, and Learning (MERL) team is an integral part of Tostan’s Program Department. Its mission is to coordinate and support the program monitoring and evaluation system in the countries where Tostan operates, as well as research and learning. Through this team, Tostan continuously monitors performance in partner communities and conducts internal evaluations, including baseline studies, midterm evaluations, and final evaluations.

**Roles and responsabilities**

Under the direct technical supervision of the MERL Focal Person and the TI MERL team, and the administrative supervision of the National Coordinator, the MERL Assistant will be responsible for supporting the MERL Country Responsible in ensuring the strict implementation of all monitoring and evaluation activities within the national coordination office.

***She/He will have as mission to :***

➔ Support the MERL Focal Person in supporting and coordinating the monitoring and evaluation strategies and activities implemented by SERA at the national coordination level

➔ Support the ERL Focal Person in overseeing the monitoring forms

➔ Support the ERL Focal Person in ensuring that data is collected;

➔ To support the ERL Focal Person in ensuring that the collected data is transmitted to the national and/or international MERL office;

➔ To support the MERL Focal Person in conducting monitoring missions in collaboration with the national coordinator to assess the progress of activities in the field;

➔ To support the MERL Focal Person in training CMCs on aspects related to Monitoring and Evaluation.

**As MERL team member:**

***Responsibility 1: support the MERL Focal Person in ensuring strict implementation of the monitoring system established by MERL***

➔ Understand the monitoring and evaluation system that has been implemented.

➔ Share the components of the system with colleagues in the coordination team (coordinator, supervisors, and other relevant stakeholders).

➔ Ensure that any challenges encountered in implementing the system are documented and shared with management.

***Responsabilité 2: Support the MERL Focal Person in building the capacity of field staff (supervisors and facilitators) in monitoring and evaluation, data collection methodology, and the completion of data collection forms***

➔ Train the coordination staff—particularly the coordinator and supervisors—on monitoring and evaluation

➔ Train supervisors on how to fill out data collection forms

***Responsabilité 3: Support the MERL Focal Person to ensure that monitoring data is collected on time according to the agreed-upon schedule***

➔ Check whether the data collection forms are up to date

➔ Ensure that each supervisor collects data in their assigned area

➔ Ensure the completeness and quality of the collected data

➔ Ensure that the collected data is submitted to MERL

***Responsabilité 4: Support the MERL Focal Person in leading the planning and collection of qualitative and quantitative data in the field during studies and evaluations***

➔ Participate in the planning of studies and evaluations

➔ Participate and play an active role in training on methodology and tools for data collection during studies and evaluations

➔ Participate in the supervision of data collection

➔ Ensure the quality and completeness of data for each study and evaluation

**Key relation:**

***Supervisor (N+1) :*** MERL Focal Person

**Direct relationships (direct functional relationships):** supervisors

**Other colleagues:** coordination staff

**Location :** Bassé, The Gambia

**Key Qualifications Required:**

***Education :***

➔ Have at least 2 years of experience in the field of monitoring and evaluation of development projects

➔ Hold a bachelor’s degree or equivalent in community/local development or in the planning, design, and management of development projects, or in project monitoring and evaluation.

***Language Skills:***

➔ Be able to speak, read, and write in English;

➔ Have a good knowledge of at least one national language spoken in the area of assignment

***Knowledge and experience :***

The MERL Assistant must have proven skills and abilities in the following areas:

➔ The ability to coordinate several different projects simultaneously

➔ Knowledge and qualifications in community development

➔ Knowledge and proven experience in the design, implementation, and monitoring and evaluation of development projects

➔ Proficiency in computer skills, particularly in using common software programs (Word, Excel, PowerPoint). Proficiency in other software such as Airtable, Tableau, etc., would be an asset.

➔ Be able to use tablets for electronic data collection.

➔ Have experience working in rural areas with local communities while respecting human dignity, and be able to work well under pressure.

***Characteristics***

➔ Be open-minded and cooperative

➔ Be able to work under pressure and in a complex, multicultural environment

➔ Have excellent time-management skills, as well as the ability to handle multiple tasks simultaneously and prioritize

➔ Have a driver's license

**Type of contract :** local contract

jobs.title: Case Manager Bangladesh
jobs.body:
**Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) is an international, independent medical humanitarian organization. As a non-profit, self-governed movement of over 63,000 dedicated professionals, we provide life-saving medical assistance to people affected by armed conflict, natural disasters, disease outbreaks, and exclusion from healthcare.**

**Our work is guided by medical ethics and the principles of impartiality, independence, and neutrality. We act based on need, and when we witness injustice, we speak out. Our commitment to professionalism and humanity can mean the difference between life and death.**

**People are our priority. At Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF)/ Artsen zonder Grenzen, we are committed to an inclusive culture that encourages and supports the diverse voices of our employees. We encourage diverse applicants including individuals of all gender identities, ages, sexual orientations, nationalities, ethnic background, religions, beliefs, social and marital status, people with different abilities and all other diversity characteristics and how they intersect together.**

With immediate effect, for our Country Programme in Bangladesh we are looking for:

## **Case Manager Bangladesh**

*(12 month assignment based in Bangladesh. This role is not based in Amsterdam)*

**Objectives of the position**

Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) OCA is seeking an experienced Safeguarding and Code of Conduct (CoC) Case Manager for the Kutupalong Project in Bangladesh. The role will support safeguarding initiatives and case management related to staff, patients, and communities in a context serving more than 1.1 million Rohingya refugees.

Reporting directly to the Project Coordinator and functionally to the Hospital Director in Bangladesh with technical support from the Safeguarding Case Management Advisor, the Case Manager will lead administrative investigations into misconduct, Coc violations, and safeguarding concerns, including complex and high-risk cases. The post holder will receive, triage, and manage subsequent complaint and investigation processes, ensure confidential case management and documentation, and serve as the primary focal point for patient and community safeguarding concerns in Kutupalong Hospital and other outreach facilities.

This position plays a key role in strengthening accountability, protecting vulnerable populations, and upholding MSF's safeguarding standards and ethical principles.

**Main responsibilities**

- Ensure proper handling of all misconduct complaints, including safe and confidential reception, timely acknowledgment, triage, and immediate reporting of high-risk allegations to the Safeguarding Unit and compliance with Intersectional Platform on Behaviour Standards for Case Management.
- Provide technical advice and support to all actors involved in case management and ensure risk-mitigation and referral measures for complainants. - subjects of complaints and witnesses, including protection, medical, psychosocial and legal referrals when appropriate.
- Conduct and lead case triage, risk assessments, and investigations, including evidence gathering, interviews, analysis, and recommendations.
- Manage investigation documentation, including archiving, minute-taking, coordination of meetings/interviews, and preparation of final reports.
- Build capacity of country programme teams by training and supporting staff involved in complaint handling and misconduct investigations.
- Propose improvements to protocols and guidelines on case management based on country programme realities.
- Ensure quality, confidentiality, and data protection in case management processes, including managing complaint databases and reporting statistics.
- Coordinate internal and external collaboration, maintain communication with the Safeguarding Unit, engage in relevant forums, and coordinate external investigation experts where necessary.

**Candidate Profile**

- BSc in law, social or organizational sciences, gender studies, social work, behavioural sciences, human rights, psychology, nursing or related field that deals with interpersonal behaviour and administrative fact-findings.
- Minimum 2 years of experience in identifying and addressing safeguarding concerns in a humanitarian setting, preferably a hospital setting with MSF or similar INGO. The 2 years of experience must include addressing concerns hands-on such as directly managing complaints, managing projects and staff, or treating patients.
- Experience working in low-resource contexts in countries of operation in the humanitarian, health, or development sector is highly desired.
- Strong analytical and advisory skills, with the ability to handle complex, sensitive, and high-risk cases independently.
- Excellent verbal communication skills, including the ability to deliver difficult information sensitively and appropriately.
- Excellent written communication skills, including the ability to draft investigation reports and present cases to senior management succinctly.
- Excellent intercultural communication skills, including the ability to work with qualified translators.
- Demonstrated commitment to confidentiality, survivor-centred practice, and fair process.
- Fluency in English, both speaking and writing, is mandatory. Bangla or Rohingya desirable.
- Ability to develop case strategies, conduct investigative interviews and deliver investigation reports of high quality and within prescribed deadlines.
- Certification as investigator highly desirable (CHS Tier 3, CFE/ CFF/ CPA/CCEP or equivalent)

**What we offer**

- Annual gross salary range: 33,500€ - 36,850€ depending on prior relevant experience. This is a level 15 of the new Program Function Grid.
- 25 annual holidays.
- Private Health Insurance for the duration of the assignment + 3 months post-assignment.
- Accommodation & utilities.
- Travel costs are covered, except for personal holidays.
- An international and multicultural work environment

jobs.title: Chief of Branch, Communications, D1
source: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
jobs.body:
**Org. Setting and Reporting**

This position is located in the Financing and Outreach Division (FOD) of the Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA). OCHA's mission is to mobilize and coordinate effective and principled humanitarian action in partnership with national and international actors in order to alleviate human suffering in disasters and emergencies; advocate the rights of people in need; promote preparedness and prevention and facilitate sustainable solutions. The Financing and Outreach Division (FOD) leads in mobilizing and allocating resources for a coordinated and principled humanitarian response, while driving innovative humanitarian financing approaches and elevating the visibility and communication of OCHA’s mission and mandate. Within FOD, The Chief of Service, Communications is responsible for developing, implementing and evaluating communications strategies and services aligned with organizational objectives and priorities. The role includes providing vision, direction, support and implementation of the main functions of communications.. This position-specific job opening is advertised for the position of Chief of Communications in New York at UNHQ. The incumbent reports directly to the Director of the Financing and Outreach Division (FOD).

**Responsibilities**

Within delegated authority, the Chief of Communications will be responsible for the following duties: • Lead and strategically guide the activities of the communication sections and units to ensure strategic alignment and effective delivery of the organization’s objectives. • Provide the vision and leadership to develop and implement the communications strategy to strengthen understanding of organizational objectives, activities and impact, drive engagement, and build support with target audiences. • Guide and manage different communications workstreams bringing them together under shared objectives, such as digital communications, media relations, outreach, campaigns, and partnerships. Convene and coordinate with other UN entities and partners, as appropriate. • Chair and lead the Inter-Agency Standing Committee communications group, alongside an IASC member on a rotating basis. • Work to review OCHA's global communications workforce and identify how best to make it fit for purpose. • Advise senior management on strategic communications, crisis communications and reputational risk. • Oversee and lead the implementation of strategic communications policy, guidance and training for staff. • Advise and oversee internal communications, as appropriate, including messaging and content creation, and in crisis situations. • Lead and coordinate the creation of content, such as narratives and key messages, including on complex, sensitive, and crisis-driven issues. • Oversee the management and coordination of communications teams in the entity, including hiring, budgeting, reporting, recruitment, and training, in compliance with UN rules and regulations. • Provide guidance to team members to promote professional development and a positive team culture. • Oversee monitoring and analysis of communications strategies, approaches, and activities to assess performance and impact. • Maintain confidentiality and integrity in information management, and handle sensitive information with discretion, ensuring compliance with the UN data privacy, policies, security requirements, and standards. • Provide vision, targets and strategy for developing and delivering impactful offline and online campaigns through appropriate channels. • Lead collaboration with internal and external stakeholders to develop and deliver joint outreach and advocacy activities and campaigns to target key audiences and advance UN priorities. • Lead the development of engagement strategies to build and enhance the Organization's brand utilizing collaborations, partnerships and existing and emerging channels and content, as appropriate. • Oversee and guide the monitoring of media and developing events to identify emerging crises and reputational risks and provide early response warning and strategic advice to senior management. • Lead and oversee the Organization's proactive interaction with local, regional and international media and partners, promote outreach activities, and implement crisis communication responses and interactions with the media. • Oversee policy development and implementation to strengthen information integrity, and the coordination of efforts to address related threats at the regional and country levels, ensuring alignment with UN global priorities • Oversee efforts to strengthen information integrity, including research, risk and response work, coalition building and policy development. • Promote organizational understanding and adoption of technology, data, and innovation initiatives by leading communications related to digital transformation, enterprise platforms, cybersecurity, information governance, and business intelligence, ensuring alignment with organizational standards, policies, and strategic priorities.

**Competencies**

Professionalism: Knowledge of the substantive field of work in general and of specific areas being supervised. Skills to communicate complex and technical matters to diverse audiences. Exhibits strategic thinking and critical thinking skills. Knowledge of risks to information integrity - misinformation, disinformation, hate speech, and threats in fragile, post conflict, and crisis environments. Ability to build and maintain partnerships. Shows pride in work and in achievements; demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter; is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines and achieving results; is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns; shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges; remains calm in stressful situations. Client Orientation: Considers all those to whom services are provided to be “clients” and seeks to see things from clients’ point of view; Establishes and maintains productive partnerships with clients by gaining their trust and respect; Identifies clients’ needs and matches them to appropriate solutions; Monitors ongoing developments inside and outside the clients’ environment to keep; informed and anticipate problems; Keeps clients informed of progress or setbacks in projects; Meets timeline for delivery of products or services to client. Creativity: Actively seeks to improve programmes or services; Offers new and different options to solve problems or meet client needs;Promotes and persuades others to consider new ideas;Takes calculated risks on new and unusual ideas; thinks "outside the box"; Takes an interest in new ideas and new ways of doing things; Is not bound by current thinking or traditional approaches. Managerial Competencies: Leadership: Serves as a role model that other people want to follow; Empowers others to translate vision into results; Is proactive in developing strategies to accomplish objectives; Establishes and maintains relationships with a broad range of people to understand needs and gain support; Anticipates and resolves conflicts by pursuing mutually agreeable solutions; Drives for change and improvement; does not accept the status quo; Shows the courage to take unpopular stands; Provides leadership and takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas. Demonstrates knowledge of strategies and commitment to the goal of gender balance in staffing. Managing Performance: Delegates the appropriate responsibility, accountability and decision-making authority; Makes sure that roles, responsibilities and reporting lines are clear to each staff member; Accurately judges the amount of time and resources needed to accomplish a task and matches task to skills; Monitors progress against milestones and deadlines;Regularly discusses performance and provides feedback and coaching to staff; Encourages risk-taking and supports creativity and initiative; Actively supports the development and career aspirations of staff; Appraises performance fairly.

**Education**

Advanced university degree (Master’s degree or equivalent) in communications, journalism, international relations, digital communications or related field. A first-level university degree in combination with two additional years of qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree.

**Job - Specific Qualification**

Not available.

**Work Experience**

A minimum of fifteen (15) years of progressively responsible experience in communications, international relations, or other relevant areas is required. Knowledge of current and emerging digital media platforms, their principles and technologies is required. Knowledge of strategic communications principles and practices is required. Skills to lead teams, guide and mentor staff, and oversee their work to ensure successful completion of projects is required. A minimum of three (3) years of experience in crisis communication in a humanitarian, development or peacekeeping setting is desirable. Ability to identify trends and provide insights, to develop and implement communications strategies and to draft and tailor clear messages for diverse audiences is desirable. Skills to communicate complex and technical matters to diverse audiences is desirable.

**Languages**

English and French are the working languages of the United Nations Secretariat. For this job opening, English is required. Either French **or** Arabic is desirable. The table below shows the minimum required level for each skill in these languages, according to the UN Language Framework (please consult [https://languages.un.org](https://languages.un.org/) for details).

## **Required Languages**

**Special Notice**

This position is funded for a finite period of one year. Extension of the appointment is subject to extension of the mandate and the availability of the funds. Staff members are subject to the authority of the Secretary-general and to assignment by him or her. In this context, all staff are expected to move periodically to new functions in their careers by established rules and procedures. Staff members of the United Nations Secretariat must fulfill the lateral or geographical move requirements to be eligible to apply for this vacancy. Staff members are requested to indicate all qualifying lateral or geographical moves in their Candidate Profile (CP) and motivation statement. At the United Nations, the paramount consideration in the recruitment and employment of staff is the necessity of securing the highest standards of efficiency, competence and integrity, with due regard to geographic diversity. All employment decisions are made on the basis of qualifications and organizational needs. The United Nations is committed to creating a diverse and inclusive environment of mutual respect. The United Nations recruits and employs staff regardless of gender identity, sexual orientation, race, religious, cultural and ethnic backgrounds or disabilities. The United Nations Secretariat is committed to achieving a 50/50 gender balance in its staff. Female candidates are strongly encouraged to apply for this position. An impeccable record of integrity and professional ethical standards is essential.

**United Nations Considerations**

According to article 101, paragraph 3, of the Charter of the United Nations, the paramount consideration in the employment of the staff is the necessity of securing the highest standards of efficiency, competence, and integrity. Candidates will not be considered for employment with the United Nations if they have committed violations of international human rights law, violations of international humanitarian law, sexual exploitation, sexual abuse, or sexual harassment, or if there are reasonable grounds to believe that they have been involved in the commission of any of these acts. The term “sexual exploitation” means any actual or attempted abuse of a position of vulnerability, differential power, or trust, for sexual purposes, including, but not limited to, profiting monetarily, socially or politically from the sexual exploitation of another. The term “sexual abuse” means the actual or threatened physical intrusion of a sexual nature, whether by force or under unequal or coercive conditions. The term “sexual harassment” means any unwelcome conduct of a sexual nature that might reasonably be expected or be perceived to cause offence or humiliation, when such conduct interferes with work, is made a condition of employment or creates an intimidating, hostile or offensive work environment, and when the gravity of the conduct warrants the termination of the perpetrator’s working relationship. By accepting a letter of appointment, staff members are subject to the authority of the Secretary-General, who may assign them to any of the activities or offices of the United Nations in accordance with staff regulation 1.2 (c). Further, staff members in the Professional and higher category up to and including the D-2 level and the Field Service category are normally required to move periodically to discharge functions in different duty stations under conditions established in ST/AI/2023/3 on Mobility, as may be amended or revised. This condition of service applies to all position specific job openings and does not apply to temporary positions. Applicants are urged to carefully follow all instructions available in the online recruitment platform, inspira, and to refer to the Applicant Guide by clicking on “Manuals” in the “Help” tile of the inspira account-holder homepage. (c) of ST/AI/2025/3 for a fixed term appointment limited to the entity are subject to an initial probationary period of one year under a fixed-term appointment. Job openings advertised on the Careers Portal will be removed at 11:59 p.m. (New York time) on the deadline date.

jobs.title: Finance Reporting Associate
source: Medecins du Monde - Turkey / Dunya Doktorlari Dernegi
jobs.body:
**Dünya Doktorları Derneği**

**Medecins du Monde Turkey (MDM-T) /** **Dünya Doktorları Dernegi (DDD)** is a Turkish based humanitarian non-governmental organisation that facilitates access to healthcare for populations affected by armed conflict, violence, natural disasters, disease, famine, poverty and exclusion.

Our organization collaborates with partners and key stakeholders to implement projects that facilitate access to primary and secondary-level healthcare services to respond to the medical needs of displaced population.

DDD is the 16th member of the Doctors of the World International Network that is committed to meeting the health needs of vulnerable people globally.

Please visit [www.dunyadoktorlari.org.tr](http://www.dunyadoktorlari.org.tr) to learn more.

**Hierarchical & Functional links**

Based in Istanbul, the Finance Reporting Associate is directly responsible to the Finance Manager.

**Organisational Positioning**

The Financial Reporting Associate operates within the Head Office Financial Performance Unit, focusing on financial consolidation, data quality and reporting.

The position supports organisation-wide financial oversight and does not assume direct responsibility for the day-to-day financial management of Country Operations, which remains under Country Finance teams.

**Position Purpose**

The Financial Reporting Associate supports the consolidation, reliability and reporting of financial information across DDD's Head Office and Country Operations.

The position contributes to the development of a consistent, accurate and timely financial reporting system, supporting organisational financial oversight, performance monitoring and management decision-making.

**Status**:Fixed-term contract

**Expected Starting Date:** ASAP

**EXPECTED PROFILE**

**Knowledge & Qualification**

• University degree in Economics, Finance, Business Administration or a related field.

**Experience**

· At least 2 years of relevant professional experience in management accounting, financial controlling, budget monitoring or management reporting.

· Good understanding of cost accounting, analytical accounting, budget management, financial performance analysis and reporting processes.

· Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including data analysis, reporting and consolidation functions.

· Experience with accounting or ERP software; familiarity with financial reporting or business intelligence tools is an advantage.

· Professional working proficiency in English and Turkish.

· Experience in the private sector is particularly welcome, including manufacturing, retail, logistics, construction, healthcare services or other industries involving cost control, budget monitoring and management reporting. Previous experience in the NGO sector is not required.

**Languages**

· Fluent Turkish (written and spoken); working level English; Arabic is an advantage;

**IT & Equipment**

· Good proficiency with Microsoft package

**Skills and Qualities required:**

· Strong analytical skills and attention to detail.

· Ability to organise, verify and interpret financial information.

· Structured and methodical approach to data management and reporting.

· Ability to meet deadlines and manage multiple reporting requirements.

· Good communication and coordination skills.

· Commitment to accuracy, confidentiality and professional integrity.

**RESPONSIBILITIES**

**A. Financial Consolidation & Reporting**

· Collect, organise and consolidate financial data from Head Office and Country Operations.

· Prepare periodic financial reports, consolidated statements and financial summaries for internal management.

· Support the production of financial dashboards, analytical tables and management reporting tools.

· Ensure consistency between accounting records, financial reports and budget monitoring data.

**B. Financial Data Quality & Analysis**

· Review financial datasets for completeness, accuracy and consistency.

· Identify discrepancies, missing information and reporting inconsistencies, and coordinate necessary corrections.

· Maintain structured financial databases, reporting templates and consolidation tools.

· Support financial analysis, including expenditure trends, budget execution and financial performance indicators.

**C. Financial Reporting Systems & Coordination**

· Contribute to the development and improvement of financial reporting procedures, standards and tools.

· Liaise with Country Finance teams to ensure timely submission and consistency of financial information.

· Coordinate with General Accounting to reconcile reporting data with accounting records.

· Support the preparation of financial information required for audits, institutional reporting and management reviews.

**D. Organisational Transition Support**

· Contribute to the progressive development of DDD's Head Office financial reporting and consolidation capacities.

· Support the standardisation of financial information and reporting practices across the organisation.

Undertake temporary operational reporting tasks during the organisational transition, as required.

**Compliance & Ethics**  
Promote and encourage a culture of compliance and ethics throughout Dünya Doktorları Derneği. As applicable to the position, maintains a clear understanding of Dünya Doktorları Derneği and donor compliance and ethics standards and adheres to those standards. Conducts work with the highest level of integrity. Communicates these values to staff and to partners and requires them to adhere to these values.

**Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse**  
Actively promote PSEA (Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse) standards within Dünya Doktorları Derneği and amongst beneficiaries served by Dünya Doktorları Derneği.

**NB:** Considering the purpose and values of the organisation, DDD requests to its employee complete flexibility in term of duties and commitment, as their job description and job title can be adjusted throughout the year according to needs and priorities.

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis.Please be advised that female candidates are highly encouraged.

*Dünya Doktorları Derneği is an equal opportunity employer whereby we ensure all hiring and employment decisions, and operates all programs, services, and functions without the practices that discriminate against any person employed or seeking employment based on race, colour, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national or ethnic origin, age, marital status, disability, genetic information or any other status or characteristic protected under applicable law.*

**How to Apply:**

Please apply with your **CV and motivation letter in ENGLISH** through our website

**Closure Date:** 06.11.2026

Due to the urgency to fill this post, DDD reserves the right to review the CVs on a rolling basis and selected candidates may be interviewed prior to the closing dates listed, therefore early applications are encouraged.  
DDD is not in a position to respond to every applicant individually due to the anticipated high number of applications.  
Please note that only short-listed candidates will be contacted for the first interview.

Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation.

**General Information**  
DDD retains the discretion to re-advertise the vacancy, to cancel the recruitment, to offer a contract with a modified job description or for a different duration, or to offer a contract at a lower grade.

jobs.title: Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL) Officer – ARCH
jobs.body:
*Help shape how ARCH measures progress, learns, and grows. Join a new cultural cooperation program connecting Denmark and Africa, and turn evidence into stronger programs and partnerships with lasting impact.*

**NOTE:** This position is based in Nairobi, Kenya, and requires working from the Nairobi office two to three days per week. Applicants must be based in Nairobi and have the right to work in Kenya. Professional working proficiency in French is strongly desired.

## **About ARCH and the role**

ActionAid Denmark manages ARCH – the Fund for African-Danish Relations through Exchange of Culture and Arts. Funded by the Danish Ministry of Foreign Affairs, this new program supports equitable cultural partnerships between Denmark and up to fourteen African countries through grants, exchange, and shared learning.

As ARCH’s MEL Officer, you will be based in Nairobi and join a Secretariat team working across Denmark and several African countries. You will report to the Head of Secretariat in Denmark.

You will join as ARCH moves from inception into implementation. Building on the MEL framework established during the inception phase, you will operationalise and manage practical systems for monitoring, evaluation and learning, ensuring that results and lessons are captured, understood and used to improve the programme. A key part of the role is making MEL useful and accessible for grantees, including small cultural organisations and collectives with limited MEL experience, so they can plan, track and report on results with confidence.

## **Your main responsibilities**

### **Monitoring, evaluation and results management**

- Operationalise, maintain and continuously improve ARCH’s MEL framework, monitoring tools, reporting templates and data collection systems, building on the Inception Report.
- Conduct ARCH’s media-coverage baseline study using the inception-phase methodology and maintain ongoing media monitoring for this indicator.
- Track progress against ARCH’s Results Framework: outcomes, outputs, indicators, baselines and targets.
- Apply and maintain a tiered partner-monitoring approach, ensuring requirements are proportionate to grant size.
- Maintain, verify, consolidate and analyse quantitative and qualitative data across the grant portfolio, including through ARCH’s digital grant management platform.
- Ensure that youth engagement, gender equality, disability inclusion, cultural diversity and human rights-based approaches are captured systematically in data and reporting.
- Quality-assure partner and grantee narrative and results reporting in English and French, and maintain organised, audit-ready MEL records.
- Support monitoring visits, spot checks and verification activities together with Secretariat colleagues, Local Liaison Officers and partners.

**MEL training and support to grantees**

- Design and deliver practical MEL training, onboarding and webinars for grantees and partners, adapted to grant tier, language and experience; develop accessible tools and provide hands-on follow-up.
- Brief and support Local Liaison Officers to help grantees with basic monitoring and data collection.

**Reporting, learning and adaptive management**

- Prepare results data, indicator updates and draft MEL sections for reports to the Danish Ministry of Foreign Affairs and ARCH governance bodies.
- Organise structured reflection after calls for proposals and regular portfolio-wide learning harvests.
- Capture and share lessons and good practices through the Annual Learning Report, Grant Learning Notes, case studies and other knowledge products.
- Identify trends, challenges and opportunities in programme data and translate them into practical recommendations that strengthen programme planning, strategic dialogue, governance, decision-making and adaptive management.
- Support learning processes linked to the ARCH Strategic Dialogue Forum and other learning events.
- Prepare data, evidence and documentation for the external Mid-Term Review in 2028 and the internal end evaluation.

## **About you**

We are looking for a structured, curious and collaborative MEL professional with a practical approach and strong analytical skills. The role is particularly suited to an early-career candidate who can explain MEL concepts clearly, support others to build their skills and turn evidence into useful insights.

### **Essential requirements**

- A relevant degree in monitoring and evaluation, development studies, social sciences, statistics, economics or a related field.
- Up to three years of relevant professional experience is preferred. Candidates with up to five years of experience are also welcome to apply.
- Hands-on experience designing or implementing MEL systems for donor-funded programmes, including collecting, analysing and reporting on indicator data against a results framework or logframe.
- Working knowledge of results-based management and theory of change approaches.
- Good quantitative and qualitative analysis skills, including experience developing indicators, data collection tools and reporting templates, and preparing clear analytical or donor reports.
- Experience designing and delivering training, workshops or coaching for partners, community groups or colleagues, with the ability to explain MEL concepts in simple, practical terms.
- Excellent written and spoken English.
- Strong organisational, problem-solving and communication skills, with integrity and close attention to detail.
- Ability to work independently and collaboratively across teams and cultures and to build constructive relationships with diverse stakeholders.
- Professional working proficiency in written and spoken French is strongly desired.

### **Additional advantages**

- Familiarity with institutional donor results and reporting requirements, such as those of bilateral agencies, the EU or UN agencies.
- Experience with MEL in grant-making or sub-granting programmes across multiple organisations or countries.
- Experience with digital data collection, analysis and visualisation tools such as KoBoToolbox, ODK, Excel or Power BI.
- Experience with participatory or qualitative learning methods, such as outcome harvesting or Most Significant Change.
- Experience with media monitoring or communications analytics.
- Knowledge of the arts, culture or creative sectors.

## **Practical information**

**Location and working arrangements**  
This is a full-time position based in Nairobi, Kenya. You will work from the Nairobi office alongside the Senior Admin and Financial Management Specialist two to three days per week, with the option to work from home on the remaining days. Some travel within ARCH countries and internationally may be required.

**Salary and benefits**  
The salary range is fixed at a junior level and informed by Kenyan NGO and INGO market benchmarks. The gross cash salary includes amounts equivalent to a 10% pension contribution and an allowance for health and life insurance, which employees arrange themselves. Salary, benefits and employment conditions will be discussed with shortlisted candidates.

jobs.title: Chargé-e de Communication
jobs.body:
**Organisation overview**

Tostan is a 501(c)(3) non-profit organization based in Dakar, Senegal, currently operating in five West African countries. At the strategic level, the organization is committed to continuing to develop its core competency of empowering education, and to document and scale the sustainable impact it creates on a range of issues. Tostan's flagship model, the three-year Community Empowerment Programme (CEP), has already reached thousands of communities in West and East Africa since 1991. Results in governance, education, health, economic empowerment, and the environment are currently being monitored, and Tostan is particularly proud to have played an important role in the large-scale empowerment of women and girls and in community abandonment of harmful practices such as female genital mutilation and child marriage.

As part of its strategic engagement plan 2023–2030, Tostan focuses on strategic scaling. The organization is developing new implementation strategies to support community leadership by unlocking broader systemic changes at the regional level. It also creates new models for sharing and replicating its programs with other development partners and expands its capacity to share Tostan's global approach to support and influence a range of local and global audiences. For more information, please visit: [www.tostan.org](http://www.tostan.org).

**Role overview**

The Communications team shapes Tostan’s narrative, advocacy, brand identity and donor visibility at community, national, regional and global levels. Tostan is part of a four-year regional programme on young women’s economic leadership in climate-resilient horticulture in Senegal and The Gambia. Within it, Tostan leads the community governance and social transformation component in partner communities across both countries.

The Communication Officer will show how changes in community governance and social norms open economic pathways for young women. The officer will turn field evidence into stories, public narratives and policy arguments, and will bring young women’s experience into the spaces where decisions on investment, finance and markets are made. Young women and community actors are the authors of this change. The officer’s job is to document it accurately and amplify their voices, never to speak in their place.

**Roles and responsibilities**

The Communication Officer reports to the Head of Communications and works in close operational coordination with the Senior Programme Manager.

1. **Programmatic Communication (35%)**
    
    ● Plan and conduct regular field missions to partner communities to document change through interviews, written stories, photography and short video, working with young women, community leaders, local authorities and producer groups.
    
    ● Work with the MEL and programme teams to turn monitoring data and evaluation findings into impact stories and case studies that show how community governance and norm change translate into economic opportunity.
    
    ● Contribute to the production of documentary films at country and regional levels, from story research and field coordination to review of edits.
    
    ● Produce local-language safeguarding communication materials in coordination with the Safeguarding Focal Points.
    
    ● Support the selection, training and mentoring of young women community storytellers, and edit their stories for publication.
    
    ● Maintain a well-catalogued multimedia library with documented consent for every image, recording and quote. ● Co-draft the communication sections of donor narrative reports with the MEL and programme leads.
2. **Digital Communications 20%**
    
    ● Produce regular content for Tostan’s and partners’ social media channels, newsletters and websites in French and English
    
    ● Feed and update the programme’s shared online knowledge platform and impact dashboard with stories, data and multimedia, in coordination with partner web teams.
    
    ● Run digital campaigns around programme milestones and international days related to women’s economic rights, food systems and climate.
    
    ● Track digital performance and report regularly on what works, what does not, and why.
    
    ● Apply co-branding, attribution and visibility guidelines across all digital assets.
3. **Advocacy (25%)**
    
    ● Contribute to policy briefs and thematic reports that turn field evidence into recommendations on public investment in women-led rural enterprises, on the integration of community-led models into national programmes, and on access to finance and markets.
    
    ● Support the preparation of the annual learning and advocacy forum, including content, speaker preparation and the meaningful participation of young women and community representatives.
    
    ● Prepare briefing notes, talking points and toolkits for Tostan leadership and programme staff attending policy dialogues, consortium meetings and regional events.
    
    ● Identify opportunities for young women and community leaders to speak directly in national, regional and global forums, and prepare them for these appearances with their informed consent.
    
    ● Monitor national policy processes, budget cycles and public debates in Senegal and The Gambia, and flag openings for advocacy to the Head of Communications.
4. **Media Relations (20%)**
    
    ● Build and maintain working relationships with journalists, editors and radio producers in national, regional and community media.
    
    ● Support the selection, training and mentoring of journalist fellows, including solutions-journalism workshops, and follow their reporting on women-led rural enterprise.
    
    ● Draft, translate and distribute press releases, media advisories and op-eds in French and English.
    
    ● Organise press trips to partner communities and coordinate media presence at key moments, including community engagement days and public declarations.
    
    ● Apply the media engagement protocol, prepare spokespeople and contribute to crisis response when needed. ● Monitor media coverage of young women’s economic rights and rural development, and report on how framing changes over time.
    
    **Key relationships**
    
    ***Direct line Manager:*** Head of Communications
    
    ***Localisation :*** Thiès. Senegal
    
    **Key Qualifications Skills, Education, and Experience**
    
    ● Bachelor’s Degree in Communications, Master’s degree, or similar advanced degree in relevant discipline preferred
    
    ● More than five years communications experience;
    
    ● Experience working in a development context and/or social sector organization
    
    ● Professional experience using and leading others on key communications technology tools such as web-based project and content management systems, social media tools as well as search engine optimization
    
    **Characteristics**
    
    ● Ability to build relationships and work effectively within a complex, multi-stakeholder environment.
    
    ● Expertise using and overseeing the production of websites, online communities, videos, webinars, infographics and other multimedia web content
    
    ● Excellent analytical, written and verbal communication and presentation skills
    
    ● Ability to quickly distill complex concepts into interesting and digestible pieces
    
    ● Passionate belief in and commitment to Tostan’s mission to empower African communities to bring about sustainable development and positive social transformation based on respect for human rights
    
    ● Ability to work in a collaborative, co-creative team, bringing value to the team’s outcomes
    
    **Language**
    
    ● High levels of English
    
    ● French as a minimum
    
    ● Other languages that Tostan works in would be an advantage – especially Wolof or Portuguese

> Our team is made up of people who strongly believe in Tostan’s mission to empower communities to develop and realize their vision for the future and inspire large-scale movements towards dignity for all.

jobs.title: AFGHANISTAN - Gender Responsive WASH Program Manager (F/M) -KABUL
jobs.body:
## About us

**Desired start date: 1st November 2026**  
**Duration of the mission: 6 months**  
**Location: Kabul**

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms.

## About the mission

SOLIDARITÉS INTERNATIONAL activities are implemented in Bamyan, Herat, Helmand, Nimroz and Farah provinces, with emergency activities that can be deployed all over the country. Operational bases are in Zaranj (capital of Nimroz Province), Farah, Herat and Bamyan city.

The team is now made of 125 national and 9 international employees with an annual budget of around 5.5 M EUR. SI currently implements WASH and Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR)/Natural Resource Management (NRM) programs.

There are currently 3 grants under implementation:

\- CDCS (French MoFA): covering emergency response interventions across several provinces.

\- ECHO consortium: In consortium with SCI (lead), INTERSOS and HI, the project responds to the returnees crisis at informal settlements and areas of return. SI response focuses on WASH, MPCA and winterization.

\- ECHO consortium: In consortium with INTERSOS (lead), and MdM, the project provides integrated Health, Nutrition, and WASH interventions in white areas. SI response focuses on WASH.

## About the job

**GENERAL OBJECTIVES**

-Lead the implementation of a strategic assessment and programme quality initiative aimed at strengthening the meaningful inclusion of women in WASH programming, ensuring delivery of agreed objectives, workplans and budgets.Oversee technical assessments, evidence generation, data analysis and production of operational recommendations to strengthen gender-responsive WASH programme design and service delivery.

-Coordinate technical engagement with implementing partners and relevant stakeholders throughout implementation.

-Build and maintain effective working relationships with women organisations, implementing partners, technical institutions and other relevant stakeholders to support project implementation and technical collaboration.

-Represent SI in technical meetings, workshops and coordination forums related to gender-responsive WASH programming, ensuring consistent communication and follow-up with external stakeholders.

-Support the development of practical tools, technical guidance and organisational learning to improve the integration of women's priorities into WASH programmes, and the inclusion, wellbeing and development of female colleagues within the organisation.

-Ensure activities are delivered in compliance with SI procedures, donor requirements and the evolving operational context, while maintaining appropriate communication and risk management.

**ISSUES AND SPECIFIC CHALLENGES**

-Working in a highly sensitive and changing operational environment affecting programming related to women and gender inclusion.  
-Coordinating assessment activities across several provinces and with multiple partners.  
-Managing large amounts of qualitative and quantitative data and translating findings into practical recommendations for gender-responsive WASH programming.  
-Balancing operational realities with the objective of strengthening the meaningful participation and inclusion of women in WASH programmes.  
-Ensuring effective coordination between programme, MEAL, grants and support departments.  
-Frequent travel to project locations is required to support field activities, partner coordination and quality assurance in line with the security context and organizational procedures.

**PRIORITIES ON THE 2-3 FIRST MONTHS**

-Complete the ongoing assessment, including supervision of data collection, quality assurance and analysis.  
-Finalize the assessment report and related technical products.  
-Coordinate review and validation of findings with SI teams and external partners.  
-Develop practical guidance and tools to strengthen the integration of women's priorities into WASH programme design and implementation.  
-Support the integration of assessment recommendations into ongoing and future WASH programmes.  
-Strengthen collaboration with women's organizations, technical partners and other stakeholders supporting the initiative.  
-Ensure effective planning, reporting, external coordination and overall project management throughout implementation.

**SECURITY CONSTRAINTS**

Volatility of the context, but access to the field is possible for all areas of intervention

## Your profile

**DIPLOMAS AND EXPERIENCE**

Bachelor's degree in a relevant field, such as Social Sciences, Public Health, Engineering, Development Studies, International Relations, Political Science, Management or another related discipline.

- Experience in the humanitarian sector : 3-4 years
- Experience on a similar position : 0-2 years

**SKILLS**

TECHNICAL SKILLS

1\. Project management: Experience planning, coordinating and monitoring projects, assessments or research activities.

2\. Analysis and reporting: Ability to analyse information and produce clear reports, recommendations and other technical documents.

3\. Digital and data management: Good computer skills (Microsoft Office); experience with Kobo or other digital data collection tools is an asset.

TRANSVERSAL SKILLS

1\. Communication and stakeholder engagement: Strong interpersonal skills and ability to build effective relationships with partners and stakeholders.

2\. Organisation and problem-solving: Ability to manage multiple priorities, work independently and adapt to changing circumstances.

3\. Leadership and teamwork: Ability to coordinate teams, facilitate collaboration and support capacity building.

**LANGUAGES**

1\. Proficiency in English is mandatory

2\. Proficiency in Dari

3\. Pashto is a plus

## SI will offer you

**A salaried position:**  
**According to experience,** starting from EUR 2365 gross per month (2150 base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 600.

SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment.

**Breaks:** During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every two months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked.

**Insurance package:** Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded.

**LIVING CONDITIONS:**

Guest House conditions: Well furnished Guest House is vailaible with the needed services. Electricity is limited but the guesthouse will be supported by the solar system and as well as generator. A small GYM is also available in the Guest House for maintaining routine excercises

 Internet and telephone network: The staff will have dedicated SIM & Mobile for his/her communication 24/7

Restaurant & social life: Social life is limited to authorized restaurants and locations, and contact with other INGO staff, with a curfew.

jobs.title: Request for proposals – External Auditor Netherlands
jobs.body:
## **About ACAPS**

[ACAPS](http://www.acaps.org/) believes that evidence must be at the heart of humanitarian action and together with our partners we turn data into decisions that truly matter. We cut through the noise and make sense out of chaos. We analyse complex data and provide clear insights so that decision-makers can take the best possible course of action.

We do this by:

- Providing independent analysis that helps humanitarians make informed choices.
- Deploying experts to support assessments and analysis in crisis.
- Driving innovation to collect better, faster, and more reliable data.

Until the end of 2025, ACAPS was a project hosted by the Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC). Since 1 January 2026, ACAPS operates as an independent foundation (stichting) registered in the Netherlands.

## **Requested services**

We are looking for a Dutch audit firm to audit the annual financial statements of Stichting ACAPS for financial year 2026 and issue a signed controleverklaring.

FY2026 is our first audited year as an independent organisation. FY2025 was covered by a compilation engagement (samenstelverklaring). ACAPS is expected to qualify as a small legal entity, so this is a voluntary audit, but it must meet the same professional standards as a statutory audit. Annual expenditure is approximately €6.5 million.

The successful audit firm will deliver the following services:

*Audit of the financial statements*

- Audit the FY2026 annual financial statements in accordance with Dutch auditing standards (NV COS).
- Issue a signed controleverklaring on whether the financial statements give a true and fair view under Title 9 Book 2 of the Dutch Civil Code and RJ 640 (not-for-profit organisations).
- Check that the Management Board report (bestuursverslag) is consistent with the financial statements.
- Include the sections on fraud and going concern required by the NBA.

*Reporting*

- Provide a management letter (accountantsverslag) with audit findings, internal control observations and prioritised recommendations.
- Present the audit findings to the Board or its audit committee, in English.
- Follow up on previous recommendations in later years of the contract.
    
    *Donor-specific reports (optional)*

Some donors and lead partners require separate assurance reports, such as NV COS 800/805 reports or agreed-upon procedures. These are not part of the core audit. Please quote them separately, per report. We will confirm the final list at contract signature.

**Areas of specific attention**

As this is a first-year audit following our separation from NRC, we expect the following areas to need specific attention:

- Opening balances on 1 January 2026, transferred from NRC. ACAPS holds the supporting documentation and has read-only access to the relevant NRC records.
- Income recognition across three funding routes: grants signed directly with donors, sub-agreements under grants held by NRC, and partnerships led by other NGOs, including EU-funded actions.
- Restricted funds, deferred income and balances with NRC and other lead partners.
- Personnel costs, our largest expense, across three employment models: direct employment in the Netherlands, staff hosted by a partner organisation, and employer-of-record providers.
- Allocation of staff time and other costs to grants.
- Related-party transactions, in particular with NRC.
- Presentation of the FY2025 comparative figures, which are unaudited and not comparable to FY2026.
- Introduction of a new ERP system during 2026.

## Indicative timeline

**Milestone and Indicative date**

- Contract award and engagement letter: November – December 2026
- Planning meeting and information request list (min. 4 weeks before start of interim audit): December 2026
- Interim audit: internal control and opening balances: January – February 2027
- ACAPS delivers year-end file and draft financial statements: 31 March 2027
- Year-end fieldwork: April 2027
- Draft auditor’s report and management letter:15 May 2027
- Presentation to the Supervisory Council and Management Board: Latest 30 May 2027
- Signed controleverklaring and final management letter: 5 June 2027

## Requirements

- Dutch audit firm registered with the NBA and authorised to issue a controleverklaring.
- An engagement partner who is a Registeraccountant (RA) or Accountant-Administratieconsulent (AA) with certifying authority.
- A licence from the AFM under the Wta is preferred. Firms without one should show a satisfactory recent quality review.
- Experience auditing non-profit organisations funded by institutional and government donors, under RJ 640.
- Experience with first-year audits, ideally of organisations that separated from a host agency.
- Experience with organisations that have an international workforce.
- An engagement partner and manager who can work and report in English.
- Independence from ACAPS, its Supervisory Council and its management.

jobs.title: Country Operations Manager – Ukraine
jobs.body:
**Place:** Kiev or Kharkiv, Ukraine  
**Starting date:** 1st December 2026  
**Duration of contract:** 12 months

**Due to the urgency of this recruitment, we encourage interested candidates to submit their applications as soon as possible. We will be reviewing applications on an ongoing basis.**

Humanity & Inclusion is an independent and impartial aid organisation working in situations of poverty and exclusion, conflict and disaster. The organisation works alongside people with disabilities and vulnerable populations, taking action and bearing witness in order to respond to their essential needs, improve their living conditions and promote respect for their dignity and fundamental rights.

Since its creation in 1982, HI has run development & humanitarian projects in more than 55 countries and responded to numerous emergencies. Today, we have a budget of approximately 200 million euros, with 4,000 employees worldwide

At Handicap International-Humanity & Inclusion, we truly believe in the importance of inclusion and diversity within our organisation. This is why we are engaged to a disability policy to encourage the inclusion and integration of people with disabilities.

Please indicate if you require any special accommodation, even at the first interview. [For more information about the organisation.](https://www.hi.org/en/index)

**JOB CONTEXT:**

From February 2022, HI has re-opened a Country Programme in Ukraine to respond to the humanitarian needs triggered by the full-scale invasion of Ukraine by the Russian Federation.

In 2024, HI pillars of interventions are:

- Health: HI aims to improve access to quality physical rehabilitation and mental health and psychosocial support services (MHPSS) for conflict-affected vulnerable population.
- Protection: Given the scale of humanitarian and protection needs, HI intervenes at various levels to ensure that vulnerable conflict-affected populations have access to multi-sectoral services tailored to their needs. In addition, HI aims to foster a disability-inclusive humanitarian response.
- Humanitarian Mine Action: Ongoing attacks dangerously exacerbated Explosive Ordnance (EO) contamination in Ukraine.
    - EORE/CPP: HI is conducting a multi-pronged approach to EO Risk Education (RE) and Conflict Preparedness and Protection (CPP).
    - Advocacy
    - NTS: HI is implementing Non-Technical Survey activities in Kharkivska Oblast since 2025.
    - VA (Victim Assistance)

HI has 2 hubs, one in the East (based in Dnipro), one in the North East (based in Kharkiv), and the coordination office is in Kyiv.

**YOUR MISSION:**   
Under the responsibility of the Country Director Ukraine, as Operations Manager you contribute within the country where you are based to the implementation of the mandate and the 10-year strategy of Humanity & Inclusion. You ensure optimal quality and impact of the projects implemented in the country, through a delegation system with appropriate control mechanisms. You share with all HI managers the responsibility of sound management and successful functioning of the global organization, through paradigm changes.

**Responsibility 1: Management**

1.1: Be the manager (direct report) of the 3 Project Managers in the country of assignment

- Foster team spirit and team functioning guaranteeing synergies and exchange of good practices between Project Managers and with head office colleagues.
- Recruit and contribute to the professional development, autonomy and well-being at work of the Project Managers: in link with the corresponding professional channels, set formalized individual objectives, ensure coherence between HI’s needs and competencies and motivation of his/her teams, develop and monitor competence development plan, evaluate individual performance, contribute to career evolution.

**Responsibility 2: Contribution to the Programme’s Operational Strategy and HI frameworks & regulations**

2.1: Contribute to the development of the Programme’s Operational Strategy, and to its implementation and annual monitoring

- With assessment of ongoing projects, contribution to context and sectorial analysis, contribution to fundraising strategy, to resource sizing, to M&E tool.
- Contribute, with his/her portfolio of projects and donors’ data, to the annual monitoring of the StratOp.
- In case of crisis/emergency, implement the framework and set-up determined by HI Operations Director.
- Actively lead to the development of opportunities, partnerships and strategy in new potential areas of implementation.
- Actively support start-up of new programmes and operations in current areas of implementation (education and preparedness).

2.2: Implement the project part of the Programme’s Operational Strategy

- Contribute to size and plan necessary resources, recruitment of the Project Managers (ensure the fit between competencies and the projects’ challenges and ambitions), develop and monitor their competence development plan, in link with the corresponding professional channels and with the Human Resources Manager.
- Develop regular contacts with current and potential donors at field level and liaise with the Programme Director, Project Managers and Technical Unit to check coherence with overall Programming and fundraising strategy.
- Within the operational framework defined in the StratOp, identify and transform funding opportunities in new potential areas, conduct the design and writing of new projects with relevant colleagues in new potential areas of operations.
- In link with the Technical Unit Manager, identify and develop local partnerships and/or consortia with NGOs, institutions, companies, on technical priorities or important topics at National Level and in new potential areas of intervention.

2.4: Ensure sound management and monitoring of projects under his/her responsibility (New potential areas of intervention)

- In link with the Technical Unit Manager and the MEAL Unit, ensure that HI technical quality standards are applied in the projects, and monitor the implementation of recommendations from support missions, evaluations and donor audits.
- Ensure compliance with project donors’ rules and regulations, including visibility.
- With the support of the MEAL Manager, deploy all adequate tools that will allow financial control and project monitoring, compliance with HI policies and frameworks, and the respect of contractual obligations towards donors: consolidation, control and reporting to the Ops Manager operational and organizational elements (dashboards and corrective measures, unrestricted funds consumption, beneficiaries’ data…).
- Facilitate internal audits (operational, financial and organizational), and ensure the implementation of their recommendations on his/her responsibility area with relevant colleagues.

2.5: With both operational opportunities and risks in mind, contribute to the monitoring and analysis made by HAS, Operations and CD, and propose mitigation measures when relevant in new potential areas of intervention.

- Implement analysis and monitoring of risks & opportunities related to HI presence and activities; implement risk mitigation actions at his/her level; and ensure the implementation of a humanitarian watch.

**Responsibility 3: Influence**

3.1: Support develop external influence of HI (forums, operational & strategic alliances, etc.) and the external representation of the organization (events, media) at the National Level

- Can represent HI vis-à-vis local, national, traditional, political, military and diplomatic authorities and bodies; and international organizations and coordination mechanisms & system.
- Take on the messages of HI global advocacy to all relevant external parties.
- Develop local partnerships.

**CHARACTERISTICS OF THE POSITION:**

- The security situation in Ukraine remains relatively stable, although air alert is frequently active. However, markets, restaurants and cafes are open, and life continues as normal. There is a strict curfew, the hours depend on the region.

**YOUR PROFILE:**

- You have at least 5 years of professional experience in humanitarian / early recovery contexts,
- You have at least 3 years of experience in management of field bases and/or programs,
