jobs.title: Research, Monitoring & Evaluation (M&E) Officer
jobs.body:
**Research, Monitoring & Evaluation (M&E) Officer**

LOCATION: Kakamega, Kenya (with field travel as required)

REPORTS TO :MEAL Coordinator

**Employment type: Full-time | Application deadline: October 30, 2026**

**ABOUT ICS SP**

For over 30 years, ICS SP (Investing in Children and their Societies) has worked across Africa to build safe and nurturing environments for children and families. Our programming spans Violence and Exploitation, Early Childhood Care and Development, Inclusive and Safe Education, and Sustainable Livelihoods. Visit [www.icsafrica-sp.org](http://www.icsafrica-sp.org) to learn more about us.

**PURPOSE OF THE ROLE**

Reporting to the MEAL Coordinator, the Research, Monitoring & Evaluation Officer will lead day-to-day implementation of results-based monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning activities for ICS SP programmes supported from Kakamega. The Officer will work with programme teams and partners to develop and operate robust M&E systems, generate credible evidence of results, strengthen reporting and use learning to improve programme quality and effectiveness.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

**1. Results-based monitoring, evaluation and programme quality**

- Develop, implement and regularly refine results-based M&E systems, results frameworks, indicator definitions, monitoring plans and practical data-collection tools in collaboration with the MEAL Coordinator and programme teams; align these with ICS SP and donor requirements.
- Monitor project activities, outputs and progress against approved plans and targets, identify performance gaps and implementation of bottlenecks, and recommend corrective actions to project management.
- Plan and undertake routine field monitoring and data verification visits; prepare clear findings, action points and follow-up reports for programme teams and management.
- Coordinate field-level inputs to baseline assessments, evaluations, research and other studies, ensuring sound methods, reliable evidence and follow-up on recommendations.

**2. Data management, analysis and quality assurance**

- Maintain accurate, timely, and secure indicator-tracking systems, project databases and supporting records, with consistent data collection and documentation procedures.
- Conduct data quality checks, cleaning, verification and analysis; reconcile figures across field tools, databases and reports, and strengthen completeness, accuracy and timeliness of project and partner submissions.
- Analyze quantitative and qualitative data, including appropriately authorized child protection case-management, capacity-strengthening and awareness-raising data, and present findings responsibly and with relevant disaggregation.
- Produce dashboards, evidence briefs and data visualizations to communicate project results and inform operational decisions, donor reports and programme improvements.

**3. Planning, reporting and M&E capacity strengthening**

- Prepare annual and quarterly M&E component plans and budgets and contribute to consolidated project work plans, target-setting exercises, and annual programme reviews.
- Prepare and consolidate monthly, quarterly and annual results reports, key-result summaries, M&E reports, and evidence-based inputs to management and donor reporting.
- Organize and facilitate M&E trainings, review meetings and workshops, including concepts, agendas, tools and learning materials; coach programme staff, partners and community structures in using the M&E framework.
- Support project coordinators to prepare performance reviews and planning workshops, using verified results to identify challenges, lessons, and recommendations.

**4. Accountability, safeguarding and responsible data management**

- Strengthen community feedback and accountability mechanisms and support appropriate documentation, referral and escalation of concerns in line with ICS SP procedures.
- Ensure ethical data collection, informed consent, confidentiality, child safeguarding and data protection standards in monitoring, research, case-related data and dissemination of findings.
- Promote safe, inclusive and participatory M&E approaches, with particular care in engagement with children and vulnerable communities.

**5. Research, knowledge sharing and coordination**

- Identify and document evidence-based success stories, achievements, lessons learned and good practices and translate findings into practical recommendations for programme improvement.
- Compile and disseminate relevant information from project data systems to programme management, donors and other authorized stakeholders in accessible formats.
- Facilitate learning exchanges, periodic reflection, and the integration of evaluation and research findings into organizational knowledge management, planning, and strategy.
- Collaborate with government agencies, NGOs, research actors and M&E networks; represent ICS SP in relevant technical forums as delegated by the MEAL Coordinator.

**REQUISITE REQUIREMENTS**

- Bachelor’s degree in Monitoring and Evaluation, Statistics, Economics, Social Sciences, Community Development or related field.
- Minimum five years of progressively responsible M&E experience in NGO, child-focused, community development or related social-impact programming.
- Demonstrated ability to develop and implement results-based M&E systems, indicators and tools, conduct field monitoring and data quality assessments, and prepare high-quality results and donor reports.
- Proficiency in Excel and digital data collection (such as Kobo Toolbox or ODK); experience using statistical analysis or data visualization tools is an added advantage.
- Understanding quantitative and qualitative research, evaluations, case-related data analysis, and ethical monitoring approaches.
- Strong planning, organization, communication, report writing, facilitation, analytical judgement and stakeholder engagement skills; ability to coach programme teams and partners.
- Commitment to safeguarding, confidentiality and responsible handling of personal and case-related data.
- Excellent written and spoken English and Kiswahili; ability and willingness to travel regularly to project sites.

ICS SP’s absolute priority is protecting children, vulnerable communities and our own staff. We have zero tolerance of incidents of violence, abuse and exploitation of children and other people in the communities we serve, whether committed by our staff or others connected to our work. Successful applicants will be required to sign and adhere to our safeguarding, child protection and prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA) code of conduct and policies.

jobs.title: DMEAL Adviser - Pacific
jobs.body:
With 75 years of experience, our focus is on helping the most vulnerable children overcome poverty and experience fullness of life. We help children of all backgrounds, even in the most dangerous places, inspired by our Christian faith.

Come join our 33,000+ staff working in nearly 100 countries and share the joy of transforming vulnerable children’s life stories!

**Here’s where you come in:**

As **DMEAL Adviser - Pacific**, you will provide strategic and technical DMEAL support, capacity strengthening, and advisory services to World Vision’s four Pacific Field Offices within the SAPO region, promoting quality DMEAL practices, evidence use, and learning. You will provide technical leadership for grant DMEAL across SAPO, including non-Pacific Field Offices, through the DMEAL for Grants Community of Practice (CoP), strengthening grant DMEAL quality, capacity, and cross-country learning while developing evidence and impact briefs. You will also provide matrix supervision and technical guidance to the DMEAL leads in Papua New Guinea and Solomon Islands, as agreed with the respective Field Offices, and report to the Regional Evidence and Impact Senior Adviser.

**Technical Assistance**

You will support Pacific National Offices in applying DMEAL and programme quality standards, guidelines, tools, and methodologies, including reviewing programme designs, baselines, evaluations, Annual Impact Measurement (AIM), and programme reports. You will provide technical guidance on iMPAQ, monitoring and MEAL systems, data quality, analysis, reporting, and evidence-based decision-making. You will also help communicate programme impact for income and influence goals and promote knowledge sharing and lessons learned to improve programme and organizational performance.

**Capacity Building**

You will assess DMEAL staff competencies, processes, structures, and approaches, identify gaps, and develop capacity-building interventions for National Offices and partners. You will facilitate workshops, peer learning, and individual support, lead regional MEAL capacity-strengthening initiatives, support the regional M&E Community of Practice, and strengthen Field Office teams’ use of monitoring data and evidence for programme quality, adaptive management, learning, and reporting.

**Strategic Management Support**

You will support the development and refresh of Pacific Field Office strategies, ensuring DMEAL and programme quality priorities are integrated. You will support Partnership and DMEAL initiatives, strengthen collaboration with donors and Support Offices, contribute to organizational programme quality strategies and standards, lead the regional AIM process and support quality Annual Child Results Reports. You will also provide technical support to relevant Pacific Field Offices in developing and implementing Integrated Programme Frameworks (IPFs), including in Solomon Islands.

**M&E Leadership**

You will develop professional networks and partnerships with universities, private-sector organizations, donors, and non-profit entities, contribute to organizational M&E discussions and guideline development, and coordinate with Support Offices and major donors to align monitoring and evaluation requirements. You will also collaborate with the Regional Grant Acquisition team to provide DMEAL and programme quality inputs and support, including participation in grant Go/No-Go decision-making.

**Requirements include:**

- Minimum of 5-7 years of experience in monitoring and evaluation at a national level (or large program level).
- Proven ability to facilitate working groups, communities of practice or other similar learning mechanisms
- Proven ability to collaborate with all levels of staff and to motivate and mobilize individuals outside their reporting line to achieve agreed strategic plans.
- Knowledge of the monitoring and evaluation requirements of one or more institutional donors (USAID, DFAT, DevCo, etc.)
- Bachelor’s degree and post-graduate certification or master’s degree in the social, statistic or related field.
- Qualitative and/or quantitative research and evaluation skills, including but not limited to study design, survey instrument design and use, establishing and measuring outcome and process indicators, sampling, data analysis plans, data cleaning, and statistical analysis.
- Demonstrated ability to report, present and communicate results, written and verbal in modern standard English.
- Master’s degree in social sciences, statistics or related field.
- Evidence of the ability to facilitate M&E capacity building approaches (workshop facilitation, 1:1 coaching, etc.)
- Business process improvement (Lean Six Sigma)
- Experience in working in pacific countries

jobs.title: Global Surge Team Roster: Emergency Grants Coordinator
jobs.body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**IRC Global Surge Team:**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world’s most severe humanitarian crises, helping people survive, recover, and rebuild their lives. Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC delivers life‑saving assistance and long‑term recovery services to people affected by conflict and disaster. Today, the IRC works in over 30 countries and 22 U.S. cities, restoring safety, dignity, and hope to millions worldwide.

The IRC’s Global Surge Team (GST) is a roster of highly qualified humanitarian professionals who deploy on short notice to emergency and non‑emergency contexts to support the IRC’s mission. GST members provide specialized, time‑bound support where capacity gaps exist, typically for deployments of up to three months.

**The GST is a flexible, occasional employment opportunity. Deployment needs vary based on demand. Staff can take on additional deployments as opportunities arise and if they are interested.** Deployment opportunities depend on organizational and operational requirements and may vary over time; as such, deployments cannot be guaranteed. Staff supporting emergency responses must be prepared to deploy within 72 hours as needs arise.

**French speaking candidates are currently being prioritized.**

**Job Summary:**

The **Emergency Grants Coordinator, Global Surge** plays a critical role in supporting emergency humanitarian responses by leading grant management, donor compliance, proposal development, and reporting functions in rapidly evolving crisis settings. As part of surge deployments, this position ensures the timely mobilization and stewardship of donor funding through the development of high-quality proposals, robust monitoring and reporting systems, and effective coordination with program teams, partners, donors, and headquarters. The role provides strategic guidance on donor regulations and compliance requirements, strengthens grants management capacity through staff training and mentorship, and supports strong information management practices to ensure accountability, program quality, and operational effectiveness. Working in complex emergency environments, the Emergency Grants Coordinator helps secure and manage resources that enable the delivery of impactful humanitarian assistance to affected populations.

**Responsibilities:**

- Ensure high quality and timely submission of funding proposals through development of timelines, coordinating technical and financial input, writing overviews, editing and formatting proposal documents, and liaison with HQ on approval and submission processes.
- Work with program and management staff to promote and ensure development of strong data collection andmonitoring & evaluation process, detailed collection and analysis of program data.
- Hire and train in-county grants staff as the need arises to efficiently support the scale and scope of the program
- Establish and ensure maintenance of comprehensive grant files and related information management processes including issuing reporting formats and schedules, maintaining donor and external contact information/files and protocols and establishing a photo library.
- Participate in and/or lead grant opening and review meetings; ensuring all required information is circulated in advance, meetings are fully documented and action items completed.
- Provide advice on donor grant compliance issues, visibility and reporting requirements; proactively engaging with program teams to ensure appropriate IRC and donor visibility
- Coordinate partner subgrant processes including preaward assessments, subgrant development, HQ review and approval processes, related partner reporting and compliance training to promote an encouraging and constructive relationship and effective oversight of subgrant activities and results.
- Prepare high quality and timely donor and management reports on grants and sector activities in close collaboration with program staff.
- Represent IRC and coordinate with other agencies, local government, donors and other partners to promote deliver of best practice humanitarian assistance and coordination of efforts.
- Support media and communications activities as requested by the emergency response team.
- Provide a comprehensive handover to successor, including ensuring transfer of all related documentation, program monitoring data and staff performance information.

**Requirements:**

- Significant experience in grants management, humanitarian program management, or a related field, including work in emergency and conflict-affected settings.
- Strong knowledge of major humanitarian donor regulations and compliance requirements, including UN agencies, USAID/BHA, ECHO/EC, and FCDO (formerly DFID).
- Proven experience coordinating donor proposals, grant management processes, reporting, and compliance across multiple stakeholders.
- Excellent English writing, editing, and communication skills; additional language skills are an asset (French fluency required).
- Strong understanding of monitoring, evaluation, and data management systems, with experience supporting program quality and accountability.
- Experience developing project budgets and working closely with finance teams on donor financial requirements.
- Demonstrated ability to build partnerships, facilitate collaboration across departments, and provide training and guidance on grants management and donor compliance.
- Strong organizational and project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and meet tight deadlines in fast-paced environments.
- Ability to work independently, adapt quickly to changing circumstances, and perform effectively in high-pressure emergency response contexts.
- Willingness and ability to deploy internationally on short notice to support humanitarian emergencies.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

jobs.title: Development of a vector control training package for wash and health practitioners in the africa region.
jobs.body:
(Find the complete folder with all relevant information including the [RFP here](https://rodekruis.sharepoint.com/sites/Meetingsinternational/Gedeelde%20%20documenten/Public%20documents/IH%20Procurement%20public%20documents/RFP%20-%20Log-2026-1374%20Vector%20Control%20Training?d=w2f16674c6c2f4567b3946c075513f3fd&csf=1&web=1&e=0j4Puk))

**Terms of Reference**

**Title of Assignment**

Development of a Vector Control Training Package for WASH and Health Practitioners in the Africa Region

**Project Name**

WASH Surge Localization Programme

**Project Country**

Global (pilot training to be conducted in Ethiopia or South Sudan)

**1. Introduction**

The Netherlands Red Cross (NLRC) and partners are working to strengthen local capacities for emergency preparedness, anticipatory action, and response across Africa. In line with their auxiliary role to the public authorities, and within the framework of localization, National Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies frequently act as first responders during disease outbreaks, flooding, displacement crises, and other emergencies.

Vector-borne diseases continue to pose a significant public health burden in many countries where the Red Cross and Red Crescent National Societies operate. At the same time, vector control knowledge among WASH and Health practitioners varies considerably. There is a need for accessible, practical training materials that can be used by National Societies, surge personnel, and humanitarian practitioners to improve knowledge and decision-making related to vector control.

The NLRC therefore seeks a consultant to develop a comprehensive training package on vector control that can be delivered by facilitators with a fair understanding of the subject matter. The package will be piloted during a training event planned for December 2026 in either Ethiopia or South Sudan.

**2. Background and Context**

Vector-borne diseases remain among the leading causes of morbidity and mortality in many humanitarian settings. Climate change, population movements, urbanization, environmental degradation, and weak health systems are contributing to changes in disease transmission patterns and increasing the risk of outbreaks.

Humanitarian organizations are increasingly expected to integrate vector control considerations into emergency preparedness, response, recovery, and resilience programmes. While specialist expertise is sometimes available, many WASH and Health practitioners involved in programme design and implementation have limited formal training in vector control.

The Red Cross movement has an important role to play through:

- Community engagement , risk communication and behaviour change
- Environmental management
- Vector surveillance and risk assessment
- Support to outbreak preparedness and response including community-based surveillance
- Coordination with health and WASH actors
- Integration of vector control into humanitarian programming

To strengthen these capacities, a practical training package is required that can be delivered in different country contexts and adapted to local disease priorities.

**3. Purpose, Objectives and Deliverables**

**Purpose**

To develop a practical, participatory and easy-to-facilitate vector control training package for WASH and Health practitioners working in humanitarian and development settings.

**Overall Objective**

To increase the knowledge and understanding of vector-borne disease prevention and vector control among WASH and Health practitioners, enabling them to support the design, implementation and monitoring of appropriate vector control interventions.

**Specific Objectives**

The training package should enable participants to:

- Understand the epidemiology and transmission pathways of major vector-borne diseases.
- Understand the roles and responsibilities of WASH, Health and community actors in vector control.
- Conduct basic vector-related risk assessments.
- Select appropriate vector control interventions based on context and risk.
- Understand operational, environmental and safety considerations.
- Integrate vector control into preparedness, anticipatory action and humanitarian emergency responses.
- Coordinate with relevant health, WASH and government stakeholders.

**Scope of the Training Package**

The consultant should develop a 3 days training package with different modules and exercises, allowing for a one to three days training depending on the modules used.

The training should cover, at minimum:

**Vector-borne Diseases**

Introduction to: Malaria (with description of different malaria carrying subspecies) Dengue, Chikungunya, Yellow Fever, Schistosomiasis, Trypanosomiasis and other relevant diseases common in African humanitarian settings

**Vector Control Approaches**

Introduction to Environmental mechanical biological and chemical and integrated Vector Management (IVM).

**Humanitarian Context**

The context considered for the training include, vector control during emergencies**,** vector control during displacement and camp settings, Flood-related vector risks, Urban vector control challenges as well as for the Red Cross important Community-based approaches, and Protection, Gender and Inclusion (PGI)

**Planning and Decision Making**

The training should include a section focusing on health and surveillance data, risk assessment, Intervention selection, Monitoring and evaluation, Coordination mechanisms

**Safety and Environmental Considerations**

This should include Safe handling of equipment and chemicals Environmental risks Waste management Safeguarding and community acceptance

**Emerging and other relevant Topics**

Climate change and vector-borne diseases Insecticide resistance, new and emerging vector control tools such as spatial repellents, Operational challenges in humanitarian settings

**Deliverables**

- The consultant will with the support of the NLRC and UNICEF will be expected to provide: Review and compilation of existing vector control training materials from organizations such as: IFRC, WHO, UNICEF and NGO’s working on vector control and identify materials that can be adapted and referenced.
- The consultant will develop a complete facilitator package in English including: Facilitator guide, Agenda for a 3-day version, Session plans, Facilitation notes, Interactive exercises Possible case studies and group work exercises, Quizzes and knowledge checks
- Participant package that should include: Participant manual, Handouts, Reference materials, Reading list Links to online resources
- PowerPoint presentation deck(s) suitable for use by non-specialist facilitators.
- Training evaluation package including: Pre-training assessment Post-training assessment Participant evaluation forms
- Facilitation of a pilot training in December 2026 in Ethiopia South Sudan or other country in the region and incorporation of lessons learned into the final training package(optional).

**4. Profile of the Desired Consultant**

The consultant should possess:

- Minimum 7 years of professional experience in vector control, public health, entomology, or related fields.
- Demonstrated experience in humanitarian settings.
- Experience with vector control in Africa, preferably in both emergency and development contexts.
- Proven experience in developing training curricula and adult learning materials.
- Strong facilitation skills.
- Experience working with Red Cross/Red Crescent, UN agencies, government institutions or international NGOs is an advantage.
- Excellent written and spoken English.
- Experience integrating participatory adult learning methodologies.

**5. Methodology**

The consultant is expected to:

1. Conduct a brief desk review of existing training resources.
2. Consult with NLRC, IFRC, UNICEF and selected technical experts.
3. Develop draft training materials.
4. Revise materials based on feedback.
5. Facilitate the pilot training.
6. Produce a final training package reflecting lessons learned from the pilot.

**6. Planning**

Indicative timeline:

**Activity Timeline**

Contracting consultant - Week of 9th November 2026

Desk review and consultations - November 20th 2026

Draft training package - November 25th 2026

Review and revisions - December 5th 2026

Pilot training (optional time permitting) - December 2026

Final training package - December 2026

**7. Climate and Environmental Impact**

The consultant should ensure that:

- The training promotes environmentally responsible vector control approaches.
- Environmental and ecological risks of vector control interventions are adequately addressed.
- Preference is given to sustainable and integrated vector management approaches.
- Training delivery methods minimize environmental impact where feasible.

**8. Responsibilities and Communication**

The assignment will be coordinated by:

- Jan Heeger, WASH Programme Advisor, NLRC
- Selam Seje, Health Advisor, NLRC
- Joey de Hamer, Programme Manager, NLRC
- Peter Mamburi IFRC technical focal points

**Submission Deadline**

The proposal shall be submitted before the deadline for reception of applications on the 4th of October 2026.

Submission Method

- Proposals must be submitted electronically by email at logistics@redcross.nl with a cc. to JdeHamer@redcross.nl.

The assignment, including the submission of the final invoice, must be completed no later than 31 December 2026.

**Bid Format**

- Email subject must be: Log-2026-1374 – Development of a Vector Control Training Package + \[Name of the bidder\]
- The attachments to be included are described in the next section.
- Language: All documents shall be submitted in English.

**9. Required Documents**

1. **Cover Letter**
2. **Curricula Vitae**
3. **Technical Proposal and methodology**
4. **Financial Proposal** (budget with clear breakdown of fee and overheads if applicable);
5. **Previous Samples:** Applicants must provide at least one, and up to two, samples of previous written work similar to that described in the ToR (such as prior health related training provided), with any sensitive information redacted.
6. **Vendor Registration Form**: Bidders are required to complete the \[[*Annex 2: NLRC Vendor Registration Form*](https://rodekruis.sharepoint.com/sites/Meetingsinternational/_layouts/15/guestaccess.aspx?share=ETvU5WP-Qq5Ah7aIFhh7RXYBKEjBFDi3JiyiO3IV3PlULQ&e=3Nh0Er)\] and submit all relevant supporting documentation referenced in the form (Administrative checklist, Part 1 and 1.9 Environmental standards).

**Vendor Code of Conduct**

NLRC is committed to upholding the highest sustainability standards and requirements (ethical, social, environmental and quality) in all our business providing high-quality services and products. Complying with all laws and regulations and ensuring fair competition are fundamental to this commitment.

The \[[*NLRC Vendor Code of Conduct - Annex 3*](https://rodekruis.sharepoint.com/sites/Meetingsinternational/_layouts/15/guestaccess.aspx?share=IQDkY_CmSWcBQ4W9oHAtgqC8ARRb9CRv9LFAU3eQCgyeOVM&e=FCc7JJ)\], expresses the expectations we hold for all NLRC vendors. The Vendor Code of Conduct outlines the behaviours expected of Vendors who commit to uphold these standards and prevent misconduct. It is legally binding and forms an integral part of the contract between the Vendor and the NLRC. The winning applicants will be requested to sign this Code of Conduct at contract stage.

**Climate & Environmental Impact**

The NLRC has signed an environmental charter. As we work towards ensuring that all our operations coincide with this new agreement, we must also demand that any collaborations we have with external parties also falls within the parameters of this charter.

Please complete the section 1.9 Environmental standards in the Vendor Registration Form \[[*NLRC\_Vendor Registration Form.docx*](https://rodekruis.sharepoint.com/sites/Meetingsinternational/_layouts/15/guestaccess.aspx?share=IQBTNSN4OdU7QISbXbwiWsG6AZBy_YDVy667BGqqVVp3tCg&e=8aZ3gj)\] and provide any additional documents that could illustrate your environmental engagement.

The consultant will work closely with NLRC and IFRC technical staff throughout the assignment and present draft outputs for review and approval.

jobs.title: Compliance Coordinator - Syria Aleppo or Idleb
jobs.body:
Established in 1977, GOAL is an international humanitarian and development agency, committed to working with communities to achieve sustainable and innovative early response in crises, and lasting solutions to poverty and vulnerability. GOAL has worked in over 60 countries and has responded to almost every major humanitarian disaster. We are currently operational in 18 countries.

GOAL began operations in Syria in 2013 responding to the acute needs of conflict-affected communities. GOAL's areas of operations include but not limited to Aleppo, Idleb and Damascus Programmes focus on Food and Nutrition Security, WASH, Shelter, Livelihoods/ERMS and Emergency Response with an emphasis on cash and voucher modalities. GOAL Syria implements its programmes directly, with staff based in Syria, and through Syrian NGO partners. GOAL's programme works at the household and community levels to improve community resilience and household coping strategies

**Job purpose:**

The Compliance Coordinator “CC” will oversee the Compliance Department, ensuring annual compliance plans are developed/followed and are appropriate to the context and management requirements. CC will manage the Compliance team who work across all departments, including programs, finance, procurement, logistics, and human resources, providing timely advice on donor regulations and feedback on the effectiveness of the internal controls in place in ensuring adherence to those regulations.

Provide leadership and oversight of the GOAL Syria Compliance Department ensuring that all responsibilities of the Compliance Department are fulfilled in a timely and effective manner, making best use of GOAL’s resources and ultimately ensuring compliance with donor and GOAL procedures and policies

**Duties, objectives and competencies:**

- Lead and manage the Compliance Department, including staff supervision, planning, and performance management.
- Develop and implement annual compliance plans and monitor compliance across all functions.
- Identify, assess, and mitigate compliance risks, ensuring timely escalation of significant issues.
- Provide guidance on donor regulations, organizational policies, contracts, partnerships, and grant management.
- Deliver compliance training and build staff and partner capacity.
- Oversee compliance reviews, audits, reporting, and follow-up on corrective actions.
- Ensure donor compliance, due diligence, sanctions screening, and regulatory requirements are effectively implemented.
- Support and monitor implementing partners to strengthen compliance systems and accountability.
- Coordinate donor audits, compliance investigations, and reviews, while escalating fraud, misconduct, or other significant breaches.

**Requirements (essential):**

- Bachelor’s degree in relevant subjects (such as Business Administration, Law, Finance, Accounting, Risk Management, international trade, or a related field).
- At least 3 years’ experience in leading compliance, audit, risk management, governance, or donor compliance within NGOs or Business Sector.
- At least 6 years professional experience in INGOs or NGOs in related fields.
- At least 5 years’ previous experience in team management.
- Proven ability to develop staff and provide training on systems and procedures.
- Any previous experience in implementing organizational internal control, SOPs and donor policies.
- Strong knowledge of donor regulations, internal controls, and risk management practices.
- Experience in compliance monitoring, risk assessment, audit follow-up, and corrective-action tracking.
- Ability to manage and priorities a varied workload in a rapidly changing work environment.
- Previous Experience in reviewing donor agreements, partnership agreements, procurement processes, waivers, exceptions, and organizational procedures.
- Willingness and ability to undertake some travel for work purposes, as required.
- Ability to work under pressure to pursue multiple tasks simultaneously to successful conclusions.
- Excellent leadership, analytical, communication, and stakeholder management skills.
- Excellent attention to detail.
- Trustworthy and honest.
- Fluency in Arabic and English

**Requirements (desired):**

- At least two years previous work experience as head of department.
- Diplomacy and negotiation skills.
- Master’s degree in related field.
- Previous experience in Anti-Terrorist Sanctions check systems.
- Previous experience in the U.S.G Vetting System "PVS".
- Data Analysis skills, including knowledge of Power BI and advanced Microsoft Excel

**General terms and conditions**

**Safeguarding**

Children and vulnerable adults must be safeguarded to the maximum possible extent from deliberate or inadvertent actions and failings that place them at risk of abuse, sexual exploitation, injury and any other harm. One of the ways that GOAL shows this on-going commitment to safeguarding is to include rigorous background and reference checks in the selection process for all candidates.

**Safeguarding Statement**  
GOAL has zero tolerance for safeguarding violations. All staff are expected to adhere to GOAL’s Code of Conduct and Safeguarding policies, including the prevention of sexual exploitation, abuse, and harassment (PSEAH). Recruitment is subject to safeguarding checks, including reference verification

**Accountability within GOAL**

- Report any concerns about the welfare of a child or vulnerable adult or any wrongdoings within our programming area.
- Report any concerns about inappropriate behavior of a GOAL staff or partner.

Due to the nature of GOAL’s work we aim to fill vacancies as quickly as possible. This means that we will close adverts as soon as we have found the right candidate and this may be before the published closing date. We would therefore advise interested applicants to submit an application as early as possible.*

**Thank you.**

jobs.title: Finance and Budget Officer, P4
source: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
jobs.body:
**Org. Setting and Reporting**

This position is located in the Budget and Finance Section (BFS), Executive Office (EO), Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) in New York. OCHA is the part of the United Nations Secretariat responsible for bringing together humanitarian actors to ensure a coherent response to emergencies. OCHA also ensures there is a framework within which each actor can contribute to the overall response effort. OCHA's mission is to mobilize and coordinate effective and principled humanitarian action in partnership with national and international actors in order to alleviate human suffering in disasters and emergencies; advocate the rights of people in need; promote preparedness and prevention and facilitate sustainable solutions. This temporary job opening is being advertised for the position of Finance and Budget Officer based in New York at UNHQ. Under the overall supervision of the Executive Officer, the Finance and Budget Officer reports directly to the Chief of Budget and Finance Section (BFS), who is based in New York.

**Responsibilities**

Within delegated authority, the Finance & Budget Officer will be responsible for the following duties: Programme Budget: • Reviews, analyses and finalizes the preparation of the Programme Plan Budget (PPB) and its revisions on the basis of Sub Programmes submissions, taking into account recommendations and decisions of specialized intergovernmental bodies. • Provides substantive support to relevant intergovernmental and expert bodies in their review of the PPB and its revisions; secures approval from the General Assembly. • Ensure legislative mandates are accurately translated into program budgets. • Liaises accordingly with relevant sections of the UN Controller’s office. Budget preparation: • Reviews, analyses and finalizes cost estimates and budget proposals, in terms of staff and non-staff requirements from Divisions/offices at headquarters and in the field. • Provides detailed input with respect to resource requirements for budget submissions. • Reviews, analyzes and finalizes program budget/financial implications of GA resolutions in light of additional mandates. • Provides substantive support to OCHA governance bodies in their budget review and approval processes. Budget administration: • Within delegation of authority, issues allotments, authorizes sub-allotments, including redeployment of funds when necessary, ensuring appropriate expenditures. • Manages and monitors budget implementation and recommends reallocation of funds as necessary. • Monitors expenditures to ensure that they remain within authorized levels. • Administers and monitors extra-budgetary resources, including review of agreements and cost plans, ensuring compliance with regulations and rules and established policies and procedures. • Prepares budget performance submissions. • Reviews and finalizes budget performance reports, analyzing variances between approved budgets and actual expenditures. • Provides substantive support to relevant intergovernmental and expert bodies and OCHA’s Budget Steering Committee. General • Provides advice and guidance, including training, to headquarters and field staff on budgetary and financial policies and procedures, including results-based budgeting. • Participates in inter-departmental meetings and/or technical survey missions on matters related to resource requirements, programming and budgetary issues. • Keeps up-to-date on documents/reports/guidelines that have a bearing on matters related to program budgets, ensuring compliance with intergovernmental recommendations and decisions as well as with United Nations policies and procedures. • Drafts reports for intergovernmental bodies and for management on budgetary issues, and correspondence. • Undertakes research and analysis of budgetary policies and procedures, makes recommendations for changes and/or modifications. • Acts as Approving Officer in accordance with United Nations Financial Rules and Regulations. • Ensures the integrity of financial and management systems and the controls that underpin them. • Represents OCHA Executive Office in inter and intra-departmental meetings. • May plan, organize, manage and supervise the work of the Unit assigned. • Collects and analyzes data to identify trends or patterns and provide insights through graphs, charts, tables and reports using data visualization methods to enable data-driven planning, decision-making, presentation and reporting. • Performs other duties as required.

**Competencies**

PROFESSIONALISM: Knowledge of financial and budgetary principles and practices, budget development and financial administration of resources. Ability to develop budgetary policies, procedures and new programmes. Ability to formulate new strategies and technical approaches to budgetary matters. Shows pride in work and in achievements; demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter; is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines and achieving results; is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns; shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges; remains calm in stressful situations. Takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work. Able to analyze and interpret data in support of decision-making and convey resulting information to management. PLANNING & ORGANIZING: Develops clear goals that are consistent with agreed strategies; identifies priority activities and assignments; adjusts priorities as required; allocates appropriate amount of time and resources for completing work; foresees risks and allows for contingencies when planning; monitors and adjusts plans and actions as necessary; uses time efficiently. ACCOUNTABILITY: Takes ownership of all responsibilities and honours commitments; delivers outputs for which one has responsibility within prescribed time, cost and quality standards; operates in compliance with organizational regulations and rules; supports subordinates, provides oversight and takes responsibility for delegated assignments; takes personal responsibility for his/her own shortcomings and those of the work unit, where applicable.

**Education**

Advanced university degree (Master’s degree or equivalent) in business administration, finance, or related field. A first-level university degree in combination with qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree.

**Job - Specific Qualification**

Successful completion of both degree and non-degree programs in data analytics, business analytics or data science programs is desirable.

**Work Experience**

A minimum of seven years of progressively responsible experience in finance, administration, budget, business administration or related area is required. Experience in working with trust funds, programme support costs, and the regular budget within a comparable international organization is required. Experience working with financial functions of an ERP (Enterprise Resources Planning) system - such as the Umoja Business Planning and Consolidation module - is required. Experience in directly supporting senior leadership during the presentation of budget proposals to legislative bodies is desirable. Experience in a management role supervising and coordinating a team working in budget and/or finance area is desirable.

**Languages**

English and French are the working languages of the United Nations Secretariat. For this job opening, English is required. The table below shows the minimum required level for each skill in these languages, according to the UN Language Framework (please consult [https://languages.un.org](https://languages.un.org/) for details).

## **Required Languages**

**LanguageReadingWritingListeningSpeaking**

**English**

UN Level III

UN Level III

UN Level III

**Assessment**

Evaluation of qualified candidates may include an assessment exercise which may be followed by a competency-based interview.

**Special Notice**

This position is temporarily available for a period of six (6) months. If the selected candidate is a staff member from the United Nations Secretariat, the selection will be administered as a temporary assignment. While this temporary assignment may provide the successful applicant with an opportunity to gain new work experience, the selection for this position is for a limited period and has no bearing on the future incumbency of the post. Subject to the funding source of the position, the eligibility for this temporary job opening may be limited to candidates based at the duty station. This temporary job opening may be limited to “internal candidates,” who have been recruited through a competitive examination administered according to staff rule 4.16 or staff selection process including the review of a central review body established according to staff rule 4.15. Staff members of the United Nations common system organizations who will reach the mandatory age of separation or retirement within the duration of the current temporary need period are not eligible to apply. Submitting an application or selection for the current temporary job opening does not delay or increase the mandatory age of separation. Retirees above the mandatory age of separation who wish to be considered for the current temporary job opening must indicate the reason for their last separation as "retirement." Such retirees shall not be employed by the Organization, unless (a) the operational requirements of the Organization cannot be met by staff members who are qualified and available to perform the required functions; and (b) the proposed employment would not adversely affect the career development or redeployment opportunities of other staff members and represents both a cost-effective and operationally sound solution to meet the needs of the service.

**United Nations Considerations**

According to article 101, paragraph 3, of the Charter of the United Nations, the paramount consideration in the employment of the staff is the necessity of securing the highest standards of efficiency, competence, and integrity. Candidates will not be considered for employment with the United Nations if they have committed violations of international human rights law, violations of international humanitarian law, sexual exploitation, sexual abuse, or sexual harassment, or if there are reasonable grounds to believe that they have been involved in the commission of any of these acts. The term “sexual exploitation” means any actual or attempted abuse of a position of vulnerability, differential power, or trust, for sexual purposes, including, but not limited to, profiting monetarily, socially or politically from the sexual exploitation of another. The term “sexual abuse” means the actual or threatened physical intrusion of a sexual nature, whether by force or under unequal or coercive conditions. The term “sexual harassment” means any unwelcome conduct of a sexual nature that might reasonably be expected or be perceived to cause offence or humiliation, when such conduct interferes with work, is made a condition of employment or creates an intimidating, hostile or offensive work environment, and when the gravity of the conduct warrants the termination of the perpetrator’s working relationship. Candidates who have committed crimes other than minor traffic offences may not be considered for employment. Due regard will be paid to the importance of recruiting the staff on as wide a geographical basis as possible. The United Nations places no restrictions on the eligibility of men and women to participate in any capacity and under conditions of equality in its principal and subsidiary organs. The United Nations Secretariat is a non-smoking environment. Reasonable accommodation may be provided to applicants with disabilities upon request, to support their participation in the recruitment process. By accepting a letter of appointment, staff members are subject to the authority of the Secretary-General, who may assign them to any of the activities or offices of the United Nations in accordance with staff regulation 1.2 (c). Further, staff members in the Professional and higher category up to and including the D-2 level and the Field Service category are normally required to move periodically to discharge functions in different duty stations under conditions established in ST/AI/2023/3 on Mobility, as may be amended or revised. This condition of service applies to all position specific job openings and does not apply to temporary positions. jobs.title: Nutrition & SBC Team leader (Syria - Hama )
jobs.body:
**Job Title: Nutrition & SBC Team leader**

**Job location: Syria – Hama**

**Reports to: Nutrition Coordinator**

**Job Style: Fulltime**

**JOB SUMMARY**

The team leader supports the Nutritionist and SBC in providing interventions, during emergency situations. Their responsibilities include Coordinate with internal and external stakeholders to coordinate the team's activities and facilitate their work during implementation, solve problems that arise in the field, maintaining records. Their role is crucial, to make sure that workflow is on truck.

**MAIN DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

The team leader for nutrition and mobile teams has the following responsibilities and duties:

• Lead the Field Nutrition and SBC Team in consultation with the Nutrition Coordinator in order to distribute tasks in the field and ensure adherence to the daily work plan.

• Solve problems that arise in the field with the Nutrition and SBC Team.

• Lead the Nutrition Team in the field after coordinating with the Nutrition coordinator according to an alternating schedule between the members of the supervised team to ensure leadership support and quality control.

• Coordinate the logistic needs of activities in accordance with the implementation plan, such as team cars, distributing nutrition materials, delivering to communities’ items related to the activities, coordinating the set-up and transportation of nutrition activity fixed point, or any other program needs.

**Technical tasks and coordination:**

• Coordinate with internal and external stakeholders to coordinate the team's activities and facilitate their work during implementation.

• Leading awareness campaigns in communities, providing advice, distributing brochures and vitamins, and referring patients to health centers or nutrition centers.

• Periodically update the nutrition and health services maps necessary for the referral process, and the links with other services and referral mechanisms, and share them with the Program Management.

• Coordinate referrals daily from the teams to treatment centers, health centers.

• Assist Nutrition Coordinator in evaluating the performance of the Nutrition Team and the quality of services provided. In addition to suggesting developments and suggesting new topics based on community and stakeholder feedback.

• Assist Nutrition Coordinator in developing key health messages in nutrition, reproductive health, hygiene, newborn care, etc. to the targeted beneficiaries, and making sure it is delivered appropriately.

• Assist Nutrition Coordinator in recognizing the evolving needs in the community, gaps in access to services, and trends among target populations relevant to program implementation.

**Reports:**

• Ensure that all relevant information is collected for reporting purposes in a timely manner and that nutrition workers collect required and relevant data from fieldwork.

• Verify the validity of the documents submitted in the lists of beneficiaries of the project in coordination and follow-up with Nutrition Coordinator.

• Submit reports on completed tasks as requested by the supervisor.

**Other:**

• Ensure that policies and guidelines as laid down in UITYD manuals and policies are always adhered to.

• Other related tasks at the request of the line manager.

**QUALIFICATIONS AND SKILLS**

Should have the following skills, education, and experience:

**Requirements (essential)**

• University or diploma degree or at least in the fourth year of university in a relevant field (nutrition, health, biomedical science, general science, or other related degrees)

• Minimum three years working experience of community nutrition activity within Syria.

**Requirements (desired)**

• Experience of leading the team in field visits within the field for at least one year.

• Preferred to have experience of community health related activities related to PLW (Pregnant and Lactating Woman) and children for at least one year.

• Participate in the distribution nutritional supplements provided to beneficiaries of the nutrition program for at least one round.

• Excellent computer skills, reporting and organizational skills and good time management.

• Strong communication skills.

• Good organizational and time management skills.

• The ability to work under pressure.

**ABOUT UITYD**

UITYD is a global humanitarian non-profit organization providing medical and health education services to people in need, including refugees and displaced persons, in disaster and underserved regions. The organization is composed of medical and public health professionals of diverse backgrounds.

**CODE OF CONDUCT**

UITYD Code of Conduct reflects the profession’s core set of beliefs and values of care, respect, trust, and integrity. These beliefs and values are fundamental to UITYD employees, volunteers, interns, consultants, and contractors to guide their practice and conduct. The Code is organized into categories, as follows:

1\. Always act with fairness, honesty, integrity, and openness; respect the opinions of others and treat all with equality and dignity without regard to gender, race, color, creed, ancestry, place of origin, political beliefs, religion, marital status, disability, age, or sexual orientation.

2\. Provide a positive and valued experience for those receiving service within and outside UITYD.

**CHILD PROTECTION POLICY**

Child abuse in all forms is unacceptable to UITYD, which recognizes its responsibility to protect children from harm in all areas of its work. UITYD is committed to ensuring a child-safe environment and is applying a zero-tolerance approach towards any kind of child abuse and exploitation.

**DISCRIMINATION, ABUSE AND HARASSMENT POLICY**

UITYD provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and expressly prohibits and will not tolerate any form of discrimination, abuse, harassment (sexual or otherwise), based upon race, ethnicity, religion, national origin, gender, age, marital status, citizenship status, disability, or military status. UITYD employees and related personnel must under no circumstances take part in any form of discrimination, harassment, or abuse (physical, sexual or verbal), intimidation or exploitation, or in any other way infringe the rights of others inside or outside the organization.

jobs.body:
**About Acted**

“We go the last mile. Founded in Afghanistan, against the backdrop of a forgotten crisis, Acted’s mission is to save lives and support people in meeting their needs in hard-to-reach areas. Millions of vulnerable people around the world need humanitarian assistance today, and hundreds of millions will need it tomorrow, in the face of the growing threat of climate change. We believe that our assistance must be conceptualised and delivered within the framework of people’s natural environments, and the territories on which they depend. Therefore, Acted pursues a triple mandate as a humanitarian, environmental and development aid actor, contributing to the relief, stabilisation, and recovery of crisis-affected people in fragile areas. This vision is guided by the motto “Think Local – Act Global” - reflecting the need to rely on a deep understanding of local territories and contexts to develop and implement actions based on local knowledge, structures and capacities. This local thinking contributes to a global response - running through all Acted programming and operations - as we work together towards the building of a 3ZERO world: a world with Zero Exclusion, Zero Carbon, and Zero Poverty”.

**Greening strategy:**

Acted’s greening strategy aims to tackle environmental degradation and climate change while meeting the needs of the most vulnerable who are often those most affected by the deepening environmental crisis. Each Acted employee will adhere to these principles through key green programming responsibilities:

• Contribute towards the adherence and development of the greening strategy plan.

• Explore innovative green programming opportunities and/or solutions within your realm of responsibilities and roles

• Encouraging and promoting environmental safeguarding processes and environmental programming standards in accordance with SOPs and technical guideline notes

**Acted PSEAH Policy:**

The Project Assistant-MSMC-CBP has the responsibility to adhere to the PSEAH Policy (Protection against Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment). Project Assistant-MSMC-CBP has the obligation to complete all mandatory trainings related to the Code of Conduct and the PSEA policy and report any safeguarding concern such as breaches of organisational policies or codes of conduct according to Acted’s procedures. Project Assistant-MSMC-CBP carries out work duties in a way that does not harm children, vulnerable adults or other staff or volunteers.

procedures.

**JOB PURPOSE**

The MSMC Community Mobilization Based Protection (CBP) Assistant supports the Community Mobilization Based Protection Officer in the implementation of the community mobilization activities in mobile response. This includes but is not limited to the development/implementation/follow-up of a Communication with Communities (CwC) scheme and the establishment/support to self-governance structures. The CBP Assistant will liaien and support the emergency committee meeting, coordinate with other actors and work on awareness session in the informal settlement, planning for event in Ils and CCs, work on focus group discussion and, support community mobilizer officer in his/her duties.

The CCCM CBP Assistant also provides support in the supervision of CCCM outreach workers in the implementation of the CwC/Self-governance activities.

If the need arises, management may ask the employee to support another camp or site (mobile) or another department from time to time.

**CHAIN OF COMMAND**

**Under the authority of:**

- CBP Officer
- MSMC team leader

**Line Management :**

- MSMC Outreach workers.

**WORKING RELATIONS**

## Internal:

- ## Other units of CCCM team
- ## HR department;
- ## Logistics for CCCM suppliers
- ## Finance for payments of outreach workers
- ## AME unit

External:

- IDPs in and out of the site;
- Humanitarian Partners (INGO/NGO; humanitarian agencies).
- Any other stakeholders inside or outside the camp except CA.

**OBJECTIVES**

- Support the Community Mobilization Based protection Officer in the development/implementation/follow-up of an effective Communication with Communities (CwC) Scheme and protection and women committees.
- Support the Community Mobilization Based protection Officer in establishment/support provision to self-governance structures in the Ils.
- Support in the management of the MSMC outreach workers;
- Support in the reporting of the CwC/Self-governance activities.
- Support in follow the health cases in coordination with health partners and the death incidents in the sites.
- Support in establishing the fire safety points, identifying the fire fighters, follow up the firefighting trainings and refilling the fire extinguishers.
- Support the CBPO in the support for other MSMC – WASH department and other partners.
- Support the CBPO in implementing initiatives and recreational and awareness activities in the sites.
- Responsibility of ComMob warehouse (physical inventory) and the monthly report.
- Support for monitoring all protection-related matters (i.e. identify services and gaps) in the camp and refer to CBPO copying MSMC team leader for follow-up with the relevant partner.
- Contribute to mainstream protection standards across all intervening partners’ programming and among the committee and MSMC Units
- Support for the identification, follow-up and referral of all cases at-risk and/or in need of protection services
- Support all camp residents and particularly women and girls to feel comfortable and safe to raise their concerns;
- Support and develop effective referral pathways in the camp with the support of your CBPO
- Report on all protection activities conducted to the CBPO
- Recommend follow-up actions to enhance meaningful engagements with communities especially women and youth.

**DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

- **Support implementation of an effective CwC scheme in identifying and monitoring the protection risks and concerns in the camp.**

- Support Community Mobilization Based Protection Officer (CBPO) in the management of CwC activities, including but not limited to: ensuring regular awareness messages and public information announcements to the community, preparing of topics and campaign material always analyzing with the protection prism.
- Engage actively the community in CwC activities such as, but not limited to, block to block messaging, FGD, and Campaigns, awareness and feedback sessions including session on protection issues.
- Ensure immediate action is taken to address camp residents request for information on service provided within the camp;
- Support the CMO in preparing/sharing with relevant stakeholders (i.e. actors active on site, regional coordination bodies, local authorities) monthly report on CwC activities in the camp, reporting on completed activities/challenges, communicating on planned ones and stress out potential gaps/foreseeable challenges;
- Support the CMO in the organization of sensitization, awareness campaigns and trainings for the community tailored to the needs and including proactive and reactive campaigns and in implementing safety and protection spot checks on site.
- Support the Protection Officer in conducting regular safety audits in coordination with protection actors in the camp.
- Outreach workers (i.e. attendance sheet signature, follow-up with finance…);
- Commitment to continuous learning through trainings and timely identification of capacity-building needs and opportunities, in coordination with the Community Mobilization Officer / CCCM Team Leader / HR department.
- Participate in the analysis of protection and safety risks on site, especially on safety risks affecting women and youth.

- **Support establishment and strengthening of governance structures**
- Support CBPO in management of self-governance activities, including preparing weekly plans, a schedule for community consultation on favored governance structures, organization of elections/appointment (if required) and draft site governance structure ToRs (if required). In the same time assess and monitor inclusiveness of governance committees and flag to Camp Manager if any issues are identified.
- Provide trainings to the appointed head of site governance structures (i.e. Humanitarian Principles, SPHERE Standards…);
- Facilitate the organization / monitor self- governance structures’ weekly meetings;
- Organize community-lead event in consultation with the heads of site governance structures and the wider camp population;
- Support the CBPO with reporting on the governance structure and CwC as required;
- Flag immediately any challenges/foreseen issues with the governance and CwC activities to the CBPO and Team Leader;
- Ensure accurate record keeping of project documentation, including photos, as requested by the CBPO.
- Participate in the facilitation of trainings and awareness sessions on protection

- **Ensure protection mainstreaming through the CwC/self-governance activities**

- Support and consider gender, protection, and GBV concerns in all aspects of activities;
- Adhere and Promote to Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse principles and guidelines (for site residents, ACTED staff, partner agencies)
- Support and promote participation of women, youth, and marginalized groups
- Refer immediately protection cases identified to the CBPO copying, the Snr Specialist Protection for referral to protection actors.
- **Supervise MSMC outreach workers:**

- Day to day supervision and management the MSMC Outreach workers (i.e. attendance sheet signature, follow-up with finance…);
- Commitment to continuous learning through training and timely identification of capacity-building needs and opportunities, in coordination with the Community Mobilization Officer / MSMC Team Leader / HR department.

- **Support in follow-up on health cases:**

- Day to day follow-up with KRC and health partners.
- Prepare a trucker for the health cases + death cases.
- Follow up on the fire tracker tools

- **Support in follow-up the sites incidents and fire safety points:**

- Support the CBPO in establishing fire safety points in the camp.
- Support the CBPO in choosing the fire fighters and ensure providing suitable trainings for them.
- Support the CBPO in the refilling of fire extinguishers process.
- Prepare truckers for refilling the fire extinguishers and fire incidents in the camp.
- Support the CMO in the fire safety campaign

**KEY PERFORMANCE INDICATORS**

Example, the key performance indicator (KPI) is a measurable value that demonstrates how effectively a company is achieving key business objectives. Organizations use KPIs to evaluate their success at reaching targets

- \#of training(s) completed with site governance structures;
- \# of community-lead events held in consultation with the population;
- \# of awareness campaigns implemented
- \# of FGDs facilitated to identify campaign topics and hot issues
- \# of women, youth, elderly and PWDs represented in governance structure and participating in FGDs and sensitization sessions
- \# of ORW attendance sheets duly filed
- \# of trainings conducted with ORWs
- \# of monthly tracker for health cases
- \# of monthly tracker for camp incidents and refilling the fire extinguishers.
- \# of monthly report + physical inventory report.
- \# of monthly attendance sheet for cleaners.
- of weekly Protection reports submitted to Protection Officer;
- \# percentage of protection cases effectively referred;

**QUALIFICATIONS**

**Required:**

- Bachelor’s degree.
- At least 6-months working experience in Information Management / administration of data using computers for an NGO (Nation or International)
- Proficient skills with the Microsoft Office Suite (Power Point)
- Experience interacting with external and internal partners;
- Fluency writing and speaking local language;
- Positive attitude and a willingness to learn;
- Ability to operate in a cross-cultural environment requiring flexibility;
- Ability to work independently;
- Strong attention to details;
- Interpersonal and communication Skills
- Does not reside in the camp
- Resides or able to reside in Deirzoir

**Preferred:**

- Degree with major in relevant field
- Translation skills (from Arabic to English and vice-versa);
- Certificate/Training in business management, accounting, or administration, database;

**Job Purpose**

The Field Monitor is responsible for tracking and monitoring project activities in the field to ensure interventions are implemented according to approved plans, quality standards, and beneficiary needs. The role includes conducting regular site visits, collecting and verifying program data, monitoring progress against targets, and documenting achievements, challenges, and lessons learned. They facilitate communication between communities and project teams by gathering feedback, complaints, and recommendations through established accountability mechanisms. Additionally, the Field Monitor prepares monitoring reports and provides timely information to support evidence-based decision-making and effective project implementation.

**Key Responsibilities**

1. Field Monitoring & Verification: Conduct regular site visits to the schools and health centers to monitor the progress of civil, structural, and finishing rehabilitation works (e.g., blockwork, plastering, tiling, painting, waterproofing) against the approved work plans, BoQs, and technical specifications.
2. Data Collection & Reporting: Collect, verify, and record accurate data on project activities, including executed quantities, daily labor, and material usage. Prepare timely and accurate monitoring reports detailing achievements, challenges, and lessons learned to support evidence-based decision-making.
3. Quality Assurance Support: Observe and report on the quality of materials delivered to the site (e.g., cement, steel, tiles, pipes) and the workmanship of the contractor. Witness basic site tests (e.g., concrete slump tests, compaction tests) and ensure works meet the required quality standards.
4. Beneficiary & Community Engagement: Support the verification of beneficiary needs and facilitate communication between the community (school staff, health center staff, and local representatives) and the project team. Gather feedback, complaints, and recommendations through established accountability mechanisms (e.g., help desks, community meetings).
5. Accountability & Transparency: Conduct post-implementation monitoring to ensure that the rehabilitated facilities are functional, safe, and meet the needs of the end-users. Ensure all project interventions are documented and visible to the community and stakeholders.
6. Coordination & Site Access: Coordinate with local authorities, community representatives, and contractors to facilitate smooth site access and implementation. Report any technical issues, delays, or non-conforming works to the Site Engineer and Project Officer immediately.
7. HSE Compliance Monitoring: Monitor and report on the contractor’s compliance with Health, Safety, and Environmental (HSE) procedures on-site, including proper waste management, dust control, and worker safety practices.
8. Documentation & Archiving: Maintain organized digital and physical records of all site visits, monitoring checklists, photos, and community feedback forms. Ensure all documentation is accurate and accessible for internal and external audits.
9. Perform any other related duties and responsibilities as assigned by the line manager within the scope of work.

**Note: The key responsibilities listed above are indicative and not exhaustive. Additional responsibilities may be assigned to the position in the future, depending on the organizational structure and management requirements.**

**Qualification (Education/Work Experience)**

**Essential Qualifications**

1. Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering or a related field.
2. At least 2 years of professional experience in supervising civil works, infrastructure, or construction projects.
3. Practical experience in field supervision of excavation works, concrete foundations, and contractor follow-up.
4. Good command of the English language.

**Desirable Qualifications**

1. Experience working in infrastructure rehabilitation projects, schools, or health centers.
2. Experience in reviewing Bills of Quantities (BoQs), drawings, and technical specifications, as well as measuring and accepting completed works.
3. Proficiency in AutoCAD and Microsoft Office applications.

**Core & Managerial Competencies**

1. **Core Competencies:**

- Communication
- Teamwork
- Planning and organizing
- Accountability
- Creativity
- Stakeholder Orientation
- Commitment to Continuous Learning
- Technological Awareness.

1. **Supervisor/Managerial Competencies:**

- Leadership
- Building Trust
- Vision
- Managing Performance
- Empowering Others
- Judgment/Decision-making.

1. **Technical Competencies:**

- Good knowledge of excavation works, preparation of foundation pits, and casting and construction of concrete foundations.
- Ability to read and interpret drawings, Bills of Quantities (BoQs), and technical specifications, and compare them with the actual implementation on site.
- Good knowledge of civil works quality control methods and monitoring of executed quantities.
- Ability to follow up with contractors, document technical observations, and monitor the implementation of corrective actions.
- Good skills in report writing and field documentation.
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Word, Excel, and Outlook.

**Compliance to Anti-Harassment, PSEA, and Child Safeguarding**

- Child abuse in all forms is unacceptable to IYD, which recognizes its responsibility to protect children from harm in all areas of its work. IYD is committed to ensuring a child-safe environment and is applying a zero-tolerance approach towards any kind of child abuse and exploitation.
- IYD employees and related personnel must not under any circumstances take part in any form of discrimination, harassment, or abuse (physical, sexual or verbal), intimidation or exploitation, or in any other way infringe the rights of others inside or outside IYD.
