jobs.title: Heya-015 Selection Sub-Committee (SSC) – Beneficiary Selection
jobs.body:
**Project: Women in Innovation from HBB to Scalable Business – Heya**

**Commissioning Organization: Plan International**

**Locations: Irbid Governorate, Azraq Camp and Remotely**

**Expected Period: November 2026 – May 2027**

## 1. Background

This Terms of Reference (ToR) is developed within the framework of the “Women in Innovation from HBB to Scalable Business – Heya” EU-funded project, implemented by RSS/iPARK in partnership with Plan International, RSCN, and DMDT in Jordan.

The action aims to address unemployment and limited economic opportunities among vulnerable populations, with a particular focus on women in underserved and rural areas. The project’s overall objective is to foster sustainable employment through entrepreneurship by equipping participants with technical, business, and life skills, and by supporting viable business initiatives. It combines capacity-building interventions – including basic and advanced entrepreneurship training, coaching, and mentoring – with business grants to enable participants to establish or expand income-generating activities.

Plan International is responsible for project activities in Irbid Governorate and Azraq Camp, targeting 900 participants for training, with 165 selected entrepreneurs receiving business grants. The project’s capacity-building component comprises:

- Foundational Entrepreneurship & Soft Skills Training (Basic Level) – targeting 900 women across 36 groups.
- Advanced Entrepreneurial Training (Boot Camp) – targeting 450 high-potential women across 15 groups.
- Hackathon – targeting 450 women as part of the Advanced stage, following the Boot Camp.
- Business Grants – awarded to 165 selected entrepreneurs based on predefined eligibility and performance criteria.

To ensure a transparent, fair, and merit-based selection of beneficiaries at each project stage, a Selection Sub-Committee (SSC) will be established under the oversight of the Selection and Coordination Committee (SCC). The SSC will be responsible for the actual screening, assessment, and selection of participants and grant recipients, using the tools and methodology approved by the SCC.

## 2. Purpose of the Sub-Committee

The Selection Sub-Committee (SSC) is established to carry out the operational selection of beneficiaries across all project stages. Operating within the framework validated by the SCC, the SSC is responsible for:

- Applying the approved eligibility criteria, scoring matrices, and evaluation tools to screen and assess applicants at each project stage.
- Conducting fair, transparent, and merit-based selection of participants for the Basic Training, the Advanced Stage (Boot Camp and Hackathon), and Business Grants.
- Documenting selection decisions and maintaining records of all assessments in line with Plan International’s accountability and reporting standards.
- Escalating any ambiguities, conflicts of interest, or edge cases to the SCC for guidance and resolution.

## 3. Composition

The SSC will be composed of three voting members, always an odd number to avoid tied decisions. Gender balance will be maintained with a preference for female representation: of the three voting members, two will be female and one will be male.

Membership will include:

- A representative from Plan International (Chairing role – observer, non-voting; not counted among the three voting members).
- Technical experts or sectoral specialists relevant to the applicant pool and business type (e.g., green technology, agriculture, industry); and/or
- A representative from the private sector or a community/youth representative, as appropriate.

## 4. Roles and Responsibilities

The SSC is responsible for the following:

**Beneficiary Screening and Selection:**

- Review and assess applications against the eligibility criteria and scoring matrices approved by the selection and coordination committee (SCC).
- Conduct individual or group assessments, interviews, or due diligence checks as required by the approved methodology.
- Score applicants objectively and consistently, using the standardized scoring tools provided.
- Where applications are divided between members (selection for the Advanced Stage, and ranking after the Advanced Stage), hold a calibration session before scoring: all three members independently score the same sample of applications (e.g. 10), compare results, and agree on how to apply the criteria. After scoring, hold a moderation meeting to review borderline cases around the cut-off point and to cross-check a random sample (e.g. 10%) of each member’s scores, so that rankings are comparable across members.
- Produce ranked shortlists and final selection lists for each project stage (selection for the Advanced Stage (Boot Camp and Hackathon), ranking after the Advanced Stage, and Business Grants).
- Provide the scoring records and any clarification requested by the Plan International focal point in relation to appeals or review requests.

**Appeals and Review Process**

Applicants who are not selected at any stage will be notified of the outcome and have the right to request a review of the decision. Review requests may be submitted in any form — in writing, over the phone, or through any other communication channel with Plan International (e.g., project team, hotline) — stating the reason for the request. Review requests will be reviewed by the Plan International focal point, who decides whether to keep the appeal open (and the follow-up action required) or to close it, and informs the applicant of the outcome. The SSC does not decide on appeals; it only provides the scoring records and clarifications requested.

**Documentation and Reporting:**

- Maintain complete and accurate records of all assessments, scores, and selection decisions.
- Flag and document any cases requiring exceptional handling or escalation.

**Compliance and Accountability:**

- Ensure all selection activities adhere to the principles of transparency, fairness, non-discrimination, and accountability.
- Comply with Plan International’s Safeguarding Policy, Code of Conduct, and data protection requirements throughout the selection process.
- Declare any conflict of interest prior to reviewing specific applicants and recuse accordingly.

## 5. Scope of Work

The SSC will operate across the following selection phases, corresponding to the project’s activity cycle:

**Selection Stage: From Basic stage to the Boot Camp (Advanced stage) Selection**

**Target Group: To evaluate 900 applications and select the best 450 applications**

**SSC Activity: Assess Basic Training graduates using the approved selection criteria and scoring matrix; select top 50% of the participants.**

**Workload per member (3 members): 300 applications per member (900 ÷ 3)**

**Location: Remotely**

**Selection Stage: After the Advanced stage (Boot Camp and Hackathon)**

**Target Group: To evaluate 450 applications and rank them top to bottom**

**SSC Activity: Score 450 applications to create a prioritization list for the grant stage.**

**Workload per member (3 members): 150 applications per member (450 ÷ 3)**

**Location: Remotely**

**Selection Stage: Business Grant Selection**

**Target Group: To evaluate at least 250 grant applications and select the top 165 entrepreneurs (grant recipients)**

**SSC Activity: Evaluate grant applications using the approved scoring matrix, pitching and due diligence framework; produce ranked shortlists.**

**Workload per member (3 members): All applications (at least 250), each reviewed by all 3 members (not divided)**

**Location: Irbid and Azraq Camp**

Applications in the first two stages (selection for the Advanced Stage, and ranking after it) are divided equally between the three SSC members; grant applications are not divided and are reviewed by all three members. Scores of divided applications are calibrated and moderated as described in Section 4. Additional SSC meetings may be convened to address re-assessments or clarifications requested by the Plan International focal point arising during any selection phase.

## 6. Decision-Making Process

The decision-making process below applies to the Business Grant Selection, where all three members score every application and the decision is based on the sum of their scores. In the first two stages, applications are divided between members and scored individually; selection follows the ranked scores after calibration and moderation (Section 4), without a committee vote.

- Each application is scored independently by all three members using the approved scoring matrix.
- The final decision for each application is based on the sum of the scores awarded by the three members. Applications are ranked by total score, and the top-ranked applications are selected up to the number of grants available.
- If applications have equal total scores at the cut-off point, the matter shall be escalated to the SCC for decision.
- Members must declare any conflict of interest prior to reviewing specific applicants and must recuse themselves from related scoring and decisions.
- Individual scoring sheets, the consolidated total scores and the final ranked list (together with minutes of any joint sessions) will be documented, signed by the members, and submitted to Plan International.

## 7. Selection Schedule

Members will carry out their individual scoring independently within each selection phase. The SSC will convene jointly for calibration and moderation sessions, grant selection decisions, and appeals or clarifications, as required. The indicative schedule is as follows:

**Phase: Advanced Stage Selection (Boot Camp)**

**Indicative date November 2026**

**Estimated timeline: November – December 2026**

**Phase: Advanced Stage Ranking (after Boot Camp and Hackathon)**

**Indicative date: January 2027**

**Estimated timeline: January 2027**

**Phase: Business Grant Selection**

**Indicative date: March 2027**

**Estimated timeline: March – April 2027**

## 8. Qualifications for SSC Members

All SSC members are external to Plan International and should meet the following criteria:

**Core (Mandatory):**

- Minimum 3 years of professional experience in a relevant field (e.g., entrepreneurship, business development, green technology, agriculture, industry, or labour market).
- Demonstrated experience in assessment, evaluation, or selection processes (grants, business plans, or project applications).
- Strong understanding of women's economic empowerment, entrepreneurship ecosystems, and/or labour market dynamics in Jordan.
- Ability to assess applications objectively and contribute professionally to a merit-based, transparent selection process.
- No commercial, financial, or personal relationship with any applicant under consideration in the selection round. Members must sign a conflict-of-interest declaration prior to each selection stage, disclosing any relationship with applicants, and must recuse themselves from scoring or discussing any application where such a relationship exists.

**Preferred:**

- Knowledge of challenges faced by the target population (women in rural areas, refugees, caregivers, women with disabilities).
- Experience working with Plan International or other INGOs in Jordan is an asset.

**Personal Competencies:**

- High level of integrity, impartiality, and professional ethics.
- Strong analytical, communication, and interpersonal skills.
- Ability to maintain strict confidentiality and manage conflict of interest situations appropriately.

## 10. Confidentiality and Conflict of Interest

- All SSC members must maintain strict confidentiality regarding applicant information, selection outcomes, and all deliberations of the committee.
- Members must declare any conflict of interest – including personal, professional, or financial relationships with applicants – before each selection session and must recuse themselves from related decisions.

## 11. Ethical and Safeguarding Statements

Plan International is committed to ensuring the rights, dignity, and safety of all participants throughout the selection process. All SSC members will be required to read, understand, and sign Plan International’s Code of Conduct and Safeguarding Policy prior to participating in any selection activity. The SSC will conduct all activities in accordance with Plan International’s Ethical MERL Framework, GDPR principles, and the project’s data protection protocols.

## 12. Duration

The SSC will be active from November 2026 through April 2027, covering all selection phases of the project. The committee will remain available for subsequent rounds of selection if applicable, or if appeals, complaints, or clarifications require its input.

## 13.Evaluation Criteria

- Applications will be evaluated according to the following criteria:
- CV and cover letter (Relevant professional experience)-25%
- Assessment, evaluation or selection experience- 10%
- Understanding of women’s economic empowerment and the labour market in Jordan- 15%
- Knowledge of the target population in Irbid and Azraq Camp, plus INGO or donor-funded experience- 15%
- Financial proposal (cost) - 30%
- Gender responsive- 5%

Plan International defines a gender-responsive business as one that meets criteria for integrating gender equality and women’s empowerment principles in its policies and practices, and which is aligned to international norms and standards. This could be: a. Women-owned business:

1. legal entity in any field that is more than 51% owned, managed and controlled by one or more women.
2. Women-led business: A legal entity in any field that has a minimum of 50% women representation in management with senior-level, strategic decision-making capabilities.

Gender-responsive business: Legal entity that actively promotes gender equality and empowerment of women and young women through their policies and labor practices

**About Acted**

“We go the last mile. Founded in Afghanistan, against the backdrop of a forgotten crisis, Acted’s mission is to save lives and support people in meeting their needs in hard-to-reach areas. Millions of vulnerable people around the world need humanitarian assistance today, and hundreds of millions will need it tomorrow, in the face of the growing threat of climate change. We believe that our assistance must be conceptualised and delivered within the framework of people’s natural environments, and the territories on which they depend. Therefore, Acted pursues a triple mandate as a humanitarian, environmental and development aid actor, contributing to the relief, stabilisation, and recovery of crisis-affected people in fragile areas. This vision is guided by the motto “Think Local – Act Global” - reflecting the need to rely on a deep understanding of local territories and contexts to develop and implement actions based on local knowledge, structures and capacities. This local thinking contributes to a global response - running through all Acted programming and operations - as we work together towards the building of a 3ZERO world: a world with Zero Exclusion, Zero Carbon, and Zero Poverty”.

**Greening strategy:**

Acted’s greening strategy aims to tackle environmental degradation and climate change while meeting the needs of the most vulnerable who are often those most affected by the deepening environmental crisis. Each Acted employee will adhere to these principles through key green programming responsibilities:

• Contribute towards the adherence and development of the greening strategy plan.

• Explore innovative green programming opportunities and/or solutions within your realm of responsibilities and roles

• Encouraging and promoting environmental safeguarding processes and environmental programming standards in accordance with SOPs and technical guideline notes

**Acted PSEAH Policy:**

**About Acted**

“We go the last mile. Founded in Afghanistan, against the backdrop of a forgotten crisis, Acted’s mission is to save lives and support people in meeting their needs in hard-to-reach areas. Millions of vulnerable people around the world need humanitarian assistance today, and hundreds of millions will need it tomorrow, in the face of the growing threat of climate change. We believe that our assistance must be conceptualised and delivered within the framework of people’s natural environments, and the territories on which they depend. Therefore, Acted pursues a triple mandate as a humanitarian, environmental and development aid actor, contributing to the relief, stabilisation, and recovery of crisis-affected people in fragile areas. This vision is guided by the motto “Think Local – Act Global” - reflecting the need to rely on a deep understanding of local territories and contexts to develop and implement actions based on local knowledge, structures and capacities. This local thinking contributes to a global response - running through all Acted programming and operations - as we work together towards the building of a 3ZERO world: a world with Zero Exclusion, Zero Carbon, and Zero Poverty”.

**Greening strategy:**

Acted’s greening strategy aims to tackle environmental degradation and climate change while meeting the needs of the most vulnerable who are often those most affected by the deepening environmental crisis. Each Acted employee will adhere to these principles through key green programming responsibilities:

• Explore innovative green programming opportunities and/or solutions within your realm of responsibilities and roles

jobs.body:
**Terms of Reference (TOR)**

**Recruitment of a Pool of Short-Term Data Collection Enumeratorsa**

**Organization:** ActionAid Arab Region (AAAR)  
**Duty Station:** AAAR Home Office, Amman, Jordan  
**Number of Enumerators:** tentative  
**Duration:** Approximately 7–10 working days per assignment, depending on operational needs  
**Compensation:** 15 JOD per working day

**1. Background**

ActionAid Arab Region (AAAR) works with local partners across the Arab region to implement development and humanitarian programmes. As part of its commitment to programme quality, accountability, and evidence-based decision-making, AAAR regularly conducts monitoring activities and data collection exercises across its projects.

AAAR is seeking to recruit short-term enumerators based in Jordan to support data collection assignments under different projects and programmes. The recruitment is intended to establish a pool of enumerators who can be engaged as needed for short-term assignments. The nature, duration, and volume of work will vary depending on programme requirements.

**2. Purpose of the Assignment**

The enumerators will support AAAR's Programme Quality, Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (PQMEAL) Unit in collecting reliable, accurate, and timely data to inform programme monitoring, accountability, and learning.

Assignments may include telephone surveys, Post-Distribution Monitoring (PDM), Key Informant Interviews (KIIs), beneficiary feedback surveys, and other monitoring and data collection activities as required.

**3. Scope of Work and Responsibilities**

Under the guidance of the PQMEAL Unit, the enumerators will be responsible for:

- Conducting telephone surveys with project participants and other relevant respondents.
- Conducting Key Informant Interviews (KIIs) and other interviews, as assigned.
- Using data collection tools and questionnaires provided by AAAR, including digital tools where applicable.
- Following the approved methodology, sampling procedures, and interview protocols.
- Recording responses accurately, completely, and objectively.
- Conducting follow-up calls and documenting call outcomes where required.
- Respecting respondents' informed consent, confidentiality, privacy, and voluntary participation.
- Applying safeguarding, protection, and data protection principles throughout the data collection process.
- Reporting progress, challenges, and any issues encountered during data collection to the designated PQMEAL focal point.
- Meeting agreed daily targets and assignment deadlines while maintaining data quality.
- Participating in briefings and training sessions before each assignment, as required.

The enumerators will not be responsible for developing methodologies, designing data collection tools, analysing data, or preparing reports. These tasks will be managed by AAAR's PQMEAL Unit.

**4. Location and Duration**

The work will be conducted from the **AAAR home office in Amman, Jordan**. Enumerators must be based in Jordan and available to work from the designated office during their assigned working days.

The expected duration is approximately **7–10 working days per assignment**, depending on the volume and nature of the data collection required. The actual duration and working schedule will be communicated before each assignment. Engagement will be on a short-term, as-needed basis, and continuous work is not guaranteed.

**5. Required Qualifications and Experience**

Applicants should meet the following requirements:

- Be based in Jordan and available to work from AAAR's office in Amman.
- Have a university degree or be currently enrolled in a relevant university programme; applicants from other academic backgrounds with relevant experience may also be considered.
- Have excellent Arabic communication skills, with the ability to communicate professionally and respectfully with diverse respondents.
- Have good English comprehension and communication skills.
- Be comfortable using smartphones, computers, and digital data collection tools.
- Demonstrate strong communication, listening, and interpersonal skills.
- Be detail-oriented, reliable, organised, and able to meet deadlines.
- Be committed to confidentiality, informed consent, safeguarding, and ethical data collection.
- Be available for short-term assignments on relatively short notice.

Previous experience using KoboToolbox, ODK, or similar data collection platforms is an advantage.

**6. Compensation**

Selected enumerators will receive **15 JOD per working day** for the days worked and agreed upon with AAAR.

The expected engagement is 7–10 working days per assignment, equivalent to **105–150 JOD per enumerator** for a full assignment of this duration.

Any additional costs, including telephone credit or SIM cards, will be addressed separately by AAAR where applicable and communicated before the assignment begins.

**7. Supervision and Reporting**

Enumerators will report to the designated focal point within AAAR's PQMEAL Unit. They will receive the necessary orientation, data collection tools, instructions, and quality requirements before commencing each assignment.

**8. Application Process**

Interested candidates are invited to submit their CV, highlighting relevant data collection, research, or interview experience, along with their contact information and availability.

Applications should be submitted to **\[ari.jobs@actionaid.org\]** by **\[2/11/2026\]**, using the subject line: *Application – Short-Term Data Collection Enumerator*.

Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. Selection will be based on relevant experience, communication skills, availability, and suitability for short-term data collection assignments.

ActionAid Arab Region is committed to safeguarding and expects all enumerators to uphold its values and relevant policies, including safeguarding, confidentiality, and ethical conduct throughout their engagement.

jobs.title: Consultancy - Mid-Term External Assessment. Project: Strengthening Legal Accountability and Inclusive Justice in South-East Asia
jobs.body:
**Background**

The International Commission of Jurists (ICJ) is seeking qualified applicants to conduct a mid-term assessment for its project on strengthening legal Accountability and inclusive justice in South-East Asia.

The project focuses on four interconnected result areas:

1. Strengthening legal aid provision.
2. Enhancing justice systems in project locations
3. Supporting gender-inclusive transitional justice and peacebuilding processes.
4. Strengthening international advocacy and accountability efforts.

As outlined in the project MEL Strategy, an independent assessment will be conducted at the project's midpoint to review progress against the approved logframe, assess implementation effectiveness, generate learning, and provide recommendations for the remaining implementation period.

- **Overview of the ICJ**

Composed of 60 eminent judges and lawyers from all regions of the world, the ICJ promotes and protects human rights through the rule of law, by using its unique legal expertise to develop and strengthen national and international justice systems. Established in 1952 and active on the five continents, the ICJ aims to ensure the progressive development and effective implementation of international human rights and international humanitarian law; secure the realization of civil, cultural, economic, political and social rights; safeguard the separation of powers; and guarantee the independence of the judiciary and legal profession.

- **Purpose of the Assessment**

The purpose of the mid-term assessment is to:

- Assess progress towards achieving project outputs and intended outcomes
- Review the effectiveness, efficiency, relevance, and adaptability of project implementation
- Assess the extent to which project activities are contributing to improved justice and accountability efforts
- Review safeguarding, security, gender, and inclusion measures taken by project interventions
- Identify lessons learned, good practices, and implementation challenges
- Generate practical recommendations for strengthening implementation during Year 2 and Year 3
- **Scope of Work**

The assessment shall cover all project activities implemented during the first 15–18 months, including:

The assessment will cover project implementation during approximately the first 15–18 months, examining progress towards expected results, key achievements, implementation challenges and outstanding activities. It will consider the effectiveness and quality of activities aimed at strengthening the capacity of legal and justice actors, supporting access to justice and human rights protection, building knowledge and skills on relevant legal and policy issues, and contributing to research, analysis, advocacy and engagement with relevant stakeholders. The assessment will also review the quality, relevance and progress of key project outputs and deliverables, including capacity-building activities, technical resources, legal and policy analysis, and other project-supported initiatives.

- **Key Assessment Questions**

Relevance

- Is the project responding to the priority of justice needs identified by legal practitioners, survivors, and justice actors?
- Do project interventions remain relevant in the relevant country’s evolving political and security context?
- Are the selected implementation approaches appropriate for project operating environments?

Effectiveness

- To what extent have planned outputs been achieved?
- Have legal practitioners increased their capacity in documentation, fair-trial standards, and accountability mechanisms?
- Are trained practitioners applying acquired knowledge in legal aid, documentation, or advocacy work?

Sustainability

- Which project approaches and capacities are likely to remain after project completion?
- Are local actors developing sufficient ownership of project processes and outcomes?
- **Methodology**

The consultant should use a mixed-methods approach consistent with the project's security-sensitive MEL framework. The ICJ’s Regional Director for Asia and Pacific Programme (Project Lead) and MEL Officer will review the methodology proposed by the evaluator. Ideally, it will include (i) a desk review of pertinent project documents and records (including the project proposal, logical framework, amended project documents, quarterly reports, intermediate evaluation, and various records containing monitoring data); (ii) primary data collection (remote and in-person). The primary data should involve mixed quantitative and qualitative research methods – including but not limited to interviews with project staffs, project partners, targeted CSO, event participants, lawyers and other target groups, quantitative survey with project beneficiaries.

- **Evaluation Implementation**

The evaluation should take place in November – December 2026 with the final deliverables due and contract concluding by **23 December 2026.**

The ICJ staff will provide logistical and technical support as appropriate throughout the evaluation process (compilation of project documents, assisting with scheduling meetings / interviews if desired, etc.).

A total of up to 22 working days (depending on national holidays in the incumbent’s country) will be available for:

- *Evaluation preparation* (including finalizing the evaluation methodology, performing the initial desk review of project materials, creating and testing data collection tools, compiling a brief inception note);
- Remote and in-person data collection;
- *Data analysis and synthesis*(including transcription, data aggregation, writing a draft report, presenting findings to the ICJ, and incorporating feedback from the ICJ into a final report).
- **Deliverables**

**Deliverable 1:** Inception Report

The Inception Report will set out the overall approach and methodology for the mid-term assessment and will include:

- Detailed assessment methodology;
- Assessment matrix;
- Data collection tools; and
- Detailed workplan and timeline.

**Deliverable 2:** Preliminary Findings Presentation

A virtual presentation of the preliminary findings to ICJ management and the project team, providing an opportunity to discuss emerging findings and obtain initial feedback.

**Deliverable 3:** Draft Mid-Term Assessment Report

A Draft Mid-Term Assessment Report presenting the findings, conclusions and recommendations of the assessment. The report should be maximum of 30–40 pages excluding annexes.

**Deliverable 4:** Final Mid-Term Assessment Report

A Final Mid-Term Assessment Report incorporating and responding to comments and feedback provided by the ICJ on the draft report.

jobs.title: IT Officer - Horn of Africa (Somali nationals)
jobs.body:
**Organisation Background**

Founded in 2011, the International NGO Safety Organization (INSO) is an international NGO that supports humanitarian aid workers by establishing safety coordination platforms in insecure contexts. INSO provides registered NGOs with a range of free services, including real-time incident tracking, analytical reports, safety-related data and mapping, crisis management support, staff orientations, and training. INSO provides daily support to more than 1,500 NGOs operating in 24 of the world’s most insecure countries. INSO is registered in the Netherlands, with its headquarters located in The Hague, a city renowned for its international focus on peace and justice.

**INSO Horn of Africa (HOA)**

HOA was launched in 2019 as a regional entity and is based in Hargeisa, Somaliland, coordinating and supporting INSO’s activities in Kenya, Somalia, and Somaliland.

We are now hiring an IT Officer, Horn of Africa. This position is based in Hargeisa, Somaliland with travel to Kenya and Somalia

**Job Summary**

Reporting to the Operations Manager, Horn of Africa, you will be responsible for providing high-level IT and application support to INSO Kenya and Somalia offices. You will coordinate with Headquarters’ IT department to administer IT services such as INSO’s Office 365 and Exchange Online accounts, Adobe, ArcGIS Licensing, and internet maintenance and troubleshooting.

You will assist the Operations Manager in delivering a first-class support service to INSO staff and offices, acting primarily in a first-line support capacity, resolving issues in person, over the phone, or via remote connectivity.

**Main Responsibilities**

- Install and configure computer operating systems, printers, networks, and applications per INSO policy and guidelines.
- Monitor and maintain INSO’s network performance.
- Troubleshoot hardware and software issues in person, remotely, and via phone.
- Ensure all INSO users have access to all relevant licensed software, including Adobe, MS Office, and GIS software via the HQ IT Team.
- Update and manage INSO SharePoint’s folders and permission structure.
- Ensure procurement of IT equipment meets INSO’s global standards.
- Ensure IT equipment is updated in the asset database and stock in cooperation with the logistics officer.
- Work closely with colleagues to understand and respond to their IT needs.
- Provide IT training for newly hired staff.
- Coordinate with the Headquarters IT team to roll out and assist in maintaining new applications and technologies.
- Develop tutorials for local staff in relation to INSO applications and software.
- Assist the Operations Manager in preparing IT budgets.
- Assess the security threat to INSO’s IT systems and ensure it is appropriately mitigated.
- Monitor usage, renewal, and billing aspects of all third-party applications and report to the Operations Manager in case of required renewals.
- Perform other duties as required.

**Mandatory Requirements**

- Minimum 3 years of experience supporting IT services in a medium to large internationally focused organisation
- Extensive experience with Windows operating systems and other Microsoft technologies such as Office 365 applications, Exchange Online, Microsoft Intune, and SharePoint Online.
- Knowledge of local network management.
- Familiarity with ArcGIS and Adobe (licensing and installation).
- Fluent in written and spoken English and Somali.
- Degree or equivalent in Information Technology, Computer Science, or relevant field.

*Nice to Have:*

- Master’s in IT or similar
- Microsoft certificates
- Somali language
- NGO experience
- Experience in Remote support

**Core Competencies**

- Problem-Solving – Identifies issues, analyzes root causes, and contributes to effective and practical solutions.
- Communication – Conveys information clearly and professionally while maintaining strong organizational coordination.
- Interpersonal – Builds productive relationships through active listening, effective questioning, and confident stakeholder engagement.
- Diligence – Demonstrates understanding and application of humanitarian principles, values, and operational practices.
- Accountability – Works independently, meets deadlines, takes ownership of responsibilities, and maintains strict confidentiality of information.

**INSO’s Safeguarding Policy**

INSO is fully committed to safe recruitment, selection and vetting of all potential new staff, trustees and volunteers. We ensure rigorous compliance with our Code of Conduct and Safeguarding Policy throughout the recruitment process. INSO is a member of the Misconduct Disclosure Scheme, and the selected candidate will be required to undergo the relevant misconduct disclosure checks as part of the final hiring steps.

jobs.title: VA26P074V02 Modernisation Officer – AI and Automation (IP3)
source: International Centre for Migration Policy Development
jobs.body:
*Note: Please note that this vacancy has been republished. Applicants who have already submitted an application do not need to reapply.* ​

Within ICMPD’s Mediterranean operations, the Modernisation Officer - AI and Automation contributes to the integration of AI enabled and automation solutions across regional portfolios and projects, including those delivered through field offices in Jordan, Lebanon, Libya and Tunisia. ​

The position focuses on supporting the implementation of fit-for-purpose automation, analytics, and digital workflows across projects, contributing to quality, timeliness, compliance, and resource efficiency within defined project scopes and operational priorities.

## **Functional Overview**

Within ICMPD's Mediterranean operations, the Modernisation Officer - AI and Automation contributes to the integration of AI enabled and automation solutions across regional portfolios and projects, including those delivered through field offices in Jordan, Lebanon, Libya and Tunisia. Working under the overall supervision of the Regional Portfolio Manager, and in close coordination with Portfolio Managers, Project Managers, and relevant HQ counterparts, the position supports the application of regional modernisation priorities within project delivery, ensuring alignment with organisational standards, policies, and operational requirements.​

The role focuses on supporting the identification, assessment, design, and implementation of fit for purpose AI enabled and automation solutions across projects in the region, contributing to quality, timeliness, compliance, and resource efficiency within defined project scopes and operational priorities. The position contributes to the development and implementation of project level solutions and outputs related to automation, knowledge retrieval approaches, delivery checklists, basic analytics and dashboards, results evidence pipelines, document workflows, and translation or proofreading support. This includes gathering and analysing requirements, facilitating stakeholder inputs, assessing solution options, including third party tools where relevant, and coordinating implementation with delivery teams, with a focus on practical and scalable outputs.

The incumbent contributes to the responsible and secure application of AI and automation in line with institutional data protection and information security requirements and with relevant principles of responsible AI, including human oversight, transparency, risk awareness, and inclusion, applying existing organisational frameworks and guidance. Where relevant and within approved project objectives, the position also provides technical support to project activities involving partner country institutions in the area of digitalisation and innovation, helping to ensure that solutions are context appropriate, practical, and sustainable.

## **Key Results**

**Coordinated Project Level AI and Automation Support:** Project teams across the Mediterranean region are supported in identifying, assessing, and advancing AI enabled and automation solutions that respond to operational needs and project delivery requirements. Project level initiatives are coordinated in line with regional priorities and organisational standards, contributing to coherence, reduced duplication, and more efficient implementation. Solutions and practices with potential for wider use are documented and shared for possible adaptation across projects where appropriate.

**Fit for Purpose Digital Solutions for Project Delivery:** Technical support is provided for the development, adaptation, and rollout of digital tools, dashboards, workflow solutions, and related delivery support mechanisms within approved project scopes. Requirements, use cases, and implementation considerations are analysed and translated into practical proposals and solution options. The operation of systems, processes, and project activities is strengthened through solutions that are feasible, user oriented, and aligned with delivery needs.​

**Responsible AI and Risk Aware Implementation:** AI and automation related initiatives are supported with appropriate consideration for privacy, information security, human oversight, transparency, and operational risk. Risks related to data sensitivity, misuse, bias, and vendor or platform dependency are identified, flagged, and addressed through practical mitigation measures within existing organisational frameworks. Project teams are supported in applying available guidance and controls to strengthen compliant and responsible adoption.

**Capacity Development and Knowledge Sharing:** Guidance notes, SOPs, templates, toolkits, and user aids are developed and maintained to support consistent implementation of modernised delivery practices across the region. Good practices and lessons learned from project implementation are captured and shared through established channels to support replication and organisational learning. Relevant project teams and stakeholders are supported through targeted training, practical guidance, and on the job assistance to strengthen adoption and effective use of AI and automation solutions.

## **Required Expertise**

- Strong analytical and conceptual skills, with the ability to support the application of AI enabled and automation approaches in project delivery and operational processes.
- Demonstrated expertise in AI, automation, digitalisation, or related methodologies, including awareness of associated operational, reputational, and governance risks.
- Proven ability to analyse delivery processes, identify improvement or automation opportunities, and contribute to practical and reusable solutions within programme and project contexts.
- Experience in gathering requirements, assessing user needs, and supporting the design and implementation of digital tools, workflows, or system improvements.
- Ability to assess and compare digital and AI related solutions, including third party tools where relevant, and to contribute to defining requirements, use cases, acceptance criteria, and implementation safeguards.
- Sound understanding of data governance, information management, and responsible AI principles, with the ability to translate them into practical guidance for project teams.
- Strong coordination skills and the ability to manage assigned initiatives and collaborate effectively across portfolios, projects, countries, and functions in an international context.
- Ability to translate technical concepts into clear, practical, user-oriented guidance and support materials for non-technical audiences.
- Proven capability to support capacity development and adoption of modernised delivery practices through training, coaching, documentation, and user support.

## **Qualifications, Experience and Language Skills**

- Master's degree (or equivalent) in a relevant field. A first-level university degree (Bachelor's degree or equivalent) with two additional years of relevant work experience may be accepted in lieu of the Master's degree.
- Minimum of 5 years of professional experience in digital transformation, automation, or AI-enabled solutions, preferably in international programme environments.
- Strong analytical, drafting, communication, and presentation skills.
- Proficiency in (verbal/written) English is required, knowledge of Arabic and/or French is an asset.
- Advanced proficiency in digital, IT, and collaboration tools.
- Relevant certifications (e.g. ITIL) are an asset.

jobs.title: HMA Technical Field Manager
jobs.body:
**HI, Humanity and Inclusion is seeking a HMA Technical Field Manager**

**Place:** Kharkiv, Ukraine  
**Starting date:** As soon as possible  
**Duration of contract:** 12 months  
  
**Application review on a Rolling Basis: Due to the urgency of this recruitment, we encourage interested candidates to submit their applications as soon as possible. We will be reviewing applications on an ongoing basis.**  
**We need you to support our field teams in deploying this massive emergency response. Your help can make a difference. Join us!**

Humanity & Inclusion is an independent and impartial aid organisation working in situations of poverty and exclusion, conflict and disaster. The organisation works alongside people with disabilities and vulnerable populations, taking action and bearing witness in order to respond to their essential needs, improve their living conditions and promote respect for their dignity and fundamental rights.

Since its creation in 1982, HI has run development & humanitarian projects in more than 55 countries and responded to numerous emergencies. Today, we have a budget of approximately 200 million euros, with 4,000 employees worldwide

At Handicap International-Humanity & Inclusion, we truly believe in the importance of inclusion and diversity within our organisation. This is why we are engaged to a disability policy to encourage the inclusion and integration of people with disabilities.

Please indicate if you require any special accommodation, even at the first interview. [For more information about the organisation.](https://www.hi.org/en/index)

**JOB CONTEXT:**   
From February 2022, HI has re-opened a Country Programme in Ukraine to respond to the humanitarian needs triggered by the full-scale invasion of Ukraine by the Russian Federation. In 2024, HI pillars of interventions are:   
• Health: HI aims to improve access to quality physical rehabilitation and mental health and psychosocial support services (MHPSS) for conflict-affected vulnerable population.   
• Protection: Given the scale of humanitarian and protection needs, HI intervenes at various levels to ensure that vulnerable conflict-affected populations have access to multi-sectoral services tailored to their needs. In addition, HI aims to foster a disability-inclusive humanitarian response.   
• Humanitarian Mine Action (HMA) : Ongoing attacks dangerously exacerbated Explosive Ordnance (EO) contamination in Ukraine.

- EORE/CPP: HI is conducting a multi-pronged approach to EO Risk Education and Conflict Preparedness and Protection (CPP), adaptable to the evolution of the conflict in Kharkivska Oblast and Dnipro.
- Advocacy
- Demining: HI has commenced TS/ MMC activities in Kharkivska Oblast in Sept 2026 and will be seeking BAC accreditation in early 2027.
- NTS: HI is implementing Non Technical Survey activities in Kharkivska Oblast since 2025
- VA (victim Assistance)   
      
    2- HI Ukraine Program:   
    • Volume: 7M€/year – 100 + staff   
    • Donors: CDCS, SDC, WHO, UNMAS  
    • Partners: Relevant Ministries, local organizations, hospitals, local authorities, etc.

 **YOUR MISSION:**   
The HMA (Humanitarian Mine Action) Technical Field Manager holds a critical role in providing expert technical guidance and support to all staff involved in HMA activities with a primary focus on Land Release Operations.

 HMA teams cover the response dedicated to the comprehensive approach to Humanitarian Mine Action by HI in Ukraine including Data collection, Non-Technical Survey (NTS), Explosive Ordnance Risk Education (EORE), Conflict Preparedness and Protection (CPP), Victim Assistance (VA), Advocacy, Demining. HI intends to implement HMA activities in areas where communities are exposed to Explosive Ordnance threats in line with needs analysis and the tasking order received by the Mine Action Center.

 The HMA Technical Field Manager (TFM) and has the primary function of providing technical advice and managing all national and/or international staff assigned to him/her throughout all Humanitarian Mine Action (HMA) activities., as part of its Integrated approach for HMA and coordinate jointly with the EORE PM activities in the project. The TFM will support NTS Operations and Demining Operations, conduct field mentoring provide technical support and quality management to the teams operating throughout the designated area of operations.

The HMA TFM reports directly to the Chief of Operations in Ukraine.

As the HMA TFM you will plan your activities closely with the Chief of Operations, Security Liaison Officer (North-East), and PM EORE, and will be expected to liaise with other technical specialists and mine action operators.

**Mission 1: Operational Implementation**

- Contribute to NTS and demining Operations planning and implementation in line with the existing frameworks
- Contribute to project monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning
- Ensure project data management for NTS and demining
- Contribute to the coordination of project teams
- Contribute to external project communication

**Mission 2: Management**

- Manager as a role model: embody HI's values on a daily basis, and be a role model.
- Manager as a coach for meaning: understand the strategy, make it explicit, translate it into operational objectives for his or her team, lead the necessary changes. Give meaning to each management action. Encourage inter and intra departmental exchanges of practice. Encourage innovation and risk-taking.
- Operational manager: organise the operational management of his or her team, structure the work around identified processes, steer performance and facilitate the resolution of problems.
- First HR & Coach: contribute to the development of his or her staff, creating the conditions for their commitment, professionalism and attachment to HI. Ensure compliance with the code of conduct and institutional policies, the mindset and expected individual and collective behaviour.

**Mission 3: Emergency Preparedness and Response**

Contribute to the program’s emergency preparedness initiatives, and in an emergency, adapt his/her working arrangements to contribute to an effective humanitarian response from HI.

- Understand and comply with all HI SOPs and inform the CoO and Security Liaison Officer/Manager of any change in the security situation.
- Provide regular security updates to HMA Supervisors for dissemination to teams.
- Provide technical guidance and oversee the safety of HMA operations conducting threat assessments

**CHARACTERISTICS OF THE POSITION:**

The security situation in Ukraine remains relatively stable, although air alert is frequently active. However, markets, restaurants and cafes are open, and life continues as normal. There is a strict curfew, the hours depend on the region. Most attacks by RF target energy structures, mainly power grids and power plants, resulting in planned or unplanned disruptions of electricity, water, heating and occasionally internet across the country.  
HI has 2 hubs, one in the East (based in Dnipro), one in the North East (based in Kharkiv), and the coordination office is in Kyiv. HI staff is accommodated in guesthouses or in hotels (during business trips), usually near HI offices, restaurants, cafes, shopping centers within walking distance and near a shelter (the shelter is either in the building or easy to reach).  
Movements between sites can be made by car (Hi drivers) or by train, depending of the region, time and security restrictions.

**YOUR PROFILE:**

- IMAS EOD 3 certification from an accredited training institution;
- Basic knowledge in EORE
- NTS and demining qualifications
- 5 years working in the field of Humanitarian Mine Action;
- Experience in coordinating and managing Land Release Operations (NTS teams and demining teams)
- Experience in analysing data, conducting desk assessment and collecting information through survey, interviews, focus group discussions
- Experience in delivering presentations and trainings;
- Experience in project cycle management, budgeting, procurement, logistics.
- English: C2
- Ukrainian : C2 (preferred)

**CONDITIONS:**   
At HI, the conditions offered are up to your commitment and adapted to the context of your mission: [Join the team](https://hi.org/en/join-the-team)

- 12 months International contract
- The international contract provides social cover adapted to your situation:
    - Unemployment insurance benefits for EU nationals;
    - Pension scheme;
    - Medical coverage with 50% of employee contribution;
    - Repatriation insurance paid by HI;
- Perdiem: 597 net/month - paid in the payroll
- Hardship: 500 € net/month paid with your salary
- Paid leaves: 25 days per year;
- R&R: according to the level of the mission 5 days every 8 weeks 
    - Payment for travel costs (air ticket & visa) and transport of your personal effects;
    - Mission of more than 12 months: a child allowance of 100€ per month, per child paid in the payroll
- Housing: Collective / taken in charge by HI;
- If you are resident in the country: local package.

jobs.title: Call for Expressions of Interest (Roster of experts and organisations)
jobs.body:
**Roster of experts and organisations — Fondation Hirondelle**

**Who we are:**

Fondation Hirondelle is a Swiss media development organisation that supports independent, reliable information in fragile and conflict-affected contexts, including through its programme in Syria.

**What we are looking for:**

We are building a roster of individual experts and organisations that we can call on for short or longer assignments, now and in the future. Applying does not commit either party. We are interested in the following areas:

- Media and journalism: editorial coaching and editing; journalism training and training of trainers; investigative journalism; verification, OSINT and digital journalism; multimedia production; audience engagement and communications; media law and freedom of expression.
- Safety and protection: journalists' safety; digital security; security risk management; trauma and psychosocial support; gender, inclusion and safeguarding.
- Organisational development: institutional capacity building; strategic planning, governance and board development; leadership development; leadership and executive coaching; team coaching and change management; media sustainability, fundraising and partnerships; project cycle management and proposal writing; financial management and donor compliance; human resources and policies; knowledge management and learning.
- Monitoring and evaluation: audience research, monitoring, evaluation and impact measurement.
- Context and themes: transitional justice; peacebuilding, social cohesion and conflict sensitivity; missing persons and enforced disappearance; law (Syrian law, international criminal law, human rights); hate speech and disinformation; civic engagement and public information; memorialisation and archives.
- Support: translation and interpretation; facilitation and event management; data analysis and digital tools; graphic design; other areas relevant to independent media.

**Who can apply:**

Individual experts and organisations (companies, associations, training and research centres), from Syria, the region or internationally. Syrian expertise is a priority.

**What to submit:**

- CV (individuals) or organisation profile.
- Number of years of experience, in total and in your main area.
- Two references, with contact details.
- A cover letter (about one page): why you wish to join and what you can offer.

**How we select:**

We assess relevant experience, knowledge of the Syrian context, languages, independence and impartiality, and the quality of references and cover letter. A small team reviews applications against these criteria and records its decisions.

**What joining the roster means:**

- It is not a contract and does not guarantee any assignment or a minimum volume of work.
- When a need arises, we select from the roster and follow Fondation Hirondelle procurement rules, which may include a request for quotations.
- Fees are set according to the assignment and the applicable rules, not by the roster.
- Registration is valid for 24 months and may be renewed.

**Data protection, independence and safeguarding:**

Your data is kept confidential, stored securely and used only to manage the roster. We ask you to declare any link with Fondation Hirondelle or its partner media outlets. Selected experts must respect our safeguarding, do-no-harm and independence principles.

jobs.title: TERMS OF REFERENCE (TOR) ; Project Entrepreneurship Training Consultant for Jenga Ajira Project
source: Center for Domestic Training and Development
jobs.body:
**1. Background**  
The Centre for Domestic Training and Development (CDTD) is a Kenyan non-governmental organization committed to advancing decent work, skills development, labour rights and economic empowerment for vulnerable populations, particularly women, youth, migrant workers, domestic workers, refugees, survivors of trafficking and host communities. For over two decades, CDTD has championed innovative interventions that improve livelihoods through technical skills development, advocacy, labour mobility and market-driven employment pathways.  
CDTD is implementing Jenga Ajira Project, an 18-month youth employability initiative that seeks to sponsor at least 80 vulnerable youth aged 18–25 years, within Kiambu and Nairobi County around Thika Road Economic Corridor. The aim is for participants to move into decent wage employment or sustainable self-employment after six months of completing training.  
The project responds to a persistent challenge where many vulnerable youths cannot afford TVET training, existing programmes that often do not match labour-market demand, youth lack practical work experience and essential employability skills, and young women face additional barriers to skills and decent work. About 90% of the new jobs created in Kenya in 2024 were in the informal sector (KNBS, 2025), so both employment and self-employment pathways are necessary for more employability outcomes. A Labor Market Assessment of accredited training institutions commissioned by CDTD confirmed five priority trades with documented labour-market demand these are;Solar PV Installation; Mobile Phone Repair; ICT & Digital Skills; Hair Dressing and Beauty Therapy and Homecare and Caregiving.  
The project model combines;  
(1)Job-ready skills assessment.  
(2)Targeted youth selection.  
(3)On-boarding to demand-driven accredited TVET training institutions.  
(4)Skilling and eventual NITA/CDACC certification.  
(5)Life-skills holistic employability development (workplace ethics, communication skills, personal branding, digital skills, mentorship, goal setting and workforce readiness).  
(6)Industrial attachments.  
(7)Job placement and enterprise support, and  
(8)Labour-market alignment and partnerships.

**2. Purpose of the Assignment**  
Technical training alone is not enough. Employers report that young people lack workplace behavior, communication and workforce readiness skills. The Labor Market Assessment (LMA) found learner behavior change, among the main challenges reported by training institutions. To improve retention, completion and transition to work, CDTD seeks to engage a qualified Entrepreneurship Training Consultant to train on components of;  
1.Entrepreneurial Mindset; Emotional Intelligence; Resilience, Critical Thinking and Leadership  
2.Business Ideation; Opportunity Mapping; Business Model Development; Business Plan; Market Feasibility Analysis  
3.Business Operations; Legal and Compliance; Sales & Marketing; Operations & Logistics; Digital Tools and Technology Integration.  
4.Financial Literacy; Foundational Accounting; Cash Flow and Working Capital; Tax; Insurance; Balance Sheet; Profit & Loss; Savings & Investment.

**3. Objectives of the Assignment**  
The consultant/institution shall:  
a)Assess participants' entrepreneurial interest, aptitude and readiness, and identify those intending to pursue self-employment.  
b)Design and deliver a practical entrepreneurship curriculum tailored to the five priority trades.  
c)Support participants to develop simple, bankable business plans aligning to the five priority trades.  
d)Facilitate identification and mapping of market linkages, group enterprises and business mentorship with established entrepreneurs in each trade.  
**4. Scope of Work**  
A. Target group and location  
At least 80 youth aged 18–25 years enrolled in accredited training within the EAIHM catchment along the Nairobi–Kiambu boundary, with intensive enterprise-development support for the sub-group that chooses self-employment.  
**B. Programme components**  
•Entrepreneurship awareness and readiness: for all participants, a minimum of 16 contact hours.  
•Develop trade-specific enterprise models: practical models such as salon and mobile beauty services, phone repair kiosks, small solar installation and maintenance services, home-based care services and digital/online services.  
•Business plan challenge; invoke a critical thinking mindset grounded on the realities of business landscape in Kenya.  
•Linkages: Mapping of financial providers, regulators and business mentors; encourage formation of savings or business groups.  
C. Cross-cutting Messaging  
•Gender-responsive delivery of training.  
•Disability-inclusive delivery of training.  
**5. Methodology and Approach**  
The consultant shall propose a participatory, experiential and learner-centered methodology suited to young people with varied education levels, including role plays, case studies, simulations, peer learning and use of local languages where possible to effectively communicate.  
The Expression Of Interest (EOI) should explain how learning will be administered, assessed (pre- and post-training), help identify where necessary at-risk trainees and propose ways to support them.  
Project indicator Consultant contribution  
Number of youth completing entrepreneurship training Attendance and completion records by sex  
% of graduates able to develop a bankable business plan Business plans template and guide  
Number of youth able to link to financial providers, regulators and business mentors Personalized linkage chat

**6. Expected Deliverables**  
\# Deliverable Indicative timing  
1 Inception report: work plan, methodology, training manual, assessment tools and safeguarding or referral plan post-training Within 2 days of contract signing  
2 Share the training manual proposed for delivery Within 5 days after contracting  
3 Action points report 4 days after each training  
4 Final report with pre/post assessment results, outcomes by sex and lessons learned At the end of the 16 contact hours training period.

**7. Duration and Timeline**  
The assignment is expected to run for up to nine months and an attachment cycle, with an estimated 16-hour support level. The final training schedule will be agreed upon after the inception report and aligned with partner training institutions' intake dates.  
**8. Qualifications and Experience**  
a. Education: Bachelor's degree or higher in Entrepreneurship, Business Administration, Economics, Development Studies or a related field. Certification in an enterprise-training methodology (e.g. ILO Start and Improve Your Business) is an added advantage.  
b. Experience: At least five years' experience delivering entrepreneurship, enterprise development or financial literacy programmes for youth and women, preferably in informal-sector and TVET contexts.  
c. Technical skills: Demonstrated experience in business planning and coaching for micro-enterprises; knowledge of youth finance sources and the MSME ecosystem in Nairobi and Kiambu; experience tracking enterprise outcomes; strong facilitation in English and Kiswahili.  
d. Other: An existing network of business mentors, finance providers and suppliers in the priority trades is an advantage.  
**9. Application Documents Required**  
a)Technical proposal (understanding of the assignment, approach, methodology and work plan)  
b)Financial proposal (in Kenya Shillings, inclusive of all applicable taxes)  
c)Updated CV(s) of the consultant and any proposed team members  
d)Copies of academic and professional certificates  
e)Valid KRA PIN  
f)Business registration certificate and company profile (for firms)  
g)Sample or an overview description of an entrepreneurship training curriculum or business-plan template previously used  
h)At least three (3) reference letters from clients confirming successful delivery of similar youth or women entrepreneurship assignments  
**10. Reporting, Safeguarding and Data Protection**  
The consultant shall report directly to the Program Officer, Jenga Ajira Project, and work closely with the training institutions' career and student-support officers where applicable. All deliverables shall be submitted in Microsoft Word and PDF formats, together with attendance registers, assessment tools and training feedback forms.

The consultant/institution will be required to sign and comply with CDTD's Safeguarding and Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) Policy and Code of Conduct, and to handle all personal data of participants in line with the Kenya Data Protection Act, 2019.  
1

jobs.title: Chief Field Office, P-4, FT, #099121, Bunia -Democratic Republic of Congo, WCAR
jobs.body:
UNICEF works in over 190 countries and territories to save children’s lives, defend their rights, and help them fulfill their potential, from early childhood through adolescence.

At UNICEF, we are committed, passionate, and proud of what we do for as long as we are needed. Promoting the rights of every child is not just a job – it is a calling.

UNICEF is a place where careers are built: we offer our staff diverse opportunities for professional and personal development that will help them reinforce a sense of purpose while serving children and communities across the world. We welcome everyone who wants to belong and grow in a diverse and passionate culture, coupled with an attractive compensation and benefits package.

Visit [our website](https://www.unicef.org/) to learn more about what we do at UNICEF.

**For every child,** ***the right to Hope***

**How can you make a difference?**

Under the guidance of the Chief Field Operations, you as the Chief Field Office (CFO) will be accountable for managing and leading the total programme commitment of a field office within a country programme. You will represent UNICEF in Bunia, leads and oversees the various program sectors and operational service teams ensuring the delivery of quality results in accordance with UNICEF’s programme of cooperation, country programme management plan and overall vision set forward by the Representative. The role operates in a protracted, multi-hazard emergency environment characterized by armed violence, large-scale displacement, severe protection risks, recurrent disease outbreaks, constrained humanitarian access, community mistrust and disruption of essential services. You will provide area-based leadership for UNICEF’s response across Ituri and, when delegated, supports operational coherence with Haut-Uélé and adjoining outbreak and displacement corridors.

In fragile and humanitarian contexts, UNICEF action is guided by its global Policy and Framework for humanitarian action: the Core Commitments for Children in Humanitarian Action.

**KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES and DUTIES & TASKS**

1. Effective management of UNICEF presence, staff and assets
2. Knowledge Management for Programmes
3. Programme Development and Management
4. Optimum Use of Program Funds
5. Programme Monitoring and Evaluations
6. Rights-Based and Results-Based Programme Management Approach
7. National and Local Capacity Building/Sustainability
8. Rights Perspective and Advocacy at the National, Community and Family Levels
9. Partnership, Coordination and Collaboration

If you would like to know more about this position, please review the complete Job Description here: [JD - Chief Field Office P-4.pdf](https://secure.dc7.pageuppeople.com/apply/TransferRichTextFile.ashx?sData=UFUtVjMtNWAKkHsLiz2HFSYUmbPc_z8pyzxzCu_jYZTSBYrvr9XuES25CImv1_GakfyFDA5DE8bsWa-N1vF7Xfu5kw-QnLBZzEisVQ_2a1Q2GVqckCfitnwWY5VrQCl9qMwcgTTWxBjTs43kaieIVdd0FD3TQg%7e%7e)

**To qualify as an advocate for every child you will have…**

jobs.body:
UNICEF works in over 190 countries and territories to save children’s lives, defend their rights, and help them fulfill their potential, from early childhood through adolescence.

At UNICEF, we are committed, passionate, and proud of what we do for as long as we are needed. Promoting the rights of every child is not just a job – it is a calling.

UNICEF is a place where careers are built: we offer our staff diverse opportunities for professional and personal development that will help them reinforce a sense of purpose while serving children and communities across the world. We welcome everyone who wants to belong and grow in a diverse and passionate culture, coupled with an attractive compensation and benefits package.

Visit [our website](https://www.unicef.org/) to learn more about what we do at UNICEF.

**For every child,** ***the right to a Future***

The Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) stands at a crossroads between immense natural wealth and extraordinary human potential. With an estimated 113 million inhabitants, including 61 million young people under 18 years of age, the DRC boasts one of Africa’s youngest populations - a generation of energy, creativity, and promise capable of shaping a future of peace, innovation, and prosperity. Spanning 2.3 million km², an area comparable to Western Europe, the DRC is Africa’s second-largest country and shares borders with nine nations, making it a natural hub for regional trade, integration, and cooperation. Beneath its soil lie some of the world’s richest mineral and environmental reserves: the Congo Basin rainforest, a vital carbon sink for the planet, and abundant deposits of cobalt, copper, gold, and uranium, which are essential to the global green transition and digital economy. This powerful combination of natural and human capital positions the DRC as a strategic engine for Africa’s sustainable development. However, decades of conflict and instability-particularly in the east-have left deep scars. As of 2024, 25.4 million people, including 14.9 million children, were living amidst violence, disease, and extreme poverty, while 7 million were internally displaced. Ongoing governance challenges and structural constraints continue to hinder progress, and the DRC ranks among the lowest on global development indices. The country hosts the second largest displaced population in the world, with children exposed to heightened risks of violence, abuse, and deprivation, and many lacking access to basic services such as clean water, healthcare, and education. Compounding these challenges, the DRC faces recurrent epidemics including Ebola, cholera, measles, and polio. Despite these adversities, the resilience of Congolese communities remains unwavering. Across the country, youth, women, and local innovators are driving positive change-from peacebuilding and education initiatives to renewable energy solutions and digital-skills programs. If nurtured through sustained investment in education, employment, governance, and innovation, the DRC’s demographic dividend could become the foundation for a new era of stability and shared growth.

In this complex environment, UNICEF continues to play a pivotal not only as a humanitarian actor but as a key development partner and catalyst for systems strengthening and inclusive growth. Through integrated, multi-sectoral programming and strong collaboration with government and partners, UNICEF bridges emergency response with long-term development and resilience-building efforts, ensuring that investments in children translate into sustainable, system-wide results. The DRC’s challenges are undeniable-but so too is its extraordinary potential. With its unparalleled natural endowment and a generation of 61 million young Congolese-motors of hope, peace, and prosperity- the Democratic Republic of the Congo holds the key to a more sustainable, inclusive, and equitable future for Africa and the world. UNICEF DRC is one of the largest and most dynamic country offices globally, with an annual budget of USD 300 million, a team of 366 staff, and six field offices in addition to the national office in Kinshasa. Operating in a context of both significant humanitarian needs and growing development opportunities, the office has recently undergone restructuring to enhance efficiency and deepen engagement with communities and government partners.

**How can you make a difference?**

The Communication and Advocacy Section, comprising six fixed-term staff and led by a P-5 Chief of Communication, plays a pivotal role in shaping UNICEF’s visibility, partnerships, and public engagement. Its work covers media engagement, supporting programmes teams, organizing World Children’s Day events, and younth engagement on environmental and climate change.

**Key accountabilities and duties & tasks:**

1. **Communication strategy:** Ensure that the Country Office has a clear communication strategy and associated work plan to support the country programme objectives and get children’s issues into the public domain, strengthen political will in support of UNICEF's mission and objectives, and enhance the organization’s credibility and brand.
2. **Media relations:** Ensure that the Country Office has a well-managed country communication team that maintains and continually develops a contact list of journalists and media outlets covering all media – print, TV, radio, web etc. – and a successful process of communicating and maintaining regular contact and close collaboration with the media to communicate the story of UNICEF's cooperation to a wider audience. New ways are identified to increase positive exposure and leverage that prominence for new opportunities for UNICEF.
3. **Communication, networking and partnerships:** Manage a country communication team to ensure that the Country Office has a well maintained and continually developed contact list of individuals, groups, organizations and fora (including business), whose support is essential to/can assist in achieving the advocacy and communication objectives of the communication strategy. Network is developed, strengthened and maintained with the UN Country Team, UN communication counterparts and high-level counterparts in key partner organizations.
4. **Celebrities and special events:** Ensure that the Country Office has a well-managed national celebrity relations programme with a well maintained and continually developed contact list of appropriate, nationally-known personalities who have been identified, engaged and support UNICEF’s efforts and who actively participate in special events and activities that support country programme goals. Among these high-profile individuals a handful are identified whose recognition level extends beyond national borders and co-ordinate closely with DOC and the regional office in extending their impact and use beyond national borders.
5. **Global priorities and campaigns:** In addition to local/national campaigns, ensure that the Country Office has an effective process in place for integrating and taking action on UNICEF’s global communications priorities and campaigns, both disseminating these elements in a locally-appropriate way, as well as providing/enabling coverage of the work in the country for global use.
6. **Resource mobilization support:** Ensure that global and country level fund-raising are supported by effective advocacy and communication strategy and activities.
7. **Management:** Ensure that the human resources (the communication team) and financial resources (budget planning, management and monitoring) for the communication section of the Country Office are both effectively managed and optimally used.
8. **Monitoring and evaluation:** Ensure that communication baselines are established against which the objectives of the communication strategy are regularly evaluated; analysis is undertaken to continuously improve the effectiveness of communication strategy, approach and activities; results and reports are prepared and shared on a timely basis.
9. **Capacity building and support:** Ensure that the Representative and the country programme team are provided with professional expertise and advice on all aspects of communication as required; opportunities for development among the country communication team and other colleagues are identified and addressed; opportunities to build communication capacity among media and other relevant partners are identified and addressed.
10. **Advisory support and communication for strategic results:** Implementation of UNICEF programme (regional) plans, ensuring communication on gender and equity issues are mainstreamed across all programmes.

If you would like to know more about this position, please review the complete Job Description here: [JD\_Chief\_of\_Communication\_P5.pdf](https://secure.dc7.pageuppeople.com/apply/TransferRichTextFile.ashx?sData=UFUtVjMt6jdqY1Or_bNHUh8zq6eggtcaQWvdrR9e3rc3qmiQwEGUW0ineUUy-9TQYA3n63cwI85G6kQ1mDl7Idd5KufyGUMp2Nx2IhrP2U395RcReD22qyqqDRO1m_QLcOuU8MWo3xyeeYLGd3HmpRLf6btcxQ%7e%7e)

**To qualify as an advocate for every child you will have…**

***Minimum requirements:***

- **Education**: Advanced university degree in Communication, Journalism, Public Relations or other related fields of disciplines.
- **Work Experience**: Ten (10) years of progressively responsible and relevant professional work experience. International and national work experience in both developed and developing countries. Professional experience in communication, print, broadcast, new media. Background/familiarity with Emergency situations.
- **Skills**: Candidates should demonstrate experience in global advocacy engagement, partnership engagement and maintenance, global and local media relations, monitoring and evaluation, and B2B engagement.
- **Language Requirements**: Fluency in French and English are required.

***Desirables:***

- Knowledge of another official UN language (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian or Spanish) or a local language is an asset.
- Relevant experience at country level, particularly in development, fragile settings and humanitarian contexts.
