jobs.title: Mission France - Responsable des activités de travail social F/H
jobs.body:
Médecins Sans Frontières, association médicale humanitaire internationale créée en 1971, apporte une assistance médicale à des populations dont la vie est menacée : principalement en cas de conflits armés, mais aussi d'épidémies, de pandémies, de catastrophes naturelles ou encore d'exclusion des soins.

La mission France recherche un.e Responsable des activités de travail social pour son projet au Littoral Nord.

**Contexte :**

Médecins Sans Frontières intervient en France auprès des personnes exilées confrontées aux conséquences sanitaires, psychologiques et sociales des violences liées aux parcours migratoires et aux ruptures de protection. La Mission France combine soins, protection et témoignage pour répondre aux besoins des personnes les plus vulnérables.

Elle concentre aujourd’hui son action sur le Littoral Nord et l’Île-de-France, tout en conservant une capacité de réponse rapide aux situations d’urgence. Portée par des équipes pluridisciplinaires, elle développe des activités médicales, psychologiques, sociales et de plaidoyer dans un contexte en constante évolution

**Votre rôle :**

Sous la responsabilité du·de la Référent·e migration, et en lien fonctionnel avec la personne responsable de la protection de l’unité migrations, vous concevrez, superviserez et suivrez les activités de travail social du projet. Vous encadrerez les travailleur·ses sociaux·les, contribuerez à la stratégie de protection et veillerez à la qualité des accompagnements proposés.

Ce poste associe pilotage stratégique, management d’équipe et intervention directe sur le terrain : vous consacrerez notamment 30 % de votre temps aux activités de travail social, aux maraudes et à l’« aller-vers ».

**Principales responsabilités :**

Piloter Définir et piloter la stratégie de travail social et de protection

- Co-définir et mettre en œuvre la stratégie de travail social du projet, en cohérence avec les orientations opérationnelles et le cadre de travail social de MSF.
- Développer les activités autour de la gestion de cas, du soutien social aux patient·es, du lien social de première ligne et des interventions communautaires.
- Analyser le contexte et les déterminants sociaux de la santé afin d’identifier les vulnérabilités récurrentes, les situations de violence, les phénomènes de déplacement et d’exclusion, ainsi que les besoins critiques d’assistance et de protection.
- Contribuer à la définition des objectifs et des interventions de protection, notamment en matière de signalement et de prévention des risques.
- Documenter les restrictions d’accès aux services et analyser les obstacles rencontrés afin de proposer des pistes d’action et de plaidoyer en lien avec la référente médicale en migration et la mission MSF France.

**Garantir un accompagnement social de qualité et gérer les situations complexes**

- Superviser les parcours d’accompagnement social : accueil, évaluation des besoins, élaboration et mise en œuvre du plan d’intervention, orientation sécurisée, suivi et clôture des situations.
- Veiller à la prise en charge des besoins sociaux critiques, dans le périmètre du projet, par un accompagnement direct ou une orientation vers des services adaptés.
- Accompagner les équipes dans la gestion des situations complexes et intervenir directement dans les cas sensibles, notamment lorsqu’il existe des risques élevés de violence ou qu’un mineur non accompagné est concerné.
- Organiser des temps réguliers de concertation autour des situations suivies, afin de partager les difficultés et de construire des réponses adaptées avec les autres disciplines.
- Favoriser le pouvoir d’agir des personnes accompagnées en leur donnant une information claire sur leurs droits, les services disponibles, les critères d’accès et les démarches pertinentes.
- Contribuer à un environnement de soins sûr, digne et confidentiel, qui respecte les droits des patient·es et facilite l’accès aux mécanismes de retours et de plaintes.

**Développer le travail social communautaire et les partenariats**

- Participer aux maraudes et aux activités d’« aller-vers » pour identifier les besoins sociaux, les vulnérabilités et les risques de protection au sein des communautés.
- Développer, avec les équipes médicales, de santé mentale et de médiation, des interventions pluridisciplinaires visant à renforcer les facteurs de protection et de résilience.
- Construire et actualiser une cartographie des services sociaux, des associations, des partenaires institutionnels et des dispositifs communautaires présents sur la zone du projet.
- Développer des relations de coopération avec les partenaires et suivre l’accessibilité, la disponibilité et la qualité des services proposés.
- Renforcer la coordination et l’orientation des personnes vers les dispositifs adaptés, en portant une attention particulière aux situations de violence, notamment sexuelle, et aux possibilités de prise en charge.
- Contribuer à la surveillance communautaire et à l’analyse des problématiques de protection rencontrées sur le terrain.

**Manager, accompagner et développer l’équipe**

- Encadrer les travailleur·ses sociaux·les et organiser les plannings en fonction des différentes activités : maraudes, entretiens individuels et activités collectives.
- Développer les compétences de l’équipe par la formation, le coaching, la supervision et le partage de pratiques.
- Identifier les besoins de développement professionnel et mettre en œuvre un plan de développement des compétences, en lien avec le département des ressources humaines.
- Former et sensibiliser les équipes aux questions de protection, de gestion de cas, de conduite d’entretien et d’orientation.
- Contribuer aux processus de recrutement, de formation et d’évaluation des équipes concernées, en collaboration avec les RH.
- Assurer la continuité des activités en apportant un soutien opérationnel et, si nécessaire, en remplaçant les membres de l’équipe absents.
- Veiller au bien-être de l’équipe et favoriser une coopération étroite avec les autres pôles du projet.

**Assurer Suivre les activités, analyser les données et garantir la qualité**

- Superviser la collecte, l’enregistrement et l’analyse des données relatives aux activités de travail social et de protection.
- Suivre les indicateurs de résultats et produire un reporting régulier permettant d’identifier les tendances, les besoins émergents et les difficultés d’accès aux services.
- Documenter les situations et les tendances en matière de protection afin d’alimenter l’analyse opérationnelle et les actions de plaidoyer de MSF.
- Développer et adapter les outils et processus de travail social aux besoins du projet.
- Garantir le respect du cadre de travail social de MSF, des règles de confidentialité, de la protection des données et des exigences légales et éthiques.
- Planifier et coordonner les ressources humaines, matérielles et financières nécessaires aux activités, en lien avec les départements support.

**Profil recherché**

**Formation et expérience :**

- Diplôme français ou étranger de travailleur·se social·e, avec au moins trois années de formation théorique et pratique.
- Au moins trois ans d’expérience professionnelle dans la gestion de programmes de travail social ou de domaines similaires : protection, accompagnement psychosocial, violences sexuelles et basées sur le genre, etc.
- Expérience en gestion d’équipe.
- Une expérience dans un contexte sanitaire, humanitaire, de protection ou de migration est fortement souhaitée.
- Une expérience avérée en gestion de cas ou en protection dans un contexte d’urgence constitue un atout.

**Compétences et qualités :**

- Capacités d’analyse et aptitude à transformer les constats du terrain en réponses adaptées.
- Sens de l’organisation, orientation vers les résultats et exigence de qualité.
- Aptitude à manager, accompagner et développer une équipe.
- Esprit d’équipe, coopération et capacité à travailler en pluridisciplinarité.
- Sens du service et approche centrée sur la personne.
- Capacité à développer des partenariats et à construire des relations de confiance.

jobs.title: Program Officer (Al Jazeera State, Sudan)
jobs.body:
**About CIVIC**

Center for Civilians in Conflict (CIVIC) is an international non-governmental organization (INGO) with offices around the world working to improve protection for civilians caught in conflict zones. CIVIC envisions a world in which no civilian is harmed in conflict. Our mission is to support communities affected by conflict in their quest for protection and strengthen the resolve and capacity of armed actors to prevent and respond to civilian harm. We are advocates who believe that no civilian caught in conflict should be ignored, and advisors who provide practical solutions to preventing and responding to civilian harm. Learn more at [civiliansinconflict.org.](https://www.civiliansinconflict.org/)

**About the Position**

CIVIC is seeking highly qualified applicants for the position of Program Officer – PROCIV Program, who will support the implementation of a new initiative on Humanitarian Dialogue and Humanitarian Diplomacy (PROCIV). The Program Officer will be part of the Sudan country team, working closely with local civil society, armed actor interlocutors, and regional/international policy stakeholders under the guidance of the Country Director and Senior Program Manager. This is a full-time position with a one-year contract.

***Job Purpose:*** Coordinate, implement, and support all activities under the PROCIV project focused on humanitarian dialogue, civilian protection, and evidence-based humanitarian diplomacy.

LOCATION: Al Jazeera State, Sudan

TRAVEL: As needed throughout Sudan

REPORTING TO: Senior Program Officer.

STAFF REPORTING: N/A

**Key Responsibilities**

- Support implementation of the PROCIV humanitarian dialogue and diplomacy activities, ensuring alignment with project outcomes and CIVIC methodologies.
- Coordinate protection risk analyses, civilian self-protection assessments, and mapping of local partners and community structures.
- Facilitate relationships with local CSOs, ERRs, community leaders, native administration, and other key stakeholders engaged in humanitarian dialogue.
- Support delivery of mentorship sessions for civil society leaders and community actors on humanitarian dialogue, negotiation, and protection priorities.
- Assist in convening confidential consultations with armed actors and authorities to create openings for constructive engagement on PoC and humanitarian access.
- Coordinate planning, logistics, and documentation for dialogue sessions, workshops, training, and joint analysis meetings, working closely with Operations.
- Support evidence generation for policy briefs, protection analysis, and outcome documentation, contributing to national, regional, and international advocacy.
- Ensure gender-sensitive and conflict-sensitive approaches throughout all activities, including representation of women, youth, and marginalized groups.
- Facilitate sharing of best practices between PROCIV partners, community representatives, and colleagues across the three target geographies (Sudan, DRC, Yemen).
- Coordinate data collection and serve as MEAL focal point for the PROCIV project, ensuring timely reporting on outputs, outcomes, and lessons learned.
- Maintain strong relationships with local partners, humanitarian actors, and coordination structures, ensuring complementarity with ICRC, OCHA, and protection clusters.
- Prepare timely reports, support documents, and updates to the Senior Program Manager, Country Director, and donor when requested.
- Represent CIVIC at relevant NGO, community, and stakeholder meetings to promote collaboration and humanitarian dialogue efforts.
- Perform any other duties as required to further the organization’s mission and the successful delivery of PROCIV activities in Sudan.

**Requirements**

- A Bachelor's Degree in international affairs, political science, conflict studies, development studies, or a related field.
- Minimum 5 years of relevant full-time experience in protection, humanitarian dialogue, civil society engagement, or program coordination in conflict-affected settings.
- Experience working in Sudan and deep knowledge of the national humanitarian landscape strongly preferred.
- Demonstrated commitment to CIVIC’s mission, humanitarian principles, and protection of civilians.
- Fluency in English and Arabic is mandatory.

**Qualities Sought**

- Strong understanding of civilian protection, humanitarian access, and conflict dynamics in Sudan.
- Experience engaging with local civil society, community structures, and humanitarian stakeholders, ideally in sensitive political and security environments.
- Demonstrated ability to work with community leaders, women’s groups, youth networks, and marginalized groups in participatory and inclusive ways.
- Ability to think analytically and strategically, including identifying opportunities for humanitarian dialogue and strengthening local protection arrangements.
- Poise, flexibility, discretion, and mature judgment in a fast-paced, high-pressure environment.
- Excellent organizational skills, self-motivation, and ability to deliver high-quality outputs with minimal supervision.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to produce clear analysis and documentation.
- Experience representing organizations in complex humanitarian or political settings is preferred.

**Additional Details**

**Application Deadline: November 6, 2026**

Due to the high volume of applications, only candidates selected for an interview will be contacted. ***Shortlisted candidates will receive an email invitation from TestGorilla to submit their resume. Please complete this step promptly to ensure your candidacy is fully considered.***

CIVIC is an Equal Opportunities Employer committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive environment, and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or any other protected characteristic.

Note to Recruiters and Placement Agencies: CIVIC does not accept unsolicited agency resumes and does not pay placement fees for candidates submitted by agencies other than its approved partners.

jobs.title: Senior Project Officer - MEAL (Livelihoods, Agriculture & Market Systems)
jobs.body:
**Job Title:** Senior Project Officer - MEAL (Livelihoods, Agriculture and Market Systems)

**Reports to:** Program Manager - MEAL

**Department:** Programming

**Location:** Kampala

This position is open to **Ugandan nationals only**

**Deadline:** Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. Candidates are encouraged to apply by November 6, 2026 no later than 5pm.

**Background**

We are seeking a highly motivated and experienced Senior Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) Officer for livelihoods, Agriculture and market systems program. CRS Uganda's livelihoods strategy leverages market systems development, private sector partnerships and church land investments including regenerative agroforestry to create sustainable livelihoods, resilient farming systems, and inclusive economic opportunities for vulnerable communities.

**Job Summary**

The Senior MEAL Officer will lead the design, implementation, and management of MEAL systems for livelihoods, private sector engagement, market systems development, economic inclusion, agricultural value chains, and resilience programming. The successful candidate will ensure robust results measurement, evidence generation, accountability, learning, and adaptive management while supporting project teams to demonstrate sustainable impact among households, enterprises, market actors, and market systems in line with CRS MEAL policies and procedures and donor requirements.

This position requires proven experience using the DCED Standard for Results Measurement and Market Systems Development (MSD) monitoring approaches. You must be skilled at tracking private sector partnerships, demonstrating impact and using field evidence to support smart, data-driven decisions including communicating results to wider community to drive learning and scale opportunities.

**Roles and Key Responsibilities:**

**Monitoring, Evaluation and Results Measurement**

- Lead the development and implementation of program MEAL system in line with CRS program quality principles, standards and MEAL policies, procedures, and practices; donor MEAL requirements, and industry good practices.
- Design and operationalize monitoring systems that measure outputs, outcomes, impact, sustainability, and systemic change.
- Develop and maintain data collection tools, databases, dashboards, and reporting systems.
- Ensure timely collection, analysis, interpretation, and reporting of project data. Analyze implementation challenges and report any inconsistencies and gaps to inform adjustments to plans and implementation schedules.
- Coordinate baseline, midline, end-line surveys, market assessments, studies, and evaluations.

**Private Sector and Market Actors Monitoring**

- Track performance and business growth of private sector partners, producer groups, MSMEs, cooperatives, financial institutions, buyers, and service providers.
- Track private-sector co-investment, additional capital mobilised, access to finance, and the extent to which successful models attract follow-on investment – potential for scale or replication.
- Monitor key indicators related to income growth, job creation, productivity, business performance, investment leveraged, and market access.
- Conduct market actor analyses and value chain performance assessments.
- Work with co-investing private sector actors (PSAs) to refine and improve their results frameworks so they can easily track business changes and manage growth
- Generate and disseminate evidence on business and market system outcomes to inform adaptive management.
- Assess changes in market relationships, incentives, service delivery models and the participation of smallholder farmers, women and youth in agroforestry value chains.

**Learning, Knowledge Management and Adaptive Management**

- Facilitate reflection meetings, pause-and-reflect sessions, after action reviews, learning events and MEAL communities of practice.
- Document best practices, success stories, innovations, and lessons learned.
- Produce learning briefs, case studies, dashboards, and analytical reports.
- Support programs to use evidence for strategic and operational decision-making.

**Accountability and Data Quality**

- Lead the program Data Quality Assessments (DQAs) and routine verification exercises.
- Lead the roll-out and implementation of the program’s feedback, complaints and response mechanism (FCRM). Support actively seeking and responding to feedback from all members of targeted communities and other stakeholders as defined by the FCRM.
- Ensure compliance with data protection, ethical standards, and organizational policies.
- Maintain high standards of data accuracy, reliability, completeness, and timeliness through supervision and ad hoc inspections of various MEAL processes and resources at program sites to ensure adherence to established process standards and procedures.
- Ensure proper tracking of resource use for program MEAL activities through periodic budget reviews and follow-up with and assistance to the private sector, dioceses and other implementing partners.
- Coordinate and oversee MEAL-related working relationships with the private sector, dioceses and other program stakeholders and serve as the liaison between them and the program team to mobilize local actors and promote project activities and impact. Identify and respond to key stakeholders’ information needs in MEAL activities, using a range of appropriate communication methods.
- Ensure safe, ethical and confidential management of data collected from farmers, enterprises, communities and institutional partners (dioceses and other market actors).

**Capacity Strengthening**

- Coordinate and facilitate consultations with the private sector, dioceses and other key stakeholders to identify MEAL system strengths, gaps, priorities, and opportunities for strengthening, and support the development and implementation of agreed capacity strengthening plans.
- Provide technical assistance and mentoring to the private sector and dioceses MEAL personnel and local partners to strengthen data collection, reporting, analysis, learning, and use.
- Provide ongoing mentoring and technical support to field teams and implementing partners.
- Develop and facilitate MEAL-related training and coaching programs.

***Knowledge, Skills and Abilities***

- Analysis and problem-solving skills with ability to make sound judgments.
- Good relationship management skills and the ability to work closely with local partners.
- Proactive, results-oriented and service-oriented mindset.
- Attention to detail, accuracy and timeliness in executing assigned responsibilities.
- Excellent communication and presentation abilities.
- Ability to effectively use MS Windows and MS Office packages (Excel, Word, PowerPoint), data analysis software such as Excel, Power BI, SPSS, STATA, R, or similar packages.

**Preferred Qualifications**

- Experience working with partners, participatory action planning and community engagement.
- Staff supervision experience a plus.
- Experience monitoring projects and collecting relevant data.
- Experience using MS Windows and MS Office packages (Excel, Word, PowerPoint).

**Required Languages** - Strong written and spoken English required

**Travel** - Must be willing and able to travel up to 30% to project locations and field offices outside Kampala

**Supervisory Responsibilities** - No

**Key Working Relationships -** Livelihoods, Agriculture and Market Systems program team, CP MEAL team and partner staff

**Agency Competencies (for all CRS Staff):**

- **Personal Accountability** – Consistently takes responsibility for one’s own actions.
- **Acts with Integrity** - Consistently models values aligned with CRS Guiding Principles and mission. Is considered honest.
- **Builds and Maintains Trust** - Shows consistency between words and actions.
- **Collaborates with Others** – Works effectively in intercultural and diverse teams.
- **Open to Learn** – Seeks out experiences that may change perspective or provide an opportunity to learn new things.
- **Agency Leadership Competencies:**
- **Lead Change** – Continually looks for ways to improve the agency through a culture of agility, openness, and innovation.
- **Develops and Recognizes Others** – Builds the capacity of staff to reach their full potential and enhance team and agency performance.
- **Strategic Mindset** – Understands role in translating, communicating, and implementing agency strategy and team priorities.

jobs.title: Evidence, Measurement, Learning and Impact Director, Climate-Smart Agriculture (CSA) Nigeria
jobs.body:
**\*\*Contingent upon Donor Funding\*\***

**Location:** Abuja, Nigeria

**Position Status:** Full-time, Exempt or Non-exempt, Regular

[**Risk Level:**](https://library.mercycorps.org/record/47705?ln=en) X **Level 3** ☐**Level 2** ☐**Level 1**

(Level 3: Frequent contact with participants, direct contact with children, access to sensitive data, and/or high level of accountability.

Level 2: Some contact with participants; unplanned non-direct contact with children.

Level 1: Likely to have no contact with participants or sensitive data)

## **About Mercy Corps**

Mercy Corps is a leading global organization powered by the belief that a better world is possible.In disaster, in hardship, in more than 40 countries around the world, we partner to put bold solutionsinto action — helping people triumph over adversity and build stronger communities from within.

Now, and for the future. Mercy Corps is transitioning to Prosper Global. Learn more [**here**](https://www.prosperglobal.org/mercy-corps). As the transition is being implemented by location, you may see the Mercy Corps and Prosper Global names used concurrently during this period. This is an administrative transition, and our teams, programs and commitments continue without interruption.

**The Program / Department / Team**

Nigeria is Africa's most populous country, and its influence spreads across the continent. Yet, inequality and insecurity have consistently undermined Nigeria's development. Mercy Corps Nigeria was established in 2012 to respond to these challenges. The Nigeria team is headquartered in Abuja, the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), and has programs across 16 states. Mercy Corps works with communities to build economic opportunities, enhance water security, drive peace and good governance, and ensure food security. Our activities aim to build resilience through an integrated approach, helping communities and the most marginalized within them cope, adapt, and thrive in the context of numerous shocks and stresses. With a strong and growing team, Mercy Corps works to achieve the vision of a Nigeria in which all people are empowered, engaged, resilient, and secure.

**The Position**

The **Evidence, Measurement, Learning & Impact Director** is a senior leadership position responsible for shaping and leading the program's evidence, learning, impact, and adaptive management agenda. The role ensures that data, evidence, technology, and learning are leveraged as strategic assets to improve program performance, inform decision-making, strengthen accountability, and support sustainable development outcomes.

The Director will lead the development and stewardship of integrated measurement, learning, knowledge management, and impact systems that transform data into actionable insights, enabling adaptive management, innovation, organizational learning, and evidence-based decision-making across the program.

Working closely with program leadership, partners, and technical teams, the Director will oversee the design and implementation of evidence, learning, and impact systems that strengthen performance management, support continuous improvement, and generate high-quality evidence to inform strategy, implementation, and learning.

The position will provide strategic oversight of digital systems, research initiatives, impact measurement approaches, evaluations, and knowledge-management platforms to better understand program effectiveness and inform adaptive action. The Director will ensure that evidence and learning are systematically translated into improved decision-making, stronger program quality, enhanced accountability, and sustainable results.

The Director will also support partner organizations in strengthening evidence generation, learning, and data utilization practices while fostering a culture of learning, accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement across the program.

**Essential Responsibilities**

STRATEGY AND VISION

- Provide visionary leadership Development Programs’ Evidence, Learning and Impact agenda, positioning evidence, data, technology, and learning as strategic assets that drive decision-making, portfolio performance, systems change, and long-term impact.
- Design and oversee a portfolio-wide Evidence, Learning and Impact ecosystem that enables harmonized data systems, shared services, real-time decision support, and consistent measurement across all consortium partners while generating insights that can be leveraged by broader sector actors.
- Champion the transformation of data into actionable intelligence by driving the use of analytics, digital platforms, participant feedback, market intelligence, and emerging technologies to inform strategy, adaptive management, investment decisions, and program innovation.
- Lead the generation and curation of evidence that demonstrates what works, for whom, under what conditions, and why, ensuring that portfolio learning informs implementation, strengthens market systems, influences policy and practice, and contributes to sector-wide knowledge.
- Establish a culture of learning, accountability, and continuous improvement across the portfolio, ensuring evidence is routinely translated into action, adaptation, and improved outcomes for young people to access job opportunities.
- Position Mercy Corps as a leader in evidence-driven programming by building partnerships with research institutions, governments, private sector actors, and learning networks, and generating influential insights, thought leadership, and scalable models that inform policy, strengthen practice, and contribute to sustainable systems-level change.

MEL SYSTEM DEVELOPMENT

- Lead the design, development, and continuous evolution of an integrated portfolio-wide **Evidence, Measurement, Learning & Impact Director,** ecosystem that enables adaptive management, real-time performance monitoring, impact measurement, and accountability to Mercy Corps standards.
- Serve as a member of the Portfolio Senior Leadership Team, providing strategic intelligence and evidence-based insights that inform portfolio decisions, resource allocation, risk management, innovation, and adaptive management across all consortium partners.
- Establish and oversee portfolio-wide data governance frameworks, standards, and protocols to ensure data quality, security, interoperability, ethical data management, and responsible use of participant information across all systems and partners.
- Design and institutionalize shared Evidence, Learning and Impact services that harmonize measurement approaches, reporting standards, analytics, learning processes, and performance management systems across the portfolio.
- Champion the use of digital technologies, automation, analytics, dashboards, artificial intelligence, and real-time decision-support tools to transform data into actionable intelligence that improves program effectiveness and accelerates impact.
- Lead the development of integrated learning, feedback, and accountability systems that strengthen participant voice, support adaptive management, and ensure evidence is routinely translated into program improvements and strategic decisions.
- Collaborate with Community Accountability and Response Mechanism (CARM) teams, safeguarding leads, and technical specialists to strengthen portfolio-wide accountability, participant-centered learning, and responsible data practices.
- Build the capacity of consortium partners to generate, interpret, and use evidence for decision-making, fostering a culture of learning, innovation, accountability, and continuous improvement across the portfolio.
- Work closely with global, regional, technology, analytics, and data teams to introduce emerging approaches, strengthen digital infrastructure, and position the portfolio as a leader in evidence-driven climate-smart agriculture programming.
- Ensure portfolio systems generate high-quality evidence and learning products that not only support implementation but also contribute to policy influence, systems change, sector learning, and the advancement of job opportunities for young people.

LEARNING AND ADAPTATION:

- Lead the Portfolio Learning Agenda, ensuring the generation of actionable evidence on what works, for whom, under what conditions, and why, to strengthen the portfolio's contribution to jobs for young people.
- Establish portfolio-wide learning and adaptive management processes that integrate implementation data, participant feedback, market intelligence, climate evidence, and partner experiences to inform strategic decisions, program adaptation, and investment priorities.
- Drive the generation, synthesis, and dissemination of high-value evidence, insights, and learning products that influence portfolio strategy, strengthen ecosystem actors, inform policy engagement, and contribute to broader sector knowledge and practice.
- Foster a culture of learning, innovation, and evidence use across portfolio partners, ensuring that lessons and insights are translated into improved performance, adaptive action, and scalable approaches that benefit both the portfolio and the wider climate-smart agriculture ecosystem.

REPORTS MANAGEMENT

- Provide strategic oversight of portfolio reporting, ensuring timely, high-quality, and evidence-based reporting that demonstrates results, impact, learning, and contribution to systems change.
- Lead the generation, synthesis, and communication of evidence, insights, and knowledge products, transforming data into actionable intelligence that informs decision-making, influences stakeholders, and supports adaptive management.
- Establish and maintain portfolio-wide reporting standards and quality assurance processes, ensuring consistency, data integrity, and effective knowledge sharing across all portfolio partners.

MONITORING AND EVALUATION/ ASSESSMENTS

- Liaise with the baseline lead to ensure baseline methodology, tools, and approaches are in line with overall program MEL.
- Support in ensuring baseline quality of data in compliance with MEL Policy, including leading on coordination for quarterly programme review meetings, regular Data Quality Assessments, record retention, and a final internal performance review.

TEAM MANAGEMENT

- Onboard the new permanent MEL Manager and other MEL team members.
- Ensure smooth handover of MEL framework, plans, and tools to the permanent team.
- Assist team members with information, tools, and resources to improve performance and reach objectives.
- Promote accountability, communicate expectations, and provide constructive feedback informally and formally via regular one-on-ones and performance reviews.
- Create and sustain a work environment of mutual respect where team members strive to achieve excellence.
- Play an active role in hiring, orienting, and leading team members as necessary.

### SAFEGUARDING RESPONSIBILITIES

- Actively learns safeguarding and integrates it into their work, including safeguarding risks and mitigations related to their area of work.
- Practices the values of Mercy Corps, including respecting the dignity and well-being of participants and fellow team members.
- Encourages openness and communication in their team; encourages team members to submit reports if they have any concerns using reporting mechanisms, e.g., Integrity Hotline and other options.

**Supervisory Responsibility**

MEL Programme managers and Advisors. Mentorship and support to local partner MEL teams

**Accountability**

### **Reports Directly To:** COP Programs

### **Works Directly With:** Country Director, Country MEL Manager, Director of Programmes, MSD Lead, Climate Director, GESI Director, HQ/ Regional MEL Team

**Accountability to Participants and Stakeholders**

Mercy Corps team members are expected to support all efforts toward accountability, specifically to our program participants, community partners, other stakeholders, and to international standards guiding international relief and development work. We are committed to actively engaging communities as equal partners in the design, monitoring, and evaluation of our field projects.

- Advanced degree/s in Statistics, Data Science, Economics, Public Policy, International Development, Organizational Learning, Information Systems, Social Sciences, or a related discipline.
- Minimum of 10 years of international experience in progressively senior leadership roles, including Director-level or above responsibilities in Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL), Evidence and Learning, Data and Analytics, Program Performance, Impact Measurement, or Performance Management for large, complex development portfolios.
- Proven experience designing and leading enterprise-scale evidence, learning, impact, and performance ecosystems that enable data-driven decision-making, adaptive management, accountability, and organizational performance improvement.
- Demonstrated success in transforming data and evidence into strategic insights that influence program direction, executive decision-making, donor investments, policy engagement, and systems change.
- Strong experience leading the development and deployment of digital and technology-enabled performance management systems, including data analytics, business intelligence, visualization platforms, automation, artificial intelligence, and real-time decision-support tools.
- Proven track record of leading portfolio-wide learning agendas, evaluations, research, impact measurement, knowledge management, and adaptive management processes for large-scale development investments.
- Experience providing strategic advisory support to senior leadership teams and serving as a thought partner on portfolio performance, impact, innovation, and organizational learning.
- Demonstrated ability to build and lead high-performing teams and strengthen the capacity of organizations and partners to generate, interpret, and use evidence to improve performance and results.
- Strong understanding of market systems development, youth employment, economic inclusion, climate-smart agriculture, resilience, and systems-change programming in Africa.
- Outstanding communication, facilitation, and influencing skills, with the ability to effectively engage senior leaders, donors, governments, research institutions, private sector actors, and ecosystem partners.
- Experience working with major international donors, foundations, or large-scale development investments; experience with Mastercard Foundation-funded programs would be a strong advantage.

***Success Factors***

The ideal candidate will have a strong curiosity for understanding and working effectively within the complex cultural, political, security, and social environment of Nigeria. They will be excellent communicators, multi-tasker, and able to work in ambiguous situations. They will be tolerant and flexible individual able to work in difficult and stressful environments and follow procedures. The successful candidate will be focused on team building and capacity-building of national staff; be a strategic thinker, and have strong skills in design, monitoring and evaluation of development programmes.

**Living Conditions / Environmental Conditions**

The Director - Evidence Learning & Impact will be based in Abuja, Nigeria. This position requires at least 40% of time traveling by flight or road to field offices in areas with varying degrees of insecurity.

Mercy Corps team members represent the agency both during and outside work hours when deployed in a field posting or on a visit/TDY to a field posting. Team members are expected to conduct themselves in a professional manner and respect local laws, customs, and Mercy Corps’ policies, procedures, and values at all times and in all in-country venues.

**Accountability to Participants and Stakeholders**

Mercy Corps team members are expected to support all efforts toward accountability, specifically to our program participants, community partners, other stakeholders, and to international standards guiding international relief and development work. We are committed to actively engaging communities as equal partners in the design, monitoring, and evaluation of our field projects.

**Ongoing Learning**

In support of our belief that learning organizations are more effective, efficient, and relevant to the communities we serve, we empower all team members to dedicate 5% of their time to learning activities that further their personal and/or professional growth and development

**Team Efficiency and Effectiveness**

Achieving our mission starts with how we build our team and collaborate. By bringing together individuals with a variety of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives, we strengthen our ability to solve complex challenges and drive innovation. We foster a culture of trust and respect, where every team member is valued for their contributions, empowered to reach their full potential, and motivated to do their best work.

We recognize that building a strong and effective team is an ongoing process, and we remain committed to learning, improving, and growing together.

**Equal Employment Opportunity**

Mercy Corps is an equal opportunity employer that does not tolerate discrimination on any basis. We actively seek out different backgrounds, perspectives, and skills so that we can be collectively stronger and have sustained global impact.

We are committed to providing an environment of respect and psychological safety where equal employment opportunities are available to all. We do not engage in or tolerate discrimination based on race, color, gender identity, gender expression, religion, age, sexual orientation, national or ethnic origin, disability (including HIV/AIDS status), marital status, military veteran status or any other protected group in the locations where we work.

**Safeguarding & Ethics**

Mercy Corps is committed to ensuring that all individuals we come into contact with through our work, whether team members, community members, program participants or others, are treated with respect and dignity. We are committed to the core principles regarding the prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse laid out by the UN Secretary-General and IASC **and have signed on to the** [**Interagency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme**](https://www.schr.info/the-misconduct-disclosure-scheme)**.** We will not tolerate child abuse, sexual exploitation, abuse, or harassment by or of our team members. As part of our commitment to a safe and inclusive work environment, team members are expected to conduct themselves professionally, respect local laws and customs, and to adhere to [Mercy Corps Code of Conduct Policies](https://www.mercycorps.org/who-we-are/ethics-policies) and values at all times. Team members are required to complete mandatory Code of Conduct e-learning courses upon hire and on an annual basis.

As an applicant, if you witness or experience any form of sexual misconduct during the recruitment process, please report this to Mercy Corps Integrity Hotline (integrityhotline@mercycorps.org).

jobs.title: 23520 Regional Data Analyst (P)
jobs.body:
Under the overall supervision of the Deputy Regional Director (DRD) for Operations, the direct supervision of the Regional Thematic Specialist (Data and Research), and the guidance of the Chief Migration and Displacement Data and Research Analytics Division in the Department of Data, Insights and Policy, the Regional Data Analyst will focus on generating and communicating analyses and insights in support of decision-making processes. The Regional Data Analyst is responsible for leading Regional Data Hub (RDH) work on migration data analysis, focusing on migration and human mobility dynamics, including mixed migration movements, drivers, trends, and characteristics across the region.

The Regional Data Analyst will work within the RDH Team to pursue its core objective to enhance, strengthen, and promote the regional evidence base on migration and human mobility, including by addressing existing primary data gaps through innovation, insight generation, foresight and scenario building, and consolidating primary and secondary data and analysis work in the region covering migration, displacement, and human mobility.

**Responsibilities**

**Data Processing and Data Use:**

- Locate and define new data analysis process improvement opportunities.
- Identify appropriate data sources for analytics projects.
- Ensure accurate and reliable data centralization to support analytical work.
- Collaborate with Data Engineers and Data Scientists in Headquarters (HQ) or other Missions as available and needed to improve data flows, data quality, etc.
- Coordinate the development and implementation of databases, data collection systems, data analytics and other strategies that optimize statistical efficiency and quality.

**Data Analysis and Reporting:**

- Conduct and coordinate regional, sub-regional, geographic and thematic analyses and reports on issues of relevance to the current human mobility and migration dynamics in the region, paying attention to routes, trends, and patterns which may necessitate additional analysis.
- Identify gaps in migration and human mobility data, specific data needs for local, national, regional, sub-regional and global policymaking, and capacities of relevant actors on migration and human mobility data. Respond to queries on gaps identified by thematic experts. Coordinate the development of tools and mechanisms to complete data gaps, in close alignment with international approaches and standards and existing IOM-supported global mechanisms.
- Support the analysis and validation of internal, cross-border, and international migration and human mobility data collected at various points along the migration journey - at departure, en route, in destination, and upon return- stranded or in need of assistance, voluntary and forced, humanitarian evacuations, support to migrants on socioeconomic inclusion and reintegration, and strengthening their development contributions to societies.
- Use existing IOM data from global, regional, sub-regional and national projects and initiatives for data triangulation to enhance cross-thematic data analysis for regional and national reporting within the region and to strengthen evidence-based policy formulation, national and regional humanitarian and development planning and operations. Coordinate and support cross-regional analysis where relevant.
- Coordinate and support desk reviews and carry out extensive and in-depth analysis of data sources identified under the desk review.
- Identify, analyze, and interpret trends or patterns, using basic machine learning techniques, qualitative, visualization, narrative, and statistical methods to identify relevant features and variables in structured and unstructured sources of information and data.
- Coordinate the development and implementation of various analysis, reporting and quality control capabilities.
- Provide analytical support to Country Offices in the Region as needed.

**Good Data Practice, Knowledge Management and Dissemination:**

- Ensure timely preparation and generation of information products.
- Adhere to IOM data protection, governance, and security standards.
- Consider ethical data collection, use, sharing, and dissemination.
- Participate in working groups and provide strategic input on behalf of IOM.

**Cross-Cutting Issues:**

- Evaluate new applications related to information systems, to new technologies, and processes to manage information in response to RDH needs.
- Ensure the integration of disaggregated data analysis to inform gender-responsive programming, including for specific needs of people such as pregnant women, persons with disabilities, the elderly, children, as well as other highly vulnerable groups within all emergency and transition activities.
- Perform other duties as may be assigned.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master’s degree in Migration Studies, Demography, Political or Social Science, Statistics, Econometrics, Public Health, Sustainability Science, Data Science, or a related field from an accredited academic institution with five years of relevant professional experience; or,
- University degree in the above fields with seven years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Experience in information management, reporting, coordination, and analysis of data triangulation and analysis from multiple large and complex information systems;
- Data analysis experience (including field experience) in the area of demographic and population studies, human mobility, internal and international migration, and refugees/IDPs in developed and developing countries; remote sensing and/or Geographic Information Systems (GIS) analysis experience is also an advantage;
- Practical field experience and analysis expertise in geographic (region and/or specific countries) and thematic (displacement, migration) relevant domain;
- Experience in data collection, data processing (incl. cleaning), data analysis for research, policy, and report writing;
- Experience in internal and/or international mixed migration data analyses is required;
- Self-service analytics and data visualization applications (MS Power BI, Qlik, Tableau or similar), or business intelligence tools (SAP Business Objects, etc.) are desirable;
- Experience with database or programming languages (SQL, Python, R) is desirable; other data analysis software may be advantageous (e.g., STATA, QGIS);
- Professional experience in coordinating multi-cultural teams and field-based staff;
- Experience in survey and questionnaire design and sampling is an advantage; and,
- Knowledge of IOM data, analytical methodologies and standards is an advantage.

**Skills**

- Excellent drafting skills; Proven skills to analyse statistical information;
- Ability to formulate IM-related technical requirements and operating procedures;
- Ability to translate planning specifications into technical briefs for data capture and analysis, and vice versa;
- Ability to compile and holistically analyse diverse datasets;
- Demonstrated team-building and information management skills; and,
- Demonstrated understanding of different data analysis methodologies.

**Languages**

For this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

jobs.title: Gender, Safeguarding and Inclusion (GESI) Director, Climate-Smart Agriculture (CSA) Nigeria
jobs.body:
**\*\*Contingent upon Donor Funding\*\***

**Location:** Abuja, Nigeria

**Position Status:** Full-time, Exempt or Non-exempt, Regular

[**Risk Level:**](https://library.mercycorps.org/record/47705?ln=en) X **Level 3** ☐**Level 2** ☐**Level 1**

(Level 3: Frequent contact with participants, direct contact with children, access to sensitive data, and/or high level of accountability.

Level 2: Some contact with participants; unplanned non-direct contact with children.

Level 1: Likely to have no contact with participants or sensitive data)

## **About Mercy Corps**

Mercy Corps is a leading global organization powered by the belief that a better world is possible. In disaster, in hardship, in more than 40 countries around the world, we partner to put bold solutions into action — helping people triumph over adversity and build stronger communities from within.

Now, and for the future. Mercy Corps is transitioning to Prosper Global. Learn more [**here**](https://www.prosperglobal.org/mercy-corps). As the transition is being implemented by location, you may see the Mercy Corps and Prosper Global names used concurrently during this period. This is an administrative transition, and our teams, programs and commitments continue without interruption

## **The Program / Department / Team**

Nigeria is Africa's most populous country, and its influence spreads across the continent. Yet, inequality and insecurity have consistently undermined Nigeria's development. Mercy Corps Nigeria was established in 2012 to respond to these challenges. The Nigeria team is headquartered in Abuja, the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), and has programs across 16 states. Mercy Corps works with communities to build economic opportunities, enhance water security, drive peace and good governance, and ensure food security. Our activities aim to build resilience through an integrated approach, helping communities and the most marginalized within them cope, adapt, and thrive in the context of numerous shocks and stresses. With a strong and growing team, Mercy Corps works to achieve the vision of a Nigeria in which all people are empowered, engaged, resilient, and secure.

## **The Position**

The Gender, Safeguarding and Inclusion Director will provide strategic leadership and technical oversight for gender equality, social inclusion, youth empowerment, and safeguarding across program activities. The Director will ensure that inclusive, equitable, and participant-centered approaches are integrated throughout the program lifecycle and embedded within implementation, learning, adaptation, and partner engagement.

S/he will be responsible for leading the implementation of gender integration strategies aimed at ensuring that program activities result in positive outcomes for male and female participants of different age groups. S/he will have overall responsibility for building team members’ and partners’ capacity to integrate a GESI perspective into activities, and raising awareness of the importance of GESI integration. The Gender, Social and Inclusion Director will work closely with other team members to ensure the effective and timely execution of activities related to gender and age-based access to opportunities. GESI Director will conduct a gender analysis to inform and guide program implementation and to ensure that men, women, girls and boys have equitable opportunities to engage in and benefit from program activities. S/he will promote innovative initiatives for inclusiveness in conformity with the donor and Mercy Corps’ gender policy.

## **Essential Job Responsibilities**

### **STRATEGY & PLANNING**

- Provide strategic leadership and vision for the integration of Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI), youth empowerment, and safeguarding across the Mercy Corps Nigerian Programs.
- Lead the development and implementation of program-wide GESI and Safeguarding strategies, ensuring alignment with Mercy Corps standards, donor requirements, and national frameworks.
- Ensure gender-transformative, youth-centered, disability-inclusive, and safeguarding approaches are embedded throughout the program lifecycle, from design and partner onboarding through implementation, adaptation, learning, and closeout.
- Serve as the principal advisor to program leadership and implementing partners on GESI, youth inclusion, protection, and safeguarding priorities, risks, and opportunities.
- Drive the development of strategies that increase equitable access to economic, social, and development opportunities for women, youth, persons with disabilities, and other marginalized group
- Provide technical leadership to ensure safeguarding considerations are incorporated into program design, implementation plans, partnership agreements, participant engagement approaches, and monitoring systems.
- Lead the identification, assessment, and mitigation of gender, inclusion, protection, and safeguarding risks across program activities and partnerships.
- Establish program-wide standards, tools, indicators, and accountability mechanisms to measure and track GESI, youth empowerment, and safeguarding outcomes.
- Collaborate with technical leads and implementing partners to ensure GESI, youth, and safeguarding commitments are reflected in annual work plans, budgets, learning agendas, and performance targets.
- Promote evidence-based decision-making by leveraging data, research, participant feedback, and learning to continuously strengthen inclusive and safeguarding-centered programming.
- Champion a culture of inclusion, safeguarding, accountability, and participant-centered programming across all program teams, partners, and stakeholders
- Represent the program externally on GESI, youth empowerment, and safeguarding matters with government institutions, private sector actors, technical working groups, and other key stakeholders.
- Ensure that safeguarding, inclusion, and participant well-being remain central to program strategy and decision-making, enabling equitable participation and access to opportunities for all participants

### **PROGRAM MANAGEMENT**

- Develop targeted GESI capacity building interventions for program staff.
- Support program team in the delivery of training and capacity building on key gender and social inclusion topics to project participants.
- Conduct periodic monitoring of field activities; ensure quality delivery of GESI interventions and coach/mentor staff technically on this.
- Document processes and achievements to ensure impact and best practices are captured and disseminated. This will include the continual re-evaluation of program activities and information, with resulting activity adjustments in keeping with new insights.

**REPRESENTATION**

- Develop relationships and linkages with organizations implementing other donor-funded programs focused on GESI in Nigeria.
- Conduct regular community consultations to ensure programming remains GESI sensitive and on track.
- Collect and share learnings and best practices from this program both internally and externally.
- Identify, build and manage collaborative partnerships with implementing partners, donors, local governments, civil society organizations, private sector actors, and other stakeholders
- Communicate effectively to ensure overall program targets and donor obligations are met.

**SECURITY AND RISK MANAGEMENT**

- Collaborate with country leadership to support preparedness and response to major disruptive events.
- Work closely with the country team’s security focal point to develop and maintain systems that promote the safety and security of all team members.
- Ensure that activities are designed and implemented with a clear analysis and understanding of security.

#### Safeguarding Responsibilities

- Actively learns about safeguarding and integrates it into their work, including safeguarding risks and mitigations related to their area of work.
- Practices the values of Prosper Global including respecting the dignity and well-being of participants and fellow team members.
- Encourages openness and communication in their team; encourages team members to submit reports if they have any concerns using reporting mechanisms e.g., Integrity Hotline and other options.

## **Supervisory Responsibility**

- Supervise Mercy Corps GESI and safeguarding team members and provide technical guidance, mentorship, and capacity strengthening support to partner organizations

## **Accountability**

**Reports Directly To:** Chief of Party / Program Director

**Works Directly With:** Program leadership team, technical leads, MEL team, finance and operations teams, partner organizations, regional teams, and HQ technical advisors

## **Minimum Qualification & Transferable Skills**

- MA/S or equivalent experience in development studies, international relations, women’s studies, gender studies, sociology or other social science discipline.
- At least seven years’ experience in gender, youth and social dynamics development work at the community level.
- Experience developing and conducting gender training, gender/youth/social dynamics mainstreaming and engaging in gender advocacy.
- 10 plus years in Senior Program level positions
- Understanding of donor regulations, compliance requirements, and program management systems for large development programs.
- Demonstrated experience in gender equality, safeguarding, social inclusion, women's empowerment, youth development, protection, or related technical leadership roles
- Experience supporting gender equality, social inclusion, youth empowerment, safeguarding, protection, economic development, resilience, or community development programs.
- Demonstrated capacity to lead the collection, analysis and utilization of information from a broad range of sources to ensure effective integration of gender and youth concerns throughout the program’s duration.
- In-depth understanding of gender, age and other locally significant socio-cultural factors in the context of food and nutrition security and resilience programming.
- Skills in participatory learning and facilitating collaborative problem-solving.
- Prior humanitarian and/or development experience working in a context similar to Nigeria.
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English.
- Excellent computer skills (especially Microsoft office applications) and ability to use information technology as a tool and resource.

**Success Factors**

The successful candidate will be a strategic and collaborative leader with a strong commitment to gender equality, social inclusion, safeguarding, and participant-centered programming. They will possess strong technical expertise and the ability to influence diverse stakeholders to ensure that inclusive and equitable approaches are integrated across all aspects of program implementation.

The ideal candidate will demonstrate excellent relationship-building, communication, and facilitation skills and be capable of working effectively with communities, government institutions, private sector actors, donors, and implementing partners. They will foster a culture of accountability, learning, and continuous improvement while ensuring that safeguarding, inclusion, and participant well-being remain central to program design, implementation, monitoring, and decision-making.

They will be an effective mentor and capacity builder, strengthening the ability of teams and partners to deliver high-quality, inclusive programming that contributes to sustainable and meaningful outcomes for participants and communities.

## **Living Conditions / Environmental Conditions**

The GESI Director will be based in Abuja Nigeria. This position requires at least 40% of time traveling by flight or road to field offices in areas with varying degrees of insecurity.

Mercy Corps team members represent the agency both during and outside work hours when deployed in a field posting or on a visit/TDY to a field posting. Team members are expected to conduct themselves in a professional manner and respect local laws, customs, and Mercy Corps’ policies, procedures, and values at all times and in all in-country venues.

## **Accountability to Participants and Stakeholders**

Mercy Corps team members are expected to support all efforts toward accountability, specifically to our program participants, community partners, other stakeholders, and to international standards guiding international relief and development work. We are committed to actively engaging communities as equal partners in the design, monitoring, and evaluation of our field projects.

## **Ongoing Learning**

In support of our belief that learning organizations are more effective, efficient, and relevant to the communities we serve, we empower all team members to dedicate 5% of their time to learning activities that further their personal and/or professional growth and development

## **Team Efficiency and Effectiveness**

Achieving our mission starts with how we build our team and collaborate. By bringing together individuals with a variety of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives, we strengthen our ability to solve complex challenges and drive innovation. We foster a culture of trust and respect, where every team member is valued for their contributions, empowered to reach their full potential, and motivated to do their best work.

We recognize that building a strong and effective team is an ongoing process, and we remain committed to learning, improving, and growing together.

## **Equal Employment Opportunity**

Mercy Corps is an equal opportunity employer committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all employees and qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, sex, sexual orientation, religion or belief, national origin, age, disability, marital status, veteran status, or any other characteristics protected under applicable law.is an equal opportunity employer that does not tolerate discrimination on any basis. We actively seek out different backgrounds, perspectives, and skills so that we can be collectively stronger and have sustained global impact.

## **Safeguarding & Ethics**

Mercy Corps is committed to ensuring that all individuals we come into contact with through our work, whether team members, community members, program participants or others, are treated with respect and dignity. We are committed to the core principles regarding the prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse laid out by the UN Secretary-General and IASC **and have signed on to the** [**Interagency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme**](https://www.schr.info/the-misconduct-disclosure-scheme)**.** We will not tolerate child abuse, sexual exploitation, abuse, or harassment by or of our team members. As part of our commitment to a safe and inclusive work environment, team members are expected to conduct themselves professionally, respect local laws and customs, and to adhere to [Mercy Corps Code of Conduct Policies](https://www.mercycorps.org/who-we-are/ethics-policies) and values at all times. Team members are required to complete mandatory Code of Conduct e-learning courses upon hire and on an annual basis.

As an applicant, if you witness or experience any form of sexual misconduct during the recruitment process, please report this to Mercy Corps Integrity Hotline (integrityhotline@mercycorps.org).

jobs.body:
**About Bodmando Consulting Group**

Bodmando Consulting Group is a feminist international consulting firm registered in **Uganda** and **Kenya.** As a women-led social enterprise, Bodmando operates at the gender and climate nexus, driven by the vision of a world free from intergenerational poverty, gender inequality, and social injustice. Our work is anchored in intersectional analysis, systems thinking, and human-centred design, ensuring that every solution we craft is both inclusive and transformative. With a multidisciplinary core team spanning Africa, South Asia, and the MENA region, we deliver high-impact research, evaluation, capacity strengthening and strategic advisory services that blend contextual understanding with global best practices.

We further leverage a global consultancy network of over 1,000 technical experts, allowing rapid mobilization of specialized skills for complex, multi-country assignments. Through thought leadership, north-south collaboration, and co-creation, Bodmando continues unlocking value and generating evidence-based, scalable solutions that advance equity, sustainability, and impact. To date, we have successfully implemented more than 65 projects across 31 countries, empowering governments, donors, civil society organizations, and communities to design, implement, and learn from transformative interventions. ***Learn more about our work at*** [***www.bodmando.org***](http://www.bodmando.org)***.***

Bodmando Consulting Group is seeking a creative, technically competent and proactive Female Web Designer & Digital Communications consultant to manage and strengthen the organisation’s digital presence. Kagoma, Wakiso district, Uganda
