jobs.title: Programme Management Consultant
jobs.body:
**Functional title:** Programme Management Consultant

**Duty station of assignment:** Istanbul, Türkiye

**Contract modality:** International ICA

**Grade:** IICA-2 equivalent

**Duration of assignment:** 6 months

**Closing date for applications:** 30 October 2026

## Background

The United Nations Human Settlements Programme (UN-Habitat) is the agency for human settlements. It is mandated by the UN General Assembly to promote socially and environmentally sustainable towns and cities with the goal of providing adequate shelter for all.

The Regional Office for Eastern Europe and Central Asia (ROEECA) leads UN-Habitat’s efforts to promote sustainable urban development across the region by supporting national and local governments in advancing inclusive, resilient, and resource-efficient cities. ROEECA is being established to facilitate regional cooperation, policy development, and capacity building to strengthen urban systems, including sustainable solid waste management and circular economy approaches. Through technical assistance, project development, and partnerships, ROEECA will support the transition towards zero-waste systems that integrate social inclusion, gender equality, and environmental sustainability, while mobilizing investments and scaling innovative solutions aligned with regional priorities and global commitments.

Urban Basic Services, including zero-waste is a core pillar of UN-Habitat’s work on sustainable urban basic services, promoting waste prevention, reduction, reuse, recycling, and recovery while avoiding disposal practices that harm health and the environment. In line with the United Nations General Assembly resolution 77/161 and the work of the UN Secretary-General’s Advisory Board on Zero Waste, UN-Habitat supports cities and regions in transitioning towards zero-waste systems that are inclusive, re-source-efficient, and socially just.

## Purpose of the assignment

To support programme and project development and provide technical expertise on zero waste and social inclusion in Eastern Europe and Central Asia, with a specific focus on circularity and integrating gender equality and disability inclusion into waste management policies, data systems, and programmes. The assignment will include coordination of regional zero-waste initiatives, development of technical publications, project proposals and engagement with United Nations Country Teams (UNCTs).

## Duties and main responsibilities

Under the overall supervision of the ROEECA Regional Director and in close coordination with the Chief, Urban Basic Services Section (UBSS), the incumbent will undertake the following duties:

- Facilitate coordination between ROEECA, UBSS, and relevant regional and country-level initiatives related to zero-waste and social inclusion.
- Coordinate the development of project concepts and proposals and support the regional roll-out and contextualization of zero-waste approaches and circularity, aligned with UN-Habitat regional priorities and the strategic plan.
- Provide technical expertise on zero waste and social inclusion, including waste prevention, organic waste management, recycling systems, and recovery solutions.
- Identify policy, institutional, and infrastructure gaps hindering the transition to zero-waste systems, with particular attention to impacts on women, persons with disabilities, and vulnerable groups.
- Represent ROEECA, as required, in technical meetings, webinars, and knowledge exchanges related to Urban Basic Services, zero-waste and inclusion.
- Support the integration of social inclusion and gender equality into project development, implementation and related technical outputs.
- Support partnership development and resource mobilization by identifying funding opportunities, engaging relevant partners and contributing to the preparation of project concepts and funding proposals.
- Perform other related duties as required.

The assignment will focus on the development of zero-waste technical publications, coordination of relevant global and regional initiatives, preparation of project concepts and funding proposals, and technical support to priority country engagements. Detailed deliverables, timelines and payment arrangements will be established in accordance with the applicable contractual procedures.

## Competencies

**Professionalism:** Knowledge in the project management cycle and of project lifetimes, from resource mobilization and inception to implementation, evaluation and audit. Ability to identify issues, analyze and participate in the resolution of issues/problems. Ability to conduct data collection using various methods. Conceptual analytical and evaluative skills to conduct independent research and analysis, including familiarity with and experience in the use of various research sources, including electronic sources on the internet, intranet and other databases. Ability to apply judgment in the context of assignments given, plan own work and manage conflicting priorities. The ability to analyze and interpret data in support of decision-making and convey resulting information to management. Shows pride in work and in achievements; demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter; is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines and achieving results; is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns; shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges; remains calm in stressful situations. Takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work. **Planning and Organising:** Develops clear goals that are consistent with agreed strategies; identifies priority activities and assignments; adjusts priorities as required; allocates appropriate amount of time and resources for completing work; foresees risks and allows for contingencies when planning; monitors and adjusts plans and actions as necessary; uses time efficiently. **Client Orientation:** Considers all those to whom services are provided to be "clients" and seeks to see things from clients' point of view; establishes and maintains productive partnerships with clients by gaining their trust and respect; identifies clients' needs and matches them to appropriate solutions; monitors ongoing developments inside and outside the clients' environment to keep informed and anticipate problems; keeps clients informed of progress or setbacks in projects; meets timeline for delivery of products or services to client.

## Required Skills and Experience

### Education

- Advanced university degree (Master's degree or equivalent) in international development, international affairs, environmental management, urban planning, public policy or a related field is required.
- A first-level university degree in combination with two (2) additional years of qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree.

### Experience

- A minimum of five (5) years of relevant professional experience in project management, programme coordination, municipal solid waste management or a related field, including experience in project development, is required. Candidates holding a first-level university degree (Bachelor's degree or equivalent) must have a minimum of seven (7) years of relevant professional experience.
- Experience in sustainable solid waste management, zero-waste initiatives or circular economy approaches is desirable.
- Experience in programme management in Eastern Europe and Central Asia is desirable.

### Language

- English and French are the working languages of the United Nations Secretariat. For this position, fluency in English is required. Knowledge of another official UN language is desirable.

jobs.title: Associate, Malaria and NTDs
jobs.body:
## **Overview**

The Clinton Health Access Initiative, Inc. (CHAI) is a global health organization committed to our mission of saving lives and reducing the burden of disease in low-and middle-income countries. We work at the invitation of governments to support them and the private sector to create and sustain high-quality health systems.

CHAI was founded in 2002 in response to the HIV/AIDS epidemic with the goal of dramatically reducing the price of life-saving drugs and increasing access to these medicines in the countries with the highest burden of the disease. Over the following two decades, CHAI has expanded its focus. Today, along with HIV, we work with our partners to prevent and treat infectious diseases such as COVID-19, malaria, tuberculosis, and hepatitis. Our work has also expanded into cancer, diabetes, hypertension, and other non-communicable diseases, and we work to accelerate the rollout of lifesaving vaccines, reduce maternal and child mortality, combat chronic malnutrition, and increase access to assistive technology. We are investing in horizontal approaches to strengthen health systems through programs in human resources for health, digital health, and health financing. With each new and innovative program, our strategy is grounded in maximizing sustainable impact at scale, ensuring that governments lead the solutions, that programs are designed to scale nationally, and learnings are shared globally.

At CHAI, our people are our greatest asset, and none of this work would be possible without their talent, time, dedication, and passion for our mission and values. We are a highly diverse team of enthusiastic individuals across 40 countries with a broad range of skill sets and life experiences. CHAI is deeply grounded in the countries we work in, with the majority of our staff based in program countries. Learn more about our exciting work: [http://www.clintonhealthaccess.org](http://www.clintonhealthaccess.org/).

*CHAI is an Equal Opportunity Employer, and is committed to providing an environment of fairness, and mutual respect where all applicants have access to equal employment opportunities. CHAI values diversity and inclusion, and recognizes that our mission is best advanced by the leadership and contributions of people with diverse experience, backgrounds, and culture.*

**Position Overview**

Your responsibilities will involve supporting the malaria program in scaling up interventions to effectively reduce the disease burden in Angola. The selected candidate will be responsible for a wide range of tasks, from conducting quantitative and qualitative analyses, to designing data-driven strategic plans, to providing operational support to ensure the execution of effective, high-impact programs. The Associate will develop and maintain strong relationships with CHAI teams supporting the malaria program, as well as with relevant government, technical, and implementing partners. They will also identify areas for intervention related to improvements in vector control, surveillance, and program implementation, and be able to initiate work plans to address these issues quickly and with limited guidance.

The candidate must have excellent analytical, problem-solving, organizational, communication, and project management skills, as well as strong cultural sensitivity and emotional intelligence. The selected candidate must embody CHAI's values, including resourcefulness, patience, tenacity, humility, independence, frugality, and a strong work ethic.

The position will be based in Luanda, with frequent travel to Angola's provinces and occasional international travel.

## **Responsibilities**

- Provide technical assistance to the national malaria program to refine malaria control interventions.
- Support the development and monitoring of government strategies, roadmaps, and costed work plans.
- Work with CHAI colleagues and government counterparts to assess strategies, identify and prioritize resource gaps, and develop new funding proposals for the country.
- Contribute to the drafting, review, and feedback of technical products, which may include strategic plans, guidelines, grant proposals, donor reports, or implementation updates.
- Contribute to the design and execution of monitoring and evaluation to measure progress toward malaria control objectives (analysis of key indicators, design, and execution of monitoring and evaluation of surveillance platforms, etc.).
- Monitor program activities against project objectives and donor commitments, identify bottlenecks or operational shortcomings, and work collaboratively with national and global CHAI teams to achieve exceptional results within tight timelines.
- Identify new opportunities within and beyond the project's initial scope, anticipate risks, and be proactive in responding to them.
- Support the drafting of programmatic reports for government and donors, as well as concept notes or other external communication products.
- Perform any other duties requested by management.

## **Qualifications**

- Professional fluency in Portuguese and English, with excellent written and verbal communication skills in both languages.
- Bachelor's degree and two to three years of relevant professional experience.
- High level of proficiency in the MS Office suite, particularly Excel and PowerPoint.
- Ability to work independently and autonomously, balancing multiple tasks simultaneously.
- Exceptional analytical, quantitative, and problem-solving skills.
- Ability to deliver persuasive presentations and reports.
- Ability to think strategically while maintaining strong organizational skills and a detail-oriented approach.
- Ability to manage multiple tasks simultaneously and set priorities.
- Excellent interpersonal skills and a proven ability to build and maintain strong relationships in a multicultural environment.
- Willingness to travel frequently (30-50 percent of the time), including occasional travel to rural areas.

**Preferred qualifications**

- A master's degree or postgraduate qualification.
- Prior knowledge of malaria control and infectious diseases.
- Experience working in resource-limited settings, particularly in Angola.
- Fluency in at least one relevant local language.
- Prior experience working in fast-paced, results-oriented environments, such as consulting, management, investment banking, or industry.
- Experience working and communicating with government officials, multilateral organizations, or development donors.
- Experience working remotely with a decentralized/remote team.
- Experience working in developing-country contexts.

jobs.title: Data Entry Assistants
jobs.body:
**POSITION INFORMATION**

- **Organization:** UNDP Lebanon Through Stars Orbit Consultants and Management Development
- **VA No.: UNDP/LBN/VA26/203**
- **Position Title**: Data Entry Assistants
- **Duty Station:** Beirut
- **Duration:** 2 Months (without exceeding 18 working days per month)
- **Vacancy Date of Issue: 21 October 2026**
- **Vacancy Closure Date: 28 October 2026**
- **National or International consultancy:** National consultancy

To review the full Terms of Reference (TOR), please follow link:

[https://drive.google.com/file/d/1T8NzJatEZrMJtUOG7VOGUkM1-S9Ncvbm/view?usp=sharing](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1T8NzJatEZrMJtUOG7VOGUkM1-S9Ncvbm/view?usp=sharing)

**BACKGROUND**

Lebanon stands at a pivotal juncture in its governance and reform trajectory. Despite years of overlapping crises, the country has made landmark progress in building an integrity and anti-corruption framework, including the adoption and (partial) implementation of the National Anti-Corruption Strategy (2020–2025), the establishment of the National Anti-Corruption Commission (NACC), and major legislative reforms on access to information, illicit enrichment, whistleblower protection, asset declaration, and public procurement. These milestones have laid the groundwork for the most coherent accountability architecture in Lebanon’s recent history.

However, these achievements remain fragile amid deep economic collapse, weakened institutions, and eroded public trust. While the strategic and legal frameworks are largely in place, implementation and enforcement mechanisms remain underdeveloped, and coordination among oversight institutions is still limited. The evaluation of the NACS highlighted the urgent need to consolidate progress by operationalizing national mechanisms, strengthening institutional capacities, and embedding corruption-risk management practices across public institutions.

In this context, the Integrity in ACTion Project is founded with the objective of improving the implementation of an institutionalised and targeted approach to prevent and combat corruption through improved coordination, operationalized oversight, enhanced preventive and enforcement mechanisms, and institutionalized integrity and risk-management practices, thereby advancing transparency, accountability, and public trust. The Project is designed to achieve this objective by working on three outputs:

Output 1: Institutional capacities to coordinate, monitor, and evaluate the National Anti-Corruption Strategy strengthened and operationalized through participatory and inclusive mechanisms.

Output 2: Legal frameworks and oversight institutions for preventing and combating corruption strengthened and effectively operationalized.

Output 3: Sectoral Corruption Risk Management mechanisms and integrity systems strengthened across key public sectors.

Under output 3, “Sectoral Corruption Risk Management mechanisms and integrity systems strengthened across key public sectors.”, the Ministry of Industry, in collaboration with UNDP, is working to integrate the Sectoral Corruption Risk Management (SCRM) Methodology into its core regulatory functions. This partnership seeks to strengthen institutional integrity, reduce opportunities for corruption, and reinforce rule-based decision-making in the industrial licensing process. By applying the SCRM framework to the directorates/sections responsible for Industrial Permits and Certificates, the initiative has aimed to identify systemic vulnerabilities, enhance risk awareness among staff, and promote a culture of accountability. Furthermore, the Ministry of Industry (MoI) plays a central role in regulating Lebanon’s industrial sector and ensuring compliance with national standards and licensing requirements. At the heart of this mandate lies the responsibility to oversee the issuance of Industrial Permits and Certificates, an essential function for enabling lawful industrial activity, protecting the environment, and promoting sustainable economic development.

Building on UNDP’s support to the ministry of Industry, UNDP is seeking to contract admin assistants to support the ministry in organizing the Ministry's records of industrial permits and industrial certificates into a structured database. The database will use consistent fields and unique identifiers so that it can later be linked to the digitized inspection system. This will also allow the Ministry to track each establishment's permits, certificates, inspections and compliance status over time, and to update them as new inspections are carried out.

**SCOPE OF WORK, RESPONSIBILITIES AND DESCRIPTION OF THE PROPOSED ANALYTICAL WORK**

Under the general supervision of the UNDP IACT manager, and in close coordination with the NACC, the Admin Assistants will support coordination, documentation, and administrative follow-up functions. The Admin Assistant will be responsible for the following:

- Review the Ministry’s existing permit and certificate files and recording practices. Prepare a short inception note with a work plan, the proposed approach, and a timeline, and agree on it with the technical committee.
- Propose and finalize, in coordination with the committee, the database structure. This includes standardized fields, data formats, and a unique identifier for each establishment and each permit or certificate. The design should allow the database to be linked later to the digitized inspection system.
- Review existing permit and certificate files and sort them, for example:
    - by document type (industrial permit or industrial certificate)
    - by the five UIIS industrial clusters
    - by subsector and activity classification
- Initiate data entry for each establishment, record the key information, including but not limited to:
    - permit or certificate number
    - issue and expiry dates
    - current status
    - location
    - available inspection and compliance records
- Apply the filtering and classification criteria agreed by the technical committee consistently across all records.
- Identify and flag incomplete, duplicate, or inconsistent records. Maintain a log of flagged records and submit it to the committee for review and decision.
- Update the database as files are verified or corrected by the committee, so that the database stays accurate and current.
- Prepare a brief user guide or data dictionary describing the fields, codes, and update procedures.
- Submit a final report at the end of the assignment, summarizing records processed, data gaps identified, and recommendations for maintaining the database and integrating it with the inspection system.
- Ensure that all information is handled with strict confidentiality, in line with Ministry and UNDP rules. The consultant will not take part in any decision on individual applications, permits, certificates, or files.

**EXPECTED OUTPUTS AND DELIVERABLES**

The Consultant is expected to complete the above tasks and activities noting that the total duration should not exceed 2 months (without exceeding 18 working days per month).

**INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS**

- The consultant will work under the day-to-day management of the Ministry of Industry relevant staff.
- UNDP will be responsible for providing the contractor with all necessary materials related to the project in a timely thorough and transparent manner. UNDP will be also responsible to provide clarifications and facilitation of the work.
- Day to Day transportation from home to office (& vice versa) shall be covered by the Consultant’s own means. The Consultant will rely on his own means of communication and transportation.

**DURATION OF WORK**

The assigned duration for this consultancy is 2 months.

The mission is expected to commence immediately after contract signature, and to be completed 2 months from the contract signature date.

The time needed to review/comment/approve deliverables and outputs is (5) five working days.

**DUTY STATION**

The Admin Assistants will be based in Beirut in the Ministry of Industry premises.

**STANDARD MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**

- **Education:** At least a High School certificate.
- **Experience:** A minimum of 1 year of Experience in administrative or operational support, including but not limited to, data entry, maintaining filing systems, preparing administrative documentation, and conducting research, etc.
- **Language:** Fluency in Arabic and English.

**“The Personnel will be covered with Health insurance and Personal accident insurance; the fees shall be deducted from personnel's monthly payment”.**

jobs.title: Safeguarding Advisor - Francophone
jobs.body:
**About MSI**

MSI Reproductive Choices is one of the world’s leading providers of sexual and reproductive healthcare. We believe that everyone should have the right to choose. From contraception to safe abortion and life-saving post-abortion care, we are committed to delivering compassionate, affordable, high-quality services for all.

Today, our organisation has around 10,000 team members working in 36 countries across the world. Our success lies in the fact that MSI teams are locally led, entrepreneurial and results-driven, and are passionate about delivering high quality, client-centred care in their own communities. As a social business, we focus on sustainable delivery, efficiency, and funding models that are built to last, so that the women and girls we serve today will have a choice in the future too.

We know that access to reproductive choice is life changing. For some, it can mean the ability to complete an education or start a career. For others, it means being able to look after the family they already have. For everyone, it means the freedom to decide their own future, creating a fairer, more equal world.

**About the Role**

The Safeguarding Adviser role primarily supports the effective implementation of MSI’s Safeguarding work and Code of Conduct in Senegal, Mali, Burkina Faso, Niger, DRC and Madagascar. Using relevant materials and resources, it also supports LSDC’s training programme on other subjects such as AFB, practical Data Privacy and Due Diligence *(together with Safeguarding and Code of Conduct*, “Core Policies”).

As Safeguarding Adviser, you will be expected to have experience in designing and delivering effective behaviour change programmes, promoting an in-depth understanding of the conduct expected of team members, creating a supportive organisational culture which values team member feedback, and quickly responds to concerns raised. The Safeguarding Adviser is also responsible for monitoring safeguarding implementation and reporting on compliance in line with policy and donor expectations.

**About You**

For us, it’s vital that every MSI team member believes in and is committed to our organisational mission, vision and values.

**This means that we will only accept applications from candidates who are unequivocally pro-choice.**

Our values act as guiding principles, providing us with a clear direction. They set the tone for how we approach our work, interact with others and align ourselves as ‘One MSI’. It’s important that our team members truly resonate with our values and demonstrate them consistently, in all that they do.

We recruit talented, dynamic individuals with diverse backgrounds who share our mission and are focused on delivering measurable results. As an equal opportunity employer, we are committed to fostering an inclusive workplace where everyone can participate and contribute meaningfully. We value open-mindedness, curiosity, resilience, and a solutions-oriented mindset, alongside a commitment to promoting equality and safeguarding the welfare of both team members and clients.

We seek exceptional communicators who are self-motivated, solutions-driven, and aligned with MSI’s mission and entrepreneurial mindset. You should be dedicated to driving social change in an environment focused on sustainable impact, both locally and globally, and comfortable working with diverse teams in an ambiguous setting.

**To perform this role, you’ll need the following skills:**

- Excellent verbal and written communicator: ability to convey concepts and influence behaviour in plain English and French to non-technical audiences
- Ability to organise and prioritise workloads to meet deadlines
- A people centred approach and passion for working on people focused behaviour change initiatives
- Strong people skills: ability to build and manage relationships with other stakeholders quickly and effectively
- Ability to maintain confidentiality, recognising when to escalate issues and respond to urgent issues
- Excellent problem-solving skills, with ability to think laterally when confronted with problems
- Excellent report writing skills
- Ability to work as part of a team and with cross-department stakeholders to deliver on projects

**To perform this role, you’ll need the following experience:**

- Designing and delivering effective face-to-face and remote learning programmes and behaviour change initiatives (essential)
- Experience in Safeguarding in Africa (essential)
- Implementing policies and guidance (essential)
- Incident investigation, documentation, and reporting (desirable)
- Familiarity with the Core Policies referenced above (desirable)
- Effectively managing stakeholder needs and expectations (essential)
- Managing a significant cross departmental and/or international workload which involves the need to prioritise, plan, collaborate etc (desirable)

**Formal education/qualification**

- No formal education / qualification requirements

Please see job description [here.](https://www.msichoices.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/2026.10.07-Safeguarding-Advisor-JD-.pdf)

**Location:** Dakar, Senegal

**Full-time:** 40 hours per week

**Contract type: Fixed Term to end 2028.**

**Salary**: Competitive

**Closing date: 12th November 2026 (midnight GMT**). Interviews may take place before this date for exceptional candidates.

***For internal employees applying from an MSI country programme, the role will be positioned within the existing salary structure of the country. Local terms and conditions of the country will apply.***

jobs.title: GCF Project Manager-National-Damascus
jobs.body:
**TEAM/PROGRAMME:** Programme Development and Quality (PDQ)   
**LOCATION:** Damascus / Syria Country Office, with travel to relevant locations as required  
**GRADE**: 2  
**CONTRACT LENGTH:** Fixed term – 9 months  
**CHILD SAFEGUARDING:**   
Level 3: The post holder will have contact with children and/or young people either frequently (e.g. once a week or more) or intensively (e.g. four days in one month or more or overnight) because they work in country programs; or are visiting country programs; or because they are responsible for implementing the police checking/vetting process for staff.

**ROLE PURPOSE:**   
The GCF Project Manager will provide country-level coordination and project management support for the implementation of the Green Climate Fund (GCF) Project Preparation Facility (PPF) and the preparation of the full GCF project for Syria.  
The post holder will coordinate the delivery of PPF activities and assessments in close collaboration with Save the Children, the Government of Syria, relevant ministries and authorities, local partners, consultants, technical specialists and other stakeholders. The role will ensure that PPF activities and assessments are well coordinated, delivered according to agreed timelines and budgets, and supported by appropriate stakeholder engagement, consultation and evidence generation. The post holder will organise and facilitate workshops, consultations and technical meetings; coordinate government and partner engagement; support the mobilisation and management of consultants; monitor data collection and technical deliverables; maintain project documentation and tracking systems; and support the preparation of the GCF funding proposal and associated project documentation.  
The GCF Project Manager will serve as a key coordination focal point between the country-level team, MO team, consultants, government stakeholders and local partners, ensuring that inputs are consolidated and actions are followed up in a timely manner.  
The role will also support quality assurance, risk management, reporting, learning and knowledge management throughout the PPF process and contribute to ensuring that the proposed GCF project is technically sound, conflict-sensitive, child-centred, aligned with national priorities and responsive to the needs and priorities identified through the project preparation process.  
**SCOPE OF ROLE:**

Reports to: Operations Director

Staff reporting to this post: No direct line management responsibility. The post holder will report to PDQD for technical aspects of the proposal development. The post holder will coordinate and provide day-to-day support to consultants, partners and relevant internal teams involved in PPF activities. The role will also work closely with the Climate Resilience Global and Member Technical Advisors. The role will be expected to also maintain close coordination with other countries part of the proposal

**KEY AREAS OF ACCOUNTABILITY**  
1\. GCF PPF Project Management and Coordination  
• Coordinate the activities of the GCF Proposal Preparation Facility (PPF) activities and assessments at country level in accordance with the approved workplan, budget, timelines and agreed responsibilities to put together a strong proposal   
• Develop and maintain a detailed PPF implementation tracker covering activities, milestones, responsibilities, deliverables, dependencies and deadlines.  
• Coordinate inputs from Save the Children teams, consultants, local partners, government stakeholders and other relevant actors.  
• Monitor progress against the PPF workplan and proactively identify delays, gaps, risks and required follow-up actions.  
• Organise regular coordination meetings with Syria team and Member office teams and ensure that agreed actions are documented, assigned and followed up.  
• Maintain an up-to-date overview of all PPF activities, deliverables, consultations, technical studies and project preparation requirements.  
• Support the Project Lead/management team in identifying and addressing implementation bottlenecks and coordination issues.  
2\. Stakeholder and Government Engagement  
• Support and facilitate engagement with relevant government ministries, authorities and GCF-related national stakeholders (Particularly NDA) throughout the PPF process.  
• Coordinate meetings, consultations, technical discussions and validation processes with government counterparts and other stakeholders.  
• Support the preparation of agendas, presentations, briefing materials, meeting notes and follow-up actions.  
• Maintain regular communication with relevant government focal points and ensure timely follow-up on agreed actions and requests.  
• Support the process of securing relevant government inputs, endorsements, clearances and other documentation required for GCF project preparation.  
• Support coordination with national and sub-national stakeholders in target locations.  
3\. Workshops, Consultations and Technical Meetings  
• Lead the logistical and coordination arrangements for PPF workshops, consultations, validation meetings and technical sessions.  
• Coordinate participant invitations, agendas, presentations, background materials, logistics and documentation.  
• Support consultants and technical teams to prepare consultation materials and facilitate data and information collection.  
• Ensure that workshop and consultation outputs are properly documented and incorporated into relevant project preparation deliverables.  
• Support participatory processes involving government, partners, communities, children and other relevant stakeholders, as appropriate.  
• Maintain an organised record of consultation findings, recommendations and agreed actions.  
4\. Consultant and Technical Support Management  
• Support the mobilisation and onboarding of consultants and technical experts engaged under the PPF in coordination with the Technical Advisors.  
• Coordinate communication between consultants, SCI teams, partners and government stakeholders.  
• Support consultants in accessing relevant data, documents, stakeholders and field-level information.  
• Monitor consultant workplans, timelines, data collection processes and deliverables against agreed terms of reference.  
5\. Data Collection, Evidence and Knowledge Management  
• Coordinate and monitor data and information collection required for the GCF project preparation process.  
• Work with consultants, partners and technical teams to identify data gaps and facilitate access to relevant national, sectoral and local information.  
• Maintain a database/tracker of key data sources, assessments, studies, consultation findings and evidence generated through the PPF.  
• Support documentation of lessons learned, good practices and recommendations emerging from the PPF process.  
6\. Partnership Coordination  
• Support effective coordination between Save the Children, consultants, and local partners involved in the GCF PPF.  
• Coordinate partner inputs to assessments, consultations, workshops, technical studies, and project design.  
• Monitor partner deliverables and agreed contributions to the PPF workplan.  
7\. Monitoring, Reporting and Risk Management  
• Monitor progress against the PPF workplan, milestones, budget and deliverables.  
• Prepare regular internal progress updates and coordination reports highlighting achievements, pending actions, risks and required decisions.  
• Maintain a PPF risk and issue tracker and support mitigation and escalation as required.  
• Support financial and administrative tracking in coordination with Awards, Finance and Operations teams.  
8\. Logistics and Administrative Coordination  
• Coordinate logistical and administrative arrangements required for workshops, consultations, field missions, meetings and other PPF activities.  
• Work closely with Operations, Supply Chain, Finance, MEAL and other relevant teams to ensure timely delivery of activities.  
• Support procurement and contracting processes related to PPF activities, in accordance with SCI policies and procedures.  
• Support travel and field mission arrangements for consultants, technical teams and relevant stakeholders where required.  
**BEHAVIOURS (Values in Practice)**  
Accountability  
• Takes responsibility for coordinating activities, following up on agreed actions and ensuring timely delivery.  
• Holds partners, consultants and relevant stakeholders accountable for agreed responsibilities while maintaining constructive working relationships.  
Ambition  
• Demonstrates a strong focus on achieving PPF milestones and preparing a high-quality GCF project.  
• Proactively identifies opportunities to improve coordination, efficiency and project quality.  
Collaboration  
• Builds effective working relationships across SCI teams, government institutions, partners and consultants.  
• Facilitates collaboration and information sharing across different technical workstreams.  
Creativity  
• Identifies practical solutions to coordination, implementation and logistical challenges.  
• Adapts approaches to complex and changing humanitarian and operational contexts.  
Integrity  
• Demonstrates transparency, professionalism and accountability in managing information, relationships and project processes.

**QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE:**   
Essential  
• Bachelor's degree in climate change, environmental sciences, development studies, international development, project management, agriculture or a related field.  
• Minimum 4 years of relevant professional experience in project/programme coordination, project management, climate change, resilience, development or humanitarian programming.  
• Experience working with government institutions, international organisations, NGOs and/or development partners.  
• Strong experience organising workshops, consultations, meetings and stakeholder engagement processes.  
• Strong project management, planning, coordination and follow-up skills.  
• Experience monitoring deliverables, workplans, timelines and project milestones.  
• Strong report writing, documentation and communication skills.  
• Excellent English language skills, both written and spoken.  
• Strong interpersonal, facilitation and negotiation skills.  
Desirable  
• Previous experience with the Green Climate Fund (GCF) or other international climate finance mechanisms.  
• Experience supporting a GCF Project Preparation Facility (PPF), GCF concept note or funding proposal development process.  
• Familiarity with GCF project preparation requirements, investment criteria and funding proposal processes.  
• Experience working on climate change adaptation, climate resilience, environmental sustainability or disaster risk reduction programmes.

Additional job responsibilities  
The duties and responsibilities set out above are not exhaustive and the role holder may be required to carry out additional duties commensurate with their skills and experience.  
Equal Opportunities   
The role holder is required to carry out duties in accordance with SCI Equal Opportunities and Diversity policies and procedures.  
Child Safeguarding:  
We need to keep children safe so our selection process, which includes rigorous background checks, reflects our commitment to the protection of children from abuse.  
Safeguarding our Staff:  
The post holder is required to carry out duties in accordance with the SCI anti-harassment policy.  
Health and Safety  
The role holder is required to carry out duties in accordance with SCI Health and Safety policies and procedures.
