jobs.title: Country Managing Director
jobs.body:
ForAfrika is an African-founded and led organisation with over 40 years of impact across the continent. We partner with communities through our integrated development continuum: saving lives and building resilience to reach self-sufficiency through our Humanitarian & Development work and unlocking commercial viability through our Social Enterprise activities. We are Africans, delivering African-led solutions for Africa, and we stand by our promise: we’re committed to the long run, until the job is done and communities are enabled to thrive.

**Role Thesis**

The Country Managing Director is the accountable leader for the ForAfrika South Africa platform and the principal architect of its next phase of growth and transformation. The MD will steward country operations, impact, people, governance, financial sustainability and risk while building the future South Africa platform. This includes developing the operating model, leadership capability, strategic partnerships, revenue pathways, market positioning, and organizational culture required for long-term success. The role is responsible not only for running the office, but for transforming it into a commercially credible, impact-led and financially resilient platform that can operate effectively across enterprise development, catalytic CSI funding and other appropriate growth opportunities. The MD will build on the foundations established during the interim leadership period and lead the next phase of ForAfrika South Africa's evolution into a market-relevant, scalable and sustainable organization.

**Position Summary**

Reporting to the Group Chief Operations Officer, the Managing Director (MD) is ForAfrika’s senior accountable leader in South Africa, with overall responsibility for the performance, resilience and future relevance of the country platform. The MD owns the full Country Office P&L, impact, revenue, delivery, people and transition outcomes, and is accountable for bringing Pre-Commercial Viability (PCV) and Commercial Transactions/FASE together within a single country strategy and operating model.

A core responsibility of the MD is to build the future South Africa operating platform — transforming the foundations established into a commercially credible, impact-led and sustainable country operation. This includes shaping the organisation, capabilities, leadership and operating systems required to support ForAfrika’s evolution, while protecting existing humanitarian, institutional, government, corporate and community commitments.

The MD translates ForAfrika’s enterprise strategy and 2026–2031 Revenue Plan into an executable country model, balancing strong operational stewardship with the development of new commercial and social enterprise opportunities. The MD brings Social Enterprise, Revenue, Operations, Finance and Impact & Evidence together around one country strategy, one P&L, one operating cadence and one accountable leadership team.

The South Africa Country Office must be flexible by design, balancing institutional funding and public-system strengthening with time-bound pre-commercial viability (PCV), corporate partnerships, transaction-linked opportunities, blended finance and FASE revenue. The MD is accountable for selecting, executing and rebalancing this mix in line with South Africa’s operating context and within enterprise guardrails.

The role therefore requires a leader who can operate simultaneously as country executive, external representative, growth leader, P&L owner and steward of mission, people and risk.

**Key Roles and Responsibilities**

1. **Leadership, Management, and Accountability**

- Model ForAfrika’s core values of Deep Love ForAfrika, Dependability, Compassion, Initiative and Discipline, while building a culture of accountability, collaboration, commercial discipline and timely execution across the South Africa Country Office.
- Translate ForAfrika’s enterprise strategy and the South Africa transformation priorities into clear country plans, Rocks, scorecards, timelines and accountabilities, ensuring the Country Leadership Team is aligned around PCV, FASE, operational delivery, financial sustainability and impact.
- Lead and manage the Country Leadership Team through clear expectations, regular performance reviews, disciplined operating cadences and timely follow-up, ensuring that each leader understands their responsibilities, decision rights and required outcomes.
- Maintain effective management oversight of country P&L, revenue and diversification, contractual delivery, cash and financial sustainability, impact, people, risk and transformation, taking timely corrective action where performance is off track.
- Establish and maintain a consistent Country Office operating cadence, including P&L reviews, pipeline and revenue reviews, delivery reviews, PCV/FASE portfolio reviews, Rocks and scorecards, ensuring issues are identified early, decisions are made and actions are followed through.
- Hold senior leaders accountable for delivery against approved plans and ensure decisions have clear owners, timelines and measurable outcomes, escalating material risks or decisions requiring enterprise approval to the VP Operations/COO.
- Coordinate effectively with GSO functions, FASE, Revenue and other Country Offices on One ForAfrika priorities, ensuring clarity of roles, accountability and execution while avoiding duplication of functional ownership.
- Ensure the South Africa Country Office consistently applies organisational policies, delegated authorities, financial controls, risk and compliance requirements, safeguarding standards and other governance requirements.
- Provide timely, accurate and decision-ready reporting to the VP Operations/COO on country performance, financial sustainability, revenue, delivery, transformation progress, leadership risks and material decisions required.
- Take overall accountability for execution of the approved South Africa strategy and operating model, ensuring that the Country Office protects existing commitments while progressing towards a sustainable, commercially credible and impact-led operating platform
    
    **2. Strategic Mandate**
- Protect today's obligations while building the next operating model. Delivery continuity, safeguarding, duty of care, cash and donor/partner commitments cannot be compromised by transformation.
- Build the future South Africa platform, translating the foundations established into a scalable operating model, high-performing leadership team, differentiated market position and sustainable growth engine.
- Own a differentiated country strategy. Configure the country around its funding mix, humanitarian context, operating maturity, assets, risk profile, leadership capacity and strongest credible revenue pathways.
- Build financial resilience. Reduce dependence on a single donor, programme, affiliate or funding channel through disciplined renewal, replacement, diversification and full-cost recovery.
- Connect operations to growth. Convert local legitimacy, government relationships, operating assets, evidence and technical capability into competitive propositions for donors, governments, corporates, DFIs, investors, primes and strategic partners.
- Operate as One ForAfrika. Share capabilities, intelligence, talent and delivery assets across countries and contribute to multi-country opportunities rather than optimising only for the local office.
- Lead the transition to one Country Office operating platform with clearly governed PCV and Commercial Transactions/FASE lanes.
- Lead the change-management process and establish clear accountability across the new leadership structure.
    
    **3. Country P&L, Financial Stewardship and Sustainability**
- Own the country P&L, annual operating plan, budget performance, cash forecast, cost recovery, working-capital visibility and structural cost base.
- Ensure every material programme, contract, PCV activity and commercial proposition has realistic costing, funding separation, mobilisation assumptions and an identified financial owner.
- Maintain disciplined fixed-cost management. Add capacity only where funded delivery, approved growth or strategic investment justifies the cost.
- Maintain a credible renewal/replacement plan for expiring revenue and actively manage concentration exposure.
- Partner with Finance to ensure auditable separation of restricted humanitarian/institutional funding, PCV co-capital and FASE/commercial activity.
- Ensure the South Africa platform is positioned to compete effectively across corporate, institutional, public and other appropriate funding markets.
- Sponsor priority strategic relationships and major country opportunities.
- Ensure revenue opportunities are supported by credible delivery capability, realistic costing, evidence and mobilisation plans.
- Hold the relevant executives accountable for pipeline, propositions, conversion, delivery and renewal performance.
    
    **4. Delivery, Impact and Operational Continuity**
- Deliver all contracted commitments safely, compliantly, on time and to agreed quality and outcome standards.
- Maintain fit-for-purpose country controls for procurement, logistics, fleet, warehousing, safeguarding, security, partner management, HR, legal compliance and business continuity.
- Own mobilisation readiness for new awards and contracts, including people, partners, supply chain, systems, cash and risk controls.
- Intervene early when programme, partner, cash, security, leadership or compliance issues threaten performance; implement recovery plans and escalate material exposure.
- Use country evidence to demonstrate outcomes, unit costs, operational reliability and value for money - not only activity completion.
- Maintain appropriate controls for procurement, supply chain, safeguarding, security, duty of care, partner management and business continuity.
- Intervene early where delivery or operational risks threaten performance or reputation.
    
    **5. Revenue Growth, Capture and Market Positioning**
- Own the country revenue target and country account plan in partnership with Global Revenue / Business Development.
- Maintain a 36-month view of priority opportunities, renewals, replacements and strategic accounts; ensure accurate country pipeline inputs and disciplined Salesforce use.
- Personally cultivate senior relationships with government, donors, corporates, DFIs, investors, primes, foundations, faith networks and strategic partners relevant to the country model.
- Participate actively in capture before proposal release: buyer intelligence, problem definition, partner selection, solution shaping, evidence, operational feasibility and win strategy.
- Convert local assets, government access, community legitimacy, technical capability and past performance into differentiated, market-facing implementation propositions.
- Do not pursue revenue that creates capability overreach, unpriced risk, unfunded infrastructure or unsupported past-performance claims.
    
    **6. Government, Partnerships and Market Access**
- Serve as a senior representative of ForAfrika South Africa with government, corporates, institutional partners, investors, communities and strategic stakeholders.
- Build a deliberate country relationship portfolio across donors, embassies, corporates, DFIs, investors, industry platforms, UN agencies, civil society, universities, faith institutions and local organisations.
- Use partner-led delivery where it strengthens localisation, market access, technical capability or entry discipline; ensure clear roles, due diligence, safeguarding, commercial terms and accountability.
- Position the country office for strategic industries and transaction-linked opportunities where relevant - including mining, energy, logistics, agriculture, health, water, infrastructure and economic corridors - without presenting ForAfrika as the mine operator, engineer, lender or security provider.
- Leverage and strengthen strategic country relationships to support national, regional and multi-country opportunities, enhance organisational positioning, sustainability and delivery, and protect ForAfrika’s reputation, and mission
    
    **7. People, Organisation and Culture**
- Build a high performing country leadership team around the approved operating model and funded work; eliminate duplicated roles and unsupported structural cost.
- Ensure right people / right seats, clear accountabilities, measurable scorecards, succession coverage and timely performance action.
- Develop national leadership and technical capability wherever feasible, consistent with ForAfrika's African-led operating model and address underperformance decisively and fairly.
- Create an accountable, collaborative culture that can operate across humanitarian, institutional and commercial disciplines without forming internal silos.
- Lead change with clarity and respect while remaining decisive when role, cost or performance changes are necessary.
- Build succession and leadership capability for critical roles.
    
    **8. Risk, Compliance, Safeguarding and Duty of Care**
- Own the country risk register and ensure legal, regulatory, sanctions, anti-corruption, safeguarding, security, financial and partner risks are actively controlled and escalated.
- Maintain country-specific security, access, medical evacuation and business-continuity arrangements proportionate to operating context.
- Ensure proposals, partnerships and commercial commitments are operationally realistic and within ForAfrika's risk appetite before commitments are made.
- Apply heightened controls in high-risk expansion markets, including beneficial-ownership, sanctions, anti-corruption, responsible-sourcing and partner due diligence where relevant.
- Protect organisational reputation by ensuring no revenue target overrides safety, compliance, evidence integrity or mission guardrails.
    
    **9. Evidence, Systems and Decision Quality**
- Treat Evidence & Learning (DMEAL) as management and revenue infrastructure. Use verified data to make decisions and prove results to government, donors, investors and partners.
- Maintain current evidence and past-performance packages for the country's strongest capabilities, including outcomes, references, delivery metrics, unit costs and lessons learned.
- Operate within common enterprise systems and standards for finance, revenue, contracts, evidence, HR, procurement, risk and technology while configuring legitimate local requirements.
- Ensure country operating data and revenue pipeline data reconcile sufficiently for mobilisation, capacity and investment decisions.
- Use AI and digital tools to improve productivity, market intelligence and analysis only within approved information-security, source-verification and human-accountability controls.
- Enterprise Contribution - One ForAfrika
- Contribute talent, assets, evidence, partners and technical capacity to enterprise priorities and other countries when this increases overall ForAfrika value.
- Support regional strategic accounts, cross-border humanitarian responses and multi-country investment opportunities through coordinated planning.
- Adopt enterprise standards and decision gates even where local practice previously differed, unless an approved country exception is justified.
- Share wins, losses, lessons, market intelligence and operating innovations so that the country network compounds learning rather than repeating it.

**First 12-Month Priorities**

- Validate and build upon the foundations established, including the existing diagnostic across contracts, cash, people, systems, assets, revenue mix, pipeline, partners, evidence, risk, humanitarian readiness and PCV / FASE potential.
- Refine and agree the country target operating model and transformation sequence with the SVP Operations; protect all current obligations before structural change.
- Establish the country EOS cadence: leadership accountability chart, annual and quarterly Rocks, weekly scorecard review, issue-solving discipline and decision log.
- Produce a 36-month country revenue and strategic-account plan covering renewals, replacements, institutional opportunities, government, corporate/DFI relationships and suitable PCV / FASE propositions.
- Reset the fixed-cost base and organisation structure against funded work and future strategy; identify critical talent, succession and capability gaps.
- Create or refresh the country's evidence and past-performance package for its highest-value humanitarian, institutional and commercial propositions.
- Establish a prioritised government and external relationship map with named objectives, relationship owners and next actions.
- Validate country risk, security, safeguarding, legal, partner and business-continuity controls; close material readiness gaps.

**Knowledge, Skills and Abilities.**

**Leadership Standard.**-The next-generation ForAfrika Managing Director must be a country enterprise executive - not solely a technical programme leader. The successful candidate must combine operational depth, financial discipline, external credibility and growth judgement, with the adaptability to lead a humanitarian-heavy, commercially led or mixed country platform.

- Bachelor's degree required in Business, International Development, Public Administration, Finance, Economics, Engineering, Supply Chain, International Relations or another relevant field; Master's degree or equivalent executive experience strongly preferred.
- 12-15+ years of progressively responsible professional experience, including at least five years in a senior country, business-unit or multi-functional leadership role in Africa.
- Demonstrated responsibility for a material operating portfolio with budget / P&L, delivery, people, risk, compliance and external-stakeholder accountability.
- Proven ability to protect current operations while leading organisational change, turnaround, integration, restructuring or operating-model transformation.
- Demonstrated ability to connect operations to growth: diversify revenue, build senior relationships, shape opportunities, develop partnerships and convert organisational capability into funded programmes, contracts or transactions.
- Strong understanding of institutional and humanitarian funding and delivery. Experience with UN agencies, bilateral donors, multilateral institutions or government-funded programmes is highly valuable.
- Commercial and financial literacy sufficient to understand customers, contracts, pricing, cost recovery, unit economics, working capital, investment readiness and the difference between grant-funded, PCV and commercial risk.
- Experience engaging corporates, investors, DFIs, infrastructure sponsors, prime contractors, philanthropy or strategic industries strongly preferred, particularly in commercially led or corridor markets.
- Strong government-relations capability and the judgement to operate credibly across national ministries, local authorities, donors, communities and private-sector leaders.
- Deep experience in operational risk, safeguarding, security, duty of care, procurement, supply chain, partner management and legal/compliance oversight, especially in complex or fragile contexts where relevant.
- Track record of using evidence, data, digital systems and performance dashboards to improve decisions, demonstrate outcomes and strengthen external credibility.
- Established professional networks in the country and/or region across government, donors, civil society, business, finance, academia or implementing partners, with the credibility to open and sustain senior relationships.
- Exceptional judgement, communication, negotiation and influencing skills; able to move from strategy and external representation to detailed operating decisions when required.
- Demonstrated ability to build high-accountability teams, coach senior leaders, confront underperformance and develop national succession capacity.
- Fluency in English required for enterprise engagement; proficiency in relevant national or regional languages is a significant advantage and may be required for specific countries.
- Willingness and ability to travel extensively, including remote, fragile or high-risk operating locations where appropriate.
- Balanced Experience Requirement-ForAfrika does not require every Managing Director to have identical career experience. A candidate may bring deeper humanitarian/institutional expertise or deeper commercial/private-sector expertise depending on the country. However, every MD must demonstrate enough fluency to govern all three operating lanes, use specialist enterprise functions effectively, and make disciplined decisions outside their original professional comfort zone.

**DISCLAIMER**: Please note candidates must have a right to live and work in South Africa

jobs.title: Director Programs Afghanistan
jobs.body:
The position is to be filled as soon as possible, with an initial contract duration of 2 years. There are very good prospects for an extension. Employment location will be Kabul, Afghanistan (AF).

For more than four decades, Welthungerhilfe has been supporting people in Afghanistan, providing humanitarian aid since the early 1980s and maintaining a permanent presence in the country since 1992. After a shift towards long-term development programming post-2002, the organisation returned to large-scale humanitarian assistance following the international sanctions of August 2021, which brought development funding to a halt. Today, Welthungerhilfe operates in nine provinces across Afghanistan, delivering life-saving interventions that reach up to 600,000 people. With food security under severe strain and widespread acute malnutrition (IPC Phase 3) as well as critical pockets of IPC Phase 4, the need for effective humanitarian programming is urgent and growing.

As Director Programs, you work under the supervision of the Country Director and play a central role in steering Welthungerhilfe’s strategic and operational program direction in Afghanistan. Positioned in the salary scale below the Head of Programs, you support the implementation of the multi-annual country strategy to ensure maximum impact in line with Welthungerhilfe’s global strategy, relevant concept papers, and quality standards. In agreement with the Country Director, you represent Welthungerhilfe in the country and contribute to the development and implementation of programs and projects, continually strengthening the overall intervention concept. You oversee the implementation of the full project portfolio, guide project managers in applying Welthungerhilfe’s standard project cycle management, and support them in analyzing implementation challenges and identifying mitigation measures. Working closely with area managers, you assess and address access-related risks to ensure safe and effective project delivery. In addition, three international experts—covering food security & nutrition, agriculture & natural resource management, and grants management—report directly to you, enabling you to coordinate technical excellence across all program areas. Within the framework of responsibilities agreed with the Country Director, you also assume specific specialised duties essential to the effectiveness and quality of Welthungerhilfe’s work in Afghanistan.

## Your responsibilities

- Coordinate and monitor the implementation of projects and programmes according to WHH quality standards, including an effective M&E system, and supervision of the use of funds and financial requirements
- Provide leadership, direction, and constructive performance management to Project Managers, Technical Experts, Grants/Donor Coordinator, and MEAL Coordinator, promoting a culture of accountability, collaboration, and mutual trust.
- Contribute to organisational planning, strategic reviews, donor engagement, and resource mobilisation.
- Identify, examine and assess (pre-select) new project ideas on the basis of the country and intervention strategy as well as the concept papers and orientation framework and set standards.
- Coordinate the development of new project proposals and assure the quality donor reporting
- Participate in the recruitment and training of team members
- Operationalize and periodically review WHH Afghanistan’s multi-year country strategy, translating strategic ambitions into annual programme priorities, technical approaches, and measurable results.
- Support the Country Director in ensuring the impact of the country programme and provide regular updates on the status of the programme
- Develop partnerships, identify new partners and advise partner organizations on organizational and conceptual matters, ensuring the quality of projects and programmes and identifying capacity building measures
- Monitor the evolution of possible crises through early warning indicators
- Monitor, and where applicable, update or modify, in consultation with the Country Director, the WHH preparedness and contingency plan
- Represent Welthungerhilfe vis-à-vis other national and international, governmental, and non-governmental bodies as well as relief and development organizations

## Your profile

- A university or college degree in humanitarian/development studies or an equivalent degree related to the position
- At least 5 years of professional experience in a similar position in which two years in fragile context,
- Regional experience working in Afghanistan, the global South, and/or in an insecure environment would be an asset
- Demonstrated experience in resilience or development programming is preferred. Specific expertise in one or more of the following technical areas is considered a strong asset: market/food systems development, economic empowerment, climate resilience, and anticipatory action.
- Experience in developing divers partnerships, including local partners, private sector, technical and research institutes
- Proven leadership and organizational skills, including financial planning and oversight
- Proven reporting skills, with excellent writing capacities for different audiences
- Ability to work under time pressure and high workload with high cultural sensibility
- You recognize the growing value of data within an organization and inspire teams to make decisions grounded in analysis and evidence
- Ability to work in an insecure environment and committed to adhere to strict security procedures
- Excellent spoken and written English

## What we offer

- Fair Compensation: A fair and equal remuneration based on a transparent salary scale.
- Commitment to Well-Being: We attach great importance to our duty of care with a focus on safety, security & health.
- Modern & Agile Work Environment: Be part of a forward thinking organization that fully embraces digitalization and innovation across all areas.
- Personal & Professional Growth: Access diverse learning and development opportunities to advance your career.
- Team: Join our dedicated and diverse teams, where passion, expertise, and joy come together to create a better world.

In addition, Welthungerhilfe offers numerous other benefits, which you can find under [**Our benefits**](https://www.welthungerhilfe.org/benefits-for-expatriate-employees).

*\*Welthungerhilfe values diversity and ensures an inclusive, non-discriminatory working environment. We welcome applications from suitably qualified people from all sections of the community.*

jobs.title: Team Lead Procurement HQ & Internal Services
jobs.body:
The position is to be filled as soon as possible to cover a period of sick leave. It is initially limited to one year, with the possibility of extension. Employment location will be Bonn, Germany.

As Team Lead Procurement HQ & Internal Services, you will ensure that the processes and tasks of both the Internal Service & Procurement HQ teams run smoothly by taking on team coordination, managing information and communication across the board. You will at as local project lead for buidling management related assessments and during the further digitalization of tools and processes in the HQ procurement domain.

## Your responsibilities

- Manage and develop the Procurement Officers and Internal Services team, covering facility management, reception, property administration and student assistants.
- Provide technical coordination and guidance to the Procurement Officers, including overseeing the development and review of procurement guidelines, policies, templates and process visualizations, and ensuring that relevant information is readily available.
- Coordinate with the Team Lead Procurement & Logistics International to align comparable procurement processes and ensure coherence and efficiency.
- Build employees’ procurement skills by organizing virtual and in-person training in collaboration with the Procurement HQ team.
- Advise internal clients on technical suitability, compatibility, delivery times and pricing, including concept development and material selection where applicable.
- Procure goods and services for HQ in line with internal clients’ requirements, taking sustainability criteria into account.
- Independently manage the full procurement cycle, including obtaining and evaluating quotations, coordinating with internal clients, awarding contracts, conducting quality checks, processing invoices through Doxis and documenting transactions in SAP.
- Support colleagues in procuring goods and services in line with defined specifications and requirements.
- Contribute to digitalization projects and the introduction of new departmental software, including testing functions and supporting colleagues in using tools such as Doxis.
- Review and approve purchase orders above the defined threshold, ensuring economic efficiency and compliance with delegated approval authority.
- Organize and oversee day-to-day Internal Services operations.
- Plan, organize and coordinate expansion and renovation works at properties managed by WHH, in collaboration with the Internal Services team.
- Oversee tendering processes and cooperation with Internal Services providers, and maintain the framework agreement database.
- Incorporate sustainability criteria into the selection of Internal Services providers and suppliers and into decisions on building alterations.
- Develop a concept for broader use of the Bonn property by external companies and organizations, in collaboration with Finance and Legal & Compliance.

## Your profile

- A university degree in a relevant field or a comparable qualification.
- Several years of relevant professional experience in procurement, internal services or a related field.
- Experience in project management, including developing business cases and conducting feasibility studies.
- An affinity for digital solutions and the ability to identify and implement process improvements.
- The ability to think strategically and translate organizational priorities into practical action.
- The ability to use data and analysis to inform decisions and encourage evidence-based decision-making within the team.
- Very good written and spoken German and English.

## What we offer

- Fair Compensation: A fair and equal remuneration based on a transparent salary scale.
- Work-Life Balance: Enjoy flexible working arrangements to support a balanced lifestyle.
- Modern & Agile Work Environment: Be part of a forward thinking organization that fully embraces digitalization and innovation across all areas.
- Personal & Professional Growth: Access diverse learning and development opportunities to advance your career.
- Team: Join our dedicated and diverse teams, where passion, expertise, and joy come together to create a better world.

In addition, Welthungerhilfe offers numerous other benefits, which are listed under [**Our benefits**](https://www.welthungerhilfe.org/benefits-for-employees-in-germany/).

*\*Welthungerhilfe values diversity and ensures an inclusive, non-discriminatory working environment. We welcome applications from suitably qualified people from all sections of the community.*

jobs.title: Logistics Manager - Manila (Filipino Nationals Only)
jobs.body:
Duration : **6 months (with a possibility of an extension)**  
Start date : **01-Nov-2026**

## **You'll contribute to ending world hunger by ...**

- Ensuring coordination between Logistics and the other departments in the Mission, in order to provide the adequate level of support to Action Against Hunger operations in the Philippines.
- Managing the Logistics department, monitoring its performance in all the processes related to Logistics and Security to ensure they are in line with the Headquarters and the Mission´s Logistics Strategy, policies and guidelines.
- Contributing to the development and implementation of the mission logistics strategy in coordination with the members of Coordination Team
- Engaging and representing Action Against Hunger Philippines in consortium -led logistics strategies and participate in relevant logistics coordination platform

## **Key activities in your role will include**

**Objective 1: Coordinate logistics at the national level**

Internal coordination of the Logistics team in the mission:

- Analyze and define logistics team members' role and responsibilities on regular basis based on the mission and project/program requirement resources between bases
- Manage, monitor and follow-up of logistics, IT and security staff and functional management of base Logistics Officers
- Lead the consolidation and monitoring of the Mission Procurement Plan
- Manage and follow up to the logistics staff when deployed in the field to support emergency response
- Ensure compliance and support to the standardization of logistics procedures and templates, particularly at Manila and field level
- Lead and ensure the implementation of Action Against Hunger´s logistics procedures (KitLog) and strategy across the operations, including application and promotion of the LINK system across the mission
- Ensure procurement forecasting is conducted regularly with programme and support departments
- Monitor compliance and escalate significant risks and deviations to senior management
- Support the mission with partners and service providers as delegated by the senior management

Drafting of Proposals and Reports to donors:

- Lead and contribute technical, logistics and security related inputs to proposals and budgets in coordination with the Head of Departments
- Ensure timely coordination between the Program, finance, HR and communication departments
- Provide logistics information and supporting documentation required for donor reporting

Supervision of the supply chain:

- Lead and ensure implementation and monitoring of Action Against Hunger´s Supply Chain Management Tools
- Monitor and ensure compliance with Action Against Hunger and donors' logistics procedures
- Monitor procurement lead times and identify bottlenecks affecting programme implementation
- Implementation of the anti-fraud policy and its tools within the logistics department
- Facilitate the preparation of tender plans and procurement schedules for major purchases
- Ensure procurement activities are aligned with project implementation timelines

Budgeting:

- Contribute logistics budget forecasts and resource planning for projects and annual budgeting
- Contribute to any budget/proposal to be submitted to donors
- Review and validate the monthly logistics expenditure forecast across the mission in coordination with field offices and Head of Departments

Reporting, analysis and information management:

- Control and analyze the Mission´s Logistics costs on a monthly basis
- Consolidate, monitor and analyze Logistics Department's information submitted by the field offices and departments
- Analyze and optimize equipment use, including forecasting, disposal and replacement of equipment in line with Action Against Hunger and donor policy and guidelines
- Ensure the implementation of Action Against Hunger´s Archiving Policy
- Support audit processes and provide logistics documentation as required
- Ensure that monthly reporting requirements to Headquarters is met by the Mission

Communication Management:

- Implement adequate and relevant communication systems
- Analyze new requirements and the cost/efficiency of existing systems
- Lead and implement Action Against Hunger´s IT policy in the Mission, including troubleshooting and addressing IT related concerns in the mission in coordination and consultation with HQ

Equipment/asset management:

- Create and implement an equipment policy for the Mission
- Manage equipment according to Action Against Hunger and donors’ guidelines
- Ensure the correct and documented transfer of equipment on the completion of projects
- Ensure adequacy and efficient management of equipment in the Mission
- Lead ensuring accommodation/office/guest house contracts are drafted, reviewed, signed and renewed based on the needs in coordination with the line manager and finance department

Fleet Management:

- Ensure an efficient fleet planning and management in the Mission
- Create and disseminate a vehicle use policy and monitor safety compliance
- Monitor the maintenance and control of vehicles in accordance with Action Against Hunger´s procedures, including renewal of Framework Agreement

**Objective 2: Contribute to the definition of the mission strategy**

- Contribute operational logistics analysis and recommendations to support the development of the Mission's strategy
- Lead and support the implementation and dissemination of the Mission's Logistics Strategy
- Lead, promote and contribute to the implementation of the carbon footprint reduction plan over the mission and ensure collection of data to measure our contribution to Co2 emissions and implementation of environmental policies
- Lead the review, identify operational improvement opportunities on regular basis and propose corrective actions to the management

**Objective 3: Line-management of the Logistics team in Manila, and technical management of the Base Logisticians in the Bases**

- Ensure the cohesion and good communication within the department
- Lead, develop and regularly monitor individual logistics staff objectives and action plans
- Contribute to the implementation of Mission Training Plan, and monitor its implementation within the logistics department
- Provide technical support to field logistics team through weekly meeting and regular field visits
- Evaluate the performance of every team member, and contribute to the development their relevant skills

**Objective 4: Support humanitarian activities of Action Against Hunger**

- Lead and ensure systems and process are in place for emergency response in the Philippines
- Build logistics staff capacity and maintain emergency response deployment ready at any time
- Be available to be deployed in the field for new emergencies as requested by the line manager
- Lead the development, monitoring and periodic renewal of Framework Agreements for frequently purchased goods and services
- Ensure Framework Agreements are strategically established to reduce procurement lead times and support emergency response capacity
- Monitor Framework Agreement utilization and supplier performance
- Monitor supplier performance against agreed service levels and contractual obligations
- Conduct periodic market assessments to identify qualified suppliers and procurement risks
- Support the development of sourcing strategies for key categories of expenditure
- Assess supplier capacity, financial stability and operational risks
- Ensure adequate supplier diversification to mitigate operational and emergency response risks

**Objective 5: Operational support to the Mission´s security management**

- Lead and analyze the safety and security context in operational areas in coordination with the assigned Security Officer, Heads of Base and Country Director
- Advise the Country Director on matters related to safety and security management
- Contribute to monitor the compliance of all staff with the Mission´s security regulations
- Lead and ensure local standard operation procedures are developed and updated according to the timeline established at the mission and HQ level in coordination with the assigned Security Officer, Head of Base and Country Director
- Ensure physical status and availability of contingency measures and equipment (e.g. hibernation boxes, back-up vehicles), as needed
- Coordinate and ensure regular updating of Business Continuity Plans of the mission, including bases in coordination with line manager and head of departments
- Support Risk Assessment and Management in the mission

## **Do you meet the profile required criteria?**

- University Degree
- Experience of logistics management with an INGO in the Philippines
- Knowledge of donor guidelines and procedures
- Ability to work strategically
- Understanding of safety and security context in the Philippines
- Good analytical skills
- At least 3 years previous hand on logistic management experience in emergency response and development programs with a NGO in the Philippines
- At least 3 years of experience in safety and security management
- Experience working with and supporting people remotely
- Experience overseeing IT services, communications systems and IT support functions is desirable
- English is a must
- MS Office very strong command
- Advanced level of Excel
- Valuable prior experience in issues related to the promotion of gender equality or personal commitment to gender equality

## **Our remuneration package:**

- Compensation: based on Action Against Hunger grid
- Benefits: health insurance, accident and life insurance, leave entitlement, government-mandated benefits
- Fixed-term Employment

**Action against Hunger is committed to preventing any type of unwanted behaviour at work such as but not limited to sexual harassment, sexual exploitation and abuse, lack of integrity and/or financial misconduct; We expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment through endorsing our code of conduct and other related policies and only those who share our values and code of conduct will be recruited to work for us.**

jobs.title: Finance Assistant
source: Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH
jobs.body:
**Job description**

GIZ has been operating in Syria since 1976. It has thus established valuable contacts in civil society and garnered experience that is now crucial for supporting the country. From 2013 onwards, it worked without government involvement with the assistance of local non-governmental organizations. Despite the difficult conditions, GIZ has consistently contributed to improving people’s living conditions.

In view of the developments since December 2024, which have led Syria into a decisive phase of transformation, GIZ reopens its Country Office in Damascus in 2026. It is currently implementing 14 projects on behalf of the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and the Federal Foreign Office (FFO), with co-financing from the European Union and other donors. From 2026, the portfolio is planned to be expanded by several new projects.

**Your tasks**

- Receive, register, and process invoices and payment requests in accordance with GIZ rules and regulations, ensuring completeness and accuracy of supporting documentation.
- Check invoices, payment requests, and related documents for required approvals, correct calculations, and compliance with established financial procedures, and follow up on missing information.
- Prepare payment documentation, payment vouchers, and supporting documents for cash and bank transactions, and submit them for further verification and approval.
- Support the processing of travel expense settlements, including checking travel-related documents, flight tickets, accommodation invoices, and other supporting documents in line with GIZ travel regulations.
- Regularly follow up on outstanding invoices, advances, receivables, payables, and pending settlements, and maintain updated records for the Finance Unit.
- Support cash and bank management activities, including preparing cash withdrawal requests, maintaining transaction records, and assisting with cash counts and bank reconciliations.
- Assist in preparing and entering financial data into GIZ accounting systems, ensuring accurate documentation and proper filing of transactions.
- Support the Head of Finance and other Finance Unit colleagues in daily financial operations and perform additional finance-related tasks as assigned by the line manager.

**Your profile (required qualifications, competencies and experience)**

- University degree or diploma in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or a related field.
- At least two years of relevant professional experience in accounting or financial administration, including checking invoices and supporting documents and maintaining financial records.
- Practical knowledge of basic bookkeeping and the documentation required for financial transactions.
- Ability to use Microsoft Excel to maintain transaction lists, sort and filter data, apply basic formulas and identify discrepancies between financial records.
- Ability to organise assigned tasks, meet deadlines and follow up on missing documents or information.
- Ability to handle financial information accurately and confidentially and to report discrepancies promptly.
- Willingness to learn and apply GIZ financial procedures and systems.
- Fluency in Arabic and good working knowledge of English are required. G

Desirable experience

- Experience using accounting software or an ERP system.
- Experience with travel expense settlements, advance monitoring, cash counts or bank reconciliations.
- Experience working with GIZ, another international organisation or an organisation with documented financial procedures and approval workflows.
- Knowledge of German is an advantage.

jobs.title: Researcher / Analyst
source: Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH
jobs.body:
**Job description**

GIZ has been operating in Syria since 1976. It has thus established valuable contacts in civil society and garnered experience that is now crucial for supporting the country. From 2013 onwards, it worked without government involvement with the assistance of local non-governmental organizations. Despite the difficult conditions, GIZ has consistently contributed to improving people’s living conditions.

In view of the developments since December 2024, which have led Syria into a decisive phase of transformation, GIZ reopens its Country Office in Damascus in 2026. It is currently implementing 14 projects on behalf of the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and the Federal Foreign Office (FFO), with co-financing from the European Union and other donors. From 2026, the portfolio is planned to be expanded by several new projects.

The Analysis and Research Unit supports the Syria portfolio with timely, evidence-based analysis on general context, including economic and social developments. It provides decision-relevant research and analysis to programme teams, senior management and commissioning parties.

The Researcher / Analyst will contribute to this work by combining strong research skills with analytical judgement, local knowledge and the ability to turn complex and sometimes incomplete information into clear and concise analysis.

**Your tasks**

- Monitor and analyse political, security, governance, economic and social developments relevant to GIZ’s work in Syria.
- Conduct focused research in response to questions from programme teams, senior management and commissioning parties.
- Analyse developments at national and sub-national level.
- Identify emerging trends, risks and changes in the operating environment and assess their potential implications for GIZ programmes and partners.
- Triangulate information across Arabic- and English-language open sources, official information.
- Draft concise analytical notes, briefings, situation updates, profiles, stakeholder mappings and other research products.
- Support assessments of institutions, organizations, stakeholders and potential partners where relevant to programme decision-making.
- Conduct key informant interviews and other consultations and contribute to developing and maintaining relevant professional information networks.
- Contribute to political economy, conflict sensitivity, access and operational risk analysis.
- Maintain structured research records, source logs, datasets and other analytical resources used by the team.
- Support the use of digital research and analytical tools, while independently checking underlying sources and analytical outputs.
- Work closely with other analysts to test assumptions, challenge conclusions and improve the quality and consistency of the unit’s analytical products.
- Develop subject-matter or geographic expertise in line with the priorities of the Analysis and Research Unit.

**Your profile (required qualifications, competencies and experience)**

- University degree in political science, international relations, economics, sociology, development studies, law, security studies, journalism or another relevant field.
- Relevant professional experience in research, analysis, journalism, international development, humanitarian affairs, governance, security analysis or a related field.
- Strong knowledge of contemporary Syria, including its political, institutional, socio-economic and security context.
- Demonstrated ability to conduct independent research using multiple sources and to assess the reliability and limitations of available information.
- Strong analytical skills, including the ability to identify patterns, assess competing explanations and explain the significance of developments rather than simply describe them.
- Ability to work with incomplete, and sometimes contradictory information and to communicate uncertainty clearly.
- Strong Arabic-language research skills, including the ability to work across formal and informal Arabic-language sources.
- Strong professional English skills, particularly in written analysis.
- Ability to write clearly, concisely and in a way that is accessible to non-specialist audiences.
- Strong online research, information verification and source assessment skills.
- Experience conducting interviews, consultations or maintaining professional information networks is an advantage.
- Familiarity with spreadsheets, data management, mapping, social-media research, data visualisation or other analytical tools is an advantage.
- Experience working with an international organisation, research institution, think tank, media organisation or consultancy is an advantage.
- Strong judgement, intellectual curiosity and attention to detail.
- Ability to work independently while contributing actively to a collaborative analytical team.
- Ability to work under short deadlines and adapt to changing analytical priorities.

jobs.title: Human Resources Administrative Assistant
source: Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH
jobs.body:
**Job description**

GIZ has been operating in Syria since 1976. It has thus established valuable contacts in civil society and garnered experience that is now crucial for supporting the country. From 2013 onwards, it worked without government involvement with the assistance of local non-governmental organizations. Despite the difficult conditions, GIZ has consistently contributed to improving people’s living conditions.

In view of the developments since December 2024, which have led Syria into a decisive phase of transformation, GIZ reopens its Country Office in Damascus in 2026. It is currently implementing 14 projects on behalf of the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and the Federal Foreign Office (FFO), with co-financing from the European Union and other donors. From 2026, the portfolio is planned to be expanded by several new projects.

The HR Unit of GIZ Country Office Syria supports the full employee lifecycle, including recruitment, onboarding, personnel administration and staff development.

**Your tasks**

As HR Administrative Assistant, you support the team with day-to-day administrative tasks, document management and scheduling. Working under the guidance of HR colleagues, you help maintain accurate personnel records, prepare recruitment activities and ensure timely administrative follow-up.

*Personnel files and document management*

- Maintain and organise physical and electronic personnel files in accordance with GIZ filing procedures and confidentiality requirements.
- Scan, copy, label, upload and archive HR documents, ensuring that records are complete, accurate and easy to retrieve by authorised colleagues.
- Check documents, follow up on missing documents or signatures and flag discrepancies to the responsible HR colleague.

*Recruitment and appointment coordination*

- Schedule interviews, written assessments and HR meetings, coordinating availability with candidates, panel members and colleagues.
- Prepare interview documents, candidate information, meeting rooms and online meeting links, and support the practical arrangements for assessments.
- Send invitations, reminders and standard correspondence using approved templates and instructions, and maintain recruitment schedules and tracking lists.
- Printing of GIZ ID and business cards and employment letters

*General HR administration and support*

- Support onboarding and offboarding by preparing document packages, coordinating appointments and following up on administrative checklists.
- Prepare routine HR correspondence and documents using approved templates for review by the responsible HR colleague.
- Enter and update employee information, approved leave records and other administrative data in HR systems and tracking lists, as instructed.
- Collect and organise supporting documents for payroll, insurance and other personnel processes for review and processing by HR colleagues.
- Support the organisation of induction sessions, training activities and staff meetings, including invitations, attendance lists and materials.
- Receive routine administrative enquiries, provide information on submission procedures and refer substantive HR questions to the responsible colleague.
- Perform other administrative and support tasks appropriate to the position, as assigned.

**Your profile (required qualifications, competencies and experience)**

- Bachelor’s degree in human resources, psychology, business administration, public administration or a related field.
- First experience in administrative or office support; experience in HR administration is an advantage.
- Experience in maintaining filing systems, handling documents and coordinating appointments.
- Good working knowledge of MS Office, particularly Word, Excel, Outlook and Teams; familiarity with digital filing systems or HR databases is an advantage.
- Strong organisational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to manage routine tasks and follow up reliably on deadlines.
- A cooperative, service-oriented approach, clear communication skills and willingness to learn.
- Excellent command of written and spoken English and Arabic.

jobs.title: Receiving Supervisor
source: Mission for Essential Drugs and Supplies
jobs.body:
Mission for Essential Drugs and Supplies (MEDS) is a faith-based health solutions provider founded by an ecumenical partnership of the Kenya Conference of Catholic Bishops (KCCB) and the Christian Health Association of Kenya (CHAK). The Organization’s core mandate is providing access to quality health products and technologies through Supply Chain, Quality Assurance and Health Systems Strengthening services. MEDS was established in 1986 and serves clients spread throughout Kenya, other regions in Africa and beyond.

The position will report to Warehouse and Logistics Manager and will be responsible for coordinating all inbound operations for both MEDS commercial business and donor-funded projects to ensure accurate, timely processing and efficient management of goods and supplier interactions.

Job Responsibilities

i. Coordinate receipt, verification, and accurate system entry of all commercial and donor-funded consignments to ensure timely receipt and inventory accuracy  
ii. Supervise receiving and inbound warehouse operations, ensuring efficient coordination of workflows, effective utilization of resources, and compliance with established warehouse procedures  
iii. Coordinate the verification and processing of suppliers' invoices to facilitate stock inspection, acceptance, and storage  
iv. Coordinate the processing of inbound returns to ensure accurate inventory reconciliation and timely resolution of customer complaints  
v. Maintain accurate records of received goods to ensure inventory integrity, traceability, and accountability  
vi. Assess operational workload and recommend temporary staffing requirements for donor-funded and other special projects to support operational needs  
vii. Supervise, coach, and develop receiving staff, including coordinating leave schedules to ensure continuous operations and adequate staffing  
viii. Ensure implementation and continual improvement of the Quality Management System (QMS), compliance with quality and regulatory requirements  
ix. Identify and recommend improvements to receiving processes and warehouse operations to enhance efficiency, accuracy, and service delivery  
x. Monitor supplier deliveries and coordinate receiving activities to ensure efficient and timely inbound operations  
xi. Verify received goods against purchase orders and delivery documentation, including quantities, batch numbers, expiry dates, and product specifications, to ensure accuracy and compliance  
xii. Coordinate the physical and system-based release of received goods for quality inspection in accordance with established warehouse procedures  
xiii. Coordinate the processing of inbound returns to facilitate inventory reconciliation and the resolution of customer complaints  
xiv. Maintain accurate receiving records to support inventory integrity, traceability, and accountability

Qualifications  
i. Bachelor’s Degree in Supply Chain Management/ Business management/ Business Administration/Operations Management/Commerce or related field  
ii. Diploma in Pharmacy  
iii. Minimum five (5) years of relevant experience in a busy Pharmaceutical or fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) Warehouse, three (3) of which should be in a supervisory role  
iv. Technical competencies: Knowledge of occupational safety standards and practices.  
Data Analysis; MS Office Suite Proficiency; use of ERP system  
v. Behavioural competencies: Supervisory Skills; Communication skills; Problem solving skills; Analytical skills; high level of integrity; keen to details

jobs.title: Solidarity for Change and Voice (S4CV) Programme Support Officer
jobs.body:
**Context of Role**

IPPF operates in a complex, global, and fast-paced environment, requiring strong administrative coordination and logistical support to enable teams to deliver effectively.

This role supports the operational functioning of global initiatives by coordinating information, schedules, documentation, meetings and finance, and other reporting requirements. Strong administrative systems and clear communication are essential to supporting collaboration across the division.

**Role Purpose**

This is an entry-level coordination and administration role that provides day-to-day administrative, program planning and logistics support to S4CV global teams.

The role ensures smooth team operations, accurate tracking of programme and project activities, finances, effective coordination of meetings, projects and events, and timely flow of information across the Secretariat.

**Deliverables**

- Coordinate and support day-to-day administrative and logistical activities for global and regional initiatives, ensuring plans, schedules and documentation are accurate and up to date.
- Utilise tools to arrange consultancies (Kofax), finance updates, invoicing (Netsuite) and other team administration activities to ensure alignment to secretariat reporting and admin timelines and expectations.
- Organise and support meetings, workshops and events, including scheduling, agendas, minutes, follow-up actions and logistical arrangements (virtual and in-person).
- Maintain centralised records, trackers and filing systems for plans, activities, risks, actions and key documents.
- Act as a first point of contact for administrative queries from internal teams and Member Associations, ensuring timely information flow.
- Support project teams with planning timelines, action tracking and progress updates, escalating issues where appropriate.
- Coordinate information requests and contributions across teams, consolidating inputs into summaries or updates (non-analytical).
- Support compliance with organisational processes by ensuring required documentation is prepared, submitted and stored correctly.
- Support administration of projects including due diligence, contracting, payment processing, record-keeping, compliance monitoring, and grant closure
- Maintain shared calendars, contact lists, distribution lists and internal communication channels.
- Support and enable a safe environment, adhering to safeguarding reporting and monitoring requirements of the role.
- Gather and collate information, ensuring that established work plans and activities are monitored and delivered consistently in accordance with requirements, standards and practice, escalating where necessary to line management to highlight potential issues.
- Support in tracking/reporting platforms; and at the instruction of S4CV leaders, maintain guidance and resource tools which support programme planning, implementation, changes and advancement.

**Desirable Skills**

- Numerate with proven quantitative and qualitative data management skills.
- Strong administrative, organisational and coordination skills, with attention to detail.
- Experience supporting teams through scheduling, documentation, meeting coordination and action tracking.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office tools, particularly Excel (basic tracking), Word, Outlook and Teams.
- Proficiency or willingness to master other tools particularly NetSuite, Kofax
- Ability to manage multiple tasks, priorities and deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to liaise confidently with diverse, multicultural and multilingual stakeholders.
- Experience working across teams and time zones is desirable.
- Comfortable handling confidential and sensitive information appropriately.

**Your, Ethos:**

- Demonstrate an understanding of and commitment to safeguarding in a local and international context.
- Demonstrates ability and willingness to work in a diverse, multicultural, multilingual and intergenerational environment that is anti-racist and respectful of others.
- An intersectional (pro) feminist passionate about sexual reproductive health care rights + justice, including safe abortion.
- Supportive of people’s rights regardless of sexuality or gender identity/expression and supportive of workers’ rights and access to health care in sex work.

jobs.title: Wash Officer - Venezuela
jobs.body:
Location: Caracas/La Guaira

Duration: Short-term contract

Reporting to: WASH Coordinator

Closing date: 3 November 2026

**Job purpose**

The WASH Officer will serve as the primary technical and operational liaison to ensure the smooth implementation of water, sanitation and hygiene interventions following the June 2026 earthquakes.

Under the supervision of the WASH Coordinator, the WASH Officer will lead the execution of technical assessments, the rehabilitation of community and health infrastructure, and hygiene promotion. They will also ensure effective coordination with local stakeholders and adherence to quality standards and reporting deadlines for programme funders.

**The main responsibilities of this post include:**

**1. Technical implementation and infrastructure**

- Lead the data collection and needs assessments for WASH in the intervention areas to identify gaps in water and sanitation services.
- To technically supervise the construction, rehabilitation or adaptation activities of sanitation structures and community water infrastructure.
- Lead the evaluation of essential equipment and coordinate the implementation of handwashing stations at scale in priority clinics in La Guaira.
- Ensure that all technical interventions comply with Sphere standards and WASH methodologies in emergencies.

**2. Supervision of community activities and promotion of hygiene**

- Carry out follow-up visits and continuous monitoring of the implementation sites to verify the development of activities and ensure that the project objectives are achieved.
- Develop, organise and support training processes, guiding communities and local teams on the use, maintenance and good practices of water and sanitation.
- Support the logistics of community activities, maintaining fluid and assertive communication with community leaders, institutions and operational partners to facilitate access and implementation.
- Proactively identify risks, problems, or delays in the execution of field activities and propose timely corrective actions.

**3. Logistics and operational coordination**

- Support the monitoring of field budgets and the tracking of requests for the acquisition of critical WASH supplies.
- Oversee community distribution and inventory control of water purification tablets and hygiene kits, ensuring that they conform to current budgetary adjustments.
- Collaborate with the logistics team to ensure that transport contracts, warehouse space rentals and material branding are aligned with distribution schedules\*.\*

**4. Monitoring, data and reports**

- Prepare periodic field reports, records, attendance lists, minutes and other qualitative-quantitative verification means related to the activities carried out.
- Consolidate and validate the information collected in the field using mobile information collection tools (e.g., Kobo Collect).
- Ensure the timely delivery of technical draft progress reports to strictly comply with the cut-off dates and reporting deadlines of the various donors.

**5. Protection and safeguarding**

- Ensure that all procedures developed in the field protect and seek dignified treatment towards programme participants and partners.
- To act with the highest level of honesty and integrity in the detection, care or referral of any possible case of mistreatment, abuse or sexual exploitation.
- Promote a protective culture, guaranteeing the privacy and strict confidentiality of the organisation's data, facts and procedures.

**5. Others**

1. Any other function that may be assigned by the WASH Coordinator.

The MENTOR Initiative works in a constantly changing humanitarian environment - reasonable duties that do not fit the above job description but help to further the overall aims and goals of the programme may be requested.

**Role requirements**

- Have the legal right to live and work in Venezuela.
- University degree in environmental health, sanitation, civil or environmental engineering, public health or related fields (Essential)[\[SB1\]](https://reliefweb.int/#_msocom_1) .
- Minimum two years of verifiable experience in supervisory roles, monitoring and implementation of Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) activities in Venezuela (Essential).
- Previous experience in community activities and hygiene promotion.
- Practical knowledge of Sphere and WASH standards in emergencies and methodologies such as Community Led-Total Sanitation (Desirable).
- Basic or intermediate proficiency in Office 365 and mobile data collection tools.
- Excellent skills in developing qualitative and quantitative reports, and good communication skills (oral and written).
- Proactive, empathic, strong service orientation and ability to work in a team.
- Experience working with NGOs in emergency contexts (Desirable).

The MENTOR Initiative is an equal opportunity employer and values diversity in the organisation. We ensure the constant non-discrimination throughout the recruitment process.

The MENTOR Initiative is committed to promoting diversity and gender equality and strongly encourages candidates from under-represented backgrounds to apply.

The MENTOR Initiative applies a zero-tolerance approach to sexual exploitation, abuse, mistreatment or harassment, and other types of unethical behaviour including fraud.

The MENTOR Initiative will contact previous employers of applicants to determine if they have any history of violating international standards and codes of conduct relating to such matters.

jobs.title: Chargé-e des Opérations - SENEGAL (JPO)
jobs.body:
**Entrée en fonction :** 1.12.26

**Durée :** 6 mois

**Lieu :** Dakar, Sénégal

**Statut :** non accompagné

Terre des hommes ne fixe pas de date de clôture pour ce poste ; le recrutement se poursuit jusqu'à ce que le poste soit pourvu.

**Tdh :**

La Fondation Terre des hommes (Tdh), dont le siège est à Lausanne et le bureau à Zurich, est la plus grande organisation suisse de défense des droits de l'enfant avec plus de 2000 collaborateurs et collaboratrices dans le monde. Nous nous engageons aux côtés des enfants pour garantir leurs droits, protéger leur vie et améliorer leur bien-être. Nous y parvenons grâce à nos programmes innovants dans les domaines de la santé, de la migration et de l'accès à la justice, conçus pour avoir un impact positif et durable.

**Contexte :**

Terre des hommes Lausanne (Tdh), fondée en 1960, est la plus grande organisation suisse de défense des droits de l'enfant. Tdh se consacre à apporter des changements significatifs et durables dans la vie des enfants et des jeunes, en particulier ceux et celles qui sont le plus en danger. Tdh est active dans une trentaine de pays, dans des contextes humanitaires et de développement.

En Afrique subsaharienne, Tdh intervient directement dans 8 pays (Burkina Faso, Burundi, Guinée-Conakry, Kenya Mali, Mauritanie, Nigeria et Sénégal,) et via des partenariats dans 6 autres pays (Benin, Cameroun, Madagascar, Niger, Togo et Ouganda).

Dans le cadre de la décentralisation de son modèle d'organisation, Tdh à ouvert un bureau régional à Dakar au Sénégal pour lequel un poste de Chargé.e des Opérations est ouvert.

**Responsabilités :**

Sous la supervision de la Conseillère Régionale en recherche de fonds, le.la Chargé.e des Opérations appuie le bureau régional et les équipes pays dans la mise en œuvre des activités liées aux subventions et à la collecte de fonds dans la région Afrique.

Ce poste contribue aux processus relatifs aux subventions et à la collecte de fonds — du suivi des opportunités à l'élaboration des propositions et au reporting auprès des bailleurs — tout en soutenant les efforts en matière d'engagement des bailleurs et de partenariats à l'échelle de la région.

Grant Acquisition Process

- Contribue à l'identification et au suivi des opportunités de financement pertinentes pour les programmes de Tdh dans la région Afrique.
- Appuie le développement et la soumission de propositions de projet régionales, multipays et pays : appui ou coordination du processus d’écriture, respect des procédures bailleurs, développement de plans d’action, écriture, traduction, enregistrement sur les plateformes de soumission.
- Contribue au contrôle qualité et à la finalisation des rapports pour des financements institutionnels tout en s’assurant de la soumission en temps voulu (suivi du calendrier et des échéances, relances lorsque nécessaire auprès des contributeurs, consolidation des données, etc.), conformément aux exigences contractuelles et aux normes de Tdh.
- Assure le suivi des besoins en cofinancement avec la CR Finance, appui l'élaboration de propositions et rapports de projets à destination de fondations en coordination avec le secteur philanthropie.
- Veille à ce que les informations relatives aux subventions et aux financements dans Engage360 et les GFU pays et région (système interne de Tdh) soient exactes et régulièrement mises à jour, et assure le suivi auprès des équipes concernées pour garantir l'exhaustivité des données. En cas d’absence de Chargé.e de Grant dans une délégation, assure directement la mise à jour des données pour le pays concerné.
- Appuie le développement des contrats de partenariats opérationnels (contenu, signature, archivage, etc.).
- Contribue à l’analyse des réponses aux demandes de financements institutionnels et philanthropiques.
- S’assure de la collecte et de l’archivage des documents institutionnels nécessaires à la signature des contrats en collaboration avec le siège, la région, les délégations et les partenaires.

Communication

- Appuie la relation avec les bailleurs de fonds et les partenaires, y compris la préparation de supports de recherche de fonds (ex. : témoignages, récits de réussite).
- Appuie le rapportage annuel à travers la vérification et la consolidation des données et informations projets, en coordination avec les équipes PREX, Q&A et Grants, ainsi qu’avec les autres parties prenantes concernées aux niveaux des délégations et de la région.
- Contribue à la communication interne liée aux projets (newsletter mensuelle, supports spécifiques, etc.) et consolide les éléments proposés par les délégations et la région, en veillant à la cohérence, à l’exactitude et à la qualité des informations rapportées.

*La description complète du poste sera communiquée aux candidats sélectionnés pour lancer le processus de recrutement.*

**Profil recherché**

**Formation :**

Etude supérieure (Master ou autre diplôme équivalant en relations internationales, développement ou autre domaine pertinent)

**Langues :**

Excellentes compétences linguistiques en Français et Anglais.

**Compétences :**

- Bonne compréhension de la gestion du cycle de projet dans les environnements de développement, d'urgence et de crises prolongées, notamment en Afrique
- Bonne compréhension du processus d’aquisition de financements.

**IT :** Maitrise des outils et applications usuels (Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook, etc.)

**Conditions :**

Contrat suisse

Salaire mensuel brut CHF 2450- x13,36 mois

Assurances : maladie, accident, rapatriement

Congés annuels : 25 jours/an

Vols aller-retour vers le lieu d'affectation

**Code Global de Conduite et Politiques Ethiques de Tdh :**

S'engage à promouvoir et à respecter le Code de Conduite Global, à rapporter systématiquement toute violation du Code à travers les mécanismes formels de rapport de Tdh et à traiter toute violation des procédures et des processus de manière appropriée.

Sensibilise la Fondation aux risques de non-respect des politiques, de violence et d'abus, et aux droits qui en découlent, à l'égard des enfants, des membres de la communauté et de nos propres employé.e.s.

S'engage à respecter les principales politiques et directives éthiques, notamment la politique de sauvegarde, la politique de lutte contre la fraude et la corruption, la politique relative aux conflits d'intérêts et d'autres politiques liées à la prévention du financement du terrorisme et des activités criminelles, ainsi qu’au comportement sur le lieu de travail.

S'engage à mettre en pratique les valeurs et les principes en adoptant un comportement exemplaire, en parfaite adéquation avec le code de conduite, et en respectant toujours les procédures et les processus établis.

S'engage à développer une culture de management conforme et éclairée au sein de l'organisation et dans notre travail avec les enfants et les communautés dans lesquelles nous opérons.

jobs.title: Digital Fundraising and Communications Officer
source: Medecins du Monde - Turkey / Dunya Doktorlari Dernegi
jobs.body:
**Dünya Doktorları Dernegi (DDD)** is a Turkish based humanitarian non-governmental organisation that facilitates access to healthcare for populations affected by armed conflict, violence, natural disasters, disease, famine, poverty and exclusion.

Our organization collaborates with partners and key stakeholders to implement projects that facilitate access to primary and secondary-level healthcare services to respond to the medical needs of displaced population.

DDD is the 16th member of the Doctors of the World International Network that is committed to meeting the health needs of vulnerable people globally.

Please visit [www.dunyadoktorlari.org.tr](http://www.dunyadoktorlari.org.tr) to learn more.

· Produce and coordinate written, graphic, photographic, and video content for digital and print publications.

· Maintain an annual calendar of international and health-related days relevant to DDD's mission and develop timely content and fundraising hooks around them in coordination with program teams.

· Work with program teams to collect field stories, photos, videos, and impact data for donor communications, newsletters, promotional materials, and fundraising content.

· Ensure compliance with DDD branding, messaging, and visibility guidelines, including consent and data protection.

· Manage the archiving and structuring of the DDD communications Sharepoint.

**Social Media and Digital Visibility**

· Manage DDD's social media presence, including Instagram, LinkedIn, X, YouTube, Facebook, and other relevant platforms for newsletters and SMS campaigns.

· Develop and implement visibility initiatives that increase audience reach and supporter engagement.

· Create, schedule, publish, and monitor content across digital channels, and recommend improvements.

**Monitoring and Reporting**

· Track and report on donor acquisition, fundraising revenue, audience growth, website performance, and digital engagement.

· Analyse fundraising and digital performance data to support decision-making and continuous improvement.

· Produce regular reports and recommendations for management.

**Reporting**

· Provide regular reporting on your activities to your Line-Manager upon his/her solicitation;

· Provide your line-manager with a Handover Report at the end of your contract

**Compliance & Ethics**  
Promote and encourage a culture of compliance and ethics throughout Dünya Doktorları Derneği. As applicable to the position, maintains a clear understanding of Dünya Doktorları Derneği and donor compliance and ethics standards and adheres to those standards. Conducts work with the highest level of integrity. Communicates these values to staff and to partners and requires them to adhere to these values.

**Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse**  
Actively promote PSEA (Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse) standards within Dünya Doktorları Derneği and amongst beneficiaries served by Dünya Doktorları Derneği.
