Collect and verify accurate field information using approved paper-based or digital tools; maintain complete records; and submit timely field updates and reports to the Sustainable Livelihood Program Coordinator.
- **Community + Stakeholder Engagement:** Maintain regular field-level communication with farmers, Lead Farmers, Farmer Groups, village governments, community leaders, and government agricultural extension personnel. Coordinate local field activities, promote meaningful participation, document community feedback, and promptly report technical, operational, environmental, safeguarding, or community-level concerns through established channels.
- **Field Planning + Program Support:** Prepare and implement weekly and monthly field activity plans in coordination with the Sustainable Livelihood Program Coordinator. Participate in required technical training and support program assessments, monitoring exercises, learning events, evaluations, and partner or donor field visits.

**EDUCATION + WORK EXPERIENCE**

- Diploma or bachelor’s degree in Agriculture, Agronomy, Horticulture, Agroforestry, Agricultural Extension, Rural Development, or a closely related field.
- Practical experience in agricultural extension, farmer training, community mobilization, crop production, or smallholder livelihood programs.
- Good understanding of smallholder farming systems and common production constraints.
- Working knowledge of Climate-Smart Agriculture and Conservation Agriculture principles.
- Experience facilitating practical and participatory farmer training through Farmer Field Schools, demonstration plots, Farmer Groups, farm-level coaching, or similar approaches.
- Experience collecting accurate field information, maintaining organized records, and preparing clear activity reports.
- Previous experience implementing Conservation Agriculture, Agroforestry, Quality Declared Seed, seed production, community seed systems, or seed-quality activities is an advantage.
- Experience using KoboCollect, ODK, or similar digital data-collection platforms is an advantage.
- Ability to ride a motorcycle and possession of an appropriate valid driving license is an advantage.

**SKILLS + ABILITIES**

- Models the Ethos in all professional interactions, demonstrating a commitment to the organization’s values, vision, and conduct standards.
- **Agricultural Extension:** Able to explain and demonstrate approved agricultural practices clearly and practically to farmers and provide reliable follow-up in the field.
- **Farmer Training + Facilitation:** Strong participatory training, facilitation, and community-mobilization skills, with the ability to work respectfully with farmers and community-based groups.
- **Field Monitoring + Documentation:** Strong attention to detail and the ability to collect accurate information, maintain organized records, document observations and feedback, and submit timely reports.
- **Communication + Collaboration:** Strong interpersonal and problem-solving skills, with the ability to communicate effectively with farmers, Lead Farmers, community leaders, government extension personnel, and project colleagues.
- **Technology:** Comfortable using smartphones or tablets for routine program work and digital data collection.
- **Language:** Able to communicate effectively in Kiswahili; knowledge of languages commonly used within the project area is an advantage.
- **Field Readiness:** Able to work independently within approved plans, travel regularly, and spend substantial time in rural communities and farmers’ fields.

**WORK CONDITIONS**

- **Work Environment:** The position is primarily field-based, with regular work in rural communities, farms, Farmer Field Schools, demonstration plots, and other project sites. Work may involve basic facilities and exposure to heat, rain, dust, and varied terrain.

Administrative duties include record keeping, digital data entry, and preparation of reports.

jobs.title: Programme Coordinator, Sustainable Livelihoods
jobs.body:
**Reports to**: Sustainable Livelihoods Manager  
**Department**: Compassionate Carbon Tanzania - Sustainable Livelihoods  
**Position classification**: Full-time  
**Location**: Lumuma, Kilosa District / Mbuga, Mpwapwa District (Rubeho Mountains Carbon Project Area)  
**Employment type:** Full-time **(note: visa sponsorship not available for this position)**

**COMPANY INFORMATION**

Compassionate Carbon Tanzania Ltd is a mission-driven organization launched by Compassionate Carbon LLC and Eden: People+Planet (Eden). Specializing in developing and implementing landscape-scale forest carbon projects through Forest Landscape Restoration (FLR) and Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation (REDD+), we collaborate with local communities to restore landscapes, create jobs, protect ecosystems, and mitigate climate change.

Our projects integrate nature-based solutions to help meet global emissions targets while ensuring community ownership and long-term sustainability. The Rubeho Mountains Carbon Project, a significant initiative in Tanzania, focuses on native forest restoration and community-based conservation efforts.

**POSITION SUMMARY:** The Sustainable Livelihood Programme Coordinator is the key operational link between program plans and effective delivery in the field, ensuring that livelihood activities translate into well-coordinated, high-quality support for participating farmers and communities. Reporting to the Sustainable Livelihood Manager, the Coordinator oversees day-to-day field implementation, supervises Field Extension Officers, and coordinates farmer mobilization, training, demonstrations, and follow-up across project communities. The role monitors progress and implementation quality, identifies and helps resolve field-level challenges, and brings forward practical insights and recommendations to strengthen delivery. Working closely with field teams, communities, government extension personnel, and other local stakeholders, the Coordinator helps ensure approved livelihood approaches are implemented consistently, responsively, and in line with program targets, technical guidance, and available resources.

**ESSENTIAL RESPONSIBILITIES**

- **Program Implementation + Coordination**: Translate approved workplans into weekly and monthly field schedules and coordinate farmer mobilization, training, demonstrations, farm follow-up, and other livelihood activities. Track delivery against targets, timelines, technical guidance, and approved budgets; coordinate field logistics and support agreed program adaptations.
- **Field Team Supervision**: Provide day-to-day supervision and coordination of Field Extension Officers, review field plans, conduct regular supervision visits, and provide practical support in resolving implementation challenges. Ensure field staff maintain accurate records and submit complete reports on time, escalating significant capacity, performance, technical, or operational concerns to the Sustainable Livelihood Manager.
- **Implementation Monitoring + Reporting:** Track implementation progress, verify field records, consolidate weekly and monthly reports, and provide timely updates to the Sustainable Livelihood Manager. Identify delays, emerging risks, operational constraints, and areas requiring corrective action. Support assessments, evaluations, learning activities, and partner or donor field visits.  
    **Stakeholder + Community Coordination:** Coordinate field-level engagement with village governments, government agricultural extension personnel, Lead Farmers, service providers, participating communities, and other relevant stakeholders in support of program implementation. Maintain effective communication among program management, field teams, and communities and ensure concerns, feedback, and implementation issues are documented and escalated appropriately.
- **Program Quality + Continuous Improvement:** Ensure field activities follow approved program approaches and technical guidance, including Climate-Smart Agriculture, Conservation Agriculture, Agroforestry, and participatory farmer training. Use field observations, monitoring information, and stakeholder feedback to identify implementation issues and recommend practical improvements to the Sustainable Livelihood Manager, supporting agreed corrective actions and program adaptations.

**EDUCATION + WORK EXPERIENCE**

- Bachelor’s degree in Agriculture, Agronomy, Horticulture, Agroforestry, Rural Development, Agricultural Extension, Project Management, or another relevant field.
- Relevant experience coordinating agricultural, livelihood, rural development, or smallholder farmer programs, including translating workplans into field implementation.
- Demonstrated experience supervising or coordinating field-based teams and supporting staff to plan, deliver, document, and report on activities.
- Practical knowledge of Climate-Smart Agriculture, particularly Conservation Agriculture and Agroforestry, and an understanding of smallholder farming systems, agricultural extension approaches, farmer organization, and participatory farmer training.
- Experience coordinating activities with rural communities, local government, agricultural extension personnel, service providers, or similar stakeholders.
- Experience tracking implementation progress, coordinating multiple field activities, and preparing clear, timely reports.
- Familiarity with Quality Declared Seed, community seed systems, seed security interventions, or digital field-data systems such as KoboCollect or ODK is an advantage.
- Experience coordinating programs across multiple villages or geographically dispersed communities is an advantage.

**SKILLS + ABILITIES**

- Models the Ethos in all professional interactions, demonstrating a commitment to the organization’s values, vision, and conduct standards.
- **Program Coordination:** Strong ability to organize field implementation, coordinate multiple activities, manage competing priorities, and maintain progress against workplans, targets, and timelines.
- **Team Supervision:** Able to provide clear direction, practical coaching, and effective day-to-day supervision to field-based staff.
- **Technical Knowledge:** Good understanding of smallholder agriculture, Climate-Smart Agriculture, Conservation Agriculture, Agroforestry, agricultural extension, and participatory farmer training, with the ability to support consistent field implementation of approved approaches.
- **Monitoring + Reporting:** Able to track implementation, verify field records, identify delivery gaps or risks, and prepare clear and accurate program updates and reports.
- **Stakeholder Engagement:** Strong facilitation and relationship-building skills, with the ability to work respectfully with farmers, communities, government representatives, service providers, and project colleagues.
- **Problem Solving + Adaptability:** Practical and solution-oriented, with the ability to respond constructively to field constraints and support appropriate program adaptations.
- **Communication:** Strong spoken and written Kiswahili and working proficiency in English.

**WORK CONDITIONS**

- **Work Environment:** Combination of office and field settings, including regular visits to forested and rural project sites under varied weather and terrain conditions. Frequent interaction with local communities and multi-stakeholder teams may involve basic field accommodations and extended time in remote areas.
- **Work schedule:** Full-time, with standard office hours, requiring occasional flexibility (e.g. early mornings, evenings, or weekends) to accommodate field requirements.
- **Physical Requirements:** Moderate physical fitness is required for fieldwork in rustic environments, including walking long distances on uneven terrain, standing for extended periods, Must be comfortable in challenging field conditions. Work also involves typical office tasks (computer use, meetings) when not in the field.
- **Travel:** Regular domestic travel within Tanzania to remote project sites for monitoring and community consultation, sometimes involving difficult travel conditions and overnight stays.
- **Safety + Special Conditions:** Adherence to all applicable safety protocols and alignment of activities with established environmental and social safeguards. **Visa sponsorship is not available for this position; only Tanzanian nationals will be considered.**

jobs.title: Regional Logistician & Administrative Coordinator
jobs.body:
**Mennonite Central Committee (MCC)** is a worldwide ministry of Anabaptist churches, that shares God’s love and compassion for all in the name of Christ by responding to basic human needs and working for peace and justice. MCC envisions communities worldwide in right relationship with God, one another and creation.

**Position Title:** Regional Logistician & Administrative Coordinator  
**Reporting to:** Area Directors for East Africa & Sahel  
**Location:** Nairobi, Kenya  
**Employment Type:** One-year renewable contract

**Annual Gross Salary:** KES 1,861,524 - 2,047,676, commensurate with experience and within the established salary band  
**Start Date:** Tentatively 15 January 2027

**Job Synopsis:**

The Regional Logistician & Administrative Coordinator manages the logistical, administrative, and communication operations of the Area Directors' office, working closely with the six country program offices in the East Africa & Sahel region. The role coordinates travel, accommodation, transportation, medical support, and other logistics for regional staff visiting Kenya for meetings, medical care, training, or site visits, and oversees the regional apartment, including guest bookings and hospitality arrangements.

The position serves as a key coordination point for the Area Directors by supporting correspondence management, procurement of goods and services, and the organization of regional meetings and events. The role also supports regional finance operations by assisting with invoice processing, payment tracking, maintaining financial records and supporting documentation, contributing to budget monitoring and reconciliations, and preparing finance-related reports and audit documentation in collaboration with the Regional Finance Coordinator.

**Responsibilities:**

**Regional Coordination**

- Plan and organize the logistics for the annual YAMEN Orientation for all global YAMENers; identify the venue, serve as the main point of contact, ensure all participants arrive and depart well, and work with CPCs to ensure participants' needs are met.
- Organize and coordinate regional events such as orientations, Rep Gatherings, and meetings, including logistical arrangements and venue bookings.
- Manage Regional Board meetings, ensuring the board meets as required, bringing items to the agenda, tracking action items and outcomes, and coordinating any required follow-up.
- Accompany donors on country visits when Area Directors are unavailable, ensuring the country office is prepared and all details are handled.
- Represent the Area Directors in-country when needed, especially during times of office transition, serving as a listening ear, observing operations, and providing feedback to the Area Directors on how systems can be improved.

**Logistics & Communication**

- Facilitate the scheduling of travel and meetings for the Area Directors, identifying important upcoming events and overseeing necessary preparations.
- Arrange transportation, accommodation, and other travel logistics for the Area Directors, ensuring smooth and efficient travel experiences and maintaining regular communication throughout.
- Manage the Regional Apartment, maintaining a schedule of visitors and coordinating cooking and cleaning arrangements for guests as needed.
- Communicate with hotels and other service providers to confirm reservations and address any concerns or challenges that may arise.
- Maintain smooth communication between the Area Directors and relevant stakeholders.
- Organize meetings (in person and virtually) as required by the Area Directors, including coordinating logistics, preparing and distributing meeting materials, and recording and distributing minutes.
- Work with the Area Directors to connect and resource MCC's Africa program offices, including maintaining current program resource materials, procedural manuals, and related documentation.
- Collaborate with planning committees to ensure the successful execution of events while adhering to timelines and budgets.
- Support the preparation of reports, presentations, and other documents through formatting, proofreading, and translation between English and French.
- Assist in managing databases and information systems, ensuring data integrity and accessibility for relevant stakeholders.
- Monitor incoming communications and prioritize urgent messages or requests requiring the Area Directors' attention.
- Relay important information promptly and accurately to ensure timely response and action.
- Foster effective communication and collaboration between the Area Directors and diverse stakeholders, including government officials, public entities, and community members.
- Provide cultural insights and guidance to enhance interactions and relationships in multicultural settings.
- Identify areas for process improvement in logistical and communication support services and propose innovative solutions to enhance efficiency and effectiveness.
- Seek feedback from stakeholders and incorporate suggestions for optimizing support mechanisms.
- Uphold professional standards in all communications and interactions, representing MCC in a positive and professional manner.
- Represent the region on various committees and working groups.

**Planning, Learning, and Disaster Response (PLDR) Collaboration**

- Assist with reporting requirements for the Planning, Learning, and Disaster Response (PLDR) Department, Communications, and other parts of the MCC system.
- Obtain quotations from consultants conducting country program reviews and work with HR to maintain and update the consultant pool.
- Compile Annual Plans and Annual Reports for review by the Area Directors.
- Track projects across the East Africa & Sahel region, maintaining a database of ongoing projects and working closely with the Area Directors to identify projects nearing completion and support renewal planning.

**Regional Connecting People's Coordination**

- Communicate logistics for YAMEN Orientation and Re-entry, ensuring participants have the required visas, are aware of travel requirements, and receive the necessary logistical support.
- Identify the needs of different YAMEN cohorts while in service, including follow-up training sessions, and coordinate such trainings with MCC staff and external service providers or counsellors. Review qualifications and rates and share recommendations with the Area Directors for approval.
- Handle confidential information with discretion and ensure compliance with data protection regulations and organizational policies.
- Support CPCs and Representatives in ensuring policies are implemented fairly and consistently. Assist with policy interpretation for workers in consultation with Representatives, Human Resources, and relevant program coordinators.
- Connect with alumni to generate interest for GSL applicants, especially in countries where there is no MCC office.

**Administrative Support**

- Manage administrative tasks, including Microsoft Office administration, filing, invoice processing, expense claims, report preparation, and financial documentation related to the Area Directors' activities.
- Support communication and information sharing with English- and French-speaking stakeholders through interpretation, translation, or coordination of language support as needed.
- Assist with managing shared regional documents and ensure they are readily accessible when needed.
- Maintain organized filing systems for documents, reports, and other administrative records, both electronically and in hard copy.
- Assist the EAS HR Coordinator and Country Representatives with talent acquisition activities as needed.

**Finance Support**

- Support finance and accounting activities under the guidance of the Regional Finance Coordinator.
- Assist with invoice processing, payment tracking, and maintaining supporting documentation.
- Maintain accurate financial records, filing systems, and document retention processes.
- Support budget monitoring, expenditure tracking, and account reconciliations as assigned.
- Assist with finance-related reporting, audit preparation, and compliance documentation.
- Coordinate with vendors, staff, and finance personnel to ensure timely processing of payments and resolution of finance-related queries.
- Perform any other duties and responsibilities as may be assigned from time to time within the scope of the role.

**Qualifications:**

All MCC workers are expected to exhibit a commitment to a personal Christian faith and discipleship; active church membership; and nonviolent peacemaking.

An invitation to an assignment is contingent on the successful completion of a criminal background check.

**Required Qualifications**

- Legally eligible to work in Kenya
- Bachelor's degree or diploma in Project Management, Business Administration, Education, Commerce, Accounting, Finance, or a related field.
- Minimum of three (3) years' experience in administration, logistics, office operations, finance support, or a related role, preferably within an international non-governmental organization (INGO).
- Fluent in English, with excellent verbal and written communication skills and the ability to foster positive relationships and open communication both in person and electronically.
- Strong interpersonal skills, with the ability to interact confidently and effectively with diverse stakeholders, including international individuals, government officials, vendors, and members of the public.
- Ability to represent MCC in a professional and welcoming manner.
- Highly organized, with proficiency in narrative documentation, data entry, spreadsheets, Microsoft Office applications, and PowerPoint presentations.
- Ability to work independently, proactively resolve issues, and handle confidential information with professionalism and discretion.
- Open to feedback, adaptable, and committed to continuous learning.
- Willing and available to work overtime, particularly before and during meetings and events.
- Willing and able to travel locally and internationally as required.
- Strong relational skills, including the ability to build and maintain positive working relationships, collaborate effectively with MCC teams and partners, and mentor young adults.
- Demonstrated cross-cultural awareness and competence, with the ability to support cross-cultural adaptation and engagement.
- Ability to provide worker care by demonstrating empathy, maintaining confidentiality, and encouraging healthy self-care practices among participants.
- Ability to work effectively in diverse and changing situations and to respond appropriately to participant emergencies with support from the Area Directors.
- Strong planning, coordination, and organizational skills, ensuring efficient use of resources and timely achievement of objectives.

**Preferred Qualifications**

- French language skills, including the ability to communicate, translate, and interpret in professional settings.
- CPA Part I-III or equivalent accounting training.
- Experience supporting regional or multi-country operations.
- Experience coordinating regional events, travel arrangements, and international logistics.

jobs.title: Short Term Adviser: Performance Stories (Bougainville)
jobs.body:
**About TSSP Phase 3**

The Australia Transport Sector Support Program Phase 3 (TSSP3) is a flagship partnership between the Governments of Papua New Guinea and Australia that strengthens the transport sector to improve connectivity, safety and accessibility, supporting economic growth, service delivery and sustainable community development. Working with government agencies, industry and communities, its multidisciplinary teams support reforms and investments in transport planning, infrastructure, governance, safety and inclusion to build stronger institutions and a more resilient, better-connected transport network. TSSP3 offers a collaborative and inclusive workplace where skilled professionals contribute innovative thinking, grow professionally and help deliver lasting outcomes for communities across Papua New Guinea.

**About DT Global Asia Pacific**

At DT Global Asia Pacific, we aim to positively impact people’s lives through delivery excellence. As a leading implementing partner across Asia and the Pacific, we co-create locally led solutions in partnership with governments, communities, and stakeholders. We bring together talented teams and deep regional expertise to deliver initiatives that promote inclusive economic growth, essential services, and resilient, secure communities. With over 1,500 staff, experts in 22+ countries and more than 60 years of development experience, we tackle complex community, national and transnational challenges — from governance and justice systems to climate resilience, infrastructure and social equity — with innovative thinking and a commitment to long-term impact.

For more information, please see [www.dt-global.com](http://www.dt-global.com/)

  
**The Role**

The Short-Term Adviser: Performance Stories (Bougainville) will lead the development of a compelling evidence-based performance story that demonstrates how TSSP3, in partnership with the Autonomous Bougainville Government (ABG) and the Government of Papua New Guinea (GoPNG), has contributed to building a sustainable road maintenance ecosystem in Bougainville. The assignment will focus on documenting the broader systems change achieved through long-term investment in local institutions, contractors, governance arrangements and communities, rather than solely reporting on infrastructure outputs.

Working closely with the MERLA, Roads, Communications and Operations teams, you will design and implement an evaluation approach that captures evidence of institutional strengthening, local contractor development, government and private sector collaboration and community benefits resulting from improved transport access. You will undertake desktop reviews, key informant interviews, community consultations and field visits, analyse findings and develop practical, credible and decision useful products that contribute to TSSP3 performance reporting and organisational learning.

This role offers an opportunity to work with a nationally significant transport program, engaging with government agencies, development partners, community stakeholders and the private sector to highlight the lasting impact of transport sector investments in Bougainville.

Click on the link or copy and paste it to access the full Terms of Reference for this position:

[https://l1nq.com/x4ocz7s](https://l1nq.com/x4ocz7s)

**About You**

You are an experienced evaluation professional who turns complex evidence into clear, credible findings. You bring sound judgement, cross-cultural collaboration and consensus-building skills, a commitment to locally led, inclusive and resilient development, and the ability to mentor others and adapt to resource-constrained environments.

- Relevant tertiary qualification and experience delivering complex development evaluations, performance studies or contribution-focused case studies.
- Strong MERLA/MEAL knowledge and experience evaluating institutional, policy, governance and systems change, capability and sustainability.
- Ability to translate Terms of Reference into practical evaluation plans, sampling strategies, stakeholder maps and research tools.
- Advanced qualitative research and consultation skills, with proficiency in Microsoft Office and qualitative/data analysis tools.
- Government and senior stakeholder experience in PNG or comparable Pacific contexts, with strong cross-cultural communication and excellent English.
- Knowledge of locally led development and ability to embed GEDSI, disability inclusion, safeguarding/PSEAH, climate change and disaster resilience throughout evaluations.
- Familiarity with Australian Government/DFAT development program performance and reporting standards is highly desirable.

**Why Join TSSP3**

Be part of a program helping build a safer, better-connected transport system for Papua New Guinea.

At TSSP3, we work alongside local partners and communities to strengthen transport systems, build lasting capability and connect people with opportunities. Join a committed team of Papua New Guinean and international professionals, where your contribution matters and collaboration, innovation and care for people underpin our work.

jobs.title: Intensive Case Management Caseworker
jobs.body:
**Job Overview:** The Intensive Case Management (ICM) Caseworker will address barriers to safety and wellness for especially vulnerable refugees, asylees, and other ORR-eligible populations. The ICM caseworker will be expected to provide strengths-based, client-centered case management to single-headed refugee households; survivors of domestic violence and gender-based violence; older refugees; youth and young adults without parents or permanent guardians; refugees experiencing mental health or psychological difficulties; refugees with physical disabilities or medical conditions; unanticipated refugee arrivals and secondary migrants; and refugees who identify as lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender or queer (LGBTQ). They work closely with clients, colleagues, and external parties to develop service plans to meet individual client needs and preferences utilizing a broad range of financial, medical, social, vocational, and other services and resources in accordance with client eligibility and program requirements.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Determine client eligibility for ICM programming and conduct intake assessments, review program expectations, outcomes, and confidentiality with each potential client.
- Develop individualized, SMART Self-sufficiency plans for each client enrolled in the ICM program.
- Evaluate client progress every six months during active program enrollment to determine the client’s progress towards goals and work with the client to identify new needs and actions needed.
- Assist clients in navigating healthcare and social service systems, which may include helping clients apply for benefits and attend and schedule appointments.
- Conduct community outreach and maintain a strong network of service providers that meet client needs. The ICM caseworker may also be expected to maintain a strong relationship with local and state level refugee coordinators and health coordinators to ensure client needs are met.
- Provide clients with extended orientation on a variety of topics such as women’s health, navigating transportation systems, and navigating physical healthcare systems at the local level.
- Respond to client crises, with guidance from supervisor as needed.
- Assist clients with requesting financial assistance when applicable and track the received financial assistance within case files.
- Maintain up-to-date documentation in client’s case file to ensure services are properly documented throughout the client’s service period; document all services provided in IRC’s database, Efforts to Outcomes (ETO).
- Attend relevant trainings and meetings at the local and national level.
- May train and lead the activities of volunteers and interns.
- Other duties as assigned.

**Job Requirements:**

**Education:** Bachelor’s degree in social work, public health, or related field of study preferred.

**Work Experience:**

- Minimum of 1-2 years of case management experience with similar populations and/or client needs required.

**Demonstrated Skills & Competencies:**

- Strong relationship building, diplomacy, and networking skills; ability to effectively build internal and external relationships.
- Demonstrated success working and communicating effectively in a multi-cultural environment.
- Self-starter with excellent problem-solving skills combined with the proven ability to prioritize and manage time effectively.
- Attention to detail and accuracy in work product.
- Fluent in English required, both spoken and written; proficiency in language(s) spoken by client group preferred, including Dari/Pashto.
- Proficient in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook); ability to use the internet and other digital tools for data entry, research, and problem-solving purposes.
- Valid driver’s license and access to a personal, insured vehicle.

**Working Environment:**

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities.
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.

***This position is expected to end on September 30, 2027.***

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $23 - $25.90/hr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

jobs.title: Education Specialist
jobs.body:
**Job Summary**

The Education Specialist facilitates educational services to enhance integration of refugee and immigrant adult clients and their children. The Education Specialist works within IRC providing a range of supportive services to meet clients’ educational needs. This position is primarily responsible for coordinating and teaching necessary educational classes as well as facilitating individual tutoring and mentoring services provided by volunteers and interns.

Responsibilities may include but are not limited to:

**Educational Service Coordination**

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

jobs.title: Case Coordination Caseworker
jobs.body:
**Job Overview:** The Caseworker provides trauma-informed services to refugees and other ORR qualified immigrants to support a positive integration experience and the achievement of client self-sufficiency. The Caseworker works closely with clients, colleagues, and external parties to develop service and/or self-sufficiency plans to meet individual client needs and preferences utilizing a broad range of financial, medical, social, vocational, and other services and resources in accordance with client eligibility and program requirements.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Conduct intake services with clients to assess needs. Develop self-sufficiency plans and timelines in partnership with each client. Provide individualized support through direct services, referrals, and advocacy.
- Receive referrals for case management for ORR-eligible and TANF-eligible clients and participate in any needed case conference meetings to assure continuity of care.
- Assess client needs, creates Family Self-Sufficiency Plans (FSSPs) and Individual Employability Plans (IEPs), focusing on removing employment barriers, stabilizing, and obtaining and retaining employment.
- Assess and monitor client progress to support their attainment of established goals, address challenges, and to ensure that available resources are utilized. Follow up with any referrals made to other programs.
- Detail each client interaction in accordance with program requirements. Input client information in database(s) and assist with tracking and reporting as needed.
- Collaborate effectively with coworkers and partner organizations. Build and maintain relationships with area service providers for the benefit of clients.
- Use personal, insured vehicle and/or public transportation (where available) to travel and transport clients and materials as needed throughout the service delivery area.
- May train and lead the activities of volunteers and interns.
- Conduct outreach to case management staff, refugee-serving agencies, ethnic community-based organizations, and others to inform service providers and refugees of programs and services.
- Complete eligibility screenings for all referral and enrollment paperwork for all eligible Program participants.
- Provide comprehensive case management services, including assisting with benefits applications as appropriate.
- Guide/assist participants to establish contact and receive support services in the community based on their service plan.
- Ensure all services are linguistically appropriate and help advocate with mainstream service providers for linguistically appropriate services.
- Complete case notes in a detailed and timely fashion.
- Ensure all family data is entered into data management system in a timely manner.
- Assist with the preparation of donor funding reports and new funding proposals.
- Participate in all program meetings, staff development activities, and fully engages as a member of the team.
- Follow all IRC policies, procedures and protocols including adherence to the IRC Way and Child Safeguarding.
- Other related duties as assigned.

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Position Reports to:** Family Stabilization Supervisor

**Indirect Reporting:** Senior Program Manager

**Job Requirements:**

***Education:***

- Undergraduate degree Social Work or similar field strongly preferred; comparable related work experience may be substituted.

***Work Experience:***

- 2+ years of case management experience in a social services environment.
- Experience working with vulnerable or under served populations preferred

***Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:***

- Computer proficiency with an emphasis on Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Teams, Outlook).
- Strong organizational skills and detail-oriented
- Public Speaking and/or presentation experience preferred
- Ability to effectively communicate and work as a team member with collaborative partners, the community, and clients in a cross-cultural, multi-disciplinary environment.
- Ability and willingness to drive 15 passenger van.
- Strong attention to detail with the ability to prioritize and manage time effectively.
- Problem solver capable of working well independently and as a part of a team.

***Language Skills:***

- Proficiency in written and spoken English, bilingual ability preferred in Spanish, Dari, Swahili, Kinyarwanda, Arabic, French or other refugee/immigrant language used in Arizona. Cross-cultural understanding and strong communication skills, both written and verbal.

***Certificates or Licenses:***

- Must have a valid driver’s license, active insurance policy, access to reliable transportation and the ability to travel regularly throughout the service delivery area.
- In accordance with Arizona State Law, must possess or be eligible to receive a fingerprint clearance card.

**Working Environment**\*\*\*:\*\*\*

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities.
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.
- Must be able to lift 35 to 50 pounds (furniture, household supplies, and food boxes).

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $20.97/hr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

jobs.body:
About : Action contre la Faim

Créée en 1979, Action contre la Faim est une organisation non gouvernementale internationale qui lutte contre la faim dans le monde. Sa charte des principes humanitaires - indépendance, neutralité, non-discrimination, accès libre et direct aux victimes, professionnalisme, transparence - fonde son identité depuis 45 ans. Sa mission est de sauver des vies en éliminant la faim par la prévention, la détection et le traitement de la sous-nutrition, en particulier pendant et après les situations d'urgence liées aux conflits et aux catastrophes naturelles. Action contre la Faim coordonne ses programmes autour de 7 domaines d'activités : Nutrition et Santé - Santé Mentale, Soutien Psychosocial - Sécurité Alimentaire et Moyens d'Existence - Eau, Assainissement et Hygiène - Plaidoyer - Climat - Recherche. En 2024, Action contre la Faim est venue en aide à plus de 26 millions de personnes dans 57 pays à travers le monde. www.actioncontrelafaim.org

jobs.title: Protection Officer
jobs.body:
**About World Vision**

For more than 75 years, World Vision has been committed to making a positive and lasting difference in the world. We have become a global leader in improving and transforming the lives of children, their families, and their communities. We help children, families, and communities overcome poverty and injustice, irrespective of religion, race, ethnicity, or gender. Every child deserves a life rich in meaning and purpose. We work with the most vulnerable children in the world so they can experience life in all its fullness.

**Location: Syria - Raqqa**

**Job purpose:**

The Protection Officer is responsible for the technical and day-to-day implementation of protection activities within the project, ensuring that interventions are relevant, inclusive, safe, conflict-sensitive, and aligned with approved project objectives, protection standards, workplans, and donor requirements. The position supports the planning, monitoring, quality assurance, and reporting of protection interventions, while providing technical guidance to protection facilitators, volunteers, partners, and other relevant field staff. The Protection Officer also works closely with relevant protection stakeholders, communities, authorities, and other project sectors to identify and respond to protection risks and promote safe, dignified, and inclusive support to children, adults, and vulnerable groups.

**Major Responsibilities:**

**1. Protection Programme Implementation and Technical Support:**

- Support the planning and implementation of protection activities in line with the approved project design, DIP, performance framework, protection standards, and relevant humanitarian principles.
- Provide technical guidance to protection case workers, PSS and ERW facilitators, volunteers, partner staff, and other field teams involved in protection activities.
- Ensure protection interventions respond to identified protection risks, needs, vulnerabilities, and barriers to accessing services.
- Support the adaptation of protection activities to the local context and the specific needs of children, women, persons with disabilities, displaced populations, and other vulnerable or marginalized groups.
- Promote safe, inclusive, gender-sensitive, child-sensitive, and conflict-sensitive approaches throughout protection programming.
- Ensure that activities are implemented according to the principles of Do No Harm, confidentiality, informed consent, dignity, participation, and non-discrimination.

**2. Protection Monitoring, Risk Identification and Referrals:**

- Support the identification and monitoring of protection risks, concerns, trends, and barriers affecting children, adults, and vulnerable groups.
- Conduct or support protection assessments, community consultations, focus group discussions, key informant interviews, and other relevant data collection activities.
- Identify individuals or groups requiring additional or specialized protection support and facilitate referrals through established referral pathways.
- Maintain updated information on available protection and other relevant services and referral mechanisms.
- Ensure referrals are conducted safely, confidentially, and in accordance with established procedures.
- Monitor emerging protection concerns and communicate significant risks or trends to the Project Coordinator/Area Manager and relevant programme teams.
- Support protection risk mitigation measures and follow up on identified protection concerns within the scope of the position.

**3. Monitoring, Quality Assurance and Capacity Building:**

• Develop and follow up on protection activity plans, schedules, and field implementation plans.

• Monitor participation, coverage, quality, and progress against agreed protection indicators and targets.  
• Conduct regular field visits and provide technical feedback and recommendations to improve protection activities.

• Support the collection, review, verification, and analysis of protection-related data and ensure that information is accurate and timely.

• Identify implementation gaps, protection risks, and emerging needs and propose appropriate corrective actions.  
• Identify capacity-building needs among protection staff, volunteers, partners, and community structures.  
• Support the delivery of training, coaching, mentoring, and awareness sessions on relevant protection topics, including protection principles, safeguarding, PSEA, referral mechanisms, and safe programming.

**4. Coordination and Stakeholder Engagemen:**

- Coordinate with relevant Protection Sector/Sub-Sector actors, authorities, partners, community representatives, service providers, and other stakeholders as required.
- Participate in relevant protection coordination meetings, working groups, technical discussions, and inter-agency coordination mechanisms.
- Engage with communities to understand protection concerns, priorities, barriers, and feedback and ensure that programme responses are appropriate and context-sensitive.
- Support community-based protection mechanisms and promote meaningful participation of women, men, girls, boys, persons with disabilities, and other potentially marginalized groups.
- Coordinate with other project sectors to ensure protection is appropriately mainstreamed across programme interventions, including Education, WASH, FSL, Health, Nutrition, and other relevant sectors..
- Support the identification and strengthening of referral pathways and linkages with specialized services.

**5. Reporting, Documentation and Learning:**

- Prepare regular protection activity updates and contribute to project reports, donor reports, situation updates, and other programme documentation.
- Maintain comprehensive and secure records of protection activities, including attendance, training, monitoring, assessments, community consultations, referrals, and field visits, in accordance with data protection requirements.
- Document protection trends, challenges, achievements, good practices, lessons learned, and success stories while ensuring confidentiality and protection of sensitive information.
- Support the implementation of community feedback and response mechanisms and ensure relevant protection-related feedback is appropriately followed up.
- Support the preparation and review of protection-related proposals, budgets, activity plans, indicators, and project documents as required.
- Coordinate with MEAL colleagues to support data quality, monitoring, accountability, and learning processes.
- Ensure protection documentation is maintained in accordance with organizational, donor, safeguarding, and data protection requirements.

**Knowledge/Qualifications for the Role**

**.Required Professional Experience:**

- At least 2–3 years of relevant experience in protection, humanitarian, development, or community-based programming, preferably with an NGO or humanitarian organization.
- Experience implementing or monitoring protection, child protection, community-based protection, protection monitoring, awareness-raising, or referral activities is desirable.
- Experience working with children, families, displaced populations, vulnerable groups, and communities affected by conflict or displacement.
- Experience providing technical support, coaching, mentoring, or capacity building to staff, volunteers, community structures, or partner organizations.

Experience working with Protection Sector/Sub-Sector coordination mechanisms, referral networks, local authorities, service providers, or other humanitarian actors is an advantage.

**.Required Education, training, license, registration, and certification:**

- Bachelor's degree in Social Work, Psychology, Sociology, Human Rights, Law, International Development, Social Sciences, or another relevant field.
- Additional qualifications or training in Protection, Child Protection, GBV, PSEA, Safeguarding, Humanitarian Action, Human Rights, or related areas are an advantage.

**.Preferred Knowledge and Qualifications**

- Good knowledge of Protection programming principles and approaches relevant to humanitarian and/or development contexts.
- Understanding of barriers to protection access and participation, particularly for vulnerable and marginalized children.
- Knowledge of child safeguarding, child participation, inclusion, gender, and conflict-sensitive programming.
- Good monitoring, data collection, analysis, and reporting skills.
- Strong communication, facilitation, interpersonal, and coordination skills.

Ability to work effectively with partners, community representatives, education

**.Travel and/or Work Environment Requirement**

 The position requires ability and willingness to travel to other WV project sites when needed

**.Physical Requirements**:

- Ability to effectively coordinate with staff and key stakeholders ensure successfully program implementation.

**.Language Requirements:**

 Arabic, English

jobs.title: Project Management Support Specialist
jobs.body:
Under UNOPS supervision, this position will support by empowering project success through operational excellence, data-driven insights, and seamless coordination.

The Project Management Support Specialist coordinates and supports the effective planning, implementation and monitoring of projects, ensuring delivery of results within the agreed scope, time, cost, quality and risk parameters. The role supports day-to-day project operations, liaises with partners, donors and beneficiaries, and ensures that project activities are in line with UNOPS policies, donor/partner requirements, and quality standards. The Project Management Support Specialist provides analytical and operational support, tracks financial and performance data, identifies risks or implementation challenges, and coordinates timely solutions in collaboration with stakeholders. The role therefore contributes towards ensuring that projects achieve their intended objectives, strengthen partner relationships, and contribute to UNOPS’ operational goals.

## **Functions / Key Results Expected**

**1. Project Delivery and Performance**

- Support in the planning, implementation and monitoring of project activities in line with approved work plans, budgets and quality standard.
- Coordinate day-to-day project operations to ensure timely delivery of outputs and adherence to UNOPS and donor/partner requirements.
- Manage and monitor progress against scope, time, cost and quality tolerances; Identify risks and deviations, propose corrective actions, and escalate when required.
- Oversee project contracts and supplier performance to ensure compliance and value for money.
- Embed sustainability principles - including gender equality, social inclusion and environmental considerations - across project activities.
- Contribute to the identification and development of new project opportunities or extensions of existing engagements.

**2. Financial and Procurement Management**

- Support financial planning, monitoring and reporting to ensure effective budget utilization and cost control in line with UNOPS Financial Rules and Regulations.
- Manage cash flow, expenditures and financial commitments, ensuring timely disbursements and accurate financial reporting.
- Support procurement and grant management processes, including preparation of Terms of Reference (ToRs), evaluation of bids, and contract administration.
- Coordinate with finance and procurement teams to ensure compliance, transparency, and proper documentation of transactions.
- Prepare and review financial reports and participate in project audits, ensuring implementation of recommendations.

**3. Stakeholder Engagement and Coordination**

- Maintain effective working relationships with donors, partners, national authorities and other stakeholders to ensure coordinated delivery and alignment with project objectives.
- Support the development and implementation of stakeholder engagement and communication plans, ensuring timely and consistent information sharing.
- Facilitate internal coordination among project teams, technical experts and support functions.
- Represent the project in meetings, consultations and external engagements as delegated by the supervisor.

**4. Monitoring, Reporting and Quality Assurance**

- Monitor project performance against agreed indicators, preparing progress, financial and completion reports in accordance with UNOPS and donor/partner standards.
- Conduct data analysis and provide inputs for management decisions and strategic planning.
- Ensure quality assurance processes are applied to all deliverables, documents and outputs.
- Support compliance with internal audit and quality standards, coordinating corrective action as required.

**5. Personnel Management (as applicable)**

- Assist in supervising, guiding and motivating project team members to achieve high performance and accountability.
- Contribute to recruitment, onboarding and performance management of personnel, ensuring gender balance and diversity principles are upheld.
- Promote a respectful, inclusive and safe working environment that aligns with UNOPS’ zero-tolerance policy for misconduct, discrimination and harassment.
- Ensure compliance with United Nations Department of Safety and Security (UNDSS) safety and security standards for all project staff and operations.

**6. Knowledge Building and Sharing**

- Support the organization, facilitation and delivery of training and learning sessions on project management.
- Participate in knowledge-sharing initiatives and Communities of Practice (CoPs), contributing insights and lessons learned.
- Conduct research on project management-related topics and contribute to the drafting of reports, summaries and briefing notes.

## **Education Requirements**

Required:

Advanced University Degree (Master's or equivalent) in Business Administration & Finance, International Relations, Political Sciences, Supply Chain Management & Logistics (5) years of relevant experience is required; OR

A first level university degree (Bachelor’s or equivalent) in any discipline with (7) years of relevant experience, may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Desired:

A globally recognized professional certificate or membership in Project Management is desired.

## **Experience Requirements**

Required:

- Relevant experience is defined as progressively responsible experience working in project management or related areas.
- Demonstrable proficiency in the use of collaboration and productivity tools (e.g. MS Office, G-Suite, etc) and web-based management systems is required.

Desired:

- Experience of working in multicultural environments or UN system organizations in a developing country is desired.
- Experience in development or humanitarian contexts is desired.

##   
Fluency in English and French are required.

jobs.title: Emergency Response Team Supply Chain Coordinator
jobs.body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

***Fluency in both written & Spoken French & English required***

**Role Bakground:**

Responding to the world’s worst humanitarian crises in a great variety of roles, the International Rescue Committee’s staff is a force for humanity and hope. If you are skilled and passionate, we would like to add your energy to ours. Through its Emergency Unit (EmU), the IRC is one of the world’s largest humanitarian agencies leading rapid emergency responses that provide life-saving assistance, early recovery, and stabilization support to people affected by conflict, displacement, natural disasters, and complex emergencies across multiple contexts worldwide. We are committed to innovation, agility, and strong partnerships to deliver timely and effective humanitarian action.

Active in public health, education in emergencies, livelihoods, women's empowerment, youth development, and protection and promotion of rights, we assist people from harm to home. The IRC recognizes that people affected by crisis and the actors closest to them are best placed, have the right, and should have the power and resources to respond and drive lasting change. We commit to increasing the share of funding channeled to local actors in emergencies, asking “Why not partner?’ whenever we plan programming, and partner as equals.

None of this work would reach clients without a supply chain that can keep pace with a crisis. The IRC's Global Supply Chain (GSC) team makes that possible, providing supply chain support to every IRC office worldwide. GSC specialists design and deliver supply chain activities that keep programs moving, in line with internal policy and donor requirements, so that life-saving assistance reaches people affected by conflict, displacement, and disaster without delay.

**Fluency in both written & spoken French Required.**

**Scope of work**

The Emergency Response Team is a specialized group within the Emergency Unit, and members are deployed to either support existing country programs in their emergency response or to initiate a new program in the crisis zone. The overall responsibility of the team is to rapidly and effectively design, develop and manage the IRC’s on-site humanitarian response to meet the immediate needs of the affected population. The ERT is also responsible for supporting the transfer of responsibilities and knowledge to the long-term staff to ensure the continuity of IRC programming and operations. All IRC ERT staff are expected to be deployed in the field, either in an emergency or roving capacity, for up to 65% of the time and must be able to deploy to the site of an emergency within 72 hours of notification.

The IRC ERT Supply Chain Coordinator provides leadership and direction to ensure an effective, high-quality, and timely emergency supply chain response, coordinating across components such as procurement, warehousing and inventory, fleet and logistics, and medical/pharmaceutical supply chains in emergency and outbreak responses, and is a member of both the IRC's Global Supply Chain and the Emergency Unit. The ERT SC Coordinator reports to the Director, Emergency and Health Supply Chain on an ongoing basis and during periods of non-deployment. During emergency deployments, ERT staff work under the direction of IRC's Emergency Response Director or the designated country/regional emergency lead, with technical backstopping provided by the Director, Emergency and Health Supply Chain in the Emergency Unit.

**Major Responsibilities**

**Leadership**

- Provide technical oversight of all Supply Chain functions for emergency response.
- Ensure that processes follow IRC GSC standard operating procedures in all aspects as followed.
- Contribute to field leadership, EmU SAP IP and GSCs strategic workplans,
- Be a voice for the supply chain team within the unit.
- Where applicable s/he will be sent to existing programs to gap fill or provide extra capacity to in country teams
- Be a Subject matter expert (SME) in IRCs ERP, Integra, training and mentoring supply chain and program staff

**Planning**

- Proactively participate in Project Cycle Meetings, including project design, project planning, project opening, project review, project close-out and project learning meetings to ensure that supply chain related issues are well articulated to all stakeholders and resolved for successful project delivery.
- Prepare and maintain emergency procurement plans and develop/maintain country program sourcing strategy for all active and pipeline grants in collaboration with program Technical Coordinators and Managers,
- Ensure that supply chain department is well staffed and roles and responsibilities of each have clear job description.

**Procurement**

Ensure:

- Compliance to IRC and donor policies for all goods and services procurement (including pharmaceuticals and medical equipment)
- In collaboration with the in-country GSC team(s) review and utilize the Procurement contracts (MPA, MSA) in place for the purchases of goods and services.
- The implementation of GSC procurement and contracting SOPs.
- The accuracy of GSC data collected; timely submission of required report(s) to advise the decision-making process.
- Disseminate through trainings the existing procurement process as well the procurement tools to all EmU GSC team members.
- Ensuring all required procurement documents are included in waivers request files (Purchase Requests, Market Surveys Proforma (3), ATC etc.)
- Management of all waivers with details of the emergency procurement circumstances, including the country program leadership approval (CD, DDO) before its approval by either the RSCD or the CGSCO.
- The suppliers’ files prepared by the procurement team are historically documenting the supplier(s) performance feedback provided by the EmU services requesters after the goods/services deliveries.
- The existence of segregations of duties in the procurement functions during the emergency deployment.
- The program requirements for supplies of items and services are timely met.
- The Grant (s) procurement and distribution plans are developed, regularly reviewed and all related issues are timely resolved or raised in collaboration with leadership.
- The end-to-end procurement processes are conducted through IRCs ERP System, Integra
- Any IRC procurement process deviations are identified, documented, and timely reported following the approved mechanism.
- Follow the Pharmaceutical Quality Assurance Policy in procurement and delivery of medical commodities.

**Inventory, Warehousing, Assets and Property**

- The implementation of the IRC inventory policies during the emergency support for all Project Items (cycle count, reporting discrepancies, pharmaceutical quality assurance as well as cold chain policies where applicable).
- The grant inventory report is accurate, regularly produced, reviewed, and approved before the Grant closing date.
- The warehousing safety and security requirements are in place.
- The assets maintenance plans are in place as per IRC policies.

**Fleet and Logistics**

- The vehicle safety policies are in place, disseminated and followed by all vehicles users.
- Effective fuel consumption management tools are developed and in use.
- The fleet legal status (registration, licenses, insurance) are updated;
- The vehicle monthly reports are regularly issued, reviewed and used to inform the leadership strategic decision-making process.
- The vehicle movement planning and tracking tool(s) are in place;
- The driver management policy is developed and followed.

**Learning and Development**

- Every new starter in the SC team receives 90-day objectives
- Accurate staff development plans are developed based on the documented training needs assessment process, discussed with the unit leadership, approved and implemented.
- Each team members' objectives are set following the organizational unit visions as well as operations context(s);
- Ensure all SC staff are trained to standard and sign the IRC code of conduct, conflict of interest following the SOPs recommendations.
- Ensure all counterparts who deal with supply chain processes are trained to standard.

**Compliance and Ethics**

- Identifies and sets mitigation plan to handle Supply Chain risks, including identification of red flags, and implementing internal and external audit corrective action plans to ensure all supply chain activities are conducted in an ethical manner.
- Ensures compliance to IRC and donor policies in the procurement and distribution of program supplies and assets.
- Ensure that assessments of supply chain policies, procedures, controls, and performance is conducted and any deviations addressed in the country program where designated
- Take lead in donor and IRC Internal Audit process of the SC department, develop and support implementation of post-audit corrective action plans and other improvement plans

**Emergency Preparedness**

- Work with the Emergency Unit and high risks country programs to implement emergency preparedness through in country training, mentoring and remote technical support.
- Participate in, and contribute to content for Emergency Unit trainings and conferences

**Partnerships:**

- Champion a culture of effective and respectful partnerships. Promote partner-led programming in line with IRC’s “why not partner?” and “partner as equals” approach
- Actively contribute to the relevant sections of Partner Capacity Analysis (PCA) and the subsequent development of partner support plans
- Be deliberate and intentional in determining whether a partner was capable of key supply chain activities in emergencies or whether IRC needed to take the lead
- Manage the implementation of action items in the Supply Chain sections of partner support plans
- Work collaboratively with partners to ensure that project budgets reflect fair market value
- Ensure appropriate budget allocation for IRC to support partners in alignment with the overall response/program design
- Actively participate in the Partnership Working Group (PWG) if applicable

**Key working relationships**

**Position Reports to:** Director, Emergency Supply & Health Supply Chain (while not deployed),

**Position directly supervises**: On deployment only

**Works closely with:** Other ERT and GSC staff, country program supply chain and management team.

**Indirect Reporting:** Emergency Team Leader/Country Director (while deployed)

**Requirements**

- Advanced Degree, 3-6 years or more of progressive Supply Chain professional experience or equivalent education and experience
- Proven experience developing and managing supply chain/logistics functions in an INGO, including in emergency/conflict areas
- Demonstrated success as a Supply Chain leader across all disciplines including planning, procurement and logistics.
- Demonstrable knowledge and experience in medical logistics and the procurement, storage, transport and distribution of pharmaceuticals
- Broad knowledge and experience in Supply Chain strategies, market analysis techniques, procurement and contracting, vehicle and fleet management, inventory, property and asset management
- Demonstrated skills in building strong teams and establishing new operations, including strong ability to communicate and work effectively with senior management, operating and program staff and functions
- Proven leadership of multi-disciplinary, cross-cultural teams, with strong mentoring, coaching, motivational, and team-building skills
- Demonstrated commitment to inclusion and fair treatment of staff, and ability to identify and address barriers to inclusion for marginalized groups in emergency response
- Strong collaborator and influencer with effective interpersonal and analytical skills who is able to work seamlessly across countries, cultures, and organizational units
- Proven experience in remote management
- Strong financial management and budgeting skills
- Strong computer, radio and communication equipment skills, and licensed and able to drive manual transmission, 4WD vehicles
- Resilient, organized, hard-working, with positive attitude
- Bilingual English and French mandatory; Arabic and Spanish advantageous

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

  
**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer.
