jobs.title: Caseworker Assistant
jobs.body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

***This position has an end date of 30 September 2027.***

**Job Overview:**

The Program for Initial Resettlement Caseworker Assistant supports refugee and other ORR-eligible populations during their integration into the United States by assisting with service delivery, client support, documentation, transportation, and resource coordination. Working under the guidance of the Cash and Medical and Initial Resettlement Coordinator, the Caseworker Assistant helps ensure clients have access to essential services and resources while promoting self-sufficiency, stability, and successful community integration.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Assist in coordinating pre-arrival and post-arrival services to ensure clients receive essential support upon arrival.
- Support airport pickups, housing setup, food assistance, transportation arrangements, and community orientation activities.
- Assist clients with navigating community resources and accessing essential services.
- Conduct client intake and assessment activities to help identify household strengths, needs, and priorities.
- Develop individualized self-sufficiency plans and SMART goals in partnership with each client.
- Provide referrals and follow up on service connections, appointments, and action items.
- Support the distribution of direct assistance and program-related resources according to organizational and funder requirements.
- Maintain regular communication with assigned clients to support progress toward established goals.
- Document client interactions, services provided, referrals, and outcomes accurately and timely.
- Enter and maintain client records in ETO and other required databases.
- Collaborate effectively with coworkers and partner organizations.
- Use personal, insured vehicle and/or public transportation (where available) to travel and transport clients and materials as needed throughout the service delivery area.
- Other duties as assigned.

**Job Requirements:**

**Education:** Associate degree in Social Work, Human Services, or a related field preferred.

**Work Experience:**

- At least 2 years’ experience working with refugee and/or immigrant populations strongly preferred.
- Experience providing customer service, case management support, or community outreach preferred.

**Demonstrated Skills & Competencies:**

- Ability to learn to navigate or familiarity with database systems such as IRIS and Efforts to Outcomes (ETO)
- Strong relationship building, diplomacy, and networking skills; ability to effectively build internal and external relationships.
- Demonstrated success working and communicating effectively in a multi-cultural environment.
- Self-starter with excellent problem-solving skills combined with the proven ability to multi-task, prioritize duties, and manage time effectively.
- Attention to detail and accuracy in work product.
- Fluency in English, both spoken and written; proficiency in language(s) spoken by IRC’s clients is desired;
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook); ability to use the internet and other digital tools for data entry, research and problem-solving purposes.
- Valid driver’s license and access to a personal, insured vehicle.

**Working Environment:**

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities.
- Will require occasional weekend and/or evening work.

**Compensation:** ($18.45). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

jobs.body:
## **Fixed term contract: 12 months from 01/01/2027**

## **PUI all around the world**

**With its 40 years of experience, Première Urgence Internationale :**

- Supports close to **6** millions beneficiaries
- With more than **100** millions € yearly budget
- Present in **22** countries, on **5** continents

Thanks to the work and commitment of :

- More than **2000** national staffs
- Around **200** expatriates from 45 different nationalities
- And **90** employees at HQ

PUI works in 10 areas of intervention and distinguishes itself by the implementation of an integrated approach in its response. This method aims to identify and understand the needs of all those affected by a crisis. Our teams come together to bring a rapid global response to the basic needs of populations affected by humanitarian crises to help them regain independence and dignity.

Learn more on [our history](https://www.premiere-urgence.org/qui-sommes-nous/notre-histoire/), [our values](https://www.premiere-urgence.org/qui-sommes-nous/notre-valeurs/), [our areas of intervention.](https://www.premiere-urgence.org/qui-sommes-nous/nos-domaines-d-intervention/)

## **What about the Country Director?**

As Country Director, you will be responsible for the smooth functioning and the development of the mission. For this purpose, you will be responsible for:

- **Safety & Security**: You will be responsible for the safety & security of the mission.
- **Programmes**: You will coordinate the teams and ensure that the programmes implemented on the mission are properly carried out. You will also monitor needs and suggest new operations and development tracks for the mission.
- **Human Resources**: You will ensure that the mission is adequately staffed and supervise the teams (defining objectives, follow-up).
- **Logistical, administrative and financial monitoring**: You will ensure that logistical and administrative practices in place respect PUI procedures and formats and are in compliance with donors’ rules and regulations.
- **Medical and technical monitoring**: You will ensure that medical and technical practices respect PUI’s procedures and formats and are in compliance with PUI’s operational framework and policy.
- **Representation**: You will represent the association in its relations with partners, donors, the media and different authorities.
- **Relations with Headquarters**: You will ensure that information is properly circulated between Headquarters and the field and ensure that due dates are respected.

## **The challenges that await you**

- **Unprecedented crisis in Gaza**: Responding to extraordinary humanitarian needs while maintaining operational continuity, staff safety, programme quality, and accountability in an extremely volatile environment.
- **Deteriorating situation in the West Bank**: Adapting programmes and operations to increasing insecurity, movement restrictions, displacement pressures, and rapidly changing access conditions.
- **Legal, registration and access constraints**: Navigating a complex and evolving regulatory environment while securing the operational access required to deliver programmes effectively.

## **What you will need to succeed**

**Training**: You hold a Master’s degree or equivalent in Humanitarian action: project management, a technical background related to one of our activity sectors, in human resources management, financial management…

**Experience**: Strengthened by minimum 3 years of experience in the field with international NGOs in project coordination, you master international team management, the project cycle and security management. Previous experience as Country Director or in an equivalent position would be appreciated. You already worked with Première Urgence Internationale? It would be a definite asset!

**Skills**: You master humanitarian project management and team management; you have a detailed knowledge of donors’ prerequisites. You also have excellent writing skills.

**Qualities**: You are a good communicator, both in writing and orally. You demonstrate good team spirit, leadership skills and the ability to make decisions, trustworthiness and a sense of responsibility, organizational skills, reactivity, ability to be thorough and to adapt. You have a strong resistance to stress and particularly in unstable circumstances.

**Languages**: English has no secrets for you! All the better, it is mandatory for this position. If you speak Arabic and/or French, it would be a definite asset.

## **A word from the manager**

*« Join PUI as Country Director in Palestine and help drive humanitarian action in one of today’s most challenging environments. Working across Palestine and Jordan, you will bring adaptability, resilience and commitment to lead through complexity, navigate uncertainty and make a lasting difference. »*

## **PUI will offer you**

- **Status:** Cadre with a Fixed-Term Contract
- **Monthly Gross Income:** 3 330,00 – 3 730,00 EUR depending on your experience in International Solidarity + 50€ per semester of seniority with PUI
- **Insurance** including medical coverage and complementary healthcare, 24/24 assistance and repatriation
- **Daily Living Expenses** (« Per Diem »)
- **Break Policy:** 5 working days at 3 and 9 months + break allowance
- **Paid Leaves Policy:** 5 weeks of paid leaves per year + return ticket every 6 months

## **Our commitments**

PUI is committed to preventing all forms of inappropriate behavior in the workplace, including harassment, sexual exploitation and abuse, lack of integrity, and financial misconduct, while promoting the well-being of children and adults with whom PUI interacts.  
PUI expects all employees to fulfill their professional duties and responsibilities in accordance with PUI’s Ethical Framework. All employees will receive appropriate training and commit to promoting, disseminating, and upholding the principles set forth in its Ethical Charter.  
The holder of this position may potentially have access to personal data concerning children and vulnerable adults as part of their work (Category 2 in the safe recruitment risk classification). Consequently, all recruitments will be subject to satisfactory references and appropriate background checks, which include criminal record and counter-terrorism financing checks.  
Première Urgence Internationale considers the diversity of nationalities, genders, beliefs, backgrounds, and statuses within its Human Resources as a major asset for its humanitarian work. The organization is therefore committed to strictly upholding the principle of non-discrimination throughout its recruitment process.  
We are dedicated to ensuring diversity and gender equality within our organization and strongly encourage candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply.  
Please note that Première Urgence Internationale shall not in any case request a financial contribution for administrative costs related to recruitment. Any such information would be fraudulent, please disregard it.  
**Early applications are encouraged, as we may close the process earlier than the deadline mentioned above if a suitable candidate is identified.**

You recognize yourself in this profile and you adhere to our commitments ? You feel ready to take up the **challenge and** to join **PUI great family ?**

jobs.title: Senior Case Management Officer
source: International Network For Aid Relief and Assistance
jobs.body:
**GENERAL INFORMATION**

Job Title : Senior Case Management Officer

Location : Ankara, Türkiye (On-site)

Job Type : Full-time

Contract Duration : The contract is for an initial period of **one (1) year**, with the possibility of extension depending on the availability of funding and the continued need for the role.

**ABOUT INARA:**

International Network for Aid, Relief and Assistance (INARA) is a U.S.-registered 501(c)(3) humanitarian organization founded in 2015 by Arwa Damon. Established in response to critical gaps in the humanitarian system, INARA works to support children affected by conflict, displacement, and natural and human-induced disasters who are often unable to access sustained medical and psychosocial care.

INARA delivers integrated, child-centered programming that combines life-saving interventions with long-term recovery support. The organization focuses on children facing complex and overlapping vulnerabilities, including injury, trauma, disability, and exclusion from essential services. Through a multidisciplinary approach, INARA provides access to medical treatment, mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), and coordinated case management, ensuring continuity of care beyond the immediate emergency phase.

INARA delivers integrated, child-centered programming across multiple sectors to support children affected by crisis. Its interventions include comprehensive medical and rehabilitative care, providing specialized treatment and long-term follow-up; mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), offering trauma-informed and community-based services; and livelihood and economic empowerment initiatives that strengthen household stability. INARA also supports education in emergencies by creating safe and inclusive learning environments, implements water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) interventions to improve health conditions, and maintains a rapid emergency response capacity to deliver immediate medical, psychosocial, food, and non-food assistance during acute crises.

**Vision**

A world where every child has the agency to create a dignified life.

**Mission**

Fostering a future where we empower children to shape their own dignified lives.

**Purpose**

Enhancing children’s capacity to shape their own fulfilling futures through integrated health, empowerment, and community-driven interventions.

**JOB SUMMARY:**

The Senior Case Management Officer is responsible for supervising and supporting INARA’s case management and MHPSS staff in Türkiye while directly managing and following up medical cases in Ankara. The position ensures that children and their families receive coordinated, timely, safe, and high-quality support throughout assessment, treatment, recovery, and case closure. The role provides day-to-day supervision to Case Management Officers and MHPSS Officers, reviews case documentation and service quality, coordinates closely with hospitals and service providers, and maintains an active caseload in Ankara. The position also verifies hospital and treatment-related expenses against services received, reconciles case expenditures and cash advances with Finance, prepares donor-required case and program reports, and works with Partnerships/Program Management and Communications to ensure reporting, case stories, and communication materials are accurate, timely, and appropriately documented.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Case Management, Medical Follow-up & Care Coordination**

- Manage an active caseload of children receiving medical support in Ankara, ensuring continuous follow-up from intake and assessment through treatment, rehabilitation, recovery, referral, and case closure.
- Conduct and/or review comprehensive assessments of children’s medical, psychosocial, protection, social, and practical needs and develop individualized care plans in coordination with children, caregivers, medical providers, and relevant INARA staff.
- Coordinate appointments, diagnostics, procedures, hospitalization, rehabilitation, medication, referrals, transportation, and other treatment-related needs, and follow up with hospitals and service providers to ensure continuity and quality of care.
- Maintain regular contact with children and caregivers, provide practical guidance and support, explain treatment pathways and next steps, and ensure that changes in needs or treatment plans are communicated promptly.
- Advocate for children and families with hospitals, healthcare providers, social services, and other relevant actors to address barriers to care and secure appropriate services.
- Ensure timely identification and escalation of safeguarding, protection, medical, or psychosocial concerns in accordance with INARA policies and referral pathways.
- Ensure medical and MHPSS services are coordinated as part of an integrated, child-centered case management approach.

**Team Supervision, Technical Oversight & Quality Assurance**

- Provide direct day-to-day supervision to Case Management Officers and MHPSS Officers, ensuring clear work planning, appropriate caseload allocation, service coverage, and accountability.
- Conduct regular team meetings, individual supervision, case review sessions, and multidisciplinary discussions to monitor progress, address complex cases, and support sound case management decisions.
- Review case files, assessments, care plans, follow-up notes, referrals, service records, and closure documentation to ensure completeness, accuracy, confidentiality, and compliance with INARA standards.
- Monitor staff caseloads, case progress, service timelines, and follow-up actions, and intervene where delays, gaps, risks, or quality concerns are identified.
- Provide coaching, technical guidance, and practical support to staff; identify capacity-building needs and support learning and consistent application of case management and MHPSS procedures.
- Promote a supportive, respectful, and accountable team environment and ensure adherence to safeguarding, confidentiality, data protection, professional boundaries, and organizational policies.
- Coordinate with relevant managers on staff performance, workload, operational challenges, and corrective actions where required.

**Hospital & Service Provider Coordination**

- Establish and maintain effective working relationships with hospitals, doctors, rehabilitation providers, pharmacies, laboratories, and other service providers supporting INARA children.
- Confirm treatment plans, services delivered, follow-up requirements, and relevant medical documentation with providers, while maintaining appropriate confidentiality and informed consent.
- Review hospital invoices, treatment bills, and related medical expenses against the treatment and services actually received by each child, flagging discrepancies or unclear charges for clarification before processing.
- Support resolution of service delivery issues, appointment delays, documentation gaps, or billing discrepancies in coordination with hospitals, Finance, and relevant INARA colleagues.

**Case-related Financial Reconciliation & Cash Advances**

- Work closely with Finance on a regular basis to reconcile medical and case-related expenditures with approved treatment plans, supporting documents, and services received.
- Maintain clear records of treatment-related expenses and provide the programmatic and case documentation required to validate hospital, pharmacy, transportation, accommodation, and other approved day-to-day medical costs.
- Manage and clear cash advances received for children’s treatment and day-to-day medical expenses in a timely manner, ensuring that receipts and supporting documentation are complete and submitted in accordance with INARA procedures.
- Follow up on outstanding advances, missing documentation, discrepancies, or corrections with Finance and relevant staff until fully reconciled and cleared.
- This role verifies and reconciles case-related costs but is not responsible for program budgeting, financial management, or budget ownership.

**Monitoring, Documentation & Donor Reporting**

- Maintain accurate, complete, and up-to-date beneficiary records, medical follow-up information, service documentation, consent records, and case progress notes in accordance with INARA’s data protection and confidentiality requirements.
- Track case progress, treatment status, outputs, outcomes, pending actions, and relevant indicators and ensure reliable information is available for internal monitoring and donor reporting.
- Prepare monthly and quarterly reports on children and case management activities using existing donor templates, ensuring that information is accurate, evidence-based, complete, and submitted on time.
- Share completed reporting inputs and supporting information with the Partnerships and Program Management Department for review, consolidation, and donor submission.
- Maintain and follow a clear calendar of donor reporting deadlines and required case-related deliverables, including narrative inputs, beneficiary information, case updates, and communication materials.
- Provide timely clarifications, case data, and supporting documentation requested by Partnerships/Program Management for donor reports, reviews, monitoring visits, or audits.

**Communications, Case Stories & Visibility**

- Work closely with the Communications Department to identify appropriate treatment journeys, case stories, milestones, and impact examples that can be documented in line with consent, safeguarding, confidentiality, and dignity standards.
    - Coordinate access to accurate case information and appropriate follow-up with children and caregivers so that treatment progress and case stories are captured responsibly and without disrupting care.
    - Review case-related facts in communication materials for accuracy and ensure that medical and treatment information reflects the services actually received.
    - Track and follow up on donor deadlines for required communication, visibility, case-story, photo, video, or other program materials, coordinating with Communications and Partnerships/Program Management to ensure timely completion.

**Cross-Departmental Coordination**

- Work closely with Program Management, Partnerships, Finance, Communications, Administration, and Operations to ensure coordinated support to children and timely completion of case-related actions.
- Participate in relevant internal meetings and provide concise updates on case progress, team workload, treatment challenges, reporting requirements, and issues requiring management attention.
- Support coordination with external service providers and relevant actors where this directly contributes to referral pathways, continuity of care, or improved services for children.

**REQUIREMENTS & QUALIFICATIONS**

**Qualification**

- Bachelor’s degree in Social Work, Psychology, Nursing, Public Health, or another relevant field; a Master’s degree is an asset.
- Strong understanding of child-centered case management, care coordination, safeguarding, confidentiality, and data protection.
- Strong organizational, interpersonal, communication, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and sensitive cases.
- Fluency in Turkish and strong working proficiency in English are required; Arabic is a strong asset.
- Ability to work on-site in Ankara and to travel locally to hospitals and service providers as required.

**Experience**

- Minimum 5 years of relevant experience in case management, medical care coordination, protection, MHPSS, or humanitarian programming, preferably with an international NGO.
- Demonstrated experience supervising case management, MHPSS, social work, or multidisciplinary teams.
- Proven experience coordinating medical cases with hospitals and healthcare providers and following treatment pathways and patient needs.
- Experience reviewing case documentation and treatment-related supporting documents and coordinating expense reconciliation with Finance.
- Experience preparing accurate narrative or beneficiary-level reports using donor or organizational templates and working to fixed reporting deadlines.
- Experience working with children and families affected by conflict, displacement, disaster, or other vulnerabilities is strongly preferred.

**CONFIDENTIALITY AND SAFEGUARDING**

**Confidentiality**

As the position is involved in sensitive topics, he/she must observe absolute discretion within and outside the organization. Non-respect of this clause or any breach of responsibility may result in a written warning or immediate dismissal.

**Safeguarding**

INARA has zero tolerance for abuse, exploitation, or harm to children and vulnerable adults. INARA employees must adhere strictly to safeguarding policies, maintain professional boundaries, and report concerns immediately.

jobs.title: Fertilizer Procurement Strategy Associate
jobs.body:
## **About One Acre Fund**

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

## **About the Role**

Seeking a procurement professional to lead fertilizer procurement, ensuring cost-efficient sourcing and reliable on-time delivery. Drive strong individual execution and contribute to team success. In this role, your focus will be dedicated to deep-dive data analysis to determine optimal purchasing windows, and managing and executing the entire procurement process independently.

## **Responsibilities**

Execute Procurement with Excellence

- Strategy & Delivery: Support the creation and execution of seasonal procurement strategies to deliver +90% OTIF (On-Time, In-Full) delivery, market-competitive costs, and 5% year-on-year cost savings.
- Quality Assurance: Ensure absolute quality control, achieving 0 quality issues reaching the farmer, and maintain an +80% on-time payment rate for suppliers.
- Supply Chain Reliability: Proactively address future supply gaps by evaluating farmer needs against global market trends, supplier capacity, and current inventory levels.
- Process Optimization: Drive lead-time improvements through streamlined delivery and process automation. Regularly improve key operations like the goods receipt process and loading quality control.
- Data & Analytics: Spend time developing, maintaining, and continuously improving complex Google Sheets data models to track global market trends and landed costs. Use this data to provide crucial decision support on when to purchase (or not purchase) fertilizers to maximize cost savings.

Build Partnerships & Market Liaisons

- Strategic Relationships: Help build and maintain deep partnerships with fertilizer suppliers and industry organizations beyond seasonal procurement needs.
- Country Team Collaboration: Act as a critical business partner for our country operations teams, actively identifying and sharing opportunities to improve our offering to farmers.
- Industry Representation: Serve as a representative for One Acre Fund externally with suppliers and market actors to drive long-term, systematic supply chain improvements.

People Management

- People Management: Manage and mentor a small team, setting clear goals, providing timely feedback, and conducting high-quality career coaching and performance reviews.
- Team Growth:Contribute to staffing, recruitment, and succession planning to build a high-performing procurement unit.

## **Career Growth and Development**

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## **Qualifications**

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

Professional & Technical Competencies:

- Supply Chain Expertise: Solid foundational knowledge of global procurement processes, international shipping, and supply chain operations.
- Data Fluency: An advanced analytical mindset with high proficiency in Google Sheets to build pricing, forecasting, and decision-support models. Comfortable spending half of your time analyzing data to help make decisions.
- Language: Fluency in written and spoken English is required.

Management & Execution Skills:

- Relationship Builder: Exceptional collaboration and negotiation skills, with the ability to influence both internal stakeholders and external global suppliers.
- Project Management: Strong organizational skills with a proven track record of managing multiple projects simultaneously in a fast-paced environment.
- Solution-Oriented: An innovative thinker who approaches obstacles with a results-driven mindset and is comfortable making data-driven decisions under medium-risk conditions.

## **Preferred Start Date**

As soon as possible

## **Job Location**

Nairobi, Kenya

## **Benefits**

Health insurance, housing, and comprehensive benefits

## **Eligibility**

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Kenya.

## **Application Deadline**

16 October 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

*One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @*[*oneacrefund.org*](http://oneacrefund.org/) *address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), **but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.***

*Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.*

*We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.*

jobs.title: Zambia Field Operations & Performance Specialist (Fixed-Term)
jobs.body:
## **About One Acre Fund**

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

In Zambia, from our hub in Kabwe, we run a specialised climate-smart input and agroforestry program to address challenges such as irregular rainfall and soil degradation. By partnering with local Tree Nursery Operators, we raise and distribute agroforestry trees that enrich soils and build long-term financial resilience. Supported by a structured frontline field team across Central and Southern Provinces, we use rigorous, data-driven frameworks to measure our impact and ensure we drive meaningful improvements in farmer yields, asset accumulation, and food security.

## **About the Role**

We are looking for an experienced, analytical, and resilient Field Operations Specialist to lead and expand our rural field operations. You will act as the key link between field leadership and headquarters, improving performance mainly through the Field Director (FD) layer while working closely with Field Officers (FOs) and Group Leaders.  
  
The ideal candidate can turn complex field data into clear, targeted operational strategies, manage teams effectively under tight deadlines, and design community leadership frameworks that can grow with the programme. You will also lead with strong emotional intelligence, especially in demanding and remote environments.

## **Responsibilities**

Field Performance Management & FD Leadership

- Lead field performance through field directors, ensuring teams deliver against key programme targets, including farmer adoption, tree survival and growth, repayment, and customer service
- Use field performance data to identify gaps, diagnose root causes and drive timely corrective action.
- Regularly engage with field teams and visit sites to validate performance, coach teams and address operational challenges.

Field HR Coordination & Risk Oversight

- Oversee key field staff processes, including onboarding, staff movements, performance management, disciplinary processes and payroll coordination.
- Provide leadership during urgent field staff and operational issues, including staff exits, fraud cases and other high risk incidents.
- Ensure field staff processes, incidents and risks are appropriately documented and managed in line with organisational policies.

Group Leader Management System

- Develop and continuously improve a strong, consistent Group Leader system across field sites.
- Establish clear approaches to Group Leader selection, onboarding, performance management, coaching and incentives.
- Strengthen accountability within groups and ensure underperforming Group Leaders and groups are appropriately supported or managed.

Training, Coaching & Staff Development

- Build the capabilities of Field Directors and field officers through structured training, coaching and mentorship.
- Strengthen communication and feedback between field teams and HQ, ensuring field realities inform programme decisions.
- Develop a strong talent pipeline and support the progression of high-performing field staff into future leadership roles.

Operational Prioritisation & Execution

- Lead the effective execution of multiple field priorities, balancing programme performance, people needs, operational risks and organisational deadlines.
- Ensure teams are focused on the highest-priority activities and that responsibilities are appropriately delegated while maintaining accountability for results.
- Identify opportunities to improve field systems, processes and ways of working as the programme grows.

## **Career Growth and Development**

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## **Qualifications**

- 3 to 5+ years leading and growing multi-layered field teams (extension agents) in agriculture, rural development, or social enterprise.
- Demonstrated ability to analyse quantitative operational metrics (adoption rates, loan repayment percentages, yield impact) and translate insights into immediate field action plans.
- Proven track record of operating effectively across expansive, remote geographical regions with limited network connectivity and challenging logistics.
- Experience building or improving systems, training materials, or community leadership models from scratch.
- Excellent communication, coaching, problem-solving, and interpersonal skills with a passion for team development.
- Deep commitment to serving smallholder farmers and living One Acre Fund’s values.
- Bachelor's degree in related fields.

jobs.title: Economic Recovery Technical Coordinator
jobs.body:
**Base:** Kyiv

**Starting date:** November 2026

**Contract duration:** 4 months' probation period with prolongation upon successful probation period end

**About PIN Ukraine:**

People in Need (PIN) has been active in Ukraine since early August 2014. Currently, PIN is one of the major humanitarian actors in Ukraine responding to the recent military escalation, providing humanitarian aid to conflict-affected people across Ukraine. Since 2014, PIN has implemented emergency food and cash assistance, NFI, shelter, protection, livelihoods and WASH interventions supporting 5 million vulnerable IDPs, returnees and host communities in urban and rural areas.

PIN is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of race, ethnicity, nationality, age, religion, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, or any other characteristic. PIN encourages applications from individuals of diverse backgrounds and values diversity.

**General information about the role of the person:**

Under the supervision of the Economic and Green Recovery Technical Lead, the Economic Recovery Technical Coordinator will provide technical and analytical support to the design, quality assurance, monitoring, and continuous improvement of PIN's economic recovery programs in Ukraine.

The position involves:

• supporting the development and adaptation of economic recovery methodologies, tools, and technical guidance;

• providing technical support to program teams without taking over the management of their implementation;

• supporting the development of proposals, concept notes, needs assessments, studies, and program frameworks;

• documenting lessons learned, best practices, and evidence generated within economic recovery programs;

• supporting capacity development of teams on relevant technical approaches and tools;

• participating in coordination and technical exchange with relevant internal and external stakeholders;

• supporting the Technical Lead in ensuring coherence and quality across the economic recovery program portfolio.

• conducting and supporting field-based technical work, including field visits, assessments, consultations, data collection, and technical follow-up, either jointly with or on behalf of the Technical Lead;

• engaging with external stakeholders and representing PIN’s interests in relevant technical discussions, meetings, consultations, and coordination forums, as needed

**Description of general duties:**

**1. Technical Quality and Methodology**

• Facilitate the development, analysis, and adaptation of technical approaches, methodologies, tools, standard operating procedures (SOPs), and recommendations for economic recovery programs. Maintain a clear record of methodological revisions, consolidate feedback from teams, and submit proposed changes to the Technical Lead for review before wider use.

• Analyze the technical quality, relevance, and consistency of programmatic approaches and provide recommendations for their improvement.

• Provide support to teams in adapting and aligning technical approaches across different projects and contexts.

**2. Technical Support to Program Implementation Teams**

• Participate in grant committees and conduct application assessments. Review applications and business plans against agreed eligibility and scoring criteria, assess technical feasibility and market assumptions, and document recommendations and clarification requests for committee consideration.

• Provide program teams with technical advice on the application of economic recovery methodologies and tools. Respond to technical questions during implementation, review practical examples with staff, and escalate unresolved methodological issues to the Technical Lead. Keep programme delivery decisions with the responsible implementation teams.

• Support teams in interpreting and applying technical guidance, targeting approaches and selection criteria, monitoring requirements, and program methodologies.

**3. Technical Monitoring and Quality Assurance**

• Conduct regular technical monitoring visits to program implementation regions and activity sites. Agree visit objectives with the Technical Lead and implementation teams; prepare checklists, review available project records, and consult participants, businesses, partners, and staff as relevant. Conduct visits jointly with or on behalf of the Technical Lead as agreed.

• Assess the technical quality of implementation against approved methodologies, SOPs, program frameworks, and relevant standards.

• Identify technical, methodological, and quality issues and prepare recommendations for corrective actions.

• Coordinate monitoring work with MEAL, Protection, Grants, Partnerships, and Programme Implementation as needed.

• Prepare technical monitoring reports, action lists, and recommendations for follow-up. Record findings, supporting evidence, recommended actions, responsible colleagues, and agreed timeframes. Follow up on technical improvements with the relevant teams and flag recurring or unresolved quality issues to the Technical Lead.

**4. Program Analysis, Evidence, and Learning**

• Support the development and interpretation of economic recovery indicators and monitoring tools. Work with MEAL on indicator definitions, data sources, collection methods, and interpretation of baseline, monitoring, and endline findings. Identify data gaps and limitations before drawing conclusions about results.

• Contribute to the analysis of program results, including economic impact and changes in livelihoods, income, employment, business performance indicators, and resilience, as relevant. Compare results across locations and participant groups where the data allow; examine barriers to economic recovery and explain the practical implications for programme adjustments.

• Support the identification of needs within the economic recovery sector.

**5. Program Development and Proposal Preparation**

• Support the Technical Lead and relevant program teams in developing new economic recovery concepts and project proposals.

• Participate in technical discussions during program design and implementation where specialized economic recovery expertise is required.

• Collect and analyze information needed for program design.

• Conduct stakeholder mapping in the economic recovery sector.

• Support the development of intervention logic, targeting approaches, selection criteria, technical methodologies, and monitoring systems. Prepare technical inputs on activities, expected outputs and outcomes, assumptions, risks, and resource needs. Check that proposed approaches are feasible, evidence-based, and consistent with the agreed programme framework.

• Support the development of new economic recovery initiatives in line with PIN's strategic priorities and identified needs.

**6. Needs Assessments, Research, and Analytical Work**

• Support needs assessments, market and sector analyses, and other economic recovery research to contribute to PIN’s evidence base on economic recovery in Ukraine. Help define research questions, assessment tools, stakeholder consultations, and field data collection plans. Analyse market demand, employment opportunities, business constraints, access to services, and recovery needs as relevant; validate findings with teams and stakeholders and prepare practical recommendations.

**Coordination with Programme Implementation and Livelihood Functions**

The Economic Recovery Technical Coordinator works closely with the Livelihood Coordinator and relevant Programme Implementation teams.

The Coordinator does not:

• manage the day-to-day implementation of program activities;

• replace the Livelihood Coordinator in coordination with operational departments;

• take on responsibility for logistics, procurement, finance, or administrative support to implementation;

• take on Programme Implementation's responsibility for delivering program activities;

• duplicate the operational reporting and control mechanisms of the Programme Implementation structure.

**Internal Coordination**

• Maintain regular coordination with Programme Implementation, MEAL, Grants, Partnerships, and other relevant departments. Agree technical priorities and follow-up actions, share findings that affect programme quality or reporting, and clarify responsibilities where technical and implementation functions intersect.

• Coordinate with technical colleagues in Protection, WASH, Shelter, and Education when economic recovery activities involve cross-sectoral approaches.

**External Technical Engagement**

Under the guidance of the Technical Lead:

• participate in relevant technical working groups, coordination meetings, workshops, and consultations;

• support technical communication with relevant CSOs, private sector representatives, service providers, research institutions, and other stakeholders;

• support stakeholder mapping and identification of relevant technical resources and partnerships;

• represent PIN at selected technical meetings as needed. Prepare agreed technical inputs and briefing points, document discussion outcomes, and share relevant opportunities and follow-up actions with the Technical Lead and programme teams.

**Functional Relationship with the Livelihood Coordinator**

The two positions are complementary:

**Livelihood Coordinator > Programme Implementation**

• oversight of implementation;

• coordination with operational departments;

• implementation planning and follow-up;

• resolution of operational issues;

• ensuring delivery of program activities.

**Economic Recovery Technical Coordinator > Programme Quality / Technical Function**

• technical quality;

• methodology and tools;

• technical monitoring;

• analysis and learning;

• technical capacity development;

• program improvement;

• technical input into program design.

**Development of the Role**

The position of Economic Recovery Technical Coordinator is being created to strengthen PIN Ukraine's technical capacity in the field of economic recovery.

As the economic recovery program portfolio expands, the position may gradually take on responsibility for specific technical areas or thematic components, including coordination of particular technical strands across multiple projects.

The role may also evolve toward greater responsibility for technical coordination, quality assurance, program development, and technical representation, depending on program needs and demonstrated performance.

**Team and Partner Capacity Development**

• Identify technical capacity needs of teams and partners and agree development activities with the Technical Lead.

• Deliver technical onboarding, refresher training, and mentoring on economic recovery methodologies and tools. Use practical exercises and programme examples, gather participant feedback, and provide follow-up support to help staff apply the tools consistently.

• When requested, support technical recruitment, preparation of terms of reference, and assessment of candidates’ technical skills; this does not imply line management.

• Provide technical guidance to PIN partners, support monitoring of their programme quality, and facilitate knowledge sharing.

**Documentation and Application of Learning**

• Document lessons learned, good practices, and research findings; prepare technical materials, recommendations, and internal updates.

• With MEAL, support review of baseline and endline tools and use evidence to improve programmes.

**Inclusion, Environmental Sustainability, and Accountability**

• Integrate age, gender, diversity, equality, non-discrimination, and do-no-harm principles into technical approaches and selection criteria.

• Under the Technical Lead’s guidance, support environmental sustainability and climate resilience in relevant economic recovery activities.

• Ensure accountability through appropriate communication and information sharing within PIN and with partners and communities.

• Comply with PIN policies and procedures, including Finance, Logistics, HR, and Security; report identified technical risks to the relevant responsible staff.

**Qualification Criteria:**

**Education and Speciality:**

Higher education in economics, development studies, business administration, agriculture, social sciences, or a related field.

**Required Skills and Competencies:**

- Strong analytical and methodological skills. Ability to conduct field visits, assessments, and technical monitoring. Skills in preparing technical recommendations, reports, tools, and training materials. Ability to advise teams without taking over implementation management functions. Strong communication and coordination skills. Fluency in Ukrainian and working proficiency in English.

**PIN OFFERS**:

- A competitive salary according to the People in Need salary scale in amount of **1882 EUR Gross (Based on qualifications) + 3% after probation period.**
- Opportunities for professional development through various capacity-building activities, including trainings, workshops, and seminars.
- 28 calendar days of annual leave, plus 3 additional New Year bonus leave days.
- Health insurance — becomes effective after completion of the first month of the probationary period.
- Life insurance — effective from the first day of employment, 24/7, providing additional financial protection for employees and their families.
- Possibility to work one day per week remotely for office-based staff.
- Coverage of accommodation and per diem costs for work-related travel outside the assigned office region and/or in cases of excessive travel distance or time, in accordance with People in Need travel policy.
- Provision of a laptop, mobile phone (including prepaid SIM cards), and People in Need branded items (backpack, thermal mug, notebook, portable power bank).
- People in Need offices are equipped with all necessary security and energy-resilience measures, ensuring uninterrupted internet access.
- Free coffee, tea, milk, and water available in all offices.
- A multicultural and friendly working environment, with approximately 400 staff members in the Ukraine programme.

**Application procedure:**

Please send clearly marked CV and Motivation letter in English. Please note, only the shortlisted candidates will be contacted. Written test and interviews will be conducted on a rolling basis and the vacancy will be closed when filled.

Please note that PIN does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process.

*We support the principles of inclusiveness and non-discrimination in the selection process. You can submit an anonymized resume - without specifying your name, age, gender, photo or other personal data. Such resumes will be reviewed on a general basis in accordance with professional experience and qualifications.*

jobs.title: Training Officer, Cultural Orientation
jobs.body:
**Job Overview:** The International Rescue Committee (IRC) is one of the leading providers of high-quality programming for refugees resettling to the United States. The IRC is committed to developing innovative programs that respond to the refugees’ unique strengths and needs, using our learning and experience to shape policy and practice, and highlighting and promoting best practices in refugee services provision.

The IRC is seeking a Training Officer, Cultural Orientation for Switchboard, an Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR)-funded program. Switchboard is a one-stop resource hub for refugee service providers in the United States. Switchboard provides training and capacity-building services to service providers in the United States, including resettlement agencies and affiliates, state agencies, ethnic community-based organizations, and others. More information about Switchboard can be found at [www.SwitchboardTA.org](https://reliefweb.int/file:///C:UsersTigestCoAppDataLocalMicrosoftOlkAttachmentsooa-fefcb179-4b91-4707-b044-59e9496f57fe69780562696ebcadf2340c5c93711aeb96e9493d8b84ea912d714b7dd9c61fdbwww.SwitchboardTA.org).

Settle In is Switchboard's digital information service for newcomers taking the knowledge and resources Switchboard offers to service providers and adapting and delivering it directly to newcomers**,** in multiple languages, through its website (SettleInUS.org), mobile app, and social media platforms. More information on Settle In can be found on https://www.settleinus.org/.

Cultural orientation is a core service in refugee resettlement in the United States, helping newcomers build the knowledge and skills to navigate life in their new communities. The Training Officer, Cultural Orientation, leads the development and delivery of capacity-building initiatives for these programs. This includes training and technical assistance (TTA) to service providers, helping them build strong cultural orientation programs and apply best practices when working with newcomers. This staff member is responsible for producing and maintaining high-quality performance by collaborating with experts, designing effective cultural orientation resources such as curricula, training materials, and learning tools, and facilitating learning experiences that improve outcomes for newcomer children, adults, and families. This role requires hands-on experience working directly with clients, subject matter experts, and partners, along with prior experience delivering cultural orientation to newcomers.

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Training and Technical Assistance**

- Design and deliver versatile cultural orientation training to service providers and cultural orientation delivery staff.
- Provide responsive and cross-disciplinary technical assistance to refugee service providers in response to cultural orientation TTAs, adapting content to meet varied organizational needs and learning styles.
- In collaboration with colleagues across teams, develop written and multimedia learning resources (e.g., toolkits, videos, podcasts) that reflect trauma-informed, client-centered, and strength-based approaches.
- Adapt materials for different literacy levels, languages, and cultural contexts
- Integrate feedback from internal and external reviewers to continuously improve training and resource contents and delivery methods.
- Facilitate communities of practice and peer learning groups to promote knowledge exchange and cross-training across service areas.

**Project Management**

- Contribute to the creation of Switchboard’s annual training and technical assistance (TTA) workplan.
- Ensure related trainings and learning resources are developed and delivered on time and on budget.
- Use effective communication and collaborative skills with a wide range of stakeholders
- Manage internal and external subject matter expert/consultant relationships and project plans as they contribute to the development of related TTA.

**Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E)**

- Oversee tracking of related TTA outputs and outcomes against targets (materials developed, trainings delivered, individuals participating, etc.)
- Together with Training Officers and Switchboard’s M&E team, review and analyze feedback data from related TTA participants
- Oversee provision of inputs into Switchboard reports, including monthly activity updates and semi-annual Performance Progress Reports.

- Other duties as assigned

**Job Requirements:**

**Required:**

- Bachelor's degree required, preferably in a related field such as Education, International Development, Social Work, Public Administration, Cross-Cultural Studies, Migration/Refugee Studies, or a related social science (or equivalent experience).
- Minimum 6 years of direct service experience with refugees and/or other ORR-eligible populations
- Experience delivering cultural orientation to newcomers
- Experience providing training and/or technical assistance to build the capacity of refugee service providers
- Experience providing client-centered, trauma-informed, and strength-based services for refugees
- Experience in supporting newcomers' access and gaining self-sufficiency for services and resources i.e. financial, medical, social, vocational etc.

**Preferred:**

- Lived experience with forced displacement or shared background with newcomer populations
- Experience managing external subject matter experts and/or consultants
- Experience contributing to project M&E (data collection, management, and reporting)
- Experience with evidence-based programming

**Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:**

- Working knowledge of programs and services related to client-centered services for refugees and newcomer families
- Strong understanding of cultural orientation frameworks, refugee/newcomer integration principles, and adult learning principles
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with fluency in English; including engaging public speaking abilities
- Self-starter with ability to work both independently and collaboratively as a part of a team
- Capacity to give and receive constructive feedback
- Strong organizational and project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple competing deadlines and efficient time management
- Adequate technology literacy including intermediate knowledge of MS Office Suite (Teams, Word, PowerPoint, Excel), and Zoom, with adaptability to learning new and innovative technology.
- Strong attention to detail

***Language Skills:*** Fluent in written and spoken English***.***

**Working Environment:** This position is a remote working environment. Required domestic travel up to 20%.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $80,000 - $85,000/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

jobs.title: P&C Compliance Sr Specialist
jobs.body:
**Job Overview:**

The P&C Employment Compliance Manager is the organization's designated subject matter expert and primary focal point for U.S. employment compliance — spanning Form I-9/E-Verify, background screening, EEO/EEOC compliance, and Employee Handbook and HR policy governance. This role exists to move IRC from a reactive, administrative approach to employment compliance toward a proactive, audit-ready one — particularly given IRC's workforce naturally includes a significantly higher proportion of employees with non-native immigration backgrounds than a typical U.S. employer, which elevates both the stakes and the complexity of getting this right.

This role is designed to make the jobs of P&C Partners easier, not to displace or duplicate them. By owning the standards, tools, training, audit processes, and regulatory tracking that P&C Partners currently have to navigate on their own, this role frees them to focus on people-centered, relationship-driven work, while giving them a dedicated expert to call on for complex or gray-area compliance questions — and appropriately escalating matters that require legal interpretation or advice.

The right candidate moves fluidly between hands-on execution — personally completing I-9 reverifications and audits, and serving as the final checkpoint before Tier 1 submits new-hire verifications — and enterprise-level program leadership: building the compliance frameworks, quality controls, vendor relationships, reporting structures, and training curricula that keep the organization audit-ready at all times. This is a deep practitioner role for someone interested in a career in this space, not a legal role — a law degree is not required.

While the role's deepest ownership sits with U.S. compliance given the concentration of legal complexity here, it also maintains lightweight visibility into policy currently across IRC's global operations.

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Employment Eligibility, I-9 & Background Screening Compliance**

- Own the organization's I-9 program end-to-end: set policy, standards, and process, and serve as the final review and confirmation point before Tier 1 submits new-hire I-9 verifications
- Personally complete all I-9 reverifications (e.g., work authorization renewals) and manage reverification timelines and tracking
- Design and deliver training and certification for everyone completing new-hire I-9 verifications (currently Tier 1 HR Operations), and serve as their go-to point of confirmation before submission when questions arise
- Conduct regular internal I-9 audits — including audits of Tier 1's completed verifications — and prepare the organization to respond to any government inspection or Notice of Inspection with confidence
- Own and oversee the U.S. background screening program, including process governance, vendor management, and continuous improvement, ensuring compliance with applicable federal, state, and local requirements, including the Fair Credit Reporting Act (FCRA)
- Own the Workday ↔ HireRight integration, coordinating with HR Technology, Talent Acquisition, and the vendor to ensure the integration meets compliance and operational requirements, and manage any future changes or new requirements as they arise

**Multistate Compliance & Regulatory Tracking**

- Maintain a living compliance matrix of federal, state, and local employment law obligations across all U.S. operating locations, including state-specific holidays, paid family leave requirements, and other jurisdiction-specific nuances
- Maintain clear visibility into where employees are located by state, so compliance obligations can be mapped accurately as the distributed workforce evolves
- Partner with Payroll to monitor wage-and-hour compliance — including meal and rest break requirements and timekeeping accuracy — in high-risk states such as California, proactively closing gaps before they become costly
- Monitor regulatory changes and proactively update policies, handbooks, and practices before deadlines take effect

**EEO / EEOC Compliance**

- Serve as the HR Operations focal point for EEO/EEOC-related compliance and reporting, including EEO-1/Affirmative Action Plan obligations and applicable state-level equivalents (e.g., New Jersey), monitoring where federal requirements have lapsed but state requirements may still apply
- Own California Pay Data Reporting (SB 1162) — coordinating with Payroll and People Analytics to compile accurate pay band, race/ethnicity, and sex data by job category, and managing the annual submission to California's Civil Rights Department ahead of the required deadline
- Coordinate EEO-1 reporting — data collection, validation, and submission — in partnership with People Analytics, HR Technology, and Payroll to ensure data integrity and reporting readiness
- Coordinate responses to EEOC-related requests, inquiries, or audits in partnership with Legal

**Audit, Quality Control & Vendor Management**

- Establish and execute a regular internal audit cadence across all compliance domains, identifying gaps and remediating errors before they escalate
- Manage relevant HR compliance vendors (background screening, I-9/E-Verify, and related third-party providers), monitoring performance and ensuring consistent application of compliance processes
- Identify opportunities to automate, streamline, and standardize compliance-related processes in partnership with HR Technology

**Policy and Handbook Currency**

- Own the review and update cycle for U.S. employment policies and the employee handbook, ensuring alignment with current federal, state, and local law across all jurisdictions, including state-specific and local addenda and the NY State/NYC regulatory environment
- Own a central repository for all P&C policies, driving a regular review cadence with each policy's subject-matter owner (Compensation, Benefits, Recruitment, etc.) to confirm currency and surface any conflicts between policies for resolution by the relevant owners — this role owns the system and process, not the content of policies outside employment law
- Partner with HR Communications to effectively communicate policy and handbook changes to employees and managers
- Maintain a lightweight annual review cycle for handbooks across IRC's non-U.S. operations — collecting the most current version from each country and flagging any that are overdue for update — without taking on deep ownership of non-U.S. policy content

**P&C Partner Enablement & Reporting**

- Act as a standing SME resource for P&C Partners, fielding compliance questions and providing guidance on complex or gray-area cases, and identifying the appropriate process, policy, resource, or escalation path
- Develop FAQs, guidance materials, tools, and job aids that enable P&C Partners to independently navigate common compliance questions

jobs.title: FIELD COMMUNICATION OFFICER
Caseworker
jobs.body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Job Overview:**

The Caseworker provides trauma-informed services to refugees and other ORR qualified immigrants to support a positive integration experience and the achievement of client self-sufficiency. The Caseworker works closely with clients, colleagues, and external parties to develop service and/or self-sufficiency plans to meet individual client needs and preferences utilizing a broad range of financial, medical, social, vocational, and other services and resources in accordance with client eligibility and program requirements.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Provide comprehensive case management services enrolled clients.
- Conduct intake services with clients to assess needs. Develop self-sufficiency plans and timelines in partnership with each client. Provide individualized support through direct services, referrals, and advocacy.
- Receive referrals for case management for ORR-eligible and TANF-eligible clients and participate in any needed case conference meetings to assure continuity of care.
- Assess client needs, creates Family Self-Sufficiency Plans (FSSPs) and Individual Employability Plans (IEPs), focusing on removing employment barriers, stabilizing, and obtaining and retaining employment.
- Assess and monitor client progress to support their attainment of established goals, address challenges, and to ensure that available resources are utilized.
- Detail each client interaction in accordance with program requirements. Input client information in database(s) and assist with tracking and reporting as needed.
- Collaborate effectively with coworkers and partner organizations. Build and maintain relationships with area service providers for the benefit of clients.
- Use personal, insured vehicle and/or public transportation (where available) to travel and transport clients and materials as needed throughout the service delivery area.
- May train and lead the activities of volunteers and interns.
- Conduct outreach to case management staff, refugee-serving agencies, ethnic community-based organizations, and others to inform service providers and refugees of programs and services.
- Complete eligibility screenings for all referral and enrollment paperwork for all eligible Program participants.
- Provide comprehensive case management services, including assisting with benefits applications as appropriate.
- Guide/assist participants to establish contact and receive support services in the community based on their service plan.
- Ensure all services are linguistically appropriate and help advocate with mainstream service providers for linguistically appropriate services.
- Complete case notes in a detailed and timely fashion.
- Ensure all family data is entered into data management system in a timely manner.
- Assist with the preparation of donor funding reports and new funding proposals.
- Participate in all program meetings, staff development activities, and fully engages as a member of the team.
- Follow all IRC policies, procedures and protocols including adherence to the IRC Way and Child Safeguarding.
- Other related duties as assigned.

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Position Reports to:**  Casework Supervisor

**Indirect Reporting:** Interns/Volunteers

**Job Requirements:**

***Education:***

- Undergraduate degree Social Work or similar field strongly preferred; comparable related work experience may be substituted.

***Work Experience:***

- 2+ years of case management experience in a social services environment.
- Experience working with vulnerable or under served populations preferred

***Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:***

- Computer proficiency with an emphasis on Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Teams, Outlook).
- Strong organizational skills and detail-oriented
- Public Speaking and/or presentation experience preferred
- Ability to effectively communicate and work as a team member with collaborative partners, the community, and clients in a cross-cultural, multi-disciplinary environment.
