jobs.title: NIGERIA - GRANTS & PARTNERSHIP HEAD OF DEPARTMENT (M/F) - ABUDJA
jobs.body:
## About us

**Desired start date: 15/12/2026**  
**Duration of the mission: 12 months**  
**Location: ABUJA**

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms.

## About the mission

**Solidarites International** launched its operation in Nigeria in 2016 as a consequence of the humanitarian needs of displaced populations and host communities caused by the current crisis with conflict and the ongoing violence in the North-East of Nigeria led by Armed Opposition Groups since 2009. The security situation and epidemics/outbreaks continue to affect millions of lives in Northeastern and North Western parts of Nigeria. As of June 2022, according to IOM Displacement Tracking Matrix, an estimated 2.2 million people are displaced within Borno State which remains, for a major part, inaccessible to humanitarian actors.

The targeted sectors of intervention are WASH, Shelter, RRM, Food Security & Livelihoods. The annual budget of the mission is around 8.3 million euros in 2022.

The mission is organized with a coordination office in Maiduguri and 3 bases located in Ngala, Dikwa and Monguno managed remotely from Maiduguri for the North-East. In the North-West, Solidarites International is conducting activities on 3 bases located in Gusau, Anka and Taleta in Zamfara State. Abuja is the representative for the mission Nigeria.

Mission staff : 165  
The Grants and Partnership HOD will directly manage the Grants coordination team composed of :   
\- A Reporting & Communications Officer   
She/he will closely work with all Departmental Heads, Field Coordinators and Project Managers of the mission.   
The Grants and Partnership HOD will report to the Country Director and be in link with Grants & Partnership department in HQ.

## About the job

**General objective:**

Working closely with the programmes and support departments, the Head of Grants and Partnerships Department is responsible for managing relations with donors, as well as developing and monitoring the country office's funding strategy. They supervise, adapt and optimise working methods and tools dedicated to managing donor accountability.   
They validate contractual documents (project proposals, reports, requests for amendments, partnership agreements, etc.) before they are submitted.   
They play a key role in defining the country office's partnership strategy and coordinates relations with the various implementing partners (see the partnership implementation framework). Ensures effective coordination between departments for grant management and provides strategic support to the country office in relation to donor relations, external representation, management of implementing partners, external compliance and accountability to donors.

**The main challenges:**

\- Access challenges and remote management due to security contraints in some areas of intervention  
\- Strategic positionning in a global trend of funding decrease   
\- Focus on partnership and localization in all areas of intervention. This requires adapted operational modalities and a support to local partners.

**Priorities for the 2/3 first months:**

\*Support the programmatic strategy (2027-2032) and PROG 2027 implementation  
\*Monitoring of partnerships and capacity building plan in coordination with other Department (Programs, E & C, etc.)  
\*Follow up on the advancement of the financing contracts   
\*Finalize partnership management/localization strategy  
\*Coordinate proposals   
\*Continue developing relationship with donor representatives and engage internally/ externally with different interlocutors to identify new funding opportunities

**Security constraints:**

No walking policy everywhere in the country / Security situation calm in Abuja, level 2 (out of 5), Maiduguri is level 3 and level 4 in other bases/sub-bases.

## Your profile

**Diploma and Experience :**

Diploma : Bachelor or masters in a related degree: humanitarian response, international cooperation

Experience in the humanitarian sector : 5 years and more

Experience on similar positions : 3/4 years

**SKILLS :**

**Technical skills**

1. Excellent reporting, writing and proof reading skills
2. Strong knowledge of main donors (ECHO, French donors, SIDA etc) and their respective policies / guidelines
3. Previous experience and achievements in developing strategic partnerships with other NGOs (MoUs, negotiations, governance, capacity building ...)
4. Proven ability to deal with donors and operational partners

**Transversal skills**

1. Critical thinking skills and the ability to adapt to fast-paced environments, while working independently to meet tight deadlines with minimal supervision
2. Good knowledge of the humanitarian project cycle management;
3. Excellent communication, networking skills, organizational and prioritization skills, ability to multi-task, Capacity to adapt and show organizational flexibilit
4. External representation

**Languages :**

1. English (fluent - Mandatory)
2. French (an asset)

## SI will offer you

**A salaried position:**  
**According to experience,** starting from EUR 2860 gross per month (2600 base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 750.

SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment.

**Breaks:** During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every three months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked.

**Insurance package:** Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded.

**LIVING CONDITIONS:**

The Grant & Partnership HOD will be based in Abuja with frequent field visit expected in the regional offices (Maiduguri. Birnin Kebbi and potentially Gusau or Sokoto).   
In Abuja, living condition are good and all commodities and goods (local or imported) can be found (supermarket, restautant, cinema, sport centers ...). Abuja GH is Comfortable with private bedroom and bathroom, 24/7 electricity and internet. GH is located in the same estate as the office, avoiding taking the car every morning but still clearly separated from working area (not the same building). Estate where GH/Office is located is providing Gym room, Swimming pool and squash court.  
At base level, (Maiduguri, Birnin Kebbi and Gusau), the bases offers a comfortable environment, in spite of limited movements outside of the compound for security reasons. The Guest House offers good living conditions, with private bedroom and bathroom and shared & comfortable common spaces. Electricity and internet are available at the office and at the GH at all times. Ping pong, pool table and some gym equipment are available in the GH in Maiduguri. All essential good (food, hygiene etc..) can be bought locally in the small shops around the office, or in the pre-validated supermarket. Visits to other NGOs are possible, as well as some pre-validated places (hotel and restaurants).  
Occasional field visit in NE sub bases, to ensure a correct program overview depedning on the security context and validation. No Overnight are possible in NE sub bases, only daily round trip with UNHAS are possible.

jobs.title: Emergency Response Manager Sudan
jobs.body:
**Background:**

The Emergency Response Manager (ERM) will oversee the overall country emergency response programme.

The ERM will lead on the coordination, quality response, management, and reporting of emergency response activities including those under the ECHO-funded Emergency Response consortium (FaSER) and UN pipelines. The ERM will support and provide technical supervision of emergency response teams in the field to respond to rapid onset crises related to conflict displacement and natural disasters, coordinating all emergency preparedness plans, minimum prepared actions (MPAs), and supervise emergency activities across NRC’s geographical spread in Sudan.

This will include pre-planning, assessment, coordination, leadership and overseeing emergency responses, in collaboration with Area Managers, Programme Specialists and other relevant programme and support departments, including safety and security and cash and market-based programming.

The role will also play a crucial function as surge capacity and will be deployed to hotspot locations across Sudan to reinforce critical emergency response programming depending on the needs of the operation.

**What you will do:**

Generic responsibilities:

1. Ensure adherence to NRC policies, handbooks, procedures and SOPs/guidelines;
2. Overall oversight, strategic development, and operational management of emergency response interventions across the Country Office;
3. Development of robust emergency set-ups based on appropriate needs analysis with an integrated programme approach;
4. Development of emergency response strategies and technical SOPs/guidelines;
5. Development and management of funding proposals, project budgets and donor reports;

Specific responsibilities:

1. **ERM Consortium Programme Management:**

- Overall responsibility for effective and efficient coordination of the emergency preparedness and response projects consistent with the project management cycle *(including reporting to the desired quality and standard)*;
- Overall budget management for FaSER projects/portfolio implemented and ensure appropriate burn-rates are maintained and that solutions to over/under expenditure are applied;
- Develop strategies, set-ups, and continuous review of technical guidance, tools, and SOPs for the overall emergency response

**2. Emergency Surge Support**

- Provide general programme support to key Area Offices during emergency responses including directly overseeing cash and other distributions.
- Lead and develop Emergency Response plans to coordinate NRC’s overall response to an emergency and provide inputs for use in fund raising, advocacy and programme development
- Lead coordination meetings with Programme, Support and Area Office colleagues.

**3. Coordination and Representation:**

- Liaise and coordinate with UN and I/NGO partners, local authorities, and beneficiaries in planning and response to emergencies, preparedness, and contextual understanding of areas of operations;
- Represent the RRM Consortium to external stakeholders - donors, government, coordination bodies, and local and international NGOs. Include the Steering Committee and other consortium staff in representation as much as possible and as appropriate. Network with relevant actors to help achieve consortium objectives;
- Conduct senior representation at state level and promote strong working relationships with government counterparts;

Please refer to the detailed [Job Description](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQBuZJQ-ramxQq178rbecg-aATvc50YqX3Sjy3I3YrYyE9A?e=NEqRjT) as the above enlisted responsibilities are just a snapshot.

**What you will bring:**

1. **Generic professional competencies:**

- At least five years in a humanitarian programming environment, including three years’ experience in project management position;
- Previous working experience in implementing emergency programme cycle in complex, fragile, and volatile contexts;
- Must have experience in cash-based programming, specifically cash distribution modalities;
- Emergency Response expertise, including Rapid Response Mechanisms (RRM) or Emergency Response Mechanisms (ERM);
- Technical expertise in one of NRC’s Core Competencies (Shelter/NFI, WASH, ICLA, Education, Camp Management/Protection from Violence), is added advantage;
- Documented results related to the position’s responsibilities;
- Fluency in English, both written and verbal;
- Computer literacy in Microsoft Office, including strong skills in Excel.

1. **Context/ Specific skills, knowledge and experience:**

- Keen interest and knowledge of the context in Sudan, previous experience in Sudan is very valuable;
- Arabic language skills is an advantage;
- Previous experience working with/ in consortiums and multi-agency projects;
- Specific experience in camp-contexts, distributions, cash programming and shelter/NFI
- Strong skills in analysis and coordination
- Experience in needs assessment, project monitoring and evaluation, and programme development;
- Strong leadership skills and a supportive management style;
- Experience of a flexible approach to managing and prioritising a high and diverse workload;
- Proven ability to work effectively across cultures, in sensitive environments and with stakeholders at all levels.

- **What we offer:**
- Duty station: Al-Geniena, Darfur, Sudan
- Contract: 12 Months (renewable based on funding and performance)
- Travel: 80%
- Salary/benefits: grade 9 on NRC’s either **national or international** salary scale.
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

Important information about the application process

- *For Internal candidates: To apply as an internal candidate, log in with your official email or click on Opportunity MarketPlace.*
- When creating your profile, include your full name as given on your passport. Complete all the system-required fields for experience, employment history and education.
- Applicants who do not fill in the required information will not be considered for the role.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV.
- Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered.
- Mandatory to submit the below when applying:
    - **Your most updated English CV and remove all previous outdated CVs.**
    - **Your most updated Cover Letter**
    - **Do not attach certificates or any other documents apart from the two mentioned above.**
    - **Incomplete applications will not be considered.**
- **This position is open for both national and international candidates. Internals might be assessed first if the pool is competitive.**
- We receive many applications for each vacant position. Therefore, only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.
- If you have any questions about this role, please email **esa.recruitment@nrc.no**with the job title as the subject line.

**Why NRC?**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

[Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/736782633) to see NRC in action.

We are looking for people who are passionate about helping refugees and people forced to flee. Are you one of those people? If you are, NRC offers you the opportunity to:

- do demanding and professional work, often in challenging contexts.
- join a work culture that empowers every employee to share ideas and take responsibility.
- be part of a welcoming and supportive community committed to human dignity.
- [Learn more about NRC](https://www.nrc.no/)
- [Learn more about Sudan](https://www.nrc.no/countries/africa/sudan/)

jobs.title: Development of a vector control training package for wash and health practitioners in the africa region.
jobs.body:
(Find the complete folder with all relevant information including the [RFP here](https://rodekruis.sharepoint.com/sites/Meetingsinternational/Gedeelde%20%20documenten/Public%20documents/IH%20Procurement%20public%20documents/RFP%20-%20Log-2026-1374%20Vector%20Control%20Training?d=w2f16674c6c2f4567b3946c075513f3fd&csf=1&web=1&e=0j4Puk))

**Terms of Reference**

**Title of Assignment**

Development of a Vector Control Training Package for WASH and Health Practitioners in the Africa Region

**Project Name**

WASH Surge Localization Programme

**Project Country**

Global (pilot training to be conducted in Ethiopia or South Sudan)

**1. Introduction**

The Netherlands Red Cross (NLRC) and partners are working to strengthen local capacities for emergency preparedness, anticipatory action, and response across Africa. In line with their auxiliary role to the public authorities, and within the framework of localization, National Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies frequently act as first responders during disease outbreaks, flooding, displacement crises, and other emergencies.

Vector-borne diseases continue to pose a significant public health burden in many countries where the Red Cross and Red Crescent National Societies operate. At the same time, vector control knowledge among WASH and Health practitioners varies considerably. There is a need for accessible, practical training materials that can be used by National Societies, surge personnel, and humanitarian practitioners to improve knowledge and decision-making related to vector control.

The NLRC therefore seeks a consultant to develop a comprehensive training package on vector control that can be delivered by facilitators with a fair understanding of the subject matter. The package will be piloted during a training event planned for December 2026 in either Ethiopia or South Sudan.

**2. Background and Context**

Vector-borne diseases remain among the leading causes of morbidity and mortality in many humanitarian settings. Climate change, population movements, urbanization, environmental degradation, and weak health systems are contributing to changes in disease transmission patterns and increasing the risk of outbreaks.

Humanitarian organizations are increasingly expected to integrate vector control considerations into emergency preparedness, response, recovery, and resilience programmes. While specialist expertise is sometimes available, many WASH and Health practitioners involved in programme design and implementation have limited formal training in vector control.

The Red Cross movement has an important role to play through:

- Community engagement , risk communication and behaviour change
- Environmental management
- Vector surveillance and risk assessment
- Support to outbreak preparedness and response including community-based surveillance
- Coordination with health and WASH actors
- Integration of vector control into humanitarian programming

To strengthen these capacities, a practical training package is required that can be delivered in different country contexts and adapted to local disease priorities.

**3. Purpose, Objectives and Deliverables**

**Purpose**

To develop a practical, participatory and easy-to-facilitate vector control training package for WASH and Health practitioners working in humanitarian and development settings.

**Overall Objective**

To increase the knowledge and understanding of vector-borne disease prevention and vector control among WASH and Health practitioners, enabling them to support the design, implementation and monitoring of appropriate vector control interventions.

**Specific Objectives**

The training package should enable participants to:

- Understand the epidemiology and transmission pathways of major vector-borne diseases.
- Understand the roles and responsibilities of WASH, Health and community actors in vector control.
- Conduct basic vector-related risk assessments.
- Select appropriate vector control interventions based on context and risk.
- Understand operational, environmental and safety considerations.
- Integrate vector control into preparedness, anticipatory action and humanitarian emergency responses.
- Coordinate with relevant health, WASH and government stakeholders.

**Scope of the Training Package**

The consultant should develop a 3 days training package with different modules and exercises, allowing for a one to three days training depending on the modules used.

The training should cover, at minimum:

**Vector-borne Diseases**

Introduction to: Malaria (with description of different malaria carrying subspecies) Dengue, Chikungunya, Yellow Fever, Schistosomiasis, Trypanosomiasis and other relevant diseases common in African humanitarian settings

**Vector Control Approaches**

Introduction to Environmental mechanical biological and chemical and integrated Vector Management (IVM).

**Humanitarian Context**

The context considered for the training include, vector control during emergencies**,** vector control during displacement and camp settings, Flood-related vector risks, Urban vector control challenges as well as for the Red Cross important Community-based approaches, and Protection, Gender and Inclusion (PGI)

**Planning and Decision Making**

The training should include a section focusing on health and surveillance data, risk assessment, Intervention selection, Monitoring and evaluation, Coordination mechanisms

**Safety and Environmental Considerations**

This should include Safe handling of equipment and chemicals Environmental risks Waste management Safeguarding and community acceptance

**Emerging and other relevant Topics**

Climate change and vector-borne diseases Insecticide resistance, new and emerging vector control tools such as spatial repellents, Operational challenges in humanitarian settings

**Deliverables**

- The consultant will with the support of the NLRC and UNICEF will be expected to provide: Review and compilation of existing vector control training materials from organizations such as: IFRC, WHO, UNICEF and NGO’s working on vector control and identify materials that can be adapted and referenced.
- The consultant will develop a complete facilitator package in English including: Facilitator guide, Agenda for a 3-day version, Session plans, Facilitation notes, Interactive exercises Possible case studies and group work exercises, Quizzes and knowledge checks
- Participant package that should include: Participant manual, Handouts, Reference materials, Reading list Links to online resources
- PowerPoint presentation deck(s) suitable for use by non-specialist facilitators.
- Training evaluation package including: Pre-training assessment Post-training assessment Participant evaluation forms
- Facilitation of a pilot training in December 2026 in Ethiopia South Sudan or other country in the region and incorporation of lessons learned into the final training package(optional).

**4. Profile of the Desired Consultant**

The consultant should possess:

- Minimum 7 years of professional experience in vector control, public health, entomology, or related fields.
- Demonstrated experience in humanitarian settings.
- Experience with vector control in Africa, preferably in both emergency and development contexts.
- Proven experience in developing training curricula and adult learning materials.
- Strong facilitation skills.
- Experience working with Red Cross/Red Crescent, UN agencies, government institutions or international NGOs is an advantage.
- Excellent written and spoken English.
- Experience integrating participatory adult learning methodologies.

**5. Methodology**

The consultant is expected to:

1. Conduct a brief desk review of existing training resources.
2. Consult with NLRC, IFRC, UNICEF and selected technical experts.
3. Develop draft training materials.
4. Revise materials based on feedback.
5. Facilitate the pilot training.
6. Produce a final training package reflecting lessons learned from the pilot.

**6. Planning**

Indicative timeline:

**Activity Timeline**

Contracting consultant - Week of 9th November 2026

Desk review and consultations - November 20th 2026

Draft training package - November 25th 2026

Review and revisions - December 5th 2026

Pilot training (optional time permitting) - December 2026

Final training package - December 2026

**7. Climate and Environmental Impact**

The consultant should ensure that:

- The training promotes environmentally responsible vector control approaches.
- Environmental and ecological risks of vector control interventions are adequately addressed.
- Preference is given to sustainable and integrated vector management approaches.
- Training delivery methods minimize environmental impact where feasible.

**8. Responsibilities and Communication**

The assignment will be coordinated by:

- Jan Heeger, WASH Programme Advisor, NLRC
- Selam Seje, Health Advisor, NLRC
- Joey de Hamer, Programme Manager, NLRC
- Peter Mamburi IFRC technical focal points

**Submission Deadline**

The proposal shall be submitted before the deadline for reception of applications on the 4th of October 2026.

Submission Method

- Proposals must be submitted electronically by email at logistics@redcross.nl with a cc. to JdeHamer@redcross.nl.

The assignment, including the submission of the final invoice, must be completed no later than 31 December 2026.

**Bid Format**

- Email subject must be: Log-2026-1374 – Development of a Vector Control Training Package + \[Name of the bidder\]
- The attachments to be included are described in the next section.
- Language: All documents shall be submitted in English.

**9. Required Documents**

1. **Cover Letter**
2. **Curricula Vitae**
3. **Technical Proposal and methodology**
4. **Financial Proposal** (budget with clear breakdown of fee and overheads if applicable);
5. **Previous Samples:** Applicants must provide at least one, and up to two, samples of previous written work similar to that described in the ToR (such as prior health related training provided), with any sensitive information redacted.
6. **Vendor Registration Form**: Bidders are required to complete the \[[*Annex 2: NLRC Vendor Registration Form*](https://rodekruis.sharepoint.com/sites/Meetingsinternational/_layouts/15/guestaccess.aspx?share=ETvU5WP-Qq5Ah7aIFhh7RXYBKEjBFDi3JiyiO3IV3PlULQ&e=3Nh0Er)\] and submit all relevant supporting documentation referenced in the form (Administrative checklist, Part 1 and 1.9 Environmental standards).

**Vendor Code of Conduct**

NLRC is committed to upholding the highest sustainability standards and requirements (ethical, social, environmental and quality) in all our business providing high-quality services and products. Complying with all laws and regulations and ensuring fair competition are fundamental to this commitment.

The \[[*NLRC Vendor Code of Conduct - Annex 3*](https://rodekruis.sharepoint.com/sites/Meetingsinternational/_layouts/15/guestaccess.aspx?share=IQDkY_CmSWcBQ4W9oHAtgqC8ARRb9CRv9LFAU3eQCgyeOVM&e=FCc7JJ)\], expresses the expectations we hold for all NLRC vendors. The Vendor Code of Conduct outlines the behaviours expected of Vendors who commit to uphold these standards and prevent misconduct. It is legally binding and forms an integral part of the contract between the Vendor and the NLRC. The winning applicants will be requested to sign this Code of Conduct at contract stage.

**Climate & Environmental Impact**

The NLRC has signed an environmental charter. As we work towards ensuring that all our operations coincide with this new agreement, we must also demand that any collaborations we have with external parties also falls within the parameters of this charter.

Please complete the section 1.9 Environmental standards in the Vendor Registration Form \[[*NLRC\_Vendor Registration Form.docx*](https://rodekruis.sharepoint.com/sites/Meetingsinternational/_layouts/15/guestaccess.aspx?share=IQBTNSN4OdU7QISbXbwiWsG6AZBy_YDVy667BGqqVVp3tCg&e=8aZ3gj)\] and provide any additional documents that could illustrate your environmental engagement.

The consultant will work closely with NLRC and IFRC technical staff throughout the assignment and present draft outputs for review and approval.

jobs.title: Oficial de Cadena de Suministro - Maracaibo
jobs.body:
El Consejo Dánes para refugiados es una de las ONG humanitarias líderes en el mundo, que trabaja en más de 40 países para brindar asistencia y protección adecuadas a refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, desplazados internos, retornados, personas en movimiento y población local vulnerable/comunidades de acogida. Actualmente, DRC está buscando un **Oficial de Cadena de Suministro** altamente calificado con sede en **Maracaibo, Edo. Zulia.**

**Acerca del trabajo:**

DRC está administrando sus operaciones en Venezuela, bajo la dirección de la oficina de país en Caracas y tres oficinas de campo ubicadas en los estados de Sucre, Apure y Zulia. DRC Venezuela está implementando actividades como monitoreo de protección, asistencia legal, asistencia de protección individual para PWSN, sesiones informativas para PoC, prevención de trata de personas, rehabilitación de infraestructura de salud y seguridad alimentaria.

**Responsabilidades:**

**Compras**

- Asegurar el cumplimiento de los procesos de compra requeridos para el adecuado funcionamiento de las operaciones de DRC en Maracaibo.
- Colaboración directa con los equipos de programa para la planificación local de las necesidades de compra y logísticas de los programas de DRC en Zulia.
- Generar seguimiento y trazabilidad de las solicitudes de compra.
- Validar la integridad documental de los procesos según los requerimientos de los donantes.
- Contacto con proveedores para cotizaciones y evaluaciones de compras locales.
- Comunicación directa con proveedores relacionados con la entrega de insumos en los programas de DRC.
- Seguimiento a devoluciones o reclamaciones con proveedores.
- Preparación de solicitudes de pago para el trámite de los equipos de Finanzas de DRC.
- Cualquier otra tarea que le asigne el Gerente de Línea / Técnico.

**Logística**

- Asegurar la entrega oportuna de los materiales solicitados, teniendo en cuenta los procesos y tiempos establecidos por DRC.
- Control, registro y seguimiento de los activos fijos gestionados en la oficina local.
- Realizar inventarios y llevar el control detallado del inventario general de DRC.
- Garantizar la gestión de los servicios generales para los equipos de trabajo (alojamiento, personal, visitantes, oficinas, lugares de almacenamiento y seguridad).

jobs.title: Líder de Equipo WASH Shelter & Infrastructure (Caracas - Personal Nacional) - Republicado
jobs.body:
Danish Refugee Council (DRC) es una de las ONG humanitarias líderes en el mundo, que trabaja en más de 40 países para brindar asistencia y protección adecuadas a refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, desplazados internos, retornados, personas en movimiento y población local vulnerable/comunidades de acogida. Actualmente, en el marco de la respuesta de emergencia al terremoto, DRC está buscando un/a Líder de Equipo WASH Shelter & Infrastructure altamente calificado/a con sede en Caracas, Venezuela.

**Acerca del trabajo:**

DRC administra sus operaciones en Venezuela bajo la dirección de la oficina de país en Caracas y tres oficinas de campo ubicadas en los estados de Sucre, Apure y Zulia. DRC Venezuela implementa actividades de monitoreo de protección, asistencia legal, asistencia de protección individual para personas con necesidades específicas (PWSN), sesiones informativas para personas de interés (PoC), prevención de la trata de personas y seguridad alimentaria.

En el marco de la respuesta de emergencia al terremoto ocurrido en el mes de junio 2026, DRC está abriendo una nueva oficina de implementación en Caracas, independiente de la oficina de país, para atender las necesidades de las poblaciones afectadas. Para ello, busca incorporar un/a el Líder de Equipo de Agua, Saneamiento, Higiene, Alojamientos e Infraestructura (WASI) de Emergencia será responsable de liderar operativamente la respuesta de emergencia y la recuperación temprana en los sectores de Agua, Saneamiento e Higiene (WASH), Alojamientos de Emergencia (Shelter) e Infraestructura.

**Objetivo general del puesto**

Bajo la supervisión del Coordinador de Emergencias y/o Gerente de Base y la orientación técnica del Especialista Nacional WASI, el Líder de Equipo de Agua, Saneamiento, Higiene, Alojamientos e Infraestructura (WASI) de Emergencia será responsable de liderar operativamente la respuesta de emergencia y la recuperación temprana en los sectores de Agua, Saneamiento e Higiene (WASH), Alojamientos de Emergencia (Shelter) e Infraestructura, asegurando la rápida evaluación de daños y necesidades, la priorización de intervenciones, la movilización eficiente de recursos y la supervisión técnica de las actividades implementadas por el equipo WASI para restablecer servicios esenciales y apoyar a la población afectada por el desastre. Además, garantizará el cumplimiento de los estándares humanitarios aplicables, la integración de los enfoques de protección, AAP y PSEA, la adecuada coordinación con autoridades, comunidades y otros actores humanitarios, y la gestión eficiente del equipo y los recursos asignados para el logro de los objetivos programáticos de DRC en contextos de emergencia.

**Responsabilidades:**

**Gestión**

- Dirigir y gestionar al equipo WASI de terreno, planificando sus actividades.
- Garantizar una adecuada planificación operativa y una ejecución de calidad de las actividades de respuesta WASI en terreno.
- Supervisar y acompañar técnicamente a los Oficiales WASI y demás personal vinculado a la implementación de actividades sectoriales.
- Asegurar el seguimiento diario de las intervenciones WASI, identificando oportunamente riesgos, limitaciones y oportunidades de mejora.
- Promover la integración transversal de los enfoques de protección, género, inclusión, rendición de cuentas a las poblaciones afectadas (AAP) y protección contra la explotación y el abuso sexual (PSEA) en todas las actividades.
- Garantizar que el personal conozca, comprenda y cumpla las políticas, procedimientos y reglamentos de DRC.
- Reportar incidentes, faltas o incumplimientos del personal y participar en los procesos disciplinarios correspondientes cuando sea requerido.

**Programas y operaciones**

- Liderar la planificación operativa y la priorización de las acciones de respuesta rápida durante las primeras horas, días y semanas posteriores al desastre, asegurando una movilización eficiente de recursos humanos, materiales y financieros.
- Garantizar una ejecución eficiente y eficaz de los proyectos WASI en emergencias, en cumplimiento de los objetivos, cronogramas, presupuestos y estándares de calidad establecidos.
- Coordinar la realización de evaluaciones rápidas de necesidades en contextos de emergencia para orientar la planificación de la respuesta.
- Consolidar y analizar información proveniente de evaluaciones, monitoreo y reportes de terreno para apoyar la toma de decisiones estratégicas y la priorización de la respuesta.
- Identificar y escalar oportunamente necesidades críticas, brechas de asistencia, riesgos emergentes y limitaciones operativas que requieran decisiones o recursos adicionales.
- Supervisar la planificación e implementación de actividades de comunicación de riesgos y sensibilización comunitaria en higiene, distribución de kits WASH, kits de alojamiento y artículos no alimentarios (NFI).
- Coordinar con el equipo de Soporte la adquisición acelerada de materiales, equipos, servicios y obras necesarios para la respuesta.
- Participar en la elaboración de informes internos, reportes para donantes, propuestas técnicas y contribuciones programáticas relacionadas con el sector.
- Dirigir al equipo en la implementación de actividades de monitoreo y seguimiento de proyectos, incluyendo verificaciones en terreno, monitoreo post distribución y acciones de rendición de cuentas.
- Liderar la transición de las actividades de respuesta inmediata hacia intervenciones de recuperación temprana orientadas al restablecimiento progresivo y resiliente de servicios e infraestructura básica.

**Obras WASH, Shelter e Infraestructura**

- Supervisar la evaluación rápida de daños y condiciones de funcionalidad de infraestructuras afectadas para orientar la priorización de intervenciones de emergencia y recuperación temprana.
- Garantizar la priorización y supervisión de intervenciones destinadas al restablecimiento oportuno de servicios esenciales de agua, saneamiento e infraestructura en comunidades, centros de salud, escuelas, refugios colectivos y otras instalaciones críticas afectadas.
- Liderar la planificación y supervisión de intervenciones de sistemas WASH, alojamiento de emergencia, refugios colectivos y soluciones temporales de alojamiento conforme a estándares humanitarios.
- Priorizar junto con el Especialista WASI y el Coordinador de Emergencia las intervenciones de rehabilitación y recuperación temprana de infraestructuras esenciales.
- Supervisar la adecuación y gestión técnica de refugios colectivos y espacios temporales de alojamiento, garantizando condiciones mínimas de seguridad, dignidad, accesibilidad y protección para la población afectada.
- Supervisar la preparación de especificaciones técnicas, alcances de obra, presupuestos referenciales y requerimientos de contratación para intervenciones de emergencia y recuperación temprana.
- Supervisar la ejecución de rehabilitaciones y mejoras de infraestructura relacionadas con sistemas de agua, saneamiento, drenaje, gestión de residuos, alojamiento y espacios comunitarios y que presten servicios esenciales.
- Supervisar la calidad técnica de las obras de emergencia y recuperación temprana ejecutadas por contratistas.
- Garantizar que todas las obras WASH, de infraestructura y de alojamientos incorporen criterios de seguridad, accesibilidad, protección, gestión ambiental y reducción de riesgos.

**Coordinación y representación**

- Coordinar con especialistas técnicos internos y externos en asuntos relacionados con los sectores WASH y Shelter.
- Mantener comunicación permanente con autoridades locales, líderes comunitarios, prestadores de servicios y socios implementadores para facilitar la ejecución de las actividades.
- Representar a DRC en mecanismos de coordinación humanitaria, incluyendo Grupos Sectoriales/Clusters de WASH, Shelter y otros espacios relevantes, asegurando el intercambio oportuno de información sobre necesidades, avances, brechas y prioridades operacionales.
- Garantizar la coordinación e integración de actividades con otros sectores programáticos de DRC, especialmente Protección, Recuperación Económica y Preparación para Desastres.

**Seguimiento de los proyectos**

- Supervisar la ejecución técnica de los proyectos, asegurando el cumplimiento de los estándares Sphere y otros estándares humanitarios aplicables.
- Garantizar la recopilación, validación y análisis oportuno de información relacionada con indicadores, registros de beneficiarios, evaluaciones sectoriales y actividades implementadas.
- Supervisar la calidad y completitud de los medios de verificación, documentación técnica, reportes fotográficos, actas, listas de asistencia y demás soportes requeridos por los proyectos.
- Coordinar la elaboración y seguimiento de planes de trabajo, cronogramas de implementación y prioridades operativas del equipo.
- Garantizar la aplicación de mecanismos de retroalimentación comunitaria y rendición de cuentas durante la implementación de las actividades.

**Logística y Finanzas**

- Apoyar el seguimiento de los compromisos financieros y gastos de los proyectos WASI en relación con los presupuestos aprobados.
- Coordinar la planificación logística de las actividades de terreno y los desplazamientos del equipo a las distintas áreas de intervención.
- Iniciar y dar seguimiento a los procesos de adquisición relacionados con materiales, equipos, servicios y obras requeridas para las actividades sectoriales.
- Coordinar con los equipos de Soporte la planificación de distribuciones y actividades de intervención de emergencia.
- Supervisar la recepción, almacenamiento temporal, control de calidad y distribución de materiales e insumos WASH y Shelter.
- Garantizar la aplicación de medidas de protección, seguridad y manejo adecuado de riesgos durante las distribuciones e intervenciones en terreno.
- Garantizar que las actividades de campo se realicen conforme a los procedimientos de seguridad, acceso humanitario y gestión de riesgos de la organización, reportando oportunamente incidentes, restricciones y cambios en el contexto operacional.

**Experiencia y competencias:**

- Mínimo 3 años de experiencia en puestos de coordinación o supervisión técnica de equipos en contextos humanitarios.
- Mínimo 3 años de experiencia en la implementación de proyectos de Agua, Saneamiento e Higiene (WASH), Shelter, infraestructura comunitaria o respuesta a emergencias.
- Experiencia demostrada en supervisión de obras de emergencia y recuperación temprana, rehabilitación de infraestructura básica, gestión de contratistas y seguimiento de intervenciones de alojamiento y alojamiento temporal.
- Conocimiento sólido de los estándares humanitarios Sphere aplicables a WASH y Shelter.
- Experiencia en coordinación con autoridades locales, organizaciones humanitarias, líderes comunitarios y mecanismos de coordinación sectorial.
- Habilidades demostradas de liderazgo, supervisión y gestión de equipos multidisciplinarios.
- Experiencia en seguimiento de presupuestos, planificación operativa y monitoreo de indicadores de proyectos.
- Compromiso con el aprendizaje y la aplicación de las políticas y procedimientos de la organización.
- Excelentes conocimientos de MS Word, Excel y PowerPoint.
- Experiencia en herramientas digitales para recolección y gestión de datos (Kobo Toolbox o similares).
- Experiencia comprobada de trabajo en terreno y disponibilidad para desplazamientos frecuentes.
- Dominio profesional del inglés (nivel B2 deseable).

[*Deseable*](https://reliefweb.int/void(0))

- Carácter tranquilo y diplomático;
- Conocimiento de principios y enfoques de Protección en la acción humanitaria;
- Capacidad para gestionar las prioridades en competencia y cumplir con los plazos;
- Capacidad para fomentar un ambiente de trabajo colaborativo y mantener relaciones efectivas con socios implementadores y actores locales;
- Conocimiento del marco legal venezolano aplicable y de los principios del derecho internacional humanitario y de los derechos humanos.

**Educación:**

- Título en Ingeniería Civil/Arquitectura u otro profesional equivalente, con experiencia en WASH y Shelter o Infraestructura.

**Idioma:**

- Ingles (B2 Deseable)
- Español

**Ofrecemos:**

- La oportunidad de pertenecer a una de las mejores ONGs a nivel mundial.
- Acceso a más de 1,000 capacitaciones y certificados en línea gratuita.
- Duración del contrato: 4 meses con disponibilidad de extensión según disponibilidad presupuestal.
- Salario: **Banda G.**

**Competencias Básicas de DRC:**

- **Lograr la excelencia**: centrarse en alcanzar resultados y garantizar procesos eficientes.
- **Colaboración:** involucrar a las partes relevantes y alentar la retroalimentación.
- **Tomar la iniciativa**: tomar posesión e iniciativa mientras se busca la innovación.

**Proceso de solicitud:** Todos los solicitantes deben cargar una carta de presentación (máx. 1 página) y un CV actualizado (**máx. 2 páginas, sin soportes**) en español, en la plataforma de empleo de DRC. Las solicitudes enviadas por correo electrónico no serán consideradas.

**Fecha de cierre de solicitudes**: 08 de noviembre a las 11:59 pm Hora Local. Tenga en cuenta que las solicitudes se revisarán continuamente y las entrevistas se planificarán tan pronto como se identifique a un candidat@ adecuado. DRC se reserva el derecho a cerrar la vacante antes de la fecha límite una vez se identifique a un candidato idóneo.

jobs.title: Operations Manager
jobs.body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**JOB OVERVIEW:**

The Operations Manager (OM) is responsible for the direct or indirect oversight and coordination of all operational functions in the Bay Area (San Jose and Oakland) grouping, resulting in a well-functioning, compliant operational environment. The Operations Manager serves as the primary liaison for HQ Regional Functional Leads including Supply Chain Advisor (SCA), Regional Safety & Security Director (RSSD), Regional IT Director (RITD) and Global Facilities Director (GFD). This position reports to the Executive Director and oversees the Operations staff in both offices. This position is based in either San Jose or Oakland, with regular weekly onsite presence within both offices.

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Safety & Security—S&S:**

- Oversee regional S&S matters.
- Responsible for the implementation and maintenance of all office S&S documentation.
- Organize all-staff S&S meetings at office or program site.
- Ensure that a minimum of one emergency evacuation is exercised at office or program site level per year and other appropriate trainings informed by Security Risk Assessment findings.
- Cascade HQ and/or office security warnings and advisories to staff, interns, and volunteers as needed.
- Report all S&S incidents involving covered persons in accordance with established protocols.
- Coordinate immediate incident management including filing police reports.
- Build and maintain strong relationships with other S&S actors or stakeholders, including but not limited to community organizations and partners, authorities, security and rescue services, and property owners.
- Assist in the development of office-specific S&S onboarding materials, ensuring the provision of S&S briefings to new staff and covered persons.

**Supply Chain—SC:**

- Serve as the region’s primary focal point for procurement, asset and inventory management, in-kind donations tracking and reporting, vehicle fleet management and transportation, and warehousing in accordance with established organizational and donor requirements.
- Lead the bidding process, including request for quotation process, request for proposal process, tender evaluation, and facilitating procurement committee functioning.
- Manage relationships with suppliers and vendors.
- Maintain up-to-date supplier and service provider records. Maintain asset register and inventory lists of purchased and donated items. Establish and manage inventory control for office supplies, stationery, and other consumables. In collaboration with the Finance Manager, ensure inventories reconcile with financial reports.
- Support program teams in meeting their match goals.
- Ensure policy compliance for the fleet of IRC-owned vehicles and oversee their maintenance and usage.
- Working with HQ Supply Chain to maintain IRC policy at all the times.
- Control and maintain the IRC policy through the PO system in Integra.

**Facilities Management:**

- Manage the region’s office and equipment leases, coordinate repairs and improvements with property managers, and lead the procurement of office equipment.
- Coordinate the allocation of workspaces and support related employee lifecycle needs such as building access.
- Support smooth functioning of office infrastructure including communications equipment and services.
- Assist with planning and coordinating office events and meetings.
- Responsible for coordinating on- and off-site storage needs.
- Maintain NorCal’s status with all counties related to annual property’s tax along with exemption status.

**Information Technology—IT:**

- Oversee grouping IT and communications infrastructure, hardware and software matters.
- Educate staff about IT support resources, including appropriate channels for incident reporting.
- Work with regional and HQ IT team to address any internet or telecommunications service disruptions, liaising with local internet and telecommunications service providers.
- Escalate any unresolved incidents or larger-scale IT projects (such as office moves or expansion) as needed.
- Ensure compliance with IT protocols, policies, and procedures including information security policy, IT procurement and asset management policy, acceptable use of IT resources policy, and new software procurement protocols.

**Other Duties**

- Provide mentorship and supervision to Operations staff, including leading team meetings, individual supervision and coaching, and conducting goal setting, and performance reviews.
- Approve Integra vendor creations and invoice journals.
- Coordinate with the Finance Director to manage administrative expenses and reports.
- Other duties as assigned.

**Key Working Relationships:**

- **Position reports to:** Executive Director
- **Position directly supervises:** Front Desk staff, Operations staff

**Job Requirements:**

- Undergraduate degree in business, non-profit management, public administration, or others related field preferred
- At least five years of related professional experience; preferably with refugee services and in a non-profit or social service environment
- Experience supervising staff preferred
- Demonstrated ability to work with deadlines and lead multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment
- Good interpersonal communication skills and ability to effectively work in a multi-cultural work environment
- Knowledge of state and federal donor compliance regulations is a strong plus
- Fluency in English, written and spoken

**Working Environment:**

- Combination of standard office environment and remote work.
- Regular weekly onsite presence split between the San Jose and Oakland offices
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.

**Compensation:** **($83,215-$93,224).** Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

jobs.title: Chief Field Office, P-4, FT, #099121, Bunia -Democratic Republic of Congo, WCAR
jobs.body:
UNICEF works in over 190 countries and territories to save children’s lives, defend their rights, and help them fulfill their potential, from early childhood through adolescence.

At UNICEF, we are committed, passionate, and proud of what we do for as long as we are needed. Promoting the rights of every child is not just a job – it is a calling.

UNICEF is a place where careers are built: we offer our staff diverse opportunities for professional and personal development that will help them reinforce a sense of purpose while serving children and communities across the world. We welcome everyone who wants to belong and grow in a diverse and passionate culture, coupled with an attractive compensation and benefits package.

Visit [our website](https://www.unicef.org/) to learn more about what we do at UNICEF.

**For every child,** ***the right to Hope***

**How can you make a difference?**

Under the guidance of the Chief Field Operations, you as the Chief Field Office (CFO) will be accountable for managing and leading the total programme commitment of a field office within a country programme. You will represent UNICEF in Bunia, leads and oversees the various program sectors and operational service teams ensuring the delivery of quality results in accordance with UNICEF’s programme of cooperation, country programme management plan and overall vision set forward by the Representative. The role operates in a protracted, multi-hazard emergency environment characterized by armed violence, large-scale displacement, severe protection risks, recurrent disease outbreaks, constrained humanitarian access, community mistrust and disruption of essential services. You will provide area-based leadership for UNICEF’s response across Ituri and, when delegated, supports operational coherence with Haut-Uélé and adjoining outbreak and displacement corridors.

In fragile and humanitarian contexts, UNICEF action is guided by its global Policy and Framework for humanitarian action: the Core Commitments for Children in Humanitarian Action.

**KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES and DUTIES & TASKS**

1. Effective management of UNICEF presence, staff and assets
2. Knowledge Management for Programmes
3. Programme Development and Management
4. Optimum Use of Program Funds
5. Programme Monitoring and Evaluations
6. Rights-Based and Results-Based Programme Management Approach
7. National and Local Capacity Building/Sustainability
8. Rights Perspective and Advocacy at the National, Community and Family Levels
9. Partnership, Coordination and Collaboration

If you would like to know more about this position, please review the complete Job Description here: [JD - Chief Field Office P-4.pdf](https://secure.dc7.pageuppeople.com/apply/TransferRichTextFile.ashx?sData=UFUtVjMtNWAKkHsLiz2HFSYUmbPc_z8pyzxzCu_jYZTSBYrvr9XuES25CImv1_GakfyFDA5DE8bsWa-N1vF7Xfu5kw-QnLBZzEisVQ_2a1Q2GVqckCfitnwWY5VrQCl9qMwcgTTWxBjTs43kaieIVdd0FD3TQg%7e%7e)

jobs.title: Consortium Manager South Sudan Juba
jobs.body:
**Background:**

NRC works to protect the rights of displaced and vulnerable people during crisis and meet immediate humanitarian needs, prevent further displacement, and contribute to durable solutions. Through our mobile emergency response capacity, we provide lifesaving multisectoral assistance to crisis affected populations in hard-to-reach areas across South Sudan. In areas throughout the country where we have established operations, we ensure that displacement affected people are safe, can exercise their rights, access quality services and protection and secure durable solutions. To that end, we contribute to safe and stable environment needed to allow for return and reintegration or integration of displaced communities. We do this through advocacy, coordination, and collaboration, as well as integrated and multi-sectoral long-term interventions.

In South Sudan, NRC established in 2004 and provides humanitarian assistance and supports durable solutions with integrated and multi-sectoral long-term interventions in six core competencies: Information Counselling and Legal Assistance (ICLA), Protection from Violence, Education, WASH and Shelter. In line with NRC global direction, our WASH and Shelter programmes are transitioning from mainly humanitarian response to support communities with more sustainable water systems and sanitation facilities in response to securing lasting solutions. Also, NRC has the ambition to grow its urban programming to facilitate durable solutions for the swelling urban population in South Sudan.

**What you will do:**

NRC South Sudan leads an EU-funded Education Agri-TVET Consortium in partnership with a wide network of both national and international partners. The Agri-skills for Resilient, Inclusive, and Sustainable Economies (ARISE) Consortium aims to bridge the critical skills gap in South Sudan’s agricultural sector by delivering competency-based Agri Value Chain TVET skills aligned to profitable value chain commodities being developed by Green Resilience Economy partners across targeted states in South Sudan. ARISE will strengthen South Sudan’s Agri–value chain TVET system so youth, especially girls/young women and displacement-affected learners, gain market-relevant, green and transferable skills that lead to decent work and viable self-employment. The action is designed to complement the EU’s Green and Resilient Economy (GRE) investments by building a reliable skills-to-jobs pipeline into existing value chain and MSME ecosystems, rather than duplicating market systems or production programming.

The Consortium Manager will oversee the Consortium and be responsible for their overall management. This position is responsible for strategic advice on the management and direction of the consortium programme(s), the operational management and implementation of the project(s), including project implementation in terms of coordinating delivery and the inputs from consortium members. The Consortium Manager will facilitate the strategic development of consortium programmes, responsible for forging strong relationships with and between consortium members, donor(s) and other relevant stakeholders, as well as ensuring compliance with donor contractual requirements, and NRC and/or Consortium internal procedures.

General Responsibilities:

1. Compliance and adherence to NRC policies, CC tools, handbooks and guidelines.
2. Provide overall direction and leadership of the Consortium to ensure seamless operations, leveraging complementarity among partners
3. Provide systematic training and build capacity of technical staff where relevant.

Specific responsibilities:

- Coordinate with consortium members to ensure high-quality implementation of activities, compliance with donor and consortium rules, and accountability to beneficiaries.
- Oversee day-to-day management of the project, including planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation and budget spending, ensuring project is always on scope and schedule
- Represent the Consortium towards relevant stakeholders, including national authorities, donors and counterparts, promoting the best interests of Consortium partners
- Line Manage and supervise the work of the Consortium Management Unit; carry out any needed recruitments, including for consultants
- Lead the consultations, design and preparation of the next phase of the Consortium based on evidenced needs, donor expectations and drawing from partners’ diverse expertise

Please refer to the full [Job Description](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQBQiZTWSdoeR7iyfO4fnOG0Acj-7BedNwjsRTUIkAUvUos?e=gLQcoH) as the above-mentioned responsibilities are just a snapshot.

**What you will bring:**

- Minimum BA in relevant areas preferably
- Minimum 5 years of humanitarian experience across multiple context with at least 2 years’ experience of youth programmes
- At least 3 years project management experience of managing multi-million (EURO) projects;
- Experience in consortium management or extensive involvement in a consortium, with a multi-year duration
- Experience developing training tools, manuals, information management systems for humanitarian action and accountability to affected people.
- Self-motivated and confident communicator, with experience in giving briefings and presentations.
- Strong inter-personal skills, working well both in teams and independently
- Able to work under pressure and good at timely decision making
- Fluency in English, both written and verbal.
- Preferred experience or knowledge of Sudan context.

**What we offer:**

- Duty station: Juba, South Sudan
- Contract: 12 Months (renewable based on funding and performance)
- Salary/benefits: grade 9 on NRC’s **international contract.**
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

Important information about the application process

- *For Internal candidates: To apply as an internal candidate, log in with your official email or click on Opportunity MarketPlace.*
- When creating your profile, include your full name as given on your passport. Complete all the system-required fields for experience, employment history and education.
- Applicants who do not fill in the required information will not be considered for the role.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV.
- Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered.
- Mandatory to submit the below when applying:
    - **Your most updated English CV and remove all previous outdated CVs.**
    - **Your updated Cover Letter.**
    - **Do not attach certificates or any other documents apart from the two mentioned above.**
    - **Incomplete applications will not be considered.**
- **This position is open for all international candidates.**
- We receive many applications for each vacant position and so only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.
- If you have any questions about this role, please email **esa.recruitment@nrc.no**with the job title as the subject line.

**Why NRC?**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

[Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/736782633) to see NRC in action.

We are looking for people who are passionate about helping refugees and people forced to flee. Are you one of those people? If you are, NRC offers you the opportunity to:

- do demanding and professional work, often in challenging contexts.
- join a work culture that empowers every employee to share ideas and take responsibility.
- be part of a welcoming and supportive community committed to human dignity.

## About Us

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is a global humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee.

Join us in assisting millions of people in areas where others cannot, tackling some of the world's most dangerous and difficult crises. Bring your skills and dedication to an organisation recognised for providing high quality aid and for defending the rights of refugees and internally displaced people.

At NRC, we give responsibility to employees at all levels and foster professional growth and innovative teams. You can expect a supportive culture and an open dialogue with management. We are committed to diversity, equity and inclusion.

Together, we save lives and rebuild futures.

Safeguarding is central to NRC’s work. We expect all employees to:

• treat everyone with respect and dignity

• contribute to building a safe environment for all

• never engage in any form of exploitation, harassment and specifically sexual exploitation, abuse and sexual harassment (SEAH)

• always report. NRC has a zero-tolerance approach to inaction against exploitation, abuse and SEAH

jobs.title: Distribution Coordinator
jobs.body:
Northern Lights Aid (NLA) is a small grassroots NGO in Kavala, Northern Greece, that focuses on improving the quality of life of people living in the nearby Perigiali Refugee Camp, as well as other vulnerable communities in the local area. We provide material support through a free store, and operate a Community Centre where we offer informal education and recreational activities.

We are looking for a Distribution Coordinator to join us in Kavala on the **7th of January 2027** for a minimum of 4 months.

The role of the Distribution Coordinator is to ensure the smooth execution of all distribution efforts, including the daily operations in our free store as well as the weekly distribution of baby items. The Distribution Coordinator acts as the central point of oversight for all distribution activities and is involved in stock management, documentation, and the guidance of volunteers. They are dedicated to creating a welcoming and dignified atmosphere for all ages, genders and backgrounds across all distribution operations.

## Responsibilities:

### Coordination of daily distribution efforts

- Facilitate a dignified and efficient experience for all community members according to the organization’s project guidelines, policies and values
- Ensure all community members receive items in a fair and consistent manner
- Respond to daily challenges such as complaints or special requests from community members
- Track daily project attendance
- Ensure information regarding store opening hours and distribution activities is available, accessible to people of all backgrounds, and shared with community members through appropriate channels
- Collaborate with the Community Centre Coordinator to align efforts and respond to community needs comprehensively

### **Management of stock levels and spaces**

- Sort and organize incoming donations
- Monitor stock levels
- Assist in developing procurement approaches and in exploring potential collaborations
- Optimize storage layout and maintain a clear and organized system in the warehouse
- Ensure the cleanliness and tidiness of the store and storage area

### **Support of volunteer management**

- Communicate daily tasks with volunteers and ensure tasks are completed
- Welcome new volunteers, conduct project inductions, and follow up to ensure clear understanding of the space, their role, and their responsibilities
- Lead daily volunteer debriefs to gather input, address concerns, and encourage suggestions
- Pass on needed information regarding volunteer management including wellbeing concerns and potential conflicts/tensions within the team to the Field Manager

### **Report to Field Manager**

- Engage in weekly meetings with the Field Manager to keep them informed about project developments
- Communicate shortages and inventory stock needs
- Draft quarterly reports in collaboration with the Field Manager
- Keep track of and share feedback from community members
- Alert the Field Manager about behaviour from volunteers or community members that violates guidelines, and report safeguarding concerns appropriately
- Participate in project development by collaborating with the Field Manager and Director of Operations to evaluate NLA’s capacity to make changes to the project

## Requirements:

### **Required Skills**

- Highly organized and proactive approach to work
- Excellent communication skills and the ability to respond calmly in challenging situations
- Politically and culturally sensitive with the ability to act with patience, tact, and diplomacy
- Ability to work well both independently and cooperatively within a team
- Ability to demonstrate clear professional boundaries with community members
- Good management abilities and capacity to take on responsibilities
- Strong commitment to the values of NLA and dedication to supporting displaced people
- Fluency in English (knowledge of Arabic, Farsi, Turkish, or Kurmanji is an asset)

### **Relevant Experiences**

- Previous experience working with displaced people
- Volunteer or professional experience in project coordination
- Strong interest in, or educational background/professional experience related to logistics, distributions, retail, or stock management

### **Other**

- Minimum time commitment: 4 months
- Minimum age: 23 years old
- Ability to reside legally in the EU for the full duration of the commitment
- Starting date: 7th of January (handover period mid-December, preferably in person)

**This is a volunteering position. NLA will provide free accommodation in a shared flat and a small monthly stipend.**
