jobs.title: Supply Chain Coordinator
jobs.body:
**BACKGROUND:**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) is one of the world's leading crisis response agencies, providing life-saving assistance and supporting recovery and reconstruction for people affected by war and natural disasters. Active in public health, education, livelihoods, women's empowerment, youth development, and protection and promotion of rights, IRC assists people from harm to home.

The IRC was registered in Uganda in mid-1998 and implements rehabilitation activities in the sectors of Child and Youth Protection and development, Health, Economic recovery and Development and women protection and empowerment as well as contributing to the response to the Southern Sudanese Refugee situation. IRC Uganda has a head office in Kampala, field offices in Lamwo, Kiryandongo, Moroto, Kyaka and West Nile.

**SCOPE OF WORK:**

Supply Chain Coordinator is a key position to the success and delivery of quality programs. Supply Chain entails all the systems and functions necessary to implement programs effectively, inclusive of planning, procurement, inventory management, constructions property and asset management as well as vehicle and fleet management. The Supply Chain Coordinator is accountable for the design, planning, execution, and monitoring of supply chain activities at the country level.

**The Supply Chain Coordinator will:**

- Collaborate and coordinate with Programs and Finance to ensure integrated and harmonized operational systems.
- Collaborate with the Deputy Director Finance to ensure that internal controls are met with minimum bureaucracy.
- Work with Field Office Supply Chain Staff and Field Managers/Senior Field Coordinator to ensure effectiveness, countrywide uniformity of Supply Chain structure and implementation of the IRC’s standard operating policies and procedures.
- Implement job and site-specific trainings to ensure that Supply Chain staff possess the knowledge and skills commensurate with their responsibilities.

**SPECIFIC DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:**

The Supply Chain Coordinator is an integral member of the country management team and reports directly to the Senior Field Management Coordinator. This position is responsible for the management and delivery of effective Supply Chain support throughout the country program in compliance with IRC and donor regulations. Key responsibilities include procurement, inventory, construction management.

**Supply Chain Planning**

The Supply Chain Coordinator is responsible for supply chain activities planning. The role holder coordinates closely with internal and external stakeholders to develop supply chain plans to support program implementation. Supply chain plans include procurement plans, warehousing plans, transport plans, staffing plans, distribution plans and training plans.

- Prepare consolidated annual procurement plans and develop country program sourcing strategy for all active and pipeline grants in collaboration with program Coordinators and Managers,
- Ensure that the program team develops distribution plan for supplies and assets of closed grants in the warehouses.
- Proactively Participate in the Project Cycle Meetings, including Project design, project planning, Project opening, project review, project close-out and project learning meetings to ensure that supply chain related issues are well articulated to all stakeholders and resolved for successful project delivery. Coordinate with supply chain field staff to ensure that there is sufficient space in the warehouses before sending program supplies to the field sites.
- Ensure supply chain staff training and capacity building plans are developed as the PMEs and incorporated into the budgets.
- Ensure that supply chain department has sufficient staff and roles and responsibilities of each have clear job description.

**Procurement Management**

The Supply Chain Coordinator is accountable for developing country procurement strategies. The Supply Chain Coordinator owns, manages, and drives IRC in country procurement strategies, policies, and procedures. The position holder ensures all country program procurement needs are met on time in accordance with Global Supply Chain and donor standards

- Ensure compliance to IRC and donor policies in the procurement of program supplies and assets.
- Ensure review and execution of procurement contracts in a timely way.
- Lead market surveys and analyses by collecting, organizing, and analyzing market data, share results with program team, Field Coordinators and Managers on a regular basis.
- Ensure the bidding process by developing and implementing the office sourcing strategy, managing the Master Agreements and RFQ/RFP Processes, and completing a purchase request process
- Develop negotiation strategies and manage negotiations for high spent categories
- Proactively engage with Programs, Suppliers, Partners, NGOs, logistics clusters and other stakeholders to ensure good coordination and adequate information sharing to address common concerns or risks affecting the market
- Organize procurement trainings sessions for procurement / tender committees in the field offices and non - supply chain staff if deemed necessary.
- Identifying fraud and corruption red flags and address them in a timely manner.
- Establish reasonable and appropriate lead-time for all procurement of program supplies and delivery of goods to the program sites.
- Make sure the supply chain monthly and quarterly reports are analyzed and communicated to stakeholders, including key actions to be taken and submitted on time to the leadership team.
- Review of SC Key performance indicators (KPIs) and set improvement plans.
- Ensure all vendors’ history and performance Information, is properly documented and procurement transaction files and supplier files maintained in accordance with applicable Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs). Work with Field Offices Supply Chain staff and Field Managers/SFC and Managers to ensure effectiveness, countrywide uniformity of supply chain structure and implementation of the IRC’s standard operating policies and procedures

**Inventory Management**

The Supply Chain Coordinator is responsible for managing and controlling all inventory and warehouses operation in the country program and to ensure excellent record keeping, in accordance with inventory standard operating procedures and controls as provided by Global Supply Chain. The Supply Chain Coordinator will:

- Ensure appropriate warehouse site selection, and Implementation of warehouse safety/security requirements
- Ensure effective handling of inventory, including drug storage, cold chain, buffer stock, contributions in kind (CIK) and food commodities
- Set up stock reorder levels as per the IRC standard operating procedures and donor requirements
- Implement the IRC inventory policies for all project Items including cycle count, investigate discrepancies and develop action plan to address them.
- Produce grants ending and year ending inventory report during each grant closing and end of fiscal year in timely manner.
- Coordinate inventory disposal procedures as per host government, IRC and donor rules and regulations

**Assets Management**

The Supply Chain Coordinator is responsible for the procurement, maintenance, safekeeping and record on all IRC country program assets and equipment. The Supply Chain Coordinator is responsible for all aspects of the administrative, financial, capital and operations of asset management in accordance with IRC and donors’ rules and regulations.

- Conduct Asset needs assessment
- Develop Assets maintenance plans as per IRC policies, including repairs tracking and insurance coverage process.
- Ensure spot-checks are done systematically on a quarterly basis, any discrepancies documented and reported; and action to address the root causes developed for all IRC assets, inventory, and equipment.
- Handle asset and property disposal, including auction management as per the IRC asset disposal process
- Ensure that the grant inventory and asset report is accurate, regularly produced, reviewed, and approved before the Grant closing date.

**Logistics and Fleet Management**

The Supply Chain Coordinator is responsible for overseeing and coordinating all IRC country fleet transportation and Logistics activities to ensure that all IRC fleet operations are conducted with adherence to IRC Fleet management policies and procedures including vehicles procurement, vehicles movement, maintenance, and reporting accuracy. The Supply Chain Coordinator:

- Implements IRC global Fleet Management policies and procedures and/or develops country specific fleet management policies and procedures needed to comply with local regulations and ensure that they are implemented and followed in all IRC in country offices.
- Ensure that legal status (customs clearance, registration, licenses, insurance) are up to date.
- Conduct transport needs assessments
- Develop and monitor fleet movement plans, vehicle maintenance, driver assignment, vehicle safety, and fuel consumption.
- Analyzes fleet spent, including fuel consumption and maintenance costs and produces reports on a periodic basis to facilitate strategic decisions and ensure fleet optimization
- Regular issuance, review, and usage of vehicle monthly reports to inform strategic decision-making process.

**Compliance and Ethics**

The supply Chain Coordinator is responsible for identifying and analyzing compliance risk in supply chain process, developing, and implementing strong procurement controls. The Supply Chain Coordinator:

- Identifies and sets mitigation plans to manage Supply Chain risks, including identification of red flags, and implementing internal and external audit corrective action plans to ensure all supply chain activities are conducted in an ethical manner.
- Ensures compliance to IRC and donor policies in the procurement and distribution of program supplies and assets.
- Ensure that assessments of supply chain policies, procedures, controls, and performance are conducted, and any deviations addressed in the country program where designated
- Implement and sustain segregation of duties in procurement and other related functions.
- Develop and support implementation of post-audit corrective action plans and other improvement plans.
- Familiarize with various donor regulations.
- Maintain and update donor guidelines related to Supply Chain field (procurement, asset, etc).
- Update as required of the IRC standards in terms of assets/equipment to be purchased.
- Finalize Procurement Plans for all grants.
- Ensure all donor reports for assets are completed and submitted to the Grants Department on time.

**Staff Management and Development:**

The Supply Chain Coordinator is responsible and accountable for overseeing all supply chain learning and development initiatives in the country by:

- Leading the recruitment of new staff through effective utilization of the IRC supply chain competency matrix.
- Ensuring that the supply chain department is well staffed and the roles and responsibilities of each have a clear job description.
- Ensuring each team members' objectives are set following the organizational unit vision as well as operations context(s).
- Identify staffing and/or skill gaps and see that these gaps/needs are filled and support the recruitment of all Supply Chain staff and provide day-to-day supervision of department.
- Provide feedback through regular performance evaluations.
- Ensure that any staff discipline follows a progressive methodology which provides for clear and structured improvement.
- Ensuring assessment of supply chain staff competency and training gaps and develop appropriate intervention programs
- Coordinating training and maintaining training records
- Develop long term plans for continued quality leadership by providing staff development and succession plans

**Pharmaceutical Supply Chain**

- In collaboration with the health team, ensure forecasts and supply planning for pharmaceutical supply are created for all health projects by project start date.
- With the guidance and support from global pharma leadership, develop a supply strategy for the supply of pharmaceuticals (global, regional, national) including freight.
- Ensure the IRC standard pharmaceutical inventory tracking tool is in place and accurately maintained in each location
- Ensure implementation of the IRC pharmaceutical quality assurance policy, associated SOPs, and procedures for Cold Chain best practice in the warehouse and in local transport.
- Ensure adequate drugs management and transportation tool and materials are available for the effective management of drugs.

**Construction Management**

- Supervise construction consultant & construction engineers
- Map construction works for all grants and making sure the procurement process is started and completed on time
- Ensure all due processes like technical drawings and Bills of Quantities (BOQ) approval are done by relevant Authorities before commencement of the procurement process.
- Work with the supervising engineer to ensure timely, cost effective and quality delivery of the works standard as per the specification, requirement, and standard of IRC & its funding agency.
- Ensure compliance with IRC Safety policies and procedures in construction.
- Develop construction tracker and regular update as work progresses

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Position Reports to**: Senior Field Management Coordinator

**Position directly supervises**: Supply Chain Manager, Construction Consultant, Construction Engineer, Transport Manager, Supply Chain Officer, Supply Chain Systems Officer.

**Other Internal and/or external contacts:**

**Internal:** Regular relationships with HQ, regional and country Supply Chain staff at all levels, Senior Field Management Coordinator, Country Director, and interacts with IRC Program departments

**External**: May Serve as IRC Supply Chain representative in outside meetings, logistics clusters, other non-governmental organizations, inter-agency groups and foundations.

**REQUIREMENTS:**

**Education:**

- Master’s Degree in Procurement and Logistics or relevant field required.
- Advanced professional certification in supply chain management and/or emergency response management are strongly preferred.

**Work Experience:**

- 8 years of progressive Supply Chain professional experience, with 3 years at a similar level of responsibility
- Experience working in an ERP environment
- Experience with Data Analysis
- Demonstrated ability to develop and roll-out supply chain policy and SOPs.
- Clear training and mentoring ability.
- Experience working with a diverse portfolio of Donors and knowledge of specific donor guidelines.

**Leadership and management skills:**

- Minimum of 5 years of progressive people management/leadership experience, including direct supervision of multi-disciplinary and/or geographically dispersed teams and demonstrated experience leading and managing teams in a complex, matrixed, or emergency response environment, including staff recruitment, performance management, and capacity building.
- Strong leadership and people management skills, with a proven ability to lead, motivate, and hold accountable multi-disciplinary teams across multiple field locations, and Proven change management skills, including the ability to build staff capacity and support succession planning within the Supply Chain function.

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:**

- A high degree of flexibility and ability to work under sometimes acute hardship conditions against tight deadlines.
- Strong computer and communication equipment skills, including in Microsoft Office applications.
- Strong collaborator and influencer with effective interpersonal and analytical skills who can work seamlessly across countries, cultures, and organizational units
- Able to work effectively in a highly matrixed structure.
- Strong financial management and budgeting skills.
- Excellent training and coaching ability.
- Ability to travel to remote field offices.

**Language Skills:**

Fluency in English is required.

**WORK ENVIRONMENT:**

**Security:** Kampala is Security Level 2 - yellow.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

jobs.title: Senior Manager Global Procurement-Corporate and Professional Services
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
jobs.body:
**Organizational Background**

Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the International Rescue Committee (IRC) helps people whose lives and livelihoods are shattered by conflict and disaster, including the climate crisis, to survive, recover, and rebuild their futures. Headquartered in New York and London, the IRC operates in more than 40 countries and supports refugee resettlement through 25 offices across the United States. Our work is grounded in bold leadership, innovation, partnership, and accountability to the people we serve.

**Role Purpose**

The Senior Manager, Global Procurement (GP) - Corporate and Professional Services provides strategic leadership across Travel, Translation, Insurance, Cash, Financial and HR Services, including payroll and benefits administration, learning and development platforms, recruitment and RPO, and global mobility and relocation.

The role establishes disciplined, forward-looking category management across this portfolio: translating business demand into sourcing strategies, shaping competitive markets, negotiating high-value agreements, and building supplier ecosystems that improve value, service quality, risk management, and staff experience. As the Senior Manager within GP for these categories, the postholder influences decisions across People & Culture, Safety & Security, Finance, Legal, Risk & Compliance, and country programs.

**Key Accountabilities**

**1. Category Strategy and Portfolio Leadership**

- Own and execute multi-year category strategies for Travel, Translation, Insurance, Cash, HR Services, and additional corporate and professional services categories as assigned.
- Convert spend, demand, market, supplier, and risk insights into clear category plans, sourcing priorities, value targets, and implementation roadmaps.
- Create fit-for-purpose sourcing guide for each category, including market intelligence, pricing and commercial models, contracting approaches, evaluation criteria, and negotiation levers.
- Build an integrated pipeline with business owners, aligning sourcing activity to contract expiries, renewal windows, benefits cycles, and operational priorities.
- Identify and deliver measurable value through cost optimization, demand management, service improvement, risk reduction, and a stronger employee experience.

**2. Strategic Sourcing and Commercial Delivery**

- Lead complex, high-value sourcing initiatives from strategy and market engagement through RFx, evaluation, negotiation, award, and implementation.
- Design sourcing and negotiation strategies that strengthen competition, improve commercial terms, and reflect the operational and regulatory realities of IRC's global footprint.
- Establish robust evaluation governance, ensuring transparent decision-making, clear stakeholder accountability, and complete audit trails.
- Advise business owners on specifications, statements of work, service levels, pricing structures, and contract models that drive performance and protect IRC's interests.
- Lead commercial escalations and resolve material supplier, service, and contractual issues in partnership with Legal, Finance, Risk & Compliance, People and Culture, and operational stakeholders.

**3. Supplier Strategy and Performance**

- Develop resilient supplier pool through framework agreements, pre-qualified panels, strategic partnerships, and appropriate regional or global coverage models.
- Segment suppliers by value, criticality, and risk; apply differentiated governance and relationship-management approaches across the portfolio.
- Set performance expectations and lead structured business reviews using service, cost, risk, innovation, and stakeholder-experience measures.
- Drive supplier accountability, corrective action, and continuous improvement, while identifying opportunities for innovation and stronger market capability.
- Evaluate and document single-source or waiver recommendations when competition is not viable, ensuring a defensible rationale and full policy compliance.

**4. Stakeholder Leadership and Business Partnership**

- Act as the principal Global Procurement partner to People & Culture, Safety & Security, and other corporate functions that depend on the assigned categories.
- Influence senior stakeholders with evidence-based recommendations on market options, supplier strategy, commercial trade-offs, risk, and total value.
- Translate functional priorities into executable procurement plans, creating clarity on scope, roles, timelines, decisions, and dependencies.
- Partner with Safety & Security on travel duty of care and traveler risk-management requirements, ensuring supplier and contracting strategies support organizational obligations.
- Build procurement capability among stakeholders by promoting early engagement, disciplined planning, and consistent use of category and sourcing standards.

**5. Governance, Risk, and Performance**

- Ensure all sourcing and supplier-management activity complies with IRC policies, donor requirements, delegated authorities, and audit standards.
- Embed privacy, information-security, ethical, and regulatory requirements into sourcing and contracting, with particular focus on HR and Insurance providers handling sensitive personal data.
- Maintain accurate spend, contract, pipeline, savings, risk, and supplier-performance data; use insights to guide priorities and demonstrate portfolio impact.
- Keep sourcing decisions and contract records complete, current, and audit-ready.
- Contribute category expertise and market insight to enterprise-wide procurement transformation and continuous-improvement initiatives.

**Person Specification**

**Essential**

- Bachelor's degree in supply chain, business administration, or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience.
- CIPS Level 4 or higher, or an equivalent procurement qualification.
- At least seven years of progressively responsible procurement experience, including substantial ownership of category management and strategic sourcing.
- Demonstrated success leading complex competitive sourcing, multi-supplier evaluations, commercial negotiations, and contract awards.
- Strong commercial judgment and a track record of improving value, supplier performance, and risk outcomes.
- Ability to influence senior stakeholders, navigate competing priorities, and convert business requirements into practical sourcing strategies.
- Strong analytical capability across spend analysis, market assessment, business-case development, and performance reporting.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present complex issues and recommendations clearly.

**Desirable**

- Master's degree in a relevant field.
- Direct category experience in travel, insurance, HR/BPO, language services, or other corporate and professional services.
- Procurement experience in an NGO or nonprofit environment, including familiarity with donor compliance frameworks.
- Working knowledge of Spanish, or Arabic.

**Professional Competencies**

- Strategic and commercial thinking
- Influence and stakeholder leadership
- Market and supplier insight
- Negotiation and decision quality
- Risk awareness and integrity
- Execution discipline and accountability
- Collaboration across cultures and geographies

jobs.title: Ebola Response Director
jobs.body:
*Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, and the vacancy may close before the advertised deadline if the position is filled.*

**Background:**

Responding to the world’s worst humanitarian crises in a great variety of roles, the International Rescue Committee’s staff is a force for humanity and hope. If you’re skilled and passionate, we would like to add your energy to ours.

Through its Emergency Unit (EmU), the IRC is one of the world’s largest humanitarian agencies, leading rapid emergency responses that provide life-saving assistance, early recovery, and stabilization support to people affected by conflict, displacement, natural disasters, and complex emergencies across multiple contexts worldwide. We are committed to innovation, agility, and strong partnerships to deliver timely and effective humanitarian action.

Active in public health, education in emergencies, livelihoods, women's empowerment, youth development, and protection and promotion of rights, we assist people from harm to home. The IRC recognizes that people affected by crisis and the actors closest to them are best placed, have the right, and should have the power and resources to respond and drive lasting change. We commit to increasing the share of funding channeled to local actors in emergencies, ask ‘Why not partner?’ whenever we plan programming, and partner as equals.

**Context:**

The Ministry of Public Health of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) declared the country's 17th Ebola outbreak on May 15, 2026, following laboratory confirmation of Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) in Ituri Province. On May 17, 2026, WHO declared the outbreak a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC), and it has since become the largest Ebola outbreak ever reported in DRC and the fastest-expanding on record. The outbreak is unfolding in a highly complex humanitarian and security context marked by chronic insecurity, armed group activity, repeated population displacement, and high levels of cross-border movement, particularly with Uganda and South Sudan.

The IRC is supporting containment of the outbreak in Ituri and North Kivu. IRC's primary focus is to support existing primary health care (PHC) facilities to ensure safe continuity of services, strengthen infection prevention and control (IPC) practices and infrastructure, raise community awareness of behaviors that limit further spread, and reinforce the protective environment, including through MHPSS support.

**Scope of Work:**

The Ebola Response Director (ERD) will lead IRC's emergency response to the Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreak in DRC, based in Bunia, driving a fast, high-quality, accountable operation that ensures continuity of primary health care, strengthens infection prevention and control, and reinforces community protection in line with IRC's strategic priorities.

The ERD will oversee all operational, financial, and programmatic aspects of the response, including supply chain, safety and security, finance, people and culture, partnerships, and program delivery. S/he will report to the Emergency Unit's ERMT Lead (Emergency Response Management Team), with a dotted line to the DRC Country Director (CD) for coordination on critical incidents, security, legal, donor, and media matters — shifting to a full reporting line into the CD once handover to the DRC Country Program is complete. As IRC's external face on the response, the ERD will be a compelling communicator with government officials, donors, UN agencies, and coordination bodies, driving visibility and funding for the response. S/he will also ensure the programmatic strategy is clear and effectively implemented, and participate in the DRC Country Program SMT to keep the response aligned with, and eventually integrated into, the broader country program.

Success in this role demands a strong, resilient leader who can motivate and steady teams operating in a highly insecure, high-pressure environment, paired with excellent communication and program implementation skills. The ERD is directly responsible for the response's overall coordination and strategic direction, oversight and coaching of the Ebola Response department leads, effective management of emergency funding, and timely reporting to donors, the CD, and the ERMT.

**Main Responsibilities:**

***Leadership and Representation***

- Serve as IRC's key representative for the Ebola response, coordinating with the DRC CD and wider country program as needed, and co-lead all donor and media engagement related to the response with the CD.
- Develop and maintain relationships with donors, UN agencies, INGOs, MOH, and local partners to promote effective collaboration and raise the visibility of IRC's response.
- Participate in DRC Country Program SMT meetings and maintain regular coordination check-ins with the CD to ensure alignment with the broader country program.
- Oversee safety and security aspects of the Ebola response, immediately reporting risks, incidents, or concerns to the CD and the ERMT.
- Join the Emergency Unit's weekly ERMT meetings and ad hoc Crisis Calls, ensuring production of a weekly Emergency Situation Report.
- Champion a culture of effective, respectful partnerships, promoting partner-led programming in line with IRC's "why not partner?" and "partner as equals" approach.

***Strategic Direction and Program Oversight***

- Lead and contribute to the execution of IRC's strategic response plan for Ebola, ensuring it reflects partnership considerations and active engagement of local partners in design and delivery.
- Oversee emergency program implementation across the Ebola response.
- Directly supervise the Ebola Response department Leads (Program Lead, Supply Chain, Finance, People and Culture, and Security) with the Program Lead further overseeing technical program coordinators, grants, and partnerships.
- Support strategic decision-making on program design, proposals, and budget development for new Ebola response funding, including appropriate budget allocation to support partners.
- Ensure staffing structures and partnership risk management are sized and aligned to the emergency context.
- Work closely with the DRC Country Program to ensure a smooth handover and integration of the response into the broader CP portfolio at time of transition.

***Stewardship and Operational Leadership***

- Drive operational excellence, efficiency, and cost-effectiveness across all Ebola Response functions, proactively identifying and eliminating redundant processes.
- Oversee the development, deployment, and utilization of financial and operational policies, procedures, and systems to ensure compliance with IRC and donor requirements.
- Ensure responsiveness and appropriate levels of in-person and remote support to all offices, particularly in the areas of people and culture, finance, and supply chain.
- Provide timely and effective oversight of the country program's financial position.
- Maintain effective and coordinated budget monitoring processes for both grant funds and discretionary funds.

***Organizational Culture and Communication***

- Role model IRC's Core Values, the "IRC Way - Global Standards for Professional Conduct," and Inclusion Principles through personal commitment and accountability.
- Foster an open, inclusive, and respectful team environment where staff feel valued and communication is honest and productive.
- Model accountability and commitment to safeguarding, including PSEAH, of all staff, partners, clients and others with whom we work; build a culture of safeguarding, where our clients and staff trust IRC and feel safe raising concerns.
- Hold all leaders accountable to their roles and areas of responsibilities for delivery in the Safeguarding Minimum Standards; dedicate and facilitate regular reviews of Safeguarding Minimum Standards progress, barriers, enablers and culture within the response to plan for action and investment needed.
- Maintain open and regular communication with DRC leadership, regional management staff, regional technical advisors, and HQ departmental staff to ensure alignment, support, and collaboration.

***People Leadership***

- Oversee the management, coaching, and development of national and international staff working in the Ebola Response to build a team of skilled, committed, engaged, and motivated staff.
- Supervise and mentor direct-report staff, including communicating clear expectations, setting performance objectives, providing regular and timely feedback, and leading performance reviews.
- Hold high-quality 1:1 meetings with each direct report on a regular and predictable basis, at least bi-weekly, focusing equally on interpersonal exchange and work priorities.
- Promote and monitor staff care and well-being, ensuring systems and practices where work supports life and modelling healthy work-life balance practices.
- Support appropriate interventions in response to identified staff care needs.
- Offer leadership support for successful adherence by all staff to IRC's country, regional, and global policies and procedures.

**Key Working Relationships:**

- Position Reports to: Emergency Unit Emergency Response Management Team (ERMT) Lead, with a dotted line to the Country Director, DRC, for coordination and information-sharing on critical incidents, security, legal, donor, and media matters. Reporting will shift to Country Director when the response management handover is completed.
- Position Directly Supervises: Ebola Response Program Lead, Ebola Supply Chain Coordinator(s), Ebola Response Deputy Director Finance, Ebola People & Culture Lead and Ebola Humanitarian Access, Safety and Security Lead
- Works Closely with: IRC DRC Country Program Senior Management Team (CD, DDP, and DDO)

**Job Requirements:**

- University degree in related field or equivalent experience preferred.
- 8 years’ experience leading complex on site emergency health response projects and/or programs requiring extensive judgment and interpretation. Diverse geographical professional experience preferred.
- Demonstrated ability to influence peer agencies, local government and community leaders to work effectively towards a common and agreed upon result.
- Demonstrated ability to evaluate and implement best practices and processes affecting multiple technical specialties to achieve rapid, consistent and high-quality outcomes.
- Experience developing, resourcing and leading large budget, complex projects spanning multiple technical specialties.
- Proven track-record of excellent management and leadership skills. Ability to set an example of leadership for staff in adherence to IRC management policies.
- High degree of comfort and successful track record in supervising in matrixed environments.
- Demonstrated commitment to inclusion and fair treatment of staff, and ability to identify and address barriers to inclusion for marginalized groups in emergency response.
- Experience working with diverse teams and communities, including women, youth, persons with disabilities, and other groups at risk of exclusion.
- Excellent verbal and written skills in English and French required.

*Les candidatures seront examinées au fur et à mesure de leur réception, et l’offre pourra être clôturée avant la date limite annoncée si le poste est pourvu.*

**Présentation :**

Répondant aux pires crises humanitaires du monde dans une grande variété de fonctions, le personnel du Comité international de secours (IRC) est une force au service de l'humanité et de l'espoir. Si vous êtes compétent(e) et passionné(e), nous serions heureux d'ajouter votre énergie à la nôtre.

Par le biais de son unité des urgences (EmU), l'IRC est l'une des plus grandes agences humanitaires au monde, menant des interventions d'urgence rapides qui apportent une aide vitale, un redressement précoce et un soutien à la stabilisation aux personnes touchées par les conflits, les déplacements, les catastrophes naturelles et les urgences complexes dans de multiples contextes à travers le monde. Nous nous engageons à innover, à agir avec agilité et à établir des partenariats solides afin de fournir une action humanitaire rapide et efficace.

Actif dans les domaines de la santé publique, de l'éducation en situation d'urgence, des moyens de subsistance, de l'autonomisation des femmes, du développement des jeunes et de la protection et de la promotion des droits, nous accompagnons les personnes du danger vers un foyer. L'IRC reconnaît que les personnes touchées par une crise et les acteurs les plus proches d'elles sont les mieux placés, ont le droit et doivent avoir le pouvoir et les ressources nécessaires pour répondre à la crise et impulser un changement durable. Nous nous engageons à accroître la part du financement destiné aux acteurs locaux dans les situations d'urgence, à nous demander « Pourquoi ne pas nouer un partenariat ? » chaque fois que nous planifions un programme, et à établir des partenariats d'égal à égal.

**Contexte:**

Le ministère de la Santé publique de la République démocratique du Congo (RDC) a déclaré la 17e épidémie d'Ebola du pays le 15 mai 2026, après la confirmation en laboratoire de la maladie à virus Bundibugyo (MVB) dans la province de l'Ituri. Le 17 mai 2026, l'OMS a déclaré l'épidémie urgence de santé publique de portée internationale (USPPI), et elle est depuis devenue la plus grande épidémie d'Ebola jamais signalée en RDC et celle qui progresse le plus rapidement jamais enregistrée. L'épidémie se déroule dans un contexte humanitaire et sécuritaire hautement complexe, marqué par une insécurité chronique, l'activité de groupes armés, des déplacements de population répétés et des mouvements transfrontaliers importants, notamment avec l'Ouganda et le Soudan du Sud.

L'IRC appuie l'endiguement de l'épidémie dans l'Ituri et le Nord-Kivu. L'action prioritaire de l'IRC consiste à soutenir les structures de soins de santé primaires (SSP) existantes afin d'assurer la continuité des services en toute sécurité, à renforcer les pratiques et les infrastructures de prévention et de contrôle des infections (PCI), à sensibiliser les communautés aux comportements qui limitent la propagation, et à renforcer l'environnement protecteur, notamment par un soutien en santé mentale et psychosociale (SMSPS).

**Portée du poste :**

Le/la Directeur/Directrice de la riposte Ebola (DRE) dirigera la riposte d'urgence de l'IRC à l'épidémie de maladie à virus Bundibugyo (MVB) en RDC, basé(e) à Bunia, en pilotant une opération rapide, de haute qualité et responsable qui assure la continuité des soins de santé primaires, renforce la prévention et le contrôle des infections, et consolide la protection communautaire, conformément aux priorités stratégiques de l'IRC.

Le/la DRE supervisera l'ensemble des aspects opérationnels, financiers et programmatiques de la riposte, notamment la chaîne d'approvisionnement, la sûreté et la sécurité, les finances, les ressources humaines et la culture, les partenariats et la mise en œuvre des programmes. Il/elle rendra compte au/à la Responsable de l'ERMT de l'unité des urgences (Équipe de gestion de la riposte d'urgence), avec un lien fonctionnel avec le/la Directeur/Directrice pays (DP) de la RDC pour la coordination sur les incidents critiques, la sécurité, les questions juridiques, les donateurs et les médias — ce lien évoluant vers une ligne hiérarchique pleine et entière vers le DP une fois la transition vers le programme pays de la RDC achevée. En tant que visage extérieur de l'IRC pour la riposte, le/la DRE sera un(e) communicateur/communicatrice convaincant(e) auprès des responsables gouvernementaux, des donateurs, des agences des Nations Unies et des instances de coordination, afin d'accroître la visibilité et le financement de la riposte. Il/elle veillera également à ce que la stratégie programmatique soit claire et efficacement mise en œuvre, et participera à l'équipe de direction (SMT) du programme pays de la RDC afin de maintenir la riposte alignée avec, puis à terme intégrée dans, le programme pays plus large.

Réussir dans ce poste exige un(e) leader solide et résilient(e), capable de motiver et de stabiliser des équipes évoluant dans un environnement hautement instable et sous forte pression, doté(e) d'excellentes compétences en communication et en mise en œuvre de programmes. Le/la DRE est directement responsable de la coordination générale et de l'orientation stratégique de la riposte, de la supervision et de l'accompagnement des responsables de département de la riposte Ebola, de la gestion efficace du financement d'urgence, ainsi que de la production de rapports en temps voulu aux donateurs, au DP et à l'ERMT.

**Principales responsabilités:**

***Direction et représentation***

- Assurer la représentation clé de l'IRC pour la riposte Ebola, en coordination avec le DP de la RDC et le programme pays au sens large selon les besoins, et co-diriger avec le DP l'ensemble des relations avec les donateurs et les médias liées à la riposte.
- Développer et entretenir des relations avec les donateurs, les agences des Nations Unies, les ONG internationales, le ministère de la Santé et les partenaires locaux afin de promouvoir une collaboration efficace et d'accroître la visibilité de la riposte de l'IRC.
- Participer aux réunions de l'équipe de direction (SMT) du programme pays de la RDC et maintenir des points de coordination réguliers avec le DP afin d'assurer l'alignement avec le programme pays au sens large.
- Superviser les aspects de sûreté et de sécurité de la riposte Ebola, en signalant immédiatement tout risque, incident ou préoccupation au DP et à l'ERMT.
- Participer aux réunions hebdomadaires de l'ERMT de l'unité des urgences et aux appels de crise ad hoc, en veillant à la production d'un rapport de situation d'urgence hebdomadaire.
- Promouvoir une culture de partenariats efficaces et respectueux, en encourageant les programmes pilotés par les partenaires conformément à l'approche « Pourquoi ne pas nouer un partenariat ? » et « partenaires d'égal à égal » de l'IRC.

***Orientation stratégique et supervision des programmes***

- Diriger et contribuer à la mise en œuvre du plan de riposte stratégique de l'IRC pour Ebola, en veillant à ce qu'il reflète les considérations de partenariat et l'engagement actif des partenaires locaux dans la conception et la mise en œuvre.
- Superviser la mise en œuvre du programme d'urgence dans l'ensemble de la riposte Ebola.
- Superviser directement les responsables de département de la riposte Ebola (Responsable du programme, Chaîne d'approvisionnement, Finances, Ressources humaines et Culture, et Sécurité), le Responsable du programme supervisant en outre les coordinateurs techniques de programme, les subventions et les partenariats.
- Appuyer la prise de décisions stratégiques sur la conception des programmes, les propositions et l'élaboration des budgets pour les nouveaux financements de la riposte Ebola, y compris l'allocation budgétaire appropriée en soutien aux partenaires.
- Veiller à ce que les structures de personnel et la gestion des risques liés aux partenariats soient dimensionnées et adaptées au contexte d'urgence.
- Travailler en étroite collaboration avec le programme pays de la RDC afin d'assurer une transition et une intégration harmonieuses de la riposte dans le portefeuille plus large du programme pays au moment de la transition.

***Gestion responsable et direction opérationnelle***

- Favoriser l'excellence opérationnelle, l'efficience et la rentabilité dans l'ensemble des fonctions de la riposte Ebola, en identifiant et en éliminant de manière proactive les processus redondants.
- Superviser l'élaboration, le déploiement et l'utilisation des politiques, procédures et systèmes financiers et opérationnels afin de garantir la conformité avec les exigences de l'IRC et des donateurs.
- Veiller à la réactivité et à un niveau approprié de soutien en présentiel et à distance à l'ensemble des bureaux, en particulier dans les domaines des ressources humaines et de la culture, des finances et de la chaîne d'approvisionnement.
- Assurer une supervision rapide et efficace de la situation financière du programme pays.
- Maintenir des processus de suivi budgétaire efficaces et coordonnés, tant pour les fonds de subvention que pour les fonds discrétionnaires.

***Culture organisationnelle et communication***

- Incarner les valeurs fondamentales de l'IRC, le « IRC Way - Normes mondiales de conduite professionnelle » et les principes d'inclusion, par un engagement personnel et une responsabilisation.
- Favoriser un environnement d'équipe ouvert, inclusif et respectueux, où le personnel se sent valorisé et où la communication est honnête et productive.
- Incarner la responsabilisation et l'engagement envers la protection, y compris la PSEAH (prévention de l'exploitation et des abus sexuels et du harcèlement), de l'ensemble du personnel, des partenaires, des clients et de toute autre personne avec qui nous travaillons ; bâtir une culture de protection où nos clients et notre personnel font confiance à l'IRC et se sentent en sécurité pour signaler leurs préoccupations.
- Tenir l'ensemble des responsables pour comptables de leurs rôles et domaines de responsabilité dans la mise en œuvre des normes minimales de protection ; consacrer du temps et faciliter des revues régulières des progrès, des obstacles, des facteurs favorables et de la culture en matière de normes minimales de protection au sein de la riposte, afin de planifier les actions et les investissements nécessaires.
- Maintenir une communication ouverte et régulière avec la direction de la RDC, le personnel de gestion régional, les conseillers techniques régionaux et le personnel des départements du siège, afin de garantir l'alignement, le soutien et la collaboration.

***Direction des ressources humaines***

- Superviser la gestion, l'accompagnement et le développement du personnel national et international travaillant au sein de la riposte Ebola, afin de constituer une équipe compétente, engagée, impliquée et motivée.
- Superviser et accompagner le personnel relevant directement de sa responsabilité, notamment en communiquant des attentes claires, en fixant des objectifs de performance, en fournissant des retours réguliers et rapides, et en menant les évaluations de performance.
- Tenir des entretiens individuels de qualité avec chaque collaborateur/collaboratrice direct(e) sur une base régulière et prévisible, au moins toutes les deux semaines, en accordant une attention égale aux échanges interpersonnels et aux priorités de travail.
- Promouvoir et suivre le bien-être et l'attention portée au personnel, en veillant à la mise en place de systèmes et de pratiques où le travail soutient la vie, et en modélisant de saines pratiques d'équilibre entre vie professionnelle et vie privée.
- Soutenir les interventions appropriées en réponse aux besoins identifiés en matière d'attention portée au personnel.
- Offrir un appui de direction pour permettre à l'ensemble du personnel de respecter avec succès les politiques et procédures pays, régionales et mondiales de l'IRC.

**Principales relations de travail:**

- **Relève de:** Le/la Responsable de l'ERMT (Équipe de gestion de la riposte d'urgence) de l'unité des urgences, avec un lien fonctionnel avec le/la Directeur/Directrice pays de la RDC pour la coordination et le partage d'informations sur les incidents critiques, la sécurité, les questions juridiques, les donateurs et les médias. La ligne hiérarchique évoluera vers le/la Directeur/Directrice pays une fois la transition de gestion de la riposte achevée.
- **Supervise directement:** le/la Responsable du programme de riposte Ebola, le/les Coordinateur(s)/Coordinatrice(s) de la chaîne d'approvisionnement Ebola, le/la Directeur/Directrice adjoint(e) Finances de la riposte Ebola, le/la Responsable Ressources humaines et Culture Ebola, et le/la Responsable Accès humanitaire, Sûreté et Sécurité Ebola
- **Travaille en étroite collaboration avec:** l'équipe de direction du programme pays de l'IRC en RDC (DP, DDP et DDO).

**Exigences du poste:**

- Diplôme universitaire dans un domaine pertinent ou expérience équivalente souhaité(e).
- 8 années d'expérience dans la direction de projets et/ou programmes complexes de réponse sanitaire d'urgence sur site, nécessitant un jugement et une interprétation approfondis. Une expérience professionnelle diversifiée sur le plan géographique est préférée.
- Capacité démontrée à influencer les agences homologues, les autorités locales et les leaders communautaires afin de travailler efficacement vers un résultat commun et convenu.
- Capacité démontrée à évaluer et à mettre en œuvre les meilleures pratiques et processus touchant plusieurs spécialités techniques afin d'obtenir des résultats rapides, cohérents et de haute qualité.
- Expérience dans le développement, la mobilisation des ressources et la direction de projets complexes à budget important, couvrant plusieurs spécialités techniques.
- Expérience avérée d'excellentes compétences en gestion et en direction. Capacité à donner l'exemple en matière de direction pour le personnel, dans le respect des politiques de gestion de l'IRC.
- Grande aisance et parcours réussi dans la supervision au sein d'environnements matriciels.
- Engagement démontré en faveur de l'inclusion et du traitement équitable du personnel, et capacité à identifier et à lever les obstacles à l'inclusion pour les groupes marginalisés dans le cadre de la réponse d'urgence.
- Expérience de travail avec des équipes et des communautés diversifiées, y compris les femmes, les jeunes, les personnes en situation de handicap et d'autres groupes exposés au risque d'exclusion.
- Excellentes compétences orales et écrites en anglais et en français requises.

jobs.title: Senior Program Manager, Safety, Health & Wellness
jobs.body:
**Background:**

IRC Arizona operates Health, Safety, and Wellness programming across both the Phoenix and Tucson offices, addressing the health, safety, and stabilization needs of refugees, asylees, survivors of trafficking and torture, and other vulnerable populations. The Health Program addresses vulnerable populations' health needs through medical case management, health education, and public health interventions, working in collaboration with the healthcare sector, public health authorities, medical providers, facilities, universities, and community agencies. The Safety & Wellness Department provides therapeutic services, asylum casework, survivor support, anti-trafficking and victim services, and case management for individuals with acute safety and stabilization needs.

As IRC Arizona continues to rebuild and adapt to changing refugee arrivals, an uncertain federal funding environment, and evolving community needs, there is a growing need for statewide coordination across these programs. Rather than operating independently across Phoenix and Tucson, IRC Arizona can strengthen its statewide impact through a unified Safety, Health, and Wellness strategy that aligns resources, expands partnerships, builds staff capacity, and improves outcomes for clients and communities in both offices.

**Job Overview:**

The Senior Program Manager for Safety, Health & Wellness provides unified, statewide program oversight, staff supervision, partnership development, and grant maintenance for IRC Arizona's Health and Safety & Wellness programs across both Phoenix and Tucson. This position maintains service provision and contract compliance for Therapeutic Services, Asylum Casework, Survivors of Torture, Anti-Trafficking and Victim Services, the Arizona Asylum Network, Preferred Communities, medical case management (Program Initial Resettlement, Matching Grant, and Refugee Support Services), and public health and health literacy programming. This position builds a shared statewide strategy that strengthens program quality, expands partnerships and diversified funding, and coordinates growth and shared learning across both offices, while preserving the ability of each office to respond to its community's distinct needs.

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Statewide Strategy & Coordination**

- Serve as IRC Arizona's statewide point of coordination for Health and Safety & Wellness programming, aligning strategy, tools, and resources across Phoenix and Tucson without centralizing day-to-day office operations.
- Identify statewide and office-specific program priorities and support leadership in decisions about program investment, expansion, consolidation, or redesign.
- Create a shared framework for collaboration and shared program standards that promote consistency and quality while preserving local flexibility.
- Build and disseminate knowledge and analysis of local and national public health, safety, and wellness trends that affect IRC clients; act as IRC Arizona's subject matter expert on these issues.

**Program Oversight & Quality**

- Oversee Health and Safety & Wellness program staff in a manner that supports the exchange of ideas, encourages camaraderie and collaboration, and fosters professional development.
- Design strategies and frameworks to effectively operate programs and coordinate logistics for grant implementation, program subcontracts, and monitoring of grant activities across both offices.
- Implement, monitor, and provide ongoing training on a trauma-informed service model for Health and Safety & Wellness staff.
- Provide appropriate supervision and case coordination to ensure acute client needs are met in a timely and culturally appropriate manner across all programs.
- Monitor provision of services through regular and systematic file reviews, client interviews, and field visits to ensure compliance with donor requirements and delivery of quality services.
- Track budgets, program expenditures, and activities across programs; ensure donor deliverables are met; compile data and draft reports as required by donor and agency specifications.

**Program Development & Community Expansion**

- Support the development of new and expanded programming, including intensive case management, anti-human trafficking and survivor support services, behavioral health and psychosocial support, chronic disease prevention, maternal and child health, healthcare navigation, community health worker initiatives, and health education.
- Identify key stakeholders, partners, resources, donors, and volunteers to support program growth.
- Assess opportunities to responsibly adapt or expand select services to broader underserved populations whose needs overlap with those of IRC's existing clients, consistent with IRC's mission, policies, and operational capacity.
- Coordinate with other IRC teams to create multi-disciplinary approaches to services that facilitate the best possible client outcomes.

**Partnership & Funding Development**

- Build and maintain statewide relationships with state and local health agencies, FQHCs, hospital systems, universities, Medicaid health plans, behavioral health providers, law enforcement, community organizations, and philanthropic partners.
- Develop strategies to enhance community outreach and engage new stakeholders.
- Review, recommend, and write new grant opportunities in alignment with the office strategic action plan and in partnership with the Grants Manager, identifying federal, state, county, municipal, foundation, healthcare, and victim-services funding opportunities.
- Support diversification of funding to reduce dependence on refugee arrival levels or any single government funding stream.

**Staff Supervision & Development**

- Provide direct supervision to program supervisors and staff across the Health and Safety & Wellness departments (see Key Working Relationships).
- Provide coaching, leadership development, technical assistance, and opportunities for cross-office collaboration to strengthen local leadership and staff capacity.
- Provide supervision to AmeriCorps members, MSW interns, and volunteers associated with each program.

**Compliance & Organizational Commitment**

- Ensure coordination with the development and implementation of outreach and training activities to meet program outcomes.
- Participate in senior management meetings and staff development activities as requested.
- Role model IRC values and commitment to mission and clients.
- Comply with all IRC policies, procedures, and protocols, including the IRC Way and Child Safeguarding.
- Other duties as assigned.

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Position Reports to:** Site Director, Tucson

**Position directly supervises:** TBD

**Position indirectly supervises:** N/A

**Indirect Reporting:** N/A

**Other Internal and/or external contacts:**

***Internal:** IRC staff, interns, and volunteers across Phoenix and Tucson*

***External:** Community partners, stakeholder partners, DES, law enforcement, medical providers, employers*

**Job Requirements:**

- Graduate degree in social work, public health, or a related field strongly preferred; undergraduate degree in social work or equivalent work experience required.
- At least 5 years of related professional experience, including proven skills supervising case management staff, grant reporting, and program development; multi-site or cross-program management experience preferred.
- Demonstrated experience with trauma-informed, victim-centered, and/or public health service models.
- Excellent written and spoken English skills; bilingual ability preferred.
- Strong organizational skills and detail oriented; excellent writing and analytical skills.
- Case management, victim's assistance, and/or workforce development experience preferred.
- Ability to effectively communicate and work as a team member with collaborative partners, the community, and clients in a cross-cultural, multi-disciplinary environment.
- Computer literacy; database experience preferred.
- Ability to work independently across multiple sites and be a flexible team player.
- Must have a valid driver's license, active insurance policy, and access to reliable transportation to travel regularly between Phoenix and Tucson offices.
- Must possess or be eligible to receive a fingerprint clearance card.

**Working Environment:**

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and field time within the service delivery area to perform the responsibilities outlined above.
- Regular travel between Phoenix and Tucson required; occasional domestic (non-local) travel required, up to 10%.
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $69,939 - $92,500/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

jobs.title: Regional Research and Learning Coordinator, PlayMatters
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
jobs.body:
**BACKGROUND:**

The International Rescue Committee’s mission is to help people whose lives and livelihoods are shattered by conflict and disaster to survive, recover, and gain control of their future. Founded over 90 years ago, the IRC is a leading humanitarian and development organization with presence in more than 40 countries. Across contexts, the IRC is committed to delivering innovative, high-impact programs tailored to the needs of communities affected by crisis.

The IRC has been working in Uganda since 1998 supporting refugees, vulnerable host communities, and various institutions in the country notably the government, community-based organizations, civil society, and the private sector. Currently, the IRC in Uganda has a presence across five sub-regions and six refugee settlements, implementing programming in the sectors of health, protection and rule of law (PRoL), women’s protection and empowerment (WPE), economic recovery and development (ERD), and education. IRC Uganda also implements cross-cutting programming focused on systems strengthening and accountability to affected persons.

**Job Overview/ Summary:**

PlayMatters 3.0 is a 4-year education initiative (2026-2030) with a goal of improving the well-being and holistic learning outcomes of pre-primary and primary school aged children (ages 3-12+), including those who are affected by conflict and crisis, in Ethiopia, South Sudan, and Uganda by strengthening education systems to deliver quality education services using active teaching and learning through play. The PlayMatters consortium is made up of the IRC, Plan International, and War Child Alliance, in collaboration with national partners and the LEGO foundation. PM prioritizes strengthening education systems to be resilient and scaling impact by working with and through existing systems rather than establishing parallel systems. PM has three main outcomes: Outcome 1: Education systems have increased capacity, uptake, and coordination of Learning through Play (LtP) as a teaching method; Outcome 2: School-aged children in refugee hosting and post-crisis recovery zones have increased access to quality learning opportunities in safe environments; Outcome 3: School-aged children's holistic development is protected in times of acute crisis.

Research and learning are core to PlayMatters, which emphasizes evidence generation and use. The Regional Research and Learning Coordinator will directly support the PlayMatters regional research team to coordinate, design, implement, and disseminate IRC-led PlayMatters research, and support the regional PlayMatters MEL teams to collect, store, analyze, use, and disseminate learning internal and external to the Consortium in Ethiopia, South Sudan, and Uganda. He/she will work closely with the regional team and country-based teams in support of quality evidence-building and actionable learning activities in support of moving PlayMatters forward on the Path to Scale. This role also serves as a key coordination point between the PlayMatters Consortium and its internal (Airbel) and external (the PlayMatters External Evaluator) research partners, ensuring alignment across technical design, implementation timelines, and evidence dissemination.

**Major Responsibilities:**

The Regional Research and Learning Coordinator will lead and support a broad range of PlayMatters research and learning activities, including the following:

**Coordinate and Manage the Operationalization of the Research Agenda and Plan:**

- Coordination and implementation of IRC-led qualitative and quantitative research studies, including a range of formative and implementation research studies that utilize a range of methods and analytical strategies, including:
    - Coordinate with Airbel's research team on study design, data management, budget/level-of-effort alignment, and quality assurance of research outputs;
    - Instrument adaptation and validation, including cognitive pretesting of tools across languages and cultures and the calibration of classroom observation tools across cultural contexts.
    - Programming of tools as needed for the different studies, in preparation for data collection activities, using CommCare and Tangerine primarily.
    - Enumerator trainings as needed for the different studies, in preparation for data collection activities.
    - Data cleaning and analysis, including both quantitative and qualitative analysis as needed.
    - Capacity building for research teams across PlayMatters.

jobs.title: Education and Early Childhood Development (ECD) Technical Advisor – MENAU
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
jobs.body:
**Background**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world’s worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world’s largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions.

The IRC’s Technical Excellence department helps achieve that aim by generating evidence, sharing learning, and providing technical assistance to IRC’s country program staff. Technical Excellence is comprised of Technical Units (TUs) – Health; Economic Recovery and Development (ERD); Education; and Violence Prevention and Response (VPR) – including Global Practice Teams, regionally aligned technical teams, and supporting units for MEAL, policy and advocacy, and partnerships and program development.

In 2025, the IRC reached over 600,000 children and youth in 20 countries with early childhood development and education programs, ensuring that even the hardest to reach children in the most challenging places are able to go learn, develop and thrive. The Middle East, North Africa & Ukraine (MENAU) region is one of IRC’s largest and most complex areas of operation, encompassing protracted conflict, displacement, and recovery contexts across multiple country programs. Regional TU teams provide dedicated, context-relevant technical assistance to these country programs across the program cycle, aligned with the IRC Technical Assistance model and service charter.

**Position Overview**

The IRC is seeking an Education & Early Childhood Development (ECD) Technical Advisor to provide temporary coverage during a period of parental leave. This is a fixed-term, 6-month assignment (September 1, 2026 – March 1, 2027) focused exclusively on the Middle East, North Africa & Ukraine (MENAU) region. IRC’s MENAU region includes Jordan, Lebanon, Libya, occupied Palestinian Territory, Syria, Ukraine and Yemen.

The role is focused on education and early childhood development (pre-natal through age 8), which is closely aligned with the Nurturing Care Framework and has key interlinkages across multiple sectors. The Education & ECD TA will provide direct technical support to MENAU country programs identified as strategic priorities for Education and ECD innovation, growth, and research, in close collaboration and coordination with the regional Education TA and other sector-specific TAs relevant to ECD (Child Protection, Nutrition, Primary Health, Mental Health, Economic Recovery and Development, Women’s Protection, Governance, etc.).

To ensure quality programming and impact for young children and families affected by conflict and crisis, the Education & ECD TA will: support country program staff to design programs and projects aligned to IRC’s outcomes and evidence framework / theories of change / core indicators; review technical quality of proposals; input into proposal go/no-go decisions; analyze data to inform course correction; conduct technical trainings and ongoing technical coaching; share cross-context learning with country program staff; design, review, and share program-level tools (e.g., assessment frameworks, M&E templates, proposal materials); and support senior technical country program recruitment and capacity-building. Development, adaptation, and quality assurance of Education and ECD content and curricula sit with the ECD Content Specialist, and the ECD TA is expected to route any content-related country requests accordingly rather than duplicate that work.

As the Education and ECD Technical Advisor for MENAU, you will be responsible for ensuring high-quality technical assistance to Education and ECD projects across the MENAU region, including collaboration with counterparts from other sectors to ensure holistic support to clients. You will promote and collaborate with relevant stakeholders to achieve high-quality, high-impact interventions that are informed by evidence and best practice, contextually appropriate, driven by client and partner voices, and widely inclusive.

**Key Duties and Responsibilities**

**Program Design & Business Development**

Support designated MENAU country and regional programs to design winning submissions and generally position IRC for continued success in our Education and ECD technical domains:

- Support designated country programs’ proposal technical lead through participation in and/or facilitation of program design meetings
- Promote and support design collaboration with partners and clients
- Advise on program modalities and strategic partnership development based on how we can best support, complement, and reinforce local systems
- Advise on and/or provide hands-on support on assessments, including application and contextualization of technical standards
- Review technical design quality, including alignment of narratives, log-frames, and budgets to IRC standards and outcomes

**Implementation Support**

Support MENAU country program staff and other key stakeholders in implementing technical interventions:

- Support country and regional programs and other stakeholders with the recruitment and training of technical coordinators
- Assess program quality and inform improvements, providing follow-up support to country programs as needed
- Collaborate with country and regional program colleagues to monitor and analyze key indicators to inform periodic review, program adaptation, and course-correction as needed
- Provide technical capacity strengthening through ongoing mentoring, coaching, and trainings with country program focal points

**Knowledge & Learning**

Support continuous sectoral learning and IRC technical leadership within the MENAU region:

- Document learnings from program activities and share takeaways and opportunities
- Share cross-contextual learnings with country program staff across the MENAU region
- Refresh the sectoral evidence base in collaboration with global and regional staff to influence approaches
- Collaborate with other technical advisors within the region to promote integrated programming leadership
- Contribute to the delivery of education strategic priorities
- Maintain currency with sectoral best practices through continual learning and development
- Coordinate closely and maintain a regular check-in with the ECD Content Specialist and relevant Regional ECD Portfolio Team to align on country requests, agree on division of labor between program-level technical assistance and content/curricula work, and avoid duplicative deliverables

**Professional Profile**

Success in this position requires an individual with expertise in designing and delivering Education and ECD technical assistance and with a keen ability to work across the range of cultural, societal, and political contexts found across the MENAU region.

**Work Experience**

- A minimum of 10 years of relevant experience in implementing and/or managing ECD education programs, preferably with on-the-ground programmatic experience in humanitarian or crisis-affected contexts
- Experience and familiarity with related donors, peer agencies, and national contexts required, preferably in humanitarian and transitional, post-crisis contexts within the MENAU region
- Demonstrated expertise in technical program design, monitoring and evaluation, research methods, and data analysis, with the ability to turn concepts and strategy into measurable action

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies**

- Excellent verbal and written communication skills
- Strong organizational and time-management skills; proven ability to prioritize and deliver projects on time and independently
- Demonstrated ability to navigate a dynamic, cross-functional, global team structure in a large multi-national organization
- Demonstrated ability to work effectively with internal and external stakeholders at all levels
- Strong analytic problem-solving skills, data analysis, and data visualization skills
- Highly proficient in Microsoft Office suite
- Ability to manage and work through change in a proactive and positive manner
- Strong cross-cultural communication skills and familiarity with the MENAU region’s humanitarian context

**Education**

Bachelor’s degree in Education or a relevant field required; Master’s degree preferred.

**Language Skills**

Fluency in Arabic (spoken and written) is required. Excellent spoken and written English is also required.

**Key Working Relationships**

This position reports to the Global Practice Lead and Director of Research, Early Childhood Development, in close coordination with the Education Technical Advisor for MENAU, based in Amman for the duration of the parental leave cover. The Kansas Office for Refugees (KSOR) serves as a “Replacement Designee” for the state of Kansas, administering the Refugee Cash and Medical Assistance (CMA) program and Refugee Support Services (RSS) program in accordance with the Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR) regulations, through the KSOR office, based in Wichita.

In addition, KSOR responds to community needs by coordinating and supporting various events, including stakeholder meetings, quarterly consultation meetings, community forums, partner coordination meetings, and training sessions with guest speakers. As part of the KSOR team, the CEPM is responsible for helping plan and/or support stakeholders in executing these events. The CEPM supports the integration of refugees, asylees, and other immigrants by leading initiatives that leverage the power of welcoming communities. They work closely with the Senior Management Team to coordinate community outreach, build effective relationships, and connect clients with community-based resettlement resources through collaboration, research, evaluation, and partnership building. jobs.title: First, a community; then a job
jobs.body:
This ad is strange and very long. It’s like this because what we want to say is “we have found the job of our dreams”, but everyone would say that. So we wrote all of this instead.

The chance that it is the job of your dreams too is tiny, but exists. In truth, it’s not a job, it’s more of a community. Some would say a life choice. [Second Tree](https://secondtree.org/). Twenty-seven people from all over the world who left much better-paid jobs to work in refugee camps in Greece. Everyone in the team is here because of their commitment to help people, and to do that in a specific way we find ethically valuable.

But this is not for everyone; it’s actually not for most people. We all do an enormous amount of work (but for something really meaningful), for very small compensation (but it’s the same for everyone: founders, directors, top management, everyone).

And this level of transparency goes beyond our compensation policy: not only can you, but you are expected to, criticise your bosses. If you don’t, you are not a good fit for a group of people who want to improve.

So, if you have been close to the reality of refugees in Greece through social solidarity networks, legal work, or just rational compassion; or if you are a disillusioned humanitarian who is looking for a place that really cares; or you work in another sector and want to start doing work that is meaningful; this might be for you.

YOU

You are someone who is driven by purpose, not profit. There is nothing wrong in wanting to get rich, but we cannot do that here: our main criterion in deciding how to invest our time is trying to make the world a better place.

You might be surprised, maybe even sceptical, while reading this ad: can a place like that even exist? You want to find out, and you will ask us all of the questions that you have in your mind. You will not be polite; you want to really understand if this thing can actually exist.

You want to work with people who care deeply, you want to be in a team that’s just as committed as you are. People who are extremely effective at what they do, because they have the skills required or are willing to put in the hard work that is necessary to develop those skills.

You have the competence and the resolution to translate your ethical drive into meaningful and effective action. You have:

- Intelligence: You have changed your mind and made someone else change their mind, through rational conversations, at least once in the last two weeks
- Honesty: There is nothing you wouldn't say, except the things you say you wouldn't say. If you mess up, you say so. If someone else messes up, you say so too
- Engagement: When you read the Wikipedia entry for Aumann's Agreement Theorem you get excited. You don’t want to “be yourself”, you will try to improve us
- Ethical drive: You have decided (no matter how recently) that it’s not about what you’re good at or what you like to do, but about what is right to do
- Sense of humour: You are ruthless. Listening to [this advice](https://secondtree.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/Ms-advice.mp3) for humanitarians, from an Afghan teenager with an extremely painful story, moves you

You also have:

- English Proficiency: Speaking good enough English is necessary since it’s our working language. Other languages (like Arabic or Persian) are valuable. But the language we communicate in is English.
