The IRC is on the ground in more than 40 countries, providing emergency relief, relocating refugees and rebuilding lives in the wake of disaster.

The IRC is committed to a culture of bold leadership, innovation in all aspects of our work, creative partnerships and, most crucially, accountability to those we serve. The IRC is a tireless advocate for the most vulnerable.

**External Relations**

The External Relations (ER) department is comprised of four complementary functions: Private fundraising, Mobilization & Marketing, Policy & Advocacy and Operations & Analytics. To enable IRC to deliver our Strategy100 commitments, the ER department has established a bold new approach that will enhance our ability to raise diverse and flexible funding aligned with IRC’s top priorities, while raising our profile and influence. The ER team is an international team, with colleagues in more than 10 offices globally.

**The Purpose of the Role**

The Admin Assistant is a critical member of the team and we are seeking dynamic Administrative Assistant to support the administrative and logistical needs of the VP of Policy & Advocacy and the VP of Marketing & Mobilization. The role varies in what it covers and will suit somebody good at prioritizing effectively, multi-tasking and working autonomously. The right candidate can make judgements on what is important, will have the ability to solve problems, be efficient, diplomatic and have the inter-personal skills to deal with senior staff, colleagues and networks internationally.

***Support to the VP of Policy & Advocacy and the VP of Marketing & Mobilization - (50%)***

- Support the daily workflow of the VP of Policy & Advocacy and the VP of Marketing & Mobilization including handling appointments and complex calendar management
- Coordinate international travel as needed, including travel briefs, flights, accommodation, visa application and ground transportation
- Collate and submit expense reports, purchase orders, contract payments and other finance transactions for approval. Support department-wide rollout of systems and processes related to expensing
- Provide finance operations support including vendor onboarding, invoice/PO/payment follow-up, workflow approval monitoring in Integra, and basic budget coding guidance as needed.

***Team administrative support and coordination (50%)***

- Schedule department/team meetings included reserving conference rooms and setting up IT for meetings
- Manage onboarding materials for new staff (includes onboarding experience, coordination with IT and office services, integra training admin paperwork, maintaining docs, email distribution lists, internal newsletter, and IRC policy and process)
- Maintain and update key team-wide materials (e.g., org charts, onboarding materials, and internal intranet/team pages) to ensure accuracy with staffing and structural changes.
- Develop collaborative relationships with the teams
- Coordinate staff offboarding logistics including equipment return and timely updates to access, distribution lists, Teams, and reference materials.

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Position Reports to:**

**Indirect reporting: Other internal and/or external contacts:** Works closely with other colleagues and departments across the organization.

**Candidate Requirements:**

***Education:***

- Bachelor’s degree preferred but not required.

***Work Experience:***

- At least one year in a fast-paced office setting (internship experience counts too!)

***Preferred:***

- Experience working in a non-profit development department
- Prior experience working as an administrative assistant
- Interest in a fundraising career
- Experience working with high net-worth individuals and/or senior partners a plus

**Demonstrated Skills and Proficiencies:**

Minimum

- Work successfully in a sophisticated, fast-paced organization serving multiple partners
- Experience with Outlook email and calendar and familiarity with complex scheduling
- Solid Microsoft Office, database management, and Adobe Acrobat Pro experience
- Have a can-do attitude with a flexible disposition to handle fast-paced, shifting priorities
- Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, interacting with a variety of internal and external contacts with confidence and poise
- Strong listening skills and the ability to accurately follow guidance
- Outstanding attention to detail and dedication to timelines
- Ability and interest to work both independently and in a multifaceted, cross-functional team structure
- Ability to handle change in a proactive and positive manner
- Dedication to respect and maintain confidentiality of donor and employee information

**Working Environment:** This role is hybrid and requires the ability to work on-site in the NYC office or Remote working. Applicants must have a home or alternate workspace they can effectively complete their work from during regularly scheduled hours.

**Compensation:** ($21-26/hour). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

jobs.title: Remote and Unpaid Internship (Research – Value Chain) Agricultural and Livestock Value Chains in Syria
jobs.body:
**Organization:** Trust Consultancy & Development (TCD)  
**Location:** Remote – Open to candidates worldwide  
**Duration:** 4 months  
**Working arrangements:** Flexible, part-time or full-time, with 1–2 online meetings per week  
**Remuneration:** Unpaid  
**Starting date:** As soon as possible

## 1. About Trust Consultancy & Development

Trust Consultancy & Development (TCD) is an independent research, third-party monitoring, and evaluation consultancy headquartered in Gaziantep, Türkiye, with sister companies in Pakistan and Iraq. Trust provides research, assessments, evaluations, data collection, and capacity development services to international organizations, NGOs, and donors across Syria, Türkiye, Iraq, and other countries.

**Website:** [https://trustconsultancy.org/](https://trustconsultancy.org/)  
**LinkedIn:** [https://www.linkedin.com/company/trust.inc/](https://www.linkedin.com/company/trust.inc/)

## 2. About the Internship

Trust is seeking motivated **Agricultural and Livestock Value Chain Research Interns** to join a multidisciplinary research team working on agricultural and livestock value chain assessments in Syria.

The interns will work alongside experienced researchers, agricultural and veterinary specialists, and market systems experts on a **four-month research project**, contributing to value chain analysis, literature reviews, data analysis, and report preparation.

The research will focus on agricultural and livestock value chains, including wheat, vegetables, fruits, meat, dairy, and related products, examining production systems, market dynamics, economic opportunities, and constraints affecting the recovery and development of these sectors in Syria.

As members of the research team, interns will participate in regular coordination meetings, receive technical guidance, and contribute to specific research assignments under the supervision of senior team members.

The internship offers practical experience in applied research, value chain assessments, and technical consultancy projects.

## 3. Main Tasks and Responsibilities

**A. Literature Review and Research**

- Conduct desk research and literature reviews on selected agricultural and livestock value chains in Syria.
- Review academic publications, agricultural statistics, sector assessments, market studies, and relevant policies.
- Examine agricultural production, livestock health and productivity, processing, storage, marketing, and supply chains.
- Identify key market actors, production constraints, costs, trade flows, and economic opportunities.
- Analyze the impacts of conflict, climate change, water scarcity, and economic challenges on agricultural and livestock sectors.
- Develop structured literature databases, evidence matrices, and research summaries.

**B. Value Chain Assessment and Analysis**

- Work with the research team to support agricultural and livestock value chain assessments.
- Assist in mapping value chain actors, market linkages, and supporting services.
- Contribute to the development and review of research methodologies and data collection tools.
- Support the analysis of research findings and identification of value chain constraints and development opportunities.
- Assist in preparing technical reports, findings, and recommendations.

**C. Research Coordination and Knowledge Management**

- Participate in 1–2 weekly online coordination meetings with the research team.
- Prepare short research briefs, analytical summaries, and presentations.
- Organize research materials, references, and project documentation.
- Support technical proposal development and other relevant research activities when required.

## 4. Candidate Qualifications

**Essential:**

- University degree or ongoing postgraduate studies in **Agriculture, Agricultural Engineering, Veterinary Medicine, Animal Science, Agronomy, or closely related disciplines**.
- Relevant academic, research, or practical experience in agriculture, livestock production, veterinary services, or agricultural value chains.
- Strong interest in agricultural development, food security, and economic recovery in Syria.
- Good analytical, literature review, and report-writing skills.
- Very good written English; Arabic is a strong asset.
- Ability to work independently and collaboratively as part of a remote research team.
- Availability to participate in 1–2 online meetings weekly throughout the four-month project.

**Desirable:**

- Master's degree or postgraduate studies in a relevant discipline.
- Knowledge of Syria's agricultural and livestock sectors.
- Experience in value chain analysis, market systems development, agricultural research, or food security programming.
- Familiarity with quantitative or qualitative research methods, Excel, and reference-management tools.
- Previous involvement in research projects, assessments, or technical proposal development.

## 5. Internship Arrangements and Learning Opportunities

This is a **four-month, remote, unpaid internship**, with flexible working hours agreed upon with the research team supervisor.

Interns will be integrated into an established multidisciplinary research team and will receive technical guidance, regular feedback, and opportunities to participate in research discussions and analytical work.

The internship provides opportunities to strengthen research and analytical writing skills, gain practical experience in agricultural and livestock value chain assessments, and develop an understanding of market systems analysis and technical consultancy assignments.

An internship completion certificate may be issued following satisfactory completion of agreed assignments

jobs.title: Tax Site Coordinator
Remote and unpaid internship (Research and Proposal Development Conflict Analysis, Peacebuilding and Social Cohesion in Syria
jobs.body:
**Organization:** Trust Consultancy & Development (TCD)  
**Location:** Remote – Open to candidates worldwide  
**Duration:** 4–6 months  
**Working arrangements:** Flexible, part-time or full-time, with 1–2 online meetings per week  
**Remuneration:** Unpaid  
**Starting date:** As soon as possible

## 1. About Trust Consultancy & Development

Trust Consultancy & Development (TCD) is an independent research, third-party monitoring, and evaluation consultancy headquartered in Gaziantep, Türkiye, with sister companies in Pakistan and Iraq. Trust provides research, assessments, evaluations, data collection, and capacity development services to international organizations, NGOs, and donors across Syria, Türkiye, Iraq, and other countries.

**Website:** [https://trustconsultancy.org/](https://trustconsultancy.org/)  
**LinkedIn:** [https://www.linkedin.com/company/trust.inc/](https://www.linkedin.com/company/trust.inc/)

## 2. About the Internship

Trust is seeking a motivated **Research and Proposal Development Intern** to support research and technical proposal development related to conflict analysis, peacebuilding, social cohesion, and community resilience in Syria.

The intern will initially contribute to a technical proposal for a nationwide study covering Syria's 14 governorates. A major component of the internship will involve conducting a **comprehensive literature review lasting up to three months** on local conflict dynamics, sources of tension, peacebuilding, and community resilience in Syria.

The position offers flexible working arrangements, practical research experience, and regular guidance from Trust's experienced research and consultancy team.

## 3. Main Tasks and Responsibilities

**A. Literature Review and Research (Up to Three Months)**

- Identify, review, and synthesize academic literature, research reports, assessments, and policy documents concerning Syria.
- Examine conflict drivers, historical grievances, displacement, identity-based tensions, governance, economic inequalities, and environmental pressures, particularly developments since December 2024.
- Analyze peacebuilding initiatives, reconciliation mechanisms, social cohesion, and community resilience.
- Review the roles of local authorities, civil society, religious and traditional leaders, women, youth, and marginalized groups.
- Develop a structured literature database, thematic evidence matrix, and research summaries.
- Prepare a consolidated literature review report identifying key findings, evidence gaps, and recommendations.

**B. Technical Proposal Development**

- Support the preparation of technical proposals for research and evaluation assignments.
- Contribute to context analysis, research methodologies, sampling approaches, and data collection tools.
- Assist with stakeholder mapping, research ethics, conflict sensitivity, and inclusion considerations.
- Support proposal editing, documentation, and internal coordination.

**C. Knowledge Management**

- Prepare short research briefs, analytical summaries, and presentations.
- Organize research resources and contribute to Trust's knowledge-sharing activities.

## 4. Candidate Qualifications

**Essential:**

- University student, recent graduate, or early-career professional in political science, international relations, peace and conflict studies, sociology, development studies, or related disciplines.
- Strong interest in Syria's conflict dynamics, peacebuilding, and social cohesion.
- Good analytical, literature review, and academic writing skills.
- Very good written English; Arabic is a strong asset.
- Ability to work independently, meet deadlines, and participate in 1–2 online meetings weekly.

**Desirable:**

- Master's degree or postgraduate studies in a relevant field.
- Knowledge of the Syrian context and humanitarian/development sectors.
- Experience in qualitative or quantitative research, literature reviews, or proposal development.
- Familiarity with reference-management tools and research software.

## 5. Internship Arrangements and Learning Opportunities

This is a **4–6 month, remote, unpaid internship**, with flexible working hours agreed upon with the supervisor.

The intern will receive guidance through 1–2 weekly online meetings and regular feedback on assigned tasks.

The internship provides opportunities to strengthen research and analytical writing skills, gain exposure to international consultancy projects, learn technical proposal development, and develop expertise in conflict analysis and peacebuilding.

An internship completion certificate may be issued following satisfactory completion of the agreed assignments.

jobs.title: Youth Education and Partnerships Supervisor
jobs.body:
**This position is open to candidates with existing work authorization in the location where the position is advertised.**

**Background/IRC Summary:**  Each year the IRC in New York provides support to more than 1500 refugee, asylee and other humanitarian entrants seeking to start new lives in the New York City area. The IRC in New York aims to help these clients achieve self-sufficiency and adapt to and become engaged citizens of their new communities. The Education & Learning unit strives to serve the entire family unit, and the need all family members have for access to relevant educational opportunities in order to thrive in the U.S.

**Job Overview/Summary:** The Youth Education and Partnerships Supervisor coordinates educational programming for newcomer youth, including planning, implementation, and reporting for 2-4 Youth Education Programs, including but not limited to World Explorers, Youth ESOL, Mini-NYSA, and Tutoring. The Youth Education and Partnerships Supervisor collaborates closely with the other supervisors and Youth Education Manager to ensure all programs integrate best practices for teaching and tutoring English Language Learners and students with interrupted education, as well as social-emotional learning principles, and to ensure that IRC NY’s Youth Education goals and objectives are accomplished using a holistic, collaborative approach, in partnership with school staff, caregivers, and newcomer youth themselves.

In addition, the Youth Education and Partnerships Supervisor will steward relevant partnerships for the Youth Education Department as needed to ensure program implementation. This will include coordinating with community-based organizations for collaboration and locations.

**Major Responsibilities:**

- Oversee 2-4 youth programs including but not limited to Work Explorers, Youth ESOL, and other programs as needed.
- Develop logical framework and program design in alignment with IRC Outcomes and Evidence Framework for all programming in consultation with the M&E specialist
- Oversee recruitment of all staff, interns, and volunteers needed for programs
- Manage 2-3 Youth Education Coordinators and Specialists responsible for program implementation
- Ensure all programming follows all IRC policies and procedures, particularly concerning child safeguarding
- Design and implement opportunities for parent/caregiver engagement
- Oversee planning of all programs, including but not limited to space allocation and field trips.
- Manage participant recruitment, retention, attendance, and family engagement
- Oversee Monitoring and evaluation for all programs
- Manage program files and databases (enrollment, attendance, outcomes monitoring); maintain accurate and complete records according to IRC and funder policies
- Implement all programs in accordance with the IRC Multi-Tiered Systems of Support
- Serve as a school leader for the Newcomer Youth Summer Academy, responsible for planning, staff and volunteer recruitment, hiring, and training
- Supervise program Academic Lead Teachers, Classroom Culture Lead Teachers, SEL Teacher and Physical Education Teacher
- Oversee teachers to coordinate, plan and develop a 6 week culturally responsive and age-appropriate curriculum, lesson plans and assessment tools using student centered teaching methodologies for English Language Learners
- Ensure effective implementation of IRC’s Multi-tiered System of Support
- Design progress report and report card templates and coordinate related systems of data collection and dissemination
- Plan and coordinate caregiver and teacher conferences
- Conduct teacher observations and coaching using the IRC Framework for Effective Teaching
- Co-lead and plan weekly community events and student award ceremonies in collaboration with other Deans
- Provide technical assistance to internal IRC programs (such as mini academies, School Success Coaching) as well as to external subgrantee organizations
- Deliver workshops on supporting refugee and immigrant students to NYC schools and other community based organizations
- Coordinate with community based organizations as needed for program implementation with consultation with the Youth Education Manager
- Maintain existing partnerships as well as seek out new partnerships that align with Youth Education Department goals
- Prepare internal and external reports for programs supervised
- Ensure program data is consistently collected and entered in relevant databases
- Other related duties as assigned

**Job Requirements:**

- Master’s degree in education or related field required
- Must be available on Saturdays as needed to oversee youth programs
- A minimum of 2 years’ professional experience working with children and youth, specifically in the context of educational and social programs, required. Teaching certification and experience in the NYC public school system desirable.
- Experience as Head of Teaching, Instructional Coach, or School Leader, highly desirable
- Responsive Classrooms and/or Restorative Justice trained, highly desirable
- Experience working with refugee and/or immigrant populations, highly desirable
- Proven success planning and delivering creative and engaging curricula for beginner to intermediate ELLs
- Cultural competency training experience, desirable
- Demonstrated ability to promote an organizational culture that reflects IRC’s core values of service, accountability, integrity, and equality. Ability to lead in a way that recognizes that IRC’s work is best accomplished through the true collaboration of individuals from many cultures with a great variety of skills and perspectives
- Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills
- Fluent in MS Office applications, especially MS Excel
- Organized, responsible, and flexible: able to maintain responsibility for multiple tasks in the context of a diverse, fast-paced work environment and maintain composure under pressure
- Fluency in a second language highly desired (such as: Spanish, Dari, Pashto, Arabic, French, Haitian-Creole)

**Working Environment:**

- A combination of standard office environment, with the potential for remote work on a limited basis.
- Occasional weekend and/or evening work required.
- Staff are required to adhere to IRC’s COVID risk mitigation policies, which may include masking, physical distancing, enhanced hygiene practices, symptom screening, and isolation and quarantine when needed. IRC policies may be stricter than federal, state, or local level policies.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $72,700/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

jobs.title: Venezuela: Oficial de Flota (Caracas)
jobs.body:
La Cruz Roja Venezolana (CRV) es una organización humanitaria cuyo mandato es salvar vidas y mejorar las condiciones de las personas en situación de vulnerabilidad. Como parte del Movimiento Internacional de la Cruz Roja y la Media Luna Roja, brinda asistencia oportuna en emergencias, desastres y contextos de necesidad humanitaria.

Guiada por sus Principios Fundamentales—Humanidad, Imparcialidad, Neutralidad, Independencia, Voluntariado, Unidad y Universalidad—la CRV actúa como auxiliar de los poderes públicos en el ámbito humanitario, trabajando para reducir el sufrimiento humano sin distinción de raza, género, religión o ideología. Su labor abarca la atención médica de emergencia, el fortalecimiento de la resiliencia comunitaria, la capacitación en primeros auxilios, la respuesta a desastres y la promoción de la salud y el bienestar.

A través de una red de voluntarios altamente comprometidos, la CRV moviliza recursos de manera eficiente y eficaz para estar presente donde más se necesita, cuando más se necesita. Su labor se fundamenta en la solidaridad, el respeto a la dignidad humana y el compromiso con la protección de la vida en todas sus formas.

Si deseas formar parte del equipo y hacer la diferencia, te invitamos a sumarte.

*¿Cómo puedes hacer la diferencia? Funciones claves / Responsabilidades*

El/La Oficial de Flota tendrá como responsabilidad principal planificar, supervisar y controlar la operatividad, mantenimiento y asignación de la totalidad de las unidades vehiculares del proyecto (incluyendo ambulancias, vehículos de carga y unidades de logística), garantizando la disponibilidad de transporte seguro y eficiente para los equipos de campo de la Cruz Roja Venezolana, maximizando el rendimiento del combustible y velando por el estricto cumplimiento de los protocolos de seguridad vial.

Será el/la encargado(a) de:

- Planificar, coordinar y supervisar el registro, control y la actualización continua del estatus mecánico, legal y operativo de los vehículos requeridos por el proyecto.
- Implementar y mantener procedimientos rigurosos para la asignación diaria de unidades, la planificación de rutas operativas y la rotación adecuada de los conductores.
- Desarrollar e implementar planes de mantenimiento preventivo y correctivo para toda la flota vehicular, coordinando las citas técnicas con talleres mecánicos previamente evaluados.
- Supervisar y controlar el sistema de inventarios de repuestos, lubricantes y herramientas críticas asignadas a cada unidad de transporte.
- Elaborar y mantener actualizados los registros e indicadores de rendimiento de la flota en los sistemas de gestión asignados (control de kilometraje, consumo de combustible, costos de reparación por unidad).
- Apoyar y supervisar el envío seguro de mercancías y personal hacia las filiales de la Cruz Roja Venezolana, verificando que los vehículos cumplan con los estándares logísticos y de seguridad exigidos.
- Verificar y consolidar las bitácoras de viaje, reportes de combustible y novedades viales presentadas por los conductores en el terreno.
- Gestionar las requisiciones de servicios mecánicos, repuestos o seguros vehiculares en coordinación con el Oficial de Compras, asegurando que los procesos cumplan con los estándares institucionales.
- Coordinar con las áreas administrativas y financieras para garantizar la disponibilidad presupuestal antes de comprometer recursos en reparaciones mayores de la flota.
- Evaluar, analizar y presentar información clara, veraz y confiable sobre el estado de la flota para facilitar la toma de decisiones por parte de la Coordinación de Logística.
- Documentar, reportar y tramitar de forma inmediata ante la dirección financiera y el área legal cualquier siniestro, choque, robo o novedad técnica mayor ocurrida con los vehículos.
- Apoyar los procesos de capacitación, inducción y sensibilización sobre políticas de conducción defensiva, mantenimiento básico y protocolos de acceso seguro (SAS) para todo el personal y voluntariado que utilice vehículos institucionales.
- Ejecutar otras tareas de supervisión de transporte asignadas por su superior inmediato de acuerdo con las dinámicas diarias de la emergencia por el terremoto.

*Reporte*

El/La Oficial de Flota le reportará al Director de Desarrollo Organizacional

*Lugar de trabajo*

Caracas, con disponibilidad para viajar a nivel nacional.

*Para calificar como un constructor del sistema humanitario venezolano deberás cumplir con los siguientes requisitos:*

- Grado universitario en ingeniería mecánica, automotriz, administración de empresas, logística o carreras afines.
- Al menos 2 años de experiencia directa en la gestión, supervisión y control de flotas vehiculares (preferiblemente de emergencia o transporte pesado) en proyectos de cooperación o ayuda humanitaria.
- Experiencia comprobada en el manejo de presupuestos de mantenimiento, seguimiento financiero de flotas y control administrativo de bitácoras.
- Familiaridad avanzada con el uso de sistemas informáticos u hojas de cálculo Excel para el monitoreo de rendimiento de combustible y costos operativos de transporte.
- Conocimiento profundo del marco regulatorio de tránsito terrestre en Venezuela, trámites legales vehiculares y estándares mecánicos generales.
- Capacidad para trabajar bajo presión en un horario flexible, liderar equipos de conductores en situaciones de crisis y en entornos multiculturales.
- Experiencia previa trabajando con el Movimiento de la Cruz Roja / Media Luna Roja o el sector humanitario y conocimiento de los protocolos de acceso seguro (SAS) es deseable.
- Excelentes habilidades de comunicación, toma de decisiones éticas, resguardo de la confidencialidad y apego estricto a los Siete Principios Fundamentales.

jobs.title: Procurement Manager, Emerging Technology and Digital Innovation Procurement
jobs.body:
**Background**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to humanitarian crises in over 40 countries and in communities across the United States and Europe, helping people whose lives have been shattered by conflict and disaster to survive, recover, and rebuild their futures.

Global Procurement, within the Global Supply Chain function, leads sourcing strategy, category management, and supplier management for the organization. As IRC continues to test and adopt new technology to support its mission, Global Procurement is establishing a dedicated Procurement Manager role to provide procurement capacity for emerging technology and digital innovation.

**Position Overview**

The Procurement Manager, Emerging Technology and Digital Innovation Procurement supports fast-moving technology sourcing needs across IRC, with a focus on early-stage digital innovation, pilots, proofs of concept, trials, and emerging tools. The role helps teams test and evaluate new technology quickly while maintaining procurement discipline, vendor due diligence, risk review, documentation, and compliance.

For this role, “digital innovation” refers to early-stage, small-scale, fast-moving technology initiatives where IRC teams are testing a new idea, tool, platform, vendor, or digital approach before deciding whether to scale. The portfolio covers AI and generative AI tools where applicable, SaaS and digital platforms, automation, data and analytics, migration and testing tools, cybersecurity tools, collaboration platforms, digital service delivery tools, field and mobile technology, low-code and no-code platforms, and other emerging digital solutions.

This role is an execution-focused, hands-on individual contributor role. It enables IRC to move quickly on emerging technology and digital innovation requests without bypassing procurement controls, vendor due diligence, information security, data protection, legal review, donor compliance, or documentation requirements. The Procurement Manager serves as the day-to-day procurement focal point for these requests

**Key Responsibilities**

**A. Emerging Technology and Digital Innovation Sourcing Execution**

- Provide hands-on sourcing support for pilots, trials, proofs of concept, small-scale SaaS, emerging vendors, startup-style tools, and digital innovation requests across IRC.
- Execute sourcing activities in line with the IT category strategy and under the guidance of the Senior Category Manager, IT.
- Conduct early market scans and market intelligence for emerging tools, vendors, pricing models, and digital innovation categories.
- Support requirements gathering, supplier identification, RFI/RFQ/RFP preparation, evaluation support, award recommendation, and contract finalization.
- Build supplier visibility for innovation and emerging technology vendors, including startup and niche providers that may later become larger enterprise solutions.
- Help bring new tools into proper procurement channels, reducing shadow IT, credit-card purchasing, and unmanaged technology spend.
- Support SaaS rationalization, renewal planning, demand management, and license optimization at the innovation and pilot tier.
- Help business teams translate technical needs into clear scopes of work, evaluation criteria, and vendor questions.

**B. Pilot, Trial, and Proof-of-Concept Procurement Frameworks**

- Build and maintain a lightweight, repeatable procurement pathway for pilots, trials, and proofs of concept.
- Develop checklists, decision tools, and methodology for short-term technology engagements.
- Define the minimum documentation required before a pilot, trial, or proof of concept can begin.
- Maintain clear approval checkpoints and escalation criteria so teams understand when a pilot can proceed and when it requires further review.
- Track emerging technology requests from intake through pilot, decision, and possible scale-up.
- Ensure required reviews and approvals are completed and all necessary checks are documented before tools are tested or used.
- Help document whether a pilot should end, continue, scale, or move into a formal sourcing process.
- Coordinate NDAs and pre-procurement documentation when teams need to test or evaluate multiple tools before selecting a vendor.
- Ensure pilots and trials are set up in a way that allows long-term success if IRC later moves to a larger phase or formal sourcing process.

**C. AI-Enabled and High-Risk Technology Procurement Support**

- Support sourcing for AI-enabled tools as part of the broader emerging technology portfolio, applied only when AI functionality is in scope.
- For AI-enabled tools, support the application of IRC’s AI assessment requirements, including use-case risk classification, provider/deployer determination, GenAI tool checks, and required approvals.
- Coordinate with the AI Governance and Risk Committee and AI Department Focal Points when applicable.
- Identify and escalate sourcing requests that may involve high-risk technology, AI functionality, personal information, confidential data, client-facing tools, cybersecurity concerns, or unapproved tools.
- Support procurement documentation for AI-enabled tools, including evidence of approvals, vendor assessments, risk reviews, and contract requirements.

**D. Vendor Due Diligence, Risk Review, and Documentation**

- Coordinate required vendor risk assessments (VRA) and due diligence across cybersecurity, privacy and data protection, legal, donor compliance, sanctions and ATC screening, financial viability, implementation risk, integration risk, operational support model, and vendor lock-in and exit risk.
- Coordinate with Information Security, Data Protection, Office of General Counsel, Risk and Compliance, and Finance to ensure required reviews are completed before pilots, trials, awards, or contract signature.
- Ensure procurement files are complete, audit-ready, and aligned with IRC sourcing policy and donor requirements.
- Support compliance with institutional donor requirements that may affect technology, AI, data hosting, data residency, and vendor selection.
- Track and follow up on missing documentation, approvals, vendor information, and risk reviews.

**E. Tool and Vendor Visibility**

- Maintain or support a list of emerging technology tools and vendors, indicating status (under review, in pilot, approved, rejected, expired) and the approved use case for each tool.
- Document the business owner, contract status, contract dates, and renewal timing for each tool.
- Document what each tool is approved for and what use would require additional approval or new procurement action.
- Help connect business owners, end users, IT, Procurement, Information Security, Data Protection, Legal, and Finance around emerging technology tools and vendors.
- Reduce situations where approved tools are used in non-approved ways, and flag misuse for review.

**F. Contracting and Commercial Support**

- Support commercial negotiation and contracting across the emerging technology portfolio, including NDAs, trial agreements, pilot agreements, proof-of-concept agreements, SaaS agreements, subscriptions, software licenses, cloud services, implementation services, and renewals.
- Review pricing models, including seat-based licensing, usage-based pricing, token usage, API calls, implementation fees, renewal escalators, and support fees, and provide commercial analysis.
- Coordinate with Legal, IT, Finance, and business owners to ensure contracts include appropriate terms on data protection, confidentiality, intellectual property, service levels, audit rights, incident reporting, termination, data return, and exit provisions.
- For AI-enabled tools, ensure contracts also address AI-generated outputs, model training restrictions, and AI-specific risk allocation.
- Support renewal planning and help prevent last-minute renewals or unplanned vendor commitments.

**G. Stakeholder Engagement and Service Support**

- Provide practical, service-oriented procurement support to teams exploring new tools, pilots, digital services, automation platforms, AI solutions, or other emerging technology.
- Help stakeholders move through the procurement process without unnecessary delays, while maintaining compliance and risk controls.
- Coordinate between business owners, IT owners, Procurement, end users, Information Security, Data Protection, Legal, and Finance to ensure tool usage remains aligned with approved scope, contract terms, procurement files, risk approvals, and any applicable usage guidelines.
- Reduce workarounds, shadow IT, and credit-card purchasing by making the correct procurement process easier to follow.
- Guide stakeholders on procurement routes, required documentation, approval steps, and realistic timelines for emerging technology procurement.
- Support early engagement with teams considering new tools, pilots, or digital approaches, before commitments are made to vendors.

**H. Reporting and Continuous Improvement**

- Track the emerging technology sourcing pipeline, renewal calendar, cycle time, savings, risk flags, documentation completion, and approval status.
- Track pilot outcomes (end, continue, scale, or formal sourcing) and capture lessons learned.
- Track user adoption issues, non-approved usage of approved tools, and other compliance signals, and surface these to the Senior Category Manager, IT.
- Identify recurring issues in emerging technology sourcing and recommend improvements to frameworks, checklists, templates, and decision tools.
- Contribute to knowledge sharing across Global Procurement on emerging technology, SaaS, AI, and digital innovation sourcing practices.
- Support the role’s value contribution by improving visibility over fast-moving technology spend, reducing duplicated tools, undocumented pilots, and audit risk.

**Key Working Relationships**

- **Reports to:** Senior Category Manager, IT.
- **Internal:** Office of the CIO and IT teams; Senior Category Manager, IT; Information Security; Data Protection; Office of General Counsel; Ethics and Compliance; Risk and Compliance; Finance; Airbel Impact Lab; Data and Analytics; External Relations; Country Program supply chain and innovation leads; program innovation teams; fundraising and digital teams; AI Governance and Risk Committee when applicable; Global Procurement peers.
- **External:** Emerging technology vendors and resellers; SaaS, cloud, cybersecurity, automation, data, and AI providers; startup and niche technology vendors; industry analysts; peer humanitarian and development organizations.

**Minimum Qualifications**

- Bachelor’s degree in procurement, supply chain, business administration, information technology, engineering, law, or a related field. Equivalent experience may be considered.
- Minimum 5 to 7 years of procurement, sourcing, contract management, or vendor management experience.
- Of the required 5 to 7 years above, at least 3 years must be in IT procurement, SaaS and software sourcing, software licensing, cloud services, cybersecurity tools, data platforms, or similar technology categories.
- Experience supporting pilots, trials, proofs of concept, or other early-stage technology procurement activities.
- Experience coordinating vendor due diligence and technology risk reviews, including cybersecurity, data protection, financial, and operational risk.
- Experience supporting sourcing events, supplier evaluations, commercial analysis, and contract coordination.
- Good understanding of technology procurement risks, including data protection, information security, intellectual property, software licensing, vendor lock-in, and third-party risk.
- Ability to work effectively with IT, Legal, Information Security, Data Protection, Finance, and business teams.
- Demonstrated ability to work quickly while maintaining compliance, controls, and documentation standards.
- Strong stakeholder service orientation and ability to balance procurement standards with customer needs.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills.
- Good judgment and ability to balance speed, compliance, risk, and stakeholder needs.
- Experience in an NGO, donor-funded organization, humanitarian agency, UN agency, or complex global organization.
- Knowledge of donor compliance requirements such as USAID/BHA, FCDO, ECHO, EU, UN agencies, or private foundations.
- Professional certification such as CIPS, CPSM, or equivalent, completed or in progress.
- Working knowledge of French, Spanish, or Arabic is an advantage.

**Working Environment**

Flexible (IRC hub city preferred; remote considered). Travel of up to 10% domestically and internationally, including occasional travel to IRC country offices.

***This is a remote position open to internal candidates based in countries where IRC operates who have the right to work in their location. Successful candidates will be hired on a local employment contract and according to local salary scale.***

***This role is open to candidates located and with the right to work in Lebanon, Germany, Kenya, Pakistan, and Jordan.***

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

jobs.title: Senior Expert, Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning (MEL), National Security
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
jobs.body:
UK, London | Full-time, conditional position

The Senior Expert, MEL will join Integrity’s Services Team and play a key technical and management role in the design and delivery of our MEL portfolio. UK national security will be a primary thematic focus, including cybersecurity, countering information manipulation, economic security, resilience and preparedness, and emerging technology governance.

This is an exciting opportunity to play a leading role in technical design and delivery of MEL projects and proposals. The Senior Expert will develop and apply appropriate, innovative, and proportionate MEL approaches and methodologies in response to client needs, drawing where relevant on Integrity’s wider expertise in research, evidence, and analysis, and data analytics.

We are looking for someone with experience and expertise that include:

- At least 7 years’ experience in MEL and research, including experience working with UK Government clients.
- Proven experience designing complex MEL bids, preferably for UK Government clients, including developing technical approaches and methodologies, work and resource plans, and commercially viable budgets.
- Strong understanding of the UK national security policy and institutional context, and the implications for the design and delivery of MEL.
- Strong expertise in MEL design including developing theories of change, results frameworks, indicators and wider monitoring and learning systems.
- Strong project and relationship management skills, including experience managing complex projects and working effectively with clients, partners, consultants, and multidisciplinary teams.
- Strong applied research and analytical skills and experience of assuring the quality of MEL, research, and evaluation.

jobs.title: Oficial de Recuperación Económica (Medios de Vida) - Guasdualito
jobs.body:
El Consejo Dánes para refugiados es una de las ONG humanitarias líderes en el mundo, que trabaja en más de 40 países para brindar asistencia y protección adecuadas a refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, desplazados internos, retornados, personas en movimiento y población local vulnerable/comunidades de acogida. Actualmente, DRC está buscando un **Oficial de Recuperación Económica (Medios de Vida)** altamente calificado con sede en **Guasdualito, Edo. Apure.**

**Acerca del trabajo:**

DRC está administrando sus operaciones en Venezuela, bajo la dirección de la oficina de país en Caracas y cuatro oficinas de campo ubicadas en los estados de Sucre, Apure, Zulia y La Guaira. DRC Venezuela está implementando actividades como monitoreo de protección, asistencia legal, asistencia de protección individual para PWSN, sesiones informativas para PoC, prevención de trata de personas, rehabilitación de infraestructura de salud y seguridad alimentaria.

**Objetivo del cargo**

Bajo la supervisión del/la Team Leader de Recuperación Económica o del Gerente de Recuperación Económica, el/la Oficial de Medios de Vida será responsable de implementar de manera efectiva y oportuna las actividades del componente de medios de vida de los programas de Recuperación Económica de DRC en Venezuela. Esto incluye el acompañamiento técnico en terreno para el fortalecimiento de emprendedores y micronegocios en comunidades vulnerables, expuestas a riesgos de protección y desastres, así como el desarrollo de habilidades blandas para emprender, la integración del enfoque verde en sus modelos de negocio y su articulación con oportunidades de mercado. Asimismo, el/la Oficial facilitará la transferencia de metodologías de formación a socios locales a través de metodologías desarrolladas por DRC, y garantizará la correcta recopilación de los medios de verificación necesarios para el seguimiento y la rendición de cuentas.

El/la Oficial promoverá una programación integrada y articulada con los equipos de Protección, WASH y Preparación para Desastres, asegurando intervenciones intersectoriales y de calidad en todas las etapas del proyecto. Además, será responsable de coordinar efectivamente con el equipo de Recuperación Económica y socios locales, y de asegurar el cumplimiento del plan de acción establecido.

**Responsabilidades:**

**Identificación de actividades propias del sector de Medios de Vida**

- Liderar diagnósticos socioeconómicos y de mercado para identificar cadenas productivas, ecosistemas de actores claves del sector público y privado, y oportunidades de inclusión financiera (instituciones, banca, sector privado) que fomenten la autosuficiencia y resiliencia de las Personas de Interés (PDI).
- Evaluar la viabilidad técnica, social, ambiental y económica de propuestas productivas, asegurando que los proyectos de medios de vida sean sostenibles, pertinentes culturalmente y sensibles a los riesgos de protección y desastres.
- Contribuir con datos del contexto local para el ajuste y formulación de propuestas, garantizando la integración del enfoque de Recuperación Económica con otros sectores (Protección, WASH y Preparación para Desastres).
- Con el apoyo y la orientación de su supervisor y coordinación técnica, sugerir ideas innovadoras y técnicas adecuadas para las intervenciones de Recuperación Económica en función del contexto.

**Implementación técnica y logística**

- Responsable de implementar la planificación, ejecución, seguimiento y cierre técnico de las actividades de medios de vida (focalización, diagnósticos, selección, formación, entregas, encuestas PDM, líneas base/salida y gestión de bases de datos), en coordinación con el Team Leader o Gerente de Recuperación económica, y con los equipos de Logística y finanzas para asegurar el cumplimiento del plan de acción y el reporte oportuno de los indicadores propuestos.
- Diseñar e implementar procesos de formación en planes de negocios, medios de vida verdes, orientación vocacional, habilidades blandas, planes de marketing, estructuras de costos, gestión y educación financiera, mediante metodologías híbridas que incluyen plataformas digitales (Moodle). Entre las actividades se contempla la facilitación directa, la Formación a Formadores (ToT) para socios y la gestión logística/financiera necesaria para su ejecución.
- Con la orientación técnica de la coordinación de Recuperación Económica, en conjunto con la supervisión del Team Leader o Gerente de Recuperación Económica, ser el punto focal de alianzas estratégicas con actores del sector privado, público o institucional para actividades propias de medios de vida, como lo pueden ser alianzas estratégicas para emprendedores.
- Realizar planes de seguimiento a las PdI relacionados al incremento de su productividad y de medición de indicadores establecidos en el programa de Recuperación Económica.
- Identificar, coordinar y entregar apoyos en especie (como insumos productivos, herramientas, equipos, etc.) de acuerdo con las necesidades socioeconómicas y productivas identificadas, así como con los lineamientos técnicos de la coordinación y el enfoque de protección.
