jobs.body:
Danish Refugee Council (DRC) es una de las ONG humanitarias líderes en el mundo, que trabaja en más de 40 países para brindar asistencia y protección adecuadas a refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, desplazados internos, retornados, personas en movimiento y población local vulnerable/comunidades de acogida. Actualmente, en el marco de la respuesta de emergencia al terremoto, DRC está buscando un/a Oficial de Protección altamente calificado/a con sede en Santa Bárbara del Zulia, Venezuela.

**Acerca del trabajo:**

DRC administra sus operaciones en Venezuela bajo la dirección de la oficina de país en Caracas y tres oficinas de campo ubicadas en los estados de Sucre, Apure y Zulia. DRC Venezuela implementa actividades de monitoreo de protección, asistencia legal, asistencia de protección individual para personas con necesidades específicas (PWSN), sesiones informativas para personas de interés (PoC), prevención de la trata de personas y seguridad alimentaria.

**Objetivo general del puesto:**

Bajo la supervisión del Líder de equipo de Protección (Zulia), el Asistente de Protección apoyará la implementación en terreno de todos los objetivos de protección bajo los proyectos de DRC. El Asistente de Protección desarrollará y mantendrá buenas relaciones con las personas de interés, las partes interesadas relevantes y otros actores humanitarios, para apoyar la implementación y coordinación adecuadas de las actividades de Protección de DRC que se desarrollarán en el área de intervención. Apoyar la implementación de enfoques diferenciales, especialmente de edad, género, y diversidad en las actividades de protección.

**Responsabilidades:**

- Contribuir eficientemente a la implementación del proyecto de protección en los municipios del sur del lago del estado Zulia de acuerdo con los objetivos acordados.
- Implementar periódica el Monitoreo de Protección en las comunidades de intervención, incluyendo el levantamiento de datos cuantitativos y cualitativos sobre necesidades/riesgos de protección mediante la aplicación de entrevistas a unidades familiares, grupos focales e informantes claves.
- Contribuir al fortalecimiento del enfoque de edad, género y diversidad en las acciones de y respuestas de protección.
- Apoyar en la identificación y documentación sistemáticamente las necesidades específicas y riesgos de protección de las personas más vulnerables en las comunidades de intervención –a través del Monitoreo de Protección, actividades informativas realizadas en las comunidades y otros medios— a fin de referir y/o brindar una repuesta oportuna a las personas de interés.
- Participar en el Comité de Asistencia de Protección Individual (IPA), y contribuir con los planes de respuestas que respondan a las necesidades específicas protección de los casos, y apoyar con los planes de entrega de las asistencias y/o remisiones a servicios especializados internos y/o externos.
- Manejar la información confidencial de manera correcta, de acuerdo con las políticas de protección de datos de DRC, gestionando los archivos de protección de manera precisa, correcta y completa.
- Apoyar en la recopilación de información para la elaboración de reportes, informes, e insumos productos del Monitoreo de Protección.
- Asegurar la más alta calidad de las intervenciones de protección y la coherencia entre todos los proyectos, en curso y propuestos, de acuerdo con la estrategia general.
- Apoyar en la orientación de las personas de interés según las rutas de protección, el mapeo de servicios y de los actores humanitarios e institucionales.
- Apoyar en la organización y facilitación de grupos focales y sesiones informativas sobre temas de protección.
- Apoyar y asistir en conjunto con la línea supervisora en el desarrollo de actividades legales conforme a los objetivos y metas.
- Participar bajo supervisión en el asesoramiento individual de las principales necesidades legales identificadas.
- Acompañar a los beneficiarios a instituciones públicas según sea necesario.
- Participar en espacios de formación y retroalimentación de las acciones de protección.
- Participar de manera colaborativa en las acciones del equipo de protección y otras áreas.
- Participar activamente a las reuniones de equipo proporcionando insumos, desafíos y lecciones aprendidas.
- Contribuir al desarrollo de herramientas de procedimiento operativos estándar.

**Programación y Operaciones**

- Asegurar la implementación eficiente y efectiva de las actividades programática asignadas, mientras el plan de trabajo.
- Apoyar en la preparación de informes y presupuestos mensuales.

**Experiencia y competencias:**

- Mínimo 1 año de experiencia relevante en protección humanitaria, trabajo social, derechos humanos u otro trabajo similar de terreno, relacionado a una ONG u otra organización sin fines de lucro.
- Experiencia de terreno y de trabajo con comunidades urbanas, y/o rurales, y/o indígenas.
- Experiencia y capacidad para entrevistar a personas de todas las edades, género y diversidad.
- Buenas habilidades para trabajar con tabletas y computadores.
- Buenas habilidades en MS Word y Excel.
- Voluntad y habilidad de aprender.

**Educación:**

Título Universitario pertinente en logística y / o gestión de la cadena de suministro o cualificación profesional equivalente.

**Ofrecemos:**

- La oportunidad de pertenecer a una de las mejores ONGs a nivel mundial.
- Acceso a más de 1,000 capacitaciones y certificados en línea gratuita.
- Duración del contrato: 6 meses con disponibilidad de extensión según disponibilidad presupuestal.
- Salario: **Banda I.**
- Seguro HCM cubierto en su totalidad por la organización.
- Contratación nacional.

**Competencias Básicas de DRC:**

- **Lograr la excelencia**: centrarse en alcanzar resultados y garantizar procesos eficientes.
- **Colaboración:** involucrar a las partes relevantes y alentar la retroalimentación.
- **Tomar la iniciativa**: tomar posesión e iniciativa mientras se busca la innovación.
- **Comunicar:** escuchar y hablar con eficacia y honestidad.
- **Demostración de integridad**: actuar de acuerdo con la visión y los valores de DRC.

**Proceso de solicitud:** Todos los solicitantes deben cargar una carta de presentación (máx. 1 página) y un CV actualizado (**máx. 2 páginas, sin soportes**) en español, en la plataforma de empleo de DRC. Las solicitudes enviadas por correo electrónico no serán consideradas.

**Fecha de cierre de solicitudes**: Miércoles 14 de Octubre a las 11:59 pm Hora Local. Tenga en cuenta que las solicitudes se revisarán continuamente y las entrevistas se planificarán tan pronto como se identifique a un candidat@ adecuado. DRC se reserva el derecho a cerrar la vacante antes de la fecha límite una vez se identifique a un candidato idóneo.

**Fecha de inicio:** Octubre 2026

**Nota:**

- Nos reservamos el derecho a cerrar la vacante antes de la fecha indicada de cierre de postulaciones
- La vacante está sujeta a aprobación del proyecto y disponibilidad de fondos
- Debido a una contratación de emergencia, DRC no se obliga a enviar las notificaciones de rechazo a los candidatos que no sean considerados en el proceso

jobs.title: Humanitarian Access &Safety(HAS) Adviser Niamey Niger- Internal Applicants Only
jobs.body:
**About the Context**

Since the beginning of 2022, the security situation in Niger remains volatile. Humanitarian access in some areas is one of the main challenges in the implementation of humanitarian responses in Niger. This is visible in a number of regions with significant humanitarian needs, including Tillabéri, Tahoua, Maradi and Diffa. The presence of multiple armed actors has contributed to restricting humanitarian space.

The purpose of the Humanitarian Access and Safety (HAS) function is to enable a principled humanitarian response in a safe manner, for the communities and partners NRC works with, and for its staff. Despite the efforts of the humanitarian community to deliver assistance to those in need, security and access constraints remain significant challenges. Obstacles such as conflict and violence, environmental and physical challenges, bureaucratic hurdles, and interference in humanitarian operations hinder the delivery of services and protection to displacement-affected people.

In this context, strengthening humanitarian coordination to promote access is essential. This is one of the reasons for the establishment of the Access Working Group (AWG) in Niger, whose objective is to contribute to a more effective and coordinated humanitarian response, to support the efforts of the Humanitarian Coordinator (HC), the Humanitarian Country Team (HCT) and other partners in the implementation and monitoring of the HCT access strategy and action plan, and to analyse access constraints with a view to resolving bottlenecks. NRC, as an active member of this body, wishes to strengthen its participation by providing a dedicated staff member to act as Co-Lead alongside OCHA.

Find out more about NRC [https://www.nrc.no/](https://www.nrc.no/%22%20/t%20%22_blank) and Watch this short video to see NRC in action [https://vimeo.com/736782633](https://vimeo.com/736782633%22%20/t%20%22_blank)

**What we are looking for**

The Humanitarian Access and Safety (HAS) Adviser supports principled response design and implementation by providing analysis, operational support, and technical guidance to ensure sustained and quality access for NRC Niger. The Adviser reports to the HAS Manager for line supervision, and technically to the Country Director (CD), and works closely with the Country Management Group (CMG) on implementing NRC's Humanitarian Access Framework.

The position combines two complementary functions. First, as NRC's internal HAS Adviser, the incumbent advises on strategic decision-making, programme design, monitoring, and operational footprints to be principled, conflict-sensitive, adaptive, and contextually driven. Second, the Adviser co-chairs Niger's Access Working Group (AWG) alongside OCHA, contributing to inform and brief humanitarian organisations and fora (notably the NGO coordination groups) on humanitarian access issues and barriers, and collecting information from humanitarian actors to inform the AWG. While the position is hosted by NRC, the incumbent is expected to spend significant time with the offices of AWG member organisations, in a spirit of collaboration and collective outcomes.

The AWG Co-Lead function drives collective action to overcome humanitarian access barriers impeding the delivery of principled and quality assistance to populations in hard-to-reach areas, and in response to new emergencies. The Co-Lead also capitalises on existing initiatives, research results, and available tools, making them accessible to AWG member organisations.

**What you will do**

***Direct support to programmes (40%)***

- Advise programme teams on the design of conflict-sensitive activities, adapted to access dynamics.
- Contribute to contextual and access analyses in proposals, reports, and strategic notes.
- Participate in Project Cycle Management (PCM), integrating access analysis and supporting programme decision-making.
- Train programme teams and local partners on humanitarian access issues and negotiations.
- Support planning and prioritisation of activities based on access constraints and risks.

***AWG Co-Lead and advocacy support (40%)***

**Strategy development & implementation**

- Provide support on periodic access strategy development processes, ensuring AWG members' perspectives and aspirations are represented in the strategy and work-plan.
- Contribute to the collection of information from humanitarian actors, notably NNGOs, to guide the implementation of the work-plan, including access severity mapping, incident reporting and monitoring, stakeholder mapping, bureaucratic constraints, negotiations, policy development, advocacy and training.

**Management & capacity building**

- Support the preparation and facilitation of monthly and ad-hoc AWG-Niger meetings, including agenda preparation, co-chairing, minute-taking, and follow-up of action points.
- Support the establishment of temporary sub-working groups/task forces on specific activities.
- Contribute to the organisation and delivery of access training and workshops, within the humanitarian community or with external stakeholders.

**Access analysis & humanitarian advocacy**

- Support the roll-out of the NRC access monitoring tool, internally and with NGO partners, to inform programme decision-making and advocacy at country and regional level.
- Draft bi-monthly access reports based on the NRC access monitoring tool, and thematic briefing notes upon request.
- Contribute to regional analyses and advocacy notes in collaboration with the Regional Access Adviser and Regional Head of Advocacy.

**Networking & coordination**

- Build synergies with existing actors and fora (OCHA, ICCG, clusters, civil-military coordination) to ensure AWG-Niger analyses are informed by programmatic and operational priorities.
- Network actively with AWG members, donors, and Country Directors of INGOs and UN agencies to ensure the relevance and visibility of the AWG's contribution.
- Co-represent AWG-Niger in meetings of the regional Task Force on Access.

***Support to the security department (20%)***

- Work with the Security Manager to analyse access-related risks and develop mitigation measures.
- Contribute to the preparation and implementation of security plans, including acceptance, protection, and deterrence approaches.
- Provide advice on engagement with parties to the conflict, including non-state armed groups and state armed forces at the country level, when requested by management.
- A working relationship with the HAS Coordinator based on functional and complementary collaboration, without any hierarchical relationship or line management responsibilities
- Support field security assessments and contribute to strategic decisions on presence and expansion.
- Participate in the management of access incidents and post-incident follow-up.
- Develop and maintain networks of community and security contacts.
- Perform any other task related to HAS and the position, as delegated by the HAS Manager.

**What you will bring**

**1.Professional Competencies**

- Minimum 5 years' experience in humanitarian work in conflict/post-conflict or volatile contexts, including in a senior role.
- Master's degree in a relevant field (or Bachelor's degree with equivalent work experience).
- Demonstrated experience in humanitarian programming and access.
- Strong understanding of humanitarian principles and how to operationalise them within a humanitarian response, including humanitarian access dilemmas.
- Previous experience in complex contexts and participating in access negotiations with an NGO and/or UN agencies.
- Demonstrated excellent writing and analytical skills.
- Fluency in French, both written and verbal.
- Working proficiency in English, both written and verbal.

***Context Related Skills, Knowledge, and Experience***

- Demonstrated experience in and/or knowledge of the Sahel region is a strong asset.
- Experience leading or contributing to coordination forums (AWG/HAWG or equivalent) would be a strong asset.
- Experience with NGOs and the UN system would be an asset.
- Experience in risk management with implementing partners.
- Experience in remote management is an added value.
- Prior experience as a trainer is an added value.

**2.Behavioural competencies**

- Handling insecure environment
- Planning and delivering results
- Working with people
- Analysing
- Communicating with impact and respect
- Coping with change

Find more details [Job Description\_ HAS Adviser Niger.pdf](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:b:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQDGEelbFCxST7N0FnOwT1vKAYFBvIV4weAB9nwtQovLINo?e=P75s2A)

**What we offer**

- Duty station: Niamey, Niger
- Contract: 12 months
- Salary&benefits: grade 8 on NRC’s salary scale (The contract is national/resident)
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.
- Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC [https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)
- Kindly send any questions about the application process to: ***cwa.recruitment@nrc.no***. *Applications sent via email will not be accepted. Please check your application status on your NRC application profile.*

jobs.title: Disaster Preparedness Coordinator - Caracas Venezuela (National/International Staff)
jobs.body:
The Danish Refugee Council is one of the world's leading humanitarian NGOs, working in over 30 countries to provide adequate assistance and protection to refugees, asylum seekers, IDPs, returnees, people on the move, and vulnerable local populations/host communities. Currently, DRC is seeking a highly qualified national o International **Disaster Preparedness Coordinator** based in Caracas, Venezuela.

**About the job:** DRC is managing its operations in Venezuela under the direction of the country office in Caracas and four field offices located in the states of Sucre, Apure, and Zulia (Maracaibo and Santa Barbara de Zulia). DRC Venezuela is implementing an integrated Action encompassing the Protection, Food Security & Livelihood, WASH and Disaster Preparedness sectors.

**The overall purpose of the role**:

The Disaster Preparedness (DP) Coordinator serves as the Danish Refugee Council's (DRC) primary expert for both institutional and community-based disaster readiness measures, with an emphasis on proactive strategies, early warning systems, and developing the resilience of communities and local stakeholders (including the local government) within Venezuela.

This role involves delivering prompt and quality technical guidance to support DRC's execution of initiatives aimed at preparedness and resilience, ensuring that these initiatives are seamlessly integrated with the efforts of DRC teams and collaborative partners.

The DP Coordinator will lead the strategic direction of the sector in Venezuela, positioning DRC as a key actor in both regional and global forums. As the technical lead, the Coordinator will also be responsible for designing donor proposals and driving innovative, impactful programming that reflects DRC’s mandate and vision.

The coordinator’s responsibilities include fostering a synergistic approach among DRC's internal teams and external partners, with the ultimate goal of mitigating the adverse effects of disasters on at-risk populations.

The Disaster Preparedness Coordinator will work closely with Base managers, project teams and partners.

**Responsibilities:**

**Technical support**

- Provide technical support and guidance to DRC Venezuela in the implementation of projects and tools related to Disaster Risk Reduction (DRD), Disaster Preparedness (DP), and Disaster Management (DM) at the organizational, government and community levels linked to anticipatory action, anticipatory early warning, and disaster resilience.
- Monitor and follow up on the implementation of DRC Venezuela projects related to disaster preparedness and resilience.
- Provide technical support for the integration, preparedness, and resilience of disasters into DRC Venezuela's plans and strategy, as appropriate.
- Promote greater understanding of disaster preparedness and resilience terminologies, tools, quality criteria, and approaches.
- Provide technical and operational support for the articulation of preparedness mechanisms in situations of imminent disaster risk, considering anticipatory measures and the link with the implementation of response actions.
- Lead the design and implementation of Anticipatory Action (AA) projects and proposals, develop tools and methodologies to guide programming, and establish systems to measure the impact of DRC’s interventions.

**Coordination and advocacy**

- Liaise DRC Venezuela with relevant inter-institutional and local partners on disaster preparedness and resilience mechanisms to ensure good coordination and identify potential synergies and partnerships.
- Contribute to DRC Venezuela's planning and resource mobilization, e.g., prepare concept notes, lead/participate in the development of projects/program proposals related to disaster preparedness and resilience.
- Co-Lead the AA sub-working group and represent DRC in regional and global forums

**Learning and Knowledge Management**

- Strengthen capacity-building and knowledge-sharing at the organizational and community levels for disaster preparedness and resilience initiatives and processes.
- Provide timely updates and advice on scientific and technical developments, trends, best practices, areas for improvement, and lessons learned.
- Finalize Impact Studies on the implementation of localized AA interventions.

**Planning & Reporting**

- Support the formulation of plans and technical reports.
- Provide feedback and quality assurance to DRC offices and teams in Venezuela on the application of the disaster preparedness and resilience approach with the aim of ensuring integration and scaling up of its approach.
- Participate in coordination meetings, providing technical support and relevant information.
- Technically line-manage DP Team Leaders in Apure and Zulia. Line manages other focal points if recruited.

**Experience and technical competencies**

- 5 years of experience in the humanitarian sector, related to the management of programs and/or operations in Disaster Risk Reduction linked to the strengthening of institutional and community preparedness capacity and emergency response operations.
- 3 years of experience working as a project manager related to disaster risk management and/or preparedness in Latin-America.
- Experience in Developing humanitarian early action and/or early warning systems.
- Good understanding of the global humanitarian environment and in Latin America.
- Good ability to lead multidisciplinary teams.
- Experience in coordination with authorities and other humanitarian actors.
- Experience in designing localized and integrated DP responses.
- Experience in narrative and financial reporting.
- Climate Change Adaptation knowledge is an advantage.

**Education**

- Advanced degree in Disaster Risk Reduction & Management, Urban Planning or another related field is highly preferred, OR
- Advanced degree in social sciences, social work, gender studies, international development / WASH / Rights Based approach / Community Empowerment or related fields, OR
- Advanced degree in Project Management

**Languages**

- Fluency in English (speaking, writing, reading) is essential.
- Communication skills in Spanish is mandatory.

**Key stakeholders**

- Internal: Head of Programme; technical coordinators; Area/Base Managers; Emergency, Economic Recovery, Protection, WASH/Shelter, MEAL, Grants, Finance, Supply Chain, IT/Information Management, and field teams.
- External: relevant inter-agency coordination mechanisms and technical working groups; UN agencies; national and international NGOs; local partners; authorities; donors; financial service providers; private-sector and research actors.

**We offer:**

- The opportunity to be part of one of the best NGOs worldwide.
- Access to over 1,000 free online trainings and certifications.
- Contract duration: subject to budget availability.
- Salary: Band G / Terms of Employment for national or expatriate staff, as applicable
- HCM insurance fully covered by the organization.

**DRC Core Competencies:**

- Achieving Excellence: Focus on achieving results and ensuring efficient processes.
- Collaboration: Engage relevant parties and encourage feedback.
- Taking the Initiative: Take ownership and initiative while seeking innovation.
- Communicating: Listen and speak effectively and honestly.
- Demonstrating Integrity: Act in accordance with DRC's vision and values.

**Application Process:** All applicants must upload a cover letter (max. 1 page) and an updated CV (max. 2 pages, without attachments) in English or Spanish, on the DRC employment platform. Applications sent by email will not be considered.

**Application Deadline:** Sunday, november 1 at 11:59 pm Local Time. Please note that applications will be reviewed continuously, and interviews will be scheduled as soon as a suitable candidate is identified. DRC reserves the right to close the vacancy before the deadline once a suitable candidate is identified.

**Start Date:** November 2026

jobs.title: Administration Senior Assistant
jobs.body:
## **Job Highlight**

The selected candidate for this role will become UNOPS personnel under its full responsibility. The incumbent will work to drive smooth office operations by supporting administration, logistics, and client-focused services.

## **Role Purpose**

The Administration Senior Assistant supports office operations by carrying out a range of standard administrative processes, ensuring accuracy, efficiency and high-quality outcomes.

## **Functions / Key Results Expected**

Administrative Support

- Research and retrieve statistical data from internal and external sources. Prepare statistical charts, tables and reports by extracting and analyzing data from multiple sources.
- Follow up on deadlines, commitments and actions, coordinating the collation and submission of reports as required.
- Provide administrative support for conferences, workshops and retreats, by coordinating with hotels, venues and catering services providers
- Process requests for quotation, purchase orders, and payments for event-related activities.
- Compile and organize information for periodic audits.
- Manage petty cash transactions in accordance with established procedures.

Travel and Logistics

- Process travel transactions (authorizations and claims) in the ERP system, including requests for visas, identity cards, and other documentation for personnel, UN officials and visitors, ensuring compliance with UN rules and regulations.
- Provide information on air services, rates, and schedules for specific itineraries.
- Process travel claims, purchase orders, payments, and contracts for travel-related activities.
- Organize shipments and customs clearance arrangements, ensuring the preparation of all required documentation for UNOPS shipments (incoming and outgoing) and timely follow-up actions.
- Prepare documentation for security clearances.
- Arrange hotel reservations and organize airport pickups, hospitality, protocol, customs, and immigration support for visiting UN System officials.
- Ensure punctual delivery of official protocol certificates and coordinate with UN departments on documentation related to visas, work permits, security requirements, and health clearances for international staff.
- Coordinate with UN departments on import/export or transfer of goods for official purposes.
- Maintain strong working relationships with government ministries.
- Provide accurate, up-to-date information to staff on required supporting documents for themselves and their dependents, including import/export or transfer requirements. Track the status of submitted documentation for staff and dependents through individual monitoring sheets, ensuring adherence to schedules.
- Provide timely updates to individuals or units on administrative steps, project file status, and pending issues.
- Supervise transportation services, ensuring quality client service, regular vehicle maintenance, insurance coverage, and monitoring of fuel consumption.
- Promptly report and investigate vehicle accidents, damage, loss or theft, and update vehicle history reports.
- Oversee external transportation service contractors, including performance monitoring and invoice processing.

Inventory and Facilities Management Support

- Conduct physical inventory checks and prepare periodic inventory and asset reports.
- Serve as custodian for office stationery suppliers, maintaining accurate stock lists, distributing supplies as needed, and keeping detailed distribution logs.
- Conduct and report on surveys assessing office maintenance needs and client satisfaction.
- Gather information for administrative surveys to support the organization and improvement of common services.

Knowledge Building and Sharing

- Provide planning support for logistics, travel, inventory and facilities management-related training sessions and learning initiatives.
- Participate in the delivery and facilitation of knowledge-sharing activities to build administrative, logistics, travel, inventory and facilities management capacity within the organization.

## **Education Requirements**

Required

- Secondary school (or equivalent) with 5 years of relevant experience OR
- Bachelor’s degree (or equivalent) in any discipline with 1 year of relevant experience is required.

Desired

- A globally or nationally recognized professional certificate in administration is desired.

## **Experience Requirements**

Required

- Relevant experience is work in administration, logistics, operations or related areas.
- Experience in the use of collaboration and productivity tools (e.g. MS Office, G-Suite, etc) and web-based management systems is required.

Desired

- Experience of working in multicultural environments or UN system organizations in a developing country is desired.
- Experience in development or humanitarian contexts is desired.

## **Language Requirements**

Fluency in English Required

Fluency in French Desired

jobs.title: Líder de Equipo de Gestión de Casos - Caracas
jobs.body:
El Consejo Dánes para refugiados es una de las ONG humanitarias líderes en el mundo, que trabaja en más de 40 países para brindar asistencia y protección adecuadas a refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, desplazados internos, retornados, personas en movimiento y población local vulnerable/comunidades de acogida. Actualmente, DRC está buscando un **Líder de Equipo de Gestión de Casos** altamente calificado con sede en **base de Caracas.**

**Acerca del trabajo:**

DRC está administrando sus operaciones en Venezuela, bajo la dirección de la oficina de país en Caracas y tres oficinas de campo ubicadas en los estados de Sucre, Apure y Zulia. DRC Venezuela está implementando actividades como monitoreo de protección, asistencia legal, asistencia de protección individual para PWSN, sesiones informativas para PoC, prevención de trata de personas, rehabilitación de infraestructura de salud y seguridad alimentaria.

**Descripción del propósito / objetivo del cargo:**

El Líder de Equipo de Gestión de Casos tendrá su sede en la oficina de Caracas, y será responsable por el desempeño eficaz y profesional de la gestión del equipo multidisciplinario con funciones de gestión de casos de protección y apoyo psicosocial en el terreno, y para apoyar a la Gerencia de Protección de DRC en Caracas. La posición incluye la supervisión de Oficiales, incluyendo el desarrollo de sus capacidades, para las acciones de protección de emergencia.

**Responsabilidades:**

- Establecer y coordinar el sistema de articulación de remisión de casos sea interna o externa en coordinación con el Líder de Equipo de Protección de DRC.
- Analizar, evaluar y averiguar los perfiles de protección de los casos remitidos asegurando la participación de los beneficiarios.
- Asegurar que cada beneficiario reciba orientación a servicios básicos, en el marco de la gestión de casos y del apoyo psicosocial, contando con el consentimiento informado del beneficiario para recibir la asistencia pertinente para abordar las necesidades de protección identificadas; y de conformidad con los principios de confidencialidad.
- Coordinar, planificar y monitorear las actividades del equipo de gestión de casos y apoyo psicosocial en el terreno; incluyendo el seguimiento de los casos.
- Garantizar que los planes de los casos identifiquen claramente los plazos acordados para la ejecución de las medidas que deben tomarse; y asegurar que los casos sean cerrados en el tiempo oportuno, de acuerdo con el marco de emergencia en el cual se implementa.
- Mantener una cooperación estrecha con las contrapartes gubernamentales y los actores humanitarios para fortalecer la ruta pública, así como la ruta de la cooperación humanitaria en el marco del mecanismo de remisión establecido.
- Trabajar activamente con el departamento administrativo y logístico de DRC para la provisión de servicios de asistencia humanitaria, entre los cuales figuran los servicios médicos, servicios de alojamiento de emergencia, servicios de transporte; y entrega en especie de artículos para abordar las necesidades específicas de protección.
- En coordinación con el departamento administrativo y logístico de DRC, asegurar que los procesos de compra sean correctamente implementado y legalizados.
- Apoyar la/el gerente de protección en el desarrollo de una base de datos para la gestión de casos.
- Mantener contacto constante con la línea técnica de apoyo psicosocial, garantizando la participación del personal de este subprograma en capacitaciones y reuniones con la línea técnica.
- Supervisar la base de datos y garantizar la actualización de esta, de manera correcta y organizada.
- Elaborar informes semanales y mensuales de alta calidad de desafíos encontrados y resultados logrados.

**Programación y Operaciones**

- Asegurar la implementación eficiente y efectiva del proyecto de acuerdo con el plan de trabajo y IPTT.
- Elaborar informes y participar a la escritura de propuestas y presupuestos mensuales / trimestrales / anuales para donantes.
- Certificar que los casos identificados, sean personas de interés según los criterios fijados por DRC, y asegurar acciones apropiadas de asistencia humanitaria interna.
- Garantizar que la documentación de los casos proporciona información adecuada para priorizar como de bajo, medio o alto riesgo y que las medidas del plan de casos abordan las necesidades y los riesgos identificados.
- Liderar el equipo de gestión de casos en la evaluación de casos y la provisión de asistencia humanitaria. Garantizar que los servicios directos se prestan de acuerdo con el plan del caso, así como el seguimiento y el cierre.

**Coordinación y representación.**

- Mantenerse en contacto con las autoridades locales, los proveedores de servicios y los actores humanitarios para el fortalecimiento de rutas de atención efectivas.
- Colaborar con expertos técnicos internos y externos en temas relevantes del sector.
- Representar a DRC en reuniones internas y externas, de coordinación técnica relevantes, etc.
- Asegurar la integración con otros sectores de DRC, incluido MEAL.

**Desarrollo del proyecto**

- Preparar planes de trabajo y cronogramas por el equipo de gestión de casos.
- Apoyar al Gerente de Protección en la preparación y desarrollo de planes de trabajo a largo plazo.
- Participar en el desarrollo de herramientas de proyectos.
- Asegurar la actualización de las bases de datos de gestión de casos.
- Reportar cualquier problema en la implementación o inconformidad al gerente de protección.
- Asegurar cumplimiento con la política de protección de datos en todas las fases del proyecto.

**Logística / Finanzas**

- Apoyar la supervisión de los compromisos financieros y los gastos y proporcionar información oportuna sobre el seguimiento del presupuesto.
- Planificar y coordinar proactivamente la logística y los movimientos de personal desde y hacia diferentes áreas operativas.
- Iniciar adquisiciones y garantizar su ejecución.
- Asegurar que los planes de entrega de la asistencia humanitaria estén preparados y compartidos con logística de manera oportuna.

**Responsabilidades de supervisor:**

- Coordinar las actividades diarias del equipo de gestión de casos en terreno.
- Contribuir al reclutamiento y encargarse de la evaluación del desempeño de los miembros del equipo de gestión de caso.
- Implementar las decisiones del Gerente de Protección a través del trabajo del resto del equipo de protección, a menudo jugando un papel en la decisión de cómo hacerlo y cómo lograr el objetivo fijado por el gerente.
- Garantizar el cumplimiento de cada persona del equipo con los estandartes y procedimiento de DRC (incluido CoC y reglamento interno) y reportar faltas de acuerdo con los procedimientos.
- Asesorar al resto del equipo de gestión de casos, sobre rutas de gestión y desarrollo de planes de acción para la atención de los beneficiarios.

**Competencias esenciales:**

- Mínimo 3 años de experiencia relevante en protección humanitaria, relacionado a una ONG, agencia de la ONU u otra organización sin fines de lucro.
- Experiencia de terreno y de trabajo en protección en zonas vulnerables de ciudades. Experiencia en la supervisión de equipo y preparación de planes de trabajo.
- Excelente habilidad y experiencia progresa en el manejo de base de datos y uso de Excel. Experiencia en el análisis de datos cuantitativos y cualitativos.
- Habilidades de escritura por encima del promedio. Excelente habilidad en MS Word
- Experiencia en provisión de servicios de asistencia humanitaria, contando con habilidades organizativas y experiencia en logística/finanza.
- Habilidades y experiencia en capacitación y desarrollo de capacidades de personal inexperto. Experiencia con medidas de responsabilidad y cumplimiento con los requisitos de DRC y sus donantes.

*Deseable:*

- Carácter diplomático.
- Capacidad para gestionar las prioridades en competencia y cumplir con los plazos.
- Capacidad de crear buen ambiente de equipo.
- Dominio de la lengua inglés es una ventaja.

**Educación (Incluir certificados, licencias)**

- Titulo profesional en Psicología, Trabajo Social u otra profesión de ciencias sociales.

**Idiomas:**

- Fluidez en inglés ( Deseable )escrito y hablado

**Ofrecemos:**

- La oportunidad de pertenecer a una de las mejores ONGs a nivel mundial.
- Acceso a más de 1,000 capacitaciones y certificados en línea gratuita.
- Duración del contrato: según disponibilidad presupuestal.
- Salario: **Banda G.**
- Seguro HCM cubierto en su totalidad por la organización.

**Competencias Básicas de DRC:**

- **Lograr la excelencia**: centrarse en alcanzar resultados y garantizar procesos eficientes.
- **Colaboración:** involucrar a las partes relevantes y alentar la retroalimentación.
- **Tomar la iniciativa**: tomar posesión e iniciativa mientras se busca la innovación.
- **Comunicar:** escuchar y hablar con eficacia y honestidad.
- **Demostración de integridad**:

**Proceso de solicitud:** Todos los solicitantes deben cargar una carta de presentación (máx. 1 página) y un CV actualizado (**máx. 2 páginas, sin soportes**) en español, en la plataforma de empleo de DRC. Las solicitudes enviadas por correo electrónico no serán consideradas.

**Fecha de cierre de solicitudes**: Miércoles 04 de Noviembre a las 11:59 pm Hora Local. Tenga en cuenta que las solicitudes se revisarán continuamente y las entrevistas se planificarán tan pronto como se identifique a un candidat@ adecuado. DRC se reserva el derecho a cerrar la vacante antes de la fecha límite una vez se identifique a un candidato idóneo.

**Fecha de inicio aproximada:** Noviembre 2026

jobs.title: Project Director, Virtual Services
jobs.body:
**Job Overview:**

The Project Director of Virtual Services at the International Rescue Committee (IRC) provides strategic leadership and operational oversight of a national portfolio of virtual resettlement programs that expand access to essential services for refugees and other newcomers across the United States, particularly those living outside traditional service areas. The portfolio includes legacy resettlement programs, state-run programs as well as [ALMA](https://welcome.rescue.org/us/en/services/alma), an AI-powered virtual assistant that helps newcomers navigate essential resources and services. The Project Director also contributes to the Resettlement, Asylum and Integration Department’s virtual and information services strategy.

The role oversees virtual program strategy, implementation, performance, and budget management. It also ensures compliance with award requirements through programmatic monitoring and rigorous direct assistance operations, and it oversees the case management and data systems that support reporting and evidence of impact. The Director leads a geographically dispersed team and cultivates partnerships with government agencies, nonprofit organizations, and other stakeholders. A central focus of the position is developing and scaling innovative, technology-enabled service delivery models that strengthen operational efficiency and promote client self-sufficiency. This position reports to the Senior Director of Resettlement.

**Major Responsibilities:**

- **Program Implementation**: Lead the design, implementation, and scaling of a national portfolio of virtual programs (some examples include Program of Initial Resettlement, Matching Grant, Preferred Communities) that expand access to essential services for refugees and other newcomers across the United States, leveraging innovative, client-centered service delivery models to reach underserved populations.
- **Interagency Collaboration:** Provide strategic leadership and oversight of interagency virtual services working groups, fostering collaboration and alignment across resettlement agencies to inform program strategy, coordinate implementation, and strengthen virtual service delivery.
- **People & Culture:** Build and cultivate an inclusive, impactful team. Support managers in their leadership of teams in line with IRC's People Manager Standards to ensure successful program delivery and a safe, supportive environment for clients and staff.
- **Monitoring & Compliance:** Design and enable effective monitoring, evaluation, and reporting on program services. Ensure a data-driven approach that informs program adaptation and provides further evidence of virtual services impact.
- **Budget & Financial Management:** Coordinate with HQ Finance staff to ensure compliance with donor and organizational requirements including financial planning, expenditure monitoring, caseload forecasting, and effective resource allocation.
- **AI Product Strategy and Management:** Lead the product strategy, development, and deployment of ALMA, IRC's AI-powered virtual assistant, in collaboration with the Airbel Impact Lab and IRC's technical development teams. Oversee product roadmaps, iterative development, testing, and the rollout of new features and international adaptations, including expansion to Poland.
- **Client Engagement and Co-Design:** Lead IRC's Service Excellence Advisory Committee, creating structured opportunities for refugees and other newcomers to inform program design, implementation, and continuous improvement. Integrate client feedback and lived experiences into service delivery, technology development, and strategic decision-making.
- **Technical Expertise and Resource Mobilization:** Provide technical expertise and strategic input into the development of grant proposals, funding opportunities, and program designs that expand and strengthen virtual service delivery across IRC's resettlement network. Identify and apply for opportunities to advance virtual services.
- **Strategic Partnerships and Stakeholder Engagement:** Cultivate and maintain partnerships with government agencies, national resettlement organizations, and other key stakeholders to advance virtual service delivery, strengthen interagency coordination, and identify opportunities for program expansion.
- Other related duties as assigned.

**Job Requirements:**

***Work Experience:***

- Minimum 5-7 years of progressively responsible work experience with refugee resettlement; experience and deep familiarity with initial resettlement programming.
- 3-4 years of program management experience; experience scaling program response preferred.
- Significant staff management, program development, monitoring, and evaluation experience.

***Education:***

- Master's degree in non-profit management, social work, sociology, migration studies, law, or international development or equivalent preferred.

***Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:***

- Demonstrated ability to promote an organizational culture that reflects IRC’s core values of service, accountability, integrity, and equality. Ability to lead in a way that recognizes that IRC’s work is best accomplished through the true collaboration of individuals from many cultures with a great variety of skills and perspectives.

- Financial management, including effective management of contract-based budgets.

- Proven people management skills; demonstrated ability to deliver results and translate words into action.

- Superior organizational skills: ability to set priorities and effectively manage time in a fast-paced team environment.

- Strong communication skills, both written and verbal.
- Strong digital literacy, including MS Office suite, database systems.

- Familiarity with generative AI in client settings.

***Language Skills:***

- Fluency in written and spoken English.

**Working Environment*****:***

- Fully remote.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $85,000 - $105,00/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

jobs.title: Programme Management Consultant
jobs.body:
**Functional title:** Programme Management Consultant

**Duty station of assignment:** Istanbul, Türkiye

**Contract modality:** International ICA

**Grade:** IICA-2 equivalent

**Duration of assignment:** 6 months

**Closing date for applications:** 30 October 2026

## Background

The United Nations Human Settlements Programme (UN-Habitat) is the agency for human settlements. It is mandated by the UN General Assembly to promote socially and environmentally sustainable towns and cities with the goal of providing adequate shelter for all.

The Regional Office for Eastern Europe and Central Asia (ROEECA) leads UN-Habitat’s efforts to promote sustainable urban development across the region by supporting national and local governments in advancing inclusive, resilient, and resource-efficient cities. ROEECA is being established to facilitate regional cooperation, policy development, and capacity building to strengthen urban systems, including sustainable solid waste management and circular economy approaches. Through technical assistance, project development, and partnerships, ROEECA will support the transition towards zero-waste systems that integrate social inclusion, gender equality, and environmental sustainability, while mobilizing investments and scaling innovative solutions aligned with regional priorities and global commitments.

Urban Basic Services, including zero-waste is a core pillar of UN-Habitat’s work on sustainable urban basic services, promoting waste prevention, reduction, reuse, recycling, and recovery while avoiding disposal practices that harm health and the environment. In line with the United Nations General Assembly resolution 77/161 and the work of the UN Secretary-General’s Advisory Board on Zero Waste, UN-Habitat supports cities and regions in transitioning towards zero-waste systems that are inclusive, re-source-efficient, and socially just.

## Purpose of the assignment

To support programme and project development and provide technical expertise on zero waste and social inclusion in Eastern Europe and Central Asia, with a specific focus on circularity and integrating gender equality and disability inclusion into waste management policies, data systems, and programmes. The assignment will include coordination of regional zero-waste initiatives, development of technical publications, project proposals and engagement with United Nations Country Teams (UNCTs).

## Duties and main responsibilities

Under the overall supervision of the ROEECA Regional Director and in close coordination with the Chief, Urban Basic Services Section (UBSS), the incumbent will undertake the following duties:

- Facilitate coordination between ROEECA, UBSS, and relevant regional and country-level initiatives related to zero-waste and social inclusion.
- Coordinate the development of project concepts and proposals and support the regional roll-out and contextualization of zero-waste approaches and circularity, aligned with UN-Habitat regional priorities and the strategic plan.
- Provide technical expertise on zero waste and social inclusion, including waste prevention, organic waste management, recycling systems, and recovery solutions.
- Identify policy, institutional, and infrastructure gaps hindering the transition to zero-waste systems, with particular attention to impacts on women, persons with disabilities, and vulnerable groups.
- Represent ROEECA, as required, in technical meetings, webinars, and knowledge exchanges related to Urban Basic Services, zero-waste and inclusion.
- Support the integration of social inclusion and gender equality into project development, implementation and related technical outputs.
- Support partnership development and resource mobilization by identifying funding opportunities, engaging relevant partners and contributing to the preparation of project concepts and funding proposals.
- Perform other related duties as required.

The assignment will focus on the development of zero-waste technical publications, coordination of relevant global and regional initiatives, preparation of project concepts and funding proposals, and technical support to priority country engagements. Detailed deliverables, timelines and payment arrangements will be established in accordance with the applicable contractual procedures.

## Competencies

**Professionalism:** Knowledge in the project management cycle and of project lifetimes, from resource mobilization and inception to implementation, evaluation and audit. Ability to identify issues, analyze and participate in the resolution of issues/problems. Ability to conduct data collection using various methods. Conceptual analytical and evaluative skills to conduct independent research and analysis, including familiarity with and experience in the use of various research sources, including electronic sources on the internet, intranet and other databases. Ability to apply judgment in the context of assignments given, plan own work and manage conflicting priorities. The ability to analyze and interpret data in support of decision-making and convey resulting information to management. Shows pride in work and in achievements; demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter; is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines and achieving results; is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns; shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges; remains calm in stressful situations. Takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work. **Planning and Organising:** Develops clear goals that are consistent with agreed strategies; identifies priority activities and assignments; adjusts priorities as required; allocates appropriate amount of time and resources for completing work; foresees risks and allows for contingencies when planning; monitors and adjusts plans and actions as necessary; uses time efficiently. **Client Orientation:** Considers all those to whom services are provided to be "clients" and seeks to see things from clients' point of view; establishes and maintains productive partnerships with clients by gaining their trust and respect; identifies clients' needs and matches them to appropriate solutions; monitors ongoing developments inside and outside the clients' environment to keep informed and anticipate problems; keeps clients informed of progress or setbacks in projects; meets timeline for delivery of products or services to client.

## Required Skills and Experience

### Education

- Advanced university degree (Master's degree or equivalent) in international development, international affairs, environmental management, urban planning, public policy or a related field is required.
- A first-level university degree in combination with two (2) additional years of qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree.

### Experience

- A minimum of five (5) years of relevant professional experience in project management, programme coordination, municipal solid waste management or a related field, including experience in project development, is required. Candidates holding a first-level university degree (Bachelor's degree or equivalent) must have a minimum of seven (7) years of relevant professional experience.
- Experience in sustainable solid waste management, zero-waste initiatives or circular economy approaches is desirable.
- Experience in programme management in Eastern Europe and Central Asia is desirable.

### Language

- English and French are the working languages of the United Nations Secretariat. For this position, fluency in English is required. Knowledge of another official UN language is desirable.

jobs.title: République Démocratique du Congo : Volontaire Finance Pays – Kinshasa
source: Agency for Technical Cooperation and Development
jobs.body:
**Volontariat (CEV) | 6 mois | Novembre 2026**

## Acted

***Qui sommes-nous***

Acted travaille avec 19 millions de personnes dans 43 pays au carrefour de l’humanitaire, du développement, et des programmes climatiques et environnementaux. Grâce à une connaissance poussée des contextes et l’adoption de technologies émergentes, nous sauvons des vies, allégeons les souffrances, et protégeons et restaurons notre planète. Travaillant avec un écosystème croissant de partenaires locaux, nationaux et internationaux, nous poursuivons un objectif commun : un monde 3Zéro : Zéro Exclusion, Zéro Carbone, Zéro Pauvreté.

***Qui cherchons-nous***

Vous apportez les compétences clefs attendues d’un travailleur humanitaire et de développement, mais également une conscience climatique et environnementale active, et vous pouvez naviguez les défis qui émergent lorsque les souffrances environnementale et humaine se rencontrent. Vous avez l’esprit entrepreneurial : vous décelez les opportunités, connectez les points, adaptez votre approche aux différents environnements, et vous prenez des risques mesurés dans la poursuite de résultats. Vous alliez les principes au pragmatisme, et l’ambition à l’humilité.

## Acted République Démocratique du Congo

La République Démocratique du Congo fait face à une crise humanitaire prolongée, marquée par la persistance des conflits armés, des déplacements massifs de populations, des chocs climatiques et des chocs épidémiques récurrents, tels que le choléra, le mpox ou la rougeole. Ces dynamiques combinées affectent durablement les conditions de vie des populations déplacées, retournées et hôtes, en particulier dans les provinces de l’Est et certaines zones de l’Ouest du pays.

Dans ce contexte, Acted intervient principalement dans les provinces du Sud-Kivu, Nord-Kivu, Tanganyika, Nord-Ubangi et Sud-Ubangi, à travers des projets financés notamment par le Department of State / US, ECHO, FCDO, SDC, le Fonds Humanitaire, ainsi que le CDCS, afin de répondre aux besoins humanitaires immédiats et aux vulnérabilités persistantes des populations les plus affectées. Afin de renforcer la couverture et la complémentarité de ses interventions, Acted intervient en coordination avec plusieurs partenaires opérationnels, et est membre de consortiums humanitaires.

Cette coordination permet à Acted de mettre en œuvre des réponses d’urgence rapides et multisectorielles pour couvrir les besoins vitaux liés aux conflits, aux déplacements forcés, aux catastrophes naturelles et aux crises sanitaires. Les interventions portent notamment sur l’assistance alimentaire, les abris et articles ménagers essentiels, l’Eau, Hygiène et Assainissement (EHA), la gestion et coordination des sites (CCCM) ainsi que l’éducation en situation d’urgence, avec une attention particulière portée, dès le premier kilomètre humanitaire, à la protection et à la dignité des personnes vulnérables. Au Sud-Kivu, Acted est par ailleurs un acteur clé du Mécanisme de Réponse Rapide (RRM), contribuant à des réponses rapides et coordonnées en lien avec les déplacements de populations et aux chocs soudains.

En parallèle, Acted développe des interventions visant à renforcer la résilience des communautés, à travers le soutien aux moyens d’existence, la relance agricole, la sécurité alimentaire et la relance économique locale, afin de réduire la vulnérabilité face aux chocs récurrents.

Acted apporte également un appui structurant aux organisations de la société civile (OSC) en renforçant leurs capacités organisationnelles et opérationnelles. Cet accompagnement inclut l’appui à la structuration des initiatives locales ainsi que la mise en place de mécanismes de financement en cascade, permettant aux OSC de développer des activités directement liées aux problématiques locales et aux priorités identifiées par les communautés.

Enfin, Acted intègre progressivement dans ses programmes des approches sensibles à l’environnement, visant à la préservation des écosystèmes et des aires protégées, à la réduction de l’empreinte environnementale des interventions et à la promotion de solutions à faible émission de carbone. À travers l’appui aux communautés, Acted encourage le développement d’activités génératrices de revenus durables et d’une économie locale plus verte, contribuant à la protection des ressources naturelles tout en renforçant les moyens d’existence.

## Rôle et responsabilités principales

Sous l’autorité du responsable finances pays, le volontaire finances sera chargé d’assister l’équipe pays finances sur le contrôle financier interne de la mission. Plus spécifiquement il sera en charge de la vérification et du recoupement des données comptables (PRATIC), de la gestion financière et des outils de contrôle des données (TITANIC).

***Principales responsabilités***

1\. Contribuer à la conformité comptable d’Acted

2\. Contrôle des outils mensuels de reporting

- *Révision comptable*
- *Revue finances*
- *Contrôle des coûts*
- *RH suivi*

3\. Apporter son aide aux tâches quotidiennes

## Qualifications et compétences requises

- Master en Finance, Audit, Business Management ou équivalent ;
- Compétences en finance et comptabilité ;
- Maîtrise de Microsoft Office, en particulier de Microsoft Excel (maîtrise des principales formules de gestion de base de données) ;
- Capacités à prendre des responsabilités et à travailler sous pression ;
- Excellentes qualités de communication, excellentes qualités rédactionnelles en français et en anglais ;
- Maîtrise totale du Pack Office.

## Termes de référence

Pour plus d'informations sur le poste, [cliquez ici ](https://www.acted.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/cfv-rdc-2026.pdf).

## Conditions

Statut : volontaire (convention de stage non obligatoire)

- Living allowance de 300 USD
- Logement en guesthouse et nourriture pris en charge par Acted
- Sécurité sociale, mutuelle (MSH) et assistance rapatriement (SOS International) pris en charge par Acted
- Transport vers la mission et billet retour totalement pris en charge (vers l’adresse spécifiée sur le contrat de travail)
- Frais de visa pris en charge par Acted
- Une semaine de préparation au départ comprenant 4 jours de formation sécurité en immersion
- Soutien psychologique (rendez-vous avec un.e professionnel.le)
- Ce poste est classé comme un poste international dans la grille de recrutement d’Acted. L’éligibilité à un contrat international est donc requise.

jobs.title: Oficial de Recuperación Económica - Carúpano
jobs.body:
El Consejo Dánes para refugiados es una de las ONG humanitarias líderes en el mundo, que trabaja en más de 40 países para brindar asistencia y protección adecuadas a refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, desplazados internos, retornados, personas en movimiento y población local vulnerable/comunidades de acogida. Actualmente, DRC está buscando un Oficial de Recuperación Económica altamente calificado con sede en Carúpano Estado Sucre, Venezuela.

**Acerca del trabajo:**

DRC está administrando sus operaciones en Venezuela, bajo la dirección de la oficina de país en Caracas y tres oficinas de campo ubicadas en los estados de Sucre, Apure y Zulia. DRC Venezuela está implementando actividades como monitoreo de protección, asistencia legal, asistencia de protección individual para PWSN, sesiones informativas para PoC, prevención de trata de personas, rehabilitación de infraestructura de salud y seguridad alimentaria.

**Descripción general del cargo**

Bajo la supervisión de la Gerencia de Recuperación Económica, el Oficial de Recuperación Económica apoyará en la implementación operativa del proyecto en terreno, facilitando la ejecución técnica de las actividades de **seguridad alimentaria y medios de vida (SAMV)**, asegurando la transversalización de la protección y garantizando la calidad, participación y rendición de cuentas durante todo el proceso. El/la Oficial de recuperación económica garantizará que se desarrollen todas las actividades del plan de acción y se compilen todos los medios de verificación para la adecuada entrega. Adicionalmente, mantendrá buena comunicación con los miembros del equipo y garantizará el buen desarrollo del personal a su cargo.

**Responsabilidades:**

**Implementación técnica y logística:**

- Apoyar en la planificación, organización y supervisión de jornadas de Distribución General de Alimentos.
- Verificar las condiciones de seguridad, accesibilidad y dignidad del sitio de distribución, garantizando el estricto cumplimiento de los protocolos humanitarios y los estándares de donantes.
- Garantizar la adecuada recepción, conciliación, distribución y registro de los paquetes alimentarios y ayudas humanitarias a la población objetivo.
- Coordinar junto al equipo de logística y protección el desarrollo de las actividades del proyecto, tales como la distribución de asistencia, aplicación de encuestas de seguridad alimentaria, desarrollo de talleres comunitarios y evaluaciones de necesidades en el terreno.
- Coordinar con el equipo de protección el acompañamiento de las actividades en el territorio para asegurar un enfoque de "No Hacer Daño" (Do No Harm).
- Garantizar la transversalización de la protección, el género y la inclusión en todas las entregas de asistencia alimentaria, acorde con los lineamientos establecidos por la organización y el donante.
- Realizar diagnósticos socioeconómicos y evaluaciones de seguridad alimentaria a personas de interés y comunidades vulnerables identificadas en terreno.
- Elaborar planes de mejora individualizados enfocados en el fortalecimiento, la diversificación o la reactivación de los medios de vida y la resiliencia comunitaria.
- Coordinar y entregar apoyos en especie (como insumos productivos, herramientas, equipos, etc.) de acuerdo con las necesidades identificadas y los planes de reactivación económica.
- Otras actividades necesarias para la correcta implementación y el cumplimiento de las metas del proyecto.

**Participación comunitaria:**

- Facilitar procesos de información transparente, convocatoria oportuna y participación de la comunidad que permitan el acceso seguro y una sólida aceptación comunitaria.
- Monitorear la participación y accesibilidad de grupos vulnerables (mujeres, personas mayores, personas con discapacidad) a los puntos de distribución, identificando y mitigando barreras específicas.
- Garantizar la difusión y el acceso de la comunidad a los Mecanismos de Quejas, Reclamos y Retroalimentación (FCRM) de la organización y del donante durante las actividades.
- Apoyar a su referente técnico y Gerente de Base en la realización de mapeos de actores clave y posibles aliados institucionales o comunitarios en las zonas de interés

**Monitoreo y reporte**

- Garantizar la recopilación oportuna y el resguardo de los medios de verificación requeridos (listas de asistencia, actas de entrega, registros fotográficos) y datos cualitativos del proyecto.

jobs.title: Associate, Malaria and NTDs
jobs.body:
## **Overview**

The Clinton Health Access Initiative, Inc. (CHAI) is a global health organization committed to our mission of saving lives and reducing the burden of disease in low-and middle-income countries. We work at the invitation of governments to support them and the private sector to create and sustain high-quality health systems.

CHAI was founded in 2002 in response to the HIV/AIDS epidemic with the goal of dramatically reducing the price of life-saving drugs and increasing access to these medicines in the countries with the highest burden of the disease. Over the following two decades, CHAI has expanded its focus. Today, along with HIV, we work with our partners to prevent and treat infectious diseases such as COVID-19, malaria, tuberculosis, and hepatitis. Our work has also expanded into cancer, diabetes, hypertension, and other non-communicable diseases, and we work to accelerate the rollout of lifesaving vaccines, reduce maternal and child mortality, combat chronic malnutrition, and increase access to assistive technology. We are investing in horizontal approaches to strengthen health systems through programs in human resources for health, digital health, and health financing. With each new and innovative program, our strategy is grounded in maximizing sustainable impact at scale, ensuring that governments lead the solutions, that programs are designed to scale nationally, and learnings are shared globally.

At CHAI, our people are our greatest asset, and none of this work would be possible without their talent, time, dedication, and passion for our mission and values. We are a highly diverse team of enthusiastic individuals across 40 countries with a broad range of skill sets and life experiences. CHAI is deeply grounded in the countries we work in, with the majority of our staff based in program countries. Learn more about our exciting work: [http://www.clintonhealthaccess.org](http://www.clintonhealthaccess.org/).

*CHAI is an Equal Opportunity Employer, and is committed to providing an environment of fairness, and mutual respect where all applicants have access to equal employment opportunities. CHAI values diversity and inclusion, and recognizes that our mission is best advanced by the leadership and contributions of people with diverse experience, backgrounds, and culture.*

**Position Overview**

Your responsibilities will involve supporting the malaria program in scaling up interventions to effectively reduce the disease burden in Angola. The selected candidate will be responsible for a wide range of tasks, from conducting quantitative and qualitative analyses, to designing data-driven strategic plans, to providing operational support to ensure the execution of effective, high-impact programs. The Associate will develop and maintain strong relationships with CHAI teams supporting the malaria program, as well as with relevant government, technical, and implementing partners. They will also identify areas for intervention related to improvements in vector control, surveillance, and program implementation, and be able to initiate work plans to address these issues quickly and with limited guidance.

The candidate must have excellent analytical, problem-solving, organizational, communication, and project management skills, as well as strong cultural sensitivity and emotional intelligence. The selected candidate must embody CHAI's values, including resourcefulness, patience, tenacity, humility, independence, frugality, and a strong work ethic.

The position will be based in Luanda, with frequent travel to Angola's provinces and occasional international travel.

## **Responsibilities**

- Provide technical assistance to the national malaria program to refine malaria control interventions.
- Support the development and monitoring of government strategies, roadmaps, and costed work plans.
- Work with CHAI colleagues and government counterparts to assess strategies, identify and prioritize resource gaps, and develop new funding proposals for the country.
- Contribute to the drafting, review, and feedback of technical products, which may include strategic plans, guidelines, grant proposals, donor reports, or implementation updates.
- Contribute to the design and execution of monitoring and evaluation to measure progress toward malaria control objectives (analysis of key indicators, design, and execution of monitoring and evaluation of surveillance platforms, etc.).
- Monitor program activities against project objectives and donor commitments, identify bottlenecks or operational shortcomings, and work collaboratively with national and global CHAI teams to achieve exceptional results within tight timelines.
- Identify new opportunities within and beyond the project's initial scope, anticipate risks, and be proactive in responding to them.
- Support the drafting of programmatic reports for government and donors, as well as concept notes or other external communication products.
- Perform any other duties requested by management.

## **Qualifications**

- Professional fluency in Portuguese and English, with excellent written and verbal communication skills in both languages.
- Bachelor's degree and two to three years of relevant professional experience.
- High level of proficiency in the MS Office suite, particularly Excel and PowerPoint.
- Ability to work independently and autonomously, balancing multiple tasks simultaneously.
- Exceptional analytical, quantitative, and problem-solving skills.
- Ability to deliver persuasive presentations and reports.
- Ability to think strategically while maintaining strong organizational skills and a detail-oriented approach.
- Ability to manage multiple tasks simultaneously and set priorities.
- Excellent interpersonal skills and a proven ability to build and maintain strong relationships in a multicultural environment.
- Willingness to travel frequently (30-50 percent of the time), including occasional travel to rural areas.

**Preferred qualifications**

- A master's degree or postgraduate qualification.
- Prior knowledge of malaria control and infectious diseases.
- Experience working in resource-limited settings, particularly in Angola.
- Fluency in at least one relevant local language.
- Prior experience working in fast-paced, results-oriented environments, such as consulting, management, investment banking, or industry.
- Experience working and communicating with government officials, multilateral organizations, or development donors.
- Experience working remotely with a decentralized/remote team.
- Experience working in developing-country contexts.

jobs.title: Data Entry Assistants
jobs.body:
**POSITION INFORMATION**

- **Organization:** UNDP Lebanon Through Stars Orbit Consultants and Management Development
- **VA No.: UNDP/LBN/VA26/203**
- **Position Title**: Data Entry Assistants
- **Duty Station:** Beirut
- **Duration:** 2 Months (without exceeding 18 working days per month)
- **Vacancy Date of Issue: 21 October 2026**
- **Vacancy Closure Date: 28 October 2026**
- **National or International consultancy:** National consultancy

To review the full Terms of Reference (TOR), please follow link:

[https://drive.google.com/file/d/1T8NzJatEZrMJtUOG7VOGUkM1-S9Ncvbm/view?usp=sharing](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1T8NzJatEZrMJtUOG7VOGUkM1-S9Ncvbm/view?usp=sharing)

**BACKGROUND**

Lebanon stands at a pivotal juncture in its governance and reform trajectory. Despite years of overlapping crises, the country has made landmark progress in building an integrity and anti-corruption framework, including the adoption and (partial) implementation of the National Anti-Corruption Strategy (2020–2025), the establishment of the National Anti-Corruption Commission (NACC), and major legislative reforms on access to information, illicit enrichment, whistleblower protection, asset declaration, and public procurement. These milestones have laid the groundwork for the most coherent accountability architecture in Lebanon’s recent history.

However, these achievements remain fragile amid deep economic collapse, weakened institutions, and eroded public trust. While the strategic and legal frameworks are largely in place, implementation and enforcement mechanisms remain underdeveloped, and coordination among oversight institutions is still limited. The evaluation of the NACS highlighted the urgent need to consolidate progress by operationalizing national mechanisms, strengthening institutional capacities, and embedding corruption-risk management practices across public institutions.

In this context, the Integrity in ACTion Project is founded with the objective of improving the implementation of an institutionalised and targeted approach to prevent and combat corruption through improved coordination, operationalized oversight, enhanced preventive and enforcement mechanisms, and institutionalized integrity and risk-management practices, thereby advancing transparency, accountability, and public trust. The Project is designed to achieve this objective by working on three outputs:

Output 1: Institutional capacities to coordinate, monitor, and evaluate the National Anti-Corruption Strategy strengthened and operationalized through participatory and inclusive mechanisms.

Output 2: Legal frameworks and oversight institutions for preventing and combating corruption strengthened and effectively operationalized.

Output 3: Sectoral Corruption Risk Management mechanisms and integrity systems strengthened across key public sectors.

Under output 3, “Sectoral Corruption Risk Management mechanisms and integrity systems strengthened across key public sectors.”, the Ministry of Industry, in collaboration with UNDP, is working to integrate the Sectoral Corruption Risk Management (SCRM) Methodology into its core regulatory functions. This partnership seeks to strengthen institutional integrity, reduce opportunities for corruption, and reinforce rule-based decision-making in the industrial licensing process. By applying the SCRM framework to the directorates/sections responsible for Industrial Permits and Certificates, the initiative has aimed to identify systemic vulnerabilities, enhance risk awareness among staff, and promote a culture of accountability. Furthermore, the Ministry of Industry (MoI) plays a central role in regulating Lebanon’s industrial sector and ensuring compliance with national standards and licensing requirements. At the heart of this mandate lies the responsibility to oversee the issuance of Industrial Permits and Certificates, an essential function for enabling lawful industrial activity, protecting the environment, and promoting sustainable economic development.

Building on UNDP’s support to the ministry of Industry, UNDP is seeking to contract admin assistants to support the ministry in organizing the Ministry's records of industrial permits and industrial certificates into a structured database. The database will use consistent fields and unique identifiers so that it can later be linked to the digitized inspection system. This will also allow the Ministry to track each establishment's permits, certificates, inspections and compliance status over time, and to update them as new inspections are carried out.

**SCOPE OF WORK, RESPONSIBILITIES AND DESCRIPTION OF THE PROPOSED ANALYTICAL WORK**

Under the general supervision of the UNDP IACT manager, and in close coordination with the NACC, the Admin Assistants will support coordination, documentation, and administrative follow-up functions. The Admin Assistant will be responsible for the following:

- Review the Ministry’s existing permit and certificate files and recording practices. Prepare a short inception note with a work plan, the proposed approach, and a timeline, and agree on it with the technical committee.
- Propose and finalize, in coordination with the committee, the database structure. This includes standardized fields, data formats, and a unique identifier for each establishment and each permit or certificate. The design should allow the database to be linked later to the digitized inspection system.
- Review existing permit and certificate files and sort them, for example:
    - by document type (industrial permit or industrial certificate)
    - by the five UIIS industrial clusters
    - by subsector and activity classification
- Initiate data entry for each establishment, record the key information, including but not limited to:
    - permit or certificate number
    - issue and expiry dates
    - current status
    - location
    - available inspection and compliance records
- Apply the filtering and classification criteria agreed by the technical committee consistently across all records.
- Identify and flag incomplete, duplicate, or inconsistent records. Maintain a log of flagged records and submit it to the committee for review and decision.
- Update the database as files are verified or corrected by the committee, so that the database stays accurate and current.
- Prepare a brief user guide or data dictionary describing the fields, codes, and update procedures.
- Submit a final report at the end of the assignment, summarizing records processed, data gaps identified, and recommendations for maintaining the database and integrating it with the inspection system.
- Ensure that all information is handled with strict confidentiality, in line with Ministry and UNDP rules. The consultant will not take part in any decision on individual applications, permits, certificates, or files.

**EXPECTED OUTPUTS AND DELIVERABLES**
