jobs.title: Provincial Health Extender
jobs.body:
Overview of position

- In 2021 an L3 emergency was announced in Afghanistan following change in power in the country. our client Health programme worked with partners to provide essential health services for children and women in need across the country. Services are provided through health facilities and mobile teams for remote, hard-to-reach and in-need areas. Monitoring and technical support are key functions to verify programme implementation and improve the quality of service, including MNCAH, EPI, and especially health in emergency activities in all provinces of the country, as well as at the regional and national levels.
- In addition, in September 2021, the world bank suspended the Sehatmandi project in Afghanistan, this threatens to collapse the health system in the country, our client and WHO have worked to sustain the services through CERF fund until a new mechanism is created. A monitoring framework of this modality is being created including monitoring field visits to health facilities receiving support through our client.
- Also, in 2021, vaccination against COVID 19 started in the country, adding more burden to the already overwhelmed health system, the introduction of new vaccine targeting different population groups, required another additional monitoring framework and tools to track the progress and ensue quality and equity.
- Objective: Extenders are expected to carry out a range of duties, as outlined below, to support monitoring functions, demand generation, accountability to affected population mechanisms, technical facilitation and programme implementation.
- Those duties, which are described in detail below, do not include neither programmatic nor financial authority. Extenders are identified among Afghani citizens with specific expertise and a thorough knowledge of the territory in which they operate, based on their residency and/or work experience.
- Due to the current emergency situation in the county and the growing needs in all areas (total health PiN in 2022 is 18.4 M) which led to a quick increase of emergency activities supported by our client, and due to the difficult geographical nature of Afghanistan and the lack of transportation infrastructure and the remoteness of many communities, which make access and monitoring a challenge in many areas. The need of our client extenders network to complement our client efforts in such areas (difficult to access by staff) is critical to achieve the programme goals. Extenders are engaged through a third-party Service Provider that is directly responsible for the administrative and security related aspects of the Extenders deployment, while our client is responsible for financial support, technical guidance and supervision.
- Accordingly, the Extenders will be contracted by a Service Provider and will be considered a staff of the contracting company for all purposes and in all circumstances. The Extenders will not be considered a our client staff member or consultant. As such, our client will not be directly or indirectly responsible for the Extenders while implementing this Terms of Reference (TOR).
- Based on the approved RWP, our client is supporting MNCAH and EPI services in the country and working to improve coordination, develop policies, strategies, and guidelines, support implementation and monitoring of activities. extenders are tasked to facilitate and support our client programme activities implementation and monitoring tasks that cannot be done by our client staff due to accessibility, security, and scale. Which make extenders modality the most reliable and efficient way to support those tasks.
- Extender will be based at their area of responsibility, and usually selected from communities in same area for easy mobility and to reduce security risks, and transportation time and cost. These extenders are not given task that is supposed to be done normally by our client staff.

Role objectives

TASK TO BE PERFORMED

- Conduct regular situation monitoring in specific areas based on requests by the programme or Zonal Office, to assess the overall humanitarian situation and document the needs of affected populations, in particular women and children health needs.
- Provide technical services to our client projects primarily in hard-to-reach areas, through ensuring regular and systematic technical advice, quality assurance and technical guidance to implementing partners and counterparts, for the efficient implementation of our client programmes and effective achievement of results for the benefit of Afghani children and women.
- Identify capacity and technical gaps of implementing partners and counterparts and provide technical support to ensure capacity building and on job training as needed.
- Support the implementation of Mobile Health and Nutrition Teams (MHNT) supported by our client through technical support and capacity building, and monitor the service implementation and quality. and work with partners at the provincial level to improve MHNT programme results.
- Monitor the work of health facilities supported through our client CERF and other funds using the common checklists and tools.
- Support EPI programme routine immunization activities including -but not limited to- service delivery, cold chain system, vaccine and non-vaccine supplies, information system.
- Support emergency preparedness and response activities implementation and monitoring.
- Report any suspected PSEA case directly to the responsible our client focal point and inform the programme specialist.
- Report any suspected fraud case to the Zonal programme specialist or relevant our client staff.
- Coordinate the monthly working\\monitoring plan with the regional extender, and share the progress and visits repots on timely manner.
- Participating in PHCC, Staff meeting with SP, EPI sub comettee and relvent meetings.

Conduct regular visits to monitor Health programme activities supported by our client, and facilitate our client staff programmatic visits, with a focus on:

- Assessing programme implementation by Implementing Partners through PCAs (Programme Cooperation Agreements) and SSFAs (Small-Scale Funding Agreements) as well as programme implementation by partners and agencies according to the our client Afghanistan Country Office Work Plans.
- Checking EPI supplies chain systems and equipment in place and their functionality status, including following SOPs in vaccine storage and utilization.
- Supporting Health information system and data registration reviews and assessments, and the implementation of Data Quality Improvement plans and microplanning activities.
- Verifying health supplies are delivered to target beneficiaries in line with relevant programme documents and flag any delays and bottlenecks.
- Conducting post-distribution monitoring (PDM) of supplies to assess beneficiaries’ feedback in terms of the quality, timeliness and relevance of supplies delivered. Other end-user monitoring of specific programmes will be conducted as required by the Zonal Office.
- Collecting direct feedback form beneficiaries and affected population about the situation and needs, and the suitability of the services provided and how to improve.

DELIVERABLE(s)

- Provincial need assessment for implementation of mobile health teams completed
- Monthly monitoring of mobile health and nutrition teams service delivery points conducted.
- Monthly report of availability of ORS/Zinc stock with CHWs submitted
- Coordination, and monitoring of community mobilization/engagement activities facilitated
- Need assessment of CHWs training for target provinces completed
- Training of CHWs supported by our client monitored
- Routine EPI monitoring checklists completed and reported (this checklist includes all components of Routine EPI).
- Oriented on new RI activities e.g., accelerated immunization, Measles interventions, awareness raising activities (IEC, media broadcast, etc.).
- Percentage of HFs equipped with SDDs reported.
- Emergency need assessment of emergency affected areas completed
- Our client supported emergency activities monitored including HF under the Sahatmandi CERF support.
- Field visits implemented and reported timely with the required quality.
- Situation monitoring reports and needs assessment data is provided.
- Programme monitoring reports are developed and shared with zonal office programme officers\\specialists and reginal health extender including progress information, gaps and challenges, supplies monitoring, and beneficiaries’ feedback.
- Partner’s capacity in area of extender technical expertise is built.

Project reporting

This role reports to the line manager.

Key competencies

Minimum Qualification and Experience:

- Having certificate in health, medicine, public health, nursing, midwife or related field.
- Minimum of 2 years of experience in in health, medicine, public health, nurse, midwife or related field.
- Proficiency in data analysis and interpretation.
- Excellent communication skills for effective collaboration with healthcare professionals and stakeholders.
- Proven ability to contribute to the enhancement of health programs through data-driven insights.
- Reporting skills

Team management

 This role has no team management responsibility.

Further information

Qualified female candidates are encouraged to apply for this role.

jobs.title: Sudan - Head of Programmes
Operations Support and Logistics (OSL) Officer
jobs.body:
## OBJECTIVES OF THE PROGRAMME

WHO’s work in countries operationalizes the General Programme of Work (GPW14) and the European Programme of Work 2025-2029 (EPW2). GPW14 focuses on accelerating progress toward Health for All by strengthening systems for health, improving access to essential services, advancing preparedness and resilience, and reducing health inequalities. EPW2, endorsed at RC75 following extensive consultation with Member States, reaffirms WHO/Europe’s role in bringing unique value to countries through five core functions:  
1\. **International knowledge hub for health** – providing authoritative evidence, norms, policies and best practices from across the Region and globally to inform national public health decision-making.  
2\. **Impartial coordinator for everyone’s health** – convening national stakeholders and partners to align strategies and support coherent, multisectoral responses to shared health challenges.  
3\. **Leader in tracking and managing cross-border health threats** – supporting surveillance, preparedness, and coordinated action on public health emergencies in line with the Preparedness 2.0 agenda.  
4\. **Driver of health system transformation** – advising national authorities on evidence-informed reforms and policies that strengthen health systems and improve performance.  
5\. **Voice for health equity** – helping countries identify who is being left behind and integrating equity considerations into health policies and strategies.

In this context, WHO Country Offices enable the translation of global and regional commitments into national action. They support Member States by providing strategic advice, convening dialogue across sectors and partners, connecting national authorities with WHO’s technical expertise, and facilitating the use of evidence and best practices to inform policy.

## DESCRIPTION OF DUTIES

1\. Provide input to and manage the implementation of the country level OSL strategy, annual workplan, business-continuity arrangements and emergency logistics plans, ensuring alignment with WHO rules, policies, technical standards, programme priorities and available resources.  
2\. Coordinate supply-chain planning for health commodities, medical equipment and operational supplies, including demand forecasting, supply planning, prioritization, requisition follow-up, shipment tracking and coordination with procurement, finance and technical teams.  
3\. Oversee importation, customs clearance, reception, transportation, warehousing and distribution, resolving complex constraints and holding freight forwarders, transporters and other service providers accountable for contractual performance and service quality.  
4\. Ensure effective warehouse and inventory operations, including stock controls, traceability, storage conditions, cold-chain requirements, shelf-life monitoring, physical inventories, loss prevention, incident management and timely disposal of unserviceable or expired items.  
5\. Coordinate national and subnational distribution plans, including rapid deliveries to priority, hard-to-reach and emergency-affected locations, and support inter-agency convoys and common logistics arrangements where appropriate.  
6\. Lead emergency logistics readiness and surge capacity through risk-based contingency stocks, framework arrangements, scenario planning, field assessments and rapid identification of logistics capacity, needs, risks and gaps; recommend timely corrective and preparedness measures to management.  
7\. Liaise with national authorities, UN agencies, the Health and Logistics Clusters, partners and service providers; represent WHO in relevant logistics coordination mechanisms and negotiations within delegated authority.  
8\. Support the establishment, update and enforcement of OSL standard operating procedures, internal controls, quality-assurance arrangements and risk-mitigation measures. Ensure compliance with WHO requirements, donor conditions, good storage and distribution practices, contractual obligations and audit recommendations, and lead corrective action where gaps are identified.  
9\. Monitor OSL performance, financial and risk-monitoring mechanisms, including relevant KPIs, dashboards, service-provider performance measures and BMS records; analyze trends and provide evidence-based recommendations to senior management and emergency coordination structures.  
10\. Supervise and guide OSL personnel as assigned, including workforce planning, delegation, coaching, staff development and performance management promote teamwork, knowledge sharing and compliance with established procedures.

## REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

### Education

**Essential:** A first-level university degree (Bachelor's level) in supply chain management, logistics, business or public administration, engineering, pharmacy, health sciences or another field relevant to the functions of the position from an accredited/recognized institution.  
**Desirable:** An advanced university degree (Master's level) in one of the above fields. Professional certification in humanitarian logistics, supply-chain management, transport, warehousing Training in information management systems and their application to supply-chain monitoring.

### Experience

**Essential**: At least five years of progressively responsible professional experience, at the national and/or international level, in logistics or supply-chain operations, including experience supporting emergency or humanitarian operations, coordinating multiple supply-chain functions, previous experience in team management

**Desirable**:

- Experience providing strategic advice to senior management and leading logistics or supply-chain operations across multiple locations in a complex field setting.
- Relevant experience with WHO, the United Nations system, Health or Logistics Cluster partners, a recognized humanitarian organization or an international nongovernmental organization.
- Experience in health logistics, import/export and customs administration, warehouse and inventory management, cold chain, last-mile distribution, emergency preparedness, service-provider or contract management, and performance, financial or risk monitoring.
- Proven experience in managing a team

### Functional Skills

• Advanced knowledge of end-to-end supply-chain and logistics management in emergency and humanitarian settings, including strategic planning, forecasting, transport, customs clearance, warehousing, inventory control, cold chain and distribution.  
• Strong strategic, analytical, planning and organizational skills, with the ability to translate programme priorities into supply-chain strategies, governance arrangements, SOPs, KPIs and practical risk-based solutions in complex and rapidly changing operating environments.  
• Demonstrated ability to lead and develop a multidisciplinary team, manage resources and performance, establish priorities, make sound decisions under pressure and maintain business continuity in high-risk operations.  
• Excellent interpersonal, advisory, coordination and negotiation skills, with the ability to influence decisions, build consensus and engage senior national authorities, UN entities, humanitarian partners and service providers with tact and diplomacy.

### **Other Skills (e.g. IT)**

• Excellent knowledge of Microsoft Office applications and demonstrated ability to use ERP and supply-chain information systems, including BMS or comparable platforms.  
• Advanced skills in database and dashboard use for demand forecasting, shipment tracking, inventory management, distribution monitoring, KPI reporting and data-quality assurance.  
• Working knowledge of communications and emergency logistics equipment, including radios and satellite telephones, is desirable.

### WHO Competencies

Teamwork  
Respecting & promoting individual and cultural differences  
Communication  
Producing results  
Creating an empowering and motivating environment  
Ensuring the effective use of resources

### Use of Language Skills

**Essential**: Expert knowledge of English. Expert knowledge of Ukrainian.

**Desirable:** Intermediate knowledge of any other UN language.

## REMUNERATION

Remuneration comprises an annual base salary starting at USD 64,825 (subject to mandatory deductions for pension contributions and health insurance, as applicable) and 30 days of annual leave.

Link to apply: [Job Description - Operations Support and Logistics (OSL) Officer (2604566)](https://careers.who.int/careersection/ex/jobdetail.ftl?job=2604566&tz=GMT%2B03%3A00&tzname=Europe%2FKiev)

jobs.title: HEAD Of Middle East Durable Solutions Platform
jobs.body:
The Danish Refugee Council assists refugees and internally displaced persons across the globe: we provide emergency aid, fight for their rights, and strengthen their opportunity for a brighter future. We work in conflict-affected areas, along the displacement routes, and in the countries where refugees settle. In cooperation with local communities, we strive for responsible and sustainable solutions. We work toward successful integration and – whenever possible – for the fulfilment of the wish to return home.

The Danish Refugee Council was founded in Denmark in 1956, and has since grown to become an international humanitarian organization with more than 7,000 staff and 8,000 volunteers. Our vision is a dignified life for all displaced.

All of our efforts are based on our value compass: humanity, respect, independence and neutrality, participation.

DRC hosts the Middle East Durable Solutions Platform (ME DSP), a membership-based NGO platform established by DRC, NRC and IRC and later joined by Oxfam, ACF and Save the Children to strengthen evidence, programming and advocacy on solutions to displacement in and from Syria. In 2022 its scope was widened to Iraq and Yemen. Following a period of hibernation since 2023, ME DSP has secured core donor funding and is in the process of re-establishing its membership, reviewing its governance and operating model, and diversify its partnerships. ME DSP is one of three DRC-hosted solutions platforms, alongside ReDSS (East Africa and Great Lakes) and ADSP (Asia), and sits within the DRC Middle East, Asia and Europe Hub under the leadership of the Hub’s Executive Director.

The **Head of ME DSP** provides overall leadership, strategic direction and management of the Platform, a membership-based, consensus-driven platform of NGOs working on solutions to displacement across the Middle East. As the Platform’s principal convener, s/he leads engagement with members and governance structures, builds consensus around shared priorities and ensures delivery of agreed commitments; leads the Platform’s evidence, learning and policy agenda so that research is translated into programming and policy guidance; represents the Platform at senior level with members, governments and donors, UN agencies and policy makers at country regional and global levels; manages ME DSP grants, staff and consultants; and works in close collaboration with DRC’s sister platforms, ReDSS and ADSP.

**Responsibilities:**

**Strategic Leadership, Governance and Management**

- Facilitate the implementation of the ME DSP Strategy 2026-2028, lead the regular review of the Platform’s work plans, and ensure ME DSP maintains a strategic, neutral and member-driven role that complements existing coordination mechanisms
- Lead the re-establishment of the Platform’s membership and the review of its governance and operating model, in line with Steering Committee decisions
- Lead annual planning and budgeting and report to the Steering Committee and members on progress, risks and results; maintain the risk matrix, commission periodic evaluation of ME DSP and integrate lessons learned
- Work in close collaboration with ReDSS and ADSP to share learning, align approaches and tools, and contribute to joint NGO engagement in global solutions fora
- Accountable for people management of direct reports, including recruitment, objective setting, performance management and staff development, and for the management of ME DSP consultants

**Membership Convening and Coordination**

- Act as the Platform’s principal convener. Design and facilitate member meetings, technical working groups and consultations in an inclusive and transparent manner that builds collective ownership of the Platform’s agenda and outputs
- Facilitate consensus-building among members, managing differing priorities and resolving issues that may affect Platform decisions and delivery
- Ensure effective coordination and information sharing among members and the Steering Committee, and support members’ engagement with the Platform at country, regional and global levels
- Lead a membership engagement strategy, including the onboarding of new members and clarity on members’ roles and contributions.

**Research, Evidence and Learning**

- Define and oversee the Platform’s research and knowledge management agenda with members, initiating and commissioning studies, managing researchers and research institutions, and ensuring methodologically rigorous, research ethics and relevance to programming and policy
- Lead the analysis of regional displacement and solutions data, strategies, policies and legislation; translate evidence into programming and policy guidance, briefing papers and policy briefs; and ensure quality control of all ME DSP publications and monitoring of their uptake
- Facilitate regular technical workshops and learning events and the roll-out of learning tools and training packages, ensuring cross-learning across countries and with global developments in solutions policy and practice
- Promote the meaningful engagement of displacement-affected communities and local civil society in the Platform’s evidence, learning and policy work

**Policy Engagement and External Representation**

- Represent the Platform at senior level with governments and national authorities, donors, UN agencies, international financial institutions, regional bodies and policy makers, building trusted relationships and navigating politically sensitive contexts with discretion and in line with humanitarian principles
- Oversee the development and implementation of the Platform’s policy and advocacy strategy with members, ensuring positions are evidence-based, agreed by members and coordinated with NGO fora and durable solutions working groups in the region
- Support members’ advocacy with governmental and inter-governmental actors and engage proactively in regional and global policy processes on solutions for displacement-affected populations
- Engage research institutions, think tanks and academia, and oversee high-quality external communications reflecting members’ agreed positions

**Business Development and Project Management**

- Manage existing and future grants, including budgets, work plans, monitoring and donor reporting, ensuring timely delivery and compliance with DRC and donor policies, including safeguarding
- Develop and implement a fundraising strategy to ensure financial sustainability, including donor engagement and partnerships, in coordination with the Steering Committee

**About you**

To be successful in this role we expect you to have **Experience and technical competencies** :

- Advanced university degree or equivalent in political science, international relations, humanitarian law, migration, Middle East studies, or related field
- Understanding of the regional displacement dynamics. Excellent understanding of
- At least 8 years' relevant experience, including 5 in people management and substantial experience leading, facilitating or coordinating a membership-based, consensus-driven consortium, network, NGO forum or inter-agency platform
- Expert knowledge of durable solutions to displacement and the relevant international frameworks, with demonstrated experience in complex and contested return and reintegration contexts
- In-depth knowledge of the displacement context of the Middle East, displacement in and from Syria, Iraq and Yemen, and of the political complexities, policy landscape and coordination architecture of the region
- Demonstrated strategic leadership, ability to manage competing priorities, and ensure accountability for results
- Proven experience in grant management, budget oversight and resource mobilization
- Proven experience in leading, conducting or commissioning research, or in working in close collaboration with researchers, and in translating evidence into programming and policy guidance
- Excellent convening, facilitation and networking skills, with the ability to build trust and broker consensus among diverse organizations; outstanding interpersonal and diplomatic skills, political and cultural sensitivity, tact and impartiality
- Excellent analytical and writing skills, with proven experience producing high quality research and policy briefs and presenting complex information in an accessible manner
- Demonstrated commitment to collaborative working across organizations and with sister platforms, ability to work in a multicultural environment, and flexibility, proactive engagement and high tolerance for change, complexity and unpredictability

**In this position, you are expected to demonstrate DRC’ five core competencies:**

**Striving for excellence:** You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.

**Collaborating:** You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.

**Taking the lead:** You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.

**Communicating:** You listen and speak effectively and honestly.

**Demonstrating integrity:** You act in line with DRC’s vision and values.

**Application process**

All applicants must upload a cover letter and an updated CV (no longer than four pages) in English. **Applications sent by email will not be considered.**

*Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, and we encourage interested candidates to apply as soon as possible. We reserve the right to close the vacancy before the advertised deadline if a suitable candidate is identified.* “

**Location:** Jordan/Amman with potential travel in the region

**Contract length**: 1 year contract

**Start date;** 1 Jan 2027

**Closing date for applications:** 16-11-2026.

If you have questions or are facing problems with the online application process, please visit [drc.ngo/jobsupport](https://forms-hr.drc.dk/view.php?id=348161).

For further information about the Danish Refugee Council, please consult our website [drc.ngo](https://drc.ngo/).

jobs.title: Climate, Environment & Health Coordinator
jobs.body:
**Join MSF OCG as a Climate, Environment & Health Coordinator !**

**We are looking for passionate candidates ready to contribute to our humanitarian mission.**

**Below, you will find the job details and the qualifications we are looking for.**

## Inclusivity and Diversity at MSF

Do your qualifications and experience not exactly match all requirements of the job?

At MSF OCG, we are committed to an inclusive culture that supports and amplifies the diverse voices of our staff members. We strive to create workplaces where teams of people with diverse backgrounds, characteristics, perspectives, ideas and experiences work together to advance MSF's social mission and create better outcomes for our patients and the communities we work with.

We understand that some people may hesitate to apply for employment if they don't meet all listed job requirements. Research shows that this is especially true for women. If you believe your profile is a good match for this position, we invite you to apply even if you don’t fulfil every listed qualification.

We encourage applications from individuals of all genders, ages, sexual orientations, ethnicities, background, religions, beliefs, ability status, and all other diversity characteristics.

MSF does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of discrimination or harassment, including sexual harassment. All selected candidates will undergo reference checks.

## Context & mission

Médecins Sans Frontières is an independent, international medical and humanitarian organization that provides care to people in need, people affected by natural or man-made disasters, and victims of armed conflict, without discrimination and without regard to race, religion, creed or political affiliation (MSF Charter).

The MSF movement is built around 5 operational centers supported by 24 sections and offices worldwide. MSF Operational Center Geneva (MSF OCG) is one of these centers.

We are looking for a Climate, Environment & Health (CEH) Coordinator to join MSF OCG.

Reporting to the Deputy General Director, the CEH Coordinator is responsible for leading and coordinating OCG’s strategic approach to reducing the environmental impact of its activities, while strengthening the integration of the health and humanitarian consequences of climate change into operational planning.The position works closely with the Logistics, Medical, Communication and Operations departments, supporting field missions and contributing to more relevant, responsible and effective humanitarian operations.

## Tasks & Responsibilities

- Develop and implement OCG’s strategy to address climate change and environmental issues across its activities.
- Support the integration of climate risks and evolving patterns of climate-sensitive diseases into operational planning to strengthen the relevance of operational responses.
- Promote the reduction of environmental impacts across OCG’s activities to enhance the environmental responsibility of MSF operations.
- Coordinate cross-functional initiatives on climate and environmental issues to ensure alignment and consistency across OCG.
- Develop frameworks, guidelines, and tools to support teams in effectively addressing climate risks and environmental impacts.
- Monitor progress towards climate and environmental objectives to ensure accountability and continuous improvement, including overseeing the organisation’s annual carbon accounting process.
- Represent OCG in intersectional and external meetings on climate, environment, and health.

## Your profile

*Education*

- Essential: Advanced university degree in environmental health, climate change, sustainability, environmental engineering, or a related field.
- Desired: Certification in carbon accounting.

*Experience*

- Essential: Experience in a similar role or in leading cross-functional initiatives involving multiple stakeholders without direct hierarchical authority.
- Field experience with MSF or another humanitarian organization is an asset.

*Languages*

- English and French are mandatory.
- Additional languages are an asset.

*Skills/ Technical competencies*

- Carbon accounting.
- Environmental sustainability and climate change.
- Health and humanitarian impacts of climate change.
- Strategic planning and change management.
- Data analytics, monitoring, reporting, and performance tracking.

*Personal Abilities/Qualities*

- Strategic thinking.
- Influencing and stakeholder engagement skills.
- Analytical and problem-solving skills.
- Coordination and facilitation skills.
- Communication and presentation skills.
- Project and change management skills.
- Ability to work effectively in a multicultural environment and demonstrate commitment to diversity, gender-responsive, inclusive, and non-discriminatory behaviours and attitudes.

## Terms of employment

- Full-time position 100% (40h/week)
- Open-ended contract
- Working place: Geneva
- Ideal start date: 1st of December 2026
- Gross annual salary (for 100%): from CHF 119’964.- to CHF 137’640.- (salary commensurate with equivalent experience and internal salary grid)
- Paid vacation: 25 days per year, prorate temporis, plus any Swiss public holidays falling within the contract period.
- Pension plan: pension contribution covered 3/4 by MSF, 1/4 by staff member.
- Relocation support available for eligible candidates.

*Vacancy Type:* **Call for Applications**  
Initial duration: **2 months**  
Closing date: **03 November 2026**

**Context:**

Since 2015, more than 30 per cent of Ni-Vanuatu citizens have experienced temporary or protracted displacement due to disasters. Vanuatu's approximately 300,000 people (Vanuatu Bureau of Statistics, 2020) spread across 83 islands are exposed to cyclones, tsunami, volcanic eruptions, ashfalls, earthquakes, mudslides, flooding and drought. As the frequency and intensity of extreme weather events increases due to climate change, disasters pose a primary threat to Vanuatu's national security and human development.

Tropical Cyclones (TC) Judy and Kevin (both of Category 4 intensity) made landfall over Vanuatu on 1 and 3 March 2023. TC Judy and Kevin affected an estimated 24,657 households (123,288 people) with 90 per cent of houses in Shefa and Tafea provinces destroyed or severely damaged. The cumulative impact of compounding events such as previous cyclones (TC Harold), high La Nina rainfall and COVID-19, has had a devastating impact on basic living conditions, access to basic services, livelihoods, and coping capacities. While traditional resilience in Vanuatu is strong, emergency preparedness needs strengthening at all levels - national, provincial, area council and community – particularly in light of intensifying climate change impacts in the Pacific.

In response, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) is implementing a project to support the Vanuatu National Disaster Management Office (NDMO) in strengthening the capacity of national and provincial government institutions, Community Disaster and Climate Change Committees (CDCCCs), Area Councils, faith-based organizations, and community leaders — particularly women leaders — to develop and maintain safe and dignified evacuation arrangements during emergencies.

This builds on the existing work being undertaken by the Displacement and Evacuation Centre Management (DECM) Cluster which brings together key partners to deliver effective multi-sectoral assistance and protection for displaced populations and host communities. It will strengthen and extend the work of the DECM Cluster to provincial and community level, moving towards improved localization of emergency response measures in Vanuatu.

Specifically, the Sef Ples Blong Yumi Phase 2 project funded by the Government of Australia’s Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT), implemented by the National Disaster Management Office, Vanuatu in collaboration with the International Organization for Migration, supports the Government of Vanuatu to strengthen disaster preparedness, coordination, and evacuation centre management across multiple hazards. The project focuses on strengthening the DECM Cluster’s coordination capacity, updating and rolling out the National Evacuation Centre Management Guidelines (NECMG) and Evacuation Toolbox / Training Materials, improving information management systems, and supporting preparedness at national, provincial, and Area Council levels.

**The Objective of the project is:**

To contribute to the protection and resilience of people at risk of displacement in Vanuatu by supporting the Government of Vanuatu to strengthen disaster preparedness and evacuation procedures.

The project will update and finalize the National Evacuation Centre Management Guidelines (NECMG) and developing the Evacuations Toolbox / Training Materials for Provinces, Area Councils, faith-based groups and communities to strengthen:

1. National, provincial and area council-level coordination of evacuations.
2. Capacity of communities, CDCCCs, faith-based groups to manage and lead their own community-based evacuations in ways that both draws on traditional knowledge about evacuations and increases protections for vulnerable groups, especially women, children, older people and people with disability.

The Outcomes and Outputs of this project are the following:

Outcome 1: Government, faith-based groups and communities have enhanced capacity to coordinate, develop, maintain and monitor safe, dignified evacuation accommodation in emergencies.

Output 1.1: Improved information management at national and provincial level to deliver effective multi-sectoral assistance and protection for displaced populations and host communities in sudden-onset emergencies.

Output 1.2: Improved coordination at national and provincial level to deliver effective multi-sectoral assistance and protection for displaced populations and host communities in emergencies.

Output 1.3: Updated National Evacuation Centre Management Guidelines and Evacuations Toolbox for Provinces, Area Councils, faith-based groups and communities to support evacuation preparedness as well as strengthen community-based management of evacuations.

Output 1.4: Roll out of Evacuations Toolbox training for national trainers, Provinces, Area Councils, faith-based groups and communities to support evacuation preparedness as well as strengthen community-based management of evacuations.

**Organizational Department / Unit to which the Consultant is contributing**

Disaster Risk Reduction - Humanitarian

Project code: CC0083

jobs.title: MEAL Coordinator (MEAL Advisor) - Caracas
jobs.body:
The Danish Refugee Council is one of the world's leading humanitarian NGOs, working in over 30 countries to provide adequate assistance and protection to refugees, asylum seekers, IDPs, returnees, people on the move, and vulnerable local populations/host communities. Currently, DRC is seeking a highly qualified national o International **MEAL Coordinator (MEAL Advisor)** based in Caracas, Venezuela.

**About the job:** DRC is managing its operations in Venezuela under the direction of the country office in Caracas and four field offices located in the states of Sucre, Apure, and Zulia (Maracaibo and Santa Barbara de Zulia). DRC Venezuela is implementing an integrated Action encompassing the Protection, Food Security & Livelihood, WASH and Disaster Preparedness sectors.

**The overall purpose of the role**:

The MEAL Coordinator provides country-level technical advice and capacity strengthening to support the development of DRC Venezuela’s Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning function. Under the supervision of the Head of Programmes, the role works closely with the existing MEAL leadership, MEAL staff, programme teams and partners to strengthen practical systems, improve the quality and use of evidence, and support accountable programming across emergency response, recovery and longer-term interventions.

The role supports a collaborative review of MEAL capacities, systems and ways of working, translates findings into a prioritised improvement plan, and accompanies its implementation through mentoring, coaching and hands-on technical support. The Coordinator promotes sustainable approaches adapted to country needs and team capacities, in line with DRC’s Global MEAL Model and donor requirements.

The position provides advisory and technical coordination support. The existing MEAL leadership retains responsibility for departmental management and day-to-day delivery. Priorities and recommendations are agreed with the Head of Programmes in consultation with relevant colleagues.

**Responsibilities:**

**MEAL development and technical advisory support**

- Facilitate a participatory review of MEAL systems, staffing capacities, workflows, tools and coordination arrangements, recognising existing strengths and identifying opportunities for improvement.
- Review how MEAL commitments are translated into workplans and delivered across country and field offices, including the factors affecting timeliness, data quality and utilisation of findings.
- Develop an achievable MEAL strengthening plan with the existing MEAL leadership and Head of Programmes, with clear priorities, responsibilities, timelines and measures of progress.
- Advise on the country MEAL strategy, departmental workplan, resourcing and division of responsibilities between MEAL, programme teams and partners.
- Provide regular, evidence-based recommendations to the Head of Programmes and support follow-up on agreed improvement actions.

**Capacity strengthening and accompaniment**

- Identify learning needs jointly with MEAL and programme staff and develop a tailored capacity-building plan covering country and field teams.
- Provide structured mentoring, coaching and practical support to MEAL leadership and staff, including through joint field visits and review of actual project tools and outputs.
- Facilitate practical learning sessions on MEAL planning, indicator design, sampling, mixed methods, data analysis, accountability and communication of findings.
- Develop accessible guidance and reusable resources and support their consistent application across offices.
- Assess the application of learning in practice and progressively transfer strengthened tools and processes to the responsible teams.

**Results monitoring and programme quality support**

- Support the integration of MEAL throughout Project Cycle Management, including proposals, grant opening, periodic reviews and close-out.
- Advise on theories of change, logframes, indicators, MEAL plans and realistic MEAL budgets, in collaboration with technical coordinators and grants colleagues.
- Review and strengthen indicator tracking tables, means of verification and reporting processes to improve consistency, completeness and timely consolidation.
- Support the design and refinement of context-appropriate quantitative and qualitative data collection methods for assessments, baselines, monitoring and outcome measurement.
- Provide technical quality assurance for sampling, data collection, data entry, analysis and reporting, and support resolution of recurrent bottlenecks.
- Work with relevant colleagues to strengthen data protection, secure storage, responsible sharing and practical use of digital collection and visualisation tools.

**Accountability to affected populations**

- Support MEAL and programme teams in strengthening accessible, inclusive and safe community feedback mechanisms and information provision.
- Review feedback workflows and advise on timely handling, appropriate referral of sensitive complaints and closure of the feedback loop, in line with DRC procedures.
- Build staff capacities on accountability, ethical data collection and Core Humanitarian Standard commitments.
- Support regular analysis of feedback trends and their use in programme reviews and decision-making.

**Evaluation analysis and learning**

- Advise on evaluation and research planning, methodologies and terms of reference in line with DRC policy and donor requirements.
- Support the analysis and interpretation of monitoring and evaluation findings and their translation into practical programme recommendations.
- Facilitate learning reviews and reflection sessions across teams and partners, documenting lessons and following up agreed actions.
- Support the preparation of clear evidence products and presentation of key findings to programme teams and senior management.

**Partner support and coordination**

- Work with partnership and MEAL colleagues to assess partner capacities and agree proportionate monitoring, reporting and accountability arrangements.
- Provide targeted technical support and capacity building to partners and facilitate joint learning and harmonisation of tools where appropriate.
- Coordinate technical exchanges across country and field offices and with relevant DRC global MEAL counterparts.
- Represent DRC in relevant technical coordination forums when delegated by the Head of Programmes.
- Perform other relevant duties assigned by the Head of Programmes within the scope of the role.

**Experience and technical competencies**

- Minimum five years of relevant MEAL experience in humanitarian or development programmes, including country-level technical coordination or advisory responsibilities.
- Demonstrated experience strengthening existing MEAL departments or systems through collaborative assessment, prioritised improvement planning and sustained technical support.
- Proven mentoring, coaching and facilitation skills, including experience supporting national staff and working effectively through technical influence and collaborative relationships.
- Strong practical knowledge of theories of change, logframes, indicator design, sampling, quantitative and qualitative methods, data quality assurance and evaluations.
- Experience translating data and community feedback into programme improvements and organisational learning.
- Experience with accountability mechanisms, CHS, ethical research and data protection in humanitarian settings.
- Advanced Excel skills and experience with digital data collection tools such as KoboToolbox or ODK; experience with Power BI or statistical analysis software is an asset.
- Experience meeting institutional donor MEAL requirements and supporting local partners.
- Strong analytical, organisational and communication skills, with the ability to propose practical solutions and support constructive dialogue.
- Previous experience with DRC systems, Latin American contexts or emergency response is an asset.

**Education**

- Bachelor’s degree in international development, social sciences, statistics, research, public health or another relevant discipline
- A relevant postgraduate qualification or specialised training in MEAL is an asset.

**Languages**

- Full professional proficiency in Spanish and English, spoken and written.

**We offer:**

- The opportunity to be part of one of the best NGOs worldwide.
- Access to over 1,000 free online trainings and certifications.
- Contract duration: subject to budget availability.
- Salary: Band G / Terms of Employment for national or expatriate staff, as applicable
- HCM insurance fully covered by the organization.

**DRC Core Competencies:**

- Achieving Excellence: Focus on achieving results and ensuring efficient processes.
- Collaboration: Engage relevant parties and encourage feedback.
- Taking the Initiative: Take ownership and initiative while seeking innovation.
- Communicating: Listen and speak effectively and honestly.
- Demonstrating Integrity: Act in accordance with DRC's vision and values.

**Application Process:** All applicants must upload a cover letter (max. 1 page) and an updated CV (max. 2 pages, without attachments) in English or Spanish, on the DRC employment platform. Applications sent by email will not be considered.

**Application Deadline:** Sunday, november 01 at 11:59 pm Local Time. Please note that applications will be reviewed continuously, and interviews will be scheduled as soon as a suitable candidate is identified. DRC reserves the right to close the vacancy before the deadline once a suitable candidate is identified.

**Start Date:** November 2026

jobs.body:
**Location:** Dakar, Sine Saloum or Casamance, with signiﬁcant national travel

**Contract type and duration:** Two years (with the possibility of extension thereafter)

**Hours:** Full-time

**Closing date for applications:** 3 November 2026

**Reports to:** Head of Technical Capacity for West Africa

**Start date:** 1 December 2026

**Remuneration:** Circa XOF 8,988,369 - 10,691,433 gross annually

## We unlock power with coastal communities

Blue Ventures connects coastal communities restoring the ocean, providing the resources and partnerships they need to unlock their power and turn local action into global impact. We link communities with allies, knowledge and influence to create unstoppable waves of change.

Together, we’re placing communities at the centre of solutions to sustain fisheries, manage ecosystems and redefine how the world protects the ocean.

## **Summary job description**

The Financial Inclusion Officer will support the delivery of Blue Ventures’ Financial Inclusion programme in Senegal and The Gambia, working closely with partners and coastal communities to strengthen financial resilience and improve household livelihoods. The role involves developing, adapting, and implementing practical tools, guidelines, training materials, and approaches related to financial literacy, VSLA management, savings and loans, business development, and income-generating activities.

The Officer will also provide technical support, training, mentoring, and peer-learning opportunities to partners and communities, contribute to knowledge development and sharing of good practices, support data collection and analysis, and help integrate financial inclusion and sustainable livelihood approaches into broader fisheries management and conservation programmes. The position requires frequent travel, and involves collaboration with local partners, communities, and Blue Ventures’ international teams. Reporting to the West Africa Head of Technical Capacity, this is a full-time role based in Senegal.

jobs.title: Website Redesign and Development Consultancy

Sightsavers Kenya, on behalf of the Kenya Business and Disability Network (KBDN), is seeking a qualified consultant or firm to redesign and redevelop the KBDN website.

jobs.title: Responsable des activités de santé mentale (psychologues & psychiatres)
jobs.body:
Médecins Sans Frontières, association médicale humanitaire internationale créée en 1971, apporte une assistance médicale à des populations dont la vie est menacée : principalement en cas de conflits armés, mais aussi d'épidémies, de pandémies, de catastrophes naturelles ou encore d'exclusion des soins.

MSF recrute en urgence des Responsables d'activités de santé mentale, notamment dans le cadre des projets médicaux déployés face à l'épidémie Ebola en cours en République Démocratique du Congo (maj octobre 2026). IMPORTANT : la durée de mission sur ce contexte est inférieure à 6 mois, de l'ordre de 3 mois. Merci d'indiquer durée de mission = 6 mois dans le formulaire de candidature, même si vous vous intéressez à un départ sur les projets de riposte contre Ebola en République Démocratique du Congo.

**Responsabilités :**

- Coordonner et veiller à ce que les activités de santé mentale auprès des patient·e·s s'accompagnent d'un suivi régulier, en assurant que l’équipe de santé mentale est calme et neutre au cours des sessions indépendamment des sentiments personnels et/ou des croyances et veiller à faire former les interprètes à la terminologie et à l'attitude à adopter durant les séances
- En collaboration avec les membres de l'équipe médicale, les patients et la communauté locale, identifier les besoins dans le but d'une co-définition et d'une co-création des activités de santé mentale et de soutien psychosocial (MHPSS). Définir, planifier et organiser la stratégie de santé mentale et de soutien psychosocial, ainsi que le budget
- Répertorier et mettre à jour les services de santé mentale existants, y compris les autres ONG internationales et locales, groupes communautaires et services de santé gouvernementaux, et maintenir une communication et une collaboration adéquates et régulières avec les autres parties prenantes du projet
- Identifier les éventuelles problématiques qui pourront faire l’objet de plaidoyer et informer le personnel de coordination médicale et de projet avant de prendre des mesures
- Assurer, en collaboration avec le département médical, l'intégration des activités de santé mentale et de soutien psychosocial (MHPSS) dans d'autres domaines/services, tels que la santé sexuelle et génésique, la pédiatrie, la malnutrition et les maladies chroniques non transmissibles, entre autres
- S’assurer que les patient·e·s psychiatrique se présentant dans les structures MSF reçoit un traitement adéquat, y compris des médicaments psychotropes et un soutien psychosocial dans un programme MSF ou par une référence à une ressource appropriée
- Veiller à la mise en œuvre de tous les protocoles et procédures standards de santé mentale MSF
- Gérer, former et superviser l'équipe de santé mentale via des activités comme le recrutement, la définition des descriptions de fonction, le développement des compétences, le briefing/débriefing du personnel et son évaluation

**Profil recherché**

**Formation :**

- Diplôme de niveau Master ou équivalent en psychologie avec formations pertinentes pour la pratique clinique, une spécialisation en psychologie clinique, conseil, psychothérapie, psychopathologie ou matière connexe
- Autorisation de pratique valide et à jour
- Une composante de formation clinique avec un nombre défini d'heures cliniques supervisées effectuées.
- La formation doit inclure des soins cliniques en face-à-face aux personnes que nous soignons (séances individuelles et en groupe) avec une supervision appropriée et le développement de compétences / techniques psychothérapeutiques clés

**Expériences :**

- Deux ans d'expérience professionnelle après le diplôme de niveau Master - avec des adultes, y compris les techniques comportementales ou le conseil
- Expérience clinique récente (au moins six mois au cours des 24 derniers mois)
- Expérience de travail avec des populations vulnérables dans un contexte interculturel

**Aptitudes :**

- Engagement dans la mission sociale et les valeurs de MSF
- Volonté de travailler dans tout type de contexte, y compris dans des zones instables
- Flexibilité et résistance au stress
- Capacité et expérience dans la formation des autres, le coaching et la supervision

**Langues :**

- maîtrise de l'anglais obligatoire (niveau B1 minimum)
- la connaissance de l'arabe littéraire ou du français est un plus

**Disponibilité** : Engagement de **3 à 6 mois.** Missions de 3 mois pour les projets déployés face à l'épidémie Ebola en cours en République Démocratique du Congo.

**Ce que nous offrons**

- Salaire en fonction de l'ancienneté et de l'expérience pertinente
- Prise en charge des frais liés à la mission (transport, visas, logement, vaccins, etc.).
- Assurances santé, rapatriement, retraite.
- Perspectives d’évolution : formations, accompagnement et développement de carrière dans un large éventail de contextes humanitaires.

**Pourquoi vous ?**

Vous êtes rigoureux·se, engagé·e, stratégique, à l’écoute, et vous souhaitez mettre vos compétences au service de populations en situation de vulnérabilité.

jobs.title: Helios+ Center Assistant
jobs.body:
**BACKGROUND:** The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world’s worst humanitarian crises and helps people to survive and rebuild their lives. Founded in 1933, the IRC offers lifesaving care and life-changing assistance to refugees forced to flee from war or disaster. At work today in over 40 countries, the IRC aims to restore safety, dignity and hope to millions who are uprooted and struggling to endure. In response to the arrival of refugees in Greece in 2015, the IRC has been offering SMS, WASH and Protection services. Among others, through its child protection programs, the IRC has been offering individual support through case management to vulnerable children and their families, non-formal educational activities for children through Safe Healing and Learning Spaces and emergency accommodation and protection to unaccompanied children. Since 2019, IRC Hellas implements an alternative care project for unaccompanied children and will now pilot this project to Greek born children and adults.

**SCOPE OF WORK:** Helios+ - Comprehensive Actions for the integration of Third Country Nationals in the Labor Market - (MIS 6016874) is a portfolio of regional Integration Projects, dedicated to fostering the integration of third-country nationals into Greece's labor market and society. Designed by the International Organization for Migration (IOM) with the support of the Government of Greece (GoG), co-financed by the European Union under the Regional Programs (RP) for 2021–2027 and aligns fully with Greece's National Strategy for Integration. HELIOS+ is committed to empowering Beneficiaries of International and Temporary Protection residing in Greece by providing them with the tools and resources needed to achieve socio-economic independence and actively participate in the Greek community, while promoting self-reliance and inclusion through a comprehensive set of services tailored to the needs of the target group.

In the Attica Region, International Rescue Committee Hellas participates as a partner of IOM Greece, together with Solidarity Now, in the consortium led by Caritas Hellas.

The IRC supports access to job counseling and job matching, life skills, education and psychosocial support – directly and in collaboration with partners. The IRC is recruiting a HELIOS+ Center assistant for the reception and registration of beneficiaries, providing first-level information, and guiding beneficiaries to the specialized services of the center. The HELIOS+ Center assistant will also be responsible for preparing the necessary documents for their registration, monitoring the security of the center, and ensuring the smooth operation of the center’s overall spaces and equipment.

**RESPONSIBILITIES:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Welcome and receive beneficiaries and visitors to the Center warmly and friendly**;**
- Provide information about the Center and its services to the beneficiaries of the subproject, as required**;**
- Provide administrative support to ensure the smooth daily operation of the Center**;**
- Manage the Center’s calendar and scheduling of sessions, appointments, etc., in coordination with the Center’s Manager**;**
- Manage the Center’s correspondence and communications (phone/email/mail)**;**
- Update and maintain a contact list**;**
- Effectively maintain filing systems, both electronic and paper-based**;**
- Collect and organize the data required for each beneficiary;
- Monitor the Center’s spaces and their security, maintain cleanliness and order, aim to ensure smooth and efficient operation, in close cooperation with the Center’s Manager;
- Other related duties as assigned by the subproject Coordinator;
- Participate in regular team meetings and external meetings as requested;

**REQUIREMENTS:**

- BA/BS Degree in Pedagogical Studies, Administrative Studies, and/or other related fields;
- At least three (3) years of experience in a corresponding position of responsibility, preferably in the field of humanitarian organizations;
- Excellent knowledge of Greek and English, spoken and written (level C1/C2).
- Computer skills, in particular word processing, excel spreadsheets and internet services;
- Excellent interpersonal, team and communication skills;
- Ability to organize and prioritize workload using initiative;
- Ability to work under pressure;

**PREFERRED EXPERIENCE AND SKILLS:**

- Experience in customer service.
- Ability to manage multiple tasks.
- Intercultural awareness and flexibility.
- Ability to work on own initiative and at the same time as part of a multicultural and interdisciplinary team.
- Knowledge of French, or Arabic, or Farsi, or Pashto, or Urdu is an advantage.

**WORK ENVIRONMENT:**

Working hours: 9:00-17:00

Travel and other requirements: Occasionally to other areas of IRC programs within Athens

**This position is expected to end on May 30, 2027.**

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: £1,300 - £1,590/month). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. jobs.title: Mobile Implementation Officer (MIO) – Sécurité F/H
jobs.body:
Médecins Sans Frontières, association médicale humanitaire internationale créée en 1971, apporte une assistance médicale à des populations dont la vie est menacée : principalement en cas de conflits armés, mais aussi d'épidémies, de pandémies, de catastrophes naturelles ou encore d'exclusion des soins.

Dans le cadre d’un remplacement, nous recherchons un·e : MIO – Mobile Implementation Officer – Sécurité (H/F)

**MISSION**

Le département des Opérations a créé en octobre 2017 un poste de MIO Sécurité. Le·a MIO travaille sous la responsabilité du Point Focal Sécurité. Il·elle a pour mission d’accompagner les équipes dans la révision de leur gestion de la sécurité, en lien avec le contexte local et les opérations.

L’intervention du MIO Sécurité consiste à soutenir les équipes sur les besoins qu’elles ont elles-mêmes identifiées tout en intégrant les différents départements (Opés, Med, Log, Admin) dans la réflexion. Elle se conclura par la rédaction d’un plan d’action. Ce plan d’action, réfléchi et travaillé par les équipes, sera dès lors adopté et mis en œuvre par la coordination et la cellule. Il·elle pourra aussi, si la demande est faite par les responsables opérationnels, aider les équipes terrain à mettre en place des procédures de sécurité standardisées. Le MIO Sécurité s’attachera aussi à promouvoir les bonnes pratiques sur les projets au sein de la mission et à les partager avec les autres terrains.

Le·a MIO Sécurité joue aussi un rôle essentiel chez MSF OCP dans la réponse à un incident critique : il·elle prépare les équipes en amont sur le terrain ; il·elle pourra être déployé·e sur le terrain en coordination ou en appui de la cellule de crise terrain.

Entre ses affectations sur le terrain, le·a MIO Sécurité appuie le Point Focal Sécurité à travailler sur la capitalisation et la diffusion des bonnes pratiques et à participer aux discussions sur la mise en œuvre d’opérations dans des zones dangereuses avec les cellules.

**Principales responsabilités :**

Le poste est principalement basé sur le terrain avec un ratio d’environ 70/30 entre terrain et siège, avec des durées de séjour entre 2 semaines et 1 mois par déplacement. Entre les missions, le MIO travaillera au siège au sein de l’unité sécurité.

**1. Organise ses visites terrain pour l’accompagnement des équipes dans la révision de leur gestion de la sécurité**

- Préparer les termes de référence des visites en fonction des objectifs fixés par la coordination terrain, le desk et la direction des opérations.
- Sensibilisation du personnel MSF à la politique de prise de risque et de gestion de la sécurité, en portant une attention particulière à la participation du personnel national.
- Diagnostic de la gestion de la sécurité, impliquant la sécurité appliquée, sur le terrain avec proposition d’amélioration.
- Animation d’atelier (mapping d’acteurs, analyse des risques…) et de sessions de formations avec les équipes terrain en impliquant le personnel national.
- Aide à la rédaction et mise en place des politiques de sécurité sur les missions.
- Ecriture avec les équipes sur le terrain d’un plan d’action.
- Être en support des cellules (RC, ARC, RRH et superlog) pour assurer une continuité du travail réalisé sur le terrain.

**2. Apporter un conseil et un support direct aux opérations en collaboration avec le SFP.**

- Participer à l’identification d’équipements dédiés à la gestion de la sécurité, à leur mise en œuvre sur le terrain et à la capitalisation d’expérience sur leur usage.
- Mettre à disposition des cellules et des terrains un ensemble de trames de documents et de protocoles pour la gestion de la sécurité et les maintenir à jour.
- Contribue à la préparation pour la « gestion » d’incidents majeurs, conseille et accompagne dans les prises de décisions relatives à la gestion de ces situations.
- Réalise des missions d’évaluation / conseil / apprentissage sur le terrain portant sur l’analyse et la gestion de risques généraux ou spécifiques (par exemple kidnapping).
- A la demande, conseille et accompagne les responsables des cellules, les responsables logistiques et les chefs de mission dans l’analyse des risques, le développement des guides de sécurité et procédures, plans de contingence et système de reporting.
- Participe, au briefing et débriefing des équipes sur les sujets spécifiques de la sécurité
- Administre le logiciel de remontée d’incident Sindy.

**3. Appuyer le département des opérations à la mise en œuvre d’opérations dans des zones dangereuses.**

- Participer à une cellule de crise à la suite d’un incident critique.
- Assurer l’intérim coordinateur projet ou chef de mission dans des zones dangereuses ou à la suite d’un incident critique.
- Participer aux discussions sur la mise en œuvre d’opérations en zone dangereuse avec la direction des opérations et les cellules.

**4. Appuyer l’unité sécurité sur la préparation de MSF OCP à la réponse d’incident critique.**

- Identifier avec les missions le personnel-cible.
- Organiser et animer un atelier de réponse à un incident critique sur le terrain.
- Identifier avec les équipes terrain les axes de travail pour améliorer notre préparation sur le terrain.
- Assister le point focal sécurité sur l’organisation d’atelier de formation à la réponse d’incident critique du personnel du siège.

**Profil recherché**

**Expérience :**

- Au moins 12 mois d’expérience sur 2 terrains humanitaires différents en tant que coordinateur (chef de mission, coordinateur logistique, coordinateur projet) sont indispensables.
- Expérience préalable dans la formation d’adultes est un atout.
- Expérience requise dans la gestion de contextes sécuritaires complexes et appréciée dans les situations de crise. Une expérience au siège de MSF à Paris est un plus.

**Compétences :**

- Production de supports.
- Méthodes d’animation et d’évaluation d’ateliers de formation (participation antérieure à la formation de formateurs ou animateur de formations dispensée par l’Unité de Formation OCP par exemple).

**Aptitudes** :

- Goût du travail en équipe, très bon relationnel, capacité d’organisation.
- Bonne capacité d’analyse, de synthèse et de transmission de compétences.

**Langues :** Français et anglais B2 minimum à l’écrit et à l’oral

**Conditions d'emploi**

**Statut :** CDD de 12 mois à temps complet. Poste terrain, rémunération niveau 13 selon la grille de salaires terrain MSF et en fonction de l’ancienneté et de l’expérience pertinente pour ce poste. **Conditions :** 70% du temps sur nos terrains d’intervention et 30% au siège (Paris ou lieu à définir). Prise en charge de l’hébergement, des déplacements et perdiem lors des passages et séjours au siège.

**Poste à pourvoir :** début novembre 2026

*A MSF, nous valorisons la diversité et cherchons à avoir un environnement de travail inclusif et accessible. Nous encourageons toutes les personnes qui possèdent les qualifications requises à postuler, indépendamment de leur origine ethnique, nationale ou culturelle, de leur âge, de leur sexe, de leur orientation sexuelle, de leurs convictions, de leur handicap ou d'autres aspects de leur identité.*

**Date limite de dépôt de candidatures :** 2 novembre 2026

jobs.title: Oficial MEAL (Proyecto RET)
jobs.body:
## **Antecedentes**

RET está comprometido a trabajar en emergencias, en crisis prolongadas y en contextos frágiles para aliviar los sufrimientos más profundos, construir la resiliencia de las personas y mejorar su autosuficiencia.

Somos una de las ONG líderes en ofrecer soluciones a medida y programas pertinentes para reducir las brechas y responder a las necesidades y retos reales de las comunidades.

Asumimos un papel catalizador decisivo en el desarrollo sostenible. Nuestro objetivo es provocar un cambio positivo significativo que permita a jóvenes y mujeres jóvenes especialmente vulnerables tomar las riendas de sus vidas y hacer realidad sus derechos sociales y económicos.

Acompañamos a las personas, a los refugiados, a los retornados, a los desplazados internos y a las comunidades de acogida, adoptando los principios fundamentales de humanidad, imparcialidad, neutralidad e independencia.

En el marco de los proyectos que RET International implementa en Venezuela, se publica la posición de Oficial MEAL (Proyecto RET).

## **Descripción del puesto**

### **Objetivo del Puesto**

El/la Oficial MEAL – Proyecto será responsable de implementar y dar seguimiento al sistema de Monitoreo, Evaluación, Rendición de Cuentas y Aprendizaje del proyecto en las intervenciones bajo responsabilidad de RET, asegurando el seguimiento sistemático del Marco de Resultados, la recolección, procesamiento, análisis, calidad, integridad y trazabilidad de la información, así como la adecuada documentación de los resultados y Medios de Verificación.

Será responsable de recopilar, revisar, validar y consolidar la información generada por los equipos y Oficiales de Monitoreo Local de RET, y remitirla oportunamente al Oficial MEAL – Punto Focal del Consorcio, de conformidad con las definiciones de indicadores, herramientas, metodologías, protocolos y calendarios establecidos a nivel consorcial.

Asimismo, asegurará la aplicación por parte de RET de los procedimientos comunes establecidos para el registro de participantes, control de duplicación y deduplicación, seguimiento de cohortes, calidad y protección de datos, rendición de cuentas a las poblaciones afectadas (AAP), evaluación y aprendizaje, generando evidencia oportuna para la toma de decisiones y la mejora continua de la implementación.

### **Ubicación del puesto**

La posición está basada en la Oficina Nacional de RET, ubicada en el Área Metropolitana de Caracas, con misiones frecuentes a las zonas de intervención, de acuerdo con las necesidades del proyecto.

### **Línea de Reporte y coordinación**

- Reporta al Oficial MEAL (Punto focal del Consorcio).
- Supervisa directamente a los/las Oficiales de Monitoreo Local del proyecto (Falcón, Carabobo y Aragua; La Guaira, Miranda y Distrito Capital).
- Trabaja en estrecha coordinación con el/las Coordinador del Proyecto, Gerencia de Programas de RET en Venezuela y el equipo MEAL del Consorcio.
- Participa en los espacios técnicos MEAL del Consorcio y aplica, en el ámbito de las intervenciones de RET, las metodologías, herramientas, procedimientos y estándares acordados para el proyecto.

**Responsabilidades Específicas**

#### ***1***\*\*. Implementación y seguimiento del sistema MEAL\*\*

- Implementar, en el ámbito de las intervenciones bajo responsabilidad de RET, el Plan MEAL, Marco de Resultados, herramientas y procedimientos de monitoreo establecidos para el proyecto.
- Monitorear periódicamente el avance de los indicadores, productos, resultados y metas correspondientes a RET, verificando el cumplimiento de los criterios y metodologías de medición establecidos.
- Mantener actualizadas las matrices y herramientas de seguimiento correspondientes a RET, incluyendo avances por indicador, territorio, actividad, población objetivo y demás desagregaciones requeridas.
- Monitorear mensualmente los indicadores clave de desempeño (KPIs) e informar oportunamente sobre el grado de cumplimiento, desafíos, riesgos y oportunidades identificadas.
- Emitir alertas tempranas sobre desviaciones, brechas o riesgos que puedan afectar el cumplimiento de las metas y resultados asignados a RET y contribuir a la definición y seguimiento de acciones correctivas
- Supervisar, acompañar y brindar asistencia técnica continua a los/las Oficiales de Monitoreo Local de RET, asegurando la correcta aplicación de herramientas, metodologías y procedimientos MEAL.

#### *2. Recolección, revisión, validación y consolidación de información de RET*

- Recopilar periódicamente la información programática y de monitoreo generada por los Oficiales de Monitoreo Local y demás equipos de RET, conforme a los formatos y calendarios establecidos para el proyecto.
- Revisar y validar la información recibida antes de su consolidación, verificando su completitud, consistencia, exactitud, oportunidad y correspondencia con las definiciones de indicadores, metas, desagregaciones y Medios de Verificación establecidos.
- Identificar inconsistencias, vacíos, errores o información faltante y coordinar con los equipos responsables de RET las aclaraciones, correcciones y ajustes requeridos.
- Consolidar la información de las intervenciones implementadas por RET en las bases de datos, matrices y herramientas de seguimiento correspondientes, asegurando la trazabilidad de la información hasta sus fuentes y Medios de Verificación.
- Remitir al Oficial MEAL – Punto Focal del Consorcio la información de RET previamente revisada, validada y consolidada, de acuerdo con los formatos, protocolos y calendarios de reporte establecidos a nivel consorcial.
- Atender y dar seguimiento a las observaciones, solicitudes de aclaración o ajustes derivados de los procesos de revisión y consolidación a nivel del Consorcio.

#### *3. Lineamientos, Estándares Institucionales y Calidad de Data*

- Apoyar la elaboración y actualización de los instrumentos de la Caja de Herramientas de M&E de RET.
- Diseñar y adaptar instrumentos para la recolección de datos operativos y de contexto, garantizando la inclusión de mecanismos accesibles de retroalimentación y quejas (AAP) con niñas, niños, docentes y familias.
- Velar por la rigurosidad, calidad, transparencia, consistencia, trazabilidad y precisión de las bases de datos del proyecto, asegurando el resguardo seguro y la confidencialidad de la información registrada (física y en la nube).
- Realizar controles y verificaciones periódicas de calidad de datos, documentando hallazgos y dando seguimiento a las acciones correctivas correspondientes.
- Asegurar la aplicación de las desagregaciones establecidas por el proyecto, incluyendo sexo, edad y discapacidad, así como otras variables definidas en el Marco de Resultados.
- Garantizar el adecuado almacenamiento, respaldo, confidencialidad y seguridad de la información generada por RET, conforme a los protocolos institucionales y del proyecto sobre protección y gestión responsable de datos.
- Garantizar la incorporación de los enfoques transversales de género (IASC GAM), inclusión de personas con discapacidad (Set Breve de Washington) y estándares de Educación en Emergencias (INEE).
- Participar en reuniones periódicas de revisión técnica con la Coordinación Nacional de M&E para evaluar el avance de los indicadores.

#### 4. Registro de participantes, control de duplicación

- Implementar en RET los procedimientos consorciales para el registro único de participantes, control de duplicación.
- Supervisar la correcta asignación y utilización de los mecanismos de identificación definidos por el proyecto, asegurando la trazabilidad de las personas participantes entre actividades y modalidades implementadas por RET.
- Realizar controles periódicos sobre las bases de RET para identificar y resolver posibles duplicaciones o inconsistencias antes de su remisión para la consolidación consorcial.
- Coordinar con el Oficial MEAL – Punto Focal del Consorcio los procesos de cruce y de duplicación que requieran comparación entre los registros de RET y los de otras organizaciones del Consorcio.
- Mantener documentación de los procedimientos y controles aplicados por RET para garantizar el adecuado conteo de participantes\*.\*

#### 5. Seguimiento de cohortes y medición de indicadores

- Asegurar la correcta aplicación de las definiciones y metodologías de medición de los indicadores correspondientes a las intervenciones de RET, incluyendo métodos de cálculo, numeradores, denominadores, fuentes, frecuencias y desagregaciones.
- Implementar los mecanismos establecidos para el seguimiento longitudinal de las cohortes de participantes atendidos por RET, particularmente para aquellos indicadores que requieren seguimiento periódico de acceso, asistencia, permanencia, continuidad, finalización, aprendizaje u otros resultados.
- Verificar la consistencia de los universos, registros, numeradores y denominadores utilizados para el cálculo de los indicadores.
- Identificar dificultades o inconsistencias metodológicas y elevarlas oportunamente al Oficial MEAL – Punto Focal del Consorcio para su revisión y orientación.

#### 6. Medios de Verificación (MoV)

- Liderar la organización, sistematización y actualización de los Medios de Verificación (MoV) correspondientes a las intervenciones implementadas por RET, de conformidad con el Plan MEAL y el Marco de Resultados.
- Elaborar los informes de monitoreo trimestrales y apoyar en la consolidación de los reportes mensuales y finales exigidos por el donante.
- Orientar a los Oficiales de Monitoreo Local en la verificación y validación periódica de la calidad de la información que alimenta los sistemas de reporte.
- Realizar verificaciones periódicas de correspondencia entre resultados reportados, bases de datos y respectivos Medios de Verificación.

#### 7. **Monitoreo de campo**

- Planificar y realizar visitas periódicas de monitoreo a las zonas de intervención de RET para verificar el avance, cobertura y calidad de las actividades, así como la consistencia de la información reportada.
- Realizar verificaciones de la calidad de los datos y evidencias generadas en terreno, conforme al Plan MEAL y los procedimientos establecidos para el proyecto.
- Documentar hallazgos, brechas y recomendaciones derivadas del monitoreo y realizar seguimiento a las acciones de mejora acordadas con los equipos correspondientes.
- Coordinar con los equipos técnicos de RET para promover la utilización de los hallazgos de monitoreo en la mejora de la implementación.

#### 8. **Rendición de cuentas a las poblaciones afectadas (AAP)**

- Implementar y dar seguimiento, en las intervenciones bajo responsabilidad de RET, a los **mecanismos de rendición de cuentas, retroalimentación y quejas (AAP)** establecidos para el proyecto.
- Asegurar que dichos mecanismos sean seguros, confidenciales, accesibles, inclusivos y apropiados para niñas, niños, adolescentes, docentes, familias y comunidades.
- Sistematizar y analizar periódicamente la retroalimentación recibida e identificar tendencias, necesidades y oportunidades de mejora.
