Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.  
  
**Compensation:** ($28-36/hour). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

jobs.title: LEBANON - DEPUTY HR RESPONSIBLE DEPARTMENT (M/F) - BEIRUT
jobs.body:
## ABOUT US 

**Desired start date: ASAP**  
**Duration of the mission: 2 months**  
**Location: Beirut**

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms.

## ABOUT THE MISSION

Lebanon hosts about 1.5 million Syrian refugees, mainly in its Northern governorates (Akkar and Tripoli) and in the Bekaa Valley. SI has been working in Lebanon since March 2013, to address the immediate needs of both Syrian refugees and Lebanese citizens affected by the crisis. In recent years, SI has transitioned to more integrated programs, and now addresses basic needs such as WASH, Shelter, Health and protection (the 2 latter through partnerships). In 2020, SI Lebanon started an ambitious DRRM project which aims at developing a river-basin integrated model to prevent, prepare for and respond to emergencies such as floods. In 2021, SI Lebanon started a WASH project to work with local Water authorities (North Lebanon Water Establishment) to improve the functioning of water supply networks. SI is also addressing the consequences of the Beirut Blast response through a two-phased project to rehabilitate damaged dwelling units and public spaces (in partnership with the Lebanese and French Red Cross).

## ABOUT THE JOB

**General objective:**

The general objective of the position is to Support the Admin Coordination of the Mission in the HR and Administrative management for the 50 national staff and 5 international staff in the Country Office.

**The main challenges:**

The Mission underwent a severe downsizing in late 2025 and a significant emergency response in 2026. Several staff in the Mission are new. HR Department capacity reduced since late 2025.

**Priorities for the 2/3 first months:**

Adaptation of the function and salary grid; training of new Admin/HR staff on SI tools and procedures; support on recruitment of new positions.

**Security constraints :**

Security 2 level in Beirut, no severe security constraints at this stage

## YOUR PROFILE

**Diploma and Experiences :**

Diploma : BA in relevant field as minimum

Experiment in the Humanitarian sector : 3/4 years

Experiment on similar positions : more than 5 years

**Skills :**

**Technical skills**

1. HOMERE and SI payroll system
2. Knowledge of FINSCAN
3. Knowlegde of SI processes and procedures
4. Experience in managing recruitment processes
5. Desirable experience in salary grid revision, function and job descriptions revisions and restructuring

**Transversal skills**

1. Ability to work with minimal supervison
2. Ability to organize and prioritize workload independently
3. Ability to train and coach others in the department and on the field
4. Willigness to do regular field visits to different bases

**Language:**

1. English
2. Arabic (desirable)

## SI WILL OFFER YOU

**A salaried position:**  
**According to experience,** starting from EUR 2640 gross per month (2400 base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 750.

SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment.

**Breaks:** During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every three months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked.

**Insurance package:** Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded.

**LIVING CONDITIONS:**

Guesthouse in Beirut with access to facilities and internet. Easy access to restaurants, cafes and all kind of facilities in Beirut.

jobs.title: Health Senior Officer
source: Hand in Hand for Aid and Development
jobs.body:
**Vacancy Ref:** HIHFAD-2026-161

**Job Title:** Health Senior Officer

**Department:** Program

**Direct report to:** Health Department Coordinator

**Job Location:** Homs, Syria, with travel to Damascus and other locations (approx. 25% of time)

**Job Type:** Full time

**Closing date:** 31/10/2026

**About HiHFAD**

Hand in Hand for Aid and Development (HiHFAD) is a Non-Profit, Non-Governmental, Charitable Incorporated Organization registered in the United Kingdom and in Türkiye (TR: İyilik İçin El Ele Derneği) that provides high standards in humanitarian and relief services to the most vulnerable wherever needed through local engagement and global support.

Established in 2011 by a group of British-Syrian diaspora, HiHFAD was born out of a desire to extend a helping hand to vulnerable groups and displaced families in Syria and beyond. Since then, HiHFAD remained at the forefront of humanitarian agencies, providing life-saving aid to Syrians in hard-to-reach areas. Our extensive Healthcare Program has enabled us to expand and reach even more communities and internally displaced people; providing a comprehensive, integrated multi-sectoral intervention in Health, Nutrition, WaSH (Water, Sanitation and Hygiene), Protection, Shelter, Non-Food Assistance, Food Security, Livelihoods, and Education.

HiHFAD mandate is to alleviate the suffering of those in need without any type of discrimination, protect the most vulnerable, promoting social justice and welfare, and fostering durable solutions through delivering community-based humanitarian and development interventions.

**Job overview**

As part of the Program Department and based in Homs, the Health Senior Officer supports the implementation, monitoring, and quality assurance of HIHFAD's health programs, supervises assigned field health staff, and represents HIHFAD in health coordination forums, ensuring that programs are high-quality, evidence-based, and impactful.

**Main Tasks & Responsibilities**

**Program Planning, Management, and Implementation**

Assist in the implementation of health program activities, ensuring alignment with HIHFAD's overall operational plan.

Support the development of budgets for health projects.

Monitor and report on program and project spending, providing variance reports in accordance with organizational processes and procedures.

Ensure health project implementation and reporting comply with donor requirements, agreed indicators, and HIHFAD procedures.

Track project indicators against targets and flag delays or deviations to the line manager with proposed corrective actions.

Contribute to the timely, high-quality submission of health program and project performance reports.

Promote evidence-based learning and document effective practices within the health programs.

**Quality of Care and Clinical Supervision**

Conduct regular supportive supervision visits to supported health facilities using standardized checklists, and follow up on action plans.

Monitor adherence to national and WHO clinical protocols and guidelines across supported services.

Ensure implementation of Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) standards in supported facilities.

Monitor the functionality of referral pathways and the timely referral of cases, including emergency obstetric and newborn referrals.

Identify capacity gaps and contribute to training plans for health staff based on supervision findings.

**Representation, Coordination, and Partnerships**

Represent HIHFAD in Health Sector coordination meetings at national and subnational levels, and in relevant technical working groups.

Maintain effective working relationships with the Homs Health Directorate, Ministry of Health (MOH) counterparts, and health facility management in project locations.

Ensure timely submission of coordination reporting (e.g., 4W, HeRAMS, Health Sector indicators) as required.

Coordinate with UN agencies, INGOs, and local partners to strengthen referral pathways and avoid duplication.

Support the development of program ideas into concept notes and grant proposals for health programs.

**Accountability and Data Protection**

Ensure community feedback and complaint mechanisms (CFM) are accessible in supported health facilities, and that health-related feedback is followed up and addressed.

Ensure patient confidentiality and the protection of personal and medical data in line with HIHFAD policies and donor requirements.

**Staff Management**

Supervise assigned field health officers, including task allocation, follow-up, and performance feedback.

Contribute to annual performance appraisals and professional development plans of supervised staff, in coordination with the Health Department Coordinator.

**Office Culture**

Promote and model a positive, professional, and respectful office culture within the health program team.

**Background Knowledge & Experience**

**Education Level:** University degree in Medicine, Pharmacy, or Nursing or related fields

**Work Experience:** 5 years of experience in health programming, including at least 2 years in humanitarian/NGO settings in Syria

**Languages:** English: Fluent Arabic: Fluent

**Skills and Abilities**

Project and grant cycle management

Report writing in English and Arabic

Budget monitoring and understanding of donor financial and compliance requirements

M&E systems and data analysis

Field supervision and remote monitoring tools

Partnership and coordination management

Strong interpersonal, team supervision, and problem-solving skills

Solid working knowledge of PHC and secondary health care service delivery in humanitarian settings

In-depth technical expertise in at least one of the following: SRH/MNCH, NCDs, MHPSS, Trauma & Rehabilitation, EPI

Familiarity with referral systems and Health Sector standards

**Disclaimer**

Hand in Hand for Aid and Development is committed to creating an inclusive and diverse work environment where all qualified candidates receive consideration based solely on their experience and capabilities. As a humanitarian organization, we recognize the importance of diversity and are committed to ensuring that discrimination on the basis of race, color, gender, age, ethnicity, religion, disability, or marital status does not occur.

We adhere to the Humanitarian Principles and believe that the rights of all individuals, including children, women, and adults at risk, must be safeguarded. We are accountable to the communities we serve, and it is our responsibility to ensure that we do not contribute to their further harm or expose them to additional risks.

Hand in Hand for Aid and Development has a zero-tolerance policy for any form of exploitation, abuse, harassment, or discrimination. To ensure the safety and protection of those we serve, we conduct a range of pre-employment screenings and checks in accordance with our Safeguarding Policy.

HiHFAD renounces all forms of terrorism and will never knowingly support, tolerate or encourage terrorism or the activities of those who embrace terrorism or money laundering. Consistent with numerous United Nations Security Council resolutions, including 1267 Committee list of terrorists and terrorist financiers, S/RES/1269(1999), S/RES 1368(2001) and S/RES1373(2001) and the European Union, HIHFAD is firmly committed to the international fight against terrorism and in particular against the financing of terrorism. It is the policy of HIHFAD to seek to ensure that none of its and its donor funds is used, directly or indirectly, to provide support to individuals or entities associated with terrorism or money laundering. Therefore, HIHFAD will match employees, volunteers and contracted persons against the Sanctions lists on a regular basis

This vacancy is contingent upon project confirmation from the donor.

Only short-listed candidates will be contacted for interview.

jobs.title: P&C Operations Training Specialist
jobs.body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Job Overview:**

The P&C Training & Learning Delivery Specialist ensures employees and managers have the knowledge and skills to work effectively as P&C transformation initiatives roll out. This role owns end-to-end training design and delivery for Workday enhancements, process changes, and digital capability rollouts.

Working closely with the Change Management Specialist, Business Analysts, and P&C Partners, this role builds training on a real understanding of stakeholder needs and readiness — turning the Change Management Specialist's impact assessments into practical, audience-appropriate learning experiences, and applying the reusable frameworks, tools, and methodology to deliver consistently at scale.

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Training Design & Delivery**

- Lead the end-to-end design and delivery of training programs for Workday enhancements, process changes, and digital capability rollouts — developing and executing training in line with the approach and standards set out in the Global Workday Learning Strategy and Rollout Training Methodology.
- Design and conduct training needs assessments ahead of every major rollout, building on the Change Management Specialist's stakeholder impact assessments, with a consistent methodology identifying what each user group needs, in what format, and by when
- Create a range of training assets appropriate to audience and context — job aids, quick reference guides, process guides, facilitator guides, and e-learning content — establishing reusable templates and standards
- Facilitate live and virtual training sessions for P&C and non-P&C users across the organization, adapting delivery style for different audiences and contexts
- Build an evaluation framework to measure training effectiveness through feedback, assessment, and post-training adoption data, iterating on content and delivery based on findings
- Establish and maintain a centralized training library, creating the structure and governance to keep materials current as systems and processes evolve

**Partnership & Knowledge Management**

- Partner closely with the Change Management Specialist to ensure training design is grounded in real stakeholder readiness and impact findings, and coordinate on rollout timing and sequencing
- Track training completion and content-effectiveness metrics, feeding into the team's broader adoption reporting
- Build the team's training capability through reusable templates, toolkits, and standards applied across all P&C transformation projects
- Conduct post-implementation reviews on training effectiveness, using findings to improve future delivery
- Stay current on Workday training approaches and adult learning principles

**Job Requirements:**

**Work Experience**

- 3–5 years of experience in training/learning & development, ideally including system rollouts or process change contexts
- Experience building training tools, templates, or frameworks
- Solid working knowledge of Workday from an end-user or training perspective is a strong advantage
- Instructional design background or certification is an advantage
- Experience in a complex, matrixed organization preferred
- Experience creating microlearning content for adult learners and/or working with tools like Articulate 360, Adobe Suite, Moodle, or equivalent

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies**

- Instructional design capability: able to assess needs, build practical learning materials, and adapt content for different roles, formats, and audiences
- Confident facilitator of live and virtual sessions for diverse groups
- Clear and adaptable communicator across audiences
- Data-aware: able to define training effectiveness metrics, interpret findings, and recommend action
- Well-organized and able to manage multiple concurrent workstreams without losing detail

**Working Environment:**

Standard office working environment with the ability to work remote 2-3 days per week.

This role is open to candidates located and with the right to work in Kenya, Lebanon, and Colombia.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

jobs.title: 23438 Finance Officer (Migrant Protection, Return and Reintegration Programme for Sub-Saharan Africa (MPRR-SSA))
jobs.body:
Under the overall supervision of the Deputy Regional Director – Management (DRD-M) in Dakar, and the direct supervision of the Project Finance and Budget Officer – Migrant Protection, Return and Reintegration Programme for Sub-Saharan Africa (MPRR-SSA) in close coordination with the Senior Regional Programme Coordinator (MPRR-SSA), the Finance Officer (MPRR-SSA) will assist the Project Finance and Budget Officer (MPRR-SSA) in the programmes budget, accounts, and financial reports of all the implementing Country Offices (COs), provide support to the programmatic unit of the MPRR-SSA team in the areas of financial monitoring and reporting. The Finance Officer (MPRR-SSA) will work closely with the European Commission Compliance Unit in IOM Global Office Brussels, Regional Office, as well as central units at Headquarters (HQ).

The MPRR-SSA is an EU-funded programme that is implemented in 16 countries of sub-Saharan Africa, including Burkina Faso, Côte d’Ivoire, Cameroon, Chad, Ethiopia, Gambia, Ghana, Guinea, Mali, Mauritania, Niger, Nigeria, Sierra Leone, Senegal, Somalia, and Sudan.

  
**Responsibilities**

1. Assist the Project Finance and Budget Officer (MPRR-SSA) to monitor and oversee the financial management of all activities, including oversight of financial expenditure and accountability, and undertake financial analysis of all activities in the offices implementing the MPRR-SSA programme.
2. Assist the Project Finance and Budget Officer (MPRR-SSA) to oversee and coordinate the preparation and review of EU financial reports in accordance with IOM regulations and EU regulations and established procedures.
3. In coordination with the Senior Regional Programme Coordinator (MPRR-SSA), Project Managers, the Regional Office (RO) Coordination Unit, Global Office Brussels, and Resources Management Officers (RMOs), prepare budget reports, proposals, and revisions in the Project Information and Management Application (PRIMA).
4. Contribute to the budget control process and analyse variances between the budget and actual expenditures for MPRR-SSA projects.
5. Contribute to the creation of draft general instructions and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) to ensure compliance with the general instructions of IOM and relevant permanent instructions in the areas of general administration, finance, Supply Chain, Information and Communications Technology (ICT), and Human Resources (HR).
6. Contribute to the capacity building initiatives to train local staff on EU and IOM’s administrative/financial policies and procedures.
7. As assigned by the Project Finance and Budget Officer (MPRR-SSA), undertake travel to offices in view to building financial management capacity of administrative and finance staff in the field.
8. Provide support to the Project Finance and Budget Officer (MPRR-SSA) in facilitating the financial audit of the MPRR-SSA programme in accordance with the donor agreements.
9. Assess monthly financial reports and advise on resolving anomalies and unusual trends.
10. Provide advice and guidance to Country Offices (COs) in the Region with management of implementing Partners (IP) under the MPRR-SSA programme.
11. Contribute to ensure compliance with all administrative and financial rules, instructions, regulations, and procedures related to the EU-funded project(s).
12. In coordination with the Project Finance and Budget Officer (MPRR-SSA) and upon approval of the Regional Financial Comptroller, undertake duty travel to the CO to increase capacity building in financial reporting in relation to assigned projects.
13. Perform other duties as may be assigned.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master’s degree in Business Administration, Finance, Accounting, Auditing, or related fields from an accredited academic institution with two years of relevant professional experience; or,
- University degree in the above fields with four years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Experience in accounting, financial management and reporting;
- Experience in preparing clear and concise financial and management reports;
- Experience working in and with international institutions;
- Experience with internal control assessment, internal or external audit;
- Previous work experience in the region is an advantage;
- Previous working experience in emergency operations is an advantage; and,
- Experience with EU budgeting rules is mandatory.

**Skills**

- Knowledge of International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS);
- Knowledge of the IOM/UN accounting system, software, and procedures, Common System regulations, policies, and procedures is a distinct advantage;
- Familiarity with financial oversight and public administration is an advantage; and,
- Knowledge of MS Office products and good computer literacy skills are required.

**Languages**

For this position, fluency in English and French is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

jobs.title: Global Finance and Compliance Business Partner
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
jobs.body:
**Location:** United Kingdom (preferred), or other approved locations where HelpAge International is legally able to employ staff (Ethiopia, Italy, Jordan, Kenya, Spain, Tanzania, Türkiye and Zimbabwe)

**Department:** Business Support Team

**Reports to (Line Manager):** Director of Finance & Business Support

**Responsible for (Line managing):** N/A

**Grade:** E- [https://helpage.sharepoint.com/:x:/r/sites/external/HR/Global%20Finance%20%26%20Comp%20BP-Grade%20E%20Salary%20Ranges.xlsx?d=w430eb70dde154b1ea879aac96f47c68f&csf=1&web=1&e=IgX0R7](https://helpage.sharepoint.com/:x:/r/sites/external/HR/Global%20Finance%20%26%20Comp%20BP-Grade%20E%20Salary%20Ranges.xlsx?d=w430eb70dde154b1ea879aac96f47c68f&csf=1&web=1&e=IgX0R7)

**Contract Type:** Open ended

**About HelpAge**

HelpAge International works with a diverse global network of around 200 organisations across 99 countries to promote the rights of older people to lead dignified, healthy and secure lives.

Through partnership and collaborations, we work to ensure the inclusion of older people across society and strive to deliver a just and fair world for everyone as they get older. Our work is driven by our desire to achieve real impact for older people, to be inclusive, to work in partnership and to learn from our shared experience.

## **About the Job**

The Global Finance & Compliance Business Partner provides high-quality financial business partnering support and oversight to assigned programmes and organisational initiatives.

The role supports managers in ensuring compliance to policy in areas of budgeting, proposal development, donor compliance, and financial reporting. The post holder will help colleagues make informed financial decisions while ensuring compliance with organisational, donor, and regulatory requirements.

The role also lead the internal audit planning and implementation, compliance, and assurance activities across corporate and partner financial reporting.

## Key areas for impact/influence and responsibilities

**Financial Business Partnering**

- Build strong relationships with budget holders and managers, providing proactive financial advice, support and oversight.
- Support managers in understanding financial compliance and managing risks.
- Contribute to financial decision-making through analysis, insight and challenge.

**Budgeting, Forecasting and Financial Planning**

- Support the preparation of programme budgets, and financial plans with a view to ensuring compliance with policy.
- Monitor expenditure against approved budgets and provide timely feedback on variances, risks and mitigation
- Contribute to organisational financial planning processes and reporting cycles.
- Support grant managers and programme teams in understanding donor rules and compliance requirements.
- Monitor and advise on cost recovery, co-funding requirements, and financial risks associated with grants.

**Partner Financial Management**

- Support financial oversight of implementing partners in line with HelpAge’s partner-led approach.
- Review partner financial reports and supporting documentation.
- Support partner financial assessments, capacity strengthening initiatives, and compliance reviews.
- Audit selected partner organisations in line with agreed audit plan

**Compliance and Audit**

- Analyse monthly management information prepared for senior management and provide audit and assurance on them
- Support the design of relevant financial reports, dashboards and performance reports needed to manage performance and risk.
- Support the annual external audit preparation and process.
- Develop and propose an annual internal audit plan for review and approval by the Audit & Risk Committee, ensuring appropriate oversight and safeguards to maintain the independence of internal audit activities.
- Develop and maintain Internal Audit Procedures to ensure best practice and that the audits address specific areas of identified risk withing corporate accounts and programmes/partners activities
- Coordinate and implement the approved internal audit plan in accordance with established procedures and appropriate independence safeguards. At the conclusion of each audit, communicate findings to Director of Finance and Business Support Department or partner organisation, document management responses and agree corrective action plans.
- Monitor and report on the implementation of any recommendations;

Skills and experience required

**Essential**

- Professional accounting qualification or equivalent audit certification and experience.
- Significant experience in financial management, budgeting and financial reporting.
- Experience working within an NGO, charity or similar organisation.
- Strong understanding of donor-funded programmes and donor compliance requirements.
- Experience in financial audit, compliance, and investigation.
- Good communication, stakeholder management, and relationship-building skills.
- Strong Excel and financial systems skills.
- Ability to manage multiple priorities and work collaboratively across teams.

**Desirable**

- Experience supporting partner-led programming and partner financial management.
- Experience preparing donor budgets and donor financial reports.
- Knowledge of UK charity finance requirements.
- Knowledge of Charity SORP and auditing standards
- Experience using MS Business Dynamics or similar accounting systems.
- Experience supporting finance process improvements and risk management.

## Key Behavioural Competencies

Working Collaboratively with Others: Work collaboratively, building mutual trust and respect, with external organizations and partners to achieve our strategic aims and objectives; being accountable for the work we do together.

Adaptability and Flexibility: Adapt to new directions or opportunities arising within the organisation and in our work area; being flexible in our role, constantly using the feedback to learn more and evolve further.

Supporting and Facilitating Change: Lead behavioural and cultural change through embracing a supportive, collaborative and highly inclusive environment where everybody feels supported, respected and engaged.

Extend HelpAge’s Reach and Impact: Extend HelpAge’s reach and impact by creating and identifying new business development opportunities and building relationships with new partners.

Diversity and Inclusion: Lead and promote a culture of including the voices of older people across our support, convening and thought leadership roles, in a way that is transformative, empowering and highly inclusive of those marginalised by gender, economic status, disability and other factors of discrimination.

Leading Others (for managers): Demonstrate strong leadership to own unit/department and manage people in a well and reputable manner. Create an atmosphere of trust and an enabling environment where staff can contribute their best and develop their potential.

**Policies and Code of Conduct**

As a HelpAge International employee, you are expected to comply with all organisational policies and standards, and to conduct yourself in a manner consistent with our values at all times.

This includes, but is not limited to:

- Code of Conduct
- Safeguarding Policy and Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA)
- Anti-Fraud and Bribery Policy
- Anti-Bullying, Harassment and Sexual Harassment Policy
- Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Policy
- Raising a Concern (Whistleblowing) Policy
- Social Media Policy

All staff are required to familiarise themselves with these policies, complete any mandatory training, and adhere to them throughout their employment with HelpAge International.

**Safeguarding**

HelpAge International is committed to safeguarding the communities with which we work, our partners, staff and any others who we come into contact with. The post holder will also be responsible for:

- Preventing harm and abuse from our people, operations and programmes to anyone that encounters our work.
    - Reporting all safeguarding incidents you see, hear, hear about or suspect, using our internal reporting mechanism.
    - Complying with all safeguarding framework policies and practices.
    - Completing mandatory training courses relating to our safeguarding policy framework and complying with HR vetting procedures.

**SAFER RECRUITMENT**

All employments at HelpAge International will be subject to satisfactory references and appropriate screening checks, which can include misconduct disclosure schemes and terrorism finance checks.

jobs.title: MOZAMBIQUE - DEPUTY COUNTRY DIRECTOR FOR PROGRAMS (M/F) - CABO DELGADO
jobs.body:
## ABOUT US

**Desired start date: ASAP**  
**Duration of the mission: 6 months**  
**Location: CABO DELGADO**

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms.

## ABOUT THE MISSION

Solidarités International (SI) has been providing life-saving assistance in northern Mozambique since March 2019, initially responding to Cyclone Idai. As the crisis in Cabo Delgado escalated, SI began operations in Mueda in July 2021 and progressively expanded to other northern districts including Nangade, Muidumbe, Palma and, more recently, Mocímboa da Praia. By 2022, SI had established a coordination office in Pemba and operational bases in Mueda and Palma.

Following the closure of the Palma base, SI opened a new base in Mocímboa da Praia in July 2023 to support urgent returnee needs. Today, SI operates from Pemba, Mueda and Mocímboa da Praia, covering not only the northern districts (Mueda, Mocímboa da Praia, Nangade, Muidumbe and Palma) but also additional districts further south, such as Metuge, Chiúre, Mecúfi and Ancuabe.

At the beginning of 2025, major BHA funding cuts forced a significant restructuring, reducing the mission from approximately 140 to around 50 staff and prompting a reorganisation of operations to maintain essential activities. This restructuring coincided with a deterioration of the security situation in Cabo Delgado, with renewed attacks, increased displacement and unpredictable access since mid-2024.

In early 2026, the mission entered a new phase with the confirmation of significant short-term emergency funding, alongside the launch of a major 3-year development-oriented WASH/FSL/Education project in Consortium. This shift requires strengthened programmatic oversight to manage simultaneous emergency and longer-term interventions within a rapidly evolving operational context.

Despite these challenges, SI continues to deliver principled, needs-based assistance across Cabo Delgado with the support of key donors such as ECHO, SDC, CDCS, IFSAN, UNICEF and WFP.

Projects and activities include:

\- Rapid Response Mechanism to shocks (conflict, natural disasters, epidemics): multisectoral WASH / Food / Shelter-NFI assistance through CVA or in-kind distributions

\- WASH: rehabilitation of large water networks, water points construction/rehabilitation, WASH in schools and health facilities, rainwater harvesting systems, sanitation and hygiene promotion

\- FSL: seeds and equipment distributions, support to cooperatives, cash-for-work and income-generating activities

\- Shelter/NFI: mainly emergency shelter and NFI through RRM

Around 50 staff in total across the mission in April 2026, but it will increase in May/June with the new funding.

SI operates 3 bases:

• Pemba (Coordination / Operational Base): 27 staff

• Mueda (Operational Base): 19 staff

• Mocímboa da Praia (Operational Sub-base): 4 staff

• Chiure (Operational Sub-base) to be opened: 6 staff

The DCDP is based in Pemba and covers operations in all bases of SI in Mozambique.

## ABOUT THE JOB

**GENERAL OBJECTIVE:**

The Deputy CD for Programs (DCDP) is responsible for the overall supervision, quality and strategic orientation of Solidarités International programmatic operations and MEAL systems in Cabo Delgado. S/he ensures effective, high-quality and compliant implementation of programmes in line with SI strategy and donor requirements. S/he supervises Program Managers and the MEAL Manager, supports adaptive programming, and works closely with the Area Coordinator and field teams to strengthen coordination, accountability and operational continuity.

**THE MAIN CHALLENGES:**

1- Major mission restructuring following BHA funding cuts in early 2025, with reduced staffing and evolving organisational set-up, followed by a rapid increase of funding in 2026, including short-term emergency grants and a multi-year development project  
2- Short implementation timelines for emergency projects (6 months) requiring strong planning, monitoring and adaptive management  
3- Volatile and unpredictable security context requiring continuous analysis and flexible programming  
4- Multi-base programme (Pemba, Mueda, Mocímboa da Praia, Chiure) with limited resources and high coordination needs  
5- High workload linked to simultaneous project closures, scale-up of emergency response and launch of new projects  
6- Strengthening and maintaining relationships with local authorities and coordination bodies in a sensitive operational environment

**PRIORITIES FOR THE 2/3 FIRST MONTHS:**

1- Ensure structured supervision of ongoing programmes across all bases and also the suppervision of the technicall departments (WASH, FSL, RRM Co, and MEAL)  
2- Strengthen MEAL systems and ensure effective use of monitoring data and accountability mechanisms for programmatic decision-making  
3- Ensure quality closure of ending projects and structured launch of new projects (Apri-May 2026)  
4- Reinforce program compliance with donor requirements and internal procedures  
5- Clarify roles, workflows and coordination mechanisms between Program, MEAL and Support departments  
6- Lead and coordinate proposal development with Project Managers, Technical Coordinators and the Grants Department  
7- Strengthen representation and collaboration with provincial and district authorities, clusters and key partners

**SECURITY CONSTRAINTS:**

Security level 2 in Pemba with limited constraints.

Mueda and Mocímboa da Praia are security level 3, with more restrictions. Movements and activities depend on local conditions and Security Department guidance.

The security situation remains volatile, with unpredictable insurgent attacks and evolving dynamics involving armed actors. Close monitoring of the context is required for daily movement validation. Travel to field bases is mainly via UNHAS flights.

## YOUR PROFILE

**DIPLOMA AND EXPERIENCE:**

Diploma : Master in humanitarian action, development, international law or any other technical area related to the humanitarian sector

Experience in the humanitarian sector : 3/4 years

Experience on a similar position : 3/4 years

**SKILLS:**

TECHNICAL SKILLS

1. Strong Project Cycle Management skills
2. Solid background or experience in at least one technical
3. Strong understanding of MEAL systems and accountability mechanisms, with ability to ensure effective use of monitoring data for programmatic decision-making
4. Good knowledge of donor compliance and reporting requirements

TRANSVERSAL SKILLS

1. Strong information management capacity and ability to coordinate multiple activities across bases
2. Strong planning, prioritisation and organisational skills
3. Ability to represent SI with authorities, partners and coordination bodies
4. Strong analytical capacity and ability to adapt programming to evolving contexts
5. Capacity to supervise and structure teams in a complex operational environment

**LANGUAGE:**

1. English (mandatory)
2. Portuguese (strong asset)
3. Spanish or Italian (asset)

## SI WILL OFFER YOU...

**A salaried position:**  
**According to experience,** starting from EUR 3300 gross per month (3000 base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 750.

SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment.

**Breaks:** During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every three months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked.

**Insurance package:** Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded.

**LIVING CONDITIONS:**

Pemba is a coastal city with good living conditions for expatriates, including stable water and electricity and reliable 4G internet. There is no curfew, and walking is allowed during the day. SI provides comfortable office and guesthouse facilities close to amenities.

The position is based in Pemba, with frequent visits to the bases. Field bases are reachable by UNHAS flight in less than one hour. Living conditions in field locations are basic but functional.

jobs.title: HQ Programme Support Officer
jobs.body:
**PROJECT´S GENERAL INFORMATION**

***Location:** Based in either Honduras or Colombia*

***Will report to:** Regional Director*

**PROGRAM OVERVIEW:**

Founded in 1977, GOAL is an international humanitarian response agency working with vulnerable communities in more than 60 countries. GOAL aims to increase the resilient wellbeing of the world’s poorest people and focuses on those who are excluded or marginalised, particularly those who are vulnerable due to socio-economic status, gender or age. See our website at: [https://www.goalglobal.org](https://www.goalglobal.org)

**OBJECTIVE OF THE POSITION:**

The Programme Support Officer will play a vital role in the support of GOAL’s country programmes and will be part of the HQ Operations Team. Working in a fast-paced environment and undertaking tasks which will touch on a wide range of GOAL’s overseas programmes and HQ functions, they will be responsible for a broad and varying range of duties including grant management and country support.

**PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES/ROLES**

**Grant & Data Management**

- Provide support to Desk officers in the administration and management of GOAL’s portfolio of grants or other country programme related tasks
- Lead on operational data management for the countries/region supported
- Support the Desk Officer in developing donor submissions (concept notes, proposals, reports, amendments).

**Information Management**

- Providing support to Desk Officers to improve integrity and ensure the Grant Management System is up to date
- Support the maintenance of key departmental systems including the internal SharePoint page and grant management system.

**Coordination and Representation**

- Lead on donor portal management for the region, supported by the Desk Coordinator (DC)
- Support on any business development strategies with FBD and other key stakeholders
- Coordinate bilaterally and across departments on projects to ensure alignment and efficiency.

**Operational Process Management**

- Work with the Communications Department and country programme teams to develop and submit high quality case studies, stories of change or success stories and media input.
- Emergency support - Providing general support for Desk during emergency response, including sitreps and GMS support.
- Support management of Partnership data, reporting, and contracts.
- Lead on regional documentation management, administration and filing across all GOAL systems

**MINIMUM REQUIRED PROFILE**

***Professional Studies:***

- Professionals in Business Administration, Project Management, or related fields.

***Professional experience:***

- Some previous experience working in an INGO either in a field-based or HQ role.
- Good understanding and or relevant experience in the core job responsibilities noted above including: Grant and Data Management, Information Management, Coordination and representation, and Operational Process Management.
- An understanding of GOALs mission, values and strategy
- Adept in Microsoft Applications like Word, Excel, PowerPoint, etc.
- Fluency in English and Spanish with excellent writing and analytical skills.

***Desired competencies:***

- Demonstrable knowledge and experience of major institutional donors (USAID, ECHO, Irish Aid, FCDO, UN agencies), including familiarity key donor priorities, compliance, monitoring and evaluation guidelines.
- Good knowledge and experience of GOAL’s thematic programmes or sectors (including health, nutrition, wash & resilience), and/or donors (including USAID, ECHO, FCDO and Irish Aid)
