jobs.title: Project Director, Preconception Nutrition & Care, India
jobs.body:
**Employment Type:** Project, Full Time

**Title:** Project Director, Preconception Nutrition & Care, India

**Location:** New Delhi, India

**Deadline for submission:** October 31, 2025 (Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis and the position may be closed once a suitable candidate is identified.)

**About us**

Nutrition International (NI) is a global organization dedicated to delivering proven nutrition interventions to those who need them most. Working in partnership with countries, donors, and implementers, our experts conduct cutting-edge nutrition research, support critical policy formulation, and integrate nutrition into a broader development agenda. For more than 30 years now, we have focused on delivering low-cost, high-impact, nutrition interventions to people in need, driven by our mission to achieve a world where everyone, everywhere, is free from malnutrition and able to reach their full potential. Our work is guided by a dedicated and talented team of experts working globally, regionally and within countries to end malnutrition worldwide.

If you are a motivated and passionate individual who shares our conviction that a better world is possible through improved nutrition, wants to leave the world a little better than they found it, and is looking to be part of a team with a clear vision, we want to hear from you. Please consider applying for the position below which is being advertised for an anticipated project.

**About the Project**

The Preconception Nutrition and Care project is an exciting new initiative in India. It aims to change how families begin: by reaching couples of reproductive ages with nutrition, health interventions and counselling before pregnancy, so that women enter pregnancy healthier and better nourished. Healthier beginnings lead to better maternal and birth outcomes. The project takes a systems-based approach. It brings together service delivery, evidence generation, learning and government partnership, so that preconception care becomes integrated into overall health system delivery. At the heart of the project is a commitment to putting the nutritional needs of women and couples at the center of design and implementation. The project aims to generate evidence and learning from implementation, and to use it to shape national dialogue on preconception nutrition and care.

**About you**

You will have PhD or MD degree from a recognized university in one of the following areas: nutrition, public health, reproductive health and/or a related field, with atleast 10-12 years of work experience with international NGOs, UN agencies or similar working on public health, reproductive health, nutrition related programs with at least 5 years of senior level experience in project management. You will also have demonstrated the experience in managing complex partnerships with multiple stakeholders, including government bodies, NGOs, and international organizations.

Fluency in English is essential. Knowledge of Hindi and /or local languages of project states would be an advantage.

**About the role**

The Project Director will lead this work from New Delhi. You will head a small, focused team, guide a range of implementing partners and engage with state and national government. You will also be the primary voice of the project with the donor, government, research bodies and the private sector. You will work closely with Nutrition International’s Maternal Newborn Health and Nutrition and Health Economics and Nutrition Financing portfolios, as well as colleagues in the Asia Regional Office and headquarters in Ottawa.

This is a rare opportunity to lead a high-visibility project, with full accountability for results, partnerships and resources. You will help set the direction for how India, and the wider region, approaches nutrition and care before pregnancy. **In this role you** **will be responsible to:**

- Serve as the primary point of contact for donor/s, national government representatives and strategic partners to lead evidence-based negotiations on project priorities, scope, and deliverables
- Facilitate shared understanding of project scope, goals and deliverables and among project staff, partners and stakeholders.
- Guide the implementation of project activities and ensure project staff and partners are executing the project according to the approved project plan.
- Manage relations with partners, service providers and consultants of the project, according to Nutrition International’s policies. This includes the development of terms of reference, service provided and consultant/firm selection, contracting, monitoring and end of contract processes.
- Oversee and work closely with government stakeholders and partners to develop detailed annual workplans that clearly define the strategies, activities and resources (time, budget and equipment etc.) required for effective implementation of the project; and update workplans regularly to ensure the timely completion of activities and achievement of the deliverables
- Cultivate and manage strong, collaborative relationships with implementing partners, government authorities, donors and other key stakeholders. Ensure open communication channels and a shared understanding of the project’s goals, responsibilities, and timelines.
- Identify and engage with potential new partners that align with the project's objectives, ensuring their capacities complement the project's needs and strategies.
- Ensure monitoring and learning strategies and systems are applied within the project in collaboration with the Monitoring, Data and Learning sub-unit.
- Ensure a monitoring plan is developed and followed by the project team and partners. Ensure monitoring data is analyzed and used for course correction as needed.
- Ensure that the project has a comprehensive staffing strategy with the appropriate composition of team members to ensure adequate oversight and quality assurance of all work within the project.
- Manage project staff contracts and consultants in a timely manner and according to local legislation and Nutrition International policies.
- Provide financial oversight for the full scope of the project. Maintain oversight on all sub-grants within the project and their associated budget(s) and ensure that partners establish appropriate financial procedures and tools required to be in alignment with Nutrition International requirements and standards
- Develop regular cash flow projections and monitor expenditure and review variance analysis to ensure the project operates within its budget parameters.
- Ensure all project funds are managed according to established accounting policies, procedures and donor regulations.
- Ensure donor stewardship with our committed donors to sustain relationships. Build and strengthen relationships with key project stakeholders and partners to ensure the project is harmonized with other donors funded project/programs and facilitates government leadership and ownership.
- Establish mechanisms for regular communication within the project team, Country leadership and across partners and with Nutrition International leadership to maximize opportunities for program integration and to elevate issues or risks

**For more detailed information about the role**, please click on the attached [**Job Description**](https://nutritionintl.sharepoint.com/:b:/s/M365_PC-JobPostings/IQCMxQN_qQI_RamHX3ndj8Y8AdbDdsV4w2nPzLuvsWJGOi8?e=BUbcaY)

jobs.title: 23246 Programme Officer (Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E)) (P)
jobs.body:
Launched in August 2021 with funding from the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO), the Better Regional Migration Management (BRMM) Programme is IOM’s flagship labour migration programme in the East and Horn of Africa (EHOA). The programme supports efforts to strengthen labour migration governance, promote fair and ethical recruitment, enhance the protection of migrant workers and their families, and expand access to safe, orderly and regular labour migration pathways. Building on earlier phases, the current BRMM FY26–27 framework focuses on operationalising skills-to-employment, skills mobility and ethical recruitment systems for safe labour migration in the EHOA. It prioritises scalable and evidence-based interventions that improve access to decent work, strengthen national and regional labour migration systems, and contribute to reducing reliance on irregular migration routes. The programme will be implemented in four priority countries—Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia and Uganda—while continuing to support regional cooperation through the Regional Ministerial Forum on Migration (RMFM), Regional Economic Communities and relevant national institutions. It places particular emphasis on vulnerable groups, including youth, women, returnees, refugees and migrant workers, and supports interventions related to labour market information systems, public employment services, skills development and recognition, bilateral labour migration agreements, ethical recruitment, migrant protection, reintegration and engagement with countries of destination, including the Gulf States. A strong monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning approach, together with communication and visibility efforts, will support adaptive management, donor accountability and the documentation of results and lessons learned.

Under the overall supervision of the EHOA Regional Director and direct supervision of the Regional Program Management Officer, Labour Mobility and Human Development, the Programme Officer (Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E)) will be responsible for the implementation of the M&E aspects of the BRMM program in line with the expectations of the donors.

**Responsibilities**

1. Lead and be responsible for the overall Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) function of the BRMM project, including the development, updating and implementation of the project M&E plan, results framework, data collection tools, quality assurance mechanisms and monitoring procedures.
2. Provide regular technical M&E support to implementing missions, including guidance on data collection, activity monitoring, results tracking, reporting requirements, data quality and the accurate reflection of M&E plans in mission-level action plans.
3. Lead the collection, consolidation, analysis and use of BRMM project monitoring data to track progress against agreed indicators, inform programme decisions, identify implementation gaps and ensure that programme-related datasets are accurate and up to date.
4. Prepare BRMM biannual and annual reports by compiling, verifying and analysing inputs from implementing missions, ensuring that reported results are evidence-based, consistent with donor requirements and aligned with the project results framework.
5. Review and provide technical guidance on activity concept notes, mission activity reports and related workplans, ensuring that M&E requirements, indicators, targets, verification methods and follow-up actions are clearly and accurately reflected.
6. Undertake monitoring visits to implementing missions, as required, to assess progress, verify reported results, support corrective actions and provide hands-on guidance on the implementation of BRMM M&E processes.
7. Design, coordinate and conduct surveys, outcome monitoring exercises, impact assessments and other learning or evidence-generation activities when required by programme needs or requested by the donor.
8. Support adaptive management, learning and accountability by tracking risks, assumptions, lessons learned and emerging results; ensuring responsible data management; and providing evidence-based recommendations to improve BRMM implementation, reporting and donor accountability.
9. Perform such other duties as may be assigned.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master’s degree in Monitoring and Evaluation, Development Studies, Social Sciences, Statistics, Economics, Public Policy, Migration Studies, International Relations, Law, or a related field from an accredited academic institution with two years of relevant professional experience; or,
- University degree in the above fields with four years of relevant professional experience.
- Specific training or certification in Monitoring and Evaluation, Results-Based Management, data analysis, research methods, or impact assessment would be an advantage.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Experience in leading Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) functions for complex projects, including the development and implementation of M&E plans, results frameworks, indicators, data collection tools, quality assurance mechanisms and monitoring procedures;
- Demonstrated experience in Project Cycle Management (PCM), Results-Based Management (RBM), monitoring data collection, consolidation, analysis and use of evidence to inform programme implementation, reporting and adaptive management;
- Experience in providing technical M&E support to implementing missions or field teams, including guidance on activity monitoring, results tracking, data quality, reporting requirements and the integration of M&E plans into action plans;
- Experience in preparing high-quality donor reports, including biannual and annual reports, by compiling, verifying and analysing inputs from implementing partners or missions and ensuring alignment with results frameworks and donor requirements;
- Experience in reviewing activity concept notes, activity reports, workplans and related documentation to ensure that M&E requirements, indicators, targets, verification methods, risks, assumptions and follow-up actions are clearly reflected;
- Experience in conducting monitoring visits, surveys, outcome monitoring exercises, evaluations, impact assessments or other evidence-generation activities to assess progress, verify results and support programme learning;
- Experience in maintaining programme datasets, ensuring responsible data management and producing evidence-based recommendations to strengthen implementation, accountability, learning and donor reporting; and,
- Experience in labour migration, migrant protection, ethical recruitment, bilateral labour migration agreements, skills mobility or related migration governance programming would be an advantage.

**Skills**

- Strong communication and coordination skills, including the ability to present M&E findings clearly, provide practical guidance to implementing missions, and communicate evidence-based recommendations to programme teams, management and donors;
- Strong analytical skills, including the ability to collect, verify, consolidate and interpret quantitative and qualitative data for reporting, learning and decision-making;
- Excellent report-writing skills, including the ability to prepare evidence-based donor, biannual and annual reports aligned with results frameworks and reporting requirements;
- Ability to provide technical M&E guidance and capacity support to implementing missions, including on activity monitoring, data quality, reporting and the integration of M&E requirements into concept notes and action plans; and,
- Ability to conduct monitoring visits, surveys, outcome monitoring, impact assessments and learning exercises to support adaptive management and donor accountability.

**Languages**

For this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian, and Spanish) or a relevant EHoA languages is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

jobs.title: Consultant.e Power BI Developer – Industrialisation des rapports Business Intelligence
jobs.body:
**Titre : Consultant.e Power BI Developer – Industrialisation des rapports Business Intelligence**

**Date : 15/10/2029**

**Référence : ​HULO-TDR-BAR-2026-004​**

Cet appel à candidatures est ouvert à tous les consultants éligibles, en accord avec les procédures et principes de hulo.

**Contexte de la consultance :**

La Coopérative hulo, créée en juin 2021, est la première Société Coopérative Européenne (SCE) opérant dans le secteur humanitaire. Son objectif est d'accroître l'impact de l'aide humanitaire en renforçant les liens et la solidarité entre les acteurs de la logistique humanitaire et en améliorant les performances grâce à la mise en commun des ressources et de l'expertise en matière de logistique et de chaîne d'approvisionnement.

Hulo développe son écosystème Data afin de renforcer ses capacités en matière de Data Science, Business Analytics et Business Intelligence (BI). Le département Business Analytics & Research (BAR) développe et maintient notamment des rapports Power BI destinés aux équipes internes et aux organisations participant aux initiatives de hulo.

Certains rapports BI sont actuellement à l'état de prototype. Ils nécessitent des améliorations fonctionnelles et techniques, ainsi que la prise en compte des retours des utilisateurs, avant de pouvoir être déployés en production.

En parallèle, hulo souhaite structurer et industrialiser son environnement de développement BI. L'objectif est de disposer de processus et d'outils permettant de développer, tester, déployer et maintenir les rapports de manière plus standardisée, fiable et efficace.

Dans ce contexte, hulo souhaite recruter un.e consultant.e Power BI Developer pour accompagner le département BAR dans la finalisation des rapports existants et la mise en place d'un environnement adapté à leur développement et à leur maintenance à long terme.

L'environnement technique concerné s'appuie notamment sur :

- Microsoft Power BI
- Microsoft Fabric
- Microsoft Power Platform
- Microsoft SharePoint

**Perimètre général du travail attendu du.de la Consultant.e :**

L'objectif principal de cette consultance est d'améliorer la maturité opérationnelle de l'environnement Business Intelligence de hulo, en finalisant les rapports prioritaires et en mettant en place les pratiques et outils nécessaires à leur industrialisation.

La mission s'articulera autour de deux axes complémentaires.

**Axe 1 – Finalisation et mise en production des rapports BI:**

- Prendre connaissance des rapports Power BI existants et de leur niveau de maturité
- Échanger avec les équipes BAR et les utilisateurs concernés afin de recueillir et analyser leurs retours
- Identifier les écarts entre les prototypes actuels et les besoins opérationnels
- Améliorer les rapports sur les plans fonctionnel, visuel et technique
- Vérifier la cohérence des indicateurs, des mesures DAX, des filtres et des interactions, en fonction du périmètre de chaque rapport
- Améliorer les performances et la fiabilité des rapports lorsque cela est nécessaire
- Vérifier les règles d'accès aux données et les paramètres de partage applicables
- Organiser les tests et la validation avec les utilisateurs
- Préparer et réaliser le déploiement en production des rapports validés
- Documenter les rapports finalisés et les principaux choix techniques.

Les rapports à traiter seront priorisés conjointement avec hulo au démarrage de la mission.

**Axe 2 – Industrialisation du développement et de la maintenance BI:**

Le.la consultant.e devra analyser l'environnement existant et proposer puis mettre en place une organisation technique permettant de standardiser le cycle de vie des rapports BI.

Les travaux pourront notamment couvrir :

- La structuration des espaces de travail et des environnements de développement, de test et de production, en fonction des capacités disponibles dans l'environnement Microsoft de hulo
- La définition d'un processus de développement, de validation et de publication des rapports
- La mise en place de pratiques de gestion des versions et de suivi des modifications
- La standardisation des conventions de nommage, de la documentation et des éléments réutilisables
- L'amélioration de l'organisation des modèles sémantiques, des connexions aux sources de données et des dépendances entre rapports
- L'utilisation des fonctionnalités de Microsoft Fabric et de Power BI permettant de faciliter les déploiements et la maintenance
- L'identification des usages pertinents de Microsoft Power Platform pour automatiser certaines tâches ou étapes du processus BI
- L'utilisation de SharePoint pour organiser l’extranet donnant accès aux rapports BI
- La définition de bonnes pratiques en matière de sécurité, de gestion des accès, de tests et de contrôle qualité
- La préparation d'une documentation et le transfert de compétences à l'équipe BAR.

Le.la consultant.e devra privilégier les fonctionnalités et licences déjà disponibles chez hulo, en identifiant clairement les éventuels prérequis techniques ou financiers supplémentaires.

La mission ne consiste pas à reconstruire l'ensemble de l'écosystème BI de hulo, mais à mettre en place une approche pragmatique, adaptée aux besoins actuels et réutilisable pour les développements futurs.

Les taches décrites peuvent être menées à bien à 100% en distanciel.

**Qualifications et expérience:**

- Expérience confirmée en développement de rapports et de tableaux de bord Power BI
- Maîtrise de Power Query, du langage DAX et de la modélisation des données
- Expérience avec les pipelines de déploiement Power BI ou Fabric et les outils de gestion de versions
- Connaissance des modèles sémantiques partagés et des pratiques de gouvernance BI
- Expérience dans la gestion de rapports utilisés par plusieurs organisations ou catégories d'utilisateurs
- Expérience dans l'optimisation des performances et la fiabilisation des rapports BI
- Bonne connaissance de Microsoft Fabric et de son intégration avec Power BI
- Expérience dans la structuration d'environnements de développement, de test et de production
- Bonne connaissance des mécanismes de déploiement, de gestion des versions et de maintenance des solutions BI
- Maîtrise de Microsoft Power Platform, notamment pour l'automatisation de processus lorsque cela est pertinent
- Expérience avec SharePoint pour la gestion d’un extranet
- Bonne compréhension des enjeux de sécurité des données, de gestion des accès et de partage des rapports
- Capacité à recueillir les besoins des utilisateurs et à les traduire en améliorations fonctionnelles et techniques
- Capacité à produire une documentation claire et à transférer ses compétences à une équipe interne

**Management et lignes hiérarchiques**

Ce · tte consultant·e sera placé·e sous la responsabilité du directeur du département « Business Analytics & Research » et travaillera de concert avec un Data Scientist et un analyste métier.

**Processus de contractualisation :**

Le.la Consultant.e séléctionné.e sera contractualisé.e par hulo sur deux tranches :

- 1 tranche ferme pour une durée estimée de 10 à 15 **jours**,
- 1 tranche optionnelle pour une durée estimée de 20 à 30 jours

**Calendrier**

Tranche ferme - Novembre – décembre 2026

Tranche optionnelle - Février - Juin 2027

Sans obligation de travailler à temps plein pour hulo durant cette période.

**Candidature**

Hulo appelle à candidater pour la provision des services décrits ci-dessus. Les Consultant.e.s intéressé.e.s devront soumettre :

- Un CV présentant les compétences et expériences pertinentes
- Une proposition technique décrivant l'approche proposée pour les deux axes de la mission
- Une proposition financière indiquant le taux journalier et le coût total de la mission
- Des références ou exemples de missions comparables, si disponibles

**Critères de sélection:**

Les candidatures seront évaluées selon les critères suivants.:

- Expertise Power BI
- Expertise Microsoft Fabric
- Industrialisation et maintenance
- Maîtrise de Power Platform et SharePoint
- Compréhension des besoins métier
- Documentation et transfert de compétences
- Rapport qualité-prix

jobs.title: Responsable Eau Hygiène et Assainissement (EHA)
jobs.body:
Médecins Sans Frontières, association médicale humanitaire internationale créée en 1971, apporte une assistance médicale à des populations dont la vie est menacée : principalement en cas de conflits armés, mais aussi d'épidémies, de pandémies, de catastrophes naturelles ou encore d'exclusion des soins.

MSF recrute en urgence des Responsables Eau Hygiène et Assainissement, notamment dans le cadre des projets médicaux déployés face à l'épidémie Ebola en cours en République Démocratique du Congo.

**Votre mission**

En tant que responsable Eau Hygiène et Assainissement (EHA), vous avez pour mission d’assurer la mise œuvre des activités  
d’approvisionnement en eau, de gestion des eaux usées, de lutte anti vectorielle et de gestion des déchets dans les structures de santé  
supportées par MSF. De plus, vous êtes amené·e à apporter les secours non médicaux, dans votre domaine, aux populations déplacées  
en raison de conflits, catastrophes naturelles, etc. Vous êtes responsable de la bonne mise en œuvre et du suivi des activités EHA au  
sein de chaque projet/mission. Le tout selon les normes universelles de santé et les procédures MSF.

**Principales responsabilités :**

- Réaliser les évaluations en collaboration avec les équipes médicales, identifiant les besoins en eau, hygiène et assainissement ;
- Assurer la quantité et la qualité de l’eau dans toutes les activités du projet et pour nos bénéficiaires ;
- En collaboration avec l’équipe médicale, vous participez à l’hygiène hospitalière et mettez en place la lutte contre les vecteurs de maladies ;
- Dimensionner les ouvrages sanitaires (douches, latrines, etc.), les systèmes de traitements des eaux usées ainsi que leurs évacuations ;
- Assurer le suivi et la mise en œuvre de la gestion des déchets hospitaliers selon les recommandations MSF ainsi que le dimensionnement des zones à déchets pour les structures de santé ;

**Activités :**

- Gérer le matériel EHA du projet : achat, installation, maintenance et suivi ;
- Gérer les infrastructures du projet : construction et travaux de réhabilitation, interventions techniques dans le domaine de l’eau-hygiène et assainissement ;
- Encadrer et former les équipes logistiques, personnel national et/ou expatrié·e ;
- Apporter le support logistique EHA aux équipes médicales ;
- Participer à la définition des orientations opérationnelles et des objectifs logistiques du projet en collaboration avec les équipes médicales et le coordinateur du projet

**Profil recherché**

**Formation / Expériences :**

- Hydraulicien·ne, spécialiste en traitement de l’eau, gestion environnementale, hydrogéologue, Ingénieur·e/technicien·ne en assainissement et/ou autres qualifications techniques en rapport avec les domaines d’activité : gestion des déchets, lutte anti-vectorielle ou en contrôle infectieux.
- Au moins deux ans d’expériences professionnelles dans le domaine de l’EHA.
- Des compétences en encadrement ou en formation sont un plus.
- Une expérience à l’international et dans le milieu humanitaire est un atout.

Aptitudes :

- Disposition à travailler au sein d'équipes multiculturelles et pluridisciplinaires.
- Diplomatie, pédagogie, flexibilité, dynamisme.
- Bonnes capacités d’adaptation et d’organisation.

**Langues :**

- Français courant
- Anglais (B1)

**Disponibilité** : Engagement de **3 à 12 mois.** Missions de 3 mois pour les projets déployés face à l'épidémie Ebola en cours en République Démocratique du Congo.

**IMPORTANT : la durée de mission sur ce contexte est inférieure à 6 mois, de l'ordre de 3 mois. Merci d'indiquer durée de mission = 6 mois dans le formulaire de candidature, même si vous vous intéressé.e à un départ en RDC sur les projets de lutte contre Ebola.**

**Ce que nous offrons**

- Salaire en fonction de l'ancienneté et de l'expérience pertinente
- Prise en charge des frais liés à la mission (transport, visas, logement, vaccins, etc.).
- Assurances santé, rapatriement, retraite.
- Perspectives d’évolution : formations, accompagnement et développement de carrière dans un large éventail de contextes humanitaires.

**Pourquoi vous ?**

Vous êtes rigoureux·se, engagé·e, stratégique, à l’écoute, et vous souhaitez mettre vos compétences au service de populations en situation de vulnérabilité.

**Pour postuler :**

Merci de déposer votre candidature complète sur notre site, à ce lien (candidature spontanée) : [Responsable Eau Hygiène et Assainissement (EHA) | Médecins sans frontières](https://www.msf.fr/agir/rejoindre-nos-equipes/decouvrir-nos-metiers/responsable-eau-hygiene-et-assainissement-eha)

*Les candidatures féminines sont fortement encouragées.*

**Date limite de dépôt de candidatures :** 15 décembre 2026

jobs.title: Trainer for "The Use of GIS in Humanitarian Operation" - Only Local Candidates from Madrid
jobs.body:
**Location:** Madrid, Spain - due to budget limitation we can only consider applicants from Madrid  
**Training Dates:** 9–10 November 2026  
**Daily Schedule:** 09:00 AM – 4:00 PM  
**Delivery Mode:** In-person  
**Participants:** 2 professionals  
**Engagement:** Short-term training consultancy

## Project Overview

Accordemy® is seeking an experienced GIS trainer and consultant to deliver a two-day, in-person professional development program titled **"The Use of GIS in Humanitarian Projects"** in Madrid, Spain.

The program aims to strengthen participants' ability to apply Geographic Information Systems (GIS) in humanitarian operations, project planning, land and asset management, risk assessment, and evidence-based decision-making.

The training should emphasize practical applications, real-world scenarios, and the effective use of geospatial information to support humanitarian project implementation and management.

## Proposed Training Topics

The program is expected to cover:

1. **GIS Applications in Humanitarian Projects** — GIS for humanitarian planning, coordination, needs assessment, and operational management.
2. **Geospatial Data Collection and Management** — Spatial datasets, data integration, mapping layers, and geographic information management.
3. **Spatial Analysis and Risk Assessment** — Identifying vulnerable areas, assessing geographic risks, and supporting project prioritization.
4. **Land and Asset Mapping** — Mapping land parcels, infrastructure, resources, and project-affected locations.
5. **GIS for Evidence-Based Decision-Making** — Spatial suitability assessment, comparison of alternatives, and management decision support.
6. **GIS Visualization and Reporting** — Thematic maps, dashboards, analytical outputs, and communicating geographic findings to stakeholders.
7. **AI Integration with GIS** — Practical applications of artificial intelligence, automation, and emerging geospatial technologies.
8. **GIS Data Security and Stakeholder Information Management** — Data privacy, access control, secure sharing, and responsible management of sensitive geographic information.
9. **Practical GIS Exercises** — Hands-on demonstrations and case studies relevant to humanitarian and development projects.

The final training outline will be agreed upon with the selected consultant, considering their technical expertise and recommendations.

## Consultant Qualifications

Candidates should demonstrate:

- Strong professional experience in Geographic Information Systems and spatial analysis.
- **Proficiency in ArcGIS and proven experience teaching or delivering professional training using ArcGIS.**
- Experience designing and delivering instructor-led GIS training programs.
- Ability to explain technical GIS concepts clearly to professionals and managers.
- Practical knowledge of GIS applications in humanitarian assistance, international development, land management, or related fields.
- Familiarity with AI-assisted geospatial analysis and GIS data management practices.
- Excellent English communication and presentation skills.
- Availability to deliver the training in person in Madrid on the specified dates.

Experience working with humanitarian organizations, development agencies, NGOs, or international institutions would be an advantage.

## Expected Deliverables

- A finalized two-day training outline.
- Instructor-led delivery with practical demonstrations.
- Relevant training presentations, exercises, and example datasets.
- Hands-on activities that allow participants to apply the concepts.
- Supporting technical reference materials, where appropriate./

jobs.title: Request for Proposals: Financial and Risk Management Compliance Audits for Sub-Grantees
jobs.body:
**Request for Proposals: Financial and Risk Management Compliance Audits for Sub-Grantees**

**Background and context**

Tiko engages various partners, including Community-Based Organizations (CBOs), Quality Assurance providers, SGBV service providers, and safe houses, through formal Sub-Grant Agreements to deliver community and health response services. These partnerships are critical for reaching adolescents and young women (AGYW). To ensure programmatic integrity, financial stewardship, robust risk management, and the highest standards of financial governance, Tiko requires periodic and comprehensive financial and risk management compliance audits of these entities.

The relevant locations for this scope are:

- **Kenya:** Nairobi, Mombasa, Kisumu, Machakos, Nakuru, Migori, Kilifi, Homa Bay, Bungoma, Nyamira, Kisii, Busia and Kakamega counties.
- **Uganda:** Wakiso and Kampala districts.
- **Ethiopia:** Addis Ababa and Hawassa.
- **South Africa:** City of Johannesburg, Ekurhuleni and Tshwane.
- **Nigeria:** Abuja FCT and Nasarawa.
- **Burkina Faso:** Ouagadougou and Bobo-Dioulasso.

Firms can apply for one or more markets where they can demonstrate the ability to deliver the assignments. Firms must be registered in each country where they seek to provide the services.

**Objective of the audit**

The primary objective is to verify that sub-grantees are operating in full compliance with the financial, risk management, and statutory requirements of their signed grant agreements and relevant regulatory standards. The audit will assess:

- Financial accountability, internal controls, and complete expenditure documentation.
- Compliance with anti-fraud, anti-corruption, and financial risk governance mandates.
- Accuracy, integrity, and reconciliation of financial and transactional data across reporting frameworks.
- Adherence to statutory obligations, procurement guidelines, and budget line allocations.

**Scope of audit**

1. **Expenditure verification:** Reconcile transaction listings, general ledgers, and bank statements against approved budget lines and the project scope of work.
2. **Milestone achievement:** Verify that disbursements are linked to confirmed deliverables as per the signed agreements.
3. **Expenditure verification and anti-double dipping:** Verify that all incurred expenditures are legitimate, supported by adequate documentation, and that there is no “double dipping” or duplicate funding from other sources for the same activities.
4. **External audit review:** Review external audit management reports and prior audit findings for the last two financial years. Test to ensure that all recommendations arising from findings have been implemented.
5. **Procurement compliance:** Inspect procurement documentation to ensure competitive bidding policies were followed.
6. **Internal controls:** Evaluate sub-recipient internal controls, including segregation of duties, delegation of authority, and financial software controls. Conduct walkthroughs for various cycles, including payments, payroll and assets, ensuring they are in line with policy.
7. **Statutory compliance:** Confirm compliance with statutory obligations, including tax filings, labour laws, and anti-corruption policies.

**Deliverables**

1. **Audit plan:** Detailed timeline and 100% review for selected sub-grantees.
2. **Individual audit reports:** Comprehensive audit reports for each sub-grantee featuring granular findings, objective risk ratings (Compliant / Partially Compliant / Non-Compliant), root-cause analysis of compliance gaps, and actionable, time-bound Corrective Action Plans (CAPs) complete with clear implementation deadlines, designated responsible owners, and re-verification milestones to ensure full risk mitigation.
3. **Summary consolidation:** High-level overview of systemic compliance gaps and recommended training/capacity-building interventions.

**Qualifications of firms and proposed personnel**

The selected firm and its proposed personnel must demonstrate a comprehensive profile aligned with financial audit and risk compliance requirements. Mandatory qualifications include:

- Extensive experience in conducting financial, forensic, and risk compliance audits within the NGO and development sectors.
- Proven technical expertise in financial risk management, internal controls assessment, and fraud prevention/detection methodologies.
- Certified financial and risk audit professionals, such as CPA, ACCA, CFE, or equivalent certifications.
- Strong analytical skills in financial data reconciliation, transaction testing, and identifying systemic governance and control gaps.
- Experience in reviewing grant agreements, evaluating statutory compliance, and producing actionable financial audit reports.

**Evaluation criteria**

Proposals should:

- Be clear about the relevant skills, experience and capacity of the participant in respect of this particular scope of work.
- Contain details of the proposed approach to be adopted to deliver the service in accordance with the scope of work.
- Clearly indicate whether bid participants have the capacity to meet the requirements of the scope of work.
- Clearly indicate compliance with the appropriate data protection, privacy, legal, social, tax and ethical requirements applicable to each country applied for.

Bidders must be registered firms in the countries where they seek to provide the services. A firm can bid for one or more markets depending on capacity.

Proposals will be evaluated against the following criteria:

**1. Experience, skills and ability of the service provider — 30%**

- Past experience in similar work of this nature.
- Team member experience, accompanied by brief CVs.
- Ability of the bidder to fulfil Tiko’s requirements.

**2. Technical approach and execution plan — 30%**

Proposals must contain details of the proposed approach to be adopted to deliver the service in accordance with the scope of work.

**3. Financial quotation — 10%**

Proposals should clearly indicate whether bid participants have the financial capacity to meet the requirements of the scope of work, based on the previous value of similar work undertaken, for example by sharing copies of recent audited financial statements.

**4. References — 10%**

Submission of at least three relevant and contactable clients previously served.

**5. Capacity — 20%**

Proposals should clearly indicate whether bid participants have the capacity to meet the requirements of the scope of work.

**Total: 100%**

jobs.title: Project Finance Officer
jobs.body:
Sightsavers implements projects in over 30 countries in Africa and South Asia working to eliminate avoidable blindness and promote the rights of people with disabilities.

**Title**: Project Finance Officer

**Location**: Monrovia, Liberia

**Contract**: Two-year fixed term contract

**Salary**: Local Terms and Conditions apply

**About the role**

Working closely with our programme and finance teams, project partners and Liberia’s Ministry of Health, you will manage project budgets, monitor expenditure, prepare financial reports and support partners to strengthen their financial processes. You will also contribute to audits, procurement and effective financial planning across the project.

This is an excellent opportunity for a finance professional who enjoys working closely with programmes and partners to ensure funding is used effectively and delivers maximum impact.

**Responsibilities**

- Preparing, maintaining and monitoring project budgets and spending plans.
- Producing monthly Budget versus Actual reports, including commentary on significant financial matters.
- Preparing accurate and timely quarterly donor financial reports.
- Monitoring project cash flow and preparing monthly cash-flow forecasts.
- Reviewing project transactions to ensure they are accurately recorded and correctly coded.
- Preparing invoice and expense projections and analysing differences against actual expenditure.
- Reviewing and consolidating financial reports submitted by project partners.
- Undertaking financial monitoring visits and supporting partners to improve their financial controls, procurement, reporting and compliance.
- Supporting audit preparation and providing the required financial documentation.
- Coordinating project procurement requirements and supporting compliance with donor rules, Sightsavers policies and value-for-money commitments.

This is a highly varied and involved role and the above is not an exhaustive list of duties or required professional skills. Please see the [Job Description](https://sightsavershh.sharepoint.com/:b:/s/HRExternal/IQD-3ZdJRH-IRb_MeChH5AeDAR2ePk8ie01YLL_B_Fw7_Sg?e=u4ghny) for full details.

**Jobholder Requirements**

**Essential:**

- A bachelor’s degree in accounting, finance, business administration or a relevant experience.
- A completed or well-advanced professional accounting qualification, such as ACCA, CPA, CIMA or an equivalent.
- At least three years’ progressive experience in project finance, ideally within an international INGO.
- Experience managing donor-funded grants and meeting donor financial reporting requirements.
- Auditing experience.
- Experience working with government organisations.
- Experience in financial management, project management and administration.
- Strong project financial management, budgeting and data analysis skills.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
- The ability to work with limited supervision

**Desirable:**

- Experience managing donor-funded projects.
- Experience supporting health or neglected tropical disease programmes.
- Experience working with Ministry of Health partnerships.
- Experience financially monitoring implementing partners and field-based activity costs.

**Closing date: 8 November 2026**

## Terms of Reference.

1. **Background**

Terre des hommes is the leading Swiss child relief agency. We are committed to improving the lives of millions of the world's most vulnerable children. Children are the first to suffer in times of war, natural disasters and because of poverty. At Terre des Hommes, our goal is to steadily improve the conditions of the most vulnerable children worldwide.

1. ## The Need/Purpose

TDH-Kenya Foundation provides nationwide health insurance coverage for its employees and their dependents. As of October 1, 2026, the organization has approximately 54 staff members based in Nairobi, Kiambu, Turkana (Kakuma), and Garissa (Dadaab and Garissa sub-counties). jobs.title: Finance Manager
jobs.body:
**1. Position Summary**

The Finance Manager has overall responsibility for managing and overseeing the day-to-day financial operations of Feed the Children in the Philippines. The position provides financial leadership, technical guidance and oversight of accounting, financial reporting, budgeting, treasury and cash management, payroll reconciliations, procurement-related financial controls, audit and risk management, and statutory compliance. The role ensures that financial transactions are accurate, appropriately authorised, adequately supported by documentation and recorded in a timely manner. It also ensures that bank accounts, balance sheet accounts, payroll, budgets and expenditure are regularly reconciled and monitored, with discrepancies investigated and resolved promptly. The Finance Manager oversees the preparation and submission of monthly financial reports, budget-versus-actual (BVA) reports, accrual schedules, balance sheet reconciliations, cash forecasts and other required financial information. The position works closely with the Country Director, programme teams, Administration, Human Resources, Procurement and the International Office to ensure resources are appropriately managed, financial risks are mitigated, and management decisions are supported by reliable financial information. The role provides functional leadership to the Finance team and ensures that financial procedures, internal controls and reporting requirements are consistently applied across the Country Office.

**2. Essential Accountabilities**

**Financial Management and Accounting:**

- Oversee day-to-day financial operations, ensuring accurate, complete and timely recording of all financial transactions.
- Ensure compliance with Feed the Children financial policies, accounting procedures, donor requirements, applicable Philippine laws and regulations, and relevant accounting standards.
- Review monthly financial reports, general ledger transactions and expenditure records to identify errors, mispostings, unusual transactions, coding inaccuracies and potential compliance concerns.
- Monitor shared cost allocations, advances, receivables, payables and other balances
- Investigate abnormal or unexplained transactions and ensure corrective action.

**Audit and Risk Management:**

- Maintain and update the financial risk tracker, tracking risks, mitigation actions and progress against agreed actions.
- Identify financial, operational, compliance and control risks and recommend preventive and corrective measures.
- Ensure effective internal financial controls, segregation of duties and policy compliance.
- Coordinate audits, donor reviews and compliance assessments.
- Monitor implementation of audit recommendations and escalate irregularities, fraud risks or policy violations.

**Reconciliations and Financial Control:**

- Oversee payroll, bank, and balance sheet reconciliations, ensuring accuracy, documentation, and timely resolution of reconciling items.
- Monitor suspense accounts, advances, and inter-account balances, investigating abnormal transactions and ensuring compliance with reporting schedules and delegated authority.

**Procurement Oversight and Payment Pack Compliance:**

- Review procurement transactions and payment packs for compliance with policies, approval thresholds, budget availability, and delegated authority.
- Verify supporting documentation, contract compliance, coding accuracy, receipt of goods/services, and budget availability before payment processing.
- Monitor procurement commitments and supplier payments, maintain audit trails in SharePoint, and escalate procurement irregularities while providing financial compliance guidance.

**Cash and Treasury Management:**

- Review procurement transactions and payment packs for compliance with policies, approval thresholds, budget availability, and delegated authority.
- Verify supporting documentation, contract compliance, coding accuracy, receipt of goods/services, and budget availability before payment processing.
- Monitor procurement commitments and supplier payments, maintain audit trails in SharePoint, and escalate procurement irregularities while providing financial compliance guidance.

**Financial Reporting & Month-End Close:**

- Ensure timely and accurate monthly financial reporting and month-end close processes.
- Maintain accrual schedules, reconcile financial records, review balance sheet accounts, and ensure proper accounting for depreciation, prepayments, and deposits.
- Prepare financial dashboards, shared-cost reports, and budget-versus-actual (BVA) analyses, presenting key variances and recommendations to management.
- Ensure all supporting documentation is uploaded to SharePoint and reports are submitted according to established timelines.

**Payroll & Statutory Compliance:**

- Oversee payroll reconciliations, payroll cost allocations, statutory deductions, and payroll-related liabilities.
- Coordinate with HR to ensure payroll accuracy, compliance, timely payments, and secure maintenance of payroll records.

**Taxation & Regulatory Compliance:**

- Ensure accurate recording, reconciliation, filing, and payment of taxes and statutory obligations.
- Oversee BIR Form 2307 compliance, maintain supporting tax documentation, monitor deadlines, and liaise with tax authorities and advisers as required.
- Escalate compliance risks, penalties, or regulatory changes impacting operations.

**Budgeting & Financial Planning:**

- Review and consolidate departmental and project budgets, ensuring alignment with organizational priorities and funding requirements.
- Monitor budget utilization, analyze variances, support forecasts, revisions, and realignments, and identify funding gaps, restrictions, overspending, or underutilization.
- Provide financial analysis to support decision-making and cash-flow planning.

**Financial Systems & Records Management:**

- Ensure accurate transaction recording and reconciliation within QuickBooks Online and other approved systems.
- Maintain complete, accurate, and accessible financial records, payment packs, reconciliations, and supporting documentation in SharePoint.
- Safeguard confidential financial information and support continuous improvement of systems, reporting processes, and internal controls.

**Team Leadership & Stakeholder Engagement:**

- Provide leadership, supervision, coaching, and technical guidance to Finance staff, ensuring accountability and high-quality outputs.
- Foster understanding of financial procedures, controls, and compliance requirements across the team.
- Collaborate with HR, Procurement, Administration, Programme teams, and International Office stakeholders to support reporting, audits, cash management, compliance, and organizational objectives.
- Promote a culture of accountability, transparency, collaboration, and sound financial stewardship.

**3. Key Performance Expectations:**

**The following deliverables will be monitored through agreed performance indicators and the organisational reporting calendar.**

- **Risk Tracker and Internal Controls**
- **Frequency:** Updated and reviewed daily, with material risks escalated promptly.
- **Internal and External Audit Support**
- **Frequency:** As required, with audit recommendations tracked through to closure.
- **Bank Reconciliations (Eight Accounts)**
- **Frequency:** Daily monitoring, with formal reconciliation and approval in accordance with the financial close calendar.
- **Balance Sheet Reconciliations**
- **Frequency:** As per the reconciliation schedule, with prompt follow-up on abnormal or outstanding items.
- **Bank Statements Against QuickBooks Online (QBO)**
- **Frequency:** Daily.
- **Accruals, Journal Entries, Depreciation, Deposits and Prepayments**
- **Frequency:** As transactions arise and during the month-end close process.
- **Payroll Reconciliations and Payroll Tax Checks**
- **Frequency:** Monthly and in accordance with statutory deadlines.
- **Procurement Transactions and Payment Packs**
- **Frequency:** Reviewed as submitted, with daily monitoring of outstanding payments.
- **Monthly Wire/Fund Transfer Requests**
- **Deadline:** By the International Office's prescribed deadline.
- **Cash and Bank Balances**
- **Frequency:** Monitored daily, with funding requirements identified promptly.
- **Budget Versus Actual (BVA) Reporting and Budget Utilisation**
- **Frequency:** Monthly, with BVA reports presented to the Country Office team.
- **Budget Requests and Forecasts**
- **Deadline:** In accordance with the established budgeting calendar.
- **Month-End Reports and Checklist**
- **Deadline:** By the 10th day of each month.
- **Financial Documentation and SharePoint Uploads**
- **Frequency:** As financial transactions are processed.
- **BIR Form 2307**
- **Deadline:** In accordance with applicable statutory requirements.
- **International Office Financial Reporting**
- **Deadline:** In accordance with prescribed International Office reporting deadlines.

**4. Qualifications and Experience:**

**Required Knowledge, Skills and Competencies**

- Strong knowledge of accounting principles, financial management, financial reporting and internal controls.
- Experience in budgeting, cash-flow management, bank reconciliations, balance sheet reconciliations and financial analysis.
- Knowledge of procurement-related financial controls, payment verification and supporting documentation requirements.
- Understanding of payroll accounting, statutory deductions, taxation and applicable Philippine financial compliance requirements.

jobs.title: Request for Proposal (RFP) On-Call IT Support Services October, 2026 India
jobs.body:
## **Request for Proposal (RFP) On-Call IT Support Services**

## **October, 2026**

**India**

## **Procurement Summary**

**Item Details**

RFP Title On-Call IT Support Services – India

Eligible Applicants India-based individual consultants and registered IT support agencies/firms

Location Remote support across India, with in-person coordination where required

Contract Period 12 months, with possible renewal subject to satisfactory performance and organisational need

Reporting To Senior IT & System Manager and India People and Operations Manager

RFP Issue Date 16th October 2026

Proposal Deadline 30th October 2026

Submission Email suppliers@girleffect.org

## **Who We Are**

Girl Effect is an international non-profit that builds media and technology that girls want, trust and need. We use evidence-based social and behaviour change approaches to help adolescent girls make informed choices about their health, education and economic future.

In India, Girl Effect’s digital-first youth programme, Chhaa Jaa, reaches girls through social media, digital content, community spaces and interactive products, including Bol Behen. Reliable IT support is essential to the teams delivering this work.

## **Background**

Girl Effect India has approximately 28 staff working across locations including New Delhi, Mumbai, Hyderabad, Pune, Nagpur, Kolkata, Ahmedabad, Noida, Gurugram and Jaipur.

Girl Effect requires dependable on-call IT support to resolve hardware and software issues, coordinate repairs and warranties, and assist with approved IT sourcing.

## **Objective**

The objective of this engagement is to maintain reliable day-to-day IT operations by providing responsive remote support, timely issue resolution, and effective coordination of repairs, warranties, and approved equipment purchases across India.

### **What You will do**

The selected service provider will be responsible for:

- Providing remote, on-call IT support to approximately 28 users across India between 10:00 a.m. and 7:00 p.m., Monday to Friday.
- Diagnose and resolve laptop, peripheral, operating-system, application, and connectivity issues within agreed service levels.
- Support IT setup and onboarding for new employees, including device configuration and troubleshooting access.
- Coordinating OEM warranty claims, repairs, and replacements, including clear communication on status, cost, and expected completion time.
- Supporting the sourcing of approved IT requirements, such as laptops and accessories, by providing specifications, availability, and quotations where requested.
- Providing access to capable support personnel and service coverage in major Indian cities, either directly or through an established support network.
- Protecting Girl Effect data, credentials and systems and complying with applicable security, confidentiality and data-protection requirements.

### **Service levels and Deliverables**

**Requirement Standard Evidence Frequency**

Support availability 10:00 a.m.–7:00 p.m., Monday–Friday Ticket or support log Ongoing

Initial diagnosis for a received deviceWithin 24 hours of receiving the device Diagnosis or update provided to the

user Per incident

Issue resolution Within three working days unless parts or

OEM action are unavailable Closure note or agreed action plan Per incident

Warranty and

repair coordination Prompt escalation and regular

status updates OEM or repair record As required

Monthly service report Incidents logged, resolved and pending; response

and resolution performance; recurring issues Approved monthly report Monthly

Where a delay is outside the service provider’s control, the provider must explain the cause, expected resolution date and any practical workaround.

Any additional costs for parts, travel, call-outs or extended services must receive Girl Effect’s prior written approval.

### **Girl Effect Responsibilities**

- Girl Effect will:
    - Maintain the required device licences and antivirus protection.
    - Provide reasonable access to staff, devices and relevant information needed to diagnose issues.
    - Approve additional costs for parts, travel or services before they are incurred.
    - Nominate the contract supervisors and provide timely feedback on service quality.

#### **Reporting**

The agency will work closely with the Senior IT & Systems Manager and the People and Ops Manager in India

#### **Expected Commitment**

- The assignment is expected to take approximately 1 year. Effective Period: November 2026 - November 2027. This is subject to renewal upon satisfactory delivery of the work.
- The consultant will be expected to present to the team if needed.

## **Applicant Requirements**

Applications are welcome from both qualified individual consultants and registered IT support agencies or firms. Applicants must be based in India and demonstrate:

- Relevant experience providing remote and on-call IT support to distributed teams or organisations of comparable size.
- Strong knowledge of laptop hardware, operating systems, productivity applications, endpoint security, connectivity and user support.
- Capacity to meet the stated support window and service levels and coordinate support in major Indian cities.
- Experience working with OEM warranty, repair, and replacement processes.
- Clear communication, accurate documentation, and appropriate confidentiality and data-security practices.
- At least two contactable references for similar assignments.

Individual applicants should submit a current CV.

Agencies or firms should submit a brief company profile and CVs or profiles of the personnel who would deliver the services.

### **Proposal Submission Requirements**

Applicants should submit a concise proposal of no more than five pages, covering the following:

- **Understanding and Approach**  
    Explain how you will provide support, manage incidents, communicate with users, and meet the required service levels.
- **Experience and Capacity**  
    Provide details of relevant assignments, geographic coverage, and the proposed individual or team responsible for delivering the services.
- **References**  
    Provide contact details for at least two clients for whom you have undertaken similar work.
- **Financial Proposal**  
    Provide fees in **INR,** with applicable taxes quoted separately. The financial proposal should clearly state:
    - Proposed monthly retainer or fixed fee.
    - Hourly or daily rates, where applicable.
    - Call-out or on-site support charges.
    - Travel or logistics charges.
    - Any other costs that may apply.
    - Items, replacement parts, and third-party costs that are excluded from the proposed fee.

### **Evaluation Process and Criteria**

Proposals will be reviewed in the following sequence:

1. Prescreening against the mandatory requirements.
2. Technical evaluation.
3. Financial and value-for-money evaluation.

Only substantially responsive proposals that meet the required technical standard will proceed to financial evaluation.

**Evaluation Criterion Weight**

Understanding of the requirement and proposed support approach 15%

Relevant IT support experience 25%

Geographic coverage, availability and ability to meet the SLA 20%

Qualifications, team capacity and references 10%

**Technical Total 70%**

Financial proposal and value for money 30%

**Total 100%**

Girl Effect may invite shortlisted applicants to an interview or clarification meeting and may conduct reference checks and due diligence before making an award.

### **Performance Measures**

Performance will be assessed against:

- Response and resolution times under the agreed service levels.
- Quality and accuracy of incident records and monthly reports.
- User satisfaction and effectiveness of communication.
- Timely coordination of repairs, warranties and approved sourcing requests.
- Compliance with Girl Effect’s data-security, confidentiality and safeguarding requirements.

### **Project Timelines**

- Terms of reference published:16th October, 2026
- Deadline for proposal submission: 30th October 2026

**On-Call IT Support Services – India**

Only submissions received through the stated application process and email address will be considered.

### **General and Commercial Terms**

- **Contracting and Payment:** The successful applicant will enter into Girl Effect’s applicable agreement. Payment will be linked to satisfactory delivery of the agreed services and receipt of a correct, approved invoice.
- **Pricing and Taxes:** Fees must be firm for the stated proposal validity period and clearly show the currency, applicable taxes and any separately chargeable costs. Girl Effect will deduct or account for taxes where required by law.
- **Additional Costs:** Replacement parts, travel, third-party services and other additional costs will only be reimbursable where agreed and approved in writing by Girl Effect before the costs are incurred.
- **Confidentiality and Data Protection:** The selected provider must protect Girl Effect information, systems, credentials and any personal, confidential or sensitive information accessed during the engagement.
- **Safeguarding and Conduct:** The selected provider must comply with Girl Effect’s safeguarding, ethical and supplier-conduct requirements and may be subject to appropriate due-diligence checks.
- **Conflicts of Interest:** Applicants must disclose any actual or potential conflict of interest that could affect the procurement process or delivery of the services.
- **Right to Award:** Girl Effect may seek clarification, negotiate, amend or cancel the procurement process, reject any or all submissions, or make no award. Girl Effect is not liable for any costs incurred in preparing or submitting a proposal.
- **Proposal Validity:** Proposals must remain valid for 90 days from the submission deadline.

jobs.title: 22867 Senior Programme Coordinator (Humanitarian Response and Recovery) (P)
jobs.body:
The International Organization for Migration (IOM) – the United Nations (UN) migration agency – in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) implements a broad, integrated programme supporting crisis‑affected populations and national institutions in a context of protracted conflict, large‑scale displacement, and limited access to essential services. The programme combines humanitarian assistance, stabilization, durable solutions, peacebuilding, migration governance, and border management interventions across multiple provinces, targeting Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs), returnees, host communities, ex‑combatants, vulnerable households, and government counterparts. Core activities include community‑based planning, rehabilitation of key infrastructure, livelihood and reintegration support, social cohesion initiatives, displacement tracking, protection services, and capacity building for national and local authorities. Through these efforts, IOM aims to strengthen resilience, restore basic services, enhance local governance, and advance sustainable solutions for displacement‑affected communities.

Under the overall supervision of the Regional Director of the Regional Office (RO) for East Horn and Southern Africa (EHSA) and direct supervision of the Chief of Mission (COM) in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), and in close coordination with the Regional Thematic Specialist (RTS) and relevant Divisions/Departments/Units at Headquarters, the Senior Programme Coordinator (Humanitarian Response and Recovery) will provide strategic leadership and oversight across the Country Office’s (CO) programme portfolio. This includes guiding programme development and implementation, leading strategic planning processes, strengthening donor and government engagement, ensuring coherence with One UN frameworks, overseeing programme support functions, and maintaining high‑level coordination with national authorities, UN agencies, partners, and stakeholders. The Senior Programme Coordinator (Humanitarian Response and Recovery) will also ensure integrated planning, quality assurance, knowledge management, and effective representation of IOM in inter‑agency fora, while supporting the COM in advancing the CO’s priorities and institutional objectives.

**Responsibilities**

1. Oversee the overall development, implementation, and monitoring of programme activities under areas of responsibility, including oversight of IOM’s cluster participation and ONE UN obligations. Identify potential and existing obstacles to programme delivery through continuous monitoring of new programme areas that reflect changes in host country and donor priorities.
2. Develop the CO’s programme overview, including all (or thematically relevant) programmes implemented by the CO, and schedule the major activities for the COM.
3. Lead the development of country strategic plans, which are in line with IOM’s global & regional strategies, the Country National Peace & Development Strategy, and the One UN Programme.
4. Lead the development of the CO’s donor and partner outreach strategies, taking into account priorities in DRC, Humanitarian Response and Recovery, and IOM’s regional and global strategic priorities and objectives; implement the strategies in close coordination with the COM and CO’s relevant units.
5. Develop and maintain Government working relationships with the ministries and international agencies involved in migration-related issues in DRC, and maintain regular liaison with key government officials and interlocutors. Serve as overall Focal Point for Humanitarian Response and Recovery.
6. In coordination with the COM and CO’s relevant units, establish liaison and maintain continuous dialogue with relevant stakeholders (i.e., national governmental authorities, donors, UN Agencies, national and international Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs), national and international institutions, Private sector) aiming at coordinating and facilitating the implementation of ongoing activities and promoting new activities and fundraising for new projects; identify synergies with IOM’s programmes and make recommendations on donor/partner engagement.
7. Lead the Programme Support Unit and supervise the Unit’s staff providing project development, public information, reporting, donor relations, government liaison and information management functions for the CO.
8. Ensure an integrated approach to CO’s programming, with required support functions such as project development, reporting, donor relations, public information and information management are provided to programme units in a timely manner.
9. Provide overall guidance to Programme Managers on project development, public information, donor relations, government liaison and information management; ensure consistency and coherence of project/ programme activities in accordance with the CO’s strategies and in coordination with the RO and relevant departments/units at HQ.
10. Provide guidance and support to the Heads of Sub-Offices on the CO’s priorities, policies and strategies.
11. Identify programme strategic priorities in relevant service areas and areas of interest in line with IOM mandate and expertise, aiming to further expand the CO’s partnership basis and the scope of activities.
12. Act as Focal Point for government liaison and oversee the CO’s correspondence and reporting to the government authorities; ensure that the CO’s interests are accurately communicated and promote IOM’s visibility.
13. Represent the CO in inter-agency fora, including but not limited to the Programme Management Team (PMT) and One UN, and One Programme.
14. Lead knowledge management and capacity building activities in the CO.
15. Prepare policy guidance notes, documentation and briefs for COM and senior management.
16. Perform such other relevant duties as may be assigned.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master’s degree in International Relations, Political Science, Business or Public Administration, International Studies or a related field from an accredited academic institution with seven years of relevant professional experience; or,
- University degree in the above fields with nine years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Extensive experience in programme formulation, implementation and evaluation;
- Demonstrated supervisory experience in staff management;
- Proven record of establishing and maintaining good working relationships with governmental and diplomatic authorities, national, regional and international institutions, as well as civil society actors;
- Previous work experience in a rapid transition or post-conflict area;
- Demonstrated experience in liaising with governmental authorities, international agencies (i.e., UN), and civil society organizations;
- Experience in project development, implementation, and reporting, including financial and budgetary aspects; and,
- Familiarity with inter-agency programme regulations of the UN and other donors.

**Skills**

- In-depth knowledge of the broad range of migration-related subject areas dealt with by the Organization;
- Sound judgment, ability to analyze information and make decisions rapidly to resolve operational problems;
- Efficiency, flexibility, high level of professionalism and ability to adhere to strict deadlines;
- Strong leadership, management, and coordination ability;
- Sound communication and interpersonal skills;
- Ability to work effectively and harmoniously with colleagues from varied cultures and backgrounds;
- Familiarity with IOM’s Migrant Management Operational Systems Application (MiMOSA) and Project Information and Management Application (PRIMA) systems;
- Knowledge of the IOM project management cycle; and,
- Knowledge of IOM’s administrative and financial management.

**Languages**

For this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.
