jobs.title: Haiti - Coordinateur.trice Terrain - Artibonite
jobs.body:
## QUE FAISONS-NOUS...

**Date de début souhaité:** ASAP  
**Durée de la mission:** 6 mois  
**Localisation**: Artibonite

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL** (SI) est une association d’aide humanitaire internationale qui, depuis plus de 40 ans, porte secours aux populations victimes de conflits armés et de catastrophes naturelles en répondant aux besoins vitaux, boire, manger, s’abriter. Particulièrement engagée dans le combat contre les maladies liées à l’eau insalubre, première cause de mortalité au monde, SI met en œuvre par ses interventions une expertise dans le domaine de l’accès à l’eau potable, l’assainissement et la promotion de l’hygiène mais également dans celui, essentiel, de la sécurité alimentaire et moyen d’existence. Présentes dans 26 pays, les équipes de SI - 3 200 personnes au total composées d’expatriés, de salariés nationaux, de permanents au siège, de quelques bénévoles…- interviennent avec professionnalisme et engagement dans le respect des cultures.

## LA MISSION

La mission Haiti a actuellement une base à Port au Prince et le bureau de la coordination. Les projets concernent la WASH et la SAME/NUT en consortium avec des partenaires nationaux et internationaux. Elle est financée par OCHA, CDCS, SDC, ECHO, UNICEF, IFSAN entre autre. Depuis deux ans, la mission a connu une bonne croissance en terme d'opérations et de budget, répondant aux urgences dans la Zone Métropolitaine de Port au Prince mais également développe des actions de plus long termes. C'est dans cette dynamique que la mission Haiti a décidé d'ouvrir une nouvelle base en Artibonite, basée à Saint Marc afin de répondre aux besoins en EHA des populations dans ce département. La base est en début d'ouverture à l'heure actuelle, la mission principale du.de la CT aura pour but de régulariser la base après son ouverture et de la terminer.

17 expatriés et 80 staffs nationaux dans l'unique base et coordination de Port au Prince. Un premier set-up de 2/3 expats et une petite vingtaine de staffs nationaux est à entrevoir pour la base d'Artibonite.

## DESCRIPTIF DE POSTE

**OBJECTIF GENERAL**

Le/la Coordinateur.trice Terrain a un rôle de Directeur Pays (DP) par délégation sur l'Artibonite pour SI.  
Il/elle propose en fonction du contexte géopolitique et humanitaire la stratégie sur l'Artibonite et s'assure de sa mise en œuvre une fois validée.  
Il/elle contrôle et garantit que les projets se déroulent en adéquation avec la charte de Solidarités International et dans   
le respect des procédures internes et contractuelles.  
Il/elle mobilise les moyens matériels et financiers nécessaires à la bonne conduite des programmes et en supervise la gestion.  
Il/elle coordonne les équipes en place et est le garant de leur sécurité sur sa zone d’affectation.  
Il/elle est l’interlocuteur.trice direct.e et privilégié.e du/de la DP

**ENJEUX ET DEFIS SPECIFIQUES**

Ce poste est une création suite à l'ouverture de la base Artibonite. Nous attendons un.e CT expérimenté sur ce type de niveau sécuritaire mais aussi possédant une grande expérience dans la structuration d'une nouvelle base après la phase d'ouverture.  
Les enjeux sécuritaires - niveau 4 chez SI - sont nombreux notamment dans le cadre d'une base nouvelle.

**PRIORITES SUR LES 2-3 PREMIERS MOIS**

Gestion et de la mise en place des projets

Gestion opérationnelle de la sécurité sur la zone et continuité du travail d'accès engagé

Support au développement de nouvelles propositions de projets sur la zone

Travailler en interne sur la structuration de la base, finaliser les recrutements, finaliser l'installation de la base vie et bureaux, formation au travail chez SI, mise en place des procédures.

Accompagner la stratégie sur l'Artibonite et continuer son développement

Contribuer à renforcer le lien avec nos partenaires locaux et internationaux et les clusters de la zone

**CONTRAINTES SECURITAIRES**

Haiti est catégorisé en Niveau 4, La sécurité est très volatile/dégradée en Artibonite dû à la présence des groupes armés et d'affrontements quotidiens, mais n’empêche pas la conduite des activités. Les règles de sécurité de la mission sont strictes (couvre-feu au coucher du soleil).

## VOTRE PROFIL

**DIPLÔME ET EXPERIENCE**

Diploma : Niveau Master

Experience dans le secteur humanitaire : 5 ans et plus

Experience sur un poste similaire : 3/4 ans

**COMPETENCES**

COMPETENCES TECHNIQUES

1. Capacité à suivre et analyser le contexte humanitaire, politique, culturel, social, économique
2. Compétences pour garantir la coordination, le développement, le suivi et l’évaluation des programmes mis en œuvre sur sa zone d’intervention
3. Proposer le dimensionnement humain, financier et logistique pour sa zone d’intervention ainsi que son organisation
4. Gestion des RH, recrutement, induction, création de dynamiques d'équipes, mise en place de la relation base éloignée - coo pour Haiti (l'autre base est à Port au Prince, directement en lien avec la coo)
5. Etre responsable de la sécurité des équipes et des biens sur sa zone d’affectation, sur délégation de la DP

COMPETENCES TRANSVERSALES

1. Analyse, décision et gestion de crise : capacité à évaluer les risques, anticiper, décider et agir sous pression.
2. Leadership et communication : encadrer, former, sensibiliser et transmettre des consignes claires aux équipes et partenaires.
3. Diplomatie et adaptabilité : négocier avec divers acteurs, entretenir des relations de confiance et s’ajuster à un environnement instable.

**LANGUES**

1. Français
2. Anglais apprécié

## SI VOUS OFFRIRA LES CONDITIONS SUIVANTES...

**Un poste salarié :** Selon l'expérience, à partir de EUR 3080 bruts par mois (2800 salaire de base + 10% d'indemnité de congé annuel versée mensuellement) et un Per Diem mensuel de USD 750.

SI couvre également les frais de logement et les frais de déplacement entre le pays d'origine de l'expatrié et le lieu d'affectation.

**Breaks :** Pendant la mission, un système d'alternance entre travail et congés est mis en place à raison de 7 jours ouvrables tous les trois mois (avec USD 850 alloués par Solidarités International). A ces périodes de pause, s'ajoute un jour de repos supplémentaire par mois travaillé.

**Couverture sociale et médicale :** Les expatriés bénéficient d'une assurance qui rembourse tous les frais de santé (y compris les frais médicaux et chirurgicaux, les soins dentaires et ophtalmologiques, le rapatriement) et d'un système de prévoyance incluant les risques de guerre. Les frais de vaccination et de traitement antipaludéen indispensables sont remboursés.

**CONDITIONS DE VIE :**

A l'heure de l'ouverture de ce poste, la mission n'a pas commencé l'ouverture, aucun lieu de vie n'est pour l'instant défini. D'ici l'arrivée du.de la CT, la mission aura identifié un lieu de vie et de bureau.  
A Saint Marc, la sécurité reste volatile avec des restrictions sécuritaires importantes. Vie sociale limitée à quelques restaurants et à la présence de MSF et NRC.

jobs.title: Advocacy Specialist: Treaty Bodies
jobs.body:
ILGA World is seeking an Advocacy Specialist on Treaty Bodies, who will work as part of our advocacy programme and coordinate the organisation’s day-to-day engagement with [the United Nations human rights treaty body system](https://www.ohchr.org/en/treaty-bodies).

**Deadline for applications:** Tuesday, 10 November 2026 – 23:59 (Central European Time, CET)  
**Start of the position:** January/February 2027, subject to successful work authorisation and any applicable notice period

## Who can apply?

Anyone

- with dedication to – and experience in regard to – the human rights of persons with diverse sexual orientations, [**gender**](https://ilga.org/glossary/gender/) identities, gender expressions and [**sex characteristics**](https://ilga.org/glossary/sex-characteristics/)
- who meets the requirements set out below

is welcome to apply.

## Overview

The Advocacy Specialist: Treaty Bodies is part of ILGA World’s advocacy prgramme and coordinates the organisation’s day-to-day engagement with the [**United Nations**](https://ilga.org/glossary/united-nations/) human rights treaty body system.

The role advances the rights of people and communities of diverse SOGIESC by connecting grassroots, national and regional advocacy with international human rights mechanisms. It provides technical assistance to ILGA World members, regions and human rights defenders; supports strategic engagement with treaty bodies; and helps ensure that movement priorities, evidence and lived realities inform [**country reviews**](https://ilga.org/glossary/country-reviews/), normative developments, jurisprudence and follow-up at national level.

Working under the strategic direction of the Advocacy Senior Manager and closely with colleagues across the advocacy programme, ILGA regions, member organisations and partner organisations, the Specialist monitors treaty body processes and opportunities, coordinates submissions and briefings, supports strategic litigation and national follow-up, analyses recommendations and jurisprudence, develops capacity-strengthening resources, and maintains relationships with treaty body members and OHCHR staff. The role also works across ILGA World programmes to connect advocacy with knowledge production and movement strengthening.

## Responsibilities

The Advocacy Specialist: Treaty Bodies reports to the Advocacy Senior Manager and is responsible for the day-to-day coordination and delivery of ILGA World’s Treaty Bodies portfolio within the Advocacy Programme.

### Specific to this position, this includes:

- Implement ILGA World’s Treaty Bodies advocacy workplan and coordinate the organisation’s day-to-day engagement with the UN human rights Treaty Body system, serving as the organisational focal point for Treaty Bodies-related advocacy.
- Monitor Treaty Body sessions, reporting cycles, country reviews, lists of Issues Prior to Reporting (LOIPRs) under the Simplified Reporting Procedure, follow-up procedures, general comments, individual communications and other developments, identifying timely and strategic opportunities for SOGIESC advocacy.
- Develop and implement advocacy strategies to advance the human rights of people and communities of diverse SOGIESC through country reviews, normative development, individual communications and other relevant Treaty Body procedures.
- Provide technical assistance to ILGA World members, regions, LGBTI organisations and human rights defenders engaging with Treaty Bodies, including advocacy planning, reporting, preparation of written and oral submissions, briefings and follow up strategies.
- Coordinate and contribute to ILGA World and joint submissions, shadow report inputs, briefing materials, statements, position papers and other advocacy products in consultation with affected communities, members, regions, partners, and external legal experts
- Facilitate the meaningful participation of human rights defenders in Treaty Body processes, including organising briefings and engagement with Treaty Body members and OHCHR staff.
- Coordinate ILGA World’s strategic litigation engagement before Treaty Bodies, including identifying appropriate opportunities, supporting individual communications and third-party interventions, and contributing to follow-up on decisions in collaboration with members, partners and relevant legal experts.
- Monitor, systematise and analyse SOGIESC-related [**concluding observations**](https://ilga.org/glossary/concluding-observations/), recommendations, general comments, jurisprudence, decisions and other Treaty Body outputs, and contribute to compilations, briefings and analytical resources.
- Support ILGA World members and human rights defenders to use Treaty Body recommendations, decisions and jurisprudence in national advocacy, including follow up and implementation, and document relevant results, challenges and good practices.
- Develop and deliver training, webinars, guidance and other capacity strengthening resources to strengthen civil society engagement with the Treaty Body system.
- Build and maintain effective working relationships with Treaty Body members, OHCHR staff, civil society organisations, legal experts, academics and other relevant stakeholders, and represent ILGA World in relevant meetings, consultations and external spaces.
- Monitor and contribute to discussions concerning Treaty Body strengthening, accessibility, effectiveness and other institutional developments affecting the system.
- Work across ILGA World programmes and advocacy portfolios to strengthen coherence between Treaty Bodies, the Human Rights Council, Universal Periodic Review, Special Procedures and thematic advocacy, and ensure that relevant ILGA World research and monitoring data inform Treaty Body engagement.
- Contribute to planning, budgeting, monitoring, evaluation and learning, donor reporting and funding proposals relating to the Treaty Bodies portfolio, and work with the Communications team to make relevant opportunities, developments and outcomes accessible to members, partners and wider audiences.

### **General**

- Actively contribute to promoting and achieving the organisation’s objectives.
- Engage and collaborate with colleagues across the Advocacy Programme and other ILGA World teams to strengthen a shared organisational culture and ensure coordinated, movement-informed work.
- Ensure that all activities are carried out with full regard to ILGA World policies.
- Work as a part of the ILGA World staff team.
- Perform other duties as required.

### **Relationships with colleagues**

ILGA values creative and inclusive approaches to work and management that have been achieved through cross-service area working and the participation of staff at all levels in the organisation. Staff have line management arrangements and specific key relationships, which are detailed in their job descriptions, but they will also need to work collaboratively with their colleagues in order to achieve their agreed targets and outcomes to the required standards.

## Performance of duties, remuneration, and benefits

- This position requires relocation to Geneva, Switzerland.
- This position is subject to the successful granting of the necessary Swiss work authorisation.
    - Where required, ILGA World will submit and support the work permit application for the selected candidate. However, the relevant Swiss authorities make decisions on work authorisation, and ILGA World cannot guarantee that an application will be successful. Any offer of employment and appointment to the position is therefore conditional upon the required work permit being granted. If the necessary authorisation cannot be secured, ILGA World will not be able to confirm or proceed with the appointment.
- The position is advertised at 100% of a full-time position.
- ILGA World remunerates under a three-tiered salary matrix structure. The annual salary offered for the 100% position is 81,060 CHF.
- In addition, ILGA World offers 32 days, inclusive of legal holidays (“bank holidays”) and annual leave and contributions to health care costs.
- ILGA World operates under a flexible working system that – among others – includes flexible working hours.
- The weekly working time is 40 hours on a 100% position.

## Requirements

### **Education and qualifications**

- A master’s university degree or equivalent in [**international human rights law**](https://ilga.org/glossary/international-human-rights-law/), law, political science, international relations or a related field, combined with 6 years of relevant work experience

or

- A first-level university degree in combination with 8 years of relevant and qualifying experience

or

- 10 years of relevant and qualifying experience instead of a master’s or first-level degree

### **Experience**

- A minimum of 4 years of relevant experience in human rights advocacy, policy or legal work, preferably within an international, regional or national civil society organisation, multilateral institution or similar setting.
- At least 2 years of direct engagement with United Nations human rights mechanisms, including substantive experience working with one or more UN Treaty Bodies.
- Experience developing and implementing advocacy strategies relating to Treaty Body country reviews, normative development or other treaty body procedures.
- Experience drafting shadow reports, written submissions, briefing materials, statements, position papers or other advocacy documentation for international human rights mechanisms.
- Experience providing technical assistance, guidance or capacity strengthening to civil society organisations and human rights defenders engaging with international human rights mechanisms.
- Experience analysing international human rights standards, concluding observations, recommendations and/or jurisprudence and translating complex legal developments into accessible advocacy guidance.
- Experience with or strong familiarity with strategic litigation, individual communications or other forms of legal advocacy before international or regional human rights mechanisms.
- Demonstrated experience working collaboratively with grassroots organisations, LGBTI human rights defenders and diverse stakeholders across different national, cultural and political contexts.
- Experience in project coordination, including planning, monitoring, evaluation, learning and narrative reporting, including in donor-funded work.
- Experience building and maintaining working relationships with UN officials and experts, civil society organisations, legal practitioners, academic partners and other relevant stakeholders.

### **Technical requirements**

- Advanced skills in legal and policy analysis, with strong knowledge of international human rights law and its application to [**sexual orientation**](https://ilga.org/glossary/sexual-orientation/), gender identity, gender expression and sex characteristics.
- Demonstrated in-depth knowledge of the UN human rights Treaty Body system, including country review processes, normative outputs, follow-up procedures and individual communications.
- Ability to monitor, systematise and analyse Treaty Body recommendations, general comments, jurisprudence and other outputs and identify strategic advocacy opportunities.
- Strong research and drafting skills, including the ability to present complex legal and policy developments clearly and accessibly to different audiences.
- Demonstrated ability to build and sustain partnerships with member organisations, human rights defenders, UN officials, civil society organisations and other stakeholders.
- Strong understanding of SOGIESC human rights issues and commitment to feminist, decolonial, intersectional and anti-oppressive approaches to advocacy.

### **Other requirements**

- Strong communication, facilitation and diplomatic skills, with the ability to communicate clearly and effectively with diverse audiences
- Excellent organisational skills, sound judgement and the ability to prioritise work, meet deadlines and adapt to changing advocacy opportunities
- Proven existing professional relationships with the [**Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights**](https://ilga.org/glossary/office-of-the-high-commissioner-for-human-rights/) (OHCHR) Secretariat staff and/or independent Treaty Body experts.
- Ability to work proficiently in English (mandatory). Knowledge of Spanish, French or another UN official language is an asset
- Adherence to and alignment with the ILGA World Code of Conduct, including a strong capacity for confidentiality, tact, discretion and respectful collaboration

jobs.title: Documents Management Assistant
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
jobs.body:
**Purpose of the Post**

The Documents Management Assistant supports the Documents Control function and IMODOCS (IMO's electronic document repository and distribution system) with documents in the six languages of the Organization.

The incumbent will manage the frontline Document Counter service during meetings, taking timely, independent decisions on document management under strict timeframes, including out-of-hours and night shifts, and is responsible for the timely internal and external distribution of documents to interpreters, Member States, NGOs and the Secretariat.

The post holder provides office support for all systems during virtual and hybrid meetings, coordinates with the relevant technical Divisions and Sections to ensure efficient distribution of documents, and supports interpreters through the timely provision of documentation. The role also assists the Senior Printer with the printing and distribution of documentation sets for interpreters, delegates and the Secretariat.

**Required Competencies**

1\. High degree of initiative and sound judgement, with a solutions-oriented approach and consistent emphasis on deadline delivery under high-pressure conditions.

2\. Technological awareness: proactive use of document management systems and tools, with the ability to identify and propose improvements to work processes.

3\. Demonstrated ability to coordinate independently with internal and external stakeholders — technical Divisions, interpreters, language sections, delegates and the Secretariat — building and maintaining effective working relationships at all levels.

4\. Tact, discretion and sensitivity in providing frontline client service within a multicultural, international environment, including autonomous decision-making under strict timeframes.

5\. Excellent verbal and written communication skills, and flexibility with regard to work hours, including willingness to work night and early shifts to ensure meeting delivery.

**Professional Experience**

At least four years' experience in document management, meetings/events management or a related field, within an international, multilingual environment is required. Experience in publishing and/or logistics management is desirable. Prior experience within the United Nations system, or another international organization, in a similar function is an advantage.

**Education**

Secondary education or equivalent to university entrance standard.

**Language Skills**

Excellent command of English, both written and oral, is required. Working knowledge of other official languages of the Organization would be an advantage.

**Other Skills**

Proficiency in MS Office applications and document management software is required. The ability to use technology confidently and effectively, and to adapt quickly to new systems and digital tools, is required. Knowledge of IMODOCS and related IMO systems, printing machinery and software is a strong asset. Familiarity with support services to translation and interpretation in the context of conference management is an advantage.

**Main Duties & Responsibilities**

***Documents control***

1 Monitor internal document management systems, including gDoc and IMODOCS, to ensure timely and accurate processing and distribution of all IMO meeting documents and other jobs (e.g. certified copies).

2 Liaise directly with submitting officers regarding any queries and transmit corrections, as appropriate, to the translation sections involved.

3 Publish final documents on IMODOCS in all working/official languages, without direct input from the line manager.

4 Coordinate with the relevant technical Divisions and translation sections during meetings to ensure timely processing of in-session documents.

***Documents Counter service***

5 Provide frontline assistance to IMO delegates at the Document Counter, independently answering a wide range of individual queries and requests, drawing on sound knowledge and recollection of decisions and practice from past meetings.

6 Distribute hard copies to Member States and NGOs prior to and during meetings according to priorities, and ensure timely distribution of in-session documents, both electronic and in hard copy.

7 Work out-of-hours and night shifts independently at the Document Counter, taking timely decisions on document management under strict timeframes.

***Printing and meeting preparation***

8 Assist the Senior Printer in the delivery of hard copies, including batch printing of sets (print-on-demand) to support interpreters and the Secretariat.

9 Coordinate with the relevant IMO Divisions and Sections involved in IMO meetings to ensure efficient distribution of documents (working papers, briefs, status reports).

10 Calculate printing figures for each meeting based on the meeting registration system (OMRS) to ensure PaperSmart distribution of documents.

1 Provide documentation (e.g. J papers) to delegations ahead of the start of each meeting in the Plenary Hall, and undertake internal posting of meeting documents to the Secretariat in a timely manner, including preparation of sets for the podium.

***Support to interpreters***

12 Provide interpreters with select background publications during meetings, choosing resources based on an understanding of the key issues under discussion.

13 Ensure timely transmission of statements received from delegations, in electronic and hard copy, to interpreters' booths and the Secretariat within critical deadlines.

14 Distribute meeting documents to interpreters prior to and during each meeting, and liaise with interpreters on documentation issues, including updating publications and reports in the interpreters' booths.

***Other***

15 Provide office support for all systems during virtual and hybrid meetings.

16 Work night shifts independently, as required, to ensure meeting delivery.

17 Undertake other duties connected to the work of the Documentation and Language Technologies Section as may be assigned.

**Contract Information**

\*Local status requires applicants to have unhindered permission to live and work in the UK.

jobs.title: Procurement expert - HLGSC - Montreuil
jobs.body:
**Beginning of contract :** ASAP

**Type of contract** : Fix-term contract until 31/08/2027

**Localisation** : Montreuil (93) / France (possible home-working from metropolitan France)

The European Cooperative Society of Collective Interest "Humanitarian Logistics Cooperative", also known as "hulo", is the first humanitarian cooperative founded in June 2021. Led by humanitarian organizations and integrating new members regularly, hulo aims to improve the impact of humanitarian aid by strengthening collaboration and the implementation of joint projects in its countries of intervention. At hulo we are convinced that the sharing and pooling of resources and expertise between organizations contributes to increasing the performance of humanitarian logistics and the supply chain

Our action is based on a collaborative and participatory approach, collective intelligence and the animation of a community of practice. All our activities are structured around a common objective, involving several autonomous and interdependent stakeholders, who cooperate horizontally. Steering is distributed, based on consultation, co-responsibility and voluntary commitment.

In our 7 countries of intervention spread over 3 regions, we set up shared initiatives in the fields of purchasing, human resources and the environment. In support of humanitarian organizations, we coordinate shared international humanitarian transport initiatives for the most serious humanitarian crises. Finally, we are constantly developing digital solutions for the humanitarian community.

To find out more, you can consult the 2026 annual report by clicking on the link [https://hulo.coop/january-2026-annual-impact-report/](https://hulo.coop/january-2026-annual-impact-report/)

**JOB DESCRIPTION**

The Procurement Expert contributes NGO-side procurement expertise to the Global Humanitarian Procurement Collaboration and Performance Initiative, the 12-month HLGSC action co-led by WFP, hulo and NRC.

Working closely alongside the Project Manager, the WFP-hosted Procurement Expert (UN) and the wider Procurement Thematic Working Group (TWG), the position provides operational NGO experience to the design, testing and refinement of procurement cooperation guidance and procurement-integration tools, and supports the organisations participating in structured testing, pilots and validation.

A core dimension of the role is co-construction with the UN-side Procurement Expert: the two work jointly to identify which UN and NGO procurement practices are common ground and can be combined, and which need to remain distinct and why, and to translate this into tangible, evidence-based recommendations for the evolution of donor policies and regulations submitted to the HLGSC Donor Group.

He/she will have the main responsibilities of:

- Contribute to targeted procurement cooperation and collaboration guidance
- Strengthen procurement integration into organisational and project-level decision-making
- Support technical validation, consultation and cross-workstream coordination
- Contribute to monitoring, reporting and knowledge management

**MAIN MISSIONS**

**\#1 : Contribute to targeted procurement cooperation and collaboration guidance**

- Co-construct, jointly with the UN-side Procurement Expert, a shared methodological framework for procurement cooperation: identify which UN and NGO ways of working are common and can be combined, and which need to remain distinct, and why.
- Prepare, jointly with the UN-side Procurement Expert, the evolutions to be submitted to the HLGSC Donor Group, factoring in changes in donor policies and regulations, and build tangible, evidence-based arguments and expected gains to support these recommendations.
- Coordinate closely with the Data Specialist and the Academic Expert to ground this methodological and donor-facing work in the evidence base.
- Support the consolidation of tested NGO approaches to procurement cooperation, including piggybacking, use of existing framework agreements, mutual recognition and shared market intelligence.
- Contribute NGO operational experience to the development of procurement cooperation principles, guidance and decision-support tools
- Contribute to refining the guidance package and defining the uptake pathway based on testing and review findings.

**\#2 : Strengthen procurement integration into organisational and project-level decision-making**

- Support the consolidation of existing NGO practice on integrating procurement earlier into proposal development, demand planning, budgeting, market assessment and implementation planning.
- Contribute to the development of the practical procurement-integration tool package
- Support five pilot organisations in testing selected tools, and facilitate structured peer exchange on implementation experience.
- Contribute to documenting pilot learning and refining the final tool package.

**\#3: Support technical validation, consultation and cross-workstream coordination**

- Contribute to Procurement TWG technical consultations, comments matrices and decision records
- Support coordination with relevant cross-TWG touchpoints and with the HLGSC Donor Group on issues relevant to procurement cooperation and integration.
- Liaise with participating organisations and their focal points to support engagement, testing readiness and documentation of implementation learning.

**\#4: Contribute to monitoring, reporting and knowledge management**

- Provide inputs to the action's monitoring records, pilot documentation, risk register and implementation roadmap
- Contribute to knowledge products, learning notes and materials for wider dissemination

**YOUR PROFILE**

**Experiences / Educational background**

- BAC+5 in Supply chain management, procurement, international development, business administration or a related field.
- Minimum of 5 years on positions with responsibilities in procurement in NGO sector
- Experience in the humanitarian sector

**Technical and transversal skills**

- Expertise on procurement, in humanitarian context :
    - Proven experience with humanitarian procurement cooperation mechanisms (e.g. framework agreements, piggybacking, shared market intelligence)
    - Knowledge of donors' rules on procurement
    - Proven experience in analyzing procurement data and developing strategic recommendations.
- Collaboration and communication skills :
    - Experience working in multi-stakeholder or cross-organisational settings (e.g. UN-NGO coordination, working groups, consortia)
    - Excellent stakeholder management and facilitation skills, including the ability to co-construct outputs with counterparts from different organisational cultures (UN/NGO)
    - Excellent communication skills, comfortable adapting communication style and tone to audience and diverse contexts
    - Attentive and active listening skills, able to make others be heard and build consensus
    - Problem-solving oriented
- Strong analytical and drafting skills, with the ability to translate operational practice into guidance, tools and donor-facing arguments
- Experience in writing reports and other donor deliverables
- Familiarity with ECHO or other major institutional donor policies and reporting requirements is an asset
- Organised, autonomous, and comfortable operating within a compressed delivery timeline
- Strong interpersonal skills and experience in multi-language and multi-cultural environments
- Fluent command of English and French (very good level read, written and spoken).

**HULO WILL OFFER YOU THE FOLLOWING CONDITIONS**

A full time position

- Based in Montreuil with the possibility of working remotely in metropolitain France.
- Employment contract under French law for a fixed term.
- Executive status on an hourly basis (based on 1607 hours worked / year).
- Salary conditions:
    - Gross annual salary: €43,075 over 13 months
    - RTT: 22 days / year
    - AXA mutual insurance and provident insurance (100% covered by hulo)
- Meal vouchers: face value of €8, 60% covered by hulo
- Specific conditions and skills: prolonged sitting, oral expression, screen work, telephone contacts.

jobs.title: Programme Coordinator - UKRAINE (M/F/X)
jobs.body:
**Working environment:**

The humanitarian situation in Ukraine remains critical amid ongoing international conflict. Since the escalation of the armed conflict on 24 February 2022, the destruction of vital civilian infrastructure continues to rise, leading to the destruction of homes across the country and cutting off access to critical services for millions of people. In 2025 in Ukraine, the UN estimates approximately 12.7 million people are in need of humanitarian assistance. Ukrainian refugee numbers abroad stand at about 6,9 million, while 3,7 million people are internally displaced (IDPs) within Ukraine.

The severe damage to critical infrastructure such as hospitals, schools, and water treatment plants has compromised access to clean water, sanitation, and essential healthcare services. Constant and long-lasting disruptions to the power grid have plunged entire regions into darkness, hindering communication and hampering daily life.

With the humanitarian situation in Ukraine being a challenge and may deteriorate further, the International Red Cross & Red Crescent Movement continues mobilising its emergency response mechanisms. Together, ICRC, IFRC, Ukrainian Red Cross Society (URCS) and Partner National Societies (PNSs) are undertaking a coordinated response in contributing to URCS interventions as per One Plan 2023-27 and URCS Strategic Plan 2026-2030.

Reporting to the Head of Delegation, the Programme Coordinator will contribute to the development and implementation of the operational strategy of the Delegation, ensure the effective leadership of the country programme - including design, development, and implementation of the programmatic strategy, and contribute to the representation of the Delegation to partners, humanitarian coordination bodies and other relevant stakeholders.

**Missions:**

- **Strategy Development & Grants Management:** Leads on all aspects of programmatic design and actively develops the strategic & operational positioning as well as the development plan of the FRC UA Delegation, in support of the Head of Delegation. Development and writing of new quality Concept Notes and Project Proposals, in coordination with URCS and in line with the Delegation's annual and multi-annual strategic programming, as validated by FRC and URCS. Leads the monitoring, follow-up and accountability of/on active funding agreements. Follows attentively the “Funding Opportunity Watch” that is shared by FRC HQ; in the context of the transition from non-restricted earmarked funding to back donors-funded resources for the FRC “Ukraine Response”.
- **Projects & Team Leadership and Coordination for “Quality Implementation” Follow-up & Monitoring:** Ensures leadership, effective and dynamic management and good coordination of all projects and programmes, the multi-lateral teams involved (FRC and URCS) and of the interactions with FRC HQ (Desk Manager), to ensure “project implementation & quality” monitoring (working closely with all relevant technical experts and counterparts as well as in constant coordination with URCS); including the adequate support to the URCS Programme & Finance teams in the planning, implementation, monitoring, evaluation and reporting of projects; in line with FRC's international strategy, procedures and MEAL obligations in the country of intervention.
- **“National Society Development” Focus:** in the spirit of contributing to the partner’s sustainable development, participates actively in identifying the needs and priorities of URCS that are matching FRC’s international expertise and potential added-value; in order to develop FRC’s knowledge & understanding of URCS strategy and the NSD reference framework of IFRC and FRC.
- **PMER/MEAL:** Ensures that all of URCS’s monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning processes and tools are in line with FRC requirements and properly activated and implemented; in order to ensure quality reporting and feedback mechanisms to beneficiaries, partners and potential donors.
- **Partnership Management & FRC Representation:** Proactively contributes to good partnership relations and the sustainable capacity building of URCS, including to any further support activities that the position may require; as well as contributes to the representation of FRC operation and interests, in support of the Head of Delegation.

**Managing lines:**

- **Incumbent reporting line**: Reporting to Head of Delegation
- **Incumbent operational links:** HQ Desk Manager
- Incumbent will manage:1 International staff (team under construction):
    - Incumbent will manage and technically support FRC Delegation’s technical programme/project delegates and managers.
    - Number and positions of technical managers is defined by the Delegation’s approved structure and can/will evolve over time.

**Qualifications and experience**

**Experiences :**

- At least 3 years’ experience in the same type of position in Coordination
- Previous experience in programme coordination positions
- Previous experience in supervising staff and supporting their professional and technical development.
- Experience and/or knowledge in communicating with various partners and donors
- Experience in developing new projects (concept note, proposal, budget, logframe, etc)
- Experience in donor reporting and contract management
- Experience working with local partners and partner-implemented projects / programmes
- Experience working with the Red Cross Red Crescent Movement
- Experience in donor reporting and financial contract management (previous experience with French donors is a strong asset: AFD, Expertise France, CDCS.
- Experience in the region and specifically in conflictual context is a strong asset
- Background in health or in health projects (including emergency medical services, nurse sciences, pre-hospital care, first aid, etc.) is a strong asset

**Education :**

- Studies in humanitarian or development project coordination or technical profile
- Mastery of the project cycle and project management tools
- Mastery of the humanitarian coordination system

**Skills**

**Mandatory job requirements**

- Organisational capacity
- Coordination capacity
- Strong writing and synthesis skills (for both proposals and reporting contributions)
- Effective capacity in grant management
- Effective capacity in MEAL procedures and processes
- Strong communication and diplomatic skills in multicultural work environments
- Teamwork skills (active listening, proactivity and consensus building)
- Experience in team management
- Initiative and ability to work efficiently and effectively without close supervision

**Valued skills**

- Proficiency in Office (Word, Excel, Powerpoint), networking (Google-Suite/Google Workspace)
- Expertise in identifying and implementing jointly capacity-improvement plans
- Experience facilitating trainings and accompanying staff to strengthen their expertise
- In-depth knowledge of the Red Cross Red Crescent Movement’s National Society Development approaches, especially through a Programme Coordination and Development lens

**Skills related to the specific environment of the mission:**

- Flexibility and quick adaptability
- Restraint, patience and diplomacy in institutional relations
- Ability to work within a coordination team and in functional link with the project and field teams
- Ability to work with a multicultural team
- Resilience to stress and high workload
- **International driving licence mandatory**

**Languages**

- English mandatory (oral and written);
- French or other language of the region would be an asset

**Conditions of employment:**

- Type of status: expatriate
- Type of contract: Fixed-term contract under French law
- Salary: According to the classification of the position on the CRf grid and the experience of the candidate
- Per diem: daily per diem which varies according to the country
- Leave: 10 to 15 days minimum every 6 months - Airfare paid at 100% by CRF for home travel
- Health coverage: CFE + Mutuelle MSH (covered 100%) - covered at 75% by the CRF
- MedEvac/repatriation insurance: YES
- Other insurances: Provident insurance (death and disability)

**SUMMARY**

- Location: Kyiv (with planned movements in Lviv, Kharkiv and possible other locations) - UKRAINE
- Duration: 12 months renewable
- Starting date: December 2026
- Mandatory driving licence

The French Red Cross reserves the right to close a recruitment before the closing date of the advertisement and the application deadline. Thank you for your understanding.

If we do not contact you within 3 weeks, please consider that we will not consider your application.

Female candidates are encouraged to apply.

**Online training**

To learn more about the Red Cross Movement, we invite you to follow two online training courses, free of charge and accessible to all. W.O.R.C. (World of Red Cross and Red Crescent): this course covers topics such as the origin and history of the Movement, its fundamental principles, the emblem, the International Federation, the ICRC and the national societies. Stay Safe aims to develop a common culture of security management within the Movement. You can find these courses on the International Federation's Learning Platform: [https://ifrc.csod.com/client/ifrc/default.aspx](https://ifrc.csod.com/client/ifrc/default.aspx)

Finance Manager Lebanon
jobs.body:
**What we are looking for**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) has been supporting people affected by displacement in Lebanon for 20 years. As we embark on an important period of strategic and operational change, we are seeking an **experienced** **Finance Manager** to provide **strategic financial leadership**, **strengthen financial systems**, and ensure the effective and accountable use of resources to deliver humanitarian assistance.

We are looking for **a strategic, analytical, and solutions-oriented finance leader** who can navigate change, translate financial data into actionable insights, and balance strong financial controls with the operational flexibility required in a dynamic humanitarian context.

This is an exciting opportunity to shape NRC Lebanon’s financial direction, support organisational transformation, and strengthen collaboration with local partners and actors.

***Applicants must be legally eligible to work in Lebanon, We are unable to provide work permits or visa sponsorships for this position.***

**What you will do**

The Finance Manager is responsible for effective financial management, budgeting, reporting, compliance and internal controls across NRC Lebanon.

This role provides strategic financial leadership by delivering accurate, reliable, and timely financial information, enabling senior management to make informed decisions and ensure the efficient use of organisational resources.

The position holder will ensure that NRC Lebanon is well positioned to respond to current and future needs and shall demonstrate strong engagement and leadership in all major Finance actions, while ensuring capacity building for Finance team members and budget holders across the entire country.

Key responsibilities:

- **Provide strategic financial leadership** across NRC Lebanon, ensuring robust financial systems, policies, internal controls, and compliance with NRC, donor, and local regulatory requirements.
- **Lead budgeting, financial reporting, and analysis**, delivering timely, accurate insights to inform senior management decisions and support effective resource allocation.
- **Oversee accounting, cash flow, and liquidity management**, ensuring operational continuity, accurate financial records, and effective audit preparation and follow-up.
- **Manage financial risks and compliance**, strengthening accountability, implementing anti-corruption measures, and addressing audit findings and financial control gaps.
- **Advise and support budget holders and programme teams** throughout the project cycle, from proposal development and budgeting to expenditure monitoring and reporting.
- **Strengthen financial capacity and team performance** through effective leadership, staff development, and technical support to Finance colleagues and budget holders nationwide.
- **Advance NRC’s localisation agenda** by strengthening financial systems, tools, and capacity to support local partners and actors in delivering compliant, effective, and sustainable humanitarian responses.

**What you will bring**

- A bachelor’s degree in finance, Accounting, or a relevant field.
- **At least four years of finance experience**, including **three years in a managerial or equivalent role** **within a humanitarian or recovery context.**
- **Experience working with local partners** and **institutional humanitarian donors.**
- **Strong financial analysis**, **budgeting, reporting**, and risk management skills, with proficiency in MS Excel and accounting systems.
- Fluency in written and spoken English.
- Experience **developing financial systems during organisational change** is highly desirable; **emergency finance leadership experience** and previous work in the Middle East are an advantage.

Please download [the detailed job description](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:b:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQDykXJd7GUEQZVDhD3vlo8xAUtc9vURiJeSfCAscQg3el0?e=oaBMOR) to learn more about the position.

**What we offer**

- Duty station: Beirut, Lebanon
- Fixed term contract: 12 months national contract, renewable based on performance, funding and need for the position
- Travel: 10-20%
- Salary/benefits: Grade 9 on NRC's national grading structure.
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

Important information about the application process

- We invite applications from qualified candidates matching the profile. ***Applicants must be legally eligible to work in Lebanon, We are unable to provide work permits or visa sponsorships for this position.***
- Please ensure you attach copies of your academic and professional certificates.
- To apply as an internal candidate, log in with your official email address or click on Opportunity Marketplace.
- When creating your profile, include your full name as given on your passport. Complete all the system-required fields for experience, employment history and education.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV.
- Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered.
- Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. We receive many applicants for each vacant position.

**Why NRC?**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

[Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/736782633) to see NRC in action.

We are looking for people who are passionate about helping refugees and people forced to flee. Are you one of those people? If you are, NRC offers you the opportunity to:

- do demanding and professional work, often in challenging contexts
- join a work culture that empowers every employee to share ideas and take responsibility
- be part of a welcoming and supportive community committed to human dignity

**Join NRC Lebanon and help shape the financial leadership, systems, and partnerships that will enable us to respond effectively to humanitarian needs and deliver greater impact.**

[Learn more about NRC](https://www.nrc.no/)

[Learn more about NRC Lebanon](https://www.nrc.no/countries/middle-east/lebanon)

jobs.title: Nigeria Regional Warehouse Coordinator (Fixed-term)
jobs.body:
## About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

We started working in Nigeria in 2018, serving just 150 farmers. That figure grew year on year, and we now serve more than 300,000 farmers across three regions in Niger State: Minna, Mokwa, and Iseyin.  
  
Between our tree program and a diverse staple crop program, xx staff are supporting farmers in Nigeria to grow their way to prosperity.

## About the Role

Seeking a supply chain professional with 2-5 years' experience to coordinate warehouse and inventory operations, team supervision, and space optimization to support efficient and scalable program delivery.

## Responsibilities

Regional Warehouse Operations & Performance

- Coordinate day-to-day warehouse operations across assigned regional facilities.
- Ensure warehouses consistently follow approved OAF warehouse processes, and SOPs.
- Monitor warehouse performance against agreed KPIs for inventory accuracy, shrinkage, service, productivity, safety and compliance.
- Identify and share best practices across warehouses to improve consistency and performance.
- Plan ahead for peak periods and ensure warehouses are ready to support field and farmer needs.
- Regularly Go to Gemba to understand operational challenges and drive practical improvements.

Inventory Management & Control

- Lead regular physical stock counts, reconciliations and inventory reviews across assigned warehouses.
- Ensure physical stock is accurately reflected in the relevant inventory management system.
- Investigate inventory variances, identify root causes and ensure corrective actions are completed.
- Monitor inventory ageing, stock movements, transfers and potential losses.
- Strengthen controls that prevent shrinkage, stock errors and unauthorized stock movements.
- Ensure inventory records and supporting documentation are complete and audit-ready.

Warehouse Systems, Documentation & Compliance

- Ensure receiving, dispatch and inter-warehouse movements are properly documented and recorded on time.
- Maintain accurate warehouse records, including stock count sheets, waybills, delivery notes, GRNs, transfer documents and quality records.
- Conduct regular compliance checks and follow up on identified gaps.
- Support internal and external audits by ensuring warehouse records and physical stock are readily available.
- Escalate suspected theft, fraud, significant loss or other serious compliance concerns through the appropriate channels.

Warehouse Layout, Quality & Process Improvement

- Ensure effective warehouse layout, product segregation, palletization, labelling and storage practices.
- Work closely with QA/QC to maintain appropriate product handling, storage and release standards.
- Identify bottlenecks and opportunities to improve warehouse flow, space utilization and productivity.
- Lead practical improvement initiatives using data, root-cause analysis and feedback from warehouse teams.
- Standardize successful improvements across other regional warehouses where appropriate.

Health, Safety & Environment

- Promote a strong safety culture across all assigned warehouses.
- Conduct regular warehouse Gemba walks and safety checks to identify and address hazards.
- Ensure appropriate use of PPE and compliance with warehouse safety standards.
- Maintain clean, organized and safe working environments for employees, casual workers and visitors.
- Ensure incidents, near misses and safety concerns are reported, investigated and followed through to closure.
- Encourage team members to speak up and take ownership of safety.

Distribution & Supply Chain Coordination

- Coordinate with Logistics, Procurement, QA/QC and field teams to ensure smooth warehouse operations and timely movement of inputs.
- Support efficient loading, dispatch and inter-warehouse transfer activities.
- Ensure warehouse capacity and dispatch plans are aligned with operational demand.
- Work with Logistics teams to resolve delivery and dispatch challenges quickly.
- Support efficient use of warehouse and transport resources to reduce avoidable operational costs.

Team Leadership & Development

- Provide day-to-day leadership and support to Warehouse Supervisors and warehouse teams.
- Set clear expectations, priorities and performance standards.
- Coach team members to improve warehouse practices, inventory controls, safety and customer service.
- Build a culture of accountability, teamwork, feedback and continuous improvement.
- Support performance reviews, recruitment, onboarding and development of warehouse staff.
- Lead by example and create an environment where people can take ownership and grow.

## Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

- Bachelor's degree or HND in Supply Chain Management, Logistics, Business Administration, Agribusiness, Science & Engineering or a related discipline. (A Masters degree with relevant professional certificate in supply chain would be an added advantage)
- At least 2 - 5 years of relevant experience in warehouse, inventory, logistics operations including supervising, managing or coordinating
- Strong leadership skills to effectively lead and motivate a team.
- Organizational skills to efficiently plan, prioritize and delegate tasks.
- Warehouse operations; inventory management and reconciliation; warehouse systems/WMS; stock control; warehouse layout and capacity planning; HSE; basic data analysis; process improvement; documentation and compliance.
- Makes day-to-day operational decisions within approved policies, SOPs and budgets; escalates significant operational, financial, safety and compliance risks appropriately.
- Quick problem-solving abilities to anticipate, identify and resolve issues with deliveries and transport operations.
- High attention to detail to accurately plan, schedule and track all deliveries.
- Excellent communication skills to effectively interact with clients, colleagues and stakeholders.
- Computer literacy to efficiently use software and systems for planning, managing and tracking deliverables.
- Efficient time management capabilities to ensure timely execution of deliveries and transport operations.
- Flexibility to adapt to evolving customer needs and requirements.
- Commercial awareness to identify cost-saving opportunities and make profitable decisions.

## Preferred Start Date

As soon as possible

## Job Location

Bida, Niger State, Nigeria

## Benefits

Health insurance, paid time off

## Eligibility

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Nigeria.

## Application Deadline

08 January 2027. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

*One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @*[*oneacrefund.org*](http://oneacrefund.org/) *address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), **but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.***

*Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.*

*We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.*

jobs.title: Senior Marine Ecology Officer - Southeast Asia
jobs.body:
**Location**: Bali, Indonesia

**Closing date for applications:** November 1st, 2026

**Start date:** As soon as possible

**Contract duration:** Permanent

**Remuneration:** IDR 255,498,264 to IDR 305,344,256 per Annum

**We rebuild tropical fisheries with coastal communities**

Blue Ventures connects coastal communities restoring the ocean, providing the resources and partnerships they need to unlock their power and turn local action into global impact. We link communities with allies, knowledge and influence to create unstoppable waves of change.

Together, we’re placing communities at the centre of solutions to sustain fisheries, manage ecosystems and redefine how the world protects the ocean.

**Summary job description**

We are currently recruiting a Senior Marine Ecology Officer - Southeast Asia, technical support to Blue Ventures’ marine ecology operations across Southeast Asia. Reporting directly to the Data Science Manager - Asia and based full-time in Denpasar, Indonesia (with regular regional travel), the role will support community-based ecology monitoring, management, and governance, working closely with teams in Indonesia, Timor-Leste, and the Philippines as well as regional partners across Southeast Asia. Working closely with the global Spatial Ecology team, you will execute the technical development, workflow standardization, field-level rollout of mobile data technologies, and tailored learning resources that bridge science and community-led conservation.

The Senior Officer will be in charge of capacity-building initiatives—including hands-on workshops, technical mentoring, and peer exchanges—to translate ecological theory into practical, community-level action. We are seeking a dynamic technical person with proven expertise in mangrove, seagrass and coral reef, participatory monitoring, and ecosystem-based fisheries governance in Southeast Asia. You will bring a strong track record in community-led natural resource management, multi-stakeholder partnership building, and optional familiarity with coastal carbon markets. If you thrive in complex environments, work independently across disciplines, and share our commitment to human rights-based marine conservation, this role offers an exciting opportunity to drive regional impact.

jobs.title: Field Researcher / Field Monitor (Researchers Pool)
jobs.body:
**Organization:** Jouri Research and Consulting (JRC)  
**Location:** Whole of Syria  
**Engagement Type:** Roster-based, assignment by assignment (full-time or part-time depending on project needs)  
**Reporting to:** Jouri Field Coordinator

**About JOURI**  
Jouri is an international development consultancy with presence and offices in Geneva, Turkey, Iraq, Jordan, Lebanon and Syria with a team based across Europe and the Middle East. We support humanitarian and development actors to increase the relevance, effectiveness, efficiency, sustainability and impact of their work. Our key services include Research and Analysis, Third-Party Monitoring and Evaluation in Conflict Contexts, and Capacity Building. Jouri is pleased to announce an opportunity for Field Researcher / Field Monitor.

**About the Role**  
Jouri is updating its pool of field researchers in Syria. Selected candidates will join our roster and be engaged on upcoming assignments, including third-party monitoring (TPM), needs assessments, baseline and endline studies, post-distribution monitoring, and programme evaluations. Assignments cover sectors such as food security and livelihoods, health, education, WASH, shelter, and protection.

**Key Responsibilities**

- Conduct field data collection using quantitative tools (household surveys, PDM, KAP surveys) on digital platforms such as KoboToolbox or ODK.
- Conduct qualitative data collection, including key informant interviews (KIIs) and focus group discussions (FGDs), and produce clear, accurate notes or transcripts in Arabic.
- Carry out site visits and direct observation at distribution points, schools, health facilities, markets, and project sites to verify implementation against agreed criteria.
- Collect market price data on essential food and non-food items when required.
- Obtain informed consent and apply research ethics, do-no-harm principles, and data protection standards in every interaction.
- Identify, document, and promptly report protection concerns, safeguarding issues, or serious gaps observed in the field, following JRC's referral and reporting procedures.
- Take photographs as evidence where appropriate and permitted, respecting the privacy and dignity of participants.
- Ensure data quality by checking submissions for completeness and accuracy and responding to supervisor feedback.
- Participate in training, piloting of tools, and team debriefs, and share field observations that inform analysis.
- Maintain professional and respectful relationships with communities, partners, and local authorities in line with humanitarian principles.

**Qualifications and Experience**

- **Education:** Bachelor's degree in social sciences, sociology, economics, development studies, public health, or a related field. An intermediate institute diploma combined with strong relevant experience may be considered.
- **Experience:**
    - At least three years of relevant professional experience.
    - Proven experience in field data collection, monitoring, or research (quantitative and/or qualitative).
    - Experience with UN agencies, international NGOs, or research firms in a humanitarian or development context is highly desirable.
    - Experience facilitating KIIs and FGDs, or using KoboToolbox/ODK, is a strong asset.
- **Skills and Competencies:**
    - Fluency in Arabic (spoken and written) is required; working knowledge of English is an asset.
    - Strong communication and interviewing skills, including with vulnerable groups.
    - Attention to detail and commitment to accurate, unbiased data.
    - Ability to work under pressure, manage multiple tasks, and meet deadlines.
    - Cultural sensitivity and strong commitment to ethical conduct, confidentiality, and safeguarding.
    - Willingness and ability to travel frequently to remote and sometimes challenging locations.

**Additional Requirements**

- Good knowledge of, and access to, the local community in the governorate(s) where the applicant is based.
- Comfortable using a smartphone or tablet for data collection.
- Female candidates are strongly encouraged to apply.

**Compensation:** Determined per assignment based on scope, duration, and location.

jobs.title: Grant Management and Learning Coordinator - International
jobs.body:
**Job profile**

The Grant Management and Learning Coordinator fulfils a key function within the Department of Programme Development, Impact and Learning, sitting in the Grant Management Unit. Under the direct supervision of the Deputy Director of Programme Performance and Monitoring, the Grant Management and Learning Coordinator is responsible for ensuring compliance with donor grants, coordinating consolidation of coherent and accurate project data, supporting timely development and submission of high-quality donor reports, building and maintaining relationships with partners and donors, and proactively identifying the need for contract changes. In addition, the role coordinates the production of high-quality research on the organisation's Climate Adaptation work and other programming, translating findings into articles, reports and other documents for donors, the NGO community, and other external audiences.

**Duties and Responsibilities**

The position covers the following key areas of responsibility:

- For assigned grants, serve as the focal point for Afghanaid’s policies and donor contract terms and conditions, maintaining comprehensive knowledge and ensuring that all grant documentation (including proposals, reports, and budgets) is properly stored and available to relevant staff, and that key reporting requirements and other compliance obligations are clearly communicated to finance and project teams.
- Upon the signing of a new grant agreement, facilitate a smooth handover of the project to the Grant Management Unit, following up on outstanding project partnership agreement (PPA) tasks, and confirming reporting responsibilities and processes with relevant parties at the project kickoff meeting.
- Maintain internal and external tracking of reporting timelines, including working with relevant departments to coordinate appropriate data collection, analysis and financial and narrative reporting by Afghanaid and its partners.
- Review and refine high-quality financial and narrative project reports, survey and evaluation reports, and other associated donor communications, ensuring timely submission and compliance with Afghanaid, donor and partner requirements.
- Independently troubleshoot issues raised by project and operational teams, serving as liaison between the project team and donor to address and resolve challenges.
- Facilitate and contribute to regular project review processes, and pre-emptively raise concerns where contractual obligations, quality standards or deadlines are at risk of not being met, especially identifying risks of donor ‘clawback’ and reputational damage.
- In coordination with project teams, partners and the finance team, lead on revisions to project budgets, logical frameworks and other project documents for assigned grants, ensuring timely submission to the donor and follow up on approvals, and communicating updates to relevant departments.
- Support the Consortium Manager in strengthening partner performance and report quality by reviewing and providing input on partner organisations’ annual and semi-annual narrative reports.
- Initiate learning exchanges and facilitate reflection and adaptive management sessions with Afghanaid staff and partners.
- Lead organisational research initiatives, including establishing and managing partnerships with research organisations, individual researchers (including PhD candidates/Masters’ students), universities and institutes, and consultants to facilitate the production of research outputs for Afghanaid. Adapt research findings into policy and practitioner briefs tailored to different audiences, including donors and external stakeholders; and producing reports drawing on the organisational database of past reports and data.
- Lead and contribute to the design of impact evaluations and internal studies, including initiating Terms of Reference, to inform the evolution of Afghanaid’s programming and implementation of the organisation’s strategy.
- Represent the organisation at external fora and in meetings with partners and donors to promote the organisation, strengthen external relations and identify opportunities for new and repeat funding and partnerships that contribute to Afghanaid’s funding pipeline.
- Support organisational learning initiatives where possible, for instance through documenting institutional knowledge and expertise and participating in lessons learned workshops.
- Contribute to organisational capacity through developing and facilitating training and workshops for Afghanaid staff, including in provincial offices, on subjects including effective reporting and impact analysis.
- Lead and support on the development of project reporting, analysis and evaluation templates and tools.
- Facilitate field visits with donor organisations, and virtual visits as required.

**PERSON SPECIFICATION**

**Requirements**

**Essential**

**Education**

- A Master’s degree in Development Studies, International Relations, Social Sciences or another relevant programme of study

**Experience**

- 3-4 years of experience of working in a development or humanitarian context, in project support, grant management, programme development or a similar role
- Proven experience of synthesising data and input from various sources into clear and cohesive narrative reports
- Strong experience with logical frameworks and/or theories of change
- Experience working in high-risk or volatile contexts, including humanitarian or emergency settings.

**Knowledge and Skills**

- Native English proficiency and demonstrated ability to write high quality, polished documents and reports that are consistent with a set brand and style
- Experience turning data and research into clear reports for a variety of audiences
- Strong data entry skills, familiarity with use of a databases, and office tools (Excel, Word)
- Experience in contract management
- Experience in donor/client relationship management in the humanitarian / development sector
- Experience in humanitarian project design or management, and/or budget development or management
- Strong organisational skills, able to plan effectively, set priorities, and meet tight deadlines under pressure
- Strong people and coalition-building skills and proven ability to form good working relations, both internally within the organisation and externally with people at all levels

**Personal Attributes**

- Intellectually curious and able to question assumptions
- Ability to work independently and as a team member, including in a coordinating capacity with other departments
- Initiative and drive to achieve results, working quickly and accurately with attention to detail
- An outgoing and engaging personality and strong sense of humour, able to build trust and manage relationships with a variety of stakeholders
- Cultural sensitivity and ability to work in diverse multi-cultural environment
- Ability and willingness to travel for work

**Desirable**

- Experience working on Climate Adaptation projects
- Experience working with, or knowledge of, key institutional donors for development and humanitarian programming in Afghanistan
- Experience with EU/INTPA grants
- Training in and/or exposure to M&E
- Understanding of the cultural, security and operating environment in Afghanistan (or in a similar context)
- Understanding of Dari and/or Pashto

jobs.title: Staff Auditor
jobs.body:
**Opportunity Type:**

Regular

**Summary:**

Habitat for Humanity International (HFHI) is currently seeking a talented professional for the role of a Staff Auditor. The Staff Auditor will help evaluate the adequacy and effectiveness of the internal controls of various departments at HFHI's headquarters, HFHI's international area offices, and selected programs of Habitat's U.S. and international organizations.

This position will be remotely based within the US and will require 40-60% domestic and/or international travel.

**Key Responsibilities:**

- Assist with the planning, execution, and reporting on operational, financial and compliance audits in the designated areas. (20%)
- Assist in the preparation of the audit planning memo, risk-based audit programs and test plans which defines specific procedures to be performed during an audit. (5%)
- Conduct audit fieldwork work papers, findings, and recommendations for compliance with the Institute of Internal Auditor International Professional Standards and HFHI Internal Audit Department (IAD) Standards. (20%)
- Conduct peer reviews of other audit staff's audit documentation and working papers to ensure consistency, quality and compliance with internal audit standards. Provide constructive feedback to support continuous improvement. (5%)
- Draft finding and recommendations audit report in accordance with and monitor the quality of audit reports to ensure compliance with International Professional Practices Framework (IPPF) and HFHI IAD Standards. (15%)
- Document processes, procedures, and test results. (5%)
- Coordinate the monitoring of outstanding audit recommendations. (5%)
- Plan, coordinate and performing consulting and advisory services as appropriate for the organization. (5%)
- Assist in the development of the IAD annual risk-based internal audit plan. (5%)
- Lead auditor assigned to the audit projects under his/her responsibility, will provide guidance and overall review of deliverables. (10%)
- Assists the VP/Director/Manager of Internal Audit on any other duties as assigned by management of Internal Audit as needed. The above duties could include supporting other internal audit units and audit activities, such as the SOAR process, audit committee package and risk assessment process. (5%)

**Key Requirements:**

- Bachelor’s degree in business administration, Accounting, Finance, Information Technology, or a related field.
- 3-5 years of professional experience with external and internal audits, forensic accounting investigations, preferably with a public accounting firm.
- Experience with international travel and/or cross-cultural communications.
- Expert level skills with Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint, as well as a good understanding of the COSO - International Control Integrated Framework.
- Excellent English, verbal and written, communication skills.
- Strong critical thinking and project management skills.

**Preferred:**

- 3 years of domestic and international experience in internal or external audit management, preferably with a large international non-profit government, corporate organizations, or Big 4 Accounting Firm.
- Experience auditing construction activities and Micro-Finance operations.
- Proficiency with auditing software such as Galvanize HighBond or others.
- Experience using data analytics tools to create queries and trend analysis reports.
- Experience in non-profit Internal Audits, particularly executing audits of controls and transactions related to government and corporate grant requirements.
- Spanish, verbal and written, communication skills would be beneficial.

**Hiring Range:**

The actual salary offered for this role will be based on a variety of factors, including location, internal equity and the candidate’s qualifications and professional experience. HFHI offers a competitive, comprehensive benefits package that varies by country and typically includes vacation leave, sick leave, personal days, health insurance options, retirement plan contributions and life insurance. For work locations in the US, the hiring range for this position is:

$55,600.00 USD

$82,675 USD

/

Annual

**About Us:**

Habitat for Humanity, founded in 1976, is a global, Christian-based nonprofit organization that grew out of an intentionally multi-racial community in rural Georgia. Seeking to put God’s love into action, Habitat brings together people of all faiths and people of no faith to build homes, communities and hope. Working alongside each other, we help families and individuals build and improve places to call home and achieve the strength, stability and self-reliance they need to build better lives for themselves. Habitat seeks individuals who have a willingness to affirm these principles and values.

At Habitat for Humanity International, we are compelled by our Koinonia roots to put God’s love for all into action and pursue housing equity and opportunity by bringing all people together to build community and drive impact. We strive to build a culture rooted in learning, accountability and trust, attracting and retaining mission-driven talent reflective of the global communities we serve.

As an equal opportunity employer, we realize our success depends on courageously committing to being a workplace where all staff feel safe, welcome, visible, respected, supported and valued, and building a workforce that reflects a variety of lived experiences, backgrounds and perspectives, in which every person experiences dignity and respect.
