Specifically this role designs and implements MEAL systems for impact investment portfolios and SGB programs, ensuring evidence-based decision-making and will contribute to global learning agendas, donor reporting, and impact measurement frameworks aligned with GIIN/IRIS+ standards.

**Key Responsibilities:**

ESSENTIAL DUTIES 1) Design and implement the MEARL framework for the SGB framework.  
Develop results chains/frameworks for SGB framework and Shelter Venture Fund investments.  
Ensure alignment with global impact measurement standards (IRIS+, SDG indicators).  
Supports SGB team in target setting for annual and multi-year projections and puts a rigorous but realistic plan in place to track and monitor against these targets.

2)Ensure Data Quality and Insight Generation to support the SGB framework and strengthen evidence of uptake.

Working with global MEARL, geographic MEARL and SGB leads, lead rigorous data collection, validation, and analysis using mixed methods. Lead stakeholder reporting requirements and ensure integrity of reporting. Produce dashboards and learning briefs for internal strategy and external stakeholders.

3)Learning and Knowledge Management.

Facilitate learning loops across regions; synthesize cross-portfolio insights. Translate evidence into actionable recommendations for the SGB framework, including investment insights and program design. Promote adaptive management. Use evidence and real-time insights to inform strategic pivots and improve program effectiveness.

4\) Capacity Building and Systems Strengthening.  
Develop and maintain digital data systems (such as CRM, Airtable, PowerBI) for real-time monitoring and data visualization.  
Keep up to date on industry trends and build insights into continuous improvement of MEAL systems.

MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS

Master’s in Monitoring & Evaluation, Development Economics, Statistics, Impact Measurement, or related field.

PREFERRED REQUIREMENTS

Minimum 5 years in MEAL roles, including impact investing or enterprise development contexts.

Proven ability to design and implement MEAL systems.

**Hiring Range:**

The actual salary offered for this role will be based on a variety of factors, including location, internal equity and the candidate’s qualifications and professional experience. HFHI offers a competitive, comprehensive benefits package that varies by country and typically includes vacation leave, sick leave, personal days, health insurance options, retirement plan contributions and life insurance.

For work locations in Slovakia, the minimum monthly gross pay starts at:

€3,060.00 EUR

**About Us:**

Habitat for Humanity, founded in 1976, is a global, Christian-based nonprofit organization that grew out of an intentionally multi-racial community in rural Georgia. Seeking to put God’s love into action, Habitat brings together people of all faiths and people of no faith to build homes, communities and hope. Working alongside each other, we help families and individuals build and improve places to call home and achieve the strength, stability and self-reliance they need to build better lives for themselves. Habitat seeks individuals who have a willingness to affirm these principles and values.

At Habitat for Humanity International, we are compelled by our Koinonia roots to put God’s love for all into action and pursue housing equity and opportunity by bringing all people together to build community and drive impact. We strive to build a culture rooted in learning, accountability and trust, attracting and retaining mission-driven talent reflective of the global communities we serve.

**Equal Opportunity Employer Statement:**

As an equal opportunity employer, we realize our success depends on courageously committing to being a workplace where all staff feel safe, welcome, visible, respected, supported and valued, and building a workforce that reflects a variety of lived experiences, backgrounds and perspectives, in which every person experiences dignity and respect.

jobs.title: Coordinateur/Coordinatrice MEALS
jobs.body:
Dans le cadre de la gestion de ses projets en **République du Congo**, la FONDATION AVSI recrute **un/e Coordinateur/Coordinatrice MEALS**.  
Le/la coordinateur/Coordinatrice MEALS est chargé de concevoir, de mettre en œuvre et de superviser les systèmes de suivi, d’évaluation, de responsabilisation et d’apprentissage des programmes d’AVSI Congo. Ce poste vise à garantir la qualité, l’exactitude et la ponctualité de la collecte de données et de l’établissement de rapports pour l’ensemble des projets en cours, à renforcer les mécanismes de responsabilisation envers les populations concernées et à favoriser l’apprentissage organisationnel grâce à la documentation systématique des bonnes pratiques et des enseignements tirés. Le/la coordinateur/Coordinatrice MEALS travaille en étroite collaboration avec le responsable des programmes, les chefs de projet et le conseiller régional MEALS.

**? Lieu d'affectation:** Pointe-Noire

**? Starting** **Date:** 01/01/2027

**⏳Période:** 12 mois

**Langue:** French

**Salary:** 1800-2300€ net

**De faire rapport à:** Représentante Pays (report hiérarchique) et MEALS régional (report fonctionnel)

**?Objectif de la position:**

- En collaboration avec le responsable régional du MEALS et les responsables des programmes et des projets, établir un ensemble fiable et cohérent d’indicateurs de résultats et de produits pour toutes les activités des programmes, des projets et les nouveaux appels à propositions.
- Superviser l’élaboration des plans de suivi et d’évaluation des projets en accord avec le cadre logique du projet et en consultation avec les équipes de projet pour tous les projets en cours.
- Fournir un soutien au suivi et à l’évaluation des organisations partenaires, à travers des ateliers de renforcement des capacités; renforcer la communication entre AVSI et les partenaires.
- Soutenir l'élaboration de procédures opérationnelles standard (POS/SoP) et de lignes directrices et les mettre à jour lorsque cela est nécessaire, en particulier pour le travail contre rémunération et la distribution d'espèces.
- Préparer des revues après action des projets en cas de besoin.
- Assurer la compilation en temps opportun des rapports d'avancement internes et externes et des rapports finaux des projets en cours (mise à jour MEALS tous les mois/deux mois) et numériser les rapports.
- Partage des défis, des bonnes pratiques, des retours d'expérience et des leçons apprises du terrain et des données collectées.
- Superviser et guider le travail du personnel MEALS d'AVSI en République du Congo et améliorer la communication entre les départements, MEALS et les programmes (réunions régulières).
- Garantir une formation constante du staff MEALS, améliorer leurs compétences et agir comme un mentor pour leurs staffs.
- Coordonner les visites sur le terrain à effectuer par le staff du département MEAL pour garantir la qualité des données collectées par les programmes et pour vérifier l'exactitude des données rapportées (au moins une visite par mois).
- En étroite collaboration avec les équipes de projet, mener des séances d’information et de retour d’information auprès des bénéficiaires pour les guider dans l’expression de leurs besoins et la recherche d’aide.
- Garantir et coordonner le système d’archivage pour les livrables des différents projets.
- Représenter l'AVSI en externe au sein du groupe de travail MEALS et établir un réseau avec d'autres organisations pour partager les apprentissages et les bonnes pratiques en matière de MEALS; Pour les projets basés sur un consortium, travailler en étroite collaboration avec les partenaires pour élaborer des plans de suivi et suivre leur mise en œuvre.

**? Autres compétences et expériences requises:**

***Compétences techniques***

- Au moins 4 ans d'expérience professionnelle dans le secteur MEALS au sein d'organisations humanitaires et de développement
- Excellentes compétences en communication orale et écrite en français, la connaissance d’une autre langue (anglais ou italien) est un avantage
- Expérience avérée dans l’utilisation d’outils de collecte, de gestion et d’analyse de données qualitatives et quantitatives.

***Atouts Supplémentaires***

- De préférence Bonne connaissance du contexte local (ou régional)
- Solides compétences en communication et de management.

?AVSI applique, dans le processus de sélection, le principe d’inclusivité et de non-discrimination, garantissant l’égalité des chances indépendamment du sexe, de l’âge, de l’ethnie, de la nationalité, de l’orientation sexuelle, de l’identité de genre, de l’état civil, des convictions religieuses, du handicap et de l’appartenance à des catégories protégées.

?AVSI se réserve le droit de demander aux employeurs précédents des informations concernant d’éventuels différends, préoccupations liées à la protection, enquêtes ou mesures disciplinaires, et de solliciter la communication des antécédents judiciaires et civils du candidat, aux fins d’évaluer son aptitude professionnelle à exercer des fonctions impliquant un contact avec des personnes vulnérables, y compris des enfants et des adultes.

jobs.title: Sudan - Field Coordinator (M/F) - Ed Daein
jobs.body:
**Desired start date: 12/01/2027**  
**Duration of the mission: 6 Months**  
**Location: Ed Daein - Darfur**

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms.

## About the mission

Following the outbreak of the conflict in April 2023 and forced evacuation of Khartoum and West Darfur (El Geneina), SI was one of the first international NGO to re-enter Darfur and resume its emergency response.  
In February 2024, SI opened a base in El Fasher (North Darfur) to provide emergency assistance to populations, as very few humanitarian organizations were operational in the state. Then, SI opened offices in Tawila (North Darfur), in Zalingei (Central Darfur) in october & November 2024 and East Darfur and West Kordofan in early 2026. In addition, an office in Khartoum was maintained and in 2025 operations were opened in Jazeera state.  
Today, thanks to the support of SHF, CDCS, SDC, GFFO, SIDA, ECHO, UNDP and Unicef, activities are being implemented in West Darfur, Central Darfur, North Darfur, East Darfur, West Kordofan, Jazeera and Khartoum States across WASH, Shelter and NFI support, Food Security and Livelihood sectors. Most of the programs are being implemented in Consortium, 2 led by SI, and require strong coordination efforts to provide area-based interventions. SI also has a strong localization approach, with diverse local partners in all states.  
Across the Darfurs and in West Kordofan, the main share of the portfolio remains WASH -from 1st line to 2nd line & beyond- with the provision of water through water trucking, rehabilitation of water points/water yards, borehole drilling, networks, hygiene promotion, sanitation (emergency latrine construction, semi-permanent latrine, showers, desludging), solid waste management, WASH NFI distribution, and WASH in Health etc.  
SI also has Emergency Response Teams based in Zalingei, Central Darfur, roving across Central and West Darfur, and in Tawila covering North Darfur, both implementing rapid responses in WASH, Shelter/NFI and Food (CVA).  
Besides, SI implements food assistance mostly through cash and voucher modalities. West and North Darfur team also implements agricultural support activities (seeds distribution, provision of tools, training) as well as market strengthening support  
In Darfurs & in West Kordofan, SI is the leader of WASH, co leading the North Darfur WASH Cluster and managing also a part of UNICEF pipeline from West Darfur to West Kordofan. SI is also coleading the SNFI clusters in East Darfur and in North Darfur, and the FSL Cluster in North Darfur.  
In May 2026, SI opened our new base in Al Dein, East Darfur and in Ghobeish, West Kordofan. The teams have been working on strong WASH and cholera responses in several localities.

## About the job

SIZING OF THE TEAM ON THE BASE / IN COORDINATION :

Mission size around 45 international staff and 190 National staff across different bases  
The East Darfur & West Kordofan is composed by 1 FC, 1 admin Mgr, 1 log Mgr, 1 WASH PM, 1 AM WASH (based in WK), a Security & access Officer, WASH Officers, a MEal Supervisor, and Log & admin assistants. The team scaling-up is underway.

GENERAL OBJECTIVES :

The Field Coordinator oversees the development of Solidarites International's (SI) presence and response in their area of intervention, in line with the Country Strategy and the organisation's mandate.  
Delegated by the Country Director, they are SI's representative in the area to aid workers, local administrative, military and political authorities, civil society and the media.  
They are responsible for ensuring the security of SI teams and assets in their area, as well as compliance with the organisation's ethical framework and values.

ISSUES AND SPECIFIC CHALLENGES :

1 - High level and severity of emergency needs  
2 - 2 bases, 2 states, vast operational area with a limited humanitarian presence compared to other States.  
3 - Access & security challenges

PRIORITIES ON THE 2-3 FIRST MONTHS :

Implementation of new activities in West Kordofan & set up of the teams  
Support the access strategy  
Security analysis

SECURITY CONSTRAINTS :

Security Level 4  
High risk environment, threats less predictable and requiring strict protocols, Curfews in place (often 6pm–8pm), Walking strictly limited to approved times, locations.

## Your profile

DIPLOMAS : Masters degree in a related field (humanitarian response, international cooperation, development studies, political sciences…).

EXPERIMENT IN THE HUMANITARIAN SECTOR : 3- 4 years

EXPERIMENT IN THE HUMANITARIAN SECTOR : 3- 4 years

TECHNICAL SKILLS :

1\. Security and access management

2.. Rapid need Assesement

3\. Strong negociations skills

4\. Conflict sensitivy skills

TRANSVERSAL SKILLS :

1\. Work under pressure

2\. Adaptability

3\. Strong initiative capacities and solution-finding attitude

LANGUAGES

1\. Fluent English

2\. Arabic would be an advantage

3\. French would be an asset

## SI will offer you

**A salaried position:**

**According to experience,** starting from EUR 3080 gross per month (2800 base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 750.

SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment.

**Breaks:** During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every three months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked.

**Insurance package:** Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded.

**Living conditions:** In Darfur, the guesthouses are of good standard with solar panels, STARLINK internet connection, and running water. Social life is limited to contact with other NGO staff. Access to Markets and local food is possible, but restaurants are scarce and not diversified.  
SI main base is located in Ed Daein (East DArfur): big building divided in 2 parts with GH & Office and is well equiped: TV, modern kitchen, salons, 5-6 bedrooms and with large outdoor space.  
SI sub base is located in Ghobeish, charming but smaller house serving as both an office and a guesthouse.

jobs.title: Emergency Human Resources Coordinator
jobs.body:
To fulfill its mission of assistance to victims of conflicts, epidemics or natural disasters, OCG has created an Emergency Pool, whose members are experienced individuals capable of evaluating a humanitarian crisis, opening, closing and coordinating emergency projects.

The Emergency Human Resources Coordinator is a key member of this pool and reports directly to the Emergency Coordinator, as well as to the E-Cell HR Referent.

The successful candidate is expected to:

- Deploy rapidly in all contexts set by the Emergency cell
- Have the flexibility to assume different HR roles according to operational needs (HR Coordinator but also HR/Administration Manager)
- Gap fill in regular cells if required.

As a member of the Emergency Pool, the Emergency HR Coordinator must be available for deployment within 48 hours for short-term emergency interventions. You will be part of a multidisciplinary response team -including medical, paramedical, and support staff - mobilized for emergencies such as epidemics, armed conflicts, natural disasters, and other acute crises. You may also be involved in exploratory missions, short-term assignments within regular missions or gap filling in the Emergency Cell in Geneva HQ.

Job Description (but not limited to)

- Act as a strategic partner to Operations by contributing to mission planning and execution. Support the design of appropriate emergency organizational structures and ensure adequate HR capacity and sizing.
- Define, adapt, and oversee the implementation of human resources policies for emergency interventions, ensuring alignment with the operational context and challenges.
- Ensure MSF operates as a responsible employer within the mission. Oversee all HR management, administrative, and legal matters, proactively addressing HR-related risks and adapting processes to the emergency context.
- Is the technical referent for all HR and Administration related issues at Mission level (recruitment, management and development of teams, contracting and remuneration of national staff, follow up of daily workers, etc.). Coordinates the urgent recruitment of HR required for the mission. Ensures the timely deployment of critical staff in coordination with the E-Cell HR Referent.

- Monitor working conditions and staff wellbeing, with a focus on high-stress environments. In collaboration with the medical department, coordinate psychosocial support as needed.
- Design, recruit and train the HR teams at coordination and project level.
- Contribute to emergency preparedness and surge capacity planning by assessing HR risks and implementing appropriate mitigation strategies.
- Participate in exploratory missions and evaluations, upon request of the Ecell.

Your Profile

Required Skills and experience

**Field Experience**

- Minimum of 2 years in HR management in the field with MSF, gained through exposure to various contexts, including emergency contexts (population displacement, epidemic outbreaks, natural disasters and/or conflicts).
- At least one field experience with MSF in HR coordination (HR Coordinator or Deputy HR Coordinator).
- Ability to quickly evaluate an emergency on the ground and propose an adapted HR strategy.
- Experience in Finance management is an advantage.

**Strategic and Interpersonal Skills**

- Ability to work effectively in volatile and insecure environments, with strong resilience and stress management skills.
- Strong interpersonal and communication skills
- Strong people management skills.
- Strong coordination and organizational skills.
- Strong adaptability and flexibility to navigate changing priorities, dynamic operational environments, and evolving team dynamics.
- Responsible behavior that contributes to the safety and integrity of everyone - prevent, report, and refuse any abusive behavior and/or behavior that goes against MSF's values.
- Ability to thrive in a multicultural environment and demonstrate commitment and support for diversity, inclusive and non-discriminatory attitudes and behaviors.

**Language skills**

- Fluency in both French and English is highly desirable. Alternatively, candidates must demonstrate an excellent command of either language and at least B1 proficiency in the other.
- Knowledge of other mission languages is an advantage (Spanish, Portuguese, Arabic).
- Proficiency in an additional language, especially Spanish, Arabic, and/or Portuguese.

Terms of Employment

- Field-based contract. One year fixed-term contract, renewable based on operational needs and performance.
- Duration of field assignments: 4 weeks to 3 months (flexibility required according to needs).
- Accommodation and travel arrangements such as visa-related costs will be taken in charge by MSF.
- Comprehensive support and guidance will be provided by dedicated technical referents throughout the assignment.

**We encourage applications from individuals of all genders, ages, sexual orientations, ethnicities, background, religions, beliefs, ability status, and all other diversity characteristics.**

**MSF does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of discrimination or harassment, including sexual harassment.**

jobs.title: Emergency Pharmacy Coordinator
jobs.body:
To fulfill its mission of assistance to victims of conflicts, epidemics or natural disasters, MSF-Switzerland has created an emergency team, of which members are experienced individuals capable of evaluating a situation, start and coordinate the missions. The position of Emergency Pharmacy Coordinator reports to the Emergency Medical Coordinator at field level and/or to the coordination team in the capital and finally to the Emergency Desk (RMP) at headquarters level in Geneva.

The candidate is expected to 1) work in all contexts set by the emergency desk and 2) work in emergency contexts with regular cells and fill gaps in regular projects if need be.

**Duty Station**

All countries where the emergency desk opens activities, which requires an urgent response. On call, the Emergency Pharmacy Coordinator should be available within 48 hours for rapid and short interventions. He/she is part of a core group of operations, medicals, para-medicals, logisticians/supply, fin/HR responsible for responding, amongst others, to:

- Exploratory missions
- Epidemic outbreaks
- Nutritional crises
- Displaced populations and/or refugees’ camps
- Surgical emergencies
- Natural disasters

**Responsibilities**

As the emergency medical supplies representative at mission level, their priority is to ensure the continuous improvement of the medical supplies management in emergency contexts and guarantee answers, strategies and interdepartmental tools adapted to the evolution of the needs and the policies of intervention defined by the department of the operations.

The other responsibilities of the Emergency Pharmacy Coordinator include:

- During preparation phase: Surveillance system through local contact (MoH, Central Medical Store, Pharmacy Directory,) Emergency Preparedness strategy and emergency response (including stock) in place (with and without MSF presence)
- During detection phase: Emergency coordination with MSF and external actors (crisis committee)
- During response phase: Exploratory mission: preparation for rapid assessments / Intervention according to the priorities defined and the strategy.
- During evaluation phase: Evaluation of the intervention (strategy, justification, resources, results vs needs) / Modification of the Emergency Preparedness strategy if needed / Hand over to MSF or MoH or others.

**Nature and activities**

**Emergency Preparedness Strategy**

- Participate to the design of new emergency supply standards (processes, procedures, tools, etc…) according to validated strategy and support related implementations with the Emergency Supply Referent
- Participate to the definition of autonomous and decentralized e-stock content based on the market control (validation sources by Headquarter Pharmacist for medical local purchase if needed)
- Define the resources (medical needs) to respond to natural disasters and other emergency context on demand according to defined strategy.
- Define, implement and monitor internal medical supplies management in emergency contexts at all levels (field, capital, headquarters)
- Define the means, the roles, and the responsibilities in terms of pharmacy management in emergency context in interaction with the Med Supply of the MOSU
- Conceive a strategy of briefing / debriefing and training centered on three axes:
- Global medical supplies management
- Modular management by specific interventions (Hospital, Mobil Clinic, Vaccination, …)
- Management tools
- Apply the standard tools and techniques of management and information (software, workflow, monitoring, and tracking) provided by technical referent.
- Guarantee good practices in pharmacy management present on the fields and management tools used judiciously in emergency context.
- Perpetuation of the partnership with MSF Logistique
- Introduce and formalize links and operational reports (regular visits, planning and common data base, development of technical projects, conception of the emergency stock …).
- Compile all the field feedback of improvement of content of kits & modules.

**Human Resources**

- Guarantee knowledge and competencies among the mission actors (training / mentoring / coaching of medical coordinator, pharmacy manager and associated HR setup)

**Monitoring & Reporting**

- Guarantee the release and availability of weekly / monthly reports (quarterly and yearly on demand) including follow-up of indicators and corrective actions.
- Field support reports.

**Your Profile**

Required:

- Pharmacy qualification sufficient to be recognized and practice as Pharmacist in your home country
- Minimum of 12 months of field experience with MSF as Pharmacy Coordinator
- Minimum of 2 years of experience in pharmacy management in the field with MSF, gained through exposure to various contexts; as part of this experience, at least one mission in an emergency context with MSF Switzerland
- Alternatively, for candidates without MSF experience, minimum of 3 years of field experience with other NGOs in pharmacy management, gained through exposure to various contexts and including experience in emergency context
- Strong knowledge and experience in medical supply & pharmacies management
- Strong proficiency in data processing tools and advanced computer literacy
- Fluency in both French and English is highly desirable. Alternatively, candidates must demonstrate an excellent command of either language and at least B1 proficiency in the other.
- Experience in supervising, coaching and training
- Professional and personal flexibility and adaptability
- Responsible behavior that contributes to the safety and integrity of everyone - prevent, report, and refuse any abusive behavior and/or behavior that goes against MSF's values
- Ability to thrive in a multicultural environment and demonstrate commitment and support for diversity, inclusive and non-discriminatory attitudes and behaviors

**Assets**

- Experience with Isystock
- Proficiency in an additional language, especially Spanish, Arabic, and/or Portuguese

**Terms of Employment**

- Field-based contract, fixed-term for one year, renewable.
- Duration of direct interventions in the field: from 4 weeks to 3 months (certain flexibility is asked in case of needs)
- Per-diem, accommodation, travel arrangements, visa requirement will be taken in charge from MSF and in the field during your assignments.

**We encourage applications from people of all genders, ages, sexual orientations, backgrounds, religions, beliefs, abilities, and all other characteristics of diversity.**   
**MSF does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of discrimination or harassment, including Sexual harassment.**

**All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo reference and criminal record checks.**

jobs.title: ETHIOPIA - FIELD COORDINATOR (M/F) - TIGRAY
jobs.body:
**Desired start date: 01/12/2026**  
**Duration of the mission: 6 Months**  
**Location: Adwa - Tigray Region**

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms.

PRESENTATION OF THE MISSION:

Solidarités International (SI) was registered in Ethiopia in December 2022, having previously implemented a WASH in Health intervention in Jijiga, Somali Region, in 2017. In November 2023, SI became the first humanitarian actor to operate in Mao Komo Special woreda (Benishangul-Gumuz) by rehabilitating water points in areas that had been inaccessible for three years. Currently, SI is operational in two regions of the country (In Tigray Region and Amhara Region).

In Tigray, bordering Eritrea, focusing on hard-to-reach areas in partnership with Mums for Mums (MfM) SI is implementing an emergency multisectoral humanitarian programme in Ahsea and Rama Woredas of central zone, to support communities affected by drought, conflict, and displacement. Running from September 2024 to December 2025 (which is now to be extended until end of June 2026), the project aims to improve access to safe water, health services, and nutrition support, while addressing gender-based violence and mental health needs. Key activities include rehabilitating water systems and health facilities, community-based malnutrition screening, cash assistance for vulnerable households, and capacity-building for local actors.

In Amhara region, Solidarités International (SI) and Première Urgence Internationale (PUI) are jointly implementing an integrated emergency response program in the Amhara region of Ethiopia, primarily focused on Health and Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) services. This program is part of a wider effort to address the significant humanitarian needs in the region caused by ongoing conflict and displacement.

SI has been granted cost extension (the donor contract is extended until end of June 2026 with additional fund allocation) of existing project in Tigray and is looking for a Field Coordinator to continue the project activities in the same area.

GENERAL OBJECTIVES :

The Field Coordinator is the representative of the organization at field level. He/she proposes a strategy for his/her area, according to the geopolitical and humanitarian context, and ensures its implementation once validated. He/she checks and ensures that projects are carried out in accordance with the Solidarités International charter, respecting all internal and contractual procedures. He/she mobilizes the material and financial resources necessary for programs to run smoothly and supervises resource management. He/she coordinates the teams in place and is responsible for their security in his/her assigned zone.  
Representation and Internal / external communication:  
The FC is the official representative of Solidarités International in his/her intervention zone for NGOs, administrative, political and local authorities and civil society. He/She participates in humanitarian forums and relevant coordination meetings  
The FC Ensure that documents produced in his/her intervention zone meet deadlines and quality standards, respecting standard formats and procedures   
The FC Organise regular Base meetings and Ensure that key operational information circulates properly, in his/her intervention zone and between the bases and the country coordination (sitrep).

ISSUES AND SPECIFIC CHALLENGES :

Implement activities across several woredas in a volatile and operationally constrained context, while ensuring quality, compliance and timely delivery of ongoing projects. Maintain access and programme continuity despite recurrent constraints linked to fuel availability, cash liquidity, telecommunications/network coverage, road access and market fluctuations. Maintain adequate preparedness for a potential deterioration of the security situation, including possible disruption of banking services, communications and movements.

PRIORITIES ON THE 2-3 FIRST MONTHS :

-Consolidate the base management structure and ensure clear responsibilities, delegation and reporting lines within Programme and Support teams.   
-Ensure timely implementation and close monitoring of ongoing activities through updated workplans, APU/OFU/LFU and procurement plans.   
-Strengthen coordination between WASH, Livelihoods, MEAL and Support departments and ensure adequate balance of management capacity between the main programme components.   
-Reinforce budget forecasting and absorption monitoring.   
-Maintain and strengthen coordination with local authorities, clusters, partners and other humanitarian actors to avoid duplication and identify operational synergies.   
-Ensure the base is prepared for emergency scenarios through updated contingency plans, communication systems, cash/fuel contingency measures and staff preparedness, especially this year with the evolving context  
-Continue effort of base development with upcoming opportunities

SECURITY CONSTRAINTS :

The security environment in Tigray remains potentially volatile and can evolve rapidly, requiring continuous monitoring and strict compliance with SI security procedures. Main operational constraints include possible access restrictions, interruptions to telecommunications and internet, fuel shortages, banking/cash limitations and disruptions to road movements. Some operational areas may have limited or no network coverage, requiring reinforced movement tracking and communication procedures. The Field Coordinator must maintain a high level of preparedness, regularly review contingency arrangements, ensure critical resources are available, and adapt programme implementation and movements according to changes in the security and access environment. Staff safety and duty of care must remain central to operational decision-making.

YOUR PROFIL :

DIPLOMAS : A master’s degree (or equivalent field experience) in Humanitarian Action, International Development, Social Sciences, Project Management, or a related field is required.

EXPERIMENT IN THE HUMANITARIAN SECTOR : more than 5 years

EXPERIMENT ON SIMILAR POSITIONS : 3-4 years

TECHNICAL SKILLS :

Relevant management skills :Operation and team management skills include leadership, communication, and problem-solving as core competencies. Other essential skills are decision-making, time management, adaptability, and organizational abilities. Including a strong understanding of finance, and logistics processes.

TRANSVERSAL SKILLS : Ability to work under pressure in a challenging and sometimes insecure environment; cultural sensitivity, adaptability, and a strong commitment to humanitarian principles and safeguarding policies (PSEA, Child Protection).

LANGUAGES : Fluency in written and spoken English is essential. Knowledge of the local language(s) (e.g., Amharic, Tigrigna) is a strong asset.

SI WILL OFFER YOU :

**A salaried position:**

  
**According to experience,** starting from EUR 3080 gross per month (2800 base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 400.

SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment.

**Breaks:** During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every three months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked.

**Insurance package:** Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded.

**Living conditions:**

Guest House conditions :

\- There will be shared guesthouse both at the project and coordination during the visit.  
-Internet and telephone network : Available both in Addis and Adwa  
-Restaurant & social life: Restaurants are available in Addis and also Adwa :

\- Social life in Adwa is limited. All the basics food items and other are available but there is strict limitations and taxation to importation of food. Food in your luggage however is allowed and you can stock up on specials from home. Good quality chocolate, cereals and dried meat products can be hard to find and/or very expensive.

jobs.title: Spécialiste Clinique Rééducation en pédiatrie (troubles du développement) F/H
jobs.body:
Médecins Sans Frontières, association médicale humanitaire internationale créée en 1971, apporte une assistance médicale à des populations dont la vie est menacée : principalement en cas de conflits armés, mais aussi d'épidémies, de pandémies, de catastrophes naturelles ou encore d'exclusion des soins.

L'ouverture de ce poste est dans le cadre d'un remplacement permanent.

**Contexte**

La Fondation MSF a lancé mi 2023 un projet de développement de la rééducation au sein du mouvement MSF. Il a pour but d’amener un support et une expertise aux missions désireuses de développer leur offre de soins en rééducation dans quatre domaines (rééducation pédiatrique, en santé de la femme, en brulure et en appareillage assisté par la technologie 3D). Nous proposons pour ces différentes catégories de soins d’évaluer les besoins, de définir les objectifs, d’aider à la mise en place et au suivi de ces projets principalement sur des missions de MSF.

Dans le cadre du développement des activités de rééducation en pédiatrie, les activités du poste visent de manière non exhaustive les champs de la neuropédiatrie et des troubles du développement neuro-moteur de l’enfant dans des contextes de malnutrition et d’épidémie. Une approche transversale des autres champs de la rééducation pédiatrique est nécessaire afin de répondre à d’autres besoins terrains avec les autres spécialistes en rééducation.

Depuis 2023, les activités de rééducation pédiatrique supportées par la Fondation MSF se sont concentrées au Yemen, au Tchad et au Nigeria. D’autres projets peuvent être amenés à se développer.

**Activités principales**

Sous la responsabilité hiérarchique du Coordinateur du programme rééducation et en lien avec l’ensemble de l’équipe de La Fondation,

**Contribuer au développement opérationnel de la rééducation dans son domaine d’expertise :**

- Apporter son expertise clinique aux terrains / Coordinations pour leur permettre de prendre des décisions stratégiques opérationnelles concernant l’ensemble des projets présents et futurs en lien avec ses domaines d’expertises
- Participer à l’exploration, l’évaluation et la mise en place de projets en lien avec son expertise avec les différents terrains, coordinations et le Responsable du développement de la rééducation
- Assurer un support technique et clinique (sur le terrain ou à distance) pour répondre aux demandes du terrain dans le cadre de projet de rééducation de La Fondation MSF et de l’application des techniques qui lui sont attachées.

**Participer à la mise en place des outils et d’équipements cliniques et techniques sur le terrain pour le traitement et le suivi des patient·e·s :**

- Identifier et mettre en place les bilans et traitements standards réplicables sur le terrain permettant l’évaluation et le suivi du traitement des patient·e·s
- Identifier les équipements cliniques et techniques nécessaires à la mise en place du projet de rééducation et participer à leur commande en lien avec l’équipe de La Fondation
- Mettre en place ces équipements cliniques et techniques sur les terrains pour que les équipes locales puissent se les approprier
- Identifier et mettre en place différents outils d’organisation sur les terrains pour que les équipes locales puissent se les approprier
- Former et suivre les équipes à l’utilisation de ces outils cliniques, techniques et organisationnels (construction et animation de formation lors de visites terrain et/ou à distance).

**Assurer le suivi de qualité de soins des patient·e·s sur le terrain et à distance :**

- S’assurer que des soins de rééducation de qualité sont prodigués sur les terrains à travers la bonne application des outils techniques et cliniques
- S’assurer du suivi des patient·e·s en lien avec les équipes locales
- Être vigilant·e sur la qualité des soins de rééducation en dehors de son domaine d’expertise et alerter si nécessaire les spécialistes concernés et le Responsable du développement de la rééducation sur des besoins observés.

**Mettre en place des processus, livrables et savoirs de son activité de rééducation à MSF**

- Réaliser la veille scientifique et l’état des lieux dans son domaine de rééducation
- Définir les pratiques cliniques en lien avec ces activités avec les référents cliniques de MSF et le Responsable du développement de la rééducation
- Structurer les processus cliniques et techniques du projet (SoP, Training etc.)
- Créer de nouveau guides cliniques / techniques / Log de son activité pour permettre de la standardiser et faciliter sa réplicabilité
- Assurer un reporting mensuel de ses activités

**Participer à la collecte, l’organisation et l’analyse des données de rééducation des différents terrains :**

- Organiser la récolte et la gestion des données concernant les patients.es et leur suivi ainsi que les données propres aux projets de rééducation qui lui sont attachés.
- S’assurer avec la mission et le Responsable du développement de la rééducation de la protection de ces dernières via l’utilisation d’outils adaptés.
- Analyser les données de rééducation avec les missions et le responsable du développement de la rééducation
- Proposer et développer avec le Responsable du développement de la rééducation des projets de recherche et d’analyse.

**Participer à la mise en place de collaborations locales et internationales dans le cadre des missions ou du développement des activités de rééducation qui lui sont attachées.**

**Participer à la communication autour du projet et le promouvoir :**

- Participer à la communication interne, publique et scientifique du projet de manière orale, audio et écrite.
- Documenter le projet sur son orientation, ses méthodes, ses outils, ses équipements et plus largement sur son évolution sur les terrains.

Ce projet ayant débuté en Septembre 2023, certains éléments ont été initiés et nécessitent d’être poursuivis et réévalués au cas échéant.

Dans le cadre de l’activité pédiatrique, la/le spécialiste peut être amené à manager un profil de physiothérapeute qui aidera à la mise en place des différents projets.

**Profil recherché**

**Expérience et formation :**

- Diplôme de Kinésithérapie / physiothérapie
- Expérience de soins d’au moins 3 ans
- Expérience en ONG (expérience dans les terrains MSF est un atout)
- Expérience de soins dans le domaine des troubles du développement neuro-moteur de l’enfant.
- Diplômes Universitaires ou autres Certifications dans le domaine recherché sont un plus.

**Compétences :**

- Capacité d’adaptation et réactivité
- Esprit critique
- Capacité d’initiative / être force de proposition
- Flexibilité
- Solides compétences en communication pour la promotion de projets en interne et en externe
- Familiarité avec la documentation et l’établissement de rapports sur les activités.

**Langues :** niveau B2 minimum requis en Français et en anglais

**Aptitudes :**

- Dynamisme ; curiosité ; ingéniosité
- Organisation, autonomie, rigueur

**Conditions d'emploi**

**Statut :** CDI à temps plein. Poste cadre, idéalement basé à Paris avec déplacements sur les terrains MSF à prévoir.

**Localisation :** Le poste est idéalement basé à Paris. Toutefois, d'autres localisations pourront être étudiées en fonction des besoins du poste et du profil du/de la candidat(e).

**Rémunération et avantages (pour un poste basé à Paris) :**

- 47,8 K€ brut annuel sur 13 mois
- 22 jours de RTT par an
- Télétravail selon les règles en vigueur chez MSF (2 j/sem.)
- Mutuelle prise en charge à 100%
- Titres-restaurant de 12€ (prise en charge à 60% par MSF).
- Prise en charge à 50% de l'abonnement de transport en commun (hebdomadaire, mensuel ou annuel) ou indemnité kilométrique vélo (0,25€ par km, limité à 450€ par an).

**Pour un poste basé en dehors de la France :** *La rémunération et les avantages seront déterminés conformément à la grille salariale et aux dispositions en vigueur dans le pays ou la localisation concernée.*

*A MSF, nous valorisons la diversité et cherchons à avoir un environnement de travail inclusif et accessible. Nous encourageons toutes les personnes qui possèdent les qualifications requises à postuler, indépendamment de leur origine ethnique, nationale ou culturelle, de leur âge, de leur sexe, de leur orientation sexuelle, de leurs convictions, de leur handicap ou d'autres aspects de leur identité.*

**Date limite de dépôt de candidatures :** 28 octobre 2026

jobs.title: Senior Director, Housing Disaster Resilience and Recovery
jobs.body:
**Opportunity Type:**

Regular

**Summary:**

The Senior Director of Housing Disaster Resilience and Recovery will lead and coordinate efforts to strengthen the housing resilience in communities where Habitat works in the context of disasters and conflict. Where appropriate the work will be done through the implementation of Habitat’s Pathway to Permanence approach that focuses on the connection between short-term and long-term interventions. The Senior Director supervises a team of disaster risk reduction and recovery specialists and works in collaboration with global and regional departments. The role involves leading the Housing Disaster Resilience and Recovery strategy, program design, technical assistance for the network, procuring funding in coordination with other departments, and engaging with external stakeholders.

**Key Responsibilities:**

- Lead the Housing Disaster Resilience and Recovery team, including line management, performance evaluation and professional development.
- Further develop and implement the strategic plan of HDRR in alignment with Habitat’s global strategy.
- Support the organization increasing capacity in the articulation of housing resilience and recovery in disasters and conflict by developing standards, systems, guidelines and monitoring and learning mechanisms.
- Consult and contribute with US and Area Office Program teams as needed for program design and implementation, align approaches, and share knowledge.
- Collaborate with and support other departments to incorporate housing resilience, and disaster risk reduction components into long-term programs and projects.
- Provide coordination between headquarters functional units and field operation activities in the different geographies where the organization is operational. This includes, levelling, supporting fundraising, supporting reporting to donors, monitoring and evaluation, and being the spokesperson as needed.
- Lead the formation and functioning of communities of practices in areas related to this role
- Lead and collaborate in the areas of research and advocacy for housing resilience, disaster risk reduction, post-disaster interventions.
- Identify and pursue institutional and private funding opportunities in coordination with fundraising departments of HFHI.
- Oversee the management of projects and programs under the HDRR department and ensure compliance with grant requirements.
- Lead HFHI’s active engagement and leadership in disaster risk reduction and housing resilience fora, alliances and coalitions, connecting the organization to peer agencies and donor networks in the sector
- Manage the team budget.

**Minimum Requirements:**

**Education**:

- Bachelor’s in urban planning, public policy, civil engineering, environmental science or field related.
- Graduate studies in resilience planning, disaster and conflict management, international development or related discipline

**Years of Related Experience**:

- Minimum of 7 years of experience in disaster risk reduction, community resilience, housing development or related field.
- Proven track record of managing complex projects, including implementing programs or projects funded by state or multi-lateral members of the International Cooperation.
- Experience of managing projects in collaboration with partner organizations, and remote management in insecure environments.
- Experience in effectively managing and leading diverse, globally distributed leaders in a federated network in the international development/humanitarian sector.
- Minimum of 5 years working internationally in at least 2 countries in the Majority World/ Global South, and familiarity working with offices in the Global North for citizens of Majority World countries.
- Experience, knowledge and commitment integrating gender and social inclusion in programs and projects

**Knowledge, Skills & Abilities**:

- Strong understanding of resilience frameworks, housing policy frameworks, humanitarian principles and International Humanitarian Law, disaster risk reduction frameworks, and environmental regulatory frameworks
- Excellent project management skills, including budgeting, planning, and reporting.
- Ability to analyze data, assess risks, and to learn through it to develop innovative solutions.
- Strong interpersonal and communication skills, cultural-awareness, and the ability to engage diverse stakeholders.

**Active support of HFHI Values:**  
\- We are part of something bigger than ourselves  
\- We do what's right, even when it is difficult or unpopular  
\- We take personal responsibility for Habitat's mission

**Safeguarding**  
HFHI requires that all employees take seriously their ethical responsibilities to safeguarding our intended beneficiaries, their communities, and all those with whom we work. Managers at all levels have responsibilities to support and develop systems that create and maintain an environment that prevents harassment, sexual exploitation and abuse, safeguards the rights of beneficiaries and community members (especially children), and promotes the implementation of Habitat for Humanity’s code of conduct.

**Hiring Range:**

The actual salary offered for this role will be based on a variety of factors, including location, internal equity and the candidate’s qualifications and professional experience. HFHI offers a competitive, comprehensive benefits package that varies by country and typically includes vacation leave, sick leave, personal days, health insurance options, retirement plan contributions and life insurance. For work locations in the US, the hiring range for this position is:

$134,200.00

$199,600 USD

**About Us:**

Habitat for Humanity, founded in 1976, is a global, Christian-based nonprofit organization that grew out of an intentionally multi-racial community in rural Georgia. Seeking to put God’s love into action, Habitat brings together people of all faiths and people of no faith to build homes, communities and hope. Working alongside each other, we help families and individuals build and improve places to call home and achieve the strength, stability and self-reliance they need to build better lives for themselves. Habitat seeks individuals who have a willingness to affirm these principles and values.

At Habitat for Humanity International, we are compelled by our Koinonia roots to put God’s love for all into action and pursue housing equity and opportunity by bringing all people together to build community and drive impact. We strive to build a culture rooted in learning, accountability and trust, attracting and retaining mission-driven talent reflective of the global communities we serve.

**Equal Opportunity Employer Statement:**

As an equal opportunity employer, we realize our success depends on courageously committing to being a workplace where all staff feel safe, welcome, visible, respected, supported and valued, and building a workforce that reflects a variety of lived experiences, backgrounds and perspectives, in which every person experiences dignity and respect.

**Habitat for Humanity International is an E-Verify employer.**

jobs.title: République Démocratique du Congo : Coordinateur.rice de Zone – Uvira
source: Agency for Technical Cooperation and Development
jobs.body:
**CDD | 6 mois | Mi-janvier 2027**

## Acted

***Qui sommes-nous***

Acted travaille avec 19 millions de personnes dans 43 pays au carrefour de l’humanitaire, du développement, et des programmes climatiques et environnementaux. Grâce à une connaissance poussée des contextes et l’adoption de technologies émergentes, nous sauvons des vies, allégeons les souffrances, et protégeons et restaurons notre planète. Travaillant avec un écosystème croissant de partenaires locaux, nationaux et internationaux, nous poursuivons un objectif commun : un monde 3Zéro : Zéro Exclusion, Zéro Carbone, Zéro Pauvreté.

***Qui cherchons-nous***

Vous apportez les compétences clefs attendues d’un travailleur humanitaire et de développement, mais également une conscience climatique et environnementale active, et vous pouvez naviguez les défis qui émergent lorsque les souffrances environnementale et humaine se rencontrent. Vous avez l’esprit entrepreneurial : vous décelez les opportunités, connectez les points, adaptez votre approche aux différents environnements, et vous prenez des risques mesurés dans la poursuite de résultats. Vous alliez les principes au pragmatisme, et l’ambition à l’humilité.

## Acted République Démocratique du Congo

La République Démocratique du Congo fait face à une crise humanitaire prolongée, marquée par la persistance des conflits armés, des déplacements massifs de populations, des chocs climatiques et des chocs épidémiques récurrents, tels que le choléra, le mpox ou la rougeole. Ces dynamiques combinées affectent durablement les conditions de vie des populations déplacées, retournées et hôtes, en particulier dans les provinces de l’Est et certaines zones de l’Ouest du pays.

Dans ce contexte, Acted intervient principalement dans les provinces du Sud-Kivu, Nord-Kivu, Tanganyika, Nord-Ubangi et Sud-Ubangi, à travers des projets financés notamment par le Department of State / US, ECHO, FCDO, SDC, le Fonds Humanitaire, ainsi que le CDCS, afin de répondre aux besoins humanitaires immédiats et aux vulnérabilités persistantes des populations les plus affectées. Afin de renforcer la couverture et la complémentarité de ses interventions, Acted intervient en coordination avec plusieurs partenaires opérationnels, et est membre de consortiums humanitaires.

Cette coordination permet à Acted de mettre en œuvre des réponses d’urgence rapides et multisectorielles pour couvrir les besoins vitaux liés aux conflits, aux déplacements forcés, aux catastrophes naturelles et aux crises sanitaires. Les interventions portent notamment sur l’assistance alimentaire, les abris et articles ménagers essentiels, l’Eau, Hygiène et Assainissement (EHA), la gestion et coordination des sites (CCCM) ainsi que l’éducation en situation d’urgence, avec une attention particulière portée, dès le premier kilomètre humanitaire, à la protection et à la dignité des personnes vulnérables. Au Sud-Kivu, Acted est par ailleurs un acteur clé du Mécanisme de Réponse Rapide (RRM), contribuant à des réponses rapides et coordonnées en lien avec les déplacements de populations et aux chocs soudains.

En parallèle, Acted développe des interventions visant à renforcer la résilience des communautés, à travers le soutien aux moyens d’existence, la relance agricole, la sécurité alimentaire et la relance économique locale, afin de réduire la vulnérabilité face aux chocs récurrents.

Acted apporte également un appui structurant aux organisations de la société civile (OSC) en renforçant leurs capacités organisationnelles et opérationnelles. Cet accompagnement inclut l’appui à la structuration des initiatives locales ainsi que la mise en place de mécanismes de financement en cascade, permettant aux OSC de développer des activités directement liées aux problématiques locales et aux priorités identifiées par les communautés.

Enfin, Acted intègre progressivement dans ses programmes des approches sensibles à l’environnement, visant à la préservation des écosystèmes et des aires protégées, à la réduction de l’empreinte environnementale des interventions et à la promotion de solutions à faible émission de carbone. À travers l’appui aux communautés, Acted encourage le développement d’activités génératrices de revenus durables et d’une économie locale plus verte, contribuant à la protection des ressources naturelles tout en renforçant les moyens d’existence.

## Rôle et responsabilités principales

Le.a coordinateur.rice de zone représente Acted vis à vis des autorités locales, des bailleurs, des populations bénéficiaires et des autres acteurs clefs.

Le.a coordinateur.rice est membre de l’équipe de management, il/elle garantit la qualité du programme et sa mise en œuvre opérationnelle, ainsi que son déploiement là où c’est approprié et réalisable, il/elle assure un fort rôle de représentation. Le.a coordinateur.rice supervise directement les responsables de projet en contrôlant que les projets et les programmes sont adaptés aux besoins des bénéficiaires et qu’ils sont mis en œuvre en accord avec la stratégie globale d’Acted , avec les orientations du bailleur. Une fois les plans de travail et les budgets validés, le coordinateur de zone supervise également au jour le jour les opérations et la sécurité dans la zone concernée.

***Principales responsabilités***

1\. Positionnement

- Analyse contextuelle
- Stratégie de mise en œuvre
- Réseau, positionnement et représentation générale
- Développement de propositions :
- Plaidoyer
- Promotion des organisations sœurs d’Acted

2\. Management et coordination interne

- Gestion d’équipe
- Coordination interne

3\. Suivi de la mise en œuvre des projets

- Suivi de la mise en œuvre des projets
- Contrôle qualité des projets
- Management des partenaires

4\. Management FLATS

- Gestion Finances
- Gestion logistique et IT
- Gestion administrative et RH
- Gestion transparence/conformité
- Gestion sécurité

## Qualifications et compétences requises

- Formation en développement international, les opérations d’urgence, les programmes humanitaires etc. ;
- Expérience approfondie de la gestion de projets dans des programmes d’urgence et/ou de développement ;
- Des compétences en gestion de base sont préférables (RH, finances, logistique) ;
- Au moins quatre ans d’expérience professionnelle pertinente, comprenant de préférence la gestion de la sécurité ;
- Capacités avérées en matière de leadership et de gestion d’équipe requises ;
- Capacité à travailler sous pression ;
- Solides compétences en négociation et en relations interpersonnelles, et flexibilité ;

## Termes de référence

Pour plus d'informations sur le poste, [cliquez ici ](https://www.acted.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/ac-uvira-rdc-2026.pdf).

## Conditions

- Salaire défini par la grille des salaires Acted en fonction du niveau d’études, de l’expertise, du niveau de sécurité et du niveau d’expérience : entre 3600 et 3700€ net mensuel (avant impôts sur le revenu)
- Indemnité mensuelle de frais de vie 300$
- Logement en guesthouse et nourriture pris en charge par Acted
- Sécurité sociale, mutuelle (MSH) et assistance rapatriement (SOS International) pris en charge par Acted
- Transport vers la mission et billet retour totalement pris en charge tous les 6 mois (vers l’adresse spécifiée sur le contrat de travail)
- Frais de visa pris en charge par Acted
- R&R tous les 3 mois (billet d’avion pris en charge jusqu’à 500$ + indemnité supplémentaire de 200$)
- Une semaine de préparation au départ comprenant 4 jours de formation sécurité en immersion
- Possibilité d’avoir un appel de 30minutes avec un.e consultant.e en fiscalité
- Soutien psychologique (rendez-vous avec un.e professionnel.le)

jobs.title: COORDINATOR - UNITED NATIONS UNIVERSITY (UNU) HUB [FIXED-TERM PROJECT POSITION]
source: International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development
jobs.body:
## Position overview

ICIMOD is seeking a Hub Coordinator for its newly established United Nations University (UNU) Hub at ICIMOD.

The UNU Hub at ICIMOD is a newly established collaborative platform that advances research, education, and partnerships to strengthen the resilience of mountain communities in the HKH region facing climate and socio-economic change. Building on the long-standing collaboration between ICIMOD; United Nations University Institute for Environment and Human Security (UNU-EHS); Eurac Research, Italy; and the Himalayan University Consortium (HUC), the Hub supports the sustainable management of mountain social–ecological systems, particularly in the HKH. It aims to generate knowledge, foster innovation, and develop a new generation of mountain researchers, practitioners, and leaders. Through research, capacity building, outreach, and advocacy, the Hub promotes evidence-based solutions and regional cooperation for sustainable and climate-resilient mountain development. The focus topics of the first years will be designed as:

- mountain climate risk and adaptation,
- sustainable management of natural resources in mountains, and
- mountain habitability, local knowledge systems and intangible heritage.

The Hub Coordinator will be responsible for the strategic, programmatic, research, and financial coordination of the UNU Hub at ICIMOD. The role includes developing and implementing the Hub’s strategy, leading fundraising efforts and project proposal development, and ensuring sustainable funding. The coordinator will supervise the Hub team; coordinate the Hub steering board, advisory board, and management board meetings; manage technical and financial reporting to partner institutions; and serve as the primary liaison among ICIMOD, UNU-EHS, Eurac Research, and HUC to ensure effective collaboration and the delivery of the Hub’s objectives.

## Person specification/competencies

\[Experience, knowledge, and skills\]

### **ESSENTIAL**

- A Master's degree, preferably a PhD, in a relevant field.
- At least 5 years of project/programme/hub management experience.
- At least 3 years of experience in leading and coordinating large and complex research programmes, including managing partnerships, leading multisectoral coordination, project development, donor liaison, managing interdisciplinary teams, monitoring and reporting, and complex budget management.
- Excellent interpersonal, teamworking and communication skills, both written and spoken, comfortable working with and to all levels, internal and external.
- Excellent communication and report writing skills (in English) and analytical skills with an ability to understand and contextualise research.
- Respect for ICIMOD’s and UN core values

### **PREFERRED**

- Prior work experience with the UN or any international organisation.
- Familiarity with HKH, its social, economic, and ecological context
- Ability to travel within and outside the HKH region.

## Duration

Three-year fixed-term project contract, with a six-month probation period. There is a possibility of an extension, subject to performance, need for the position, and the Hub’s future funding levels.

## Remuneration

This is a Specialist/Senior Officer position at ICIMOD with a competitive salary and benefits. Salary comprises basic salary, provident fund, and family/post adjustment allowance. We offer a comprehensive benefits package which includes insurances (medical, life and accidental), children allowance and children’s education grant for a maximum of 2 children below 18 years of age, severance pay, paid leave (30 holidays and 10 public holidays per year) and day care facility.

For expatriates, there is a tax exemption in Nepal; they are responsible for paying their home country’s taxes. Expatriate staff are entitled to housing allowance, annual home leave ticket, shipment of personal effects, and an installation and repatriation allowance.

## ICIMOD’s core values

Our core values are integrity, neutrality, relevance, inclusiveness, openness, and ambition. These values express our culture and are central to the guiding beliefs and principles of our work and behaviour. Our core values will lie at the heart of ICIMOD operations and delivery. They will underpin everything we do and frame how we work with our partners. They reflect our founding intentions and the balances we seek to hold, while equipping ourselves for the future.

## UN Core Values and Behaviours

**Values:**

- **Inclusion** - Take action to create an environment of dignity and respect for all, regardless of age, culture, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, gender expression, geography, grade, language, nationality, racial identity, religion, sex, sex characteristics, sexual orientation, social origin or any other aspect of identity.
- **Integrity** - Act ethically, demonstrating the standards of conduct of the United Nations and taking prompt action in case of witnessing unprofessional or unethical behaviour, or any other breach of UN standards.
- **Humility** - Demonstrate self-awareness and willingness to learn from others.
- **Humanity** - Act according to the purposes of the United Nations: peace, dignity and equality on a healthy planet.

**Behaviours:**

- **Connect and Collaborate** - Build positive relationships with others to advance the work of the United Nations and work coherently as One UN
- **Analyse and Plan** - Seek out and use data from a wide range of sources to understand problems, inform decision-making, propose evidence-based solutions and plan action
- **Deliver Results with Positive Impact** - Hold oneself and others accountable for delivering results and making a positive difference to the people and causes that the United Nations serves
- **Learn and Develop** - Pursue own learning and development and contribute to the learning and development of others
- **Adapt and Innovate** - Demonstrate flexibility, agility and the ability to think and act in novel ways

## Diversity, equity, inclusion, and safeguarding

ICIMOD’s human resource selection process is based on the qualifications and competence of the applicants. As an employer, ICIMOD is committed to promoting diversity, equity, and inclusion, and offers equal opportunities to applicants from all backgrounds and walks of life, including but not limited to gender, age, national origin, religion, race, caste, ethnicity, sexual orientation, disability, or social status. ICIMOD strongly encourages applications from all eligible applicants, especially women, from all parts of the HKH region.

ICIMOD is dedicated to establishing and upholding a safe and nurturing work environment, where all its employees can participate fully and meaningfully without fear of violence, harassment, exploitation, or intimidation. Any type of abuse or harassment, including sexual misconduct \[including child abuse\], by our staff, representatives, or stakeholders is not condoned or tolerated.

jobs.title: Casework Supervisor
jobs.body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

***This position has an end date of September 30, 2027.***

**Job Overview:**   
The Casework Supervisor manages staff providing direct client services across the Program for Initial Resettlement (PIR) and Refugee Social Service (RSS) case management program. The Casework Supervisor plans programming, coordinates service delivery, supervises a team, ensures program goals are met, and satisfies budgetary, compliance, and reporting responsibilities for the assigned portfolio. This position is based in Louisville, Kentucky, with regular on-site presence within the office.

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Staff Supervision responsibilities**

- Lead and develop direct service staff through facilitation of team meetings and individual supervision, including coaching and goal setting.
- Liaise regularly with HQ colleagues for guidance, case consultations, direct financial assistance, and other support as needed, and share relevant information with the casework team.
- Cultivate a respectful and supportive environment for team members and clients.
- Recruit, train, and manage the team in accordance with IRC’s People Manager Standards.
- Carry out timely, professional interventions to ensure responsive, appropriate, and client-centered service delivery.
- Train direct reports on using IRC systems such as Integra, ETO, and IRIS.
- Representing IRC in public, professional, and governmental fora as needed.
- Other duties as assigned.

**Service Delivery**

- Guide PIR program implementation and ensure all required services are completed in a timely manner.
- Assign cases to caseworkers and manage timely provision of services including airport pickups, provision of safe, sanitary, and affordable housing, home visits, school enrollment, domestic health assessments, and connection to community resources as applicable.
- Supervise the RSS Case Management Program, including staff referrals, connection of clients to services, and tracking client participation and progress
- Ensure follow-up on all necessary services, including application to public benefits as applicable, referrals to immigration services, applications for Supplemental Security Income (SSI), and medical and mental health needs.
- Provide oversight so each client receives at least one meaningful interaction every 30 days during their service period.
- Ensure case closeout procedures are followed once a client has reached the goals of their program.

**Partnership Building**

- Manage relationships with property owners and managers to expand access to sources of affordable housing.
- Collaborate with colleagues to encourage timely internal referrals for additional services, such as employment, immigration services, and intensive case management.
- Identify and maintain relationships with local government and community-based organizations to connect clients with necessary benefits and services.
- Develop relationships with community resources such as shelters for temporary housing, domestic violence shelters, mental health providers, and medical specialists.
- Develop and maintain vendor relationships that create budgetary savings and improve efficiency.

**Documentation, Reporting and Contract Compliance**

- Ensure that case file documentation is maintained in compliance with contract requirements.
- Guide the timely implementation of program updates as needed.
- Liaise with the HQ colleagues to ensure thorough understanding of program guidelines and disseminate guidelines to the direct service team.
- Review data to meet donor reporting requirements.
- Assist with the preparation for all monitoring visits, including IRC, the Kentucky Office for Refugees (KOR), and the Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR).
- Monitor program execution to ensure compliance with all funding requirements; communicate program needs to the management team.

**Job Requirements:**

**Education:**

- Bachelor’s degree is strongly preferred, preferably in social work or related field

**Work Experience:**

- Minimum two to three years of experience implementing domestic refugee resettlement or similar programs
- Experience supervising, supporting, and training staff strongly preferred
- Experience in program management and responsibility for budget management preferred

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:**

- Familiarity with Integra, IRIS, SMART, and Efforts to Outcomes (ETO) strongly preferred.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications
- Ability to prioritize and manage time effectively
- Demonstrated ability to work effectively as a team member in a multicultural environment
- Excellent written and oral communication skills in English; proficiency in a language spoken by client populations is a plus
- Valid driver’s license, reliable access to a vehicle with current insurance, and the ability to travel regularly throughout the service delivery area

**Working Environment:**

- A combination of a standard office environment and ‘field’ time in and around the service delivery area to perform the above-outlined responsibilities.
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.

**Compensation:** ($$59,962.5 - annually). Compensation is based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements”.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

jobs.title: Consultancy for the Development of a Facilitation Guide and Facilitation of Trainings for Beach Management Unit (BMU) Members in Kwale County
jobs.body:
## **The full Request for Proposals (RFP) document is available at the following link:** [**https://drive.google.com/drive/u/1/folders/17XdKj9sJdsiyUeuwm7_8UrN15OJ6Zo97**](https://drive.google.com/drive/u/1/folders/17XdKj9sJdsiyUeuwm7_8UrN15OJ6Zo97)

## **About CEFA**

**CEFA** - European Committee for Training and Agriculture (Comitato Europeo per la Formazione e l’Agricoltura) is an Italian Non-Governmental Organisation established in 1972 and active in countries across Africa, Latin America and Eastern Europe. CEFA’s medium- and long-term interventions in the agricultural, environmental and human rights sectors focus on the sustainable development of communities, achieved by involving local counterparts and promoting the active participation of beneficiaries.

## Project Summary

The project **AGROBLUE - Promoting Sustainable Agriculture and Blue Economy in Kenya** is a 36-month initiative implemented in four sub-counties (Galole, Tana Delta, Msambweni and Lunga Lunga) within Tana River and Kwale Counties, Kenya. The project is implemented by a consortium of partners with extensive experience in resilient agricultural models and the blue economy, led by Action Against Hunger (ACF) in collaboration with CEFA, MWARP and Politecnico di Milano. The initiative works closely with the Ministry of Agriculture and the Ministry of Health to ensure institutional sustainability and long-term impact.

The project aims to increase food security, income and resilience to food crises through an integrated, climate-smart and gender-sensitive approach. It addresses barriers such as low productivity, high post-harvest losses and the limited economic participation of women by providing farmers and fishermen with the tools, technologies and knowledge needed to diversify their livelihoods and increase their incomes, while protecting natural ecosystems. The project works across three result areas:

- Increasing access for small-scale farmers and artisanal fishermen to products and services for climate-resilient production and fishing systems, and to community practices that prevent ecosystem degradation;
- Increasing access of farming and fishing families in rural and coastal areas to technical and financial services, infrastructure and knowledge to sustainably manage supply chains that add value to their food production, in order to increase and diversify their income;
- Sensitising communities on nutritional needs, with a focus on vulnerable groups such as women and children, to improve access to and consumption of diverse, nutritious food.

Within the project, CEFA works in the fisheries and beekeeping components, targeting farmers’ groups and Beach Management Units (BMUs) through training and the provision of equipment. The intervention adopts a value chain strengthening approach covering production, post-harvest handling and marketing.

## Objectives of the Consultancy

The objectives of the consultancy are:
