- The development of a **facilitation guide** covering practical offshore fishing techniques and best practices; basic navigation, including the use of navigation equipment and the interpretation of weather and sea conditions; maritime safety, emergency preparedness and response procedures; sustainable management of marine resources, including marine ecosystem conservation, pollution prevention, overfishing and the impacts of climate change; and fisheries data collection and analysis, including data on fishing fleets, fishers, fishing gear, fishing effort and landings. The guide will provide practical guidance and standardised messages to support the delivery of the planned training sessions.
- The delivery of **four training topics, through five trainings and 18 sessions in total**, to BMU members, including fishermen, boat owners, members of BMU executive committees and fish traders, through refresher and cascading trainings, to strengthen technical skills, maritime safety practices, environmental awareness and the capacity to collect and use fisheries data.

## Timeline and Duration of the Consultancy

The consultancy covers a total of **37 days**:

- 10 days for the design and preparation of the training sessions and the drafting and finalisation of the facilitation guide;
- 24 days for the facilitation of the trainings, divided among the training sessions as set out under Methodology below;
- 3 days for the drafting and submission of the final consultancy report.

The consultancy shall commence in **November 2026** and will extend over a period of four months, concluding in **February 2027**. The allocation and scheduling of the training days will be agreed with the CEFA team according to the availability of participants, the project implementation timeline and the logistical requirements of each session, within the overall number of consultancy days established in the contract.

## Methodology

**Participants**

The trainings will be delivered to members of Beach Management Units, notably:

- Fishermen;
- Members of BMU executive committees (e.g. chairperson, secretary, treasurer);
- Boat owners and individuals involved in eco-tourism activities;
- Fish traders and dealers.

The total number of participants across all trainings will be **501**, drawn from **three** BMUs already selected in Msambweni and Lunga Lunga Sub-Counties.

**Content and Design of the Trainings**

BMU members will participate in five trainings covering, progressively, offshore fishing, marine resource management, maritime safety, and fisheries data collection and analysis:

- **Refresher Training on Offshore Fishing:** 20 members from each of the three BMUs will participate in a two-day training per BMU. The training will focus on practical offshore fishing techniques, navigation, interpretation of weather and sea conditions, and basic safety practices during fishing operations. One practical **at-sea session** is planned as part of the two-day training for each BMU. CEFA will provide the boat and all necessary safety equipment.
- **Refresher Training on Offshore Fishing (Restitution Session):** A one-day feedback and cascading session on offshore fishing will follow, reaching 210 BMU members (70 per BMU) through three sessions, so that the trained participants can pass on the knowledge acquired to a wider group of BMU members. The trained BMU members will deliver the cascading sessions under the supervision of the Consultant.
- **Environmental Impacts and Conflict Reduction in the Use of Marine Resources:** 20 members from each of the three BMUs will participate in a one-day training per BMU. The training will address marine ecosystems and their conservation, pollution and its impact on marine resources, overfishing and sustainable fisheries management, climate change and its effects on marine ecosystems, and approaches to reducing conflicts over the use of marine resources. It will also include a module on co-management areas and co-management plans for sustainable use.
- **Maritime Safety Training for Offshore Fishing:** 50 members from each of the three BMUs will participate in a one-day training, delivered through six sessions in total (two per BMU), each targeting 25 fishermen. The training will focus on the risks of illegal fishing, safety procedures, safe use of protective gear, safe operations at sea, risk prevention, emergency preparedness and response, and appropriate action in case of accidents or other emergencies during offshore fishing.
- **Fisheries Data Collection and Analysis:** 7 members from each BMU will participate in a two-day training delivered through three sessions, for a total of 21 participants. The training will cover data collection methodologies, data sources and basic data analysis, with a focus on fisheries information such as fleet characteristics, number of fishers, fishing gear, fishing effort and fish landings.

## Safeguarding and Do No Harm

The Consultant shall comply with CEFA’s safeguarding, PSEAH (Protection from Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment), Code of Conduct and data protection requirements. Personal data collected from participants, including attendance lists and pre- and post-training assessments, shall be handled in line with the Data Protection Act, 2019 and used only for the purposes of this assignment.

## Management and Implementation Responsibilities

The Consultant will report directly to the CEFA Project Manager and the CEFA Project Officer in charge of AGROBLUE implementation.

The Consultant will be responsible for their own insurance during the contract period, and CEFA will not be responsible for any injury or damage incurred during the assignment. The Consultant will also meet their own communication and incidental costs. The Financial Proposal must include all anticipated expenses, including travel to and from the assignment sites, local transport in Kwale County, meals and accommodation.

## Qualifications of the Consultant

**Essential**

- A minimum of a bachelor’s degree in Fisheries, Marine Resources, Aquaculture or a related field from a reputable institution;
- Relevant professional experience in fisheries development, sustainable fisheries management, offshore fishing, marine ecosystem conservation and/or capacity building of fishing communities and BMUs, preferably at least 7 years;
- Demonstrated experience in training fishermen and/or BMU members in the thematic areas of this assignment;
- Strong participatory training and facilitation skills, and good report-writing skills;
- Ability to deliver training in Kiswahili and English.

**Desirable**

- Previous experience working with fishing communities on the Kenyan coast, particularly in Kwale County.

jobs.title: Digital Development and Connectivity Program Specialist
jobs.body:
***Candidates must be authorized and able to work daily in Bogotá.***

**Position Summary**

The Digital Development and Connectivity Program Specialist serves as the Foreign Assistance Unit's (FAU’s) technical adviser for digital-infrastructure and connectivity programming across South America. The position provides technical analysis and recommendations to support Government officials in identifying, assessing, and structuring U.S. Government-funded digital development programs that advance U.S. foreign-policy and national-security objectives and respond to partner-country priorities. The portfolio may include information and communication technologies (ICT) deployment (fiber, wireless, satellite, and last-mile connectivity), digital inclusion strategies, cybersecurity considerations for critical digital infrastructure, and broadband/connectivity expansion planning.

The incumbent reports to the FAU’s Programs Team Lead and translate digital connectivity needs into technically credible and implementable program designs. Responsibilities include preparing technical scopes of work; contributing to program-design and acquisition or assistance documents; reviewing proposals, market studies, network designs, specifications, cost estimates, schedules, and other technical products; and providing input to the FAU on technical alternatives, implementation risks, project readiness, sustainability, and operations and maintenance considerations. The Specialist collaborates with other FAU technical and program personnel to ensure that digital infrastructure investments are appropriately incorporated into sector-specific programs.

Drawing from practices used across the U.S. Department of State and other U.S. Government agencies, the incumbent provides technical analysis and recommendations to support programming aligned with the America First foreign policy framework, including economic security, strategic competition, trusted and secure digital infrastructure, supply chain resilience, and partnerships that reinforce U.S. interests. The salary will be commensurate with an FSN 11 position within Colombia.

**Major Duties and Responsibilities**

**1. Strategic Digital Infrastructure Program Development (35%)**

Supports the identification, assessment, and design of USG-funded digital-connectivity programs that advance U.S. foreign-policy and national-security objectives. Responsibilities include:

- Identifies potential digital-development programming opportunities based on USG priorities, partner-country needs, connectivity gaps, existing investments, and regional market developments.
- Supports programs involving ICT infrastructure deployment, broadband and last-mile connectivity expansion, digital inclusion initiatives, secure network architecture, and cybersecurity-conscious infrastructure design.
- Translates connectivity needs and policy objectives into technically credible, feasible, and sustainable program concepts.
- Supports the development of technical scopes and statements of work, program descriptions, acquisition and assistance planning documents, budgets, implementation approaches, and other program-design products.
- Develop recommendations regarding the technical scope and requirements for market assessments, network design studies, cybersecurity risk assessments, digital-inclusion needs analyses, and other project-preparation activities.
- Provides technical recommendations regarding requirements, performance standards, implementation assumptions, schedules, cost parameters, and risk-mitigation approaches in collaboration with relevant FAU personnel.
- Assesses project readiness, technical feasibility, implementation risks, operational requirements, and the capacity needed to operate and maintain proposed digital infrastructure.
- Incorporates sustainability, commercial viability, and operations and maintenance considerations throughout program design.
- Coordinates technical, programmatic, procurement, financial, monitoring, and stakeholder inputs into coherent digital-development programs.
- Supports the adaptation, expansion, or modernization of existing connectivity programs when performance findings, policy changes, or market conditions warrant revised approaches.
- Identifies technical capability gaps and provides input on potential needs for short-term telecommunications, network engineering, or cybersecurity expertise.

**2. Technical Review and Quality Assurance (30%)**

Provides technical review and quality-assurance support for proposed and ongoing digital-development activities. Responsibilities include:

- Reviews proposals, market studies, network designs, technical specifications, pricing structures, cost estimates, schedules, work plans, and other technical submissions.
- Conducts market research and performs technical and commercial analysis of proposals for pricing, competitiveness, and commercial viability relative to comparable connectivity solutions.
- Conducts technical assessments of proposedapproaches to evaluate if they are credible, implementable, appropriately scaled, priced, and responsive to program requirements.
- Evaluates design assumptions, technology choices, deployment methodologies, energy and energy storage requirements, equipment specifications, sequencing, and operations and maintenance requirements.
- Reviews technical products for consistency with applicable host-country, U.S., and international standards, including relevant cybersecurity and data-protection standards.
- Compares technical and commercial alternatives and provides recommendations to the FAU on their relative feasibility, risks, lifecycle implications, and expected performance.
- Identifies technical gaps and potential implementation risks—including cybersecurity vulnerabilities—and recommends corrective actions or additional analysis.
- Reviews quality-assurance and quality-control approaches, testing requirements, commissioning arrangements, maintenance plans, and other measures necessary to support reliable digital-infrastructure performance.
- Provides technical input during proposal reviews and other procurement or assistance processes, as requested and consistent with applicable procedures and conflict-of-interest safeguards.
- **Conducts technical reviews for** GORs (Grant Officer’s Representatives), CORs (Contract Officer’s Representatives), and FAU leadership on whether technical products appear responsive to applicable requirements while preserving formal acceptance authority for designated USG officials.
- Confirms that designs, certifications, and other regulated technical products are prepared or approved by appropriately qualified professionals when required.

**3. Digital Infrastructure Portfolio Planning and Strategic Analysis (25%)**

Under Programs Team Lead guidance, provides analysis and planning support to guide the FAU's digital-development and connectivity portfolio. Responsibilities include:

- Maintains visibility over proposed, active, and emerging digital-connectivity initiatives supported by the FAU.
- Develops and maintains a digital-development opportunity pipeline that captures project status, technical-preparation needs, strategic relevance, principal risks, and required next steps.
- Provides analysis and recommendations to inform prioritization of large strategic connectivity investments and community-level digital-inclusion activities based on policy relevance, feasibility, readiness, and potential results.
- Conducts technical assessments of how individual digital-infrastructure activities contribute to broader economic-security, digital-inclusion, or strategic-competition objectives, including trusted-vendor and secure-supply-chain considerations.
- Identifies opportunities to connect digital-connectivity investments with complementary programming managed by other FAU specialists, including training, sustainability, and wraparound services needed to achieve public policy goals alongside commercial viability.
- Identifies recurring technical and management risks across the digital-infrastructure portfolio and recommends improvements to future program design.
- Captures and shares lessons from completed and ongoing activities to strengthen technical quality, implementation, and sustainability.
- Prepares technical briefing materials, analytical memoranda, talking points, and recommendations for FAU and Embassy leadership.

**4. Program Quality, Monitoring, and Reporting (15%)**

Supports GORs and CORs in monitoring assigned programs and awards, and assessing their continued strategic relevance and performance. Responsibilities include:

- Reviews program reports, work plans, technical deliverables, deployment updates, schedules, cost information, and performance data as requested by the responsible GOR or COR .
- Collaborates with the Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning Specialist to gather, validate, analyze, and synthesize information from assigned programs.
- Participates alongside the responsible GOR or COR in site visits, monitoring activities, portfolio reviews, and meetings with implementers, contractors, government counterparts, private-sector partners, beneficiaries, and other stakeholders.
- Analyzes implementation progress and identifies technical, quality, cost, schedule, management, sustainability, cybersecurity, and operations and maintenance concerns.
- Reviews information on network quality, testing, contractor quality-control processes, security posture, commissioning, and readiness for intended use, as applicable.
- Provides recommendations to GORs and CORs when independent technical review, testing, cybersecurity assessment, or other specialized support may be required.
- Prepares monitoring observations, technical analyses, and evidence-based recommendations for consideration by the GOR, COR, and FAU leadership.
- Supports performance-management processes and internal reporting on program results, implementation risks, lessons, and strategic alignment.
- Supports assessments of whether programs require technical adjustment, additional analysis, specialized assistance, or revised implementation approaches.

All monitoring and award-support functions shall be performed under the direction of the responsible GOR or COR. The Specialist shall not direct recipients or contractors, approve or reject deliverables, certify technical products, modify award requirements, commit USG funds, or exercise responsibilities reserved for authorized USG officials.

**Supervisory Controls**

The Digital Development and Connectivity Program Specialist exercises independent technical judgment in assessing digital-infrastructure concepts, reviewing network and connectivity designs, evaluating cybersecurity considerations, developing technical requirements, and recommending approaches to address implementation challenges. The Specialist consults with the Programs Team Lead, responsible GORs or CORs, and other technical personnel when assignments involve significant policy, procurement, financial, security, or specialized technical considerations.

Work is reviewed for technical soundness, responsiveness to program requirements, compliance with applicable procedures, alignment with USG priorities, and contribution to effective program performance.

**Minimum Qualifications**

**Minimum Education:** One of the following combinations of education and professional experience is required:

- Master's degree in telecommunications engineering, information and communications technology, computer science, cybersecurity, digital development, or another closely related discipline, plus at least six years of relevant professional experience; or
- Bachelor's degree in one of these disciplines, plus at least 10 years of relevant professional experience.

Telecommunications, ICT, computer science, and digital-development degrees are equally acceptable. A professional certification (e.g., PMP, CISSP, or equivalent) is not required but is beneficial.

**Professional Experience:**

- Progressively responsible experience designing, reviewing, deploying, managing, or monitoring ICT and connectivity infrastructure projects.
- At least two years of direct experience with digital-connectivity projects of different sizes, technologies, and sectoral focus.
- Experience in aligning digital communications projects to social and economic development goals.
- Experience conducting market research and evaluating proposals for pricing, competitiveness, and commercial viability.
- Experience assessing cybersecurity considerations relevant to digital infrastructure and connectivity deployments.
- Experience preparing technical scopes of work and assessing project feasibility, implementation risks, quality, sustainability, and operations and maintenance requirements.
- Experience structuring subcontracted training, sustainability, and wraparound services to support public policy goals alongside commercial viability.
- Experience supporting project implementation, site monitoring, and multidisciplinary teams through clear technical analysis and recommendations.

**Preferred Professional Experience:**

- Experience supporting digital-development or connectivity programs funded by the U.S. Government, multilateral organizations, bilateral donors, or international development institutions.
- Experience working with the Department of State, USAID, MCC, USTDA, DFC, another U.S. Government agency, or a multilateral development institution.
- Experience with digital-inclusion strategies targeting underserved or rural populations.

**Language:** Level IV (Fluent) English and Level V (Fluent) Spanish required.

**Skills and Abilities:**

- Design complex international digital-development programs
- Lead proposal development efforts
- Build relationships with private-sector telecommunications and technology companies
- Translate policy into operational programming
- Integrate technical input into coherent program designs
- Develop strategic partnerships
- Communicate effectively with executive audiences
- Manage competing priorities under tight deadlines
- Produce high-quality analytical and written products
- Evaluate commercial pricing and competitiveness of technical proposals

**Comprehensive knowledge of:**

- ICT infrastructure deployment and connectivity-expansion planning
- Digital inclusion strategies and approaches
- Cybersecurity considerations for critical digital infrastructure
- Program design methodologies and proposal development
- Results-based management
- Digital-infrastructure program design and project-management methodologies
- Market research and competitiveness analysis
- Technical risk identification and mitigation

**Working knowledge of:**

- U.S. foreign policy objectives
- Environmental and social considerations applicable to digital-infrastructure activities
- Government digital-infrastructure planning and public-investment processes
- Procurement and implementation models
- Subcontracting structures for training, sustainability, and wraparound services

**Other Requirements**

- **Candidates must be authorized and able to work daily in Bogotá.**

jobs.title: Coordinator and legal institutional representant of the programme in Brazil
jobs.body:
HEKS/EPER has been engaged in **Brazil** since the 1980s and focuses its interventions on the Cerrado region (Minas Gerais and Bahia). HEKS/EPER works currently with five local partner organizations which cooperate among each other, supporting key networks of family farming and Traditional Peoples and Communities regarding access to land, sustainable natural resources management, agroecology, bioeconomy and inclusion to markets. Special attention is given to the inclusion of young people and women. The programme is closely supported by global staff: the head of programmes Latin America and Caribbean, a thematic advisor specialized in biodiversity, land governance and sustainable food systems, an M&E-advisor, a finance controller, and others.

For our programme in Brazil, we are looking for an experienced, strategically minded and inspiring coordinator to take up this position on 1rst of December 2026 or by agreement:

## **Coordinator and legal institutional representant of the programme in Brazil**

### **Your responsibilities:**

- Assume the institutional legal representation of the HEKS/EPER Swiss branch in Brazil, via power of attorney.
- Lead the forward- thinking and creative strategic development of the programme in cooperation with the local and global teams and local actors within the financial framework.
- Ensure the effective and efficient implementation of the programme through participative monitoring, evaluation, learning and steering of the projects.
- Support the partners in drawing up annual and phase project-reports and write annual programme-reports, based on the reports of the partners.
- Support fundraising for the projects with Swiss donors by contributing to the drafting of projects and writing of reports and presenting them to the donors.
- Prospect for funding opportunities and lead the acquisition of national, regional and international funds through engagement with donors and the development of proposals.
- Represent HEKS/EPER towards the government, the public and international, regional and local organisations and networks including the Act Alliances structures.
- Establish and maintain close cooperation with other actors in Brazil, incl. international and local NGOs, public authorities and research institutions, businesses, for joint activities and resource mobilization in consortia.
- Supervise and assume final responsibility for financial and administrative matters, in accordance with HEKS/EPER standards.
- Supervise the finance officer and ensure compliance with local laws and obligations, the guidelines, and the institutional governance of HEKS/EPER.
- Contribute to reflection and learning with the other teams of HEKS/EPER in Latin America and the Caribbean and with Global Cooperation of HEKS/EPER.

### **To be successful you bring:**

- Minimum of 10 years of experience in the development sector, including 5 years in a similar position, ideally for international NGOs in Brazil.
- Excellent conceptual, strategic development, monitoring and evaluation skills.
- Excellent communication and networking skills.
- Strong financial management skills.
- Successful track record in the acquisition and implementation of internationally funded projects.
- Cultural sensitivity, flexibility, initiative, commitment.
- University degree or equivalent in a relevant field (agricultural, environmental or social sciences).
- **Excellent skills of oral and written English and Portugues** are compulsory, good knowledge of Spanish an asset.
- **We are looking exclusively for a Brazilian resident (this is not an international/expat position).**

### **What you can expect from us:**

- A varied and multidisciplinary position.
- Attractive employment conditions.
- The position may be contracted either under Brazil’s Consolidation of Labor Laws (Consolidação das Leis do Trabalho – CLT), the country’s statutory employment regime, or through a service agreement with an independent contractor registered as a legal entity (Pessoa Jurídica – PJ).
- Duty station: preferably Brasilia, with regular visits to the projects in Minas Gerais and Bahia and occasional international traveling.
- Contract of indefinite duration.

jobs.title: Pediatrician
jobs.body:
**PAEDIATRICIAN – EBOLA EMERGENCY RESPONSE**

**PURPOSE**

Providing outpatient and/or inpatient paediatric care to patients/beneficiaries according to adapted and updated medical knowledge, MSFprotocols, values and universal hygiene standards to improve the new-born and child/beneficiaries health conditions

**WHO WE ARE LOOKING FOR A PAEDIATRICIAN IN THE DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF THE CONGO – EBOLA EMERGENCY RESPONSE**

- Available for deployment within the next 3 months for your first rotation of 12-16 weeks, followed by a mandatory 21-day post-deployment monitoring period.
- French proficiency (at least B2)
- Experienced in Ebola response, VHF, outbreak, or emergency response (strong asset)
- Flexible and adaptable in fast-changing environments
- Resilient under high-pressure humanitarian conditions
- Committed to teamwork and MSF principles
- Ready for remote and resource-limited field settings
- Medical Doctor diploma in a recognized university
- Paediatrics qualification preferred
- 2 years’ experience minimum as a Medical Doctor in paediatric hospital

**Accountabilities**

- Applying medical knowledge and skills to prevention, diagnosis and treatment of children, ensuring integrated new-born and paediatric care through Emergency, OPD, and IPD services in New-borns and cases of malnutrition. Prescribing the necessary treatment, respecting MSF protocols.
- Collaborating closely with the different department of the hospital (e.g. Maternity), Knowing and ensuring all updated MSF medical protocols and universal precautions are followed and implemented, reducing bio-hazard risks and improving infection control.
- As an expert in paediatrics, proposing strategy (modification on current new-born and paediatric care management) and implementing them after validation of Operation and Paediatric Advisor.
- Ensuring on-going new-born and paediatric training (formal and bedside) of the medical/paramedical multidisciplinary team in order to optimize the new-born and paediatric quality of care. Reviewing and discussing selected complicated cases or mistakes and giving technical input.
- Keeping patients and their families informed of the illness and the treatment to follow, checking that they have been understood. Ensuring professional autonomy and confidentiality are respected and a good attitude and proper bedside manner towards the patient and their care takers and the rest of the medical team.
- Following up the evolution of the hospitalized/IDP patients through daily visits, consultations and examinations, prescribing the necessary treatment following MSF protocols, deciding whether they can be discharged or transferred to other departments – in collaboration with other doctors- and informing their family about the patient’s evolution.
- Monitoring the proper functioning of the department, equipment or material and addresses the list of the missing item for new-born and paediatric activities. Providing inputs about general organization of the different paediatric wards, including the admission, transfer and discharge criteria + referral procedure from Maternity and post-delivery wards
- Checking and controlling the rational distribution of medicines and equipment under his/her responsibility and taking care the quality, disinfection and sterilization of the medical material. Assuring general compliance with standing hygiene standards.
- Participating in the introduction / improvement of the collection and analysis of epidemiological new-born and paediatric data, checking its validity and informing the line manager or project coordinator about any problems or complications of the patient’s illness and medical errors. Collecting Clinical cases for further trainings and list a series of comments to improve the current MSF protocols
- Managing the team under his/her direct responsibility according to MSF HR policies and procedures, supervising their performance, organizing and scheduling shifts and rotations, directly participating in emergencies and on calls if necessary.
- Designing and providing training to staff as required.
- Debriefing with coordination, Headquarter (including Paediatric Advisor) and providing written report on main findings, activities, conclusions and further recommendations.

**What MSF Offers:**

- A fixed-term contract for deployment assignments and additional 21 days
- Travel, accommodation, and medical coverage during missions.
- Daily allowances in line with MSF policies.
- Access to training and professional development opportunities.

jobs.title: ASSISTANTE OU ASSISTANT RECHERCHE
jobs.body:
About : Action contre la Faim

Créée en 1979, Action contre la Faim est une organisation non gouvernementale internationale qui lutte contre la faim dans le monde. Sa charte des principes humanitaires - indépendance, neutralité, non-discrimination, accès libre et direct aux victimes, professionnalisme, transparence - fonde son identité depuis 45 ans. Sa mission est de sauver des vies en éliminant la faim par la prévention, la détection et le traitement de la sous-nutrition, en particulier pendant et après les situations d'urgence liées aux conflits et aux catastrophes naturelles. Action contre la Faim coordonne ses programmes autour de 7 domaines d'activités : Nutrition et Santé - Santé Mentale, Soutien Psychosocial - Sécurité Alimentaire et Moyens d'Existence - Eau, Assainissement et Hygiène - Plaidoyer - Climat - Recherche. En 2025, Action contre la Faim est venue en aide à plus de 21 millions de personnes dans 54 pays à travers le monde. www.actioncontrelafaim.org

Mission :

Nous recherchons un·e stagiaire capable d'apporter un appui par les missions suivantes :   
  
Consolidation des besoins de recherche d'Action contre la Faim (30%) - en lien avec la Responsable Recherche, Analyses et Apprentissages  
Participation à la définition du cadre de révision de la stratégie de recherche ACF France  
Participation aux échanges en cours  
Si nécessaire : définition d'une méthodologie de travail (analyse documentaire, enquêtes si nécessaire) pour collecter et centraliser les besoins de recherche interne et prioritaires   
Création d'un corpus de données qualitatives disponibles à ACF (60%) - en lien avec la Référente Approches sociales et Communautaires  
Synthèse bibliographique des documents ACF  
Réalisation d'enquêtes auprès des Bureaux pays / chercheurs/ départements  
Si la charge de travail le permet : analyses et proposition de synthèse, recommandations opérationnelles  
Contribution à la valorisation du travail de la recherche et de l'apprentissages d'Action contre la Faim France (10%) - en lien avec la Responsable Recherche, Analyses et Apprentissages  
Mise à jour des tableaux en lien avec l'équipe de 10 chercheurs  
Mise à jour de l'Intranet No Hunger Forum  
Participation à la réalisation du Rapport Final d'Activités Recherche&Analyses&Apprentissages

  
Profile :

 Nous recherchons un·e candidat·e qui partage notre engagement et qui dispose des qualités suivantes :   
  
Tu prépares un Master en Sciences Sociales (sociologie, anthropologie, sciences politiques, développement international ou équivalent).  
Tu disposes de bonnes capacités d'analyse, de synthèse et de rédaction.  
Tu apprécies le travail de recherche et l'exploitation de données qualitatives.  
Tu fais preuve de rigueur, d'organisation et d'autonomie.  
Tu es à l'aise pour échanger avec des interlocuteurs variés dans un environnement multiculturel.  
Tu as un intérêt pour les enjeux humanitaires, de développement et de capitalisation des connaissances.  
Tu maîtrises les outils du Pack Office, notamment Excel et PowerPoint.  
Un bon niveau d'anglais (écrit et oral) est apprécié.  
  
Conditions d'emploi  
  
Condition Obligatoire : Avoir une convention de stage délivrée par un établissement scolaire de droit français  
  
Durée du Stage : 3 mois (basé à Montreuil, 102 rue de paris)   
Date de début de contrat souhaitée : 01/10/2026   
  
Conditions Salariales :   
Stage indemnisé à hauteur de 4,57euros net par heure (sur une base de 35h par semaine).   
Temps de travail hebdomadaire (38,75h).   
Titres restaurant à 8 EUR (pris en charge à 60% par ACF).   
Prise en charge à hauteur de 50 % des frais de transport en commun.

jobs.title: CANADEM is recruiting for its French-Speaking OB/GYN Roster
jobs.body:
CANADEM is seeking seasoned **French-speaking** **Obstetrician/Gynecologist** professionals with previous relevant experience for its **French-speaking OB/GYN** **Expert Roster.** CANADEM is a Canadian-based NGO that works with various UN agencies through the Standby Partnership Programme. We regularly deploy candidates in various areas of expertise all around the globe. Registration with CANADEM is always free. We are looking to expand our pool of experts for potential/upcoming opportunities with different UN agencies' field offices. Most positions are for 3 to 6 month deployments.

**QUALIFICATIONS & EXPERIENCE**

- Valid Doctor of Medicine (MD) or equivalent from a recognized institution with an advanced degree or board certification in Obstetrics and Gynecology. Active, unrestricted license to practice medicine in the home country, with the ability to obtain temporary registration in the host country.
- Minimum of 3 to 5 years of post-residency experience in active clinical OB/GYN practice. Proven track record in performing emergency obstetric surgeries independently under challenging conditions.
- Experience in Emergency/Humanitarian Contexts. Prior experience working in low-resource settings, disaster responses, conflict zones, or with international NGOs or UN agencies is highly preferred.
- Technical Skills: Deep understanding of the Minimum Initial Service Package (MISP) for sexual and reproductive health in crises; Comprehensive knowledge of Emergency Obstetric and Newborn Care (EmONC) signals and guidelines. Familiarity with WHO, UNFPA, and international humanitarian health standards.

Languages: Fluency in **French and English** (verbal and written) is required. Fluency/working knowledge of Arabic is desirable.

*CANADEM and its partners have a no-tolerance policy for inaction to prevent, respond to and follow up on alleged cases of* [*Sexual Exploitation, Abuse*](https://www.canadem.ca/_files/ugd/add124_d0a1c71e1e2048489099add12e081b7b.pdf)*, and* [*Harassment*](https://www.canadem.ca/_files/ugd/add124_7c5b3ddfcc68480eaed81712fa798e7c.pdf) *(SEAH). For this reason, we adhere to all policies, procedures and training of the United Nations on The Prevention of Sexual Exploitation, Abuse, and Harassment (PSEAH). CANADEM mandates all deployees successfully complete the* [*PSEA online course*](https://agora.unicef.org/course/info.php?id=7380)*. This e-learning course is composed of a set of lessons designed to raise awareness about SEAH, become familiar with a range of measures to combat SEAH, understand the impact on victims and the consequences for UN Personnel who commit Sexual Exploitation, Abuse, and Harassment.*

jobs.title: Chargé.e de Communication Audiovisuelle - Dakar - H/F
jobs.body:
ALIMA (The Alliance for International Medical Action) est une ONG humanitaire médicale internationale, créée en 2009. Elle offre des soins de santé de qualité aux populations vulnérables confrontées à des crises sanitaires, des [épidémies](https://alima.ngo/decouvrir/expertises/epidemies-maladies-emergentes/) ou des catastrophes naturelles.

ALIMA intervient lors des crises humanitaires, dans les [zones de conflits](https://alima.ngo/conflits-populations-deplacees/), [d’épidémies](https://alima.ngo/decouvrir/expertises/epidemies-maladies-emergentes/) et de malnutrition où les besoins médicaux sont les plus urgents. ALIMA associe des [soins d’urgence](https://alima.ngo/reponse-urgences/) à des [projets de recherche de plus long terme](https://alima.ngo/decouvrir/expertises/recherche-innovation/) pour développer de nouvelles solutions et améliorer durablement la prise en charge des populations les plus vulnérables.

8 domaines d’expertise

- [Épidémies et maladies émergentes](https://alima.ngo/decouvrir/expertises/epidemies-maladies-emergentes/)
- [Malnutrition](https://alima.ngo/decouvrir/expertises/malnutrition-aigue/)
- [Santé des femmes](https://alima.ngo/decouvrir/expertises/sante-femmes/)
- [Pédiatrie](https://alima.ngo/decouvrir/expertises/pediatrie/)
- [Santé mentale](https://alima.ngo/decouvrir/expertises/sante-mentale/)
- [Recherche et innovation](https://alima.ngo/decouvrir/expertises/recherche-innovation/)
- [Renforcement du système de santé](https://alima.ngo/decouvrir/expertises/renforcement-systeme-sante/)
- [Chirurgie](https://alima.ngo/decouvrir/expertises/chirurgie-humanitaire/)

ALIMA collabore avec des autorités sanitaires nationales et locales, des [ONG locales](https://alima.ngo/agir/nous-soutenir/devenir-partenaire/partenaires-operationnels/), des communautés, et des instituts de recherche pour bâtir des solutions humanitaires innovantes et adaptées. Son siège opérationnel à Dakar reflète son ancrage au plus près du terrain et 95 % de ses équipes viennent des pays d’intervention.

Depuis 2009, ALIMA a soigné plus de 46 millions de personnes dans [ 16 pays](https://alima.ngo/decouvrir/nos-operations/), principalement en Afrique. L’organisation se distingue par son expertise en [malnutrition](https://alima.ngo/decouvrir/expertises/malnutrition-aigue/), [pédiatrie](https://alima.ngo/decouvrir/expertises/pediatrie/), [santé des femmes](https://alima.ngo/decouvrir/expertises/sante-femmes/) et [réponse aux épidémies et maladies émergentes](https://alima.ngo/decouvrir/expertises/epidemies-maladies-emergentes/), entre autres.

Grâce à la [recherche et à l’innovation](https://alima.ngo/decouvrir/expertises/recherche-innovation/) issues de l’expérience sur le terrain, et au renforcement des capacités locales dans nos pays d’opération, ALIMA s’efforce de transformer la médecine humanitaire et de mieux protéger les populations des crises sanitaires de demain.

**PRÉSENTATION DU POSTE**

**Liens hiérarchiques et fonctionnels** :

**Superviseur hiérarchique** : Responsable de la Communication digitale

Personnels sous sa responsabilité hiérarchique : aucun

Il/elle collabore avec :

- L’équipe Communication (siège et pays)
- Les Missions dans les pays et les Desks au Siège de Dakar
- L’équipe Développement / Collecte (Sénégal, France, USA, UK, Suisse)
- L’équipe Bailleurs
- Les équipes et partenaires Recherche
- Les prestataires externes

**Enjeux du poste** :

Garantir la qualité, l'éthique et la cohérence de tous les contenus photo et vidéo d'ALIMA, de leur production à leur archivage, afin de rendre compte de l'action d'ALIMA dans le respect de la dignité des personnes accompagnées.

**Missions et objectifs** :

Conformément aux orientations stratégiques et aux priorités fixées par la Direction de la Communication, vous avez pour missions principales de :

- Monter et postproduire les vidéos d’ALIMA
- Concevoir et animer des contenus en motion design (vidéos explicatives, infographies animées, habillages…)
- Concevoir, écrire et tourner des contenus vidéos, au siège et sur le terrain
- Garantir la qualité et la cohérence des contenus vidéos et photos produits par les équipes pays et les prestataires
- Produire des photos en appui, selon les besoins
- Archiver et assurer la traçabilité des contenus audiovisuels (consentements, droits)

**Lieu du poste**

Dakar, Sénégal, siège opérationnel d'ALIMA.

Déplacements possibles pour un besoin de reportage ponctuel le justifiant.

**Activités principales**

1. Monter et postproduire les vidéos d’ALIMA

● Narration et dérushage stratégique

- Visionner, trier et dérusher les rushs (tournages en propre, équipes pays, prestataires)
- Construire un récit clair et rythmé : repérer les moments forts, structurer la narration et maintenir l’attention du spectateur du début à la fin
- Monter des formats variés : formats courts réseaux sociaux (verticaux et carrés), témoignages et reportages terrain, vidéos bailleurs et institutionnelles et formats longs

● Rythme et plans d’illustration (B-roll)

- Intégrer des plans d’illustration pertinents pour dynamiser les interviews et casser la monotonie du « face caméra »
- Privilégier les images d’ALIMA et encadrer l’usage des banques d’images (ex : photos AFP)

● Conception sonore (sound design)

- Traiter et égaliser la voix principale, nettoyer l’audio (bruits de fond, niveaux)
- Choisir des musiques adaptées au propos, ambiance voulue, avec des droits d’utilisation vérifiés
- Utiliser avec justesse les bruitages et effets sonores

● Finalisation et diffusion

- Réaliser l’étalonnage, créer et relire les sous-titres (français et anglais)
- Réaliser les exports adaptés à chaque plateforme (site, YouTube, LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, X , bailleurs)
- Intégrer les retours des équipes et gérer les versions successives jusqu’à validation
- Utiliser l’IA de manière encadrée (transcription, sous-titrage, nettoyage audio)

2\. Concevoir et animer en motion design

- Vidéos explicatives et pédagogiques
    - Concevoir et réaliser des vidéos explicatives animées pour rendre accessibles des sujets médicaux et humanitaires complexes (malnutrition, épidémies, recherche, innovations médicales)
    - Construire le storyboard et le découpage visuel à partir d’un script, en lien avec les chargés de communication et les équipes médicales et recherche
- Data visualisation animée
    - Transformer les données et chiffres clés d’ALIMA (rapports annuels, bilans de réponse d’urgence, résultats de recherche) en infographies et cartes animées, claires et fiables
- Habillage et identité visuelle animée
    - Créer et faire évoluer la bibliothèque d’éléments graphiques animés d’ALIMA : génériques, titres animés, bandeaux nom/fonction, transitions personnalisées, logos animés, cartons de fin et appels à l’action
    - Garantir la cohérence de l’identité visuelle animée sur toutes les productions, internes et prestataires, dans le respect de la charte graphique et de la charte vidéo d’ALIMA
    - Produire des modèles réutilisables (templates) pour accélérer la production
- Formats réseaux sociaux
    - Réaliser des formats courts animés et dynamiques : typographie cinétique, citations animées, carrousels animés, formats verticaux
    - Animer des visuels existants (photos, illustrations, captures d’écran) pour les rendre plus engageants

3\. Concevoir, écrire et tourner les vidéos

- Préparation
    - Être force de proposition sur les sujets et les angles éditoriaux
    - Écrire ou co-écrire les scripts, trames narratives et voix off avec les chargés de communication, et proposer en autonomie des scripts corporate
    - Préparer les tournages : repérages, liste de plans, questions d’interview, logistique
- Tournage
    - Tourner au siège et sur le terrain : interviews, plans d’illustration, événements
    - Mener des entretiens pertinents et en autonomie, mettre les personnes filmées à l’aise
    - Recueillir les informations de contexte (lieu, date, pays, projet, histoire de la personne, soins reçus)
- Éthique, consentement et sécurité
    - Recueillir un consentement éclairé dans une langue comprise par la personne (accord du parent ou du tuteur pour les mineurs), collecter et archiver les formulaires
    - Respecter les règles de sécurité des missions et obtenir les autorisations de tournage (autorités, sites, drone le cas échéant)

4\. Garantir la qualité et appuyer les équipes

- Être le référent vidéo des chargés de communication pays : guides de tournage (smartphone et caméra), briefs, modèles de liste de plans, retours techniques sur les rushs reçus
- Former les équipes à distance ou lors des missions, notamment à l’utilisation des templates d’habillage
- Gérer les prestataires au siège, de l’expression du besoin au paiement de la facture : cahier des charges, devis, supervision du tournage, validation, suivi des droits et crédits
    - Les commandes aux prestataires dans les pays restent gérées par les chargés de communication pays et le Responsable Communication Opérations
- Assurer une veille sur les formats, tendances vidéo et motion design, et proposer des formats innovants, notamment pour les réseaux sociaux

5\. Produire des photos

- Réaliser des photos lors des tournages, des missions et des événements (portraits, activités, siège et missions ALIMA)
- Assurer la postproduction des photos (sélection, retouche) et rédiger les légendes détaillées (projet, bailleur, contexte)
- Appliquer les mêmes règles de consentement et d’éthique que pour la vidéo

6\. Archiver, gérer les droits et le matériel

- Organiser et classer les fichiers sources, projets de montage et d’animation, éléments graphiques et exports finaux
- Enregistrer les contenus validés dans le Drive et/ou la Media Gallery (Bynder), avec légendes et tags pertinents, en coordination avec le/la Chargé.e de communication en charge de la Media Gallery
- Assurer le suivi des consentements, des droits musicaux
- Entretenir et sécuriser le matériel et le studio, tenir la fiche des entrées et sorties du matériel

## Expériences & Compétences

- Niveau d’étude
- Formation supérieure en audiovisuel, montage, motion design, cinéma ou design graphique, ou expérience professionnelle équivalente
- Expérience
    
    
    - Expérience d’au moins 5 ans en montage vidéo, dont 2 à 3 ans en motion design
    - Références techniques en conception et production de supports photos et vidéos (Portfolio obligatoire)
    - Références techniques en écriture de scripts vidéos
- Connaissances en langues
    
    
    - Excellente maîtrise en Français et bonne maîtrise en anglais
    - Excellente maîtrise des deux langues écrites (relecture des sous-titres des vidéos)
- Compétences
    
    
    - Excellente maîtrise du montage et de la narration vidéo (Premiere Pro ou DaVinci Resolve)
    - Excellente maîtrise du motion design 2D (After Effects) et de la création graphique (Illustrator, Photoshop)
    - Savoir-faire en écriture de script vidéo et de storyboards
    - Maîtrise du traitement sonore, de l'étalonnage et du sous-titrage
    - Maîtrise des suites Google Workspace et Microsoft Office
    - Bonne maîtrise de la prise de vue vidéo et photo : cadrage, lumière, prise de son, interviews et reportage terrain
    - Retouche photo (Lightroom)
- Autres qualités
    
    
    - Sens du récit, créativité et sensibilité à l'éthique de l'image
    - Autonomie, rigueur, respect des délais
    - Capacité à travailler sur plusieurs projets en même temps et à prioriser
    - Esprit d'équipe

## Conditions

- **CDI de droit sénégalais**
- **Prise de poste** : Dès que possible
- **Salaire** : selon la grille de salaire en vigueur au Siège de Dakar.
- Avantages extra contractuels :
- Cinq semaines de congés payés par an et système de jours de récupération pour les déplacements
- Couverture santé complémentaire pour l’employé et ses ayants droit.

jobs.title: HAITI - RESPONSABLE LOG ADMIN (H/F) - SAINT-MARC
jobs.body:
## Que faisons nous ...

**Date de début souhaité:** 01/11/2026  
**Durée de la mission:** jusqu'au 28/02/2026  
**Localisation**: Saint-Marc, Haiti

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL** (SI) est une association d’aide humanitaire internationale qui, depuis plus de 40 ans, porte secours aux populations victimes de conflits armés et de catastrophes naturelles en répondant aux besoins vitaux, boire, manger, s’abriter. Particulièrement engagée dans le combat contre les maladies liées à l’eau insalubre, première cause de mortalité au monde, SI met en œuvre par ses interventions une expertise dans le domaine de l’accès à l’eau potable, l’assainissement et la promotion de l’hygiène mais également dans celui, essentiel, de la sécurité alimentaire et moyen d’existence. Présentes dans 26 pays, les équipes de SI - 3 200 personnes au total composées d’expatriés, de salariés nationaux, de permanents au siège, de quelques bénévoles…- interviennent avec professionnalisme et engagement dans le respect des cultures.

## La mission

Présente en Haïti depuis 2004, Solidarités International (SI) possède une solide expérience de réponse d’urgence, construite après la tempête Jeanne et renforcée lors de crises majeures (cyclone 2016, séisme 2021, épidémies). Acteur clé du secteur EHA, mais aussi de la sécurité alimentaire, des moyens d’existence et de la nutrition, SI intervient depuis plus de dix ans auprès des populations les plus vulnérables, notamment les personnes déplacées internes (PDI) et les communautés hôtes. Face à la dégradation sécuritaire liée aux groupes criminels organisés, SI opère aujourd’hui dans 17 sites de déplacés à Delmas, Cité-Soleil et Port-au-Prince, améliorant l’accès à l’eau, aux infrastructures d’assainissement et contribuant à la prévention des maladies hydriques. SI répond aussi aux besoins immédiats via des activités génératrices de revenus et des actions de prévention nutritionnelle ciblant enfants, femmes enceintes et allaitantes.

  
En mars 2026, le bureau pays est composé d'une coordination et d'une base opérationnelle à Port-au-Prince. La mission espère ouvrir de nouvelles zones d'intervention en 2026 selon les financements disponibles.

La mission Haïti a un volume budgétaire de 5 millions d'euros essentiellement financés par :  
\- Programmes d’urgence EHA financés par - ECHO / UNICEF / SDC / CDCS  
\- Programme de sécurité alimentaire financé par - IFSAN

Elle a également des projets en cours de discussions dont :  
\- Programme d’urgence EHA avec US DoS via OCHA / ECHO

Les principaux bailleurs de la mission sont : ECHO – UNICEF – IFSAN - CDCS - SDC. Les activités sont mises en oeuvre avec 1 partenaire local et plusieurs partenaires internationaux.

## Descriptif du poste

**OBJECTIF GENERAL**

Le/la Responsable support (Logistique/Admin/Fin/RH) est responsable du traitement des opérations comptables et financières, des tâches et procédures liées aux Ressources Humaines ainsi que de la mise en œuvre et la supervision de l’ensemble des activités logistiques.

En tant que tel, il/elle :  
\- Supervise et garantit la performance de la chaîne d’approvisionnements ;  
\- Gère la flotte de véhicules, les équipements et les moyens généraux ;  
\- Gère la comptabilité et le pilotage budgétaire de la base ;  
\- Assure la gestion de la trésorerie ;  
\- Assure la gestion des ressources humaines sur la base (gestion contractuelle, gestion de la paie mensuelle, évaluation et évolution des carrières, gestion du cadre disciplinaire, etc.) ;  
\- Est garant/e du respect des procédures admin/log de Solidarités International sur sa base ;  
\- Encadre et accompagne les équipes Logistique, Finance et RH de la base ;  
\- Contribue à la gestion de la sécurité opérationnelle ;

**ENJEUX ET DEFIS SPECIFIQUES**

\- Marché local peu développé, nécessitant des approvisionnements auprès de fournisseurs situés à Gonaïves et Port-au-Prince.  
\- Niveau de prix local très élevé, avec un impact sur les coûts d’approvisionnement et de fonctionnement de la base.  
\- Connaissances limitées du mandat et des principes humanitaires.  
\- Marché de l’emploi local offrant un nombre limité de profils correspondant aux compétences recherchées.

**PRIORITES SUR LES 2-3 PREMIERS MOIS**

\- Finaliser l'ouverture de la base  
\- Finaliser les recrutements et inductions des équipes  
\- Mise en place de contrats cadres  
\- Accompagner et former les assistants log & admin  
\- Important renforcement de capacités et formations et rappels PSEAH à prévoir pour l'ensemble des staffs  
\- Continuer/lancer les achats pour les activités

**CONTRAINTES SECURITAIRES**

La ville de Saint-Marc est classée niveau 4, avec un contexte sécuritaire volatile. Le couvre-feu est à 19h

## Votre profil

**DIPLÔME ET EXPERIENCE**

Diplôme universitaire de niveau minimum BAC + 3 dans l'un des domaines suivants : Logistique, Comptabilité, Administration, Finance, Gestion Ressources Humaines.

- Expérience dans le secteur humanitaire : 3-4 ans
- Expérience sur un poste similaire : 3-4 ans

**COMPETENCES**

COMPETENCES TECHNIQUES

1\. Maitrise des logiciels excel, SAGA, Homere et LINK

2.Gestion de la chaine d'approvisionnement, du parc automobile, équipements de communication, parc informatique, stock et de la sécurité.

3\. Gestion de la comptabilité, de la trésorerie et des finances.

COMPETENCES TRANSVERSALES

1\. Expérience de travail dans un contexte sécuritaire volatile

2\. Connaissances des principes du PSEAH

3\. Compétences en matière d'organisation et de priorisation, et capacité à gérer plusieurs choses en même temps

**LANGUES**

1\. Français

2\. Créole serait un atout

3\. Anglais serait un atout

## SI vous offrira les conditions suivantes

**Un poste salarié :** Selon l'expérience, à partir de EUR 2310 par mois (2100 salaire de base + 10% d'indemnité de congé annuel versée mensuellement) et un Per Diem mensuel de USD 750.

SI couvre également les frais de logement et les frais de déplacement entre le pays d'origine de l'expatrié et le lieu d'affectation.

**Breaks :** Pendant la mission, un système d'alternance entre travail et congés est mis en place à raison de 7 jours ouvrables tous les trois mois (avec USD 850 alloués par Solidarités International). A ces périodes de pause, s'ajoute un jour de repos supplémentaire par mois travaillé.

**Couverture sociale et médicale :** Les expatriés bénéficient d'une assurance qui rembourse tous les frais de santé (y compris les frais médicaux et chirurgicaux, les soins dentaires et ophtalmologiques, le rapatriement) et d'un système de prévoyance incluant les risques de guerre. Les frais de vaccination et de traitement antipaludéen indispensables sont remboursés.

**CONDITIONS DE VIE :**

La base de Saint-Marc a ouvert en septembre 2026. Le bureau et la guesthouse sont situés dans une même maison, dont un étage est dédié à la guest. À l’ouverture de la base, la maison est équipée du mobilier essentiel. Elle dispose également d’une cour extérieure avec un manguier, et une lumière de type "guinguette" est attendue sous peu.

La connexion Starlink ainsi que les réseaux de téléphonie mobile sont fonctionnels sur la base.  
La ville de Saint-Marc a une offre limitée de loisirs et de restauration. Les restaurants validés sont au nombre de deux. La Guesthouse est située face au bureau/Guesthouse d’ACTED et à environ 50 mètres de la Guesthouse de MSF.

Les principaux supermarchés de Saint-Marc permettent de trouver une grande partie des produits nécessaires au quotidien. Certains produits spécifiques doivent toutefois être approvisionnés depuis Port-au-Prince.

Le couvre-feu est fixé à 19h.

jobs.title: Chargé·e de projets CDI (H/F)
Assistive Technology Technical Officer - Afghanistan
jobs.body:
## Description

Humanity & Inclusion is an independent and impartial aid organization working in situations of poverty and exclusion, conflict and disaster. The organization works alongside people with disabilities and vulnerable populations, taking action and bearing witness in order to respond to their essential needs, improve their living conditions and promote respect for their dignity and fundamental rights.

Since its creation in 1982, HI has run development & humanitarian projects in more than 55 countries and responded to numerous emergencies. Today, we have a budget of approximately 200 million euros, with 4,000 employees worldwide

At Handicap International-Humanity & Inclusion, we truly believe in the importance of inclusion and diversity within our organization. This is why we are engaged to a disability policy to encourage the inclusion and integration of people with disabilities.

Please indicate if you require any special accommodation, even at the first interview.

**JOB CONTEXT:**

The HI Afghanistan operating framework is outlined in the operational strategy (“Stratop”) 2026-2029. The pillars are Rehabilitation & Health / Resilience & Inclusion / Armed Violence Reduction / Atlas logistic.

HI is currently involved in different sectors of activities:

- Physical and functional rehabilitation (both on service provision and training – tech assistance), in development and emergency crisis settings
- Mental Health and Psycho-Social Support (MHPSS)
- Disability & Inclusion - Inclusive Humanitarian Assistance – Inclusive Governance – protection integration
- Inclusive livelihood
- Explosive Ordnance Risk Education
- Atlas shared storage and transportation

The central office is in the capital city (Kabul) and hosts the management team (including operations, finance, logistics, human resources, technical unit, humanitarian access and security).

HI has three offices located in the different provinces of intervention: Herat, Kunduz, and Kandahar, are fully operational with dedicated support services and project management teams.

HI Afghanistan employs around 450 national and 9 international staff and has a budget of around 7 million euros. Most fundraising efforts and donor relationships are held at the Kabul level.

HI is also part of different fora/coordination bodies (ACBAR, ICCT, HCT, etc.) and a member of several clusters, including health, and protection.

**YOUR MISSION:**   
Under the line management of the Rehabilitation Specialist and in close coordination with relevant Project Managers and the rehabilitation technical team, the Assistive Technology (AT) Technical Officer contributes to the implementation of Humanity & Inclusion's (HI) mandate and strategy in Afghanistan by providing specialized technical support to strengthen the availability, accessibility, quality, and sustainability of assistive technology services and supplies.

The position focuses primarily on wheelchairs and positioning devices (i.e. CP chair), although other devices may be analyzed as well, with particular attention to strengthening HI's AT supply and service systems. The AT Technical Officer will conduct a comprehensive assessment of the existing AT market and supply chain, including mapping and assessing potential suppliers, reviewing product availability and technical specifications, analyzing pricing and market conditions, and identifying opportunities to improve procurement, sourcing, forecasting, stock management, distribution, and after-sales support.

 Working closely with rehabilitation teams, logistics/procurement colleagues, relevant project teams, suppliers, and other stakeholders, the position will support quality assurance of assistive products, including reviewing product specifications, assessing quality and suitability for the Afghan context, and contributing to the development or strengthening of appropriate technical standards and quality-control mechanisms. The position will also identify gaps and opportunities to improve the availability of appropriate, affordable, and user-centered assistive products, including wheelchairs and other mobility and functional assistive devices.

The AT Technical Officer will provide technical guidance and capacity strengthening to relevant HI staff and partners on AT-related topics, including product selection, basic technical specifications, fitting and provision considerations, maintenance and repair, and appropriate referral and follow-up mechanisms. The position will promote coordination between rehabilitation, logistics/procurement, and other relevant teams to strengthen an efficient and sustainable AT system.

The assignment places particular emphasis on improving equitable access to appropriate and quality-assured assistive technology for persons with disabilities, including people living in underserved and hard-to-reach areas and groups facing barriers to accessing rehabilitation and assistive products.

In this framework, your main responsibilities are:

**Responsibility 1:** Assistive Technology market and suppliers analysis:

- Assess the technical capacity of pre-selected local workshops to produce wheelchairs and positioning devices/CP chairs.
- Provide intensive on-the-job coaching and technical support to workshop staff on production processes, product quality, design, assembly, fitting, and finishing.
- Support workshops to improve their ability to consistently produce safe, functional, and appropriate wheelchairs and positioning devices/CP chairs.
- Identify technical gaps in equipment and machinery and provide recommendations on necessary improvements or additions, where appropriate.
- Provide technical support to selected workshops based on identified needs and feasibility, with Kabul expected to be a key location while allowing flexibility to support other relevant locations.

**Responsibility 2:** Assistive Technology product quality and technical review

- Review and support the development and improvement of wheelchair and positioning device/CP chair designs suitable for the local context and user needs.
- Establish or strengthen practical technical specifications, quality criteria, and production processes for the two priority products.
- Support workshops in applying quality control measures throughout the production process.

**Responsibility 3:** Supply chain and procurement technical support

- Provide technical guidance to workshops on production planning, costing, pricing, marketing and business models related to wheelchair and positioning device/CP chair production.
- Identify practical measures to improve the efficiency, sustainability, and continuity of local production.
- Support workshops to strengthen their capacity to maintain product quality while developing sustainable production models.

**Responsibility 4:** Technical support and capacity building

- Provide targeted training, coaching, and on-the-job mentoring for workshop staff and relevant rehabilitation stakeholders.
- Facilitate practical technical workshops and other capacity-building activities according to identified needs and the assignment workplan.
- Develop or adapt practical technical resources and tools to support continued application of the knowledge and skills gained during the assignment.

**Responsibility 5:** documentation and recommendations

- Document key findings, progress, lessons learnt, and remaining technical gaps.
- Provide practical recommendations for continued strengthening of local wheelchair and positioning device/CP chair production.
- Prepare a concise handover package to support HI and relevant stakeholders in continuing the work after completion of the assignment.

**CHARACTERISTICS OF THE POSITION:**

- The position is based in Kabul, with occasional travel to other provinces as required by project needs. The position reports to the Rehabilitation Specialist and will work closely with relevant HI technical, programme, logistics, procurement, and field teams throughout the four-month assignment.

## Requirements

**YOUR PROFILE:**

- You hold a Bachelor's degree or professional qualification in Physical and Functional Rehabilitation, Prosthetics and Orthotics, Occupational Therapy, Physiotherapy, Assistive Technology, or related fields,
- You have minimum 5 years of relevant professional experience, including demonstrated experience in Assistive Technology, particularly wheelchairs and other mobility and functional assistive devices,
- You have a Strong experience in AT product assessment, selection, quality assurance, technical specifications, and fitting,
- You have a Practical experience in AT market analysis, supplier assessment, sourcing, and supply-chain management, preferably in complex or resource-constrained settings,
- An experience in training, coaching, or mentoring rehabilitation professionals and relevant stakeholders is desirable.
- Excellent written and spoken English is required; working knowledge of Dari and Pashto is desirable.

## Benefits

**CONDITIONS:**   
At HI, the conditions offered are up to your commitment and adapted to the context of your mission:

- 4 months International contract starting from 1st January 2027;
- The international contract provides social cover adapted to your situation:
- Unemployment insurance benefits for EU nationals;
- Pension scheme;
- Medical coverage with 50% of employee contribution;
- Repatriation insurance paid by HI;
- Salary from 2346 € gross/month upon experience;
- Perdiem: 599 € net/month - paid in the field
- Hardship: 500 € net/month paid with your salary;
- Paid leaves: 25 days per year;
- R&R: according to the level of the mission 5 days every 8 weeks => + possible transport/package support;
- Position unaccompanied
- Housing: Collective taken in charge by HI;
- If you are resident in the country: local package.

jobs.title: Vice President, Global Human Resources
jobs.body:
**ABOUT CHILDFUND**

**ChildFund** is a child-focused international development organization that connects children with the people, resources and institutions they need to grow up healthy, educated, skilled and safe, no matter where they are. We work directly in 23 countries, with extended reach to more than 60 countries through our global partnership network.

**ChildFund’s Values**

We aspire for every person in our organization—program participants, supporters, staff, and volunteers alike—to feel free, safe, and confident to be themselves. In our culture of connection, you will have ample opportunity to grow, learn, and lead while contributing your talents and innovations to our inspiring mission.

**ChildFund’s Commitment**

ChildFund International has a zero-tolerance policy regarding sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment (SEAH) and all other forms of harm by its staff, partners, and other representatives in the delivery of its mission and services for children. ChildFund is committed to creating a safe environment in the workplace as well as in the communities where it delivers programs and services. ChildFund expects every staff member, partner, and representative to adhere to this commitment and to ensure all organizational policies and standards are followed. This position is subject to a range of vetting checks, including a criminal records check and/or disclosure to ensure program participants are safeguarded.

**ABOUT THE ROLE**

The Vice President, Global Human Resources is a key executive leadership position in ChildFund, responsible for the critical talent strategies and infrastructure delivering the organization’s strategy, Growing Connections.

As ChildFund pursues its “bold goal” to reach 100 million children by the year 2030, the Vice President plays a pivotal role in enhancing employee experience, developing talent capacity, strengthening systems, and promoting a value-aligned and engaging work culture.

Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer and serving as a member of the Executive Team and Global Leadership Team, the Vice President leads a global, matrixed Human Resources team and partners with regional leadership and Country Offices to align Global Human Resources strategies with organizational strategy and objectives. The Vice President is a key advisor to the CEO on people matters while traveling periodically and maintaining strong relationships across the organization.

An expert in HR practice, the Vice President leads organization-wide transformation initiatives while overseeing compliant, consistent service delivery and high performance of the global HR team. The Vice President coaches and mentors executives and HR professionals to support ChildFund’s culture of innovation and learning while staying current with global HR innovations and best practices in the international development sector.

**REQUIRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE**

- Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field required; Master’s degree preferred (MBA, MPA, Human Resources, or similar).
- At least 15 years of experience in the human resources function, with experience in international development strongly preferred.
- At least 10 years of experience leading teams.
- Experience leading the HR function in international organizations across multiple country locations.
- Significant experience developing and implementing people – and culture-centered, strategy-aligned HR initiatives.
- Experience advising, consulting, and influencing at the C-suite level preferred.
- Advanced knowledge of HR operations in the US; foundational knowledge of HR operations and/or labor laws in other ChildFund countries of operation is preferred but not required.
- English fluency is required; proficiency in another language is a plus.
- Impeccable integrity, judgment, and ethics.
- Excellent, demonstrated relationship-building skills.

**Please click here:** [**ChildFund International Job Description – VP, Global Human Resources.pdf**](https://pod6.app.loxo.co/redactor-files/4601?hash=65492b94955a37f9e9d762fed6dd7707114d365b9f3c3507f65241a5af152067) **for a full job description, which outlines the role’s primary responsibilities and ChildFund’s Leadership and Core competencies .**

**APPOINTMENT TERMS**

**Location: Richmond, Virginia, US**. This is a full-time hybrid position. Candidates located in Richmond, VA or willing to relocate are preferred. Candidates must have the ability to work on site in Richmond, Virginia two days per week. We are open to candidates willing to commute weekly from nearby metro areas.

**To be eligible, candidates must have current work authorization in the US.**

**Salary and Benefits:** The anticipated salary range for this position is $177,500-$225,000 per year.

**Contract length:** Permanent

jobs.title: COORDINATEUR.TRICE PROJET TILLABERI - NIGER - H/F
jobs.body:
## **TYPOLOGIE DU POSTE**

Fondée en 2009, ALIMA est présente au Niger aux côtés de son partenaire local l’ONG nigérienne BEFEN « le Bien Être de la Femme et de l’Enfant au Niger » depuis sa création. En effet, le tout premier projet d’ALIMA a été mis en œuvre au Niger, dans le district de Mirriah, région de Zinder. ALIMA possède une grande expérience dans la réponse aux épidémies (Diphtérie, Méningite, Rougeole, Choléra et COVID-19), la nutrition, la santé primaire et maternelle, les VBG (violences basées sur le genre) ainsi que le WASH (eau, assainissement et hygiène).

Il s’agit de:

1\. Un projet en consortium avec plusieurs ONG - ALIMA/ BEFEN met en œuvre le volet Santé Nutrition, ACF met en œuvre les activités WASH ; Agriculture et sécurité alimentaire et l’ONG DIKO le volet protection).

Objectif général : Contribuer à la réduction de la morbidité et de la mortalité des populations hôtes et déplacées dans la région de Tillabéry (districts de Say, Téra et Bankilaré) par une réponse d'urgence intégrée

Dont l’objectif est : D'améliorer l'accès aux soins de santé communautaires, primaires, secondaires et nutritionnels pour les enfants de moins de cinq ans ainsi que pour les femmes enceintes et allaitantes parmi les personnes déplacées et les communautés d'accueil, touchées par la crise dans les districts de Say, Téra et Bankilaré.

2\. Un projet de Réponse d’urgence pour l’accès et l’amélioration des soins de santé des populations affectées par un choc et la contribution à la réduction de la morbi-mortalité infantile dans les régions de Tillabéry (Abala, Banibangou et Ayerou), Tahoua, Maradi et Zinder

Durée de l'action (en mois) : 36 mois

Zone d’intervention : Tillabéri : 3 HD, 5 CSI et 2 cliniques mobiles. (Abala : 1 HD, 3 CSI, et 1 clinique mobile, Ayorou : 1 HD, 2 CSI et 1 clinique mobile, Banibangou :1 HD).

LIENS FONCTIONNELS ET HIERARCHIQUES

- Il·Elle rend compte au chef ou à la cheffe de mission basé·e en coordination.
- Il·Elle encadre l’équipe de cadre du projet (par exemple le ou la Référent.e Médical·e, le ou la Responsable Administration, le ou la Responsable Logistique et le ou la Responsable des soins infirmiers) ainsi que les équipes nationales en collaboration avec ses référent·es techniques au niveau du projet.
- Il·Elle collabore avec la coordination (médicale, logistique et financière et des ressources humaines) et avec les partenaires.

## **MISSION PRINCIPALE**

Sous la supervision du Chef de Mission, le.la coordinateur.rice projet est responsable de la mise en œuvre de la stratégie opérationnelle pays dans sa zone d’intervention, en lien avec le plan stratégique et la mandat d’ALIMA.

Plus spécifiquement, il.elle est responsable de la mise en œuvre du projet et de contribuer aux résultats fixés pour le projet en fonction de l’évolution de la situation humanitaire et des besoins dans la zone d’intervention et sur la base des objectifs médico-opérationnels préfixés en collaboration avec la coordination, dans le respect des principes humanitaires et du mandat de ALIMA. Il·Elle est le garant ou la garante de la sécurité de ses équipes dans toute sa zone d’intervention. Il·Elle est responsable de l’encadrement des équipes, du suivi des indicateurs programmatiques et des indicateurs contractuels bailleurs et du suivi des dépenses du projet - avec l’appui de la coordination, et de la communication avec les acteurs gouvernementaux et non gouvernementaux en relation avec le projet.

## **ACTIVITÉS PRINCIPALES**

Le CP, avant tout, doit:

- agir en lien avec le mandat d’ALIMA, les principes humanitaires et le principe de “do no harm / ne pas nuire”.
- Respecter la stratégie opérationnelle définie avec les autres coordinateurs (collaborer avec les autres acteurs humanitaires, internationaux et gouvernementaux présents dans la zone d’intervention.

1. Définition et planification stratégique
2. Mise en oeuvre des programmes
3. Analyse des données et reporting
4. Encadrement et animation d’équipes
5. Analyse et gestion de la sécurité
6. Développement des outils informatiques
7. Mise en œuvre des mesures de prévention contre les abus de pouvoir, les violences sexistes et sexuelles

## **Expériences et Compétences** 

- Expérience préalable à un poste équivalent en ONG Internationale.
- Expérience préalable dans contextes d’urgence.
- Une qualification médicale ou paramédicale ou une expérience en gestion de projets médicaux est un atout
- Expérience préalable en gestion d’équipe multiculturelle.

**COMPÉTENCES**

- Capacité d’écoute et empathie.
- Communication facile.
- Capacité d’analyse de contexte, compréhension des enjeux médicaux et humanitaires.
- Animation et motivation d’équipes.
- Capacité à identifier et anticiper les problèmes et les risques.
- Esprit orienté vers la résolution de problèmes.
- Organisation des rôles et délégation de tâches au sein d’une équipe.
- Capacité à définir des priorités.
- Établissement de réseaux de contacts et capacité à maintenir une posture neutre face à des acteurs opposés dans le cadre d’un même conflit armé.
- Sens des responsabilités.
- Capacité de prise d’initiative et de décision.
- Bonne gestion du stress.
- Flexibilité.
- Maîtrise de l’outil informatique (GSuite et pack office).

**Langues :**

- La maîtrise orale et écrite du français est indispensable

**Conditions :**

- Durée et type de contrat : CDD de droit français
- Prise de poste : Automne 2026
- Salaire : Selon grille salariale ALIMA + valorisation de l’expérience + Perdiem
    
    ALIMA prend en charge :
    
    
    - Les frais de déplacements entre le pays d’origine de l’expatrié et le lieu de mission
    - Les frais d’hébergement
    - La couverture médicale du premier jour de contrat à un mois après la date de départ du pays de
    - Mission pour l’employé et ses ayants droits
    - L’évacuation pour l’employé et ses ayants droits

## Documents à envoyer

- Pour postuler, veuillez envoyer votre CV et Lettre de Motivation en ligne avant le 27/10/2026
- Les candidatures sont traitées suivant l’ordre d’arrivée. ALIMA se réserve le droit de fermer l’offre avant le terme initialement indiqué si une candidature est retenue. Seules les candidatures complètes (CV en format PDF + Lettre de Motivation) seront étudiées.
- Les candidatures féminines sont fortement encouragées.

jobs.title: Senior Compensation & Benefits Advisor, EU and Strategic Initiatives- UK or NL
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
jobs.body:
**Location:** UK, or NL flexible working from home (NL base location preferred)

**Status:** Full-time

**Starting salary range:** NL: € 70,920; UK: £60.030; hiring range commensurate on professional experience

[**Risk Level:**](https://library.mercycorps.org/record/47705?ln=en) ☐ **Level 3** ☐**Level 2** ☐**Level 1**

(Level 3: Frequent contact with participants, direct contact with children, access to sensitive data, and/or high level of accountability.

Level 2: Some contact with participants; unplanned non-direct contact with children.

Level 1: Likely to have no contact with participants or sensitive data)

**About Prosper Global**

Barely enough is not enough for anyone. Prosper Global is a humanitarian organization working alongside communities facing conflict, climate change, and economic hardship to meet urgent needs and create the conditions for lasting progress. Today's challenges demand new solutions, so we pair local knowledge with global resources to help communities build what's needed, test what's possible, and scale what's proven so that people everywhere can pursue a full life on their own terms. In 2026, we changed our name from Mercy Corps to Prosper Global, to reflect our belief that when every community can prosper, all of humanity moves forward.

## **The Department**

The People Team ensures that Prosper Global has the people, strategies and learning that will enable it to be a world-class, cutting edge, humanitarian organization, creating transformational change in the world. We do this through the recruitment, retention and development of the best global talent.
