jobs.title: Nigeria Trees Execution Specialist
jobs.body:
## **About One Acre Fund**

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

The Nigeria program, established in 2018, is headquartered in Minna, Niger state. We're currently serving over 100,000 unique farmers across the state via our inputs on credit 'Core' program, inputs on cash 'Retail' program, and have a free tree seedling distribution 'Agroforestry' program. To learn more about our work, look at our Nigeria program blog.

## **About the Role**

The Nigeria program, established in 2018, is headquartered in Minna, Niger state. We're currently serving over 100,000 unique farmers across the state via our inputs on credit 'Core' program, inputs on cash 'Retail' program, and have a free tree seedling distribution 'Agroforestry' program. To learn more about our work, look at our Nigeria program blog.

## **Responsibilities**

Operations & Data Management Protocols

- Own and maintain operational data management protocols across seedling production, farmer enrollment, and distribution.
- Design, build, and maintain advanced data dashboards to track real-time operational KPIs, inventory, and performance metrics.
- Analyze operational data to identify bottlenecks, forecast capacity, and drive data-informed decision-making across field teams.
- Ensure data integrity, standardization, and seamless reporting across all operational sites and regional teams.

Expansion Mapping & Scaling

- Lead expansion mapping efforts, both internally within existing sites and externally into new states, in close collaboration with the Expansion Team.
- Conduct nursery location feasibility, logistical assessments, and operational modeling to guide successful market entry and program rollout.
- Standardize operational launch playbooks to ensure rapid, high-quality setup of new nurseries.

Process Optimization

- Interrogate current operational models to drive continuous productivity, operational efficiency, and year-on-year unit cost reductions.
- Identify, test, and integrate field technology solutions (e.g., automated nursery tools, mobile tracking, GIS mapping) to streamline systems in collaboration with the tech team
- Go to Gemba regularly to audit field operations, map processes, and eliminate operational waste in nursery management and logistics.

Cross-Functional Execution

- Collaborate regularly with Supply Chain, Expansion, and Tech teams as it aligns with the requirements of this role.
- Manage vendor, logistics, and resource procurement relationships necessary for seamless field execution.
- Map and mitigate operational risks that impact program timelines, input delivery, seedling delivery, or cost efficiency.

Team Leadership and Talent Management

- Lead, mentor, and motivate teams to achieve operational targets and maintain high performance.
- Create standard operating procedures (SOPs) and conduct regular training on data tools, field technology, and lean operational practices.
- Conduct bi-annual performance development reviews, set clear targets, and foster a culture of accountability and continuous learning.
- Support recruitment efforts and lead execution of recruitment plans at state or regional level.
- Could be responsible for OAF field operations at a regional level (one or two states).

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## **Qualifications**

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

- 3+ years years of relevant professional work experience, including leading teams
- Experience implementing projects at the field level
- University degree in Agricultural Economics, Supply Chain Management, Business Analytics, Data Science, Industrial Engineering, Agroforestry, International Development, or a related quantitative/operational field. Preferred: Project Management Certification.
- Advanced Data Analysis & Dashboarding: High proficiency in visualization tools (e.g., Power BI, Tableau, Looker), SQL, or advanced Excel for building dynamic operational dashboards.
- Scale mapping: Strong understanding of operational cost drivers and efficiency metrics
- Experience with mobile data collection platforms (e.g., CommCare, ODK, Kobo)
- Operations Management: Proven track record managing complex logistics/inventory/distribution operations in rural context.
- Strategic Problem-Solving: Ability to analyze complex field data, diagnose root causes, and execute pragmatic, timely decisions.
- Team Management: Demonstrated ability to lead, inspire, and manage teams across geographically dispersed locations.
- Project Management: Highly organized, self-driven, and adept at managing multi-state project timelines under tight deadlines.

As soon as possible

Health insurance, paid time off

jobs.title: Senior Program Quality and Learning Officer, POWER Partnership
jobs.body:
**Background**

The International Rescue Committee helps people affected by conflict and disaster to survive, recover, and regain control of their future. The Violence Prevention and Response Unit leads IRC's work across women's protection and empowerment, child protection, and protection and rule of law, positioning social work in crises as the connective practice across these areas.

POWER is a multi-country strategic partnership funded by Irish Aid, running from 2025 to 2027 across Burundi, Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, South Sudan, and Sudan. Its core logic is holistic gender-based violence prevention and response delivered through strengthened local women-led organizations, including partners such as SSWC in Somalia and FODDAJ in Kenya, with a quarter of country budgets channeled directly to local partners under a feminist partnership framework and the PEERS power-sharing principles. The program includes a dedicated advocacy pillar, an emergency response pillar, and a partnership learning pillar, and it works through practices such as women-led safety audits that already constitute community-generated risk analysis feeding into local advocacy and decision-making.

**Job overview**

The Senior Program Quality and Learning Officer coordinates quality and learning across the six POWER country programs. The role works through country WPE and program teams, POWER’s women-led and local partners, and the WPE Global Practice, and coordinates with the Award Management Unit (AMU), which leads the donor relationship with Irish Aid. It is accountable for technical quality assistance against IRC core WPE standards and the IASC GBV Minimum Standards for the design and delivery of the partnership learning pillar, and for tracking and reporting delivery against scope, timeline, and budget across the six countries so that deviation is identified early. The position contributes to the partnership’s advocacy pillar and to the design of the next partnership phase.

**Major responsibilities**

The role holds the technical quality of POWER delivery to IRC's WPE standards, keeps the partnership and the WPE Global Practice in two-way exchange ,rather than a one directional flow of standards downward, and tracks delivery across six countries against scope, timeline and budget so that deviation is flagged early enough for adaptive management

- Provide quality oversight across the six country programs, so that survivor-centered response, case management, women and girls' safe spaces, clinical and MHPSS referral pathways, and social norms work meet IRC WPE technical standards and the IASC GBV Minimum Standards.
- Serve as the connective role between the POWER partnership and the WPE Global Practice, translating core standards into partnership contexts and carrying partnership-generated practice back into the core.
- Support the sequencing of prevention and social norms activities to context, so they are introduced only where women-led community analysis confirms the preconditions for safe implementation are met.
- Maintain coherence of approach across the six countries without flattening contextual difference, identifying where a shared standard applies and where local adaptation is warranted.
- Track and report on delivery against scope, timeline, and budget across the six country programs, flagging deviation early enough for adaptive management rather than end-of-cycle correction.
- Ensure MEAL and program data feed directly into program adaptation, so that what the data shows changes what the program does, not only what it reports.
- Connect program data and implementation evidence to wider sector trends and debates, including comparable protection and GBV programming elsewhere.

**Learning, evidence, and the partnership learning agenda**

The role leads the program's learning function, treating implementation learning as a legitimate evidence pathway rather than a lesser substitute for external research. It also support the partnership’s advocacy pillar, so that evidence generated with the partners informs partners’ own advocacy and IRC’s policy positioning.

- Lead the design and delivery of the partnership learning pillar, coordinating cross-country learning cycles, documentation, and structured reflection between IRC and partners.
- Position women-led safety audits as community-generated risk analysis, and strengthen the pathway from that analysis into local decision-making and adaptive management.
- Build the program's evidence base on what enables and constrains change in protracted crisis settings, surfacing failure modes honestly, including referral systems that exist on paper but not in practice, and norms work that shifts survey scores without shifting community behavior.
- Ensure learning is co-owned with partners and feeds their own institutional positioning, not only IRC's reporting obligations.
- Steward the POWER advocacy pillar, supporting partners to carry community-generated analysis into local, national, and global advocacy where they hold standing in their own right.
- Work with advocacy and policy colleagues so the partnership's evidence informs IRC positioning toward donors, multilaterals, and normative bodies.

**Strengthening the core and surge capacity of women-led and local organizations**

The role supports partners on two distinct fronts, their institutional core and their capacity to surge in emergencies, resisting the pattern where localization language coexists with authority still held by the international actor.

- Support partner institutional strengthening across governance, financial systems, safeguarding, and MEAL in ways partners define and lead, consistent with the PEERS principles and the direct funding commitment.
- Strengthen partner surge and emergency response readiness under the emergency response pillar, so local organizations hold a credible role when crises escalate rather than being displaced by international surge.
- Advance the shift of analytical and decision-making authority toward partners with genuine institutional standing, including SSWC in Somalia and FODDAJ in Kenya, co-designing tools and thresholds with them rather than imposing them.
- Support the broader civil society and women's movement ecosystem the partnership connects to, recognizing partners as governance and coordination actors in their own right.

**Strategic focus on women and girls in conflict settings**

The role keeps women and girls in active conflict and protracted displacement at the center of the partnership, including where conflict-related sexual violence is a feature of the context.

- Ensure program design and adaptation are anchored in the realities faced by women and girls across the six contexts, several of which are shaped by active conflict and large-scale displacement.
- Support conflict-related sexual violence sensitive practice where relevant, including safe and consent-based documentation, clinical pathways, and Do No Harm decisions taken at closest proximity to violence, with pattern awareness fed upward.
- Keep adolescent girls visible as a distinct group rather than folded into a general women-and-girls category.

**Partnership and donor relationship management**

The role supports coherence of technical delivery across countries and reporting cycles, contributing technical content into the strategic relationship with Irish Aid, which AMU stewards and holds overall.

- Serve as a central program coordination point for the POWER partnership, supporting planning, adaptive management, amendments, and quality reporting to Irish Aid in coordination with the European DE & Frameworks team (Irish Aid).
- Feed technical content on program direction, learning, and strategic opportunities into AMU's communication with Irish Aid and the Department of Foreign Affairs. .
- Coordinate across the six country teams and the relevant IRC technical, advocacy, awards, and finance functions to keep the partnership coherent and its commitments met.
- Contribute technical input to AMU's design and negotiation of the next Strategic Partnership phase (post-2027), including program scope, theory of change, and the monitoring, evaluation and learning framework, coordinating input from WPE pillar leads, country teams, and partners, under AMU's overall lead on negotiation, timeline, and the donor relationship.

**Key working relationships**

**Works closely with:** AMU, Global and VPRU Advocacy; VPRU MEAL/METAL Unit.

Country WPE and program leads across the six POWER countries; POWER women-led and local partners, including SSWC in Somalia and FODDAJ in Kenya; IRC Awards Management Unit (AMU); VPRU Business Development; Irish Aid and Department of Foreign Affairs counterparts.

**Job requirements**

**Education:** Advanced degree in a relevant field such as social work, gender studies, international development, human rights, public health, or law, or an equivalent combination of qualification and experience.

**Work experience:** A minimum of 8 years professional experience in GBV, WPE, or protection programming in humanitarian and conflict-affected settings, at a technical lead level, including demonstrated experience in partnership and locally-led social action, in program quality or learning, and in program or grant management including budget oversight.

**Demonstrated skills and competencies:**

- Strong technical grounding in WPE practice and the IASC GBV Minimum Standards.
- Practical experience in feminist partnership and localization, including working with women-led organizations as partners rather than subgrantees.
- Learning and MEAL capability, with the judgment to treat implementation learning as evidence and to surface difficult findings.
- Program and grant management across multiple countries, including tracking and reporting r delivery against scope, timeline, and budget, and the systems to flag deviation early.
- Ability to translate program evidence into policy-relevant framing for donors, multilaterals, and normative processes.
- Multi-country coordination across diverse and often insecure contexts, with contextual and political sensitivity.
- Sound Do No Harm and safeguarding judgment, particularly in conflict-related sexual violence contexts.

**Languages:** Fluent English required. French is an asset given the East and Central Africa footprint, and Arabic is an asset for the Sudan and South Sudan contexts.

**Working environment and travel:** Possible travel across the six countries, including to hardship and conflict-affected locations.

***This is a hybrid position open to internal candidates based in countries where IRC operates who have the right to work in their location. Successful candidates will be hired on a local employment contract and according to local salary scale.***

***This role is open to candidates located and with the right to work in Kenya, Uganda, Burundi.***

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. jobs.body:
## **National Technical Experts in Eastern and Southern Africa (M/W)**

Departement Economie Durable et Inclusive - EDIN > Pôle Entreprenariat et Innovation  
Published on : 2026/08/25

**SUB-SAHARAN AFRICA BURUNDI**

### Mission description

Expertise France is launching a call for applications for the position of National Technical Experts (NTEs) to be based in the 3 potential countries of implementation of the SWITCH to Circular Economy in Eastern and Southern Africa (SWITCH 2 CE in ESA) Programme, namely: Burundi, Malawi and Mozambique,

These NTEs will support the implementation and success of the SWITCH-2-CE in ESA Project through the following thematic areas.

**ACTIVITY 1. Stakeholder Engagement and coordination**

I. Map and maintain relationships with key national stakeholders, including:

a. Relevant line ministries (e.g., Environment, Industry, Trade, Finance, SME Development) and RECs.

b. National development agencies, investment promotion authorities, and Environment Agencies.

c. Financial institutions (banks, micro-finance institutions, development banks) and Micro, Small and Medium Scale Enterprises involved in CE, in particular in the 2 Project Value chains.

d. Business Associations, CE Advocacy Associations, and CSOs involved in CE.

II. Support Project engagements with the stakeholders and facilitate implementation efforts.

**ACTIVITY 2. Enabling CE Policy Frameworks**

I. Act as the first point of contact for stakeholders in-country regarding Outcome 1

II. Policy Support Facility

a. Coordinate support efforts to beneficiaries of the Policy Support Facility.

b. Support efforts to raise awareness on the Policy Support Facility

III. Policy Dialogues

a. Support the implementation of national policy dialogues on CE

IV. Knowledge Production and dissemination on CE

a. Support Project efforts on knowledge production and dissemination activities relating to CE

**ACTIVITY 3. Matching Grant Facility (MGF)**

I. Act as the first point of contact for stakeholders in-country regarding the MGF

II. Assist in the identification and pre-screening of potential applicants for 3rd party organisations that would manage grants

III. Assist in the identification and pre-screening of BDS providers that would provide CE technical expertise to CE businesses.

IV. Facilitate outreach to local financial institutions.

V. Facilitate the outreach to potential eligible MSMEs that could benefit from the MGF

VI. Provide local insights and intelligence on financial ecosystem dynamics, MSME challenges, and enabling environment.

VII. Monitor in-country developments in circular economy and report on opportunities or risks for the MGF.

**ACTIVITY 4: Monitoring and Learning**

I. Produce periodic reports on Project activities and progress made in CE in the respective country.

II. Carry out monitoring activities and contribute to the collection and consolidation of M&E data to feed into project indicators and reporting requirements.

**Activity 5: General Support**

Provide general country support such as identifying local experts and supporting with local administrative processes.

### Project or context description

Expertise France and GIZ are jointly implementing the Switch to Circular Economy (SWITCH-2-CE in ESA) programme, funded by the European Union. The overall objectiveof the SWITCH-2-CE in ESA programme is to foster an inclusive transition to circular economy in East and Southern Africa (ESA). The programme seeks to contribute to the mitigation of climate change by promoting green and circular business models and strengthening the regulatory and policy framework for circular economy.

The SWITCH-2-CE in ESA Project would be implemented in 13 ESA countries, namely Angola, Botswana, Burundi, Ethiopia, Kenya, Malawi, Mozambique, Namibia, Rwanda, South Africa, Tanzania, Uganda and Zambia. The identification of these countries is provisional and may be further validated or adjusted based on the outcomes of the inception and analysis phase.

SWITCH-2-CE in ESA programme is structured around three main objectives (outcomes), with two priority value chains: “packaging/plastics waste” and “electronics/e-waste”. The three main objectives are:

· **Outcome 1:** Establish an enabling policy framework for circular economy across the ESA region.

*Under Outcome 1, the Project efforts will seek to improve access to resources on inclusive circular economy (CE) best practices by Policymakers, support integration of CE principles into policy frameworks and grow public sector capacity to support CE through Extended Producer Responsibility schemes.*

· **Outcome 2:** Enhance the participation of formal and informal workers and SMEs, including women and youth, in circular economy models.

*Under Outcome 2, the Project efforts will seek to support the integration of CE topics into Higher Education and TVET with gender-sensitive approaches, improve the availability of inclusive CE training to women, youth, and informal workers, and improve firm’s access to CE knowledge and best practice materials across the region.*

· **Outcome 3:** Improve access to and use of financing by circular economy businesses.

*Under Outcome 3, the Project efforts will seek to improve access to financial services to CE start-ups and SMEs, especially those led by youth and women, and improving availability of incubation and advisory support for business planning, financial readiness, and technology development.*

*The MGF will be implemented via third-party organisations, which will be responsible for co-selecting and disbursing grants to eligible businesses operating within the two targeted value chains.*

***Structure of the MGF:** Expertise France → Third-party organizations → Final beneficiaries (MSMEs & start-ups)*

In terms of definitions, **E-waste** encompasses discarded electrical and electronic equipment with a plug or battery, including items like smartphones, laptops, televisions, refrigerators, and small household appliances. **Plastic packaging** includes plastic materials used to contain, protect, handle, or deliver products, such as bottles, containers, wrappers, films, and single-use plastics like bags, straws, and takeaway food packaging.

### Required profile

- At least 5 years’ experience in stakeholder mobilisation, coordination or policy advocacy preferably in sustainable development, private sector development or green economy.
- Advanced University degree in economics, business administration, environment or related fields.
- Strong knowledge of national economic, financial, and environmental policy landscape.
- Proven track record of engaging with government ministries, RECs, private sector actors, and development partners.
- Proven experience working in supporting the private sector and knowledge of the MSME support ecosystem is a strong advantage.
- Familiarity with circular economy concepts and green financing mechanisms is an added advantage.
- Individual with strong networks and a solid understanding of their national circular economy landscape
- Ability to work independently and remotely, with strong organizational skills.
- Nationality or proven professional expertise in one of the 13 target countries
- Excellent communication, facilitation, and reporting skills.
- Language: English and Portuguese in the case of Mozambique

### Additional information

**Documentation to Be Submitted**

· CV (Focused on relevant experiences, not more than 2 pages)

· A brief technical proposal (2-3 pages max). The technical proposal should explain how the consultant will meet requirements (addressing Chapter “Assignment” of this ToR), specifying particularly which actors they can mobilize and how they plan to reach out to them.

· Explicitly state which country you are applying to be focal point for in the technical proposal.

**Accountability and Oversight**

The NTE will report to the SWITCH-2-CE Project Co-Lead or the designated officer.

**Nature of the contract and duration**

· Individual consultancy framework contract with purchase orders

· 40 months contract (expected start date – January 2026)

· Approximately 30 to 60 days per year subject to demand.

**Compensation**

· Daily fees will be assessed based on qualifications, level of expertise, and the applicant’s financial offer

jobs.body:
## About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

## About the Young Professionals Program

One Acre Fund’s Young Professionals Program offers high-performing African graduates meaningful internships and training opportunities at a high-performing, mission-driven organization. Our internships are paid and all interns can expect to receive substantive work assignments working on high-impact projects that support One Acre Fund's operations.

When joining, interns will participate in an onboarding program and receive training on how to design and execute projects. Over the period of your internship, you will get the opportunity to work with like-minded individuals and receive learning opportunities to build strong foundations for your future career.

## About the Role

You will provide support to all departments within the Burundi Program in carrying out recruitment activities for all junior-level positions. You will also handle administrative tasks and support Global Recruitment on a need basis.

## Responsibilities

Direct ownership of 10 - 12 pipelines

- Manage the recruitment process for all junior-level positions, from the application stage through to the offer stage.
- Review CVs and conduct phone interviews in French or English.
- Ensure timely posting of job openings both internally and externally; proactively collaborate with job posting agencies.
- Edit and format job descriptions to ensure clarity and consistency.
- Organize data and manage all communications within the electronic applicant tracking system (Greenhouse).
- Maintain and regularly update the recruitment tracker (for new and closed positions) to support timely reporting to the hiring commission.
- Identify and manage small-scale process improvement projects.
- Collaborate effectively with the Corporate Operations department to coordinate logistics for final interviews and ensure candidates have a positive experience throughout the recruitment process.
- Manage the Burundi Recruitment email inbox used for receiving applications for certain junior-level positions:
    1. Respond to candidate inquiries.
    2. Import candidate files into the electronic applicant tracking system (Greenhouse).

Global Recruitment Team support

- Provide support to the global recruitment team with any additional tasks related to daily recruitment operations, as delegated by the manager.

Other duties: As requested by your manager to advance our mission

## Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we deeply invest in our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training, and regular feedback on your performance. We’ll hold career reviews every one-three months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and gain rewarding technical experience.

## Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

- A Bachelor's degree in Human Resources Management, Business Administration, Communications, or a related field.
- Must be a Burundian national.
- Language proficiency: English (required), French (required), Kirundi (preferred).

## Preferred Start Date

As soon as possible

## Job Location

Bujumbura, Burundi

## Benefits

Interns will be provided with a reasonable stipend for the duration of their contract. Rural area based fellows will be provided assistance in locating suitable housing.

## Eligibility

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Burundi.

## Application Deadline

11 December 2026. We hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

*One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @*[*oneacrefund.org*](http://oneacrefund.org/) *address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), **but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.***

*Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.*

*We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.*

jobs.title: Palestine - Program Coordinator (M/F) - Jerusalem
jobs.body:
## About us

**Desired start date: 15/10/2026**  
**Duration of the mission: 12 months**  
**Location: Jerusalem**

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms.

## La mission

In response to the attacks of 7 October 2023, the Israeli army launched a massive offensive in the Gaza Strip, beginning with a campaign of air strikes followed by a series of ground offensives that successively hit all the enclave's governorates. The intensity of the fighting, repeated strikes and successive evacuation orders have forced more than 1.7 million people to move, sometimes several times, to sites less directly affected by the fighting. The first displacements towards the south of Gaza, and more particularly the governorate of Rafah where 1.7 million Palestinians were displaced in April 2024, were followed by the displacement of more than 1 million people towards the central part of the Gaza Strip when the offensive on Rafah was launched in May 2024.

Displaced people are living in schools, organised sites and informal sites where it is more difficult to organise assistance. The destruction by the fighting of vital infrastructure, such as health facilities, water and electricity supplies, schools and other public services, is having a major impact on the displaced and host populations.

**SOLIDARITÉS INTERNATIONA**L teams have been working in Gaza since February 2024. Activities are currently being developed in the governorate of Deir el-Balah, in the centre of the Gaza Strip, where a base was opened in March.  
SI teams are implementing WASH activities, which include the installation and rehabilitation of water desalination plants to ensure the production of drinking water, the transport of water to displacement sites by tanker truck, and activities aimed at reducing health risks and improving the living conditions of displaced people through hygiene promotion sessions and the distribution of hygiene kits.

## Job description

**General objective:**

The Program Coordinator oversees the development and quality of SI’s programs, ensuring they are needs-driven, context-adapted, and impactful. S/He supports strategic planning, program monitoring, technical compliance, and coordination across teams, partners, and donors, while strengthening staff capacities and safeguarding ethical standards.

**The main challenges:**

1\) Developing strategy and defining SI value add for West Bank, including positioning on coordination architecture, and preparedness in the case of a medium-scale escalation.  
2\) Developing SI strategy and relevance in Shelter and FSL for Gaza.   
3\) Challenges include compliance, resource allocation, staff capacity, and integrating cross-cutting themes while mitigating operational and ethical risks.

**Priorities for the 2/3 first months:**

Support the structuration of the mission, including onboarding new staff, expanding activities, and developing new sectors and areas of intervention.   
Reinforce quality monitoring of program strategies and ensure the implementation and harmonization of SI’s frameworks, tools, and procedures across all teams.  
Implement the strategy of the mission and develop the activities of SI in the West Bank   
Continue to support the activities and Gaza to kept Gaza as a key Wash actor

**Security constraints:**

The mission faces no particular security constraints in Jerusalem, however, there are major security and access challenges in the Gaza Strip.

## Votre profil

**DIPLOMAS AND EXPERIENCE**

Master's degree in Humanitarian Action, human rights, social science (geography, sociology, anthropology, history) or Political Science is more preferable.

Experience in the humanitarian sector : 5 years

Experience on a similar position : 3/4 years

**SKILLS**

TECHNICAL SKILLS

1\) Program strategy development

2\) Multi-sector program design (WASH, FSL ).

3\) Partnership development and coordination

4)External coordination: engagement with clusters, international partners, and national actors

TRANSVERSAL SKILLS

1)Leadership and team management

2)Coordination across multi-level teams

3)Capacity building and training

**LANGUAGES**

**- English**

**- Arabic is an asset**

## SI will offer you

**A salaried position:**  
**According to experience,** starting from EUR 2860 gross per month (2600base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 750.

SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment.

**Breaks:** During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every three months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked.

**Insurance package:** Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded.

**LIVING CONDITIONS:**

To date, SI have a coordination office and a guesthouse in Jerusalem. The office is fully furnished, and the guesthouse is equipped with all necessary equipment (internet, kitchen, laundry facilities, living room, etc.). Jerusalem is generally very safe, and staff can move freely across most areas of East and West Jerusalem. Walking is permitted.
